title: 10x Faster Vector Indexes: GPU Acceleration in Amazon OpenSearch with NVIDIA cuVS (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speaker: Corey Nolet, Vamshi Vijay Nakkirtha, Navneet Verma
abstract: At billion-vector scale, vector index construction can become a performance and cost bottleneck for retrieval, RAG, and AI workloads. Amazon OpenSearch Service Vector Acceleration uses NVIDIA cuVS to accelerate index construction, delivering up to 10x faster builds at a quarter of the indexing cost while preserving the OpenSearch experience. This 300-level session goes under the hood of the architecture: how eligible builds are offloaded to managed GPU workers, how cuVS and CAGRA accelerate graph construction through the Faiss backend, and how the graph is converted into an HNSW index for CPU-based search. We will examine how segment size, quantization, and ingestion patterns affect GPU utilization, build speed, and efficiency. Attendees will leave with guidance for identifying good-fit workloads, optimizing ingestion, and modeling performance and cost benefits for their own deployments. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Roman I

title: 10x or bust: How Amazon's Frontier teams ship with Kiro
speaker: McLaren Stanley, Eva Knight
abstract: Amazon teams using Kiro and AI-native workflows are shipping features in hours that used to take weeks. But the gains didn't come from better prompts. They came from better practices, from rethinking how developers and teams work instead of just adding shiny tools on top of existing SDLC processes. This session dissects three real experiments: a pathfinder initiative, a structured sprint, and in-situ pilots across 50+ teams. You'll learn the five practices that compound into 4.5x–10x gains, the mistakes that kill momentum, and how to run your own pilot starting Monday.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: 15 Minutes Is Too Late: Stop AWS Intrusions with CrowdStrike’s Cloud SOC Agent (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
speaker: Vinayak Shastri
abstract: In seconds, adversaries can move from a stolen credential to the AWS control plane, workloads, and Kubernetes before the SOC even begins triage. In this session, see how CrowdStrike Falcon Cloud Security turns a complex AWS attack into one high-confidence incident. Follow an end-to-end intrusion as adversary-informed correlated detections connect identity, control-plane and workload activity; AI-based anomaly detection exposes behavior static rules miss; and Real-Time CDR analyzes AWS activity as it streams in. Then watch CrowdStrike’s Cloud SOC Agent investigate, enrich and prioritize the intrusion, staging rapid response actions for human analyst approval before it becomes a breach. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: 171 agents at scale: How Halter automated internal ops and engineering
speaker: Antony Southworth, David MacDonald
abstract: Halter built and deployed 171 AI agents across its internal operations and engineering functions, saving 215 engineering hours. This session covers how Halter identified which workflows to automate, how they built and scaled that many agents, and what it takes to get an organization comfortable running that much of its internal work through AI agents.

title: 3 a.m. and Already Fixed: How PagerDuty’s SRE Agent Is Rewriting Incident Response (sponsored by PagerDuty)
speaker: Samrat Ghosh, Alice McElroy
abstract: Every SRE knows the pattern: an alert fires, and the next 20 minutes disappear into triage before you've even confirmed what's broken. Context is scattered across dashboards, runbooks, and tribal knowledge, and much of incident response is just reconstructing what already happened. This session explores how autonomous operations changes that story. PagerDuty’s SRE Agent investigates before a human is even involved and proposes fixes you simply approve. See it firsthand through PD Labs, a hands-on site for trying autonomous workflows, and SRE Workbench, launching in early access, where humans, agents, and automation meet in order to investigate, diagnose, and remediate issues. This presentation is brought to you by PagerDuty, an AWS Partner.

title: 4 primitives for an AI SRE that runs on-call and improves reliability (sponsored by ResolveAI)
speaker: Steven Karis, Varun Krovvidi
abstract: Why should engineers still be on call? Agents you trust should take the pages, close them autonomously, drive incidents to resolution, and even fix the underlying issues behind them. Trusting agents on this critical path for production reliability comes down to four primitives: does it know production better than any single tool or team, does it deliver frontier SRE quality, can it be trusted to act on your behalf, and do the costs stay in check. Steven Karis, Chief Architect at ResolveAI, shows how each primitive shapes an SRE agent that owns on-call and improves reliability autonomously. Engineering leaders from Figma and Autodesk join him to walk through how their teams are using agents to run on-call and drive reliability.

title: 50k daily iOS builds with virtualization on Amazon EC2 Mac
speaker: Kyle Krall, Francisco Costa, Jonas França
abstract: A leading automotive manufacturer migrated its CI/CD infrastructure from on-premises to AWS to support over 130,000 daily builds (50k + iOS) across 1,300+ microservices. To accelerate iOS mobile app development, the team adopted Amazon EC2 Mac instances with virtualization using OpenAI Tart virtualization toolset, enabling ephemeral macOS VMs that boot in seconds with pre-configured toolchains. This approach reduced average build times from 90 to 35 minutes, a 61% improvement, while eliminating hardware management overhead. The platform now scales to 50,000+ daily iOS builds, serving 3,000+ developers with cost-optimized, reliable, and secure pipelines across hundreds of AWS accounts worldwide.

title: 5 Amazon ECS features that prevent common production incidents
speaker: David Ugarte
abstract: Five configuration mistakes cause the majority of Amazon ECS production incidents. All five are fixable in under a minute. AZ spread off means one zone failure takes your service down. Short health check grace periods kill containers that are still starting. Disabled circuit breakers let bad deploys roll forward across every task. Default dependency timeouts turn one slow call into a cascading outage. Placement constraints pack tasks onto too few hosts. In this lightning talk, see the incident each feature prevents, the specific attribute to verify, and the fix. Leave with a production-readiness checklist your team can use before every release.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: 5 Questions Terraform, OpenTofu, and CloudFormation Can't Answer (sponsored by Spacelift, Inc.)
speaker: Jonah Kowall
abstract: Every infrastructure change is one run: code, an engine, a plan, an apply. That run is still a wall of unstructured log text, and the questions about your estate go unanswered. Five to ask of your IaC: Did Terraform, OpenTofu, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, or Ansible run it, and does it matter? Where does the time go, and can OpenTelemetry tracing show you? What happens outside the engine: providers, state, policy-as-code, drift, queue time? What about unmanaged resources, the half of your AWS account no run ever touched? Who gets self-service, and can an AI agent be trusted with an apply? This presentation is brought to you by Spacelift, Inc., an AWS Partner.

Move into automated wave planning and landing zone deployment. See how network architectures convert into production-ready VPCs and workloads rehost to Amazon EC2 at scale. Then hear from StarHub, a leading Singapore-based telecommunications provider, on how agentic AI accelerated their infrastructure modernization and move to AWS in record time.

title: Accelerate database protection and testing with EBS Snapshots and clones
speaker: Shibin Michaelraj, Santhosh Arunuri
abstract: Teams that rely on backups alone risk slow dev cycles, compliance gaps, and prolonged recovery times. Learn how Amazon EBS Snapshots and Volume Clones solve these challenges together. See how Snapshots deliver incremental, cross-region data protection with automated lifecycle policies for compliance, while Volume Clones create instant local copies for development and testing. We'll compare cost, performance, and architectural tradeoffs. You'll leave with a decision framework for when to snapshot, when to clone, and how to combine both in production architectures.

speaker: James Kuhlke, Juha Sarimaa, Tom Edward Bailey, Sara Kilbride, Kathy Huffstetler
abstract: Protecting your data and troubleshooting issues are essential for running production self-managed databases on AWS. This builders’ session tackles both. Get hands-on with EBS Snapshot Lock for immutable backups, Recycle Bin for accidental deletion recovery, and Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager for automated, application-consistent snapshots. Learn Provisioned Rate for Volume Initialization for predictable restore throughput and use EBS Volume Clones to create virtually instant point-in-time copies without impacting production. You will leave with a practical playbook to improve your database resilience. Bring your laptop to participate.

speaker: Sebastien Allamand, Shani Adadi Kazaz
abstract: Build an Internal Developer Platform on Amazon EKS using managed capabilities — ArgoCD, AWS Controllers for Kubernetes (ACK), and kro. title: Accelerate service onboarding with composable AI plugins
speaker: Aditi Pendharkar, Aryan Desai
abstract: Service onboarding workflows consume hours across security, risk, and governance teams through manual approvals, evidence gathering, and threat modeling. These tasks are auditable, repetitive, and ripe for agentic decomposition. In this chalk talk, we walk through a composable AI plugin pattern that decomposes service onboarding into lightweight modules any agentic client can consume. We discuss how each plugin integrates with any agentic client to execute governance checks end-to-end. We share architecture patterns, working code examples, and show you how to reduce security review time. You’ll leave with a decomposition pattern and an open-source repo to get started.

title: Achieving Operational Excellence at Scale with AWS Unified Operations

abstract: As cloud environments grow in complexity, maintaining resilience across business-critical workloads demands more than reactive support, it requires embedded expertise, proactive monitoring, and continuous optimization. AWS Unified Operations combines designated AWS specialists, AI-powered incident detection, and expert-led resilience reviews to help enterprises reduce operational and security risks while accelerating their most critical cloud initiatives. In this session, we'll share findings from an independent Forrester Total Economic Impact study* that quantifies the business value of this approach: 181% ROI, 33% fewer business-critical incidents, 40% faster resolution times, and payback in under six months. Learn how designated domain specialists and 24/7 monitoring shift your operating model from reactive to preventive and how to build the business case for your organization. *The Total Economic Impact Of AWS Unified Operations - a commissioned study conducted by Forrester Consulting, October 2026. Results are based on a three-year composite organization representative of interviewed customers

title: A closer look at AWS Lambda durable functions
speaker: Eric Johnson
abstract: Lambda durable functions let you write reliable, long-running workflows as sequential code. We start with how durable execution works: checkpointing, replay-based recovery, and the programming model. Next, we explore production patterns including sagas, fan-out/fan-in, and human-in-the-loop waits. Finally, we cover observability, a decision framework to help you choose when to use durable functions versus AWS Step Functions, and operational considerations like concurrency, cost, and versioning.

speaker: Mohammed Atiq, Sean Kendall
abstract: In this code talk, follow a Serverless application from first line of code to production deployment, all live. Along the way, see how recent Serverless launches change the workflow: faster deploys, built-in observability, and simplified local testing. No slides, no diagrams. Just a terminal, an editor, and the workflow a Serverless developer uses in 2026.

speaker: Matt Luttrell, Khaled Sinno
abstract: Every API call in AWS passes through IAM policy evaluation, but few truly understand what happens in that moment between request and access decision. In this chalk talk, we go deep into the weeds of how IAM actually evaluates your policies: how the request context is assembled, how each policy type interacts in the evaluation chain, where implicit and explicit denials come from, and why some evaluation scenarios behave in ways that may be surprising. We will work through real scenarios, common gotchas, and edge cases live.

That culture is built through DevOps. Clear communication, team empowerment, and frequent experimentation and measurement are what separate teams that recover from teams that hope. This session covers the technical requirements for recovering cloud workloads at scale, and the DevOps practices that make those requirements actually work under pressure. You'll leave with practical knowledge to drive full recovery in the face of the worst disasters.

title: Adopt evolving Amazon DynamoDB resiliency design patterns
speaker: John Terhune, Jason Hunter
abstract: In this session, discover recently developed resilience mechanisms for DynamoDB workloads and how existing, advanced resilience patterns have been evolving. Learn how to use the global tables architecture with specific metrics and thresholds that drive effective failover decisions, as well as DR patterns that achieve low RTO and RPO without global tables overhead. Through whiteboard discussion, explore a variety of resilient DynamoDB workload solutions for specific use cases, including incremental export for undoing bad writes, which is faster and less disruptive than a full PITR table restore, approaches to protect against ransomware and data destruction, and cross-account table migration strategies.

Optimizing your usage of DynamoDB requires a different approach to data modeling than traditional relational databases. In this session, explore advanced techniques to help you get the most out of DynamoDB. Learn how to “think in DynamoDB” by learning the DynamoDB foundations and principles for data modeling. title: Advanced Optimization & Cost-Saving Strategies for Amazon Athena
speaker: Sundeep kumar, Scott Rigney
abstract: Dive deep into Amazon Athena's most powerful capabilities in this interactive chalk talk for experienced practitioners. We'll explore cost-saving techniques—CTAS for materializing expensive query results, partition projection to eliminate metadata lookups, and EXPLAIN-based tuning to minimize bytes scanned. Discuss workgroup budgets, provisioned capacity for predictable pricing, and query result reuse to avoid redundant scans. We'll cover Athena's latest innovations including Amazon S3 Tables integration for fully managed Iceberg tables and enhanced Spark notebooks.

title: Advanced S3 performance engineering: From multipart to resilience
speaker: Mark Twomey, Bob Holmes
abstract: Master advanced Amazon S3 performance optimization techniques across storage classes, including S3 Standard for general purpose storage and S3 Express One Zone for the highest performance needs. This expert-level workshop focuses on implementing sophisticated data transfer patterns using multipart uploads and Transfer Manager. Design and deploy resilient applications with advanced retry strategies and robust error handling mechanisms. Through technical exercises, build high-performance solutions for large-scale data transfers across different S3 storage classes. Learn to optimize your applications for specific performance requirements, from cost-effective general storage to ultra-low latency implementations. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

Join the S3 security team for a structured discussion of the patterns that solve the hardest multi-account access problems at scale.

title: Advanced vaulting: Ransomware resilience with AWS Backup
speaker: Vivek Mishra, Fathima Kamal
abstract: Bad actors increasingly target backups alongside production data, and organizations need a vaulting strategy that puts them out of reach. Isolation, immutability, and encryption form the pillars of that strategy, and this session dives deep into how to implement all three with AWS Backup. We'll cover logically air-gapped vault architecture, including how backups are stored in isolated, immutable infrastructure by default, encryption with AWS-owned and customer-managed keys, and durable recovery pathways with Multi-party approval. We'll also cover how these vaulting patterns feed into recovery workflows so that what's protected stays recoverable.

title: After the Agents Write the Code: A Field Report From 100 Million Code Reviews (sponsored by CodeRabbit)
speaker: David Loker
abstract: What does it take to move from human-centered software development to fully agentic development, so you can ship dramatically faster without sacrificing quality or security? More than 2 million times a week, CodeRabbit reviews a change before it merges, whoever or whatever wrote it. From where we sit, we see teams solving agentic coding, but not yet agentic shipping. Now that code is cheap to write, four things have become bottlenecks: review, understanding, prioritization, and security. CodeRabbit hit all four and cleared them, which is how it ships 10x more software without adding engineering headcount. David Loker, VP of Applied AI, shares the four practices that helped, how roles and workflows changed, and why a team has to build trust to ship fast. This presentation is brought to you by CodeRabbit, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic AI Meets Real Money: 5M+ Customer Chats With Amazon Payments

abstract: Where is my refund? What is this charge? How much is left on my gift card? Alexa for Shopping customers asked about their money, but the assistant couldn't reach payment systems, so two-second questions became contact-center calls. Meet the Amazon Payments agent. It reasons about each customer's need, securely retrieves their payment data, asks instead of guessing, and escalates to human specialists when needed. Guardrails keep money safe: payments-only scope, bounded tool calls, encrypted sensitive fields, and evaluation gates. Results: 5M+ interactions, 3M+ customers, and 50%+ higher refund satisfaction. title: Agentic fairness: Practical methods to detect bias in AI-driven decisions
speaker: Bharathi Srinivasan, Denis V Batalov
abstract: AI agents are increasingly making real-world decisions — approving loans, issuing refunds, offering discounts — yet most fairness testing still focuses on whether chatbots use offensive language. This gap creates real business and regulatory risk. Join this session to explore how to assess whether your agentic AI systems apply equitable treatment across chosen demographic attributes using defined fairness criteria. Through hands-on examples spanning financial services, customer support, and commerce, discover how to move from language-level toxicity checks to decision-level fairness audits. Learn to identify disparate treatment, choose appropriate fairness metrics for your use case, and implement testing frameworks that catch bias where it matters most: in the outcomes that affect people's lives.

title: Agentic Memory: Build AI Agents That Learn from Every Interaction
speaker: Abhishek Pandey, Ankur Taunk
abstract: Today's AI agents forget everything after each conversation ends. A customer calls back about the same issue for the third time, and the agent starts from zero. In this chalk talk, we explore how to architect persistent memory systems for Amazon Connect Customer AI agents, enabling them to remember customer preferences, recall prior issue context, and adapt resolution strategies over time. We walk through three memory patterns: episodic (past interactions), semantic (customer knowledge graphs), and procedural (learned resolution paths). We whiteboard real architectures using Customer Profiles, Bedrock knowledge bases, and DynamoDB to build agents that reduce repeat contacts and deliver personalized experiences, without retraining models. Bring your memory challenge and we'll design the persistence layer on the whiteboard.

title: Agents at Work, Humans in Control: Stopping the Action No Single Check Can See (sponsored by Cyera)
speaker: Sean Cordero
abstract: Every agent action answers three questions at once: what data it touches, whose access it uses, and what it is attempting to do. Your data, identity and AI tools each answer only one, so an agent can pull regulated records, act on someone else’s access, and send them outside the company while every tool lets it through. Controlling an agent means deciding on all three at once, and that control is what lets agents take on more of the work. This session shows why no single control, however good, can make that call alone, what it looks like when you do, and how Cyera and AWS are putting it to work for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents.

title: Agents can delete your data lake. Can you recover it? (sponsored by Rubrik)
speaker: Adam Rusho, Jérôme Cousin, John Mallory
abstract: AI is multiplying the identities and agents that can change your AWS data. One over-scoped role or runaway agent can delete or overwrite the data your models depend on, in an S3 lake or Iceberg lakehouse. Replication copies a bad write, versioning is often off. How do you recover without a valid backup? Learn where recovery breaks across S3, Glue Data Catalog, S3 Tables, and databases and pipelines around them, then how Rubrik recovers petabytes in hours, restoring only what changed, critical data first, within your RTO. Resilience spans your estate. Hear how TGS built a ransomware-resilient platform with Rubrik. This presentation is brought to you by Rubrik, an AWS Partner.

abstract: As AI agents proliferate, the internet needs a decentralized way to name, discover, and trust them. This session explores how AWS contributes to open source projects like DNS-AID (IETF/Linux Foundation) and AI-Catalog (Linux Foundation) to define the agent discovery layer atop existing DNS infrastructure. We'll walk through the specs — SVCB records, W3C DIDs, Verifiable Credentials, HTTP Message Signatures — and show how anyone can resolve and verify an agent with off-the-shelf libraries and a single DNS query. No vendor lock-in. Standards in, standards out.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Agents on call: Autonomous DB ops on Amazon Aurora with Expedia Group
speaker: Hao Nguyen, Anum Jang Sher
abstract: Expedia Group manages thousands of database instances across hundreds of AWS accounts. When incidents strike at this scale, every second counts. In this session, learn how a customer-driven vision for agentic AI evolved into a joint design partnership for autonomous database operations on Amazon Aurora. Discover how agents diagnose incidents across fleet-scale telemetry and deliver actionable recommendations to engineers. This joint initiative demonstrates how AI agents reduce incident response time and serves as a blueprint for teams seeking to automate database operations at scale. Learn how AWS is building the underlying capabilities to make autonomous operations real.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Agents run at the edge. The blast radius lives in the cloud (sponsored by Sysdig)
speaker: Conor Sherman, Eric Carter
abstract: Every agent your company runs, on a developer laptop, in a CI runner, or in an Amazon EKS pod, ends its work the same way, with an API call against your AWS account using a credential nobody reviewed. Endpoint tools stop at the laptop. The credentials that matter live in the cluster. This year's worst agent incidents involved no attacker. An agent did what it was permitted to do, and nobody rendered a decision at the moment a permitted step became an incident. In fifteen minutes, Sysdig follows one person's agents from their laptop into EKS, shows what each action would reach in your account, and stops the one whose reach includes admin-equivalent permissions before it executes. Bring your own agents. Ask us what they can reach. This presentation is brought to you by Sysdig, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Agents that train themselves: autonomous reinforcement learning on AWS
speaker: Rachit Mehta, Arron Bailiss, Patrick Gray, Gautam Sirdeshmukh, Bryan Lu
abstract: Can an AI agent teach itself to land a spacecraft? In this hands-on Builders' session you hand a Strands agent one goal: land the lunar lander gently. Then you watch it write its own reward, run reinforcement learning, and grade the result, looping until it sticks the landing. You'll catch it cheating, then watch it diagnose and fix its reward. When a run stalls, you fan out parallel agents and let a sealed judge crown the winner before shipping it to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Give an agent a goal and a judge it can't game, and it trains itself.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Agents That Use Desktop and Mainframe Apps: Governance Lessons Learned
abstract: Your critical workflows run in desktop and mainframe applications that expose no APIs, and scripted automation breaks each time a screen changes. Join peers from business and engineering teams, along with Amazon WorkSpaces experts, to swap stories about using governed agents to operate these applications. Compare notes on which workflows to hand to agents first, how to govern agents with scoped permissions, agent identity, and audit trails in CloudWatch and CloudTrail, and how to choose tools, models, and reusable skills that balance cost and accuracy. Bring your use cases, governance questions, and lessons learned.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Agents under oath: Designing agentic AI to support HIPAA compliance on AWS
speaker: Vignesh Srinivasan, Ray Chang
abstract: AI agents in government healthcare don't just query databases. They reason, remember, and act. Each of those capabilities opens a new surface where protected health information (PHI) can leak model responses, persistent memory, tool calls, RAG retrieval, and agent traces. Traditional RBAC and encryption were not built for this. In this chalk talk, we will walk through a real prior authorization determination scenario together, map where PHI bleeds through an ungoverned agent and then redesign the architecture as a group — four trust zones, sixteen controls, all mapped to HIPAA Security Rule safeguards. Come ready to draw and debate.

title: AgentX: Agentic customer service transformation (sponsored by Capgemini) (BIZ104-S)
speaker: Vivek Sandell, Mohammed Shadab Maved, Andreea Manolache
abstract: Capgemini and Bayer developed AgentX, an AWS-native agentic AI solution that empowers customer service agents with GenAI insights and turns customer interactions into actionable business intelligence. AgentX combines knowledge retrieval, real-time agent assistance, automated summaries, governance controls, predictive analytics, and AI-enabled workflows with human oversight. It helps agents work faster and more consistently, supporting higher-quality interactions and a better customer experience. Built using Amazon Connect, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Lambda and other AWS services, AgentX provides a reusable, scalable foundation for AI-enabled customer service. Discover how Bayer and Capgemini use a customer-centric, business-driven approach to create value for agents, supervisors and business leaders. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

title: AI-accelerated migration from self-managed Kubernetes to EKS Auto Mode
speaker: Aritra Nag, Hari Charan Ayada
abstract: Most teams start with one or two Amazon EKS clusters and grow into a fleet. AWS manages the control plane, but on standard EKS your team still owns version upgrades, add-ons, node lifecycle, and operational efforts. This session shows how to move that undifferentiated work to Amazon EKS Auto Mode, and how AI accelerates the migration itself. See how agentic tooling inventories your EKS clusters, translates node and add-on configuration, and flags what must change before you cut over. Learn patterns for enabling EKS Auto Mode with minimal disruption, then scaling the migration across your fleet in a fraction of the time manual work takes.

title: AI agents are crawling your website? Identify, optimize, rate-limit, & monetize them
speaker: RISHU GUPTA, Philon Terving
abstract: AI agents are the new web visitors, but how do you protect your content while unlocking new revenue? In this code talk, we deploy a Single Page Application on CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, and Bedrock, then progressively secure and monetize AI agent traffic. We integrate AWS WAF Bot Control to identify agents via the WBA protocol, implement intelligent routing in CloudFront Functions to serve optimized content per visitor type, and enforce rate limits by bot identity and actual resource consumption. Finally, we enable AI Traffic Monetization in WAF and demonstrate end-to-end paid content access using the x402 payment protocol with a Bedrock AgentCore.

abstract: When a data pipeline fails, how much should an AI agent be allowed to do? Join data engineers, architects, and AI builders to discuss agent-assisted troubleshooting and recovery using Amazon Bedrock and Strands Agents. Explore how agents can investigate failures, use operational tools, recommend fixes, and request human approval before making changes. Bring a pipeline challenge or lesson learned to compare approaches for access controls, evaluation, observability, and cost. Through small-group discussions, attendees will exchange practical ideas for moving from useful prototypes to trustworthy production workflows.

speaker: Manu Pillai, Marissa Powers
abstract: Managing HPC infrastructure shouldn’t slow down science and engineering. Learn how AI-powered agents with AWS Parallel Computing Service (AWS PCS) automate workload placement, detect and recover from failures, and simplify day-to-day cluster operations. Through practical examples, we’ll show how intelligent automation reduces operational overhead, improves resource utilization, and enables platform teams to spend less time managing infrastructure and more time supporting research and innovation.

title: AI agents for PostgreSQL replication and partitioning
speaker: Jim Mlodgenski, Chirag Dave
abstract: Recent PostgreSQL releases introduced transformative capabilities for logical replication and partitioning, including filtering, parallel apply, sequence replication, and improved planning for partition-heavy workloads. These features are powerful, but tuning them for a specific environment remains complex. In this session, learn to build agents for these core PostgreSQL concepts on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: one that analyzes workloads to recommend optimal logical replication configuration, and a partitioning agent that evaluates query patterns and table bloat to guide table partitioning strategy.

title: AI Agent Teams at Scale
speaker: Prashanth Krishnamurthy, Pavan Dusanapudi
abstract: When one event impacts hundreds, or even thousands, of customers simultaneously (a cancelled flight, a power outage, a system failure), contact centers cannot scale human agents fast enough. In this hands-on workshop, you orchestrate parallel AI agent teams using Amazon Connect Customer. You configure AI agents that fan out across dozens of affected customers at once: rebooking flights, issuing credits, and scheduling callbacks, all while a single human orchestrator monitors progress, approves exceptions, and intervenes only where needed. Walk away with a working parallel orchestration pattern and the configuration to deploy 1-to-many AI response at scale. This is not 1-to-1 AI coaching. This is 1-to-many crisis orchestration.

abstract: Public sector organizations serve diverse populations with strict boundaries: students and administrators, citizens and case workers, patients and providers. They need AI that works across these groups without compromising data isolation, compliance, or governance. Multi-tenant environments demand security frameworks most AI assistants were not built to meet. Hear from a higher education customer who faced these constraints and displaced their incumbent tool in favor of AWS Quick's governance-first architecture: tenant-level data isolation, role-based access controls across distinct user populations, and compliance frameworks built for regulated environments. Learn why existing solutions fell short, how Quick's native governance model met their requirements without custom engineering, and what the transition looked like from decision to deployment.

speaker: Kevin Willis, Keren Tseytlin, Robert McCauley, Greg Krumm, Lee Hannigan

Architect complex data models using sophisticated techniques right inside an AI-powered IDE, then go from modeling to production, building a full-stack, serverless application powered by DynamoDB and other AWS services via a coding agent of choice. Optimize access patterns, leverage secondary indexes, and express application requirements in natural language to generate and refine a complete solution built on DynamoDB. Discover how AI-assisted database design accelerates complex NoSQL decisions at every stage of development. Bring your laptop to participate.

In this chalk talk, AWS Customer Incident Response Team (CIRT) leaders share exactly how we made that transition and what we learned along the way. We'll diagram the pipeline live, simulate an investigation, and spend real time working through your scenarios at the whiteboard.

title: AI can predict your health. Can it change it?
speaker: Wilson To, Melissa Iftimie, Rowland Illing
abstract: Health AI has gotten very good at predicting who will get sick. Improving what happens next is much harder. Researchers and industry leaders working on that gap share what it takes to move a model from a published result to a better outcome for a real patient. They'll discuss how to design tools that adapt to patients in real time, how to overcome the data gaps and trust issues that stall deployments, and how to scale it across different populations and health systems, not just the one where it was first tested.

title: AI Didn't Wait for Security: Now What?
speaker: Stav Ochakovski, Ran Isenberg
abstract: AI didn't wait for your security review. Developers already ship code with agentic AI, coding assistants, and MCP servers without governance; blocking them lowers efficiency and leaves you falling behind. This builder-focused session dissects the architecture of a governed AI platform. You'll learn how to build a centralized MCP broker with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and Runtime, and how agent requests gain identity and permissions. You'll build and distribute a curated agentic skills catalog and reusable agentic blueprints. Finally, you'll see how AI SDLC frameworks bring consistency and higher-quality artifacts, with DevOps and security agents woven into key stages.

title: AI discipline: UCLA's data foundation and framework for saying no
speaker: Mary Strain, Aditya Singh
abstract: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) invested in their data foundation first. Their large-scale data modernization—Bruin Cloud and the campus Data Hub—created a unified, governed data environment across a sprawling research university, but it wasn't enough. As AI demand surged, Deputy CIO Veronica Garcia and her team built a disciplined product management approach to evaluate, prioritize, and scale AI use cases against UCLA's mission. Learn how UCLA’s technical architecture accelerated data modernization, the framework used to determine AI priorities, and the governance model that keeps it all aligned that launched high-impact use cases from increasing fundraising, advancing research, and supporting student safety and success.

Amaze, CP Group's super app, built an AI shopping assistant for shoppers across the group's brands, including 7-Eleven Thailand; Byte by Yum! powers personalized ordering and team member tools at Taco Bell; and Amorepacific built an AI beauty concierge delivering precision skin diagnoses across 10 countries.

Attendees will learn how to connect AI strategy to top- and bottom-line impact through real-world examples, including procurement optimization, contract leakage detection and citizen-developed agents that accelerate safe, responsible AI adoption across the enterprise. abstract: AI is changing how video gets made, understood, and monetized across broadcast, streaming, ad tech, and startups. This meetup gathers practitioners working through the hard parts: encoding efficiently, scaling, extracting scene-level metadata from live video in real time, and turning that metadata into smarter ad insertion and new revenue. abstract: The AI revolution is upending organizations’ security and GRC programs. Shadow AI is exploding as employees adopt new agent harnesses, workflows, platforms, and plugins. Even sanctioned AI poses new challenges that don’t yet have standardized solutions. Meanwhile, developers are moving AI applications from experimentation to production, introducing new risks. This session will break down what AI Governance is all about, cover common concerns that it’s meant to resolve, and provide attendees with practical tips for solving some of their most pressing AI Governance challenges. What you’ll learn. What AI Governance entails, from practical policy to active protections. How to solve AI Governance concerns across different layers of the AI stack. title: AI is Breaking Data Security… And Fixing It (sponsored by Concentric AI)
abstract: AI is rapidly becoming one of the biggest drivers of productivity and innovation in the enterprise — and one of the fastest-growing sources of data security risk. As copilots, assistants, and public AI tools become integrated into daily work, sensitive data is flowing into systems that most security teams can’t fully see, understand, or control. The problem is that traditional data security controls were never built for this. In fact, many organizations were already struggling to operationalize data security before AI accelerated the challenge. The good news? AI isn’t just creating the problem — it’s also enabling a smarter, more effective way to solve it. Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how AI is reshaping data security — and how they can use that same technology to gain control, minimize exposure, and support safer AI adoption across the business. This presentation is brought to you by Concentric AI, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: AI Is Getting Smarter. AI-Generated Code Isn’t Getting Safer. (sponsored by Veracode, Inc.)
speaker: Christian Dalomba
abstract: AI-generated code is scaling fast, but its security performance is not keeping up. Across more than 100 models tested since 2023, the average security pass rate remains stuck at 56%, even as syntax performance approaches perfection. For security leaders, this is no longer a developer tooling discussion. It is a verification, release-control, and accountability issue. In this session, Veracode leaders unpack the findings from the 2026 GenAI Code Security Report and turn them into practical actions for secure software delivery at scale. Whether you’re a developer, security lead, or business decision-maker, this session will help you navigate the real-world security implications of GenAI in your development workflow. This presentation is brought to you by Veracode, Inc., an AWS Partner.

title: AI Meets Production: The New Reliability Playbook for Financial Services (sponsored by Traversal)
speaker: Anish Agarwal
abstract: Financial services depend on software that needs to be available around the clock. When that software fails, the consequences can affect millions of customers and create regulatory, financial, and reputational risk. This panel brings together technology leaders from some of the world’s largest financial institutions across banking, payments, and investment management for a conversation moderated by Anish Agrawal, CEO & Cofounder of Traversal, the AI SRE helping diagnose, fix, and prevent incidents across complex enterprise environments. Together, they’ll discuss how AI is changing production reliability across financial services, where it’s already being used, the emerging role of AI SREs, what teams look for when evaluating new approaches, and what it takes to deploy AI safely in highly regulated environments. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.

title: AIOPs for cloud data infrastructure (sponsored by NetApp)
abstract: Cloud data infrastructure rarely stays optimal — workloads change, configurations drift, and data infrastructure expertise is scarce. AIOps applies AI-powered, agentic automation to cloud data storage operations: continuously assessing the environment, analyzing it against workload-specific best practices, recommending fixes, and applying them at the level of autonomy you choose. In this lightning talk, we’ll explore how NetApp Workload Factory does all this while providing customers with right-sized cost, on-target performance, stronger resilience and protection — without the need for deep data infrastructure expertise, and while always staying in control. title: AIOps for SAP on AWS: Proactive Log Intelligence with Amazon Bedrock Agents
speaker: Adam Hill, John Gray
abstract: SAP operations teams spend hours sifting through thousands of log lines to diagnose outages, often only after business impact has occurred. In this workshop, learn how to implement AI-powered operations for SAP workloads on AWS, whether customer-managed or RISE with SAP. Ingest SAP system logs into Amazon CloudWatch using the CloudWatch Agent and SAP ECS LogServ, then deploy an AI agent that will enable proactive analysis and reactive root-cause investigation. Leave with a deployable architecture, real customer examples, and guidance to get started in days with your own agent.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Pompeian IV

title: AIOps strategy: foundations before capabilities
speaker: Brian Simpson-Adkins, Rovan Omar
abstract: Most teams turn on AI-driven operations before thinking about how they will scale. This chalk talk works through an AIOps strategy at the whiteboard, using real support-case patterns showing that most critical failures are catchable before they reach production. We discuss areas your strategy should consider that will allow you to scale to additional capabilities more quickly and where Frontier Agents could help. Leave with a foundational framework and a maturity discussion for your team.

title: AI Powered Business Intelligence with Amazon Quick
speaker: Anabel Montero
abstract: Amazon Quick brings AI-powered analytics, automation, and research into a single workspace. In this bootcamp, build interactive dashboards and visualizations with Quick Sight, organize team knowledge resources in Spaces with appropriate permissions, create custom Chat Agents to surface insights conversationally, automate repetitive workflows with Quick Flows, and conduct multi-source research with proper validation. The three hands-on labs give you practical experience to apply these skills immediately in your organization
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom I

title: AI-Powered FinOps: Cloud Cost Optimization in Practice
speaker: Rupesh Lunia, Enrico Bonaccorsi
abstract: Embed FinOps as an operational discipline using AI-powered cost optimization. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how to shift left on cloud financial management by integrating cost discipline throughout development. Explore AWS services for automated optimizations, rightsizing, and savings plans. Gain experience with AI/ML and container workload cost allocation, multi-cloud reporting, and AI-powered spend analysis. Implement automated strategies using real workload data. Laptop required

title: AI-Powered Profitability: How Partners Are Winning with AWS
speaker: Niraj Nath, Julia Chen
abstract: AI is reshaping partner economics. Hear from AWS VP Julia Chen about how to build a profitable AI-first business. This session covers the evolution of AWS Partner Programs, from transactional resell to outcome-driven partnerships, and reveals which programs, incentives, enablement, and tools deliver the highest ROI. Discover how AI-powered differentiation lowers your cost of sales, attracts high-value customers, deepens relationships, and enables innovation at scale. You'll leave with insights about where to invest and pathways for growth.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Roman I

title: AI-Ready Data Foundation: Improve AI Accuracy in Healthcare and Life Sciences
speaker: Navneet Srivastava
abstract: Most healthcare and life sciences organizations are experimenting with AI, but far fewer are able to move out of pilots and into production at enterprise scale. More often than not the blocker is not the model, it is the data foundation beneath it, especially for healthcare and life sciences customers who operate with fragmented and heavily regulated data. This session shows how an AI-ready data foundation becomes the strategic control point that governs meaning across the enterprise and makes AI accurate, trustworthy, and reusable on real data. We present a framework for building a unified data stack on AWS, from governed open storage through the semantic and agentic layers, and how to build it incrementally while keeping control, context, and accountability.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: AI-ready tables, served fresh. Hold the custom pipelines. (sponsored by Confluent)
abstract: Real-time data loses value when it gets stuck in pipelines. In this session, learn how Confluent, IBM and AWS are helping make streaming data immediately usable for analytics and AI. See how Confluent Tableflow turns Kafka topics into Apache Iceberg tables and registers them in the AWS Glue Data Catalog—eliminating the need for custom streaming pipelines. Discover how this integration enables data engineers to reduce ingestion complexity, strengthen governance and put real-time data to work for analytics and AI with Amazon Athena.​
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: AI security without borders: A global defense strategy
speaker: Varun KM, Tiffany Bloomquist, Shai Morag
abstract: 7AI, OAK, and CloudSEK makes the case for AI security without borders, arguing for a global defense strategy against AI-driven threats. This session covers why security approaches need to transcend regional and organizational boundaries as AI threats scale globally, what a global defense strategy looks like in practice, and what these industry leaders have learned building security products meant to defend against borderless AI threats.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: AI spend decoded: Open the black box with FinOps for AI (sponsored by Cloudability)
speaker: Andrew Midgley
abstract: AI spend often arrives as a black box: a rising bill with little clarity into which teams, models or features drove it. Learn why AI cost behaves differently and how teams use IBM Cloudability to apply FinOps discipline on AWS: categorizing costs, connecting spend to business goals and identifying waste. Then follow IBM Cloudability's own AI assistant as the example, turning visibility into action on Amazon EKS through GPU efficiency and request rightsizing, and applying the same discipline to Amazon Bedrock, from IAM principal allocation to prompt caching and provisioned throughput, so teams can explain, defend and optimize AI spend.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: AI Spreadsheets and the Modern Data Stack: An AWS Story (sponsored by Row Zero)
speaker: Nick End
abstract: AWS relies on spreadsheets for planning, forecasting, business intelligence, and self service analytics. To improve self-serve data analysis, AWS rolled out Row Zero, a cloud-based AI spreadsheet that can open billion row datasets, connect directly to data warehouses, and provide enterprise grade security controls. This session covers how AWS solved their legacy spreadsheet problems that are constrained by the compute and memory resources of employee laptops and a 1 million row limit. By adopting Row Zero, business users can derive insights and have secure access to governed data in Amazon S3, Redshift, or Athena at massive scale. This presentation is brought to you by Row Zero, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: AI Systems Performance Engineering on AWS: A practitioner's deep dive
speaker: Keita Watanabe, Aravind Neelakantan
abstract: Extracting useful throughput from GPU clusters is a discipline: profiling kernels, tuning collectives, keeping the GPUs fed, and handling the failures that grow with scale. In this hands-on workshop, work through the full stack on Slurm-managed NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, covering compute, network, storage, and the ML software stack from drivers to distributed frameworks. Set up the observability that ties them together, from GPU, EFA, and Lustre counters to training throughput and MFU. At each layer, measure, attribute, and fix with the right tool. The workshop concludes with self-built dashboards and a goodput methodology for training clusters.

title: AI That Answers: PepsiCo Reimagines Customer Experience with Amazon Connect (sponsored by PwC)
speaker: Alex Halper, Harsha Desai
abstract: Join PwC and PepsiCo to hear how Amazon Connect is helping the company transform customer experience and deliver business outcomes. This session showcases cutting-edge omnichannel solutions across voice, chat, and messaging, along with agentic AI capabilities driving automation in areas like order management and real-time updates. Hear how PepsiCo is deploying next-generation, AI-powered voice solutions in production, with new innovations continuing to emerge. Discover how these advancements deliver measurable business value, backed by PwC's outcome-based approach that ties technology investment directly to efficiency gains and improved customer and business performance. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: AI That Scales Fast for High-Growth Businesses. (sponsored by Accenture)
speaker: Serena Smorti, Dusshyant Roy
abstract: Big AI outcomes are within reach for high-growth businesses looking to scale value from Amazon Quick. See how Accenture Edge, built for organizations with $300M-$3B annual revenue, combines AI, cloud, and pre-built solutions to help organizations move faster, work smarter, and achieve enterprise-grade outcomes without enterprise-level complexity. A session for resource-constrained IT and business teams that need to deliver measurable impact in weeks, not quarters.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: AI Transformation: Redesigning How Work Gets Done (sponsored by Lucid Software)
speaker: Birch Eve
abstract: Every major technology shift starts the same way. We use new technology to do the old thing. Early factories replaced steam engines with electric motors, but real transformation came when they redesigned the factory around what electricity made possible. We’re doing the same thing with AI. AI transformation isn’t about adding agents to existing workflows. It’s about redesigning how work gets done. That starts with context. In this session, we’ll show how teams can make work visible, give humans and AI a shared understanding of it, redesign workflows around agents, and turn that understanding into action. This presentation is brought to you by Lucid Software, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: AI Under Fire: How to Stop AI-Powered Attacks and Secure AI Coding (sponsored by Palo Alto Networks)
speaker: Lahary Ravuri, Andy Piazza
abstract: Frontier AI is transforming cyber threats, acting as a force multiplier across the kill chain. Adversaries leverage AI to scale social engineering, accelerate vulnerability discovery, and iterate malicious code. In this session, we highlight Palo Alto Networks’ approach to securing the frontier, by combining AI-powered Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW) and Frontier Virtual Patching (FVP) to preemptively block zero days, alongside identity controls and Secure AI Coding to protect developer workflows. Attendees will learn how threat intelligence and proactive defense outpace machine scale adversaries. This presentation is brought to you by Palo Alto Networks, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: AI Writes the Code. Who Reviews the Reviewer?
speaker: Rossana Suarez
abstract: AI coding assistants now write, refactor, and even review code at scale but who's actually accountable when something breaks in production? This session explores how AI has reshaped the code review process: faster first-pass reviews, AI-generated suggestions, and agentic tools running directly in CI/CD pipelines. We'll examine where AI genuinely improves review quality, where it creates false confidence, and why human judgment remains the deciding factor. You'll leave with a practical framework for combining AI speed with human accountability in your own review process.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: A leader's guide to advanced teams models in an agentic world
speaker: Jonathan Allen, Carrie Wood
abstract: Agents made execution cheap. The work did not disappear. It moved into deciding what should exist, checking what agents produce, and owning it when something breaks. Most team designs were not built for that. This session gives you four questions to ask of any piece of work: what is it for, what does it touch, how will we check it, and whose name is on it. Then we walk through the team models leaders reach for, what each gets wrong, and where the pager and the name should sit. You leave knowing who does what now.

title: A leader's guide to escaping proof-of-concept purgatory
speaker: ラフール Pathak
abstract: Drawing on 1,000+ customer conversations about building competitive advantage with data and AI, Rahul Pathak, VP of AWS Data & AI GTM, shares what separates organizations getting real value from agentic AI from those stuck in pilots. When everyone has the same models, your data is the only differentiator. Rahul covers how to set goals worth deploying against, why working backwards from outcomes matters, why cross-functional teams outperform centralized AI functions, what governance must exist before agents reach production, not after, and how to create urgency without a mandate. Field notes from 1,000+ rooms, and a playbook for Monday morning.

title: A leader’s guide to governing AI, on behalf of humans
speaker: Ryan Seaman, Dr. Bernadette Han
abstract: AI deployments can reason, problem-solve, and act with increasing agency. Leaving governance models built for deterministic software no longer sufficient. AWS Executive in Residence Ryan Seaman and Dr. Bernadette Han, organizational psychologist at the American Psychological Association (APA), bring technology and human behavior into one governance conversation. As AI interacts with people, influences decisions, and takes actions, governance must address not only what AI can do, but how it behaves with people and what happens as a result. Bernadette introduces the EEI-AI Behavioral Architecture™, translating psychological science into behavioral requirements organizations can design for, test, observe, and govern responsibly.

title: A leader's guide to how AI is changing Amazon’s ways of working
speaker: Stephen Brozovich, Ian Wilson
abstract: AI is changing how Amazon hires, builds, manages, and deploys teams across every function to innovate and deliver on behalf of customers. This session shares Amazon's emerging framework: the mental models fueling transformation, a state model for understanding where teams are on the AI journey, and real case studies of teams that have crossed from AI-enhanced to AI-native and beyond. We'll walk through the implications, share the questions we're still wrestling with, and offer practical recommendations for leaders navigating the same transition. First-person data from an organization at scale, shared with candor.

title: A leader's guide to how Amazon built its data foundation for agents
speaker: Anas Fattahi, G2 Krishnamoorthy
abstract: Organizations racing to put AI agents on top of their data keep hitting the same walls: security, privacy, scale, and data they can't trust. In this session, Anas Fattahi (VP, Amazon Business Data Technologies) and G2 Krishnamoorthy (VP, AWS Databases) share how years of foundational investment positioned Amazon to move quickly when the agentic AI moment arrived, and where the hard problems still live. You'll hear which bets paid off, what's working now, what they're still building, and how to inspect your own setup against what they've learned.

title: A leader's guide to modernizing systems for AI, with AI
speaker: Matthias Patzak, Sree Ratnasinghe
abstract: Every enterprise faces the same sequencing problem: "Before we can deploy AI, we need to fix our legacy systems." This is technology's most expensive false binary. Organizations that made real progress rejected that sequence. They use AI to understand undocumented code, decompose monoliths, and rebuild the very systems blocking deployment. One airline uses AI to comprehend reservation logic only three people understand. Another enterprise uses agents to reverse-engineer decades of business rules into microservices. The recursive unlock: the technology you want to deploy removes what blocks it. This session covers the funding, sequencing, and organizational decisions that make it work.

title: A leader's guide to moving from AI investment gridlock to acceleration
speaker: Chris Hennesey, Paul Krebs
abstract: Fund the platform or the use case? Demand proof before investing, or invest to generate the proof? These decisions determine whether AI compounds or stalls, and can't wait for the annual budget cycle. To move at the pace of AI, the CIO and CFO must be in lockstep. Two former operators share how the best pairs manage AI like a venture portfolio: bets in the face of uncertainty, recycling of wins into the next ones, and governance that scales across the portfolio rather than project by project — plus the key questions every pair should answer before their next AI investment.

title: A leader's guide to predicting and proving AI value
speaker: Chris Hennesey, Lindsey Drake
abstract: Every organization faces the same AI questions: How do we predict and manage costs? How do we prove value when outcomes are hard to measure? How do we move fast without losing control? Two finance leaders, one advising enterprise executives and one managing AI economics at scale inside Amazon, share what is working, what is not, and where teams go wrong. Learn how to measure AI cost and value in terms finance and technology leaders agree on, which guardrails to set as investment grows, and how to make the case for AI value to your board.

title: A leader's guide to reimagining complex business processes with agents
speaker: ヘレナ・イン Yin Koeppl, Romeo Romeo, Simone Zucchet
abstract: Most enterprises use AI as an assistant, automating individual tasks for incremental 20% gains. The leaders unlocking profound productivity gains are doing something different: reimagining entire business processes from the outcome backward, so every step hands forward context, confidence, and decision authority, not just data. This session shows what it takes to transform your most strategic operations with agentic AI and scale them, then Thomson Reuters walks through the lessons of rebuilding its M&A process end-to-end. You leave knowing which processes to reimagine and how to move them into production, where value compounds.

title: A leader's guide to scaling AI adoption without losing control
speaker: Daniel Slater, Erin Kraemer
abstract: I gave the organization AI tools — why did adoption stall? Most enterprises equip teams with AI and expect transformation to follow. It doesn't. Amazon scaled agentic AI to thousands of production deployments not by mandate, but by investing in what surrounds the model: governance that guards what truly matters — customer trust, privacy, security, and cost — while loosening its grip everywhere else, a culture where experimentation and oversight coexist, and upskilling that turns casual prompters into confident builders. This session names the structural bets that move adoption, the debts you're quietly acquiring, and why losing control isn't the failure — over-constraining is.

title: A leader's guide to security at the speed of AI, powered by Mythos
speaker: Sarah Davenport, Rush Carskadden
abstract: As AI capabilities advance, so do the capabilities of those who attack software. The pace of modern development has outgrown point-in-time security reviews, leaving vulnerabilities exploitable longer than any leader should accept. Periodic snapshots cannot keep up when code changes constantly, so security has to become continuous, evaluating posture as the code itself evolves. Amazon used frontier-model capabilities, through Mythos, to make security continuous at its own scale, finding issues and guiding builders to fix them as they work. This session explores that shift. Senior leaders will learn how to secure their organizations at AI speed.

title: A leader's guide to the AI speed trap
speaker: Matthias Patzak, Laura Tacho
abstract: Your developers are faster with AI. Your organization isn't. AI tools accelerate individual teams, but organizational outcomes depend on what happens between teams: coordination, dependencies, and end-to-end value streams that extend far beyond code. Most productivity metrics miss this entirely because they stop at the team boundary. In this session, we present real patterns from startups, scaleups, digital natives, and large organizations, introduce measurement frameworks that capture what matters at the organizational level, and share practical approaches for turning team-level acceleration into outcomes your customers will notice.

title: A leader's guide to the AI you haven't seen yet
speaker: Ishit Vachhrajani, Matt Wood
abstract: Most AI strategy is built for the AI leaders can see. The models in production today are the constrained ones, gated by capacity and cost, and that gate is lifting. When it lifts, a dozen breakthrough applications becomes a million, and AI systems get as cheap and as common as a website. Progress has stopped being predictable too: capability arrives in step changes that can obsolete a year of work in a quarter. This session asks what you would build if AI were free and never made a mistake, and how to tell a durable bet from a disposable one.

title: A leader's guide to what separates AI leaders from the rest
speaker: Tom Godden
abstract: In early 2026, the Reimagine research program interviewed senior technology leaders under conditions of candor: off-the-record, non-attributable, no marketing follow-up. What they said contradicts the prevailing conference narrative. Nobody is running agents autonomously, not one. The most advanced organizations are carrying the most technical debt. The AI generating real value looks nothing like the demos. This session synthesizes the patterns that emerged when executives stopped performing confidence and started sharing reality.

title: A leader's guide to what your board must know about AI (and shouldn't)
speaker: Taimur Rashid, Mario Thomas, Jennifer Nason
abstract: Your board is asking about AI — and that's a good thing. Their curiosity is the opening you need. But that attention can create more heat than light: dashboards and benchmarks that generate activity without moving the organization forward. The real opportunity is to channel that interest — show AI's true potential and turn your board into a genuine partner for a transformation that needs their conviction to succeed. In this session, assess where your board sits, understand the personas at play, and learn proven tactics to move them from curiosity to conviction.

title: A leader's guide to why agentic AI just made your data problem urgent
speaker: Tom Godden, Karolis Urbonas
abstract: The data problem you tolerated for years just became an emergency. Agents do not politely work around missing metadata. They guess confidently, and you find out three weeks later. Enterprises assumed they could solve AI first and data second. They can't. You get the framework that separates compounding value from programs that never finish. AWS Marketing built an agentic system over thousands of warehouse tables. It worked. Its first output: an inventory of every undocumented decision in the warehouse. That exposure was worth more than the answers. You leave knowing what to fix first, and why analytical demand climbs.

title: Align cost with value through outcome-based pricing in AWS Marketplace
speaker: Jihye Kwon, Swami Jayaraman
abstract: Customers increasingly expect software to be priced in terms of value delivered, paying only for results like resolved tickets or documents processed not API calls or compute hours or seats. In this Code Talk, learn how to implement outcome-based pricing and see live examples of metering and billing in AWS Marketplace. Follow along as we go from prototype to published listing, billing per resolved ticket, processed document, or any measurable result you choose.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Allianz: Building domain AI agents that scale across the enterprise
speaker: Lars Nettemann, Lennard Ufer, Patrik Nagel
abstract: Delivering one coherent agent experience across a large enterprise means connecting agents to core business systems, each with its own identity, compliance, and security requirements. Learn how Allianz moved a reusable agentic framework into regulated production, with one entry point routing every request to specialist domain agents through open standards like MCP. The session covers the trust model, with scoped authorization at every boundary, and how shared services for identity, data protection, and consent let business teams focus on their domain. Finally, discover go-live lessons and who owns a shared agent service across legal entities.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Amazon API Gateway: Migration strategies and agent-ready APIs
speaker: Zac Burns, Ronan Prenty
abstract: Unlock the full potential of Amazon API Gateway for modern workloads. In this chalk talk, we discuss migration strategies from legacy API platforms using OpenAPI extensions, schema validation, and Infrastructure as Code. Then we tackle the agentic era: how do you design APIs that AI agents can discover, authenticate against, and call reliably? We explore the different authorization mechanisms available as well as how to expose your endpoints as MCP-compatible tool definitions. Bring your questions—we'll work through them on the whiteboard.

title: Amazon Aurora architecture patterns for open table format analytics
speaker: Tim Stoakes
abstract: Modern analytics architectures increasingly rely on open table formats like Apache Iceberg but combining operational and analytical data remains complex. This session explores emerging patterns for bridging Amazon Aurora with open table format analytics. Learn architectural patterns for bidirectional data flow between databases and data lakes. Topics include design patterns for analytical workloads, performance optimization and reverse ETL, and deep dives into maintaining transactional consistency when streaming database changes to Amazon S3 Tables, delivery guarantees, and type mapping.

title: Amazon Aurora DSQL: A developer's perspective
speaker: Raluca Constantin, Marc Bowes
abstract: In this live coding session, we'll show you how to work with Amazon Aurora DSQL from a developer's perspective. We'll develop a sample application to highlight some of the ways developing for Aurora DSQL is different than PostgreSQL. We'll cover authentication and connection management, optimistic concurrency transaction patterns, primary key selection, analyzing query performance, and best practices.

title: Amazon Aurora HA and DR design patterns for global resilience
speaker: Grant McAlister, Tim Stoakes
abstract: Amazon Aurora is a serverless relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and DSQL. Aurora provides managed high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) capabilities in and across AWS Regions. In this session, explore the Aurora HA and DR capabilities and discover design patterns that enable the development of resilient applications. Learn how to establish in-Region and cross-Region HA and DR using Aurora features including Multi-AZ deployments and Aurora Global Database, and how Aurora DSQL multi-Region clusters provides the highest level of availability and application resilience.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Amazon Connect Lounge: Meet the Team
abstract: Stop by the Amazon Connect Lounge to meet AI agents designed to work the way you work. Experience them in action, see them tackle real-world scenarios side by side with you, and leave knowing how these AI agents can drive results for your business. Four AI agents, four experiences.

title: Amazon DocumentDB for expert practitioners
speaker: Inderpreet Singh, Douglas Bonser
abstract: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fully managed database service for native document data model enterprise workloads. It removes the undifferentiated heavy lifting of operating a database so that teams can focus time on delivering value for customers. In this session, dive deep into the implementation details and trade-offs of features to improve compression and performance while lowering cost for various workloads.

title: Amazon DynamoDB: How to build a foundational service
speaker: Craig Howard
abstract: Whether to take a dependency or reimplement something are important decisions in any system architecture, affecting performance, durability, and availability. Amazon DynamoDB serves millions of customers while also underpinning many AWS services, a dual role that forces rigorous decisions about dependencies, failure isolation, and multi-Region architecture. In this session, the DynamoDB engineering team walks through how those constraints shape architectural choices, including when DynamoDB uses DynamoDB to implement itself. The session presents a structured framework for dependency analysis, covering multi-zone and multi-Region tradeoffs, applicable to any system you build and operate, to help identify design risks before they become failures.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Amazon EC2: New silicon, new instances, new possibilities
speaker: Scott Malkie, Art Baudo
abstract: Amazon EC2 continues to push the boundaries of cloud compute. Join this session to explore the latest innovations — from new AWS Graviton processors to the newest Intel, AMD, and Mac instances built for demanding workloads. Hear how customers are using EC2 to accelerate application development, high-performance computing, and AI inference on the CPU. Learn how the AWS Nitro System delivers strong isolation and performance, and leave with practical guidance to match the right EC2 instance to your workload.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Amazon EKS incident response and remediation with AWS DevOps Agent
speaker: Balachandra Hebbagilu Nagaraj, Frank Fan, Swarna Kunnath, Shyam Sunder Kulkarni, Luis Arcega
abstract: When an incident hits, engineers lose time pivoting between kubectl, metrics, logs, and traces to find root cause. In this builder session, you'll drive the AWS DevOps Agent through a production-realistic incident end to end: detect the anomaly from observability signals, correlate metrics, logs, and traces to a root cause, and execute automated remediation with a human-in-the-loop gate. You'll wire the observability inputs the agent consumes, review its diagnosis journal, and validate recovery. Leave with a repeatable detect-diagnose-remediate-verify pattern and a permission-scoped remediation playbook you can adapt to your own clusters.

You'll wire the observability inputs the agent consumes, review its diagnosis journal, and validate recovery. Leave with a repeatable detect-diagnose-remediate-verify pattern and a permission-scoped remediation playbook you can adapt to your own clusters.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Amazon EKS: Infrastructure as code, GitOps, or CI/CD
speaker: Alessandro Germer, Sebastien Allamand
abstract: Explore diverse architectures for deploying workloads including agents on Amazon EKS. Learn about secure software supply chain automation options including CI/CD pipelines, IaC (using Terraform & CDK), and GitOps patterns with Argo CD. Discover how Amazon EKS Capabilities, a suite of fully-managed platform features for deployments and resource orchestration eliminate operational overhead for building on Kubernetes. You will understand how these approaches complement each other from developer, architect, and operator perspectives. Get insights on selecting the right deployment strategy based on team structure and skill sets, and learn how to effectively combine DevOps and GitOps patterns to match your needs.
