title: Amazon EVS: How to deploy & operate your VMware stack in the cloud
speaker: Andy Reedy, Spiros Tsitsonis, Alastair Pooley
abstract: What if you could rapidly migrate your VMware-based workloads to the cloud without giving up control over how you build, configure, and operate your environment? Amazon EVS lets you run the latest VMware Cloud Foundation software within your Amazon VPC using EC2 bare-metal instances. Use the tools and processes your team already knows, now backed by AWS scale and flexibility. Retain control of your virtualization stack, from networking and storage to disaster recovery. We'll walk through deployment workflows and integration patterns with AWS Partners and native AWS services. Hear lessons from a customer who fast-tracked their migration with EVS.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Amazon Leo: Connectivity Beyond the Reach of Existing Networks (sponsored by Amazon Leo)
speaker: Damian Robo
abstract: Amazon Leo is building a constellation of over 3,200 low Earth orbit satellites to deliver fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities worldwide. In this session, learn how Leo's advanced satellite technology, purpose-built customer antennas, and deep integration with AWS will extend reliable connectivity to enterprises, governments, and individuals — wherever they are. Walk away with a clear understanding of Leo's architecture, use cases, and how it complements existing network infrastructure to close the global digital divide. This presentation is brought to you by Amazon Leo, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Amazon Linux: Securing and scaling your workloads on AWS
speaker: Sree Sunku, Stewart Smith
abstract: Amazon Linux powers the majority of workloads on AWS, from containers and AI/ML to enterprise applications and managed services. In this session, we introduce Amazon Linux 2027 (AL2027), cover its security enhancements, optimizations, and key features. Learn how AL2027 addresses the needs of modern AI/ML and container workloads, and what the roadmap means for your infrastructure planning. Whether you are planning a migration or evaluating your OS strategy, this session is for you.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Amazon S3 cost optimization: when to tier, and when not to
speaker: Mark Twomey, Eric Jones
abstract: Moving data to a colder storage class is the obvious way to cut Amazon S3 costs, but sometimes it makes your bill go up. Learn about the full cost model behind storage-class decisions: transition requests, minimum billable object sizes, per-object overhead, minimum durations, and retrieval. See why small objects, high-churn datasets, and request-heavy workloads are frequently cheaper left where they are, and how to spot them. Using S3 Storage Lens, S3 Inventory, and S3 Metadata, diagnose where you're spending and leave with clear guidance on when to tier, when to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and when to do nothing.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Amazon S3 performance: Architecture, design, and optimization
speaker: Greg Benjamin, Jonathan Wong
abstract: Go behind the scenes of Amazon S3 performance architecture while learning practical optimization strategies for today's most demanding workloads. Explore how internal systems for S3 manage massive throughput, handle concurrent requests, and balance loads across its distributed infrastructure. From request routing and partitioning strategies to multipart transfers and byte-range fetches, understand the technical foundations that power real-time analytics, AI/ML training, and high-frequency data pipelines. Then see how S3 Express One Zone extends these capabilities with consistent single-digit millisecond latency through directory buckets and compute co-location. Walk away with patterns to maximize performance at every tier.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Amazon S3 security and access control best practices
speaker: Sam Parmett, Will Cavin
abstract: As organizations consolidate critical data in Amazon S3 across accounts, teams, and workloads, security and access control decisions multiply. Which identity model scales without becoming brittle? Where do you enforce encryption policy? How do you detect misconfigurations? This session walks you through a layered security framework for S3: perimeter controls that prevent unintended public exposure, identity and attribute-based access that scales across organizational boundaries, encryption options that satisfy compliance without adding operational friction, and monitoring that continuously validates your posture. You will learn how these layers compose into a cohesive strategy and which controls matter most as your environment grows.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Amazon S3 security: Implementing access controls, policies & audits
speaker: Erick Dame, Christie Lee
abstract: Amazon S3 provides security settings and granular access controls to suit virtually any workload. In this workshop, learn how to manage access and define scalable user and resource-based policies using Amazon S3 access management tools. Learn techniques for monitoring and auditing data to find out who is accessing what data, from where, and when. Through practical scenarios, learn how to apply various S3 security tools and capabilities to meet diverse security requirements. Gain expertise in implementing robust security measures, from basic access controls to advanced audit systems, suitable for any workload complexity. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

title: Amazon S3 Tables: A deep dive into storage built for Apache Iceberg
speaker: Abhinav Goyle, Amy Yu
abstract: Amazon S3 Tables are setting a new standard for Apache Iceberg data lakes: fully managed, open, and AI-ready. In this session, learn everything you need to know about S3 Tables, from how we continuously optimize Iceberg tables as your data scales, to support for ingestion, migration, data protection, cost-efficiency, and performance. We’ll explore how S3 Tables make it easy for AI agents to build on Iceberg tables and dive into the latest re:Invent announcements. Hear real-world customer stories and walk away equipped to bring S3 Tables to your organization.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Amazon’s World Famous Chicken Wing Eating Competition
abstract: Join us at re:Play for Amazon's World Famous Chicken Wing Eating Competition, where brave competitors will face off at 6:45 PM. Competitors must register prior at the Attendee Experiences Desk (Venetian | Level 2 | Artist Foyer) to devour as many wings as possible in this epic battle of endurance for a chance at a re:Invent 2027 Ticket. This is one of re:Invent's most memorable and exciting spectacles.

title: Ambient accessibility: Architecting real-time ASL on a Wearable
speaker: Suresh Poopandi, Rob Koch, Alak Eswaradass
abstract: What if a DHH person could wear a device and get sign language translation of every conversation around them in under a second? We architect a pipeline that ingests Amazon Bee's ambient audio, transcribes it, transforms English to ASL grammar, generates avatar animations, and streams signed video back. That one-second constraint drives every architectural tradeoff, from whether translation stages run on-device for speed or in the cloud for accuracy, to whether we sign full sentences or start mid-utterance with partial context. We explore the edge-cloud splits and pipeline staging that make sub-second delivery feasible.

title: Analyze your portfolio, prioritize what to fix, and transform it
speaker: Aritra Nag, Lucas Soriano Alves Duarte, Manmohit Pal Singh
abstract: You know your portfolio needs modernization, but which apps go first, and based on what criteria? In this workshop, you'll run the full analyze-prioritize-transform cycle end to end. Using AWS Transform's Agentic Readiness Analysis and Modernization Analysis, you'll evaluate applications from two angles: whether agents can safely reach your logic (API exposure, identity, state, guardrails, observability) and how cloud-native mature your architecture is (compute, data, security, operations). You'll interpret scores, scale across a portfolio with the orchestrator, then close the loop by triggering a containerization transformation on the app that needs it most. Laptop required.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Pompeian IV

title: An Epic Tale: Hyperscale Storage & Compute for the Fortnite Ecosystem
speaker: Paul Sharpe, Dan Backhaus, Mattias Jansson
abstract: The metaverse will not be built by one studio. It will be built by thousands of teams shipping petabytes of content, running millions of build and render jobs across regions every day. The engineers behind Lore, Epic's distributed version control system for massive binary repositories, and Overmind, a multi-region ephemeral compute orchestrator, reveal the AWS architecture that makes it possible: self-managed scheduling on EC2, S3/DynamoDB/Keyspaces/Aurora for the data plane, EKS-hosted control planes running durable workflows, and MSK for replayable event streams. Leave with a concrete reference architecture and lessons on tenant isolation, regional sovereignty, and global platform scale.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: An insider’s look into architecture choices for Amazon DynamoDB
speaker: Craig Howard
abstract: To overcome the performance and scale limitations of relational databases, AWS built Amazon DynamoDB to deliver single-digit millisecond performance at any scale - whether your application has tens of thousands or hundreds of millions of simultaneous users - for the most demanding applications on the planet. In this session, learn how some basic data structure decisions led to these characteristics. And how those same decisions provide immutable, point-in-time restore. Leave with a better understanding of why DynamoDB can operate at the scale it does, and a framework on how to use it for decisions in your own applications.

title: Answering CX questions 10x faster with Amazon Connect Customer and Amazon Quick
speaker: Kobe Xu
abstract: Amazon Connect Customer generates a deep set of signals from every customer interaction. Sentiment, intent, conversation analytics, resolution outcomes. It's all there and Connect Customer gives you built-in tools to explore it. But we wanted to go further. We wanted anyone in the organization to ask questions about customer interactions in plain language and get answers instantly. So we paired Connect Customer's analytics data lake with Amazon Quick. In this session, we walk through how we did it, including how we handled cross-account Lake Formation access, and show how our broader team now asks questions and reshapes queries on the fly. 10x faster from question to action.

title: Aon: Turning raw exposure data into faster underwriting
speaker: Hasan Mehdi Rizvi, Sudipto Dasgupta
abstract: Insurers and brokers process thousands of Statements of Values annually, complex unstructured documents that require manual extraction and validation and delay quoting and bind decisions. In this lightning talk, learn how Aon built an AI-powered exposure data ingestion platform on Amazon Bedrock using Anthropic Claude, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. See how the platform transforms unstructured data into standardized, risk-ready information with improved address quality, geocoding precision, and hazard identification, reducing document processing from days to minutes and feeding higher-quality inputs to catastrophe models.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Apache Iceberg V3 on AWS: Lower Costs, Better Lakehouse Performance
speaker: Parul Saxena, Sreeji Gopal
abstract: Apache Iceberg V3 is now production-ready, and adopting deletion vectors, row lineage, and new data types across your lakehouse requires careful planning. In this session, explore implementation patterns using Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, and Amazon S3 Tables. Learn when deletion vectors outperform copy-on-write, how row lineage enables compliance without extra pipelines, and how V3 incremental processing cuts batch costs. Leave with a practical migration strategy for your Iceberg upgrade.

title: Apache Iceberg V4: Fast commits, smart metadata, and portable tables
speaker: Rishabh Bhatia, Shawn Chang
abstract: Apache Iceberg V4 is the biggest architectural evolution of the format, shifting from batch-first to real-time ready. Explore how single-file commits eliminate metadata bottlenecks for streaming ingestion, how Parquet-based metadata and redesigned content statistics accelerate query planning, and how relative paths make tables portable across regions and clouds without costly rewrites. We'll walk through what's changing under the hood and what it means for the way you design and operate lakehouses. Discover how V4 delivers the speed and flexibility modern lakehouses demand.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: Aperf: An all-in-one tool for performance data collection and analysis
speaker: Congkai Tan, Arthur Petitpierre
abstract: Aperf is an open-source project created by AWS to accelerate the performance debugging process by enabling experienced users to deep dive into extensive data and less experienced users to identify issues without specialized knowledge. During this session, we'll present its key features and run a demo showing the analysis workflow, from installation, data collection, and then analysis. Finally, we'll open the conversation to collect feedback and feature requests from the audience.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: API Gateway unleashed
speaker: Eduardo Rodrigues, Peterson Larentis
abstract: Gain essential hands-on skills to create, deploy, and manage APIs efficiently with Amazon API Gateway. Learn message transformation, request validation, and security best practices. Master deploying APIs using Infrastructure as Code and integrating with AWS serverless services. Dive into monitoring and debugging to ensure your APIs perform optimally, and explore building and testing WebSocket backends. Whether you're creating REST APIs or real-time communication layers, this workshop equips you with the knowledge to streamline application development and enhance API management. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Application Archeology: Digging up lost knowledge with Kiro
speaker: Ben Turnbull, Fiona McCann, Deric Martinez, Sofia Kendall, Sulaman Khan
abstract: Every organization bleeds knowledge when people leave. For mission-driven teams, a single departure can erase years of context from codebases, runbooks, and integrations. In this builder session, use Kiro — AWS's AI-powered development environment — to reverse that loss. Configure steering files that encode your team's conventions, connect MCP servers to pull context from docs and APIs, and deploy subagents that generate living architecture diagrams and knowledge bases as your code evolves. Walk away with a Kiro workspace that turns any new hire into a productive contributor from day one — no more tribal knowledge walking out the door.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Builders' Session

title: Apply Amazon's frontier team playbook to your organization
speaker: Dan Kiuna, Alok Dhamanaskar
abstract: AI coding agents sped up code generation, but not how fast it reaches customers. Teams seeing 4.5x to 10x gains aren't just adopting tools. They've redesigned how they work. In this chalk talk, learn what these "frontier teams" do differently: investing in agent context and steering files, making intent explicit before code is written, feeding agents well-scoped work instead of babysitting them, shifting testing left so agents self-correct before they reach the pipeline. We'll unpack real examples from teams across Amazon and talk through how to run your own pilot. Bring your questions about making AI work in your organization.

title: Applying the Well-Architected Framework to AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
speaker: Adam Duffield, Manthan Raval
abstract: AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones bring cloud closer to your end users and workloads but introduce architectural decisions that do not exist in a purely cloud-native model. Designing for resilience when infrastructure sits in your facility, and balancing security and cost across hybrid topologies, calls for rethinking each pillar. In this chalk talk, the session walks through the AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar by pillar, exploring how each applies and where it bends at the edge. Bring your toughest design questions. The session draws out real-world patterns, discusses trade-offs, and builds a practical mental model for well-architected hybrid solutions.

title: A practical guide to Amazon S3 data protection
speaker: Denton He, Ed Gummett, Jonathan Wong
abstract: Learn step-by-step methods to protect your critical Amazon S3 data against accidental deletion, ransomware, and corruption, even at billion-object and petabyte scale. This chalk talk provides hands-on guidance for implementing essential safeguards through S3 Versioning, Replication, Object Lock, and Resource Control Policy guardrails, plus techniques for recovering from unwanted changes across large datasets. We also cover how GuardDuty Malware Protection for AWS Backup lets you verify data is malware-free before restoring. Whether you’re meeting compliance requirements or ensuring business continuity, leave with actionable steps from basic backup policies to advanced immutability and malware-scanning controls.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: A practical guide to Apache Iceberg migration on AWS
speaker: Stefano Sandonà, Salim Tutuncu
abstract: Many organizations want to adopt Apache Iceberg but face a practical challenge: how do you migrate existing data lake tables — Hive-style, Apache Hudi, or Delta Lake — without disrupting production workloads? In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn and implement the full spectrum of migration techniques on AWS, from zero-copy in-place approaches to full data rewrites targeting both self-managed Iceberg tables in S3 and Amazon S3 Tables. Beyond the mechanics, you'll implement real-world migration strategies and learn how to choose among them based on downtime tolerance, writer constraints, and data volume. You'll leave with a repeatable playbook for migrating your data lake to Iceberg with minimal risk and zero data loss.

title: A practitioner’s guide to data for agentic AI
speaker: David H Gardner, Jason Dalba
abstract: In this session, gain the skills needed to deploy end-to-end agentic AI applications using your most valuable data. This session focuses on data management using processes like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and provides concepts that apply to other methods of customizing agentic AI applications. Discover best practice architectures using AWS database services like Amazon Aurora, DynamoDB, and Neptune, along with analytical, data processing and streaming experiences found in SageMaker. Learn data lake, governance, and data quality concepts and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Bedrock Knowledge Bases, and other features tie solution components together.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: A practitioner’s guide to migrating from 3rd-party CDN and WAF to AWS
speaker: Etienne Munnich, Achraf Souk
abstract: Considering migrating from a third-party CDN/WAF provider to AWS services? In this chalk talk, we’ll walk through the migration phases together: defining success criteria, running low-risk proof of concepts, designing your target architecture with Amazon Route 53, Amazon CloudFront, AWS WAF, and edge compute, executing the DNS cutover, and managing post-migration operations. Most of this session is open discussion: you bring your questions and stories, and we’ll share what we’ve learned running these migrations in production.

title: Architect AI-powered analytics with AWS Quick across your data platforms
speaker: Jackson Dowden
abstract: As organizations adopt AI-powered analytics, they need architectures that connect BI and conversational AI experiences to their existing data platforms. In this session we'll diagram architectural patterns for connecting AWS Quick to structured data sources and integrating with third-party catalogs and semantic layers. We'll compare the available connectivity approaches, including data sources and MCP-based action connectors, and discuss when to use each. Considerations will span production use cases like BI dashboards, embedded analytics, text-to-SQL Q&A, and agentic workflows. Together we'll tackle real-world integration challenges including authentication, performance optimization, and governance. This session is ideal for architects and technical leaders looking to build AI-powered analytics across their data platforms.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Architect and optimize your VMware environment on Amazon EVS
speaker: Talha Kalim, Ben Lipman
abstract: Dive deep into the architectural decisions that shape a resilient, high-performing VMware environment on Amazon EVS. Explore VCF 9 support, Windows Server license-included entitlements, networking designs, storage configurations tuned for performance and cost, and operational patterns for backup, patching, and disaster recovery. Hear from AWS experts and learn best practices for running production workloads on EVS. Leave with actionable architectures tailored to your VMware workloads.

title: Architect for production AI: A decision framework that scales
speaker: Brent Rabowsky, Hazim Qudah
abstract: Organizations deploying AI workloads face a critical decision at every step: which AI service handles which job, and will it hold up at scale? This chalk talk delivers an opinionated framework for choosing between Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and when to use them together. We'll ground it in a real example: an agentic coding system pairing a Bedrock frontier model for complex coding with a fine-tuned open weight model on SageMaker AI for high-volume automated PR reviews. It runs on AgentCore, which supports any model or provider mix, including Bedrock and SageMaker AI, for cost- and performance-optimized architectures.

title: Architecting anti-piracy defenses for video streaming with Amazon CloudFront
speaker: Matt Carter, Christer Christer
abstract: Modern streaming demands instant revocation, concurrent stream limits, device-bound sessions, and per-user policy decisions at the edge. In this chalk talk, whiteboard the full decision space with us. We'll map the trade-offs between signed URLs, signed cookies, and emerging token approaches like Content Access Tokens (CAT) built on CBOR Web Tokens, then diagram the architecture patterns behind them: embedding custom claims and evaluating them in CloudFront Functions, using CloudFront KeyValueStore for real-time revocation without key rotation, and chaining tokens across HLS/DASH segments. Bring your hardest content protection scenarios, such as credential sharing, restreaming, geo abuse. We'll work through them together at the board, leaving you with a framework for matching protection mechanisms to your security and business requirements.

title: Architecting AWS Outposts networking for enterprise and ultra-low-latency workloads
speaker: Harsha Sanku, Leonardo Solano
abstract: This session covers networking on second-generation AWS Outposts, spanning scalable multi-site topologies and ultra-low-latency bare-metal deployments. Learn how the second-generation dedicated network rack, local gateway routing domains, and intra-VPC and inter-VPC communication form the foundation for segmentation and local connectivity. See how the design extends to multi-site interconnections spanning Outposts and AWS Local Zones, extended VPC designs, and resilient architectures grounded in AWS Well-Architected principles. Explore how bare-metal instances with high-throughput accelerated networking and rack topology support co-located workloads where every microsecond matters.

title: Architecting Enterprise Agents on Bedrock
speaker: Namrata Shah, Ellliott Cordo
abstract: Enterprise agents on Amazon Bedrock are complex distributed systems, combining models, tools, memory, and orchestration into something that has to behave predictably in production. In this session, I walk through practical architecture patterns for building enterprise-grade agents: multi-agent coordination, tool routing, session management, and hybrid workflows using AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Drawing from real production systems, I cover the trade-offs that matter most when moving agents from prototype to production, where reliability and scale actually get tested. Walk away with concrete patterns you can bring back to your own agent architecture.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Architecting firewalls on AWS: a layered defense strategy
speaker: Jonathan Woods, Patrick Duffy
abstract: With automated traffic now more than half of the web, a single firewall layer can't separate good bots from L7 attacks. This chalk talk covers how AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall work together. We cover deployment patterns for internet-facing apps, outbound controls, and workload segmentation, including firewall patterns attached to AWS Transit Gateway. Then we dig into the tradeoffs, including centralized versus distributed inspection, cost versus latency, and when one service can carry the load and when you need both. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we whiteboard a design for your environment.

title: Architecting for digital sovereignty with AWS Hybrid Cloud solutions
speaker: Sherry Lin, Lakshmi VP
abstract: This session uses real-world case studies to understand how AWS hybrid cloud architectures such as AWS Local Zones, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS Outposts help customers meet their digital sovereignty needs. It examines data residency boundaries, network separation, operational controls, and security guardrail options available in hybrid cloud solutions. It then shows how to configure governance controls, including Service Control Policies (SCPs), to help customers comply with regulatory requirements. Finally, it covers how to detect and prevent unauthorized data flows between hybrid infrastructure and the parent Region.

title: Architecting for five nines with multi-region: Capital One’s journey (sponsored by Capital One)
speaker: Mats Lannér, Prem Dhayalan
abstract: Five nines of availability leaves an annual downtime budget of just 5.2 minutes, meaning a single regional failover can consume your entire year. Traditional disaster recovery models simply don't scale to meet this standard. In this session, discover how Capital One evolved its multi-region architectures to sustain regional outages while supporting critical production workloads. We share lessons learned from building and operating active-active topologies, focusing on real-world data consistency models, fault isolation via cell-based architecture, and continuous fault-injection testing. Attendees will walk away with a field-tested matrix for architecting high-availability cloud workloads. This presentation is brought to you by Capital One, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Architecting for non-deterministic components
speaker: John Walker, Kunle Adeleke
abstract: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.

title: Architecting for resilience and data residency
speaker: Mike Haken, Jamie Pasterick, Andy Orlosky
abstract: Your data can't leave the jurisdiction, but your workload still has to survive a Region degradation. This chalk talk explores architecture patterns that address both resilience and data residency together. We break the challenge into practical layers: where data lives, how workloads recover, what isolation looks like, and how to maintain business continuity across geographic boundaries. We map each layer to AWS capabilities including Dedicated Local Zones, Outposts, and policy controls, then work through real scenarios together. Bring your architecture challenges and we will whiteboard design patterns and tradeoffs with you.

abstract: Orchestrating AI conversations across channels requires more than just connecting APIs. Learn how to build agents that understand context, respond instantly, and adapt to channel constraints. Explore Twilio Agent Connect and Amazon Bedrock integration patterns, plus the operational playbook for deploying engagement AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Twilio, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Architecting vector-driven AI applications with Amazon S3 Vectors
speaker: Bimal Gajjar, Arik Porat, David DeLuca
abstract: Vector search is the engine behind intelligent AI, transforming data into meaning-driven insights that power smarter search, recommendations, and generative experiences. In this session, discover how to combine cost-optimized, fully elastic vector storage delivered by Amazon S3 Vectors with multimodal embedding models in Amazon Bedrock to extract and index text and image semantics at scale. Learn how to leverage S3 Vectors with popular AWS AI services to power AI-driven applications that can efficiently search through large vector datasets. Whether you’re building media search applications or search-enabled AI, you’ll learn how to optimize your use of S3 Vectors.

title: Architecting video search at trillion scale with Amazon S3 Vectors
speaker: Ran Pergamin, Efim Dimenstein
abstract: Storing and querying 1.5 trillion vectors demands rethinking traditional vector database architecture. Join this talk to learn how Bright Data built its video search retrieval layer on Amazon S3 Vectors, covering index partitioning across massive collections, embedding storage layout for sub-second nearest-neighbor queries, and cost/latency trade-offs versus dedicated vector databases at this scale. Bright Data walks through its approach to sharding, metadata filtering, and query routing, with benchmarks comparing throughput and cost per million queries. You'll leave with concrete architectural patterns for evaluating S3 Vectors in large-scale search, RAG, or embedding retrieval systems.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Architect, launch, and optimize solutions with AWS Marketplace
speaker: Joseph Shih, Diego Colombatto
abstract: Discover how new AWS Marketplace capabilities can help turn your solutions into scalable commercial offerings including AI-powered and multi-product offerings. In this interactive workshop, explore key decisions across architecture, packaging, deployment, pricing, and launch readiness. Connect directly with AWS Marketplace subject-matter experts to evaluate approaches for your business, validate your listing strategy, and identify opportunities to simplify the customer experience. Leave with practical guidance and an actionable plan to accelerate launch, drive recurring revenue, and improve customer retention.

title: Architect Oracle Database@AWS for resiliency and scale
speaker: Javeed Mohammed, Eric Felice
abstract: Dedicated Exadata infrastructure inside AWS data centers gives Oracle workloads full feature compatibility alongside cloud native flexibility, but architecting for resiliency at scale demands deliberate design choices. In this session, explore architecture patterns for primary and disaster recovery deployments on Oracle Database@AWS, including strategies for multi-terabyte migration and managing petabyte-scale Oracle estates. Join a live whiteboarding discussion where AWS experts cover ODB@AWS deployment options, DR configurations, and operational design choices. Architect with validated best practices drawn from real customer deployments.

title: Architect production MCP servers on Amazon ECS
speaker: Piyush Mattoo, Abhishek Nanda
abstract: Your MCP server works perfectly on a single Amazon ECS task. Then agents multiply, sessions collide, and scaling breaks everything. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the infrastructure patterns that make MCP servers production-ready on Amazon ECS. We'll cover horizontal scaling with externalized session state, request routing, fine-grained authentication, and autoscaling based on agent request patterns. We'll discuss multi-service topologies where different tool categories run as independent ECS services behind a shared ingress layer. Bring your current MCP architecture, and we'll design the production upgrade together.

title: Architect resilient agentic systems: Patterns beyond the happy path
speaker: Folarin Ayodeji Alamu, Nayan Karumuri, Oren Waldman, Cheng-Lun Chen, Srividhya Pallay
abstract: Every agentic system works on the happy path. The real test is what happens when your AI agent times out mid-reasoning, returns a malformed action, or cascades a single failure across an entire chain. In this session, you implement four resilience patterns built for non-deterministic agents: circuit breakers that trip on semantic failure, fallback hierarchies from AI to rules to human, bulkhead isolation between agents, and timeout budgets for chain-of-thought latency. Leave with a decision framework mapping failure modes to pattern combinations you can implement immediately. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Architect resilient, multi-region workforce access on AWS
speaker: Laura Reith, Prashob Krishnan, Alex Milanovic
abstract: Most AWS workforce access hinges on a single Region and a single identity provider. When either one goes down, everyone who signs in is affected—developers can't ship, DevOps engineers can't deploy, and administrators may be locked out just when they need access most. This session applies defense in depth across four layers: IAM Identity Center multi-Region replication, direct IAM federation through AD FS, Regional AWS STS endpoints, and break-glass IAM users. You learn how to decide which layers your environment needs, the order to fail over in, and how to test the full path without disrupting production.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Architects of literacy: Building AI tools for the next generation
speaker: Chris McAvoy
abstract: AI arrived in classrooms before most schools had a policy for it. Students use it daily, teachers are improvising, and the skills employers want keep shifting. Bringing together architects shaping the future of global learning, this panel led by AI education strategist Amanda Bickerstaff unpacks a critical paradigm shift: What does education look like when answers are free, and how do we build tools that teach students how to think rather than just what to produce? Together they cover how AI changes teaching and assessment, what learners of every age need to build, and what technologists owe the people learning to use their tools.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: Architectural patterns for predictable multi-agent costs at scale
speaker: Aran Singh, Ayushi Goyal
abstract: Agents consume several times more tokens than chat interactions, and multi-agent coordination pushes that higher. Monitoring alone isn't enough to manage costs, token economics must be considered when building agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architectural patterns that improve token economics for multi-agent applications, covering orchestration design decisions (orchestrator-subagent, generator-verifier, shared state) and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's temporal policies and cost optimization features improve cost-determinism. We'll illustrate these patterns with practical examples, then open the whiteboard for attendees to share their challenges and solutions.

title: Architect your metadata hub with AWS Glue Data Catalog
speaker: Mihika Naik, Vidit Ochani
abstract: Your data is scattered across warehouses, lakes, databases, and streams. In this session, learn how AWS Glue Data Catalog serves as a single metadata hub that connects all of your data, enforces consistent governance across it, and makes it discoverable across engines and teams. See how to enrich, curate, and share metadata at scale, and give AI agents the context they need to get work done accurately and efficiently. Ideal for data engineers, architects, and platform teams.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: A responsible AI challenge: Audit your agentic AI before the regulator does
speaker: Rachna Chadha, Isha Dalal
abstract: Accuracy is necessary, but it isn't enough for agentic systems. Your agents can handle most requests correctly and still fail when someone asks how a decision was made, who approved it, or how to override it. In this hands-on workshop, you inherit a multi-agent claims system seeded with responsible AI gaps. Using the Well-Architected Responsible AI governance skill in your IDE, you audit the code against responsible AI dimensions like fairness, transparency, and accountability, investigate what you find, fix it, and generate an evidence-backed report. Walk away with a repeatable audit workflow you can run on your own agentic systems.

In this session, discover how Armis - now part of ServiceNow - delivers complete asset visibility and real-time threat detection across IT, OT, and IoT environments. Hear directly from a customer who faced these challenges head-on and learn how Armis, powered by AWS, helped them identify risk, respond faster, and build a stronger security posture across their entire enterprise. title: Ask the AWS Workflows Team: Durable Agents and Workflows
abstract: Come talk with the AWS Workflows team about running agents in production. We'll cover how to keep a long-running agent from losing its work when something fails, how to fit agents into the workflows you already run, and how to orchestrate agents that run code in isolated sandboxes (Lambda MicroVMs). We'll also get into when Step Functions is the better fit, when Lambda durable functions is, and how teams use both together. It's an informal conversation, so bring your use cases and the problems you're stuck on. We want to hear what's working for you and what isn't.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Ask the News: Making Decades of Publisher Content Instantly Searchable (sponsored by MongoDB)
speaker: Ashwin Gangadhar, Joey Marburger
abstract: TPublishers sit on enormous archives: decades of articles, millions of photos, entire histories of coverage. Most of it is invisible the moment someone needs more than a keyword match. ArcXP built Ask the News to close that gap: a standalone, API-first product giving publishers natural-language access to their own content, powered by MongoDB Atlas Vector Search. The system combines lexical and vector search so results reflect what was meant, not what was said. One of the hardest parts was visual: a pipeline that generated descriptions and embeddings for roughly five million historical images, making decades of archives searchable by meaning for the first time. You'll leave understanding a working pattern for combining lexical and vector search, and a model for exposing natural-language search as an API-first product, not a bolt-on feature. Featuring ArcXP, presented by MongoDB. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Assess your workloads with SELinux compatibility on Amazon Linux 2027
speaker: Chris Bilbo, Ovais Siddiqui, Steve Zarkos, Sai Harsha Suryadevara, Stewart Smith
abstract: AL2027 preview enforces SELinux by default. In this session, deploy an application that hits SELinux denials, learn to read audit logs, diagnose the root cause, and write a custom policy that resolves it. You will leave with the practical skills to adopt AL2027's security defaults.

title: Assume breach, prove recovery: a ransomware resilience workshop
speaker: Danny Wright, Christopher Strug
abstract: Most organizations have backups. Few can prove clean recovery after ransomware, and regulators now demand exactly that proof. In this hands-on workshop, you configure a resilient backup architecture on AWS using vaults and immutable storage. You then experience a simulated ransomware event, validate that your recovery infrastructure held, restore to an isolated clean room environment, and scan recovered resources for attacker persistence using GuardDuty Malware Protection. You leave with a recovery validation approach and an understanding of why least privilege, vault lock, and validation are non-negotiable.

title: AtoZ AI Co-Scientist: Multi-Agent Systems That Do Research With You
speaker: Amila Weerasinghe, Olcay Boz
abstract: Can an AI system move beyond answering questions to actually conducting research alongside you? We built one. AtoZ AI Co-Scientist is a multi-agent orchestration platform where specialized agents collaborate through a unified interface to discover literature, synthesize knowledge via graph-routed retrieval, generate hypotheses, implement baselines from papers, and run experiments autonomously. In this chalk talk, we dissect the compositional architecture, the graph-routed retrieval system achieving <200ms with structural signals flat search cannot capture, and Co-Scientist Bench—our agent-agnostic evaluation framework. Bring hard questions about reliability, memory, and human oversight.

Join The Access Group CTO Thad Széll and Coralogix CEO Ariel Assaraf to learn how unified telemetry is moving the business from reactive troubleshooting to continuous product improvement. title: Attesting to Secrets in Zero Knowledge
speaker: Tristan Ravitch
abstract: It is possible to prove factual statements about systems to observers without revealing any details about those systems beyond the stated claims. This is surprising, but not as surprising as the fact that it is borderline practical using Zero Knowledge Proofs. This talk will give an overview of the mathematical foundations of Zero Knowledge Proofs and introduce both interactive and non-interactive proof schemes. It will then dive into the details of some of the current general purpose Zero Knowledge proof systems (e.g., zk-SNARK and zk-STARK) and show how to use Zero Knowledge libraries to attest to (or prove) properties of software systems without sharing the implementations of those systems.

speaker: Anudeep Athlur, Jad Naim, Gordon Shannon
abstract: As a telecom operator, your customers demand resilient, scalable last mile connectivity for their AI workloads. This session shows new options for delivering that. You'll learn how to integrate AWS Interconnect - last mile with your control plane, provisioning connections directly from the AWS Management Console. AT&T shares how they're deploying Interconnect last-mile to expand their connectivity portfolio. They'll also share how they're working with Amazon Leo to bring broadband satellite connectivity to areas with limited connectivity. Leave with a clear model for extending your own connectivity offerings.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: A Unified AWS Data and AI Strategy for SAP Customers
abstract: Explore how AWS and SAP customers can unlock value through converging data and AI strategies. From zero-copy integration with SAP Business Data Cloud and Amazon S3, to enterprise AI agents via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, learn practical approaches to automate SAP processes and accelerate innovation at scale.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Authentication, authorization, and audit for agentic AI on AWS
speaker: Meric Degirmenci, Rickard Löfström
abstract: In this session you will learn how to secure identities and permissions for AI agents across your agentic workflows. Using Strands SDK, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, Cognito, and Verified Permissions, you implement user and machine authentication, fine-grained authorization, consent management, and permission delegation for agents, tools, and LLMs. The session follows a "choose your own adventure" format so you focus on the scenarios most relevant to you, whether that is agent-to-agent delegation, human-in-the-loop consent, or least-privilege tool access. You leave ready to apply these patterns to your own agentic AI systems.

title: Automate AI governance and risk management with John Deere
speaker: segolene Dessertine-Panhard, Carl Kubalsky
abstract: Governance frameworks designed for static deployments struggle to keep pace with AI systems that learn, adapt, and act autonomously. Walk through AWS Responsible AI best practices for governing AI across the full development lifecycle. Then see how John Deere applied these principles through AI Risk Intelligence (AIRI) to automate risk management. Learn how static checks verify controls at code and documentation level while dynamic checks analyze APIs and traces in real time, achieving over 30% reduction in assessment time and continuous visibility into AI risk posture. Learn what it takes to move from periodic manual assessments to continuous, automated governance.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Automate and Scale Cloud Operations with Purpose-Built AI Agents (sponsored by Datadog)
abstract: Engineering teams lose time correlating telemetry, triaging alerts, investigating threats, and turning findings into fixes. This session explores how Datadog’s purpose-built AI agents can reduce that operational burden by applying organizational context and production telemetry to focused developer, SRE, and security workflows. Using the AWS Well-Architected Framework, we’ll examine where agents can improve operational excellence, reliability, security, performance efficiency, and cost optimization. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Automated compliance evidence from day one
speaker: Bill Ohlson, Pal Patel, Nicole Klatt, Marc Luescher, Desiree Brunner
abstract: Your compliance team spends weeks collecting evidence manually before every audit. Automated evidence collection eliminates that burden from day one. In this builders' session, you'll learn how to leverage AWS GRC services, including AWS Config, AWS Organizations, AWS CloudTrail, and Control Catalog, to configure automated evidence collection, map controls to your target framework, use the AI compliance agent to validate both technical controls and procedural policies, and build continuous drift detection that alerts you before your next audit finds the gap.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Automated forensics at scale with generative AI
speaker: Chris Lamont-Smith, Barry Conway
abstract: Forensics is one of the hardest, most manual parts of incident response, and it usually requires a specialist. In this code talk, we work through a realistic Kubernetes cluster compromise where an Amazon GuardDuty finding kicks off the forensics investigation. We watch as an AI agent identifies injected code, and reconstructs the attack chain. Then we tackle the real problem. Forensic evidence needs determinism and a defensible chain of custody, and generative AI is not deterministic. We show the techniques that close that gap, so an AI-driven investigation produces evidence you can defend.

title: Automate disaster recovery with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
speaker: Chiara Marzano, Arnav Khare
abstract: Financial institutions face stringent regulatory requirements for operational resilience, demanding reliable disaster recovery with tight RTO/RPO targets across complex application portfolios. Yet failover procedures often remain manual and prone to error under pressure. In this chalk talk, we explore how to design a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that orchestrates end-to-end disaster recovery automation for regulated workloads. We’ll walk through how a coordination agent delegates to specialized sub-agents for readiness verification, infrastructure operations, Terraform code generation, Git operations, and deployment validation—each with human-in-the-loop approval gates.

speaker: Kalindi Vijesh Parekh, Ajay Desai, Arnab Chakraborty, Madhavi Evana, Nirav Patel
abstract: Dispute resolution calls require agents to navigate multiple systems simultaneously, frustrating customers and driving up costs. In this session, integrate Amazon Connect with Amazon Bedrock to build an AI-assisted dispute workflow. Amazon Connect flows retrieve transaction context from Amazon DynamoDB while an Amazon Bedrock agent drafts resolution options ranked by policy compliance. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway manages tool calling with Cedar-based access policies and centralized observability across each interaction. Real-time transcription surfaces relevant account history and post-call summarization auto-populates the CRM. Implement PII redaction in call recordings, configure retention policies, and test escalation paths when AI cannot resolve a dispute.

speaker: Mackenzie Zastrow, Liz Radway
abstract: Your agent is only as safe as the constraints it can’t bypass. This chalk talk covers how to enforce hard invariants on LLM-driven agents using formal policy languages: Cedar for stateless authorization, Dogwood for temporal reasoning over action history, and human-in-the-loop for the decisions machines shouldn’t make alone. We’ll look at different techniques for integrating this kind of enforcement with agents, including the Strands Agents intervention system and how deterministic policy can sit alongside a probabilistic model.

title: Automate Investigations to Resolve Application Failures with AWS DevOps Agent
speaker: David Carbone
abstract: Every minute of downtime is a minute your customers notice. What if an agent could correlate your logs, metrics, and change history the moment an application fails? In this hands-on lab, use AWS DevOps Agent to autonomously investigate operational issues across your AWS environment. Trigger investigations from simulated application failures, observe the agent correlate logs, metrics, and change history in real time, and review root cause analyses with actionable mitigation plans.

title: Automate patching and compliance with AI-powered visibility
speaker: Justin Thomas, Ravindra Kori, Ganesh Sambandan, Yukitaka Ohmura, Jim Grabinski
abstract: Tracking patch compliance across hundreds of accounts is manual, slow, and hard to prove to auditors. In this hands-on builders' session, you automate patching and continuous compliance in your environment, then let AI do the heavy lifting: generate a multi-account compliance dashboard with Apps in Amazon Quick and answer compliance questions with natural language instead of hand-building reports. By the end, you'll know how to turn raw patch data into audit-ready answers on demand.

speaker: Alan Meridian
abstract: Security testing shouldn't require weeks of manual effort anymore. In this hands-on lab, configure and execute automated penetration tests using AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing. Set up an Agent Space with VPC networking, verify target domains, scope tests by risk type, and monitor execution in real time. Analyze findings with CVSS scores and reproduction steps, then generate actionable reports for your development teams
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Palace Ballroom II

title: Automate savings with AWS Billing and Cost Management services
speaker: Savanna Jensen, Haritha Chitalia
abstract: Managing Savings Plans well is a continuous job. In this chalk talk, we discuss approaches to making commitment purchases more intelligent and less manual. We will cover how you can build a purchasing cadence that incorporates your organization's demand patterns through automation and the right level of human oversight. We'll also cover Automation, a feature within AWS Compute Optimizer that enables you to apply optimization recommendations to your AWS resources, which can help you reduce costs and improve performance. Bring your questions and challenges.

title: Automate threat detection and response across your logs
speaker: Vikash Agrawal, Ravikumar Sola, Vinod Kisanagaram, Rizwan Mohammed, Jean Velez Torres
abstract: Security teams cannot manually hunt through every log for the one event that matters, and threats move faster than analysts can query. In this hands-on builders session, you will build automated detection and response on your security telemetry: metric filters and anomaly detectors that flag suspicious activity, findings routed to alarms that page the right people, and automated remediation that acts before an analyst logs in. After tuning detections to cut false positives, walk away with a pipeline that watches your logs so your team does not have to.

title: Automate your AWS partnership with a unified agentic operating model
speaker: Jesus Rodriguez, Raj Kandaswamy
abstract: Getting the most from your AWS partnership requires thoughtful and sustained engagement from both sides. Instead of heavy manual lifts, an agentic partner operating model supports this engagement at scale through strategic automation, delivering the right guidance, insight, and capabilities to team members who need them most. In this workshop, build a unified agentic operating model that connects pipeline, co-sell coordination, and AWS consumption measurement into a single orchestration layer using your CRM, AWS Partner Central, and Amazon Quick, enabling all team members to easily leverage AWS tools, insights, and investments from one agentic surface to increase your AWS engagement.

title: Automate your business processes with workflow agents on AgentCore
speaker: Will Matos, Daniela Kinsella, Heeki Park
abstract: The agents with the clearest ROI don't wait for a prompt. They wake on an event and run a process to completion. A new lead triggers a prospecting agent, a filed ticket triggers IT resolution, a spend threshold triggers a campaign adjustment. This session covers best practices for building workflow agents on AgentCore: triggering agents from event sources, running long tasks asynchronously on Runtime, connecting to systems of record through gateway, holding state with memory, adding human-in-the-loop approvals, and enforcing actions with policies the agent cannot bypass.

title: Automate your landing zone and network migration with AWS Transform
speaker: Suhail Fouzan, Todd Gruet
abstract: Designing landing zones and translating on-premises networks into cloud-native architectures is complex and time-consuming. AWS Transform automates both. In this workshop, you'll see the landing zone agent analyze your requirements and deploy AWS Control Tower, organizational units, service control policies, and workload accounts as infrastructure as code. Then the network agent translates VMware networking components or firewall configurations into VPCs, subnets, security groups, and transit gateways with hub-and-spoke or isolated topologies, ready for deployment in CDK or Terraform modules. Laptop required.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano IV

title: Automating data pipelines with agentic AI and Apache Iceberg
speaker: Utkarsh Mittal, Sudipta Bagchi
abstract: Join this session to experience the power of agentic AI and Apache Iceberg coming together on AWS to build a self-correcting data pipeline. We will dive in to an agentic architecture for an Iceberg-based data pipeline - governed end-to-end through AWS Glue Data Catalog - where critical telemetry signals such as data loss, schema drift, cost spikes are not only detected and diagnosed but also remediated and verified - all in real time. Attendees will walk away with a blueprint on how to unify DataOps, MLOps, and FinOps for their data pipelines, with Glue Data Catalog as the metadata backbone tying governance, lineage, and discovery together across the pipeline.

title: Automating macOS at scale: AMI build, TCC, and provisioning on EC2 Mac
speaker: Kyle Krall, Caitlin Rawlins
abstract: Automating macOS in the cloud brings challenges Linux and Windows don't. Going from a fresh EC2 Mac instance to a production-ready fleet means clearing non-obvious hurdles: building AMIs with EC2 Image Builder and Packer, pre-approving TCC permissions, bootstrapping Systems Manager, and working with Apple's security model. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through the real friction points teams hit: image pipelines, the TCC dialog problem, remote access, MDM enrollment, and fleet provisioning. Bring your toughest macOS automation questions; most of the session is open Q&A.

title: Automating Serverless migrations at scale with AWS Transform
speaker: Ana Barragan, Jonathan Tuliani, Dan Fox, Bhuvan Annamreddi, Robert Hanuschke
abstract: Runtime deprecations pile up. Legacy code sits untouched because manual upgrades across hundreds of functions take weeks your team doesn't have. In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to assess, plan, and execute Lambda runtime upgrades at scale. Working hands-on, you'll run the full agentic loop: codebase assessment, transformation planning, incremental code changes committed to Git, and self-validating test execution. You'll scale transformations across hundreds of functions in parallel using AWS Batch and Fargate. Walk away with patterns for automated, large-scale modernization. Bring your laptop.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Autonomous AI Ops with AWS DevOps Agent and New Relic Autopilot (sponsored by New Relic)
speaker: Elliot Markowitz, Anush Jayaraman, Bill Fine
abstract: Incident investigation still consumes 1-2 hours of engineering time per event. See how New Relic's Intelligent Observability Platform integrates with AWS DevOps Agent to: Autonomously triage incidents, pinpoint root cause, and deliver actionable remediation with no custom tooling required. Investigate incidents agentically correlating telemetry, code, and deployments across AWS, multi cloud, and on-prem environments. Demonstrate how this innovation proactively prevents future incidents by analyzing patterns and recommending improvements. Learn how customers are cutting MTTR by 75% and shifting from firefighting to prevention, and walk away ready to get started. This presentation is brought to you by New Relic, an AWS Partner.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Autonomous DBOps: Agentic AI for maintaining databases
speaker: Shirish Kulkarni, Paola Lorusso, Rinisha Marar, Dustin Brown, Sudhir Amin
abstract: Maintaining performance for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS often requires manual effort, such as tuning queries, managing indexes, and handling alerts. In this builders' session, learn how to leverage agentic AI solutions implementing LLM-powered autonomous agents to monitor, diagnose, and optimize relational databases in real time. We will demonstrate how AI agents can analyze slow query logs, recommend or apply tuning actions, and trigger intelligent alerts using Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Cloudwatch, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Systems Manager. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Autonomous Multi-Agent system for Manufacturing: Live Demo with Kiro
speaker: Christophe Renard, Mourad Alia
abstract: To achieve the operational agility markets require, manufacturers are turning to AI agents that can reason and act autonomously across the product lifecycle. This session demonstrates how to rapidly build autonomous multi-agent systems using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Kiro that connect CMMS, MES, and ERP systems through Model Context Protocol (MCP). Watch a live demo where we use Kiro to develop specialized manufacturing agents that detect anomalies, diagnose root causes, and orchestrate corrective actions autonomously. Discover how Kiro's spec-driven development workflow compresses multi-agent system development from months to days. Leave with proven architecture patterns that you can apply to transform your production planning, supply chain optimization, and anomaly management processes.

title: Autonomous operations: reducing MTTR at scale, feat. BMG Bank
speaker: Everton Queiroz, Matheus Arrais
abstract: Operations teams face a growing volume of production incidents, but investigating root cause manually is slow and doesn't scale. At Banco BMG, one of Brazil's most established financial institutions with more than 9 million customers, roughly 350 operational events occurred daily, each investigation taking hours. In this lightning talk, see how AWS DevOps Agent began investigating these events autonomously, reducing root cause identification from hours to minutes. Learn to integrate the agent with your observability tools, correlate telemetry, logs, and code, and turn every investigation into compounding efficiency that lowers MTTR.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Autonomous Remediation with OpenTelemetry and DevOps Agent
speaker: Jones Zachariah Noel, Julia Furst Morgado
abstract: You instrumented everything. You have metrics, logs, and traces. And when production breaks a human still has to piece it together, tab by tab, signal by signal, under pressure. That is not an observability problem, it’s an automation problem. We'll show you an architecture on AWS that closes it. OpenTelemetry captures signals across EKS, ECS, and Lambda. AWS DevOps Agent runs the investigation, finds the root cause, and prepares the fix. By the time a human looks at it, the pull request is ready. Come learn the triggers, investigation loop, and guardrails you need before letting an agent touch production.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk

speaker: Manik Chopra, Prem Dhayalan
abstract: In this session, learn how a large financial institution deploys AWS DevOps Agent as an autonomous SRE teammate to reduce incident investigation time from hours to minutes and free engineering teams from reactive firefighting. Explore the architecture spanning CloudWatch, Splunk, GitHub, and Slack integrations, and see how the agent correlates telemetry across data sources to identify root causes and generate mitigation plans. Walk away with practical patterns for deploying agentic operations in regulated, compliance-sensitive environments.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Auto Scaling meets Capacity Reservations: Patterns that work
speaker: Jon Burns, Harsh Bhimjyani
abstract: Capacity Reservations hold your instances. Auto Scaling right-sizes your fleet. Together, they give you both availability and cost efficiency. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to make them work seamlessly. We'll walk through strategies that keep reservation utilization high during scale-in, mixed-instance policies that balance cost and availability, and fallback patterns for Capacity Blocks transitions. Bring your scaling architecture and we'll work through it on the board.

title: AWS AI agents accelerate SAP migration and modernization on AWS
speaker: Beth Sharp, Nikhil Chetwani
abstract: The legacy ERP system that once gave you a competitive edge may now be limiting your ability to innovate. Modernizing SAP can be complex, expensive, risky, and every delay is a missed opportunity to innovate. In this Chalk Talk, you will learn how AI Agents can make it possible to upgrade to SAP's Cloud ERP safely and cost-effectively in weeks, not months. Whether you're running SAP ECC, moving to RISE with SAP, modernizing ABAP and PI/PO, or migrating SAP Business Warehouse (BW), discover how AI-powered agents can take on the heavy lifting for you

title: AWS AI Factories: Bring production scale AI to your data center
speaker: Pranav Chachra, Gareth Tucker, Daniel Xu
abstract: Data sovereignty, data gravity, and latency requirements prevent many organizations from running all AI workloads in the public cloud. AWS AI Factories bring AWS and NVIDIA AI infrastructure directly into your data center, fully operated, maintained, and continuously updated by AWS. Run leading foundation models on premises for training and inference without building and managing AI infrastructure yourself or negotiating separate agreements with model providers. In this session, learn how organizations are accelerating AI adoption, reducing time to value, and maintaining full control of their data while benefiting from the AWS experience in their own facilities.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: AWS AI from chips to agents: The end-to-end production AI foundation
speaker: Alex Thewsey, Denis V Batalov
abstract: The AI experiment is over. Now it has to work. This session walks through the AWS AI Platform end-to-end, starting at the chip layer with AWS Trainium and AWS Graviton delivering up to 40% better price performance. From there, model inference and customization through Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI. Then production agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Every layer co-designed so workloads move across the stack without rearchitecting. You will leave knowing which service handles which job, where the layers connect to accelerate production timelines, and how to keep your architecture open as your AI strategy evolves.

title: AWS AI League: Build agents with AgentCore (Agentic Football Cup)
speaker: Parth Desai, Gonzalo Ron, Ian Holtz
abstract: Coordinating agents is where multi agent systems break. They duplicate work, drop handoffs, and burn tokens. In this workshop, build and deploy five autonomous agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Kiro and the Strands Agents SDK, then field them five versus five in live Agentic Football matches. Write the tools your agents call, orchestrate multi turn reasoning across a maze like arena, and solve coordination problems that decide the match. Tune prompts, roles, and tactics between rounds and watch your score climb a live leaderboard. Leave with working code, production ready multi agent patterns, and a shot at the Finale.

title: AWS AI League: Build domain specific AI
speaker: Rajesh Babu Nuvvula, Jai Vumma, Natasya Idries
abstract: In this hands-on workshop you’ll compete head-to-head with other builders to build your own domain specific AI. You’ll tackle real-world challenges as you generate synthetic datasets, experiment with model customization, and fine-tune models to improve accuracy, clarity, and relevance. You’ll learn just how accessible and cost-effective AI customization can be. Whether you’re chasing the championship or simply sharpening your AI expertise, this session delivers practical techniques you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate

title: AWS AI League Championship Grand Finale: Agentic Football Cup
abstract: Experience the ultimate AI showdown from your theater seat as fifty finalists from the AWS AI League season battle head-to-head in real time for the $50,000 championship prize. This electrifying viewing experience offers ML practitioners, developers, and AI enthusiasts unique insights into agent orchestration, model customization, and multi-agent coordination at scale, as five-versus-five AI agent squads face off live in Agentic Football, built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK.

title: AWS AI League: Models, Tools, Strategy with SageMaker, Bedrock & AgentCore
speaker: Ruchi Bhatia, Dana Bullukian, Seyha Kry
abstract: Turn a generic model into one that wins on your task, and prove it with data. In this hands-on workshop, you customize a foundation model on Amazon SageMaker AI using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), with no infrastructure to manage. Then you build an agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that orchestrates the model end to end: preparing datasets, triggering training, registering models, evaluating with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploying to a real-time endpoint. Your score posts to a live leaderboard, and you tune between rounds to climb it. You walk away knowing when customization beats a strong prompt.

title: AWS and Nu: Building scalable architecture using IAM Account access manager
speaker: Hugo Feijó, Laura Reith, Tim Kosanke
abstract: As organizations grow across teams, AWS accounts, and countries, workforce access often becomes a bottleneck. This is especially true when you depend on existing IAM roles you don't want to re-engineer. Learn how IAM account access manager helps you assign your existing IAM roles to users and groups in IAM Identity Center, give native AWS CLI access to your workforce, and carry each user's identity into every role session, all on a resilient architecture. Then see how Nu, the largest digital bank in Latin America, modernized a decade-old authorization model across 11 organizations and hundreds of AWS accounts to securely scale for more than 140 million customers.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: AWS Backup: Centralized data protection for your cloud environment
speaker: Bisman Sethi, LeelaVinod Bandla, Mathew Patrick, Fathima Kamal
abstract: Managing data protection across a growing cloud environment requires a centralized strategy. AWS Backup was designed around this principle, giving more than 150,000 organizations a fully managed service to automate backup operations, enforce protection policies at scale, and safeguard 20+ AWS services from a single console. From human error to infrastructure failures to targeted attacks, AWS Backup helps ensure you can recover the right data, at the right time, with confidence. In this session, learn how AWS Backup works, how you can use it to protect mission-critical workloads, and hear directly from customers about their implementation strategies and operational outcomes.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: AWS Backup clean room recovery: Comprehensive resilience framework
speaker: Wali Akbari, Sabith Venkitachalapathy
abstract: Having an isolated vault is only half the battle. When a cyber event hits, you need confidence your backups are clean and recoverable. In this chalk talk, learn how to design an Isolated Recovery Environment using AWS Backup that validates and restores data in a secure space separate from production: reducing blast radius, breaking the kill chain, and proving recoverability on demand. We'll cover immutable air-gapped copies, automated restore testing with malware scanning, and Multi-party approval to control recovery access during account compromise. Leave with a framework for building recovery confidence into your backup strategy.

title: AWS CDK - Contributing AI safety tooling to the IaC ecosystem
speaker: Praneeta Prakash, Jorge Diaz Alvarado
abstract: AI agents generate infrastructure-as-code that looks correct but fails 38% of the time at deployment. The open source Agent Toolkit for AWS provides skills for validation, linting, and security checks that any MCP-compatible AI tool can consume before deploying. This chalk talk covers how we contributed these capabilities as open source tooling that works across cfn-lint, Checkov, and cdk-nag, improving first-deploy success from 62% to 82%. Attendees discuss how to build similar validation layers for their own IaC tools and the tradeoffs between blocking vs advisory checks in agent workflows.

abstract: Skills decay at unprecedented speed as AI reshapes what proficiency means. Certifications still validate expertise, but practitioners now need to demonstrate they can design, build, and optimize AI-powered systems alongside traditional cloud architecture. This lightning talk explains how AWS Training and Certification developed exam content, hands-on labs, and simulation-based assessments for agentic AI domains. You will also see how our team validated new competency frameworks, mapped learning paths to job roles, and built assessment experiences that measure real-world readiness rather than knowledge recall alone.

title: AWS Escape Room: Exam Prep for AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner

abstract: Prepare for AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner by playing this 3D virtual escape room game where Certification prep meets competitive gaming. Step into a 3D virtual world, choose your avatar, and race other players through rooms locked behind AWS Cloud Practitioner exam-style challenges. Each room combines interactive puzzles with hands-on labs that reinforce foundational cloud concepts like Compute, Storage, Networking, Security, and pricing models. Solve challenges collaboratively or compete solo, unlock rooms, and escape first to claim the leaderboard.

title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs: Strong isolation for agents & beyond
speaker: Anton Aleksandrov, CJ Avilla, Alexander Vladimirov
abstract: Agents running generated code, multi-tenant platforms, and untrusted workloads all need strong isolation, but each traditional compute option forces a tradeoff. VMs isolate well but start slowly. Containers are fast but share a kernel. Functions scale to zero but limit state. Teams close the gaps with isolation logic they build and maintain themselves. Lambda MicroVMs offer sandboxes with VM-level isolation for each agent, tenant, or task: state that persists across invocations, automatic suspend on idle, resume on demand. This session covers how MicroVMs work, the security and isolation model, lifecycle management, and patterns for agentic sandboxing and untrusted code execution.

title: Benchmarking Bedrock knowledge bases for agents in production (sponsored by Braintrust)
abstract: In this talk, we’ll walk through an independent eval of Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, which manages the ingestion, parsing, and retrieval steps in a RAG application. In the first half, we’ll cover our methodology, including how we developed a dataset that queries documents such as tickets, wiki pages, and product docs, and what we decided to score: latency, cost, relevance, and citation support. We’ll also cover how we analyzed the results with research rigor, including p50 and p95 latency and confidence intervals around our metrics. In the second half, we’ll expand this into a conceptual understanding of evals and observability: why they’re important, how other companies are implementing them in production, and the terminology you need to know. This presentation is brought to you by Braintrust, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Best path forward: Rehost & replatform to containers with AWS Transform
speaker: Yogesh Bhatia, Diego Dalmolin
abstract: Not every app needs the same migration path, and figuring out which ones to rehost versus containerize is where teams get stuck. In this workshop, you'll use AWS Transform to plan a combined migration and modernization across your application portfolio, then execute a mix of container and rehost migrations deploying to Amazon ECS or EKS. You'll work through the full lifecycle. Learn how to order waves and coordinate cutover across a mixed portfolio. Leave with a realistic multi-wave plan you can apply to your own environment. Laptop required.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Pompeian IV

title: Best practices for agentic-driven operations
speaker: Dave Schnorr, Bill Fine, Metanat Hooshsadat
abstract: AI agents are moving from assistants to operators, but how do they actually work within your operational workflows? Understand the architecture of agents that detect anomalies, diagnose root cause across distributed systems, and execute remediation like rollbacks, scaling, and traffic shifts. Learn how agents reason over telemetry, sequence actions, and determine when to escalate. Explore best practices for shaping agent behavior through guardrails, approval gates, and feedback loops as core design elements. Leave with a framework for evaluating where agents should act autonomously versus where human judgment remains essential.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Best practices for AI-powered software development on Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Ajit Mahareddy, Alfredo Castillo
abstract: You already use a coding agent for software development. It touches your codebase, infrastructure, and production environment and needs guardrails, permissions, and rules to operate safely. In this workshop, you connect an agent of your choice, such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex, to Amazon Bedrock and deliver a real application from brief to production. You define specs the agent can act on, wire in automated test gates, apply Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and lock down permissions before anything reaches infrastructure. The app serves as a tested reference implementation your team can adapt to its own development workflows. Laptop required.

title: Best practices for building an observability strategy in the age of AI
speaker: Helen Ashton, Adam Rubinsky
abstract: Most observability strategies were built for a pre-AI world and are no longer enough. Your data foundation remains critical, but the way you use that data is changing fast. In this chalk talk, we explore what stays the same, what must evolve, and what's new as AI reshapes observability. We'll cover the shift from static dashboards to dynamic experiences, from reactive alarms to AI-driven insights, and the new questions you need to answer, like how well your agents are performing. Join us as we share what AWS is learning as we embrace AI-led observability.

title: Best practices for cost optimization with AWS Backup
speaker: Lakshmi Nair, Samreen Taj K P
abstract: AWS Backup protects workloads across more than 20 AWS services, and each resource type brings its own cost profile. In this chalk talk, learn practical approaches to managing your data protection TCO by tailoring your AWS Backup strategy to each workload. We'll dig into full versus incremental backups, lifecycle policies, cold storage tiering for S3 and other resource types, and backing up direclty to logically-air-gapped-vault to protect data from ransomware without maintaining multiple copies. Then we'll cover how to build cost observability using AWS Backup reporting and monitoring to track and optimize spend.
