title: Best practices for making coding agent orchestration more deterministic
speaker: Arundeep Nagaraj, Romain Dura
abstract: As agents work on longer, more complex tasks, the context window fills up and the agent can lose track of its plan and execution steps. The manual setup required to get multi-agent orchestration to reliably complete these kinds of tasks can be complex and brittle. In this chalk talk, we will walk through best practices, tools, and patterns that power users have perfected to set up and scale multi-agent workloads. Bring questions, challenges, or edge cases you ran into and we'll walk you through how to approach them to improve reliability.

title: Best Practices for .NET modernization with AWS Transform
speaker: Chan Zaw, David Pallmann, Renuka Krishnan, Runeet Vashisht, Neeraj Handa
abstract: As organizations look to reduce tech debt for their .NET applications, builders are looking to accelerate modernization with AI tools. In this hands-on session, we'll explore best practices for modernizing .NET Framework applications with AWS Transform. You'll learn how to work alongside the agent to reach a desired outcome. Together, we will apply plan customizations, steering documents, checkpoints, and iteration. Come ready to share your use cases and leave with practical steps to efficient, cost-effective modernization. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Builders' Session

title: Best practices for operating an Apache Iceberg lakehouse at scale
speaker: Aditya Challa, Priyanka Chaudhary
abstract: Operating an Iceberg lakehouse at scale means taming the operational overhead that grows with your data. In this chalk talk, we dive into table maintenance strategies—compaction, snapshot expiration, and orphan file cleanup—and discuss how Amazon S3 Tables automates these tasks. We'll whiteboard patterns for metadata management with AWS Glue Data Catalog, storage cost optimization through lifecycle-aware file pruning, and partition evolution without rewriting data. You will leave with battle-tested operational patterns for production Iceberg workloads.

title: Best practices for production agents on AgentCore, with Nasdaq
speaker: Anila Joshi, Isaac Privitera, Mike O'Rourke
abstract: Learn best practices for the full agent lifecycle on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Ship agents to production with microVM isolation, persistent memory, and any framework. Use gateway to connect agents to MCP servers, knowledge bases, and APIs with automatic authentication. Trace model calls with OpenTelemetry-compatible observability and run continuous evaluations. Nasdaq joins to share how its GenAI platform empowers 10,000 employees build agents for research, coding, and workflow automation. Hear how Nasdaq scales agent runtime infrastructure and handles multi-account isolation and agent identity, and the operational patterns required to run agentic AI reliably in a regulated financial services environment.

title: Best practices for scaling self-managed GPU workstations
speaker: Shreya Manjunath, Avi Mittal
abstract: Artists, engineers, and scientists need GPU-powered virtual workstations, but managing VDI at scale means navigating instance selection, capacity, and cost. In this chalk talk, learn how to match EC2 G instances to user personas, from fractional GPU for task workers to full GPU for power users running 3D modeling, compositing, or subsurface visualization. Explore the decision framework covering instance types, DCV streaming, storage, security, and fleet orchestration. Whether supporting a VFX render farm's artist desktops, an oil company's subsurface workstations, or an automotive design studio, leave with guidance balancing performance, cost, and simplicity.

title: Best Practices for Successful Multiplayer Game Launches
speaker: Juho Jantunen, Chad Lingmann
abstract: The session covers best practices, architectural guidance and lessons learned for successful multiplayer game launches at scale. It's based on experience from helping hundreds of game customers from indie studios to AAA titles launch their games on AWS.

title: Best Practices for Successful Multiplayer Game Launches
speaker: Juho Jantunen, Chad Lingmann
abstract: The session covers best practices, architectural guidance and lessons learned for successful multiplayer game launches at scale. It's based on experience from helping hundreds of game customers from indie studios to AAA titles launch their games on AWS.

title: Better, faster, cheaper: How Valkey is revolutionizing caching
speaker: Meet Bhagdev, Madelyn Olson
abstract: Discover how the powerful combination of open source Valkey and Amazon ElastiCache is transforming the landscape of distributed caching. In this session, explore recent innovations including advanced search capabilities such as full-text search, hybrid search, a memory-efficient btree that can double the performance of leaderboard workloads, and a new replication architecture that can cut the memory overhead of replication by up to 50%. Learn about the infrastructure that enables ElastiCache to patch hundreds of thousands of customers while maintaining high availability, even for extreme workloads like Prime Day's trillion requests per minute.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Beyond AIOps: Operating safely in the age of agent sprawl
speaker: Ash Thankey, Paul Moran, Tarran Benson-West, Samuel Walls
abstract: As organisations move from a small number of AI assistants to a distributed ecosystem of agents that can discover tools, make decisions, and act, operational excellence must evolve. Drawing on HMRC’s work to develop a governed platform model for agentic systems, this session explores a practical maturity model spanning inventory, ownership, identity, delegated authority, observability, blast-radius controls, evaluation, and human accountability. Learn how existing platform engineering, SRE, security and service-management practices can be extended across cloud and SaaS ecosystems without creating a separate governance regime for every agent or vendor. Designed for platform leaders, SREs and architects preparing to scale agents safely in complex, regulated environments.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Beyond AI Productivity, What It Takes to Deliver Real Business Value (sponsored by JetBrains)
abstract: AI is making it easier than ever to write code. But more code doesn't necessarily mean better software or better business results. As companies invest in AI tools and agents, the bigger question is whether they're getting real value from them. How do they measure what's working, maintain quality, and keep costs under control? This presentation is brought to you by JetBrains, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Beyond Batch: Modernize with Event-Driven Architecture & Serverless
speaker: Sundar Shanmugam, Ramesh Mathikumar, Elie Elmalem, Ray Chang, Rajdeep Banerjee
abstract: In this builders' session, transform a batch-oriented data processing pipeline into a real-time, event-driven architecture using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and AWS Step Functions. Working hands-on in small groups, you'll decompose a monolithic batch process into discrete event-driven steps, implement file-processing triggers, and design fan-out patterns for parallel execution. Learn when to keep batch and when to go event-driven, and leave with a working modernization pattern. You must bring your laptop to participate.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Evaluating AI Safety with Formal Guarantees
speaker: Qian Hu, Weitong Ruan
abstract: As AI systems become increasingly capable and autonomous, safety evaluation is emerging as a critical challenge. While current evaluations largely rely on benchmark performance and empirical red-teaming, these approaches provide limited guarantees about real-world risk. This talk will explore an emerging direction in AI safety: evaluating model behavior with formal statistical guarantees. We will discuss how ideas from reliability engineering, robustness certification, and risk assessment can be applied to quantify catastrophic failure probabilities, the assumptions behind such guarantees, and their implications for deploying and governing frontier AI systems. This topic is highly relevant to the future of trustworthy and accountable AI.

title: Beyond capability: Designing AI for an era of converged privacy & trust
speaker: Jamie Angell, Emily Choi-Greene, Gerald Friedland, Nuala O’Connor
abstract: As AI advances faster than the frameworks meant to govern it, technology, safety, and privacy are converging. The defining question of the next era is no longer just how fast we can build, but how we design AI systems that earn absolute trust. Getting this right turns governance into a competitive advantage and sets a standard of integrity that improves how people live and work. This panel brings together voices from privacy policy, AI product security, and privacy research to openly explore the market's unresolved tensions at a pivotal moment. Panelists will share how privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) and trust-by-design practices give organizations the foundation to build privacy and trust into AI systems from the start so that responsible innovation can move faster.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: Beyond chatbots: Event-driven AI agents on Apache Flink
speaker: Weiqing Yang, Mayank Juneja
abstract: Most AI agents wait for a prompt. Apache Flink Agents flips that—agents react autonomously to live event streams as Flink operators, with exactly-once guarantees, durable state, and millisecond latency. Learn how this event-driven foundation differs from request-response frameworks, then see an ops agent detect a failing Flink job, diagnose it with an LLM on Amazon Bedrock, retrieve a runbook, and remediate—no human in the loop. Hear from Flink committers on production agents at Alibaba and LinkedIn, and from AWS contributors building Bedrock and other AWS integrations upstream.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Beyond code generation: accelerating the entire SDLC on AWS
speaker: Ryan Bachman, Adnan Bilwani, Tony Patino
abstract: Teams pour AI into code generation and wonder why they're not shipping faster. In reality, accelerating one stage just moves the bottleneck downstream. This session follows a single task across its entire lifecycle and shows where AI compounds. We'll design and build with Kiro, pay down tech debt with AWS Transform, catch vulnerabilities early with AWS Continuum (formerly known as AWS Security Agent), ship through safe CI/CD pipelines, and resolve production issues with AWS DevOps Agent—then feed what we learn back into the next task. Come see our vision for an SDLC where every stage moves at the same speed.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Beyond Coding Agents: Inside the Self-Improving Software Factory (sponsored by Factory)
speaker: Leo Tchourakov
abstract: Top engineering teams have outgrown simple coding agents and are automating their entire development lifecycle with Software Factories. Agents proactively pick up signals like alerts and bug reports, carrying work through triage, design, implementation, testing, review, QA, deployment, and monitoring. Engineers set goals and approve what ships, and every run makes the loop better. This session answers the key questions engineering leaders ask: How do you minimize risk and maintain oversight? How do you raise quality, control costs, and ship faster? How do you compound organizational knowledge? Learn from enterprise teams running Software Factories in production.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Beyond English: Architecture Patterns for Multilingual AI Voice Agents
speaker: Mark Macdonald, Prabhakar Rajasekar
abstract: Deploying AI voice agents beyond English introduces unique challenges: accent handling, language detection, code-switching between languages mid-conversation, and cultural nuances in conversation flow. In this chalk talk, we share architecture patterns for building multilingual voice agents using Amazon Connect Agentic Voice. We cover real-world scenarios from deployments like Spanish and English coexistence, German with regional dialects, and Italian conversational AI. We discuss when speech-to-speech models work natively, when to fall back to TTS pipelines, how to handle polyglot but non-native accent scenarios, and practical approaches to knowledge base localization. Bring your language challenge and we'll design your multilingual architecture on the whiteboard.

title: Beyond Evals: Setting up your agents and your enterprise for success (sponsored by LangChain)
speaker: Joel Johnson
abstract: We are witnessing models and agents continually becoming more capable, all while the process of meaningfully evaluating them continues to be a challenge. In this session, we will dissect eval best practices observed both in the field and internally at LangChain. This session will go beyond just your technical evaluation toolkit and provide practical organizational and process takeaways and a better understanding of what future capabilities are unlocked downstream of good evaluation. This session will be especially relevant to teams deploying agents in cross-functional domains. This presentation is brought to you by LangChain, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Beyond fine-tuning: RL for reasoning agents with AWS Trainium
speaker: Hiroshi Tokoyo, Maen Suleiman
abstract: Supervised fine-tuning teaches a model to follow instructions, and reinforcement learning (RL) teaches it to reason. In this chalk talk, explore what RLHF and GRPO add beyond fine-tuning and how to run them on AWS Trainium, purpose-built for price performance. Start with a co-located GRPO loop in Hugging Face TRL on native PyTorch, then see a disaggregated loop on Ray and verl or SkyRL, in which TorchTitan trains the policy and vLLM generates rollouts, so each side can be sized for its own load. Learn when each architecture fits, and leave ready to use the AWS Neuron SDK to implement RL loops that train agents to reason.

title: Beyond Next-Token Prediction: World Models for Human Health
speaker: Chenyan Xiong
abstract: Next-token prediction has been effective for language, but is it the right learning objective for achieving clinical intelligence from longitudinal human health data? In this talk, we show that treating health records as flat token sequences limit the advancement of foundation models in healthcare. We then introduce a Health State–Action World Model that abstracts longitudinal records into learned representations of patient health states and clinical actions, and models how these states evolve under different interventions. This abstraction enables pretraining models to predict future health events, diagnoses, treatments, and responses to treatment. Across large-scale datasets, we show that moving from token-level prediction to state–action modeling enables clinical intelligence that cannot be achieved through token prediction alone, while generalizing strongly to unseen patients.

title: Beyond pilots: agentic AI transforming mortgage operations and IT at scale (sponsored by Tata Consultancy Services)
speaker: Rajesh Kannan Ganesan, Sophie Marchal
abstract: Mortgage lending still runs on handoffs, exceptions, and manual review. See how a leading US mortgage lender is rebuilding origination and servicing with agentic AI on AWS, cutting cycle times while keeping controls and auditability intact. We will also show how the same agent patterns reach IT operations, resolving incidents before customers feel them. Tata Consultancy Services shares the reference architecture, guardrails, and adoption model behind both. Built for financial services business and operations leaders, CIOs and IT operations heads, and data and AI leaders, this session gives you a practical path from promising pilots to production at enterprise scale. This presentation is brought to you by Tata Consultancy Services, an AWS Partner.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Beyond Prompt Engineering: Optimize the Agent Harness
speaker: Jonathan Buck, Po-Shin Chen
abstract: An agent’s performance depends on far more than its model or system prompt. Tools, instructions, context management, memory, orchestration, and runtime policies form an agent harness that can determine whether the same model succeeds or fails. This session introduces harness optimization: a systematic, evaluation-driven approach to improving the complete agent system. Learn how to identify high-leverage changes, design controlled experiments, optimize for quality, latency, and cost, and avoid overfitting to benchmarks. Leave with a repeatable method for turning agent development into an engineering discipline.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Beyond Prompts: Crafting Production GenAI from Scratch
speaker: Steven Leung
abstract: Building reliable GenAI applications requires deliberate systems engineering, not just prompt engineering. After collaborating with AWS Professional Services on an enterprise client, I learned how to build production-grade web apps the official AWS way. Bypassing basic buzzwords, we map a compound serverless conversational assistant engineered from scratch using AWS CDK, CloudFront, Cognito, API Gateway, and ⁠Amazon Bedrock. Examine how to handle real-world token streaming failures, manage state in DynamoDB, and implement strict Infrastructure as Code. Leave with complete source code and a concrete approach to balancing model performance against infrastructure cost in highly concurrent production environments.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Beyond RSA: Post-quantum data encryption using ML-KEM in AWS KMS
speaker: Vipul Gupta
abstract: RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography secure nearly every application today, and both are vulnerable to future cryptographically relevant quantum computers. Data captured now can be decrypted later, so applications needing long-term confidentiality should adopt post-quantum encryption well before those computers arrive. AWS KMS now offers ML-KEM, the NIST-standardized replacement for RSA and ECDH key establishment and ultimately encryption under asymmetric keys. It protects the private keys in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSMs. In this session, learn about ML-KEM and how to use it as a building block for quantum-safe encryption using Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE).

title: Beyond Search: How Gilead Built a Multi-Agent AI That Reasons Like a Scientist (sponsored by Thoughtworks)
speaker: Shayan Mohanty
abstract: Gilead is pivoting from virology leader to oncology and immunology powerhouse, targeting 10+ transformative therapies by 2030. With Thoughtworks, Gilead built an AI co-scientist on AWS that reasons across 1M+ ELN assay records, 3M+ internal documents and external literature. It reads assay, compound and target data like a scientist, returning one cited answer with conflicts flagged. Scientists now reach evidence-backed decisions in minutes, not days. Gilead and Thoughtworks share how the solution earned scientists' trust. This presentation is brought to you by Thoughtworks, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Beyond the Build: Scaling and Governing AI Agents with Dataiku and Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Dataiku)
abstract: As enterprises move from experimenting with AI agents to deploying them at scale, the challenge is no longer just how to build agents, it’s how to maintain visibility, performance, and control across the growing agent ecosystem. This session will explore how Amazon Bedrock and Dataiku Agent Management support the agent lifecycle from creation through enterprise-wide management. Attendees will see how organizations can build and deploy agents with AWS while using Dataiku to discover agents, monitor performance, and identify risk across environments, helping teams scale agentic AI with greater confidence and governance. This presentation is brought to you by Dataiku, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Beyond the Buy Button: Cisco on AWS Marketplace, a Partner-Led AI Win (sponsored by Cisco)
speaker: Dave Gervon
abstract: AWS Marketplace isn't just a procurement channel, it's a financial lever. A typical ISV saves a procurement cycle. Cisco draws down committed spend against the infrastructure your agents run on: connectivity from cloud to edge, visibility into agent behavior, and protection for models, identities, and data. Partners add the expertise to deploy it right, turning a procurement decision into an architectural one, a true better together win with AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cisco, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Beyond the coding assistant: Build a software factory for your startup
speaker: Alain Krok, Karl Baria
abstract: Startups need to turn customer requests into reliable releases without overwhelming a small engineering team. This demo-driven session explores how software factories combine AI agents, repeatable workflows, independent verification, and human judgment to handle engineering work from request to delivery. We'll follow a bounded change through implementation, testing, review, and release, and show what happens when the generated solution fails a required check. Attendees will learn how to start with one useful workflow, measure its value, and expand delegation as evidence builds confidence.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Beyond the Docs: Operating Scoped VPC Endpoints in Real Environments
speaker: Kenneth Attard, Meg Ashby
abstract: Scoped VPC endpoint policies look simple, until production traffic proves otherwise. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through real-world failures we've encountered while deploying account- and org-scoped endpoint policies and trace the identity flows, auth chains, and hidden dependencies behind them. Together, we'll explore a key lesson: endpoint policies evaluate the request that's actually made, not the request you think you're making. Bring your questions and experiences as we whiteboard the assumptions that lead to outages and learn how to spot them before they impact production.

title: Beyond the GPU count: Engineering inference at scale
speaker: Mai Nishitani
abstract: You have enough GPUs in your server to cover your software requirements. But is that all you need to consider? In a world where everyone is fighting for GPUs, picking the wrong server type is one of the most expensive mistakes an engineering team makes at scale. This session shares lessons running GPU inference across AWS and bare metal connected privately. You'll see how EKS Hybrid Nodes provides a single scheduling plane, failure modes, and how to use AI to accelerate decisions without replacing engineering judgement. Leave with a cloud and bare metal architectural pattern and a GPU selection framework covering workload fit and server tradeoffs.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Beyond the GPU: Optimizing AI performance with storage architecture
speaker: Aditi Garg, Edward Naim, Randy Seamans
abstract: When AI workloads need scale or speed, the instinct is to add more compute, but GPU speed only pays off when the data keeps pace. From training to inference, storage architecture shapes performance at every stage: optimizing checkpoints for uninterrupted training, reducing model load times, extending context windows beyond GPU memory, and accelerating retrieval for RAG and inference workloads. Learn how Amazon FSx for Lustre, FSx for OpenZFS, and Amazon S3 Express One Zone give you those levers.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Beyond the IDE: autonomous development with Kiro web and mobile
speaker: Artur Rodrigues, Massimo "Max" Becker
abstract: Kiro web and mobile bring agentic development to your browser—every session in an isolated cloud sandbox, no local setup, accessible anywhere you have an internet connection. In this hands-on workshop, you'll work with Kiro two ways. First, iterate interactively: connect a repo, explore the codebase, and shape changes in real time. Then go hands-off: assign a task from a tracked issue, let Kiro plan and implement autonomously, and review the pull request it opens. Sessions run in the cloud and keep going after you close your laptop—check in and review diffs from your phone with the Kiro iOS app. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Beyond the pilot: How customers scaled Kiro and proved the value
speaker: Michael Erdman, Rory Richardson (AWS), Diana Kennedy, Kym Weiland
abstract: Adopting a coding agent is as much an organizational challenge as a technical one. In this panel, engineering leaders from companies that deployed Kiro at scale share what worked: rollout strategies that drove adoption, training approaches that met developers where they were, governance guardrails that satisfied security teams, and the metrics they use to measure productivity impact. Bring your questions—this is an open conversation about the patterns, pitfalls, and payoffs of making AI-assisted development the default across an engineering organization.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Beyond the pilot: Why VCs are betting on FDE-led growth
speaker: Shane Rai, Asa Kalavade, Jon Lehr
abstract: Successful AI pilots no longer guarantee revenue. As enterprise pricing shifts toward consumption and outcomes, startups capture value only when customers deploy, adopt, and realize results. Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) can close that gap. Moderated by Shane Rai, Principal AI Strategist at the AWS GenAI Innovation Center, the panel features Asa Kalavade, VP of AWS Forward Deployed Engineering; Anu Bharadwaj, Partner at ICONIQ; and Jon Lehr, Co-founder and General Partner at Work-Bench. They will debate whether FDE is consulting under a new name or a compounding moat, and examine the economics and metrics linking deployment to retention and expansion. Series A+ founders and investors will gain a practical framework for building FDE capabilities and moving enterprise pilots into production.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Beyond the simulator: Quantum chemistry workflows on real hardware
speaker: Tyler Takeshita, Veronika Liutarevich, Sebastian Stern, Nick White, Nicola Smyth
abstract: Get hands-on experience running quantum computing experiments using the Kvantify SDK; the same workflow used by researchers. In this workshop, participants will set up and execute computational workflows, testing them locally, on a classical simulator via Amazon Braket, and finally on a real quantum processing unit (QPU). Through practical exercises in enzyme engineering and battery development, learners will see how quantum computing accelerates discovery in life sciences and materials science, bridging the gap from simulation to real quantum hardware.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Beyond Tool Sprawl: Scalable, Trusted Access to APIs, MCP, and Data (sponsored by Apollo GraphQL)
speaker: Matt DeBergalis
abstract: Enterprises have spent years building APIs for applications and developers. They now need to make those systems accessible to AI agents, and MCP is only the beginning. Turning every API into a tool leads to sprawl and inefficient access, and building a custom tool for each possible task isn’t feasible. How do agents retrieve only the fields they need without runaway token costs, and access only what’s authorized? This session presents a standards-based architecture: a graph-based domain model describes what each API means, each agent has its own identity, policy is set on individual fields, and all access is audited. This presentation is brought to you by Apollo GraphQL, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Booking.com's playbook for cloud transformation at global scale
speaker: Mainu Kalita, Gary Krige, Valentina Muñoz
abstract: Booking.com connects millions of travelers to over 28 million listings across 43 languages. Their cloud transformation had to match that scale. In this session, hear how Booking.com dissolved organizational silos, broke through bottlenecks, and compressed timelines to fundamentally change how they build, operate, and innovate. You'll learn the architectural decisions, migration frameworks, and repeatable patterns that scaled cloud adoption across the enterprise, and how embedding AI from the ground up now powers next-generation customer experiences. Leave with a playbook for turning cloud transformation into continuous, cloud-fluent competitive advantage.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Boost Apache Spark performance and reduce costs with AWS Analytics
speaker: Kalyan chakravarthi Janaki, Suthan Dhas Phillips
abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore best practices for building high-performing, cost-efficient Spark applications using AWS analytics data processing services. We'll discuss the AWS performance-optimized runtime for Apache Spark—delivering up to 4.5x faster execution across Amazon EMR, Amazon Athena, and AWS Glue—meaning faster jobs and lower compute spend. Explore flexible deployment models—long-running clusters, on-demand elasticity with EMR Serverless, Kubernetes integration with EMR on EKS, and Graviton instances for up to 30% cost reduction. We'll also highlight how Glue's auto scaling, Flex execution class, and Iceberg integrations simplify pipelines while optimizing costs.

title: Boost Performance: Salesforce, Slack and AWS Headless Connectivity (sponsored by Salesforce)
speaker: Hrushikesh Gangur, Nehal Padia, Sameer Vuyyuru
abstract: Disconnected systems slow teams down. See how Agentforce, Slack and AgentCore Bedrock enable your Headless agentic strategy to unlock seamless collaboration and boost productivity across teams in real time. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Bootstrapping GitOps on Amazon EKS with Argo CD, ACK, and kro
speaker: Jesse Butler, Carlos Santana
abstract: Deploying an application to Kubernetes is straightforward. Provisioning its AWS resources, IAM roles, policies, and supporting infrastructure is more complex. Separate infrastructure and application toolchains create fragmented workflows and increase the risk of drift. In this session, we'll build a GitOps platform using EKS Capabilities, Argo CD, AWS Controllers for Kubernetes (ACK), and kro. See how kro packages Kubernetes workloads and their AWS dependencies behind a single, self-service custom resource. Learn how Argo CD continuously reconciles the entire application stack from one Git repository. Finally, watch several microservices deploy, with their cloud resources provisioned and continuously managed alongside their workloads.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Break free from on-premises NAS: Migrating to AWS
speaker: Eugene Kiliar, Saurav Majumder
abstract: Learn how Amazon FSx simplifies migrating on-premises workloads to the cloud while preserving the compatibility and performance your applications depend on. See real-world migration patterns for general-purpose file shares, high-performance applications, and mission-critical databases running on fully managed AWS storage that eliminates operational overhead. Discover how organizations are reducing costs while accelerating innovation.

title: Break free from Oracle licensing and modernize to Aurora PostgreSQL
speaker: Harpreet Virk, Tejpreet Reen
abstract: Oracle modernization promises freedom from licensing, lock-in, and operational overhead, yet projects stall on PL/SQL packages, schema quirks, and application logic that resists automated translation. In this workshop, you'll migrate a live Oracle workload to open-source Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL end-to-end and tackle the hardest schema conversion challenges that derail real-world projects. You'll work through PL/SQL translation, dependency resolution, and validation using AWS agentic AI.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano I

title: Breaking down batch inference with Ray Data on Amazon EKS
speaker: Andy Palmer, Vara Bonthu
abstract: Batch inference is more than running a model over a large dataset. In this interactive chalk talk, we build an end-to-end batch inference architecture on Amazon EKS one component at a time. We examine when to use Spark with Ray Serve and when Ray Data can unify preprocessing and inference. Along the way, we address data sharding, storage and data movement, GPU scheduling, autoscaling, batch sizing, checkpointing, retries, observability, security, isolation, and cost. Attendees will leave with a practical decision framework and a production architecture for operating reliable, scalable batch inference with Ray Data and the KubeRay Operator.

title: Breaking up with closed frontier models (sponsored by Modal)
speaker: Omkaar Kamath
abstract: Your agents work. Your frontier model bill hurts. Is it time to move off closed models? This talk walks through a practical decision flow: good eval practices, inference, post-training with RL. Drawing on Modal’s work helping companies migrate to open models, we show when an open model wins with no training at all, when reinforcement learning is worth it, how to choose between shared and dedicated inference, and levers to optimize serving models.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Break it to prove It: Fault-isolated architecture built to recover
speaker: Serafin Sedano Arenas, Shivani Sharma
abstract: Your recovery plan is only as good as the architecture backing it. This workshop presents single-Region and multi-Region resilience patterns built along fault isolation boundaries, where failure scope dictates which recovery mechanism to engage. Using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC), you architect for discrete blast radii, then validate each boundary through fault injection with AWS Fault Injection Service. Observability surfaces the failure, alarms classify scope, and automated recovery executes without intervention. The result: proof that your architecture recovers the way you designed it to. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Breathing Life into Game Worlds with Amazon Neptune & GraphRAG
speaker: Heungsu Ha, matthew nimmo, JP Velasco, Daniel Lee, Yeonho Lee
abstract: Static NPC dialogue can't unlock rich game worlds. This session shares a production pattern using Amazon Neptune, Bedrock GraphRAG, and the "Entity as Agent" approach. We will live-demo natural-language character relationship search, in-character AI dialogue, and in-game party composition recommendations.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Bridging clouds: Building global multicloud and hybrid networks on AWS
speaker: Mike Jager, Mike Bentzen
abstract: It's no secret, enterprises today run workloads across multiple clouds and on-premises data centers, but stitching together global connectivity without complexity remains a challenge. In this workshop, easily extend AWS connectivity to other clouds and on-premises environments using AWS Interconnect, AWS Direct Connect, and AWS Cloud WAN. Build a global multicloud network, then apply Amazon VPC Lattice to enforce security and handle overlapping IP address spaces without complex NAT configurations. Leave equipped to architect and deploy hybrid network architectures using modern application networking patterns. Bring your laptop.

title: Bringing better Amazon EC2 price performance to your pipeline with AWS Graviton
speaker: Diego Nieto Marin, Allan Henrique Homenhuck
abstract: Which workload should move to AWS Graviton first? And what actually changes in your pipeline? In this code talk, we answer both live. We profile an application portfolio to find strong Arm64 candidates, check dependency and library compatibility, and update a working CI/CD pipeline to build multi-architecture container images for x86 and Arm64, so you see exactly what changes and why. Then we deploy the workload and run a side-by-side load test to compare price performance. You'll leave with a repeatable workload-selection checklist and pipeline patterns you can apply to your own AWS Graviton adoption with minimal disruption.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Bring Oracle Databases to AWS Without Starting Over (sponsored by Oracle)
speaker: Vishal Patil, Muneer Mirza, Tushar Pandit
abstract: Organizations want the flexibility and innovation of AWS, but they cannot afford to rearchitect the mission-critical Oracle Database applications their businesses depend on. This session explains how Oracle AI Database@AWS provides a simpler path from on-premises Oracle Exadata and RAC environments to AWS with minimal to no database or application changes. Explore how customers can maintain full database capabilities and architectural compatibility, connect Oracle data to AWS applications with low latency, and unify data with AWS analytics, machine learning, and agentic AI services. We will also examine the operational value of familiar AWS tools, collaborative support, integrated security, and simplified purchasing. Attendees will learn how migration can reduce infrastructure constraints while creating a stronger foundation for innovation across Oracle and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Oracle, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Bring Your Own Ontology: Ground AWS Quick in Enterprise Knowledge with AWS Context
speaker: Tom Ron, Fatima Khakwani
abstract: Enterprise questions rarely have answers in a single document. Your business runs on connections — customers to products, teams to processes, risks to regulations — but vector search doesn't see any of that. In this chalk talk, we show how to ground AWS Quick in your enterprise context by integrating it with a knowledge graph built from your domain knowledge. We'll walk through how we built this pattern using GraphRAG for real customers and the results they achieved. Then we'll open the whiteboard — bring your toughest use case and we'll sketch your ontology live, showing how Quick would traverse it to deliver dramatically better answers.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan I

title: Bring your S3 data to your compute with S3 Files
speaker: Prabir Sekhri, Tom McDonald, Andrew Peng
abstract: S3 Files makes the data in your S3 buckets available to your compute as a high-performance file system, so any POSIX-based tool or workload can work with S3 objects in place. We will work through the two ways customers use it: giving established file-based applications direct access to data already in S3, and giving agents and other short-lived compute a durable, isolated file workspace they can leave behind. We'll whiteboard the decisions that matter: connecting compute to S3 Files across VPCs, accounts, and on-prem; tuning for price and performance; and securing access with IAM, POSIX permissions, and encryption.

title: Bring your tech debt: build a custom transformation that fixes it
speaker: Gokul Sarangaraju, Suresh Natarajan, Dinesh Balaaji Prabakaran, Shivansh Singh, Chetan Makvana
abstract: Every codebase has that annoying pattern: the deprecated internal library, the logging convention nobody follows, the framework migration that keeps getting deferred. In this small-group builder session, you'll tackle yours. Bring a real modernization problem from your own code and build a custom transformation in AWS Transform custom that solves it—defining the transformation in natural language, running it against a repository, and refining it until it holds up. No fixed curriculum and no slides: this is open-ended, hands-on time. Stuck for an idea? We'll have a few ready-made problems on hand. You must bring your laptop to participate.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Builders' Session

title: British Airways: Using agentic AI to modernise Java services at scale
speaker: Avi Nidumbur, Shane Routley, Gary Holland
abstract: How do you modernise hundreds of business services without manually re-engineering every one? British Airways is tackling this across 250+ services and 750 code repositories. Using AWS Transform custom, BA is migrating Java services from Amazon EC2 to a containerised, auto-scaling architecture on Amazon ECS Fargate and AWS Graviton. Its repeatable 20-step lifecycle combines deterministic automation and agentic AI with baseline testing, security scanning, and human review. The approach reduces manual effort, validates business logic, and frees engineering capacity for innovation. Discover how BA built its transformation engine and balances AI-driven change with robust engineering controls.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Build a backend before your coffee gets cold with AWS Blocks
speaker: Salih Güler
abstract: What if you could stand up a full application backend—database, auth, real-time messaging, file storage, even an AI agent—in TypeScript, running locally, with no AWS account required? AWS Blocks is an open-source framework where each "Block" bundles your app code, a local dev implementation, and production AWS infrastructure. Compose the Blocks you need, run one command to develop locally, then deploy the same code to AWS unchanged. Built for a world where AI agents write the code, Blocks ships steering files that guide agents to correct architecture from the start. In this lightning talk, see how fast full-stack can be.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Build a brand knowledge graph for retail and CPG AI
speaker: Martin Sakowski, John Mousa, Matt Barbieri, Liam Strye, Imran Dawood
abstract: Retail and CPG brands invest years building product expertise, from visual styling rules to ingredient pairing and formulation knowledge, that generic AI simply cannot replicate. In this builder session, you'll construct a Graph RAG solution that encodes brand-specific curatorial knowledge into an Amazon Neptune Analytics knowledge graph with multimodal vector embeddings. Using a CPG product catalog, you'll build graph schemas capturing formulation relationships, brand hierarchies, and cross-category pairing rules. Then see how vector similarity search combined with graph traversal enriches retrieval context before grounding Amazon Bedrock LLM responses. Leave with a working deployed architecture adaptable across retail and CPG.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Build a community portal with Connect Customer agentic voice in 60 minutes
speaker: Lawrence Gohar, Pramod Halapeti, Archit Malpure, Doug Gartner
abstract: City governments face rising citizen expectations with shrinking staff. In this builders' session, learn how to deploy a fully functional AI-powered community engagement portal using Amazon Connect Customer agentic voice in under one hour. See how to build a voice agent that answers common citizen inquiries about permits, utilities, parks, and city services, routes callers to the right department, and seamlessly escalates to live agents with full conversation context when needed. Walk away with a production-ready reference architecture that operations team can configure, deploy, and manage independently.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Build a container pipeline that blocks tampered images at the gate
speaker: Andrea Rossi, Andre Baumeier, Desiree Brunner, Jann Wild, Michael Tschannen
abstract: What if you want to prove cryptographically that every container in your environment is untampered and fully inventoried? In this builders' session, you build exactly that. Dive deep into the AWS Signer cryptographic model: KMS-backed keys, ECDSA P-256, COSE_Sign1 envelopes, and notation trust policies. Implement ECR managed signing, generate SBOMs with Amazon Inspector, slim images to reduce attack surface, and enforce admission on EKS with Kyverno. Then stress test it with attack simulations against the pipeline you just built.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Build a cost optimization playbook for your AI workload
speaker: Yaakov Tayeb, Jamie Brearton, Shivi Bhatia, Eitan Sela, Shreeya Sharma
abstract: Learn how to cut the cost of your AI workloads without sacrificing quality. In this builders session, you work through a curated set of representative prompts and apply three high-impact levers: prompt caching, Intelligent Prompt Routing, and right-sizing model choice. You measure token cost before and after each change, so you see exactly which levers move the needle and which do not. You're welcome to bring a prompt from your own workload to test alongside the guided examples. Leave with a repeatable cost optimization playbook and the evidence to support each decision.

title: Build a cost-optimized multi-agent system on Amazon EC2 CPUs and GPU
speaker: Leo Simberg, Efren Mercado
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, you build a production-ready multi-agent system that splits workloads between CPU and GPU EC2 instances — the best of both worlds. Starting with an autonomous customer-support pipeline, you deploy reasoning agents on GPU and orchestration, tool-calling, and retrieval agents on CPUs. You profile each stage, measure latency and cost per agent call, and implement routing policies that dynamically assign tasks to the optimal compute tier. By the end, you have a hybrid deployment with a live cost dashboard showing 30–45% savings vs. GPU-only baselines.

speaker: Kiran Kuppa, Rodney Bozo, Hrushikesh Shah, Mike Kuznetsov, Sassan Hajrasooliha
abstract: You're planning a data center exit and need leadership to say yes. That means persuasive data, realistic cost estimates, and a proposal that makes financial sense. In this builders' session, you'll use AWS Transform's agentic AI capabilities paired with Discovery Agent data to assess your existing environment, generate cost estimates, and build a compelling business case for migration. You'll work through the end-to-end workflow from discovery and analysis to financial modeling, and leave ready to present a data-driven migration proposal to your stakeholders.

title: Build a digital asset tokenization issuance solution
speaker: Arvind Raghu, David-Paul Dornseifer, Everton Fraga, Joshua Smith, Simon Goldberg
abstract: The emergence of digital assets and stablecoins requires bridging traditional message-based finance protocols such as SWIFT and ISO 20022 to programmable settlement rails while preserving institutional security, auditability, and governance. In this session, learn how to build a production-ready end-to-end hybrid settlement architecture on AWS that ingests financial messages, normalizes them into canonical settlement instructions, and executes tokenized asset transfers on-chain. Explore hardware-backed signing with AWS KMS, on-chain signer governance, and three settlement patterns: issuance, redemption, and transfer, with full audit trails, idempotent transaction handling, and EIP-712 typed signing. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Build a fully managed data lake with Amazon S3 Tables
speaker: Sumaja Kapa, Ran Pergamin
abstract: Data lakes have evolved from raw Parquet files with Hive-style partitioning to fully managed Apache Iceberg tables. In this hands-on workshop, you'll understand that evolution, then build a working analytics data lake with Amazon S3 Tables in under two hours. You'll create an S3 table bucket, ingest real-world data, migrate data into the bucket, and query it with Amazon Athena. You'll also learn how to connect third-party tools like DuckDB for interactive exploration. Along the way we’ll cover the benefits of fully managed Iceberg tables and when to use Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation for open data architectures.

title: Build a fully managed open source observability stack on AWS
speaker: Anirudha Jadhav, Lucas Vieira
abstract: You want open standards without the operational burden of self-managing backends. In this code talk, we live-code a complete open source observability architecture: instrument a service with OpenTelemetry (auto and manual), configure the OTel Collector pipeline, and route metrics to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Walk through each integration decision from SDK selection to collector topology, and leave with a working, production-ready stack built entirely on open source standards with zero infrastructure to manage.

title: Build a fully managed open source observability stack on AWS
speaker: Anirudha Jadhav, Lucas Vieira
abstract: You want open standards without the operational burden of self-managing backends. In this code talk, we live-code a complete open source observability architecture: instrument a service with OpenTelemetry (auto and manual), configure the OTel Collector pipeline, and route metrics to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Walk through each integration decision from SDK selection to collector topology, and leave with a working, production-ready stack built entirely on open source standards with zero infrastructure to manage.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Build agentic AI applications with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS
speaker: David Greenshtein, Nathan Yee
abstract: Transform your organization's data landscape and eliminate silos in this hands-on workshop with the open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Unify data management and design data interoperability across data lakes, data warehouses, and federated data sources. Through practical exercises, discover how to create a single source of truth while maintaining security and governance across your entire data estate. You'll implement real-time analytics, optimize query performance, and design scalable architectures. Perfect for data engineers, ML practitioners, and solution architects looking to modernize their data infrastructure for building agentic AI applications.

title: Build Agentic AI That Understands Your Business with SAP and AWS (sponsored by SAP)
speaker: Haridas Nair, Ted Way
abstract: Enterprise AI falls short when agents lack live business context. See how SAP's Business AI Platform and AWS solve this: Joule Studio enables developers and business users to build and deploy custom AI agents grounded in SAP's process knowledge, while bidirectional, zero-copy integration between SAP Business Data Cloud and Amazon Athena gives AWS services secure access to trusted SAP data. Watch a live demo of building agents that reason with business context, collaborate across SAP and AWS, and act across enterprise processes with governance.​ This presentation is brought to you by SAP, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Build agentic automations for business processes with AWS Quick
speaker: Reagan Rosario, Zuhayr Raghib
abstract: In this session, learn how to build an enterprise-grade automation using AWS Quick Automate. Through a financial services example, explore how specialized AI agents work together to handle complex interactions across web pages and business applications. You'll create a production-ready automation featuring custom agents that leverage knowledge and tools to transform a merchant onboarding process. Using Quick Automate's chat based authoring and visual studio, you'll configure a workflow with multiple agents, integrate with multiple tools, test and debug the workflow, and then deploy it using robust enterprise controls. Walk away knowing how to develop agentic automations for real-world use cases.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano I

title: Build agentic fraud detection with a transaction foundation model
speaker: Omer Dawelbeit, Sudhir Kalidindi
abstract: Organized fraud rings exploit the gaps between siloed detection systems, making them invisible to traditional rules-based approaches. In this workshop, you’ll construct a fraud detection optimization system that tackles them at scale. Load 24M transactions into Apache Iceberg, build a knowledge graph with Amazon Neptune to reveal hidden fraud networks, and train an ensemble combining transaction foundation model embeddings with graph embeddings for measurable score improvement. Then deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that autonomously investigates patterns, expands fraud rings, and creates validated detection rules. Leave with an end-to-end working system you can replicate in your own environment.

title: Build agentic GraphRAG apps with Amazon Neptune
speaker: Melissa Kwok, Hal Cooper, Jayaraman Sampath, Kelvin Lawrence, Dustin Brown
abstract: GraphRAG combines knowledge graphs with RAG to produce explainable responses grounded in semantic relationships between concepts, entities, and underlying content. Agentic GraphRAG takes this further, allowing agents to autonomously decide which GraphRAG tools to use to achieve information goals. In this session, build an agentic GraphRAG application using the open source AWS GraphRAG Toolkit. You will transform unstructured and semi-structured data into a catalog of domain-specific GraphRAG tools to enable agents to answer multi-faceted questions that require context from multiple distinct knowledge sources to provide a contextually complete answer. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
speaker: Shayon Sanyal, Radwan Deeb, Rinisha Marar, Sudhir Amin, Kanishka Chaturvedi
abstract: What if your agent's most convincing answer rests on the wrong evidence? Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Aurora PostgreSQL across more than 500,000 product listings in three connected hands-on labs. Debug SQL combining full-text search, pg_trgm fuzzy matching, and pgvector semantic search under shared filters. Repair reciprocal rank fusion, inspect Amazon Bedrock reranking, and compare retrieval settings against judged queries. Then build a Strands agent, connect its retrieval tools through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, and deploy it to AgentCore Runtime. Trace its searches to cited specifications and reviews, and test what happens when requirements change. Leave with reusable retrieval SQL and working agent code.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Build agentic observability workflows with AI tools from AWS Marketplace
speaker: George Maroulakos, Tuan Vo
abstract: In this workshop, discover how to create an AI agent that takes a single user prompt, finds anomalies using observability and monitoring tools, and takes proper actions on your behalf. Using solutions available in AWS Marketplace, you can incorporate leading generative AI models into your agentic AI workflows while maintaining privacy leveraging stands agents. Deploy third-party products in your AWS account, ensuring that prompts, data, and model responses stay within the boundaries of your account and are not shared with model providers. This is important for business use cases where competitive or confidential information may be used with models. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build agentic payment investigators on Aurora PostgreSQL & AgentCore
speaker: Aditya Samant, Vlad Vlasceanu
abstract: Payment dispute resolution and ledger reconciliation require agents that reason over transactional history, retrieve precedent with precision, and write through idempotent workflows. In this session, learn how to build two production-grade payment agents on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: a dispute investigator that classifies cardholder disputes and drafts representment narratives, and a reconciliation agent that resolves breaks between internal ledgers and bank statements. Both share one investigator pattern: an agent reasoning over structured records, retrieving precedent with pgvector, and writing through an idempotent ledger. Go deep on SERIALIZABLE state machines, hybrid retrieval that knows when a trigram index beats an embedding, confidence-scored human-in-the-loop routing, and trace-to-row observability with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

title: Build Agentic Video Streaming Observability Using Kiro and Bedrock
speaker: Osmar Bento Junior, Dirk Boekee, Adrian Ramos, Devendra Sharma, Abhimanyu Varshney
abstract: Media operations teams struggle to correlate issues across complex live streaming pipelines. In this hands-on session, build an agentic video observability and analytics application using Kiro and Amazon Bedrock that monitors the entire live streaming chain using AWS Elemental MediaConnect, MediaLive, MediaPackage, MediaTailor and Amazon CloudFront. Deploy AI agents using Strands Agents SDK and MCP servers to ingest, visualize, and investigate end-to-end QoE/QoS analytics across three layers: origin health, CDN performance, and client-side CMCD telemetry. Learn how to create a unified dashboard and natural language interface for streaming quality investigation across every pipeline stage.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Build agents on OSS models with blazing fast inference on SageMaker AI
speaker: Dan Ferguson, Piyush Daftary
abstract: Stop paying frontier-model prices for agentic workloads. In this hands-on session, build production-ready AI agents powered by open-source models like Qwen3 and Gemma4 running entirely on Amazon SageMaker AI. You'll deploy models with optimized serving, connect them to multi-turn tool-use workflows through OpenAI-compatible APIs, and enable real-time bi-directional streaming for responsive agent interactions. Leave with a working cost-optimized agent stack you fully control — fast inference, zero vendor lock-in, and patterns for scaling agentic workloads on your own terms.

title: Build agents that take orders like your best sales reps, with PepsiCo
speaker: Bharathi Srinivasan, Ganapathi Krishnamoorthi, Muralidhar Ambekar
abstract: Your best sales reps understand what a customer means, remember the conversation, check the right systems, and close the order in one exchange. This session shows how to build conversational agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that work the same way: stateful sessions on runtime, memory for multi-turn context, enterprise APIs as tools, and deterministic controls that keep the agent accurate and on task. PepsiCo shares how it built a WhatsApp ordering agent for roughly one million retailers in India, where a shopkeeper can order by text, voice note, or a photo of a handwritten list in their own language.

title: Build a governed semantic layer with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and MCP
speaker: Itziar Molina Fernandez, Andrea Perez Isla, Paula Iglesias Ahualli, Ignacio Fernandez Gonzalez, Angel Emmanuel Hernandez Cebrian
abstract: Financial services organizations struggle with inconsistent metric definitions, AI hallucination risks, and analyst bottlenecks. In this session, you’ll build a governed semantic layer with three key pillars (accuracy, consistency, and explainability) essential for agents to operate securely at scale. You’ll then connect to AI agents powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that query, interpret, and act on financial data via MCP, enabling natural language access to complex financial metrics. Your agents reason rather than guess, with full auditability for financial regulators. Leave with a production-ready architecture pattern that goes beyond "chat with your data" demos.

title: Build a grounded AI support assistant on Amazon OpenSearch Service
speaker: Arun Lakshmanan, Gene Alpert
abstract: You want to build an AI assistant: where do you even start? A model alone is not the answer. The hard part is grounding it in your own data so it gives real answers, remembers the conversation, and holds up as that data grows, and grounding is a search problem. In this hands-on workshop, you build a customer support assistant grounded in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Starting from a pre-deployed base, you create an OpenSearch Serverless collection, add hybrid search for relevance, and add agentic memory so your assistant retains context across the conversation. You connect your tools and data with the OpenSearch MCP server, the AWS Knowledge MCP, and the AWS MCP. You leave with working code, an architecture that scales itself, and a clear path from a blank page to an assistant that answers from real data.

title: Build AI agents on Amazon S3 Files
speaker: Beerinder Mann, Sebastien Perreault, Ananta Khanal, Samuel Ouvrard, Matt Boyd
abstract: S3 Files is the first cloud object store with fully-featured, high-performance file system access to your data. In this hands-on session, you'll create an S3 file system, attach it to an Amazon EKS cluster, and build an AI agent that loads model weights and processes data directly from S3 via standard file I/O. No SDK rewrites, no data duplication, just native POSIX access. You'll fine-tune synchronization behavior between S3 and the file system, controlling how data flows between object and file interfaces. Finally, you'll configure cross-Region replication to establish a disaster recovery strategy for your production workloads.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Build AI agents to operate desktop and mainframe apps on WorkSpaces
speaker: Stephen Stetler, Dave Jaskie
abstract: You rely on desktop and mainframe applications for critical workflows, but these interfaces remain inaccessible to AI agents. Your Robotic Process Automation efforts have struggled to keep pace as applications and configurations constantly change. Amazon WorkSpaces lets AI agents securely operate the same desktop and mainframe applications your employees use, without any application modernization. WorkSpaces supports Model Context Protocol (MCP), so it works with any agent framework. In this workshop, connect to a pre-provisioned WorkSpace, build a custom agent, run agents that complete desktop workflows, and monitor agent sessions with CloudWatch and CloudTrail. Bring laptop to participate.

title: Build AI photo discovery with Amazon S3 Vectors
speaker: Bimal Gajjar, Arik Porat, RK Vyas, Krutarth Doshi, Saket Jangle
abstract: Learn how S3 Vectors turns millions of untagged images into a semantically searchable collection without standing up a separate vector database. In this builders' session, you will generate multi-modal embeddings from photo assets, store and index them in S3 Vectors with metadata predicates for filtered search, and wire an AI agent that discovers images using natural language queries. You will explore index configuration, batch ingestion throughput, and cost patterns at scale. You will leave with a working prototype and production patterns for building vector-native search directly on S3.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Build AI-Powered Analytics with Conversational BI on AWS Quick
speaker: Neeraj Kumar, salim khan
abstract: Construct a complete AI-powered analytics pipeline, from data ingestion to conversational consumption. Use AWS Quick's Data Catalog to discover data, query it live without moving it into SPICE, then enrich and import metadata with semantics inherited to build natural-language Q&A. In this hands-on workshop, you start with seven raw banking tables: no catalog, no definitions. An agent inspects the data and builds the catalog for you. You ask questions in plain English and get answers. An agent generates a dashboard showing which top customers are slipping. Another agent, aware of the bank's compliance rules, checks every offer before it ships. Then you automate the full response as a Quick Flow and wrap it in a custom app your team can use. You leave with a working banking command center that agents built, and that you can rebuild in your own account using conversational analytics.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano IV

title: Build AI-Powered Contact Center Agents with Amazon Connect
speaker: Ted Trentler
abstract: Customer-facing AI Agents can resolve issues end-to-end. In this bootcamp, build two complementary AI agents on Amazon Connect AI Customer. First, create an agent-assistance copilot that watches live chats and surfaces real-time knowledge base answers and customer data lookups to human agents. Then build a self-service AI agent that handles routine customer requests autonomously, using MCP tools for Cases and Customer Profiles, and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context when a human is needed.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom I

title: Build a KMS key lifecycle dashboard with usage and cost insights
speaker: Alex Goff, Jeremy Stieglitz, Tobias Nickl, Svenja Moehring, Jonas Buecker
abstract: Determining which KMS keys are actively in use and which can be safely retired has historically required manual CloudTrail log analysis, and meanwhile, unused keys accumulate as operational clutter. In this hands-on builders session, you'll use the GetKeyLastUsage API to identify which keys are protecting production workloads and which are candidates for retirement. You'll configure policy conditions that prevent accidental deletion of active keys, and build a Amazon Quick dashboard that surfaces usage and cost optimization opportunities across accounts. You leave with a working multi-account key lifecycle solution you can recreate in your organization.

title: Build a knowledge graph-based agent guardrail with Amazon Neptune
speaker: Melissa Kwok, Varma Gottumukkala, Taylor Riggan, Don Simpson, Chun Schiros
abstract: AI agents assert relationships such as compatible products, cleared counterparties, or approved suppliers, derived from LLM reasoning rather than verified data. When these assertions are wrong, downstream business decisions fail. In this session, explore how to implement Amazon Neptune as a post-generation verification layer. Before the agent responds, a graph traversal confirms or contradicts the assertion against a live knowledge graph. Learn how to build the verification tool, the override pattern when Neptune contradicts the model, and the graph data model for storing authoritative relationship data that constrains agent behavior. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build a Live App in Under 20 Minutes, Then See How It Actually Worked (sponsored by MongoDB)
speaker: Nina Lopatina, Justin LaBreck
abstract: Most teams know what they want to build long before they have something they can show someone. This workshop gets you there fast, then shows you what's behind that build. First, you'll build a real app. Using MongoDB Build Lab from your laptop, turn an idea (a search tool, an AI assistant, a dashboard, anything) into a working, deployed app backed by MongoDB Atlas. No repo setup, no infrastructure work. You'll touch the full stack, generation, database, and deployment, and walk away with a functional prototype. Then we open up the system behind it: planning, safety checks, a durable job queue, containerized workers on Amazon EC2, automated testing, targeted repairs, and deployment. We'll unpack what makes it repeatable, like isolating generated code, keeping credentials at trusted boundaries, and preserving state across restarts with Atlas. A MongoDB Build Lab workshop, with AWS. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Build a multi-agent system for hyper-personalized customer journeys
speaker: Islam Elhamaky, Sachin Kulkarni
abstract: Delivering personalized experiences across complex customer journeys requires agents that understand intent, maintain context, and coordinate across systems. In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI personal banker using a home buying scenario as the example. Your agents extract intent from natural conversation, build dynamic customer profiles, and orchestrate workflows across internal banking systems and external ecosystem APIs. Implement multi-agent patterns for shared memory, readiness signals, and coordinated decisioning using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents Framework, and MCP. Walk away with reusable orchestration patterns you can apply to any personalized customer experience.

title: Build a multi-Region, active-active rewards app with Aurora DSQL
speaker: Eric Kraemer, Dan Blaner
abstract: In this session, get hands-on experience with Amazon Aurora DSQL, a serverless distributed SQL database that delivers active-active high availability. Learn how to build a retail rewards points application with active-active resiliency across multiple Availability Zones and two Regions. Explore how ACID transactions and active-active replication work in Aurora DSQL. Discover best practices for data model and application design and more. Bring a laptop to participate.

title: Build an Agentic AI Marketing Engine Powered by Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Jeremy Bartosiewicz, Sanhawat Taongern, Hari Radhakrishnan, Vanessa Ji, Celine Zhu
abstract: In this hands-on builder session, construct a multi-agent AI system that automates campaign planning, activation, and optimization. Build four specialized agents on Amazon Bedrock including a planner, media buyer, analyst, and creative generator that turns campaign parameters into audience targeting, budget allocation, performance forecasts, and localized creative grounded in your brand guidelines and historical data. Activate campaigns through Amazon Ads DSP, then add an optimizer agent with human-in-the-loop approvals that reallocates budget across channels as performance shifts. You'll build a running multi-agent workflow and take away the Bedrock agent definitions to adapt for your own campaigns.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Build an agentic AI system on Amazon EKS with CPU-only inference
speaker: Christian Melendez, Oussama Kandakji
abstract: In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI system on Amazon EKS with EKS Auto Mode that serves every model on CPU instances. Deploy four inference components: a fine-tuned intent router and a fine-tuned embedding model for vector search (both ONNX, trained on CPU), a cross-encoder re-ranker for retrieval quality, and a quantized generative analyst served with llama.cpp and grounded by RAG context from OpenSearch. Amazon Bedrock generates the synthetic training data, judges every answer through a faithfulness gate, and answers the edge cases the small models cannot. You'll finish by running the control test that puts a frontier LLM in the same seat, so you know whether the small model is good enough on your workload. By the end, you'll have a working multi-agent system on standard compute, using open-source tooling you can adapt.

title: Build an agentic context layer with ontologies on Amazon Neptune
speaker: Taylor Riggan, Jeff Bascle
abstract: Most knowledge graphs answer questions but never close the loop with operational systems. In this session, explore how to build an ontology-driven context layer that transforms a knowledge graph into an active control plane for AI agents. The session covers RDF ontology design, SHACL constraint validation, synchronization patterns, agent integration, and write-back mechanisms that propagate decisions to systems of record. Hear how Lockheed Martin applied these patterns in production, enabling agents to reason across supply chain, manufacturing, and engineering domains. Leave with a concrete architectural blueprint and lessons learned from building context layers that act while increasing your trust.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Build an Agentic Enterprise to Enable Autonomous Action (sponsored by Snowflake)
speaker: John Pulikkottil, Santiago Giraldo
abstract: Building an agentic enterprise empowers organizations to automate complex work and drive measurable business outcomes. True transformation happens when autonomous AI operates across systems using trusted data, flexible models, connected applications, and a unified, agentic control plane. By bringing knowledge workers and technical builders into a shared agentic environment, teams move faster without sacrificing governance. Learn how the Snowflake AI Data Cloud unifies enterprise context, model choice, and app connections into a single architecture. Discover how to turn enterprise data into reliable, autonomous action and long-term competitive advantage in your AWS cloud environment. This presentation is brought to you by Snowflake, an AWS Partner.

title: Build an AI navigator that makes every frontline worker an expert
speaker: Paul Mietz Egli, vtbloise Bloise, Vanitha Sugumaran, Tim Ness, Krishna Kadiyala
abstract: A member is on the line, a regulation changed last week, and the answer isn't in any manual yet. Frontline staff don't need a search box — they need a guide that surfaces the next right action in the moment. In this builder session, build a self-improving frontline navigator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness: ground it in your policies with a Managed Knowledge Base, keep it current with live rule changes via AgentCore Web Search, and close the loop with AgentCore Optimization so it measurably improves from every real interaction. Unlike a static knowledge base, this agent recommends actions, adapts as policies shift, and learns on the job. Whether you serve members, patients, or beneficiaries, leave with a deployed self-improving navigator and the architecture behind it.

speaker: Aram Koukia, Azat Penjiyev, Siddhesh Chavan, Daimon Songer, Soumyajit Das

In this builders' session, you'll construct a multi-agent system that analyzes your AWS Backup environment across four dimensions: coverage gaps, ransomware resilience scoring, vault security, and cost optimization. You'll build an MCP server exposing backup APIs as agent tools, wire specialist subagents into an orchestration graph, and run a remediation agent with human-in-the-loop approval on AWS Bedrock AgentCore Harness. The system runs in your own environment after the session.

title: Build an AI-powered student services with Connect Customer
speaker: Varun Pole, Ekta Vasa
abstract: Education institutions field thousands of student inquiries each semester across enrollment, financial aid, and academic support. In this chalk talk, we architect agentic AI-powered student services using Amazon Connect Customer. You’ll configure a knowledge base with university content and connect it to Connect Customer for real-time AI-generated recommendations during live calls, then deploy a self-service experience that resolves common inquiries over voice and chat. We'll cover when to use deterministic intent handling vs. agentic reasoning, MCP tool integration with student systems, and guardrails for FERPA compliance. By the end, you'll have a working prototype that boosts advisor productivity and reduces student wait times.

title: Build an AI testing safety net before you modernize
speaker: Peter Giuliano, Jean-Francois Landreau
abstract: Modernizing applications is risky without comprehensive test coverage, and most apps that need modernization don't have it. In this workshop, you'll build an AI-powered testing safety net before touching a line of production code. Starting with a deployed insurance application, you'll use Kiro to generate spec-driven tests from source code and Nova Act to discover UI tests through autonomous exploration. Then you'll apply AWS Transform to modernize the codebase and re-run your AI-generated test suite to prove functional equivalence. You'll leave knowing how to de-risk modernization by letting GenAI build your safety net first. Laptop required.

title: Build and Optimize AI Pipelines with Ray on SageMaker HyperPod
speaker: Ioan CATANA, Varun Rajan, Chakravarthy Nagarajan, Tomonori Shimomura, Anoop Saha, Mijanur Palash
abstract: Ray provides a unified Python framework for petabyte-scale data processing, large-model training, and low-latency inference. In this hands-on workshop, you will use Ray on SageMaker HyperPod to a model and set up endpoints. Create a Ray cluster from SageMaker Studio and attach a JupyterLab notebook to build the pipeline from Ray train to Ray Serve. Simulate a node failure and watch training auto-resume in seconds. Experience HyperPod's native Ray integration with embedded observability, tiered checkpointing, hung-job detection, and managed KV cache for inference. You leave with a working endpoint and patterns you can apply to your own workloads.

title: Build and optimize data transfers with AWS DataSync Enhanced mode
speaker: Harshi Surampalli, Phani Surampalli, Shaguna Awasthi, Santhosh Arunuri, Mathieu Riverin
abstract: When you're moving petabytes from on-premises file servers and multicloud object stores into AWS, transfer speed and operational visibility are equally critical. In this builders session, you'll configure AWS DataSync Enhanced mode to move data from diverse source environments into AWS using its parallel pipeline for high-throughput transfers. Enhanced mode generates detailed task reports and transfer logs as it works. You'll then use Amazon Bedrock to analyze that data, surfacing performance bottlenecks and generating optimization recommendations. Walk away with reusable patterns for fast data movement and AI-powered transfer visibility.

Whether you're accelerating decision-making, automating operational workflows, or putting insights directly in the hands of end users, this session shows how Quick Apps collapses the gap between having an idea and shipping a solution. Bring your laptop and be ready to build.
