title: Build and test HA/DR architectures for Microsoft workloads on AWS
speaker: Sivasekar Elumalai, Sagal Farah, Kevin Sookhan, Chase Lindeman, Luciano Bernardes
abstract: Can your Windows Server applications and SQL Server databases survive a system outage? In this builders' session, you'll find out by building and testing HA/DR architectures against simulated failures. Get hands-on experience with Elastic Disaster Recovery and Systems Manager to construct resilient infrastructure and recovery automation. Measure RTO and RPO in real time as you purposely break production workloads. Explore additional topics like RDS, S3, Elastic Beanstalk, and AWS Managed AD. You'll leave with a validated resiliency blueprint and the confidence to protect your most critical Microsoft workloads.

title: Build a per-tenant observability stack for Agentic SaaS
speaker: Rocket ., Matt Tichenor, Venkatavaradhan Viswanathan, Yoginder Sethi, Ulli Hinze
abstract: Multi-tenant ISVs need per-tenant observability that traditional dashboards can't deliver — aggregated metrics hide the tenant causing the problem, and shared traces don't tell you whose agent misbehaved. In this session, build a per-tenant observability stack for agents. You'll instrument agent invocations with tenant-aware traces and session replay, build tenant-scoped dashboards that surface noisy neighbors and latency outliers, and configure alerting that fires on per-tenant thresholds rather than aggregate signals. By the end, you'll have an observability setup that scales with your tenant count without a separate data pipeline — and patterns to extend it as your agent architecture grows.

title: Build a Physical AI Model Factory on SageMaker HyperPod
speaker: Nathan Arnold, Nicolas Jourdan
abstract: Physical AI teams in robotics and autonomous vehicles can't collect enough real data for the rare edge cases that dominate risk. The answer is a continuous data flywheel: generate synthetic scenarios, post-train policies, evaluate, repeat. Running that at scale is GPU-hungry and orchestration-heavy. This chalk talk shows how to run the full Physical AI model factory on SageMaker HyperPod with EKS: provision heterogeneous GPU pools, schedule multi-stage jobs, and leverage auto-healing infrastructure.

title: Build a production multi-Agent Systems with Strands
speaker: Nicholas Clegg, Elizabeth Fuentes Leone, Albert Zhao, Joy Chakraborty, Owen Kaplan
abstract: Build, deploy, and scale agents with re-usable multi-agent patterns in Strands Agents. You will create an agentic system that is capable of decomposing complex tasks and delegating sub-tasks to specialized worker agents. These agents will manage shared state and memory across boundaries, gracefully handle failures, and enforce quality guardrails. Subsequently, these agents will be deployed to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for production scaling and observability, featuring harness capabilities for checkpointing and long-running multi-agent workflow capabilities. Upon completion, you will be equipped with reusable design patterns and industry best practices to construct production-grade multi-agent systems utilizing the Strands Agent SDK.

abstract: Real applications have frontends, APIs, workers, and databases that all need to communicate reliably. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tier containerized architecture on Amazon ECS from scratch. Configure service-to-service networking with Service Connect, implement per-tier autoscaling policies, deploy updates with automated rollback, and observe your application using CloudWatch Container Insights. Walk away with a working architecture you can use as a reference for your own workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build a real-time data lakehouse with CDC streams on S3 Tables
speaker: Lee Kear
abstract: Learn how to build a real-time transactional data lakehouse using Amazon S3 Tables with Apache Iceberg. In this hands-on session, you will ingest CDC streams from Amazon MSK into a medallion architecture, transform batch and streaming data into business-ready gold layer tables with Amazon SageMaker, and query the results through Amazon Quick. You'll configure S3 Tables maintenance policies per layer and compare binpack, sort, and z-order compaction strategies to optimize query performance. You will leave with production patterns for continuous ingestion, incremental processing, and low-latency analytics at scale.

speaker: Steve Drew, Ashley Chen, Andrew Powell, Pranjal Gururani, Daniel Wirjo
abstract: A SaaS control plane - tenant onboarding, billing, configuration management, agent provisioning is the most repeatable software every software vendor builds from scratch. In this builder's session, use Kiro specs to define the control plane requirements and let Kiro implement the scaffolding, then wire multi-tenant agent capabilities using Strands' open-source constructs. You'll build a working onboarding flow, a tenant configuration store, and a simple agent provisioning endpoint - all from a spec, not from scratch. Leave with a reusable starting point for your own control plane and a pattern for using Kiro and Strands together to accelerate platform development.

title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
speaker: Alin Scurtu, Leonardo Azize, Pedro Rosinholi, Prabhu G, PRAVEEN HOSUR NARAYANA GUPTA
abstract: Teams deploying AI agents inherit two exposures. Any client reaching the endpoint can invoke the agent, and it can reach any destination its tools name. In this builders' session, learn to close both gaps with AWS managed controls. Put AWS WAF Bot Control in front of your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to classify callers and admit only the classes you choose, then route the agent through AWS Network Firewall and use domain category filtering to decide which destination categories it may reach. Run each control in count or alert mode, then enforce it and verify the allowed and the refused path. Leave with a two-boundary pattern you can apply to your own agent deployments.

title: Build a team of agents: From incident diagnosis to safe remediation
speaker: George Agiasoglou, Hisyam Jukifli
abstract: Most AI agents stop at the root cause report, leaving engineers to act under pressure. In this workshop, build three cooperating agents on a pre-provisioned workload using Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon Application Recovery Controller. A live app throws 4XX errors and a troubleshooting agent runs root cause analysis. Then build a remediation agent to apply the fix. When 5XX errors signal an Availability Zone impairment, you'll extend the remediation agent to consult a resilience agent before acting. Leave with a working reference implementation you can adapt to your financial services or enterprise environment.

title: Build at scale real-time ingestion pipelines for Apache Iceberg tables
speaker: Pratik Patel, Umesh Chaudhari
abstract: Landing streaming data into Apache Iceberg at scale is a complex undertaking. In this chalk talk, we dissect three reference architectures for real-time ingestion into Iceberg tables on Amazon S3 Tables: zero-code delivery with streaming tables for Amazon MSK and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, in-stream enrichment with Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, and change data capture from operational databases with Apache Flink CDC and zero-ETL integrations. Learn which architecture fits your latency and cost requirements, how to keep Iceberg tables query-ready under continuous writes, and how these pipelines feed downstream analytics and AI workloads.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan I

title: Build a unified student insight platform on AWS Quick
speaker: Jumana Nagaria, Akash Doshi, Mohamed Salah, Mohammed Reda Mohammed Reda, Abdilmajide Ali
abstract: Advisors triaging at-risk students, deans auditing course difficulty, executives tracking retention: every university role needs student-success insights, but the tools they rely on today are disconnected, static, and slow to surface risk before it becomes attrition. In this builders’ session, learn how to use AWS Quick to understand your institutional data and deliver explainable, persona-aware insights through one architecture. See how advisors can identify at risk students with cited data, trigger early intervention when a student’s risk score changes, and generate executive ready reports that connect student outcomes to optimized resource allocation and institutional strategy.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Build Autonomous Agents and Run AI-Powered AppSec on Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
speaker: Nick McCarthy, Marco Muttoni, Sunil Bemarkar
abstract: Go hands-on with OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock across two builder tracks. First, stand up a fully managed autonomous agent with Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents: define instructions and tools, wire action groups for API access, and ground responses in your own data through knowledge bases. Then shift to code security, using OpenAI's Codex Security Plugin to review a real vulnerable app by running scans, threat modeling, triaging findings, and fixing one with verified remediation. Throughout, inference runs securely on Bedrock under your account's controls. You'll leave with repeatable blueprints for building agentic OpenAI applications and for AI-assisted application security on AWS. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed. Labs are 30-60 min. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Innovation Labs

title: Build a Video Semantic Layer for AI Agents on AWS
speaker: Amit Kalawat, James Wu
abstract: An AI agent’s accuracy depends on the context it can find. Enterprises have made video understandable to people with transcripts, tags, and summaries built for human search. Agents need context they can retrieve, connect, and reason over. In this advanced, hands-on workshop, you will build a video semantic layer for agents step by step, from multimodal embeddings to hybrid search to a knowledge graph, using Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You will leave with a working agent that queries, enriches, and continuously improves its understanding of video, plus a blueprint for grounding agents in trustworthy context from unstructured data.

title: Build a well-governed natural language-to-SQL agentic solution for Amazon Redshift
speaker: Andre Hass, David Pasha, Vinayaka Gangadhar, Ivan Fernandez Perea, Ajay Kumar Govindaram
abstract: The Amazon Redshift MCP Server enables AI agents to generate and execute SQL using natural language, but going from demo to production means answering critical security questions on preventing query hallucination, prompt injection, unbounded scans, and inadvertent PII exposure by the LLM. In this session, you will build a well-governed text-to-SQL agentic solution for Amazon Redshift with security gates that validate every AI-generated query before execution including schema allow-listing to constraining LLM context, authorized tables, columns and rows, SQL AST validation and enforced read-only access.

title: Build better agent retrieval with OpenSearch Service
speaker: Mikhail Vaynshteyn, Muthu Pitchaimani
abstract: Your AI agents and assistants are only as good as the answers they retrieve. Out-of-the-box frameworks get you started, but production-ready AI applications demand more from their search layer including higher relevance on complex queries, persistent memory across sessions, and tools the model can invoke reliably. Amazon OpenSearch Service delivers these capabilities natively. In this chalk talk, we dig into how to make OpenSearch Service the backbone of your AI agents and assistants, covering hybrid retrieval for better accuracy, MCP-based access to your data, and built-in conversation and long-term memory so your applications maintain context across interactions. Bring your architecture questions. Whether you're optimizing retrieval accuracy, adding persistent context, or connecting your agent to search via MCP, we work through it together and leave you with patterns you can apply.

title: Build Bidstream Agents and Simulate Auction with AgentCore
speaker: Zelle Steyn, Negin Rouhanizadeh
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, build Agentic Real-Time Framework (ARTF)-compliant agents that operate inside the bidstream, using the Agents for Advertising framework on Amazon Bedrock. You'll construct an agent container that accepts bid requests and returns pricing decisions to the ARTF specification, then orchestrate a multi-agent pipeline that simulates adversarial auction scenarios and scores your bidding strategy against the outcomes. Run interactive simulations that generate learning signals, and plug in your own bidding model to see how it performs. You'll leave with a working ARTF container and auction-simulation harness you can point at your own models.

title: Build Composable Agents with the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit
speaker: Mahesh Jadhav, Pragnesh Shah
abstract: Partners spent years building their modernization tooling. AWS Transform now meets them where they are, ATX agents exposed via MCP, callable from any partner-native orchestrator. We'll cover the integration pattern, agent-card model, and field-tested wins from GSI and ISV partners already in production.

title: Build Composable Agents with the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit
speaker: Mahesh Jadhav, Pragnesh Shah
abstract: Partners spent years building their modernization tooling. AWS Transform now meets them where they are, ATX agents exposed via MCP, callable from any partner-native orchestrator. title: Build consistent, explainable agents with ontologies & graph memory in Neptune
speaker: Brad Bebee, Meet Bhagdev
abstract: Your agents can answer questions. Can they explain why, and would two agents give the same answer? Most enterprise AI stalls in pilot because business meaning lives in scattered prompts, pipelines, and code. In this session, learn how to use Amazon Neptune to turn entities, relationships, policies, and rules into an ontology and knowledge graph that any agent framework can query and use to organize memories. See how LLM-assisted ontology generation cuts modeling from months to hours. Learn how one rule update propagates across every agent and each answer carries an inspectable reasoning trace. Designed for architects building production agentic systems.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Build conversational AI agents for query federation with Amazon Athena
speaker: Arturo Bayo, Steve Phillips, Shoukat Ghouse, Pathik Shah, Sandeep Mishra
abstract: Stop copying data just to query it. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use MCP server integration with Amazon Athena for fast conversational analytics where agents translate natural language to federated SQL queries across custom databases and a multi-vendor data store – without moving or copying data. You’ll learn how federated queries eliminate complex ETL pipelines, enable cross-source joins in a single SQL statement, and integrate with your lakehouse on AWS for unified governance.

title: Build, customize, and deploy on SageMaker AI with learnings from BMW Group
speaker: Naidile Murali, Marco Goergmaier, Jason Berkowitz
abstract: AI/ML teams want to move fast, experimenting with models, fine-tuning them on their data, and serving them in production. This session is for customers that want to learn how Amazon SageMaker AI lets you build, customize, and deploy models and introduces recently launched features. BMW Group will share their Industry AI vision, the challenges to achieving it, and how they're using Amazon SageMaker AI to get there, including a case study on fine-tuning LoRA adapters to improve domain reasoning over off-the-shelf models and accelerate vehicle development.

title: Build deeper into AWS with a traffic layer you own (sponsored by HAProxy Technologies)
speaker: Nathan Wehrman, Eric Martinson
abstract: Most teams on AWS accumulate separate systems for load balancing, WAF, bot management, rate limiting, and Kubernetes routing. Each brings its own config model and failure domain, another hop in the request path, and a configuration that does not travel. This session makes the case for one layer, on Graviton, benchmarked at over 2 million HTTPS requests per second, with no traffic leaving your VPC for inspection, managed and observed from one control plane. Because that layer runs unchanged in every environment you add, it becomes the one part of your architecture that never has to move. This presentation is brought to you by HAProxy Technologies, an AWS Partner.

title: Build, Deploy, and Scale AI Agents with Cloudera on AWS (sponsored by Cloudera)
speaker: Nijjwol Lamsal
abstract: Join this exclusive hands-on workshop to master building and deploying high-impact AI agents with Cloudera on AWS. Move from experimentation to production using trusted data, scalable workflows, and governed infrastructure. Led by Cloudera solution architects, you will use Mistral Vibe, Mistral’s coding agent to build agentic data experiences, develop governed apps for data warehouse access, integrate Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Amazon Web Services (AWS) services including Amazon Bedrock alongside your preferred LLMs, and explore the latest Cloudera AI Workbench enhancements. Designed for data scientists, developers, engineers, and analysts ready to enable secure, scalable, open AI across hybrid environments.

title: Build durable AI agents with AgentCore and Temporal (sponsored by Temporal)
speaker: Cornelia Davis
abstract: An AI agent completes five steps, waits for approval, and then its runtime is replaced. How does it recover without repeating costly tool calls or losing the business process? In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, and Temporal combine AWS-native agent infrastructure with durable execution. We’ll build a production agent that preserves progress across failures, coordinates tools, agents, and people, and safely evolves while work is still running. You'll see how Temporal natively supports serverless compute infrastructure, complementing AgentCore Runtime with durable execution, preserving workflow progress across failures, approvals, runtime changes, and scale to zero, without pushing recovery and coordination logic into application code. This presentation is brought to you by Temporal, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Roman I

title: Build End-to-End Testing & Self-Healing Framework for Agentic AI
speaker: Pallavi Bhat, Abilashkumar P C
abstract: Organizations are accelerating their deployment of agentic journeys yet a critical gap remains - how reliable are they in handling self-service queries? This workshop delivers a hands-on framework for the complete testing and operational lifecycle of agentic on Amazon Connect Customer. First, build a layered testing strategy using native Testing & Simulation - functional, integration, and regression tests to validate self-service customer journeys, wired to dashboard-driven observability. Then, implement automated operational responses such as threshold-based alerting that triggers pre-approved remediations. You will leave with a reusable testing playbook and an implementable pattern for closed-loop operational automation - reducing manual validation effort and moving toward self-managing AI agents at scale.

title: Build eval-driven skills for Aurora PostgreSQL operations
speaker: Shayon Sanyal, Maxym Kharchenko
abstract: Turn Aurora PostgreSQL runbooks into agent skills and test whether they improve an agent's advice. Work through three incidents on a live cluster: RDS Proxy session pinning that starves checkout connections, a payout job whose open transaction blocks checkouts, and stalled order delivery alongside a long-running transaction that holds back vacuum cleanup. Complete and refine skills that cover pre-flight checks, execution, validation and rollback. Freeze a grading rubric, then compare the same agent, hosted on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, without and with your skill. Write Python recovery checks that reject incomplete fixes, perform the repairs yourself, and verify customer recovery using independent database and business records.

title: Build event-driven applications with AWS Streaming and Messaging
speaker: Amar Surjit, Varsha Palepu, Ashley Millette, Charishma Makineni, Mayank Juneja
abstract: Dive deep into AWS messaging services in this hands-on workshop where you'll build a real-world, event-driven application. Learn to architect sophisticated event-driven systems using Amazon SQS, SNS, MSK, and Amazon MQ. Through guided exercises, implement critical features including fan-out architectures, FIFO queues, and hybrid patterns while optimizing for security, cost, and performance. Gain practical insights into how architectural decisions impact scalability, latency, and operational complexity in production systems.

title: Build explainable AI agent observability with DynamoDB and Neptune
speaker: David H Gardner, Varma Gottumukkala, Kevin Willis, Don Simpson, Chun Schiros
abstract: Unintended agent actions and incorrect outputs are difficult to investigate without a structured provenance layer. In this session, learn how to design an agent observability system using Amazon DynamoDB to capture the operational audit log and Amazon Neptune to model causal dependencies between retrieved facts and agent decisions. Explore the data model, instrumentation patterns, and graph query techniques that answer what data an agent retrieved, what it concluded, and how those conclusions shaped the final output, making every agent decision traceable and explainable. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Build GenAI-Powered Workflows with AWS Serverless and AWS AI Services
speaker: Swarna Kunnath, Jas Narula, Michael Hume, Diego Santiviago, Rahul Pisal
abstract: In this builders' session, design and deploy a workflow that chains AI service calls—document analysis, content generation, and decision routing—using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for checkpoint and recovery. Working in small groups, you'll implement error handling, human approval gates, and cost controls for AI-powered pipelines. Walk away with reusable patterns for production-ready GenAI workflows. You must bring your laptop to participate.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Build governed agentic AI search with Aurora, RDS, & Bedrock AgentCore
speaker: Shayon Sanyal, Aditya Samant
abstract: Build an agentic retail assistant that answers from business facts under explicit controls. Across four connected labs, combine Aurora PostgreSQL full-text search and pgvector with reciprocal rank fusion and Cohere Rerank on Amazon Bedrock. Connect search and inventory tools to specialists built with the Strands Agents SDK, then deploy them to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Runtime, Memory, Gateway, and Policy. Protect customer records with identity binding and PostgreSQL row-level security, and enforce Cedar policies on Gateway tool calls. Approve a store credit, query the audit records, and verify denied calls don't execute and retries don't duplicate credits. Patterns are reusable across Aurora and RDS for PostgreSQL.

title: Build governed remediation workflows for Aurora database operations
speaker: Chirag Dave, Anum Jang Sher, Nazneen Jafri, Maxym Kharchenko, Sudhir Amin
abstract: AI-powered database intelligence can surface recommendations for Aurora performance issues, but acting on those recommendations safely in production requires governance. In this session, build a governed recommendation-to-remediation workflow for Aurora PostgreSQL. Starting from a performance investigation, review recommendations and apply remediation through human-in-the-loop approval gates backed by scoped IAM permissions and API guardrails. The session covers capturing an auditable trail from insight to action, and planning for post-change verification and rollback actions when needed. Bring a laptop to participate.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Build, Govern, Optimize: Trustworthy, Cost-Aware Agents with the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speaker: Kevon Mayers, Chris Smith
abstract: Bring a laptop and take one multi-agent system through its whole lifecycle on AWS: discover, build, deploy, govern, and optimize. You’ll compose it from versioned parts in an open registry alongside AWS Agent Registry, declare it once, and run it with Strands Agents on your laptop, Amazon EKS, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You’ll govern it with one policy enforced at the model boundary, at every tool call, and at the kernel, using NeMo Guardrails, NeMo Relay, and OpenShell beside Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and AgentCore Policy. Then you’ll optimize it, routing each call across NVIDIA NIM and Amazon Bedrock with NeMo Switchyard and putting every change through CI/CD before it ships. You’ll leave with a working reference deployment in your own AWS account. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: Build hybrid data planes for government GenAI pipelines
speaker: Mohamed Salah, Usama Salama
abstract: Strict national security mandates block government agencies from adopting cloud GenAI. To resolve this, architects deploy a decoupled edge-to-cloud tokenization pattern. In this workshop, use AWS CDK to build a three-phase data plane that isolates sensitive citizen data in a simulated edge environment. You will deploy local data tokenization, route masked payloads to Amazon Bedrock for stateless inference, and reconcile state on-premises. Leave with an infrastructure-as-code blueprint to unlock frontier AI and satisfy federal localization mandates.

title: Build hybrid quantum-classical solutions for science and engineering on Amazon Braket
speaker: Tyler Takeshita, Sebastian Stern
abstract: Take the next step into hybrid quantum computing. This expert-level workshop combines Amazon Braket and AWS Parallel Computing Service to build hybrid quantum-classical resources that enable scientific and engineering research in fields like physics and chemistry. You learn how to structure hybrid programs, manage classical resources, and interpret results from real quantum devices. Expect hands-on exercises, detailed guidance, and examples you can use as a foundation for your own projects.

title: Building 10x Organizations - Using Modern Productivity Metrics (sponsored by Atlassian)
speaker: Justin Reock
abstract: 10x developers may be a myth, but 10x organizations are very real, as proven by the influential study performed in the 1980s, ‘The Coding War Games.’ In this keynote-style session, teams will take a detailed, granular look at the barriers to productivity developers face today and modern approaches for removing them. You’ll learn about the history of productivity theory, and how previous practices have influenced our current understanding. DevOps and Platform Engineering philosophy is clearly converging on developer experience. But which of these approaches works? DORA? SPACE? DevEx? What should we invest in and create urgency behind today so we don’t have the same discussion again in a decade? This presentation is brought to you by Atlassian, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Building a brain in under an hour: The knowledge layer for physical AI agents
speaker: Ankit Patel, Parth Desai
abstract: Agents don't fail because the model is weak. They fail because they lack context. In this hands-on session, we will build a live demo: a Raspberry Pi robot dog powered by Amazon Bedrock. You'll see how to layer context from the ground up: live camera and voice input, memory, and safety guardrails that keep it from doing something dangerous. Walk away with a reference architecture for agent knowledge layers, patterns for connecting Bedrock to physical hardware, and a blueprint for prototyping embodied AI on low-cost hardware.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Building a Cost Governance framework for AI that scales
speaker: Adam Richter, Jason Wu
abstract: AI spend starts with model tokens but often misses costs from agent runtimes, memory, data, and supporting services. In this chalk talk, we'll map an AI workload from architecture to bill, then apply a practical framework to measure, attribute, optimize, and govern its cost and value. Using AWS FinOps Agent as an example, we'll examine how its architecture creates costs across Amazon Bedrock and supporting services, and how to govern those costs. Bring your AI cost challenge and leave with a model that helps FinOps and engineering teams assign ownership, find waste, and set effective controls.

title: Building a culture of security
abstract: Security culture is now a board-level concern, yet few organizations have a repeatable way to build one. Share how you grow, measure, and sustain security culture, from engineering practice to executive engagement to team structure. Leave with practical approaches you can take back to your own organization.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Building Advanced Agentic AI Systems on AWS
speaker: Thomas Utsey
abstract: Multi-agent systems unlock powerful workflows, but production demands more than chaining agents together. This bootcamp covers advanced patterns using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Implement agent-as-tool communication, share memory across agents, optimize context windows for cost and performance, and secure deployments with policy-based access control and VPC integration. Configure distributed tracing, build evaluation frameworks, and design deployment strategies that take your agentic systems from prototype to production-ready state.

title: Building Agentic AI architectures with AWS Serverless
speaker: Debasis Rath, Michael Hume, Chris Wells, Jay Formosa, ISHITA CHAKRABORTY
abstract: Build production-ready AI agent architectures using AWS serverless services. In this builders' session, design and deploy an agentic system that uses AWS Lambda for agent hosting, tool execution, Amazon Bedrock for reasoning, and Amazon EventBridge and AWS Step Functions for inter-agent communication and orchestration. Working in small groups with AWS experts, you'll implement tool-calling patterns, configure agent memory, and wire up event-driven and workflow-based coordination between specialized agents. Walk away with a working multi-agent architecture you can extend for your own use cases. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building agentic apps with serverless: Lambda as your agent's toolbox
speaker: André Stoll, Uri Segev
abstract: Agents need tools—functions they can call to retrieve data, take actions, and interact with external systems. Lambda is well-suited for this, but designing functions as agent tools requires different thinking than traditional API backends. In this chalk talk, discuss design principles for agentic Serverless: single-responsibility tools with clear input/output schemas, MCP-compatible interfaces for universal agent consumption, and multi-tenant isolation that keeps workloads secure. We'll whiteboard the trade-offs that matter—provisioned concurrency versus on-demand cold starts, cost per invocation at agent scale, and where Serverless fits versus where you need different compute.

title: Building AI Agents with Vercel and AWS (sponsored by Vercel)
speaker: Andrew Barba, Hedieh Zandi
abstract: This session explores how Vercel and AWS work together to support the development and deployment of AI agents. You’ll learn about first party connectivity to AWS databases and services through the Vercel Marketplace, along with the backend capabilities agents need, including APIs, durable workflows, queues, cron jobs, and MCP servers. You’ll see how these building blocks, together with the EVE framework, can simplify agent development, followed by a live demo showing how to build an agent using Vercel and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

title: Building AI agents you can trust: From models to supply chain
speaker: Michael D'angelo, Yair Saban, Jean Malha
abstract: Deploying AI agents across the enterprise requires trust at every step: the models powering them, the orchestration layer controlling them, and the ecosystem of tools they consume. OpenAI provides the foundation—state-of-the-art language models that can reason, plan, and act autonomously. Runlayer solves the orchestration challenge: giving every employee a safe, governed path to delegate work to agents, with policy enforcement, identity integration, and audit trails built in. AIR addresses an emerging concern—the AI supply chain—ensuring the skills, plugins, and MCP servers agents use are vetted and secure. From capable models to controlled deployment to verified tooling, this panel illustrates how organizations can scale agent adoption while maintaining security, auditability, and control.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Building AI products at startup speed
speaker: Paul Vincent, Anupam Mishra
abstract: Startups building AI products face a different speed problem than traditional software: models change weekly, and what worked last month may already be outdated. This session covers how to build AI products that keep pace, drawing on patterns for iterating quickly, evaluating new models, and shipping AI features without getting stuck re-architecting every time the underlying technology shifts.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Building a Knowledge & Context Engineering Foundation for AI Agents
speaker: Kahu Tawhai, Nelson Martinez
abstract: Every enterprise building agentic AI hits the same wall: AI agents can't deliver trusted guidance without governed knowledge behind them. In this session, learn how AWS solved this internally with an agentic specialist teammate for Amazon Connect powered by a structured knowledge governance framework. We'll show how specialist reasoning is captured, validated, and scaled across 92 domains to 30K+ field members, and demonstrate the live workflow from governed knowledge delivery to human escalation. Walk away with a repeatable reference architecture for making your own AI agents production-ready and trustworthy.

title: Building a live context layer at Crane Worldwide Logistics (sponsored by Materialize)
speaker: Nate Stewart
abstract: Crane Worldwide Logistics serves 10,000+ clients across six continents, where a single international shipment can touch hundreds of systems. To let agents and apps act on what is happening right now, Crane built a live context graph: every business object from every core system, kept current within seconds and queryable in SQL. Jared Noynaert, SVP of Engineering and AI at Crane, and Nate Stewart, CEO of Materialize, walk through the requirements, the engines Crane evaluated, and an architecture that serves reads in under 200ms without breaking transactions. See the agents Crane runs on it today.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Building an AI Travel Assistant with AgentCore Gateway
speaker: Jimmy Silva, Bruno Marcondes
abstract: Your agent handles conversations well, but to search for flights or check weather it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this SimuLearn session, you create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and register Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tool targets. You then deploy a travel planning agent using the Strands Agents SDK that connects to the Gateway, sequentially invokes flight search and weather tools, and synthesizes results into a trip recommendation through one secure MCP endpoint.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom V

title: Building and scaling inference workloads on Amazon EKS
speaker: Shivam Dubey, Eric Anderson
abstract: Kubernetes has become the platform of choice for production gen AI inference at scale. This builders' session covers deploying and scaling large language models on Amazon EKS with NVIDIA GPUs - from cluster setup optimized for GPU workloads to efficient model serving with vLLM, distributed inference with Ray, and observability using Prometheus and Grafana. Real-world patterns address cost optimization and enterprise-grade reliability for teams moving beyond experimentation. Attendees leave with hands-on experience and best practices for running production-grade gen AI infrastructure on Kubernetes. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building and scaling low latency web applications with AWS Lambda Web Functions
speaker: Fabrianne Effendi, Jan Michael Go Tan
abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this code talk, join us to build a full-stack application live with AWS Lambda Web Functions. See how each execution environment handles concurrent HTTP requests, serving server-sent event streams alongside API traffic while scaling on demand. Using Express and React without Lambda-specific adapters, add routing, static assets, runtime configuration, business logic, and DynamoDB persistence. Then go global with multi-Region latency routing, observability, canary deployments, and fast rollback. Leave with practical patterns for building and scaling low-latency web applications on AWS Lambda.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Building and securing AI agents on Amazon EKS
speaker: Aaresh Sharma, Sai Charan Teja Gopaluni
abstract: AI agents now generate and run their own code at runtime, turning secure agent execution into a platform engineering problem. Containers alone were not built to run untrusted, autonomous code safely at scale. In this hands-on workshop, you will build an agent on Amazon EKS using the Strands Agent SDK, MCP, and Amazon Bedrock, then progressively harden and operate it: run it with stronger workload isolation, apply controls over what it can access, establish scoped identity for secure communication, and manage its lifecycle in production. You will leave able to architect, deploy, secure, and operate production-ready agentic workloads on Kubernetes.

title: Building an interconnectivity fabric across AWS accounts and orgs
speaker: Jamie Wenzel, Yécine Allouache
abstract: Deploying workloads across AWS accounts - whether across an organization, between business units, or alongside acquired entities - creates connectivity complexity that traditional networking options don’t cleanly solve. You face IP coordination headaches, overly broad network surface exposure, and heavy per-resource infrastructure just to share a service privately. In this session, build a private interconnectivity fabric: a federated architecture where multiple organizations share services privately and bidirectionally with independent governance. Combine Amazon VPC Lattice, resource gateways, AWS PrivateLink, and AWS Resource Access Manager into a cross-organization platform covering bidirectional topologies and federated governance.

title: Building a partner business on Amazon Lightsail
speaker: Murat Guven
abstract: Amazon Lightsail is a simple, low-cost cloud platform designed for small and medium business workloads. In this chalk talk, we start with an overview of what Lightsail offers and common use cases partners are delivering today. We then introduce the Lightsail Partner Program and the benefits available to partners who build their practice on Lightsail. Bring your scenarios. We'll work through partner economics, discuss real use cases, and how Lightsail helps partners tackle onboarding and scaling challenges. You'll leave with a clearer understanding of how to leverage Lightsail to build your partner business.

title: Building a semantic layer with AWS Glue Data Catalog and AWS Context
speaker: Syed Humair, Varshni Muralidharan
abstract: In this chalk talk, we dive into how AWS Context assembles semantic data from multiple semantic stores to create a semantic layer, which is then turned into a unified context layer through a knowledge graph. This enables AI agents and analytics engines to understand business meaning, relationships, and intent — not just schema and location. We'll work through architecture patterns for defining semantic data annotations, propagating semantics across lakehouse tables, and exposing discoverable, agent-ready metadata at query time.

speaker: Shashi Raina, Kishore Tatavarthi, Henry Axelrod, Krishna Prasad Prasad, Reet Takkar
abstract: AI agents create identity, authorization, governance, and tenant-isolation challenges that map directly to partner revenue streams. In this builders' session, you'll work hands-on with the Zero Trust Agent Maturity (ZAM) Framework and configure Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity and Gateway to enforce verifiable agent identities, auditable interaction chains, and centralized policy authorization that scopes every agent action to its tenant boundary. You'll run a live ZAM assessment on a sample multi-tenant deployment, revealing security gaps that become partner opportunities: red-teaming engagements, MCP security proxies, multi-tenant isolation reviews, and compliance automation. Leave with a repeatable assessment methodology to secure multi-tenant agent deployments.

title: Building better quantum computers with digital twins
speaker: Tong Shen, Benchen Huang
abstract: Quantum computers could revolutionize fields like pharmacy and logistics, but today's hardware is too error-prone for practical use. To design better error-correction strategies, simulating how real quantum hardware operates is essential, yet computationally intractable. In this talk, we demonstrate quantum processor digital twins developed by Quantum Elements and powered by AWS HPC infrastructure - that faithfully mimic real hardware at experimental scale. Attendees will leave understanding why error correction matters and how classical compute accelerates the path to useful quantum computing.

abstract: IBM Power organizations support mission-critical workloads across industries. Now, there are more infrastructure options than ever before, providing hybrid transformation opportunities and challenges. This session explores how to develop a hybrid strategy that balances performance, resiliency, security, and business objectives. Hear how enterprises are exploring a phased modernization strategy that rehosts IBM workloads in a hybrid cloud environment, connects to AWS, and evolves their infrastructure. Learn how they establish secure, low-latency AWS connectivity and integrate IBM business logic with cloud-native services. This session provides proven frameworks, architectural insights, and modernization strategies to reduce risk, accelerate transformation, and maximize infrastructure value. This presentation is brought to you by Lightedge, an AWS Partner.

title: Building Context-Aware Agents with AgentCore Memory
speaker: JP Schramek, Sri Kola
abstract: Customers expect personalized service and context retention without repeating themselves every session. In this lab, you build a customer service agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that remembers each client across conversations. You create a Memory resource with Semantic, Summary, and User Preference strategies, deploy a Lambda-based agent backed by Amazon Nova Lite, and seed multi-turn conversations. The agent retrieves preferences and facts from long-term memory to personalize responses and recommend products from a DynamoDB catalog.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom V

title: Building conversational AI with Amazon Nova 2.5 Sonic
speaker: Logan Campi, Gui Ruggiero
abstract: We'll explore how bidirectional audio streaming enables natural, low-latency dialogue, with expressive voices across multiple languages. See how new capabilities like cross-modal voice-and-text switching, asynchronous tool calling for multi-step tasks, and a large context window let you build voice agents, customer service automation, and conversational apps.

title: Building Cross-Enterprise AI Agents with MCP and A2A on AWS
speaker: Arne Knoeller, Ganesh Suryanarayanan
abstract: Enterprises run hundreds of applications from ERP, CRM, supply chain, and beyond and yet orchestrating intelligent actions across these systems remains a challenge. In this chalk talk, learn how to architect and manage cross-enterprise agentic orchestration using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We explore how Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication enable AI agents to seamlessly interact across application boundaries through a single, unified chat interface. Walk away with practical architecture patterns for connecting SAP and adjacent enterprise systems like SalesForce, ServicesNow etc into a cohesive, AI-powered automation layer

title: Building distributed multi-agent architectures on serverless
speaker: Alexander Günsche, Ben Freiberg
abstract: Moving from a single AI agent to an multi-agent system creates architectural questions: Can we increase scalability of the agent’s building blocks through decomposition? How do multiple agents coordinate, where does state live? How to retain control while allowing for emergent outcomes? This chalk talk explores distributed, multi-agent architectures on AWS Serverless. We discuss approaches to dividing responsibility, coordinating work, and choosing between centralised, structured, and decentralised designs. Along the way, we examine the questions that shape these decisions, including resilience, state management, failure handling, observability, and agent autonomy.

title: Building enterprise agent platform on AgentCore
speaker: Chaitra Mathur, Madhu Pai, Pankaj Sharma
abstract: As agents multiply across teams, platform owners need control without becoming a bottleneck. In this session, learn best practices for building a governance foundation for your agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Use gateway as a central control point for all agent-to-tool traffic, enforce authorization with policies at the infrastructure layer that agents cannot bypass, and propagate identity end to end for a complete audit trail. Use the Agent Registry to catalog, discover, and approve agents and tools across the organization, and end-to-end tracing for fleet-wide visibility. Includes a demo. Leave with a governance blueprint teams can adopt.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Building enterprise-scale event buses with Amazon EventBridge
speaker: Tolga Orhon, David Roberts, Rana Kiziltoprak German, Rodrigo Cabrera, Robert Hanuschke
abstract: Discover how Amazon EventBridge enhanced Custom event bus simplifies enterprise-scale event routing across accounts and teams. In this hands-on builders' session, you will create a central Custom event bus that connects multiple domains, so teams can publish and consume events without depending on each other. Bring existing producers onboard by publishing events in open formats, configure Subscribers for each application independently to receive only the events it needs, recover from missed events with point-in-time replay, and keep related events in sequence with ordered delivery. Work in small groups with AWS experts. Bring your laptop and come ready to build!
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Building eval-driven observability for AI agents
speaker: Sudhir Kumar, Raviteja Sunkavalli
abstract: Multi-agent systems fail in ways your dashboards cannot show: one agent hands off bad context, another retries, and the API still returns 200. In this live coding session, start with a multi-agent app on LangGraph, Strands, and CrewAI, and instrument it with OpenTelemetry and OpenInference. Trace it from the first prototype run, evaluate agents on demand with LLM-as-judge evaluators, A/B test prompt and model variants before promoting to production, pull production traces into a versioned dataset, reproduce the failure locally, and ship the fix. All from your IDE, without switching tools.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk

speaker: Rajesh Kumar Pandey, Tarun Rai Madan
abstract: Event-driven architectures have powered Serverless applications for a decade. Now AI agents bring non-deterministic producers, multi-step reasoning chains, and agent-to-agent coordination via events. Learn how the patterns you already know, such as queues, events, and retries, evolve when your consumers are autonomous agents rather than just microservices.

title: Building event-driven architectures
speaker: Katherine Vishnevskaya, Geoffroy Weyer
abstract: Event-driven architectures help development teams operate more independently, release features faster, and build more scalable applications. In this workshop, learn the fundamentals of event-driven design using Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and more. Through hands-on exercises, discover how to choose the right AWS messaging and eventing service for your use case, design loosely coupled systems that scale independently, and optimize for both cost and performance. Whether you're starting your event-driven journey or refining existing patterns, you'll leave with practical skills you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building faster: AI-native development workflows
abstract: What changes when AI is woven into the software development lifecycle itself, not just bolted on at the end? Moderated by Nate Slater, Solutions Architect Leader at AWS, this panel brings together Brad Menezes, co-founder and CEO of Superblocks, Gautam Kedia, co-founder of Starfolk AI, and Ross Cefalu, Member of Technical Staff at Factory, to discuss how they build faster with AI-native workflows. They'll explore the patterns that make an AI-native Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) work in practice, and what founders can take from their approach to rethinking how software gets built.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Building fast, serverless web apps with AWS Lambda Web Functions
speaker: Samrat Karak
abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this lightning talk, see how AWS Lambda Web Functions runs Express, Fastify, Hono, and other frameworks as they are, with no adapters. Learn what active-CPU pricing means when requests wait on databases or LLMs, and what it takes to run in one Region or several. Then secure your app for production with IAM auth, Amazon CloudFront, and private access to resources in your VPC. Leave knowing how Web Functions differ from Event Functions so you can choose the right fit for your web workload.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Building fast with automated reasoning at Amazon S3 scale
speaker: Rajeev Joshi, Cezara Dragoi
abstract: S3 has a long history of using automated reasoning, but a core challenge has been applying these techniques to large systems while maintaining development velocity. Over time, we've learned to balance cutting-edge science with engineering velocity to accelerate development. We'll share diverse techniques for validating critical storage components, from black-box model-based validation using formal API specifications, to white-box verification with specialized concurrency checkers for ensuring transaction serializability and crash consistency. You'll learn how S3 engineers and scientists are advancing systems verification with new tools and ideas that you can apply to your own systems.

Gain practical insights into architecture patterns, governance, real-time data access, key tradeoffs, and lessons learned that can help accelerate your own modernization and AI initiatives. title: Building globally distributed applications with DynamoDB global tables
speaker: Amrith Kumar
abstract: Failures happen. Regions degrade, Availability Zones go offline, and networks partition. In this session, learn how to architect Amazon DynamoDB applications that maintain availability and data integrity across a spectrum of failure modes, from single-AZ impairments to full-Region disruptions. Explore the DynamoDB primitives that underpin resilience, including global tables, multi-Region strong consistency, backup and restore, snapshots, and streaming, and how to compose them into patterns that meet strict RTO and RPO objectives. Using scenarios drawn from recent large-scale events, examine trade-offs between consistency, latency, and availability, and discover operational best practices for detecting, responding to, and recovering from failures.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Building high-quality data products for AI agents
speaker: David Victoria, Lakshmi Ramchandran Nair
abstract: AI agents are only as effective as the data they rely on. This chalk talk focuses on how to build and manage high-quality data products and contextual information for use by AI agents. You'll learn how to deliver accurate, up-to-date, and well-governed data for AI systems, including context engineering, RAG strategies, fine-tuning dataset curation, and automated quality checks. We'll cover how to manage AI context, handle data drift, and perform classical data management activities in the Agentic AI world.

Working in small groups with AWS experts, run an HTTP server on Lambda, serve static assets alongside application routes, render a DynamoDB-backed product catalogue, and stream live activity with Server-Sent Events. Walk away with a working app and deployment patterns for interactive web workloads. Bring your laptop.

In this session, learn how AWS Security Hub Extended, AWS Artifact, and other tools combine to create a powerful foundation for partners delivering managed security and compliance services at scale. Security Hub Extended gives MSSPs a single pane of glass and OCSF-normalized findings that eliminate integration headaches. Pair this with our extended security portfolio to create the foundation for audit-ready compliance frameworks across financial services, healthcare, and public sector, and you have a differentiated "detect, respond, and prove compliance" offering your customers can't get elsewhere. Whether you're an MSSP building SOC-as-a-Service, an ISV integrating into the Security Hub ecosystem, or a consulting partner delivering compliance transformations, this session shows you the better together story of working with AWS.

title: Building migration readiness when the timeline is tight
speaker: Sean Lewis, Katherine Garber, David Piet
abstract: Most organizations don't get years to plan a large-scale migration. Licensing changes, compliance requirements, or rising hardware costs can compress your timeline fast. This session covers how to build readiness quickly so your team can move hundreds of workloads with confidence. Learn how to assess your environment, build team capability, and match the right migration pathway to each workload. Hear best practices from Vanguard, who moved hundreds of applications under real pressure with zero critical outages. Walk away with a practical framework for getting your organization ready to move at any speed.

title: Building modern web applications on AWS Serverless
speaker: Erik Hanchett, Felix Gerberding
abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this session, discover how to build full-stack web applications entirely on AWS serverless services—from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. Learn architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers. Explore how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

speaker: Aakash Upadhyay, Hans Nesbitt
abstract: Customers building multi-tenant RAG platforms must balance tenant data isolation, cost, and operational scale. This chalk talk examines a production architecture serving thousands of tenants on Amazon Bedrock and compares multiple approaches. We whiteboard isolation patterns, tenant routing, per-knowledge-base scaling and limits, managed embedding models, and multimodal document parsing. We will discuss the tradeoffs that determine when to build your own retrieval stack and when to use a fully managed knowledge base.

abstract: Large language models pattern-match on tokens, not business meaning, which causes subtle failures when applied to enterprise data. Ontologies address this by giving AI systems a formal structure for knowledge: a graph defining what exists, how entities relate, and what questions are meaningful. In this workshop, build an ontology-driven semantic layer using Amazon Neptune to power accurate, trustworthy agentic workloads across diverse data sources. Bring a laptop to participate.

speaker: Sandeep Sovani, Francesco Ruffino
abstract: High-fidelity Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations require significant compute infrastructure. We’ll discuss how organizations are migrating CAE and CFD workloads from on premises to AWS, combining scalable HPC infrastructure with cloud-native engineering applications to accelerate product development. Learn how to architect your enterprise HPC system to optimize cost, queue wait times, and throughput with Amazon EC2 HPC-optimized instances, Savings Plans, and Amazon FSx.

title: Building production AI agents on AWS: compute, security, state, and cost
speaker: Uma Ramadoss, Heeki Park
abstract: Agents are moving from demos to production, and the compute you pick shapes security, state, and cost downstream. This session follows a real agent running on AWS and the decisions behind it. Explore serverless compute choices for agents: Lambda durable functions for orchestration and long-running workflows, and Lambda MicroVMs for running untrusted agent-generated code in isolation. Learn how to secure agents with IAM, AgentCore Identity, gateways, and secrets management, making agents stateful with RAG knowledge bases and AgentCore Memory. Control cost through token visibility, caching, pause-snapshot-resume, and right-sizing. Bring your agent architecture and the tradeoffs you're weighing.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: Building Production Graph Pipelines with Nodestream and Amazon Neptune
speaker: Kelvin Lawrence, Taylor Riggan
abstract: Nodestream is an open source declarative framework for building, maintaining, and analyzing graph data, built collaboratively by engineers at Intuit and AWS. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Nodestream connects data sources like Apache Kafka, APIs, and files to graph databases with automatic schema migrations and zero database-specific code. We'll dive into the Amazon Neptune plugin, discuss how declarative pipelines eliminate brittle ETL, and share lessons learned from real world customer scenarios. Bring your graph data challenges and we'll solve them live.

title: Building production-ready agents securely: lessons from AWS at scale
speaker: Hardik Thakkar, Max Tybar
abstract: Most AI agent demos work on stage but break in production. Real enterprise agents need multi-layer guardrails, tenant identity isolation, graceful degradation, and continuous evaluation. In this code talk, we share patterns from shipping two production security agent systems on AWS: one that investigates incidents across customer accounts, and one that helps security practitioners author threat detections. We cover practices that any team can adopt such as prompt injection defense, tenant-scoped sessions, circuit breakers, observability, and eval-driven improvement.

We’ll showcase these principles through real-world applications, including complex real employee- and customer-facing banking use cases while meeting rigorous business standards around accuracy, reliability, and risk management. title: Building resilience against ransomware using AWS Backup
speaker: Palak Desai, Sabith Venkitachalapathy, Ivan Velickovic
abstract: To counter evolving cyber threats, organizations must fortify their backup infrastructure for recovery resilience. This session applies threat modeling to design a multi-account AWS Backup architecture across three pillars: immutability with isolation, integrity validation, and guaranteed accessibility. Walk through a phased reference architecture using logically air-gapped vaults for tamper-proof backups, restore testing and GuardDuty malware scanning for integrity assurance, and multi-party approval for secure recovery during account compromise. Learn how to define your minimum viable company to sequence recovery priorities, distinguish cyber RPO from operational RPO, and align your strategy to NIST CSF 2.0 for recovery resilience and business continuity.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Building resilient Amazon ECS applications: a multi-layer approach
speaker: Nitheesha Myneni, Sai Kumar Samala
abstract: In this interactive chalk talk, we explore how to build resilient Amazon ECS architectures by examining failure modes across multiple layers of the stack. We walk through specific scenarios such as deployment failures, Availability Zone impairments, and dependency cascades that cycle tasks faster than you can debug them. We discuss architectural patterns, ECS capabilities for resilience, and common mistakes to avoid that turn minor issues into incidents. You'll leave with a concrete mental model for hardening your ECS services and a checklist you can apply to your own workloads.

title: Building resilient authentication with Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication
speaker: Abrom Douglas III, Edward Sun
abstract: Authentication is the front door to your app, and if that's unavailable, everything is unreachable. Amazon Cognito is the managed CIAM service that handles sign-up, sign-in, federation, and threat protection at scale. In this chalk talk, learn how Cognito's new multi-Region replication (MRR) unlocks resilient authentication across Regions. We'll whiteboard reference architectures for B2C, B2B, and M2M workloads, cover implementation considerations like customer managed keys and in-Region dependencies, and walk through failover strategies. Leave ready to architect authentication that keeps customers connected.

title: Building resilient deployment pipelines with Amazon ECS
speaker: Mike Rizzo, Islam Mahgoub
abstract: Every application has a different risk profile when you ship a new version. A payments API needs different safeguards than a marketing page. In this workshop, learn how to match Amazon ECS deployment strategies to your workload requirements. Configure blue/green deployments for services requiring instant failback, canary deployments for APIs where you validate with real traffic before full cutover, and linear deployments for gradual migrations that build confidence at each step. Integrate pause hooks for manual approvals and external validation, and set alarm-based triggers that automatically revert bad releases before customers notice. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building searchable live sports with AWS Elemental and Amazon CloudFront
speaker: John Councilman, Brian Bedard
abstract: Live sports fans no longer watch one feed and wait for the recap. They expect every angle live and every key play instantly findable. In this session, see how you turn live sports into searchable fan moments on AWS. Using AWS Elemental inference, the platform generates highlight clips in real time and pairs them with conversational AI powered by Amazon Bedrock, so fans can ask for "the catch in the third quarter" and get it in seconds instead of hours. Then go deeper into the delivery workflow: composing multi-view experiences so viewers follow simultaneous matches and camera angles, enriching clips with AI-generated titles and captions, and delivering live feeds and clips globally through a single Amazon CloudFront architecture.

title: Building serverless applications with Terraform
speaker: Lavanya Tangutur, Debasis Rath
abstract: Master the integration of serverless technology with Infrastructure as Code using Terraform on AWS. In this hands-on workshop, learn to efficiently define, deploy, and maintain serverless architectures—from Lambda functions and API Gateway endpoints to DynamoDB tables and EventBridge rules. Whether you're new to Terraform or looking to apply it to serverless workloads, you'll gain practical experience writing reusable modules, managing state, and automating deployments across environments. Walk away with patterns you can immediately apply to your own serverless projects. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Building Serverless applications at AI speed
speaker: Josh Rodgers, Archana Venkitaramanan, Charleston Telles, Sahil Malhotra, David Lamb
abstract: Manually wiring up Lambda functions, API Gateway routes, and IaC templates for every new service is repetitive work that AI handles well. In this builders' session, use Kiro to go from natural language specifications to a deployed serverless application. You'll configure MCP tool servers to give the AI agent access to AWS APIs, author steering documents that produce consistent output, and iterate on generated infrastructure until it passes validation. Walk away with techniques for getting reliable, production-ready code from AI-assisted workflows. Bring your laptop.

title: Building Serverless distributed data processing workloads
speaker: Anshuman Chakravarty, Jesus Bernal, Praveen Koorse, Mukunthan Doraiswamy, Hanish Garg
abstract: Processing large-scale data shouldn't require provisioning clusters or managing batch infrastructure. In this builders' session, design and deploy a distributed data processing pipeline using AWS Step Functions Distributed Map, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. Working in small groups, you'll implement fan-out patterns that process thousands of objects in parallel, handle partial failures gracefully, and optimize for cost and throughput. Learn when Distributed Map is the right choice versus other parallelization strategies, and walk away with a reusable pipeline template. Bring your laptop.

title: Building stateful AI workflows with Serverless orchestration
speaker: Leandro Cavalcante Damascena, Mark Curtis, Anushree Umesh, Surya Sai D, Hanish Garg
abstract: AI workflows need state such as conversation history, intermediate results, and human approvals, but managing it shouldn't require a database and custom recovery logic. In this builders' session, build a stateful AI workflow that checkpoints progress, recovers from failures automatically, and pauses for external callbacks. Working hands-on with AWS experts, you'll implement multi-step reasoning chains with retry semantics, compare orchestration approaches for different workflow shapes, and deploy a working agent pipeline. Bring your laptop.

title: Building the Construction Cloud: How Procore AI &Amazon Bedrock Power the Built World (sponsored by Procore)
speaker: Thiago da Costa
abstract: Construction generates massive volumes of structured and unstructured data, such as drawings, RFIs, and safety reports, that most AI infrastructure isn't built to handle. In this session, we'll break down how Amazon Bedrock's model access, guardrails, and enterprise controls power Procore AI, and why that combination is what makes construction-specific AI viable at enterprise scale. You'll leave with a clear picture of the architecture, and why we think this is the first real blueprint for AI in the built environment. This presentation is brought to you by Procore, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Building the Future: Transforming SaaS with Agentic AI
abstract: The room drives the agenda. These are the three threads we will work through together. - From pilot to production - Where are companies on the agentic adoption spectrum, what is blocking them, and which real-world use cases are working today? - Platform patterns for agentic SaaS - Multi-tenancy, isolation, security models, and accelerators you can apply directly to your own roadmap. - Monetization and Cost optimization - How are companies packaging and charging for agent capabilities as they move from seat-based to consumption and outcome-based pricing, and how are they managing unbounded inference cost? What you will walk away with: - Validated agentic strategy. Pressure-test your approach against peers and pick up new ideas from peers navigating the same transformation. - Insight into architecture patterns. Multi-tenant isolation models, data blueprints, and monetization frameworks. - A peer network. Fellow technologies actively shipping agentic capabilities, not just evaluating them
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Building the Intelligent Health System, CXO blueprint for the agentic era (sponsored by PwC)
speaker: Geoffry Hook, Rares Almasan, Abbas Mooraj
abstract: The health systems that will lead the next decade are not simply digitizing existing processes. They are reimagining what a health system looks like with AI native to every layer. On AWS that means a unified data foundation across electornic health records, claims, images, devices, and genomics; real-time AI at the point of decision; agentic workflows that absorb entire categories of administrative burden; and governance that holds up to audit at scale. Chief Information, Digital, and AI Officers building this now share what worked and what they would do differently. Attendees leave with a practical sequence, from data foundation to agentic deployment. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Building the semantic intelligence layer for enterprise AI agents
speaker: Jordi Macià Ferrer, David Christian
abstract: Every AI agent in the enterprise reasons better when it shares a common semantic understanding of the business. In this chalk talk, we show you how to build an Agentic Intelligence Layer that resolves meaning across every system and makes it innately consumable by any agent. We break down how to combine semantic embeddings, knowledge graph relationships, and natural-language memories into a single, governed layer that every agent reads from and writes back to. We take product and customer intelligence as the first domains and show how the same architecture extends to supply chain, operations, finance, and workforce. The result is a semantic intelligence layer that compounds learning across the business and transforms everything from demand forecasting to conversational commerce to enterprise decision-making.

abstract: Join AWS and Amazon Together Community for an evening reception celebrating those who make the world better. Connect with builders and developers who use AWS AI and cloud technology for positive change. Over light bites and beverages at Tableau in the Wynn, explore skilling and social impact, spark new ideas, and celebrate the work we do best — together. All builders welcome.

title: Building Trust in AI Agents through Skills-Based Verification (sponsored by Pearson)
speaker: Juan Garcia, Chris McAvoy
abstract: As AI agents become part of the enterprise workforce, organizations face a critical question: How can they trust that these digital teammates are capable, reliable, and ready to work? Pearson and IBM are exploring how enterprise AI expertise, skills assessment, and verification can help organizations address this challenge. This session will offer a preview of their collaborative approach to that joint agent verification solution, examining how skills-based evaluation could help organizations build confidence in AI agents as they scale adoption and integrate human and digital talent across the workforce.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Building Trust into Agentic AI on AWS in the Age of Autonomous Agents (sponsored by Check Point)
speaker: Shahar Tal, Dhanil Parwani
abstract: AI agents are evolving from assistants into autonomous systems that call APIs and take actions on behalf of users. Traditional perimeter controls aren't enough; threats now emerge from prompt injection, excessive permissions, and unmonitored tool use. In this session, we'll show how Check Point's AI security intelligence integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to enforce real-time guardrails at the agent runtime layer inspecting intent, validating actions, and preventing policy violations before they execute. Walk away with a practical framework for securing agentic AI on AWS with Check Point. This presentation is brought to you by Check Point, an AWS Partner.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Building Wealth Advisor Agents with Full Stack Architecture
speaker: Mar Cánovas, Bruno Marcondes
abstract: In this SimuLearn session, you leverage the entire Amazon Bedrock AgentCore platform ito build production-grade wealth management advisor. You create Memory resources for client personalization, configure a Gateway with MCP tool targets for account and market data, deploy specialist agents and a supervisor to Runtime, and authenticate users through Cognito. The result is a multi-agent advisor that recognizes each client, remembers their goals, and produces auditable financial guidance through governed tools.

title: Building Worlds for Machines: VAMS and 3DGS for Autonomy
speaker: Eric Cornwell
abstract: Autonomous platforms are only as capable as the environments they train and validate in. In this Lightning Talk, see how AWS uses the Visual Asset Management System (VAMS) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) to turn real field data collected during Project MAVERICK exercises into high-fidelity, simulation-ready environments. We walk the pipeline from sensor capture to reconstructed, simulation-ready worlds, and the content management that makes them reusable. These environments are not the autonomy; they are what builds, improves, and validates it. If you build or validate autonomous systems, you leave knowing how to turn field capture into reusable simulation-ready environments.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Building Your AI Practice: From Business Model to Partner Revenue
speaker: Scott Bends, Lynn Cain, Erik Farr
abstract: Enterprises expect agentic outcomes. That changes how solutions are built and deployed. Traditional delivery practices are evolving to agentic delivery, outcome-based models, and scalable IP transacted through AWS Marketplace. Partners moving first are delivering measurable business outcomes faster and building new revenue alongside their customers. In this session, learn the three-stage practice-building path. See how Forward Deployed Engineering gives partners a new engagement architecture and faster delivery: pod-based, and time-boxed. See where AWS co-investment programs and AI-specific enrollment paths de-risk each stage of practice growth. Walk away with example GTM models and a concrete action plan.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Building your first event-driven application
speaker: Mohammed Atiq, Sarath Kumar Kumar, Tamas Santa, Vinodh Kannan Sadayamuthu, Akanksha Bodhankar
abstract: A customer places an order. Inventory updates. Payment processes. Notifications fire. In a monolith, one failure cascades through everything. In this builders' session, build a retail order system where each step runs independently using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. Through guided exercises, you'll publish and subscribe to events, handle failures in one service without breaking others, and trace event flows across your system. No prior event-driven experience required—you'll leave with a working application and the core patterns for decomposing synchronous workflows into resilient, asynchronous systems. Bring your laptop.

title: Building Your Software Factory: From Code to Production (sponsored by Harness)
speaker: Trevor Stuart, Nick Durkin
abstract: A coding agent can open a pull request in minutes, and then it waits... on reviews, pipeline runs, approvals, and everything else between code and production. Most teams building a software factory stop at code generation, even though testing, securing, deploying, and optimizing code safely decides how fast software ships. This session shows how to extend your factory from your first ticket to production. We’ll look at how the agents at each stage pass work to the next and pull in a person only when a decision needs judgment, all within governance your organization already trusts. Then we’ll show it live. Cosmos, the Harness Software Factory Agent, will fix an issue, then feed the change back into Harness for policy checks and deployment. You’ll leave knowing where your factory is waiting and what it takes to close each gap. This presentation is brought to you by Harness, an AWS Partner.

title: Building zero-trust personal AI with EC2 confidential computing
speaker: J.D. Bean
abstract: Learn how Bee built a personal AI assistant where privacy is cryptographically guaranteed - not policy-promised. Bee processes user data exclusively within hardware-isolated EC2 Confidential VMs powered by AWS Nitro, where no one - including Amazon - can access unencrypted data. We'll dive into NitroTPM attestation that lets devices verify server integrity before sharing keys, Sigstore transparency logs for auditability, mutual TLS with embedded attestation proofs, and key lifecycle management within encrypted VM memory. A practical blueprint for building zero-trust AI on Amazon EC2.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Build interactive web apps with AWS Lambda
speaker: Julian Wood, Salih Güler
abstract: Web applications need persistent connections, session state, and native HTTP handling - capabilities that don't map obviously to Lambda's request-response model. In this session, see how to run web frameworks like Express, Hono, and Next.js directly on Lambda using runtime adapters that preserve the framework's native patterns. If you're running containerized web apps today, we walk through practical migration paths that move your existing framework code to Lambda with minimal changes.
