title: Build It, Govern It, Ship It: CI/CD for AI Agents with the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speaker: Kevon Mayers
abstract: Shipping an AI agent once is easy. Shipping it again, cheaper, better, and still within policy, is the hard part. In this session we treat an agent like any other software, using the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit on AWS: every part it’s built from, its skills, tools, models, and policies, goes through a pipeline before an agent can use it. We pull a skill from a public registry, test whether it actually helps with NVIDIA SkillEvaluator, and publish it to a private registry alongside AWS Agent Registry, pinned by version and digest. Then we route each call to the right model across NVIDIA NIM and Amazon Bedrock with NeMo Switchyard, and turn what the run’s checks caught into the next policy rule. Leave knowing how to make each release of your agent cheaper, better, and safer than the last. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Build It or Bring It: Getting AI Agents into CX Faster
speaker: Matt de Neef, Soumya Unni
abstract: Getting agentic AI from prototype to production in your customer experience application is slow, and the gap is widening. In this chalk talk we give you two levers to close it on Amazon Connect Customer. Build new AI agents on the agentic CX designer canvas, describing what you want in natural language and applying enterprise guardrails to reach production-grade quickly. Or bring the agents your business has already built, anywhere, and orchestrate them through Connect Customer using the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol. We demonstrate both, then whiteboard how they fit together architecturally. Come ready to challenge the design and share where you would use each.

title: Build layered defenses for agentic AI from prompt to tool execution
speaker: Reetesh Surjani, Anshu Bathla
abstract: Attendees build a defense-in-depth security architecture for an AI agent. You start with a pre-deployed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with Lambda tools, then run adversarial test scenarios to observe how gateway and tools respond without controls. You layer defenses from Bedrock Guardrails for prompt-attack detection, through AgentCore Policy Engine with Cedar policies-based tool authorization, including Dogwood temporal policies, and finally native rate limits paired with CloudWatch anomaly detection. By progressing through each scenario again, you verify how each protection aligns with a layered security pattern you can apply to your agentic workload.

title: Build long-running agents that persist for days on AgentCore
speaker: Prasanna Venkatesh Sridharan, Dheeraj Hegde
abstract: Most agents handle a single request and forget everything. Production workloads are different — an incident investigation spans hours, a document review takes days, a customer onboarding stretches across weeks. These agents need to persist state, survive restarts, and pick up exactly where they left off. This session covers how to build long-running agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Runtime for durable execution and Memory for cross-session context. Learn checkpointing patterns, human-in-the-loop pause and resume, and cost strategies that keep idle agents from burning through your budget.

title: Build low latency real-time bidding workloads with AWS RTB Fabric
speaker: Sergio Serra, Luca Passani, Amin Bandeali
abstract: With the growth of digital media, including streaming video and retail media, customers that operate advertising platforms need to buy, sell, deliver, and measure millions of ad transactions per second while meeting stringent latency requirements. In this chalk talk, you will learn how to run real-time bidding workloads with your AdTech partners on a dedicated network in the cloud using AWS RTB Fabric. You will learn how to setup, onboard, and integrate AWS RTB Fabric with your supply and demand-side-platforms. Additionally, you will learn about key features including the core network, modules, and pricing model of the service.

title: Build multi-agent warranty and repair intelligence for automotive
speaker: Amit Kumar, Venkat Devarajan, Ajit Kumar KP, Vijai Thoppae, Gopi Krishnamurthy
abstract: Warranty and repair workflows span claim history, technical service bulletins, supplier quality records, and regulatory thresholds — a high-cost, fragmented data challenge for automotive OEMs. In this builders session, construct a multi-agent warranty and repair intelligence system using Strands SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Build a triage agent that classifies incoming cases, a research agent that queries Bedrock Knowledge Bases across TSBs and repair records, and a resolution agent that synthesizes findings into a structured decision with cited evidence routed for technician approval via human-in-the-loop controls.

title: Build Multi-Agent Workflows with AWS Quick, MCP & AgentCore
speaker: Vishnu Elangovan, Josh Anderson
abstract: Design and build a multi-agent system inside AWS Quick where specialized agents collaborate to automate complex business processes. Connect to enterprise systems through MCP servers on Bedrock AgentCore, implement inter-agent communication, configure OAuth 2.0 authentication, and deploy autonomous workflows using Quick Flows. Modeled after production deployments running 12+ coordinated agents across ERP, finance, and procurement, you'll leave with a working multi-agent solution you can replicate in your own environment.

title: Build nanochat models with PyTorch and Trainium-Easier than you think
speaker: Josh Longenecker, Pinak Panigrahi
abstract: Can you train an LLM on AWS Trainium, our purpose-built AI chip for better price performance, using PyTorch with minimal code changes? We'll show you with nanochat, a 560M-parameter GPT you can train in about two hours on a single Trainium instance using familiar PyTorch workflows. We cover end-to-end training across data preparation, distributed configuration, and model test practices with interactive chat, showing what works out of the box and what few changes are required. You'll walk away with knowledge to train your own LLM on Trainium with PyTorch.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Build Once, Deploy Anywhere: Agentic AI from Data Center to Edge with Qualcomm & AWS (sponsored by Qualcomm)
abstract: AI is moving beyond the cloud, requiring developers to deploy intelligent workloads across data centers, edge infrastructure, vehicles, industrial systems, PCs, and mobile devices. The challenge is scaling AI efficiently across diverse hardware environments. In this session, learn how Qualcomm and AWS enable developers to build agentic AI applications across the compute continuum, from cloud training to real-time edge and on-device inference. Discover how open frameworks, portable AI runtimes, and streamlined workflows accelerate development and deployment. Through examples spanning automotive, IoT, industrial edge, mobile, datacenter, and cloud use cases, explore how a unified developer experience reduces complexity, increases flexibility, and helps deliver scalable AI applications anywhere. This presentation is brought to you by Qualcomm, an AWS Partner.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Build on top of large codebases without breaking your code
speaker: Kenneth Sanchez, Anil Maktala
abstract: Your AI agent writes code fast, but when you unleash it on a large codebase, context can fill up quickly and the agent can make questionable implementation choices. Learn how Kiro uses neurosymbolic techniques to understand what you want to build, removing ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. Then, learn simple practices you can use to keep your agent implementation surgical, and detect drift before it spreads all over your codebase.

title: Build optimized, resilient inference endpoints on Amazon SageMaker AI
speaker: Dmitry Soldatkin, Apoorva Chandra
abstract: Deploy, optimize, and monitor an LLM inference endpoint end to end on Amazon SageMaker AI. In this hands on workshop, use GenAI Inference Recommender to discover optimal configurations, cutting model deployment time to days instead of weeks, learn how to train EAGLE speculative decoding heads on your own data for up to 2.5× throughput gains, and benchmark results. Then, configure capacity aware instance pools with priority based GPU fallback and weighted autoscaling for production resilience. Throughout, interact with endpoints via OpenAI compatible APIs. You keep the working notebooks to reuse on your own endpoints.

abstract: What happens when you give an AI agent the keys to your ETL infrastructure? In this builder session, you'll build an agentic workflow using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that accepts natural language instructions and autonomously orchestrates ETL jobs on AWS Glue. Using MCP servers, your agent will reason job configurations, construct parameters, execute transformations, interact with the Glue Data Catalog, handle retries on failure, and surface results—all from a single conversational prompt.

title: Build production agent skills on AWS Quick: automate your own work
speaker: Jed Lechner, Mrunal Shridhar
abstract: Agent skills turn repeatable work into instructions an agent carries out reliably. In this hands-on workshop, you build production skills on AWS Quick. You author skills from scratch with AI-powered assistance and apply engineering best practices as you build. You put your agents and skills to work automating real business use cases, measure the impact of what you built, and leave able to build and refine skills and agents that automate your own work.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano I

title: Build production AI assistant with Hugging Face Libraries and models
speaker: Jeff Boudier, Louise Ping, Andre Gomes
abstract: Every product team wants an embedded AI assistant, but closed APIs erode margins and limit customization. In this chalk talk, we architect a production solution using open building blocks: retrieval, reranking, and generation models working together in real time. We diagram how to fine-tune for your domain, orchestrate multi-model pipelines, and serve thousands of concurrent users cost-efficiently. You will leave able to run native Hugging Face models and libraries on AWS Trainium and own your AI stack end to end.

title: Build Provable Zero-Trust Agents with Automated Reasoning checks
speaker: Nafi Colette Diallo, Wale Akinfaderin
abstract: Neurosymbolic AI pairs the language understanding of LLMs with the mathematical rigor of automated reasoning, enabling agent decisions that are provably correct, not just statistically likely. In this hands-on workshop, you'll take real-world business rules (e.g. insurance eligibility or financial compliance) and formalize them into Automated Reasoning policies that agents invoke at decision time. Starting from natural-language documents, you'll translate requirements into verifiable logic, then integrate your policies with agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, validating outputs at inference time. Leave able to build Automated Reasoning policies that guarantee correctness, where every decision is logically grounded, traceable, and auditable.

title: Build ransomware recovery with AWS Backup air-gapped vaults
speaker: Ameen Khan S, Santosh Setty
abstract: When ransomware compromises your account, your backups are the last line of defense. The question is whether they're isolated, verified, and accessible when you need them most. In this workshop, you'll work through a simulated account compromise using AWS Backup logically air-gapped vaults. You'll configure vault isolation policies to put backups out of reach, validate their integrity through restore testing, and orchestrate recovery when primary credentials are compromised. Backup Audit Manager ties it together with compliance monitoring to prove your posture holds. You'll finish with a tested recovery playbook built against a live compromise scenario. Participants must bring a laptop.

In this workshop, build a multiplayer application with live updates and group chat functionality using AWS Amplify Gen 2. Define your backend—data model, auth rules, and real-time subscriptions—in TypeScript and deploy to a cloud sandbox in seconds. Connect your frontend to a serverless backend powered by AWS AppSync WebSockets. You must bring your laptop to participate.

Fine-tuning an LLM with domain data brings precision in how the agent responds and executes. In this hands-on lab, build reliable AI agents by fine-tuning an LLM on Amazon SageMaker AI for valid tool-call output and consistent persona, and connect it to Amazon Bedrock RAG to ground responses in your latest policies and customer data.

In this lightning session, learn how Oracle Maximum Availability Architecture helps protect AI workloads running on Oracle AI Database@AWS. Explore proven patterns for high availability, disaster recovery, data protection, and automated failover across AWS Availability Zones and Regions. See how capabilities such as Oracle Active Data Guard and integrated backup and recovery services help minimize downtime, reduce data loss, and keep AI applications operating through planned maintenance and unexpected disruptions. title: Build resilient apps on AWS: AI-driven resilience at any scale
speaker: Juan Ga Quintero, Jonathan León
abstract: Most teams discover resilience gaps during outages, not before. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through the next generation of AWS Resilience Hub to map user journeys, define recovery objectives, identify dependencies, and run AI-powered failure mode assessments. We'll explore how to get prescriptive HA and DR recommendations and automate your DR mechanisms with meaningful tests for your architecture and use case. Walk away with a step-by-step approach to strengthen the resilience posture of your critical applications, from identifying their business impact all the way to test and automate their recovery.

title: Build, run, and improve: inside a production AI inference platform (sponsored by Baseten)
speaker: Sai Maddali
abstract: Getting a model to work is the easy part. Keeping it fast, cheap, and reliable in production is the hard part. Sai Maddali, Product Manager at Baseten, walks through the platform behind some of the highest-volume inference workloads running today: how GPU capacity is sourced and managed across clouds, how runtimes are tuned per workload, and how dedicated inference, model APIs, and training sit on one pool of compute. He shows why the teams pulling ahead treat build, run, and improve as a single loop, and what that changes about latency, cost, and model quality. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Build scalable streaming and messaging applications with Amazon Kinesis and AmazonMSK
speaker: Nishit Nagar, Ali Alemi
abstract: Messaging and streaming should be simple, elastic, and cost-efficient, no matter how your workloads change. In this session, discover how Amazon MSK and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is making it easier and more affordable to build messaging and streaming applications at any scale. Learn how you can stop worrying about capacity planning and reduce costs automatically as your traffic scales up and down. See how you can land your streaming data directly into Amazon S3 and S3 Tables without building or managing separate pipelines so you can focus on deriving insights instead of maintaining infrastructure. Join us to see how these innovations come together to help you move faster, spend less, and eliminate operational overhead at any scale.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Build Secure AI Agents on AWS: XAA, Bedrock AgentCore and the AI Blueprint (sponsored by Okta)
speaker: Steven Tamm, Wayne Smiley, Jose Alvarez
abstract: Building AI agents is easy, but securing enterprise data access without slowing development is hard. Teams often rely on static, over-privileged credentials, creating major security risks. But there’s a solution. This session explores how to secure agentic workflows with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Okta. We’ll introduce the Blueprint Alliance, of which AWS and Okta are founding members, and cover how standards like Cross App Access (XAA) and SCIM for Agents transform AI identity. You'll learn how replacing static keys with dynamic, delegated permissions enables real-time policy evaluation at every tool call, empowering developers to build scalable, trusted AI agents that operate strictly within verified boundaries. This presentation is brought to you by Okta, an AWS Partner.

title: Build secure APIs faster with Amazon API Gateway and Kiro CLI
speaker: Josh Rodgers, Raphael Lima, Jacob Cravinho, David Lamb, Archana Venkitaramanan
abstract: Secure your APIs with confidence and build them faster. In this builders' session, dive into Amazon API Gateway authorization strategies including Amazon Cognito user pools, Amazon Verified Permissions, Lambda custom authorizers, IAM authorizers, and machine-to-machine scenarios. Through hands-on exercises, implement each strategy and understand their trade-offs. Once secured, ship faster—use Kiro CLI, OpenAPI, and MCP servers to go from spec to deployed API in minutes. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Build self-healing agents from diagnosis to disaster recovery
speaker: George Agiasoglou, Hisyam Jukifli
abstract: Most AI agents stop at the root cause report, leaving engineers to act under pressure. In this workshop, build three cooperating agents on a pre-provisioned workload using Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon Application Recovery Controller. A live app throws 4XX errors and a troubleshooting agent runs root cause analysis. Then build a remediation agent to apply the fix. When 5XX errors signal an Availability Zone impairment, you'll extend the remediation agent to consult a resilience agent before acting. Leave with a working reference implementation you can adapt to your financial services or enterprise environment.

title: Build self-healing Serverless applications with AWS DevOps Agent
speaker: Parnab Basak, Mark Curtis, Jay Colodner, Itziar Olivera Goicolea, Udit Parikh
abstract: Production incidents at 2 a.m. don't wait for your team to wake up. In this builders' session, work with a deployed serverless application and use AWS DevOps Agent to resolve real-world failures autonomously. You'll inject common production issues—such as Lambda throttling, timeout cascades, DynamoDB throughput exceeded, and SQS dead-letter queue buildup—then configure the agent to perform root cause analysis, propose remediation, and apply fixes. You'll tune detection sensitivity, set approval gates for automated actions, and evaluate where autonomous remediation is safe versus where human oversight is required. Bring your laptop.

Configure AI Guardrails for content safety and structured escalation paths that preserve full conversation context for human agents.

title: Build, simulate, and validate physical AI-driven robotic systems
speaker: Fabrizio Manfredi, Vikram Krishna, Jan Metzner, Gezim Musliaj, Hubert Asamer
abstract: Commissioning industrial robots typically takes weeks of physical testing. Digital twins with real-time physics simulation and multi-agent AI optimization can compress that timeline from weeks to hours. In this builders session, construct a digital twin of a multi-robot manufacturing cell using virtual PLCs and controllers, real fieldbus connectivity, real-time physics simulation in NVIDIA Omniverse, and Amazon EC2 as the compute backbone. Leave with an AI-optimized robotic program validated against real-world conditions before ever touching real hardware. Generated in 60 minutes using open standards and open toolchains, the result is a reusable blueprint that scales across cells, lines, and sites.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

speaker: Nikolay Vlasov, Jinsung Huh, Hun KIM, Munkyu Seong, Sudhir Kalidindi
abstract: Stablecoins are redefining payments and settlement infrastructure in financial services. In this session, build a production-ready stablecoin infrastructure on AWS spanning secure key management with AWS Key Management Service and and AWS Nitro Enclaves, multi-signature governance workflows, token minting/burning/swapping operations, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments for autonomous agent-to-agent transactions. Get hands-on experience building wallet infrastructure and executing USDC stablecoin operations end-to-end. Walk away with a working architecture that bridges traditional key management with the emerging agentic commerce paradigm.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Build stateful agentic AI workflows with Aurora, MCP, and AgentCore
speaker: Shayon Sanyal, Aditya Samant
abstract: How do you take an AI agent from a local prototype to a governed application that recovers from failure? In this session, follow a reference application through five phases: querying business data with SQL, connecting agents to Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, adding hybrid retrieval, deploying to production, and enabling durable workflows. See how Aurora PostgreSQL unifies relational data, pgvector embeddings, full-text search, and workflow state. Explore Strands Agents on Bedrock AgentCore, verify identity and enforce row-level security for data access, and govern tool calls with AgentCore Policy. Code walkthroughs show recovery from saved steps, idempotency to prevent duplicate actions, and audit records that make outcomes traceable.

title: Build the Agentic Workplace: What's New on the Slack Developer Platform (sponsored by Salesforce)
speaker: Josh Milas
abstract: Slack is becoming a multiplayer work operating system, where humans and AI agents build together, not just chat. This session shows AWS developers how to ship on the modern Slack Platform: Code Channels, a new space where agents like Claude Code, Devin, and Cursor collaborate with teams in real time; the Slack Agent Kit for building first-class agents; deep bidirectional MCP support, including the Slackbot MCP Client; Real-Time Search (RTS) for grounding agents in live workspace context; and Block Kit for rich, interactive UI. Leave with a clear path to build your first agentic app on Slack. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Build the full agent optimization loop on AgentCore
speaker: Rajesh Kumar Ravi, Ben Coombs
abstract: How do you know your agent is still performing? Stop guessing. This workshop walks you through the full optimization loop on AgentCore: instrument with OpenTelemetry traces, score with built-in and custom evaluators, generate data-backed recommendations that rewrite your system prompt or tool descriptions, validate offline with batch evaluation, then split live traffic with A/B testing through AgentCore Gateway until you have statistical confidence to promote. You will run every step hands-on, ship a measurably better agent configuration, and leave with a repeatable process that replaces guess-and-check prompt iteration with evidence.

title: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
speaker: Chris Haddad, Umair Khalid, Brian Warwick, Laks Sundararajan, MIRZA BAIG
abstract: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Build the right inference strategy on Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Chintan Vyas, Aswath Ram A Srinivasan
abstract: Generative AI workloads place very different demands on inference. Customer support chatbots and coding assistants may prioritize responsiveness, while large-scale document processing can favor greater cost efficiency. Some workloads can tolerate flexible processing times, while others need predictable capacity and performance. Healthcare applications may also need inference processing to remain within a specific geography. Learn how to match Amazon Bedrock inference offerings to different workload needs, balancing performance and cost while meeting data residency requirements.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Build the Right Next Thing: A Forward Deployed Approach to AI ROI (sponsored by Slalom)
speaker: Mike Ostrowski
abstract: Two years ago, standing up generative AI technology was the hard part. Today, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore make the path to production more straightforward—but technology alone does not create value. AI initiatives often stall because ROI is undefined and business, user, and technical priorities are disconnected. Learn how Slalom’s Forward Deployed Expertise (FDX) model places a cross-functional team spanning product, business, industry, UX, and technology alongside customers. Using real data, these teams compare opportunities, prioritize the highest-value use cases, and co-build the right next thing through production, adoption, and measurable outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Slalom, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Build-time context for faster agentic incident response
speaker: Jared Nance, Arun Chandapillai
abstract: AI agents can fix production issues, but only with the right context. In this talk, an AI agent builds a feature and, in the same pull request, creates the context it needs on call: instrumentation, alarms, dashboards, and skills, all as code. Then you break the live app. Watch an agent use those skills with Amazon CloudWatch Omni and AWS DevOps Agent to triage, find the root cause, and ship the fix. Leave with patterns that give agents the context to operate what they build.

title: Build Trust in AI with Agent Observability​ (sponsored by Splunk by Cisco)
speaker: Greg Leffler
abstract: AI agents behave (and fail) in unpredictable and nuanced ways that erode customer trust before engineering teams know anything is wrong. Teams want to deploy agents into critical business workflows, but it's hard to know if agents are behaving as intended or returning wrong answers.​ ​ In this talk, you’ll learn how to observe the entire AI stack, optimize tokenomics, and see a demo on how to evaluate and control agent behavior with guardrails to stop harmful or inaccurate outputs. All of this can be done in near real- time and at low cost.​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk by Cisco, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Build Voice AI experiences with Amazon Polly and Transcribe
speaker: Veerdhawal (Veer) Pande, Nikie Xiong, Suyin Wang
abstract: Give your applications a voice and ears. This session shows how Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text and Amazon Polly turns text into lifelike speech. See how to build real-time voice agents, and multilingual experiences, with practical patterns for latency, accuracy, and scale.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Build voice-enabled applications with Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe
speaker: Venkat Gomatham, Deepthi Devanira
abstract: We'll use Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe to add natural speech and accurate transcription to your applications. With Polly, you'll build expressive, emotionally engaged voices using its generative and long-form engines, covering streaming audio, speech marks for word-level timing, and newscaster styles. With Transcribe, you'll turn speech into text for captions, search, and analytics, handling real-time streaming and batch workloads. We'll show how these services work together to power voice agents, accessibility features, and conversational experiences, giving your applications the ability to both speak and listen naturally across a wide range of use cases and customer scenarios.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Build What’s Next with an AI-Ready Programmable Network (sponsored by Lumen)
speaker: Marc Andre Oriani
abstract: As AI, cloud, and data-intensive applications reshape business, infrastructure must become as dynamic as the workloads it supports. In this session, Lumen explores how programmable networking helps organizations simplify connectivity, improve performance, and securely scale across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments. Learn how real-time network orchestration gives teams greater agility and control while accelerating AI and modernization initiatives. Through examples, including Lumen’s collaboration with AWS to streamline enterprise connectivity, discover how a programmable network creates the resilient digital foundation needed to build what’s next. This presentation is brought to you by Lumen, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Build Your Agentic Transformation Roadmap with AWS Transform
speaker: Apoorva Kulkarni, kevin shin
abstract: You want to adopt agentic AI, but with hundreds of applications at different maturity levels, knowing where to start is the real challenge. In this chalk talk, we'll work through a practical framework for turning AWS Transform's automated agentic readiness and modernization analyses into a phased transformation plan. You'll see how to interpret portfolio-level scores, prioritize applications by business value and technical debt, sequence work into actionable phases, and connect readiness gaps to concrete next steps. Bring your portfolio challenges — you'll leave with a prioritization approach you can apply immediately

title: Build your AI data pipeline to Amazon S3 and Bedrock
speaker: Cy Hopkins, Allyn Henderson
abstract: Agentic AI applications are only as good as the data supporting them, and that data often lives across on-premises systems, other clouds, and distributed AWS storage. In this workshop, you'll build an end-to-end pipeline that moves data from these sources into Amazon S3 and connects it to Amazon Bedrock to build agentic applications. You'll configure data movement services including Storage Gateway, DataSync, and Transfer Family, establish secure transfer patterns, and integrate your migrated data into a gen AI workflow. Leave with a working architecture pattern for scalable data lakes that feed AI applications, grounded in real-world migration and processing scenarios.

title: Build your controls strategy org-wide to accelerate innovation
speaker: Oscar Diaz Cordovez, Paul Y Wu
abstract: AWS Organizations policies drive governance through native service integrations. In this session, explore service control policies and resource control policies for data perimeters. Use declarative policies to enforce resource configurations, such as Amazon S3 public access restrictions, and centralize AWS Security Hub settings org-wide. Deploy AWS Config organizational rules and conformance packs for continuous compliance, leverage multi-party approval, enforce best practices via the AWS Control Tower controls catalog, and explore automated compliance assessments. Leave with a governance architecture driven by policy integrations.

title: Build your own crew: hands-on with Kiro Crew
speaker: Ryan Tan, Megan Sattler
abstract: Kiro Crew is an open-source, multi-agent workspace you can bend to your own workflows. In this hands-on workshop, you'll put it to work. Hand your crew a real task and watching it plan, spawn parallel subagents, and gate each action for your approval. Then personalize: wire in the tools you already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold. Finally, assemble a purpose-built App to run a workflow end-to-end, from intake through review. You must bring your laptop to participate.

Then personalize: wire in the tools you already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold. Finally, assemble a purpose-built App to run a workflow end-to-end, from intake through review. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Built by Agents: Rethinking Reliability for AI-Native Companies (sponsored by Traversal)
speaker: Anish Agarwal
abstract: AI is changing how quickly software can be built, shipped, and scaled. For AI-native companies, that can mean more services and complexity earlier in their growth. Many traditional reliability practices were designed for a different pace, when teams had more time to document, instrument, and build operational knowledge as they scaled. This conversation brings together leaders from a fast-growing legal AI company and one of the world’s largest digital banks, alongside leaders from Traversal, the AI SRE that diagnoses, fixes, and prevents incidents across enterprise environments. They’ll discuss how AI is changing development and operations, new failure modes in AI-native systems, how lean teams approach reliability as they scale, and the role of AI SREs in a broader shift toward AI understanding, managing, and improving production systems. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Canva's migration to AWS Graviton: from 2% to 54% in 10 months
speaker: Lucky Ray, Rory McCormick
abstract: Canva shifted its massive compute fleet from 2% to 23% Graviton adoption in just two months, then scaled to 54% over the following eight months, delivering meaningful cost savings and performance improvements along the way. This session covers the technical blockers the team encountered and overcame and the strategies that made rapid migration possible at enterprise scale. Walk away with practical, battle-tested patterns for planning and executing large-scale Arm migrations, whether you're just getting started or looking to accelerate an existing effort.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Can You Stop ALTERED SPIDER? A Live AWS Cloud Breach Challenge (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
speaker: Allie Barnes, Jay Flora
abstract: The breach is underway. Watch CrowdStrike Experts put cloud detection and response into action during a live, audience-driven investigation of a simulated AWS intrusion. They will uncover evidence, determine the next move, and capture flags hidden across identities, workloads, and cloud activity. Get briefed on cloud-focused adversary ALTERED SPIDER, then connect the clues, contain the threat, and stop the attack. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.

title: Capital One's WorkSpaces Journey: 320 to 20,000 Desktops in 72hrs
speaker: Joshua Schlumpberger, Rafael Blanco, Valeria Pascucci
abstract: Learn how to achieve enterprise-scale cloud desktop deployment from Capital One, who went from 320 manual provisions per day to 20,000 compliant desktops in 72 hours. Gain production-tested architectural patterns for meeting compliance requirements without slowing delivery. You'll also get a first look at the latest WorkSpaces innovations and our vision for the future of cloud desktops, including how we're expanding what's possible for IT teams managing modern workloads at scale. This session is for those migrating from VDI, scaling an existing fleet, or planning for what's next.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Capturing the chaos - observability for agentic applications on Amazon EKS
abstract: Observability for Agentic Applications on Amazon EKS looks at what breaks when your monitoring was built for deterministic services and your workload isn't. The same prompt might trigger one tool call or twenty, and finish in seconds or wait days for approval. Using OpenTelemetry, we follow an agentic request end to end, with metrics that catch runaway loops and attribute token cost, logs that hold prompts without overwhelming storage, and traces you can tell are complete. We then decide what to keep and what to believe: sampling, evaluating agent output, and which spans to trust. You'll leave with patterns and guardrails for moving from prototype to production.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Catch it before production: Instrument your AI agents
speaker: Siddhesh Kumbhare, Puneeth Ranjan Komaragiri
abstract: You need visibility into your AI workloads before they reaches production, not after they fails, yet most teams have no telemetry on their agents at all. In this workshop, you instrument a live AI agent end to end, capturing token cost, latency, tool calls, and reasoning traces. You make the instrumentation decisions, build the dashboards and anomaly alerts. Leave with a working setup you can apply to your own agentic workloads.

title: Catch risky changes and triage incidents with AWS DevOps Agent in AWS Startup Advisor
speaker: Sean Helmes, Saket Gupta
abstract: Downtime can cost startups customers, yet early-stage teams rarely staff a dedicated operations engineer, even as they own both release safety and on-call. The AWS DevOps Agent, delivered through AWS Startup Advisor, runs inside the IDEs and coding agents engineers already use. It surfaces risky changes before they ship and helps triage production incidents by correlating signals, suggesting likely causes, and guiding remediation, all without a context switch. In this chalk talk, we trace one release and incident scenario end to end on the whiteboard, covering agent setup and cost model. Bring your on-call questions and we'll pressure-test it against your stack.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: CDK Lovers: Meetup for AWS CDK Contributors & Power Users
abstract: Calling all AWS CDK lovers! Whether you're a CDK user, construct library author, or aws-cdk contributor, join fellow enthusiasts for a discussion-driven meetup. In small table groups, we'll dig into three themes: what we love about CDK, the pain points we hit in real projects, and the improvements we'd like to see, especially as AI coding agents change how we write and review infrastructure code. Share your war stories, swap construct design and testing tips, and leave with new peers in the CDK community and maybe a few ideas worth turning into your next contribution.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries
speaker: Mark Jones, Jennifer Tipecska
abstract: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.

title: Centralize AWS PrivateLink endpoints at scale with Amazon VPC Lattice
speaker: Henning Schroeder, Victor Babasanmi, Mankaran Singh, Tega Odjegba, Kimberley Clements
abstract: Organizations scaling across multiple AWS accounts need AWS PrivateLink endpoints in every VPC, driving up costs and fragmenting access controls. In this session, construct a centralized endpoint architecture in a shared services VPC and expose endpoints to consumers through Amazon VPC Lattice. Configure resource gateways to front endpoints and custom domain names to simplify DNS management, which eliminates Amazon Route 53 Profiles or manual records. Learn how to layer in fine-grained access controls that scale with your environment. Walk away with a deployable pattern for endpoint consolidation at scale.

title: Centralized governance for multicloud environments
speaker: Craig Edwards, Simone Pomata
abstract: When AI agents and automated pipelines ship changes across AWS, Azure, and other providers in minutes, governance that runs on separate toolchains can't keep pace. You end up with disparate security findings along with mis-aligned operational metrics, and a team that spends its time reconciling dashboards instead of actually reducing risk. In this session, see how to collapse multicloud governance into a single operating model across AWS and Azure, leveraging Amazon CloudWatch unified telemetry for centralized observability and AWS Security Hub for aggregated findings into a single surface.You'll walk through a deployable architecture that gives one analyst a unified view across clouds, so your governance moves at the same speed your engineering teams already do.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: CEO Keynote
speaker: Barbara Karuth-Zelle, Matt Garman, Tony Xu
abstract: Join AWS CEO Matt Garman for the re:Invent 2026 CEO Keynote as he shares the latest innovations powering the agentic era. From AI infrastructure and inference to data, agent platforms, and the software agents AWS is building, see how AWS gives you the depth, breadth, and integration to build what's next with new announcements and stories from customers already doing it.

title: Champagne AI on a beer budget: Cost-optimized AI architectures live
speaker: Mike George, Shawn Abdi
abstract: A surprise cloud bill can wipe out a nonprofit's budget, but running frontier-quality generative AI doesn't have to cost frontier prices. In this code talk, we build an architecture that gets premium model output on a fraction of the spend. Starting with a naïve workload where every request hits the same large model, we layer in routing to send requests to the lowest-cost model meeting the quality bar, caching to reduce token counts, and token budgets with kill switches that gracefully degrade. You'll leave with working code your engineers can implement, and your finance team won't panic over.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Change. Wait. Debug. Let AI drive the infrastructure loop. (sponsored by HashiCorp)
speaker: Kyle Ruddy, Cole Morrison
abstract: Make a change. Deploy it. Wait. Dig through the logs. Try again. For years, that loop has cost infrastructure engineers countless hours—time that could be spent shipping what comes next. In this session, discover how to take engineers out of the routine operational loop without giving up oversight. Define the outcome, let AI work through the iterations, and step back in only when a real decision needs you. See the pattern in action with Terraform, Vault, Kubernetes, Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, and more.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Chaos engineering: Network fault injection with Gateway Load Balancer
speaker: Gonzalo Escarra, Harold Morales, Anuj Saxena, Elshan Hasanov, Rob Fulton
abstract: Your application works perfectly in the lab, but what happens with 45ms latency and 0.1% packet loss? In this session, deploy a transparent network fault simulator using AWS Gateway Load Balancer and Linux Traffic Control (TC) on Amazon EC2. Inject delay, jitter, packet loss, and bandwidth constraints into live traffic, then observe how a tightly coupled application degrades in real time. Use the results to set SLA thresholds, validate AWS Direct Connect failover behavior, and justify architectural decisions. Leave with a reusable, parameterized emulator pattern deployable via AWS Systems Manager.

title: Choosing a game server instance without guessing
speaker: Jake Wolf, Santiago Cardenas
abstract: Most game studios pick server instances by vibes. This chalk talk replaces that with a number you measure on your game: cost per player at your tick rate. At the whiteboard we answer three questions: what does one tick cost, how many players fit, and what does a player cost? You’ll see how to time the whole tick in Unreal Engine and Unity, load a server with bots or thin clients against a failure rule set up front, and repeat across instances. Then we share what we measured on modern Amazon EC2 instances across AWS Graviton, AMD, and Intel: where clock speed pays, and where price decides.

title: Choosing the right AWS storage for low-latency workloads
speaker: John Mallory, Mike Houle
abstract: Not all latency-sensitive workloads have the same storage requirements. From AI/ML training checkpoints to real-time analytics and high-frequency data pipelines, choosing between Amazon S3 Express One Zone, Amazon FSx for Lustre, and instance storage depends on access patterns, throughput needs, and cost constraints. In this chalk talk, we break down the decision framework for selecting low-latency storage across common workload types. Bring your architecture questions as we compare directory buckets, parallel file systems, and caching strategies side by side. Leave with a clear mental model for matching your performance requirements to the right AWS storage tier.

title: Choosing the right AWS storage service
speaker: Christian Smith, Hiren Chandiramani
abstract: AWS storage spans block, file, and object services alongside purpose-built storage for vectors, tables, and migration, each optimized for distinct access patterns, latency requirements, and cost profiles. Choosing the most efficient option can help you reduce complexity, over-provisioning, or rearchitecting later. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts walk you through a decision framework based on workload characteristics, not product names. Bring your architecture questions and work through real scenarios interactively. You will leave with a clear mental model for matching workloads to storage services and the confidence to make the right decision as your requirements evolve.

title: Choosing the right hybrid deployment for your AI workloads
speaker: Shivam Saggar, Shelby Seward, Hai Lu, Chris McEvilly
abstract: Organizations are running AI workloads for model training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning and inference, across an expanding set of environments, including AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, AWS Outposts, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS AI Factories. The right deployment option depends on latency, data sovereignty, compute density, and scale. See how customers deploy accelerated AI across the hybrid spectrum: NVIDIA GPU-based and AWS Trainium-powered instances in Local Zones, purpose-built AWS AI Factories for large-scale training and model serving, and edge deployments for real-time inference. Hear how customers navigate these decisions, including Databricks tapping GPU capacity on AWS Local Zones and T-Mobile running latency-sensitive distributed inference, and learn which environment fits each AI workload without compromising performance and compliance.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Citizens Bank: Building AI-Native CX from Vision to Production
speaker: Sheila Smith
abstract: Financial services customers expect fast, personalized service, but compliance, security, and regulatory requirements make automation a high-stakes challenge. Discover how Amazon Connect Customer enables financial institutions to design agentic customer experiences, where AI self-service blends autonomous reasoning with deterministic guardrails for identity verification, fraud checks, and regulatory disclosures. Learn how business teams, not only engineers, build and refine these experiences, automating complex interactions like account servicing, disputes, and payments while maintaining full compliance and governance. See how Citizens Bank lifted containment by 30 points, elevated CSAT, and transformed their contact center without compromising trust.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: Claude Code: From first feature to optimized agentic workflows (sponsored by Anthropic)
speaker: Alex Weeden, Shan Kandaswamy
abstract: Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. Point it at a codebase and choose your path, self-paced in the browser on Amazon Bedrock. In the Build with Claude track, give Claude project context, explore an unfamiliar repository, then plan, implement, and test a change you watch run - no experience required. In the Scale with Agents track, orchestrate parallel subagents across an agentic app, add review and verification gates, then apply Anthropic-authored skills to improve its performance and lower cost. Terminal experience assumed. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed. Labs are 30-60 min. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Innovation Labs

title: Claude It Your Way: Anthropic on AWS
speaker: Ayan Ray
abstract: Your teams want Claude for coding, agents, and knowledge work, and there are more ways than ever to reach it. This session maps every path to Anthropic on AWS. Start with the models, served two ways: Amazon Bedrock, with Haiku for speed, Sonnet for balance, and Opus for long-running agentic work, or Claude Platform on AWS for Anthropic's first-party API. Add applications on top: Claude Code for agentic development, Claude Desktop for broader knowledge work. Govern both with the Claude apps gateway, one control plane across them. See how these layers fit your teams' needs.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Claude Keeps Building: How Coding Agents Change Software Development (sponsored by Anthropic)
speaker: Morgan Lunt
abstract: Coding agents make sustained, autonomous progress on real software. The question is what happens to the rest of the software development lifecycle. Claude Code runs for hours unattended, works beyond the terminal, and takes on more of the work around the code. We'll show where it stands and how engineering changes when the whole lifecycle becomes automatable: what engineers do, how review and testing evolve, where quality comes from when code is cheap. Live demos on AWS and numbers from our engineering, where Claude writes most of our code. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.

title: Cleared for Takeoff Hybrid Observability at the Busiest Airport (sponsored by SolarWinds)
speaker: Cedric Reed, Gregory Fetterhoff
abstract: Managing over a thousand network nodes across terminals, baggage systems, and cloud infrastructure requires more than reactive troubleshooting. Join Cedric Reed, Network Administrator at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, and SolarWinds to discover how the world’s busiest airport replaced manual oversight with proactive observability. Learn how unified visibility across on-premises hardware and AWS Cloud eliminates noise, reduces downtime, and keeps critical systems online for millions of daily travelers. Discover how hop-by-hop visualization and real-time telemetry seamlessly monitor a vast network of surveillance systems covering the entire 7-mile campus to optimize operational resilience and passenger safety. This presentation is brought to you by SolarWinds, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: CLI Agent Orchestrator: Open source multi-agent AI for developer CLIs
speaker: Anil Kumar, Haofei Feng, Augusto Dias, Stan Fan, Joe Guo
abstract: Complex projects outgrow a single AI agent's context and capability. CLI Agent Orchestrator (CAO), an awslabs open source project, coordinates 8 CLIs including Amazon Kiro CLI, Claude Code, and Codex into a multi-agent powerhouse via the Model Context Protocol and tmux. It provides a centralised harness with shared skills, memory, and integration with OpenClaw and Hermes Agent. In this builders' session you'll install CAO, launch a supervisor and specialist agents, and put the team to work on a real change in a sample repo. You'll walk away with a multi-agent workflow to drop into your projects.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Clinical Trials, Reimagined at the Speed of AI (sponsored by PwC)
speaker: Sidd Bhattacharya, Chuck Liu, Terry Morris
abstract: Bringing a new drug to market takes over a decade, and much of that time is lost to paperwork rather than science. In this session, you'll learn how pharma leaders Eli Lilly and AbbVie are transforming clinical development with agentic AI on AWS. Attendees will hear how PwC’s Digital Trial Core turns clinical protocols into structured, machine-readable data, powering AI agents that draw on historical insights and reusable, modular content to streamline study startup activities such as vendor selection, budgeting, negotiations, and trial documentation. Industry leaders will share how these solutions move from proof of concept into live studies, bringing treatments to patients sooner. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Close the gap between alert and resolution without growing your security team
speaker: Himanshu Verma, Ryan Holland
abstract: For most security teams, the delay sits in manual triage and tool switching after an alert. This chalk talk covers the newest AWS detection and response capabilities, including enhanced threat detection, automated vulnerability management, and AI-assisted security operations, and how they shorten the time between finding a risk and resolving it. We work through how to connect AWS security services across AWS and your other clouds so the team you already have can resolve findings faster.

title: Close the loop: From guardrail blocks into layered defense
speaker: Sanghwa Na, Wei Chen, Jason Schamp, Jonathan Woods, Patrick Duffy
abstract: Guardrails block malicious prompts. Every blocked attempt is a signal: proof of what your defenses caught and a clue toward what will be attempted next. Capture that signal instead of discarding it. In this session, you design and deploy a layered enforcement architecture that closes the loop. A stateful detection tier identifies repeated probing across sessions and propagates block decisions to the network edge. You evaluate signals from guardrail violations and apply policies to classify and block the threat. You leave with a deployed pattern applicable to any AI agent workload. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Closing the academic advising gap with AI agents
speaker: Nityanand Singh, Maria John
abstract: Universities lose students to inadequate academic advising: advisors are overwhelmed, and students wait days for answers. In this chalk talk, we explore the end-to-end architecture of an AI student advising agent: specifying and building the agents with Kiro on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, connecting it to student record systems via MCP, adding guardrails for sensitive student welfare queries, and surfacing the agents to students through AWS Quick embedded in their existing LMS. We'll whiteboard real-world advising scenarios, turn them into agents you can evaluate, and discuss the trade-offs between automation and human escalation.

title: Closing the compliance loop when agents change your infrastructure
speaker: David Sokolik, JaQuan Thompson
abstract: AI agents and automated pipelines now change your infrastructure faster than any review can keep up, and not every change comes through CloudFormation. In this workshop, you'll close the compliance loop end to end: author a CloudFormation Hook that enforces encryption and tagging before deployment, then extend the same logic into an AWS Config custom rule with CloudFormation Guard so out-of-band changes get caught continuously. You'll build auto-remediation with SSM Automation, package it into a Conformance Pack for org-wide reach, and use Resource Timeline to trace drift. You leave able to keep compliance closed however fast change arrives.

title: Closing the Loop: How Cognition’s AI Continuously Improves Itself (sponsored by Datadog)
speaker: Whitney Lee
abstract: As AI accelerates software development, production systems are changing faster than teams can understand manually. Cognition is closing that gap by giving Devin, its software engineering AI agent running on AWS, access to its own production telemetry through Datadog. Devin uses that context to reason about its production behavior and take action when needed. That feedback loop turns production insights into improvements to Devin’s reliability and future task performance. In this session, we’ll show how Devin investigates alerts, correlates metrics and logs, distinguishes real issues from noise, and uses those insights to improve its harness and workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Closing the loop: using frontier agents for continuous governance
speaker: Emir Ayar, Peter Grainger, Charles Roberts, Cameron Smith, Ryan Dsouza
abstract: Wire two AWS frontier agents into an automated find-and-fix security loop aligned to the Well-Architected Framework. AWS Security Agent pen-tests a web application and flags a privilege-escalation vulnerability. You author a DevOps Agent skill that queries findings through AWS Continuum MCP Server on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, correlating the operational symptom to the vulnerability in your codebase and generating a GitLab merge request, with human approval at every gate. Trigger the exploit, approve the fix, watch AWS Continuum revalidate it closed, and update your pipeline to block similar vulnerabilities before they reach customers. Automated detection, investigation, remediation, verification, and ongoing prevention closes the loop and provides continuous governance.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Cloud agent work needs infrastructure. We built it. (sponsored by Asana)
speaker: Amritansh Raghav, Arnab Bose
abstract: Organizations need an operating layer where humans and agents can run critical workflows together. That’s Asana. As software development shifts toward work performed by agents in the cloud, engineering teams need the same connected approach at enterprise scale. Command brings Asana’s operating layer to engineering, giving developers one surface for project management and coding work—connecting planning, assignment, and execution across the organization. Command works with coding agents teams already use, including Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. See the challenges Command solves for product and engineering teams and how it works against real engineering workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Asana, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Cloud governance from complexity to control
abstract: Multi-account estates and autonomous agents are outgrowing manual governance. This discussion covers policy enforcement across accounts, automated compliance evidence, and where agentic AI can take over routine governance operations. Compare how teams keep central control while giving builders room to move.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Cloud migration journey tabletop experience
abstract: Experience a dynamic simulation of leading a digital transformation initiative. Navigate cloud migration, security automation, and operational excellence challenges. Architect secure cloud environments while balancing stakeholder needs and compliance. Compete to optimize speed, security, and innovation amid real-world obstacles. Gain actionable insights into cloud security governance and risk-aligned architecture.

title: Cloud migration journey tabletop experience
abstract: Experience a dynamic simulation of leading a digital transformation initiative. Navigate cloud migration, security automation, and operational excellence challenges. Architect secure cloud environments while balancing stakeholder needs and compliance. Compete to optimize speed, security, and innovation amid real-world obstacles. Gain actionable insights into cloud security governance and risk-aligned architecture. Walk-ins welcome.

title: Cloud-native Java on Amazon EKS
speaker: Andrei Shakirin, Dumitru Pascu, Yuriy Bezsonov, Sascha Moellering, Laura Schlosser
abstract: Learn how to build cloud-native Java applications based on best practices, and discover ways you can optimize application performance for fast startup and efficient resource usage in containerized environments. In this builders’ session, gain hands-on experience as you learn how to reduce memory overhead, lower cold start latency, and achieve sub-second startup times when building Java applications on Amazon EKS. You will also learn how to use Amazon Bedrock to analyze profiling and thread dump data to uncover performance patterns and generate optimization insights.

title: Cloud-Ready Checklist: What Providers Need to Know Before Migrating
abstract: Thinking about migrating your EHR or other mission-critical workloads to the cloud? Join Matt Dinger, Global Epic Lead, and Angela Shippy, Senior Physician Executive, for an informal, open-floor meetup designed to help provider organizations prepare. Drawing on lessons from large-scale health system migrations, this session tackles the questions you should be asking before you start — from infrastructure readiness and security planning to data strategy, governance, clinician preparedness, and partner alignment. Whether early in evaluation or finalizing your approach, bring your toughest questions and leave with practical guidance to move forward with confidence.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Cocktails to Code Building AI Bartenders with Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Jimmy Dahlqvist
abstract: Plain-language AI orders fail if models hallucinate items that are out of stock. I built a reliable AI bartender grounded strictly in live inventory data. This session covers how an AI agent on Amazon Bedrock uses Strands Agents, AgentCore, and MCP tools to fetch real-time menus. We will dive into the serverless architecture, see what breaks during live text streaming, and evaluate the cost versus performance tradeoffs of production grounding. You will leave with a reusable pattern and the repository to build reliable, data-driven agents.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Code real-time multi-agent AI systems with Amazon ElastiCache
speaker: Kevin McGehee, Elad Bernstein
abstract: Modern algorithmic trading platforms deploy fleets of specialized AI agents, including market analysts, risk assessors, order executors, and compliance monitors, that must coordinate in real time without conflict. In this session, follow along as a trading platform's multi-agent workflows are coded live using Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey. Valkey Streams organize agent task queues, pub/sub channels broadcast market signals to agent swarms with low latency, and vector similarity search gives agents memory of prior market scenarios. Discover how atomic Lua scripts prevent duplicate orders and enable exactly-once workflow transitions.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Coding an AI agent from scratch with AWS Lambda durable functions
speaker: Serda Kasaci Yildirim, Rana Kiziltoprak German
abstract: AI agents need multi-step reasoning, tool execution, human approvals, and long-running waits, all while keeping resilient state across failures. In this code talk, we build an AI agent from scratch using Lambda Durable Functions. You'll see how to implement a tool-use loop, add retries with exponential backoff, pause for human approval without paying for idle time, and recover cleanly from a mid-execution failure. We'll experiment with agent suspend and resume live, and watch it resume from a checkpoint deterministically. Leave with production-ready patterns for building stateful AI agents using familiar programming constructs.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Coding event-driven retry patterns that prevent outages
speaker: Patrick Meiler, Dirk Fröhner
abstract: In this code talk, you'll instrument an event-driven integration layer with the patterns that contain failure: exponential backoff with jitter, circuit breakers, poison-pill isolation, and replay-from-archive - all live, in code. See how jittered retries prevent thundering herds, how circuit breakers protect healthy services from impaired ones, and how idempotency makes every replay safe. By the end, you'll have hands-on patterns for EventBridge and Step Functions that shrink your blast radius from total outage to graceful degradation.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Coding high-throughput data pipelines with AWS Lambda durable functions
speaker: Tom Romano, Matt Kahn
abstract: Processing large datasets usually means hand-wiring queues, coordinators, and state tracking. In this code talk, we live-build a high-throughput data pipeline with Lambda durable functions instead. You'll see the fan-out/fan-in pattern in code: split a large dataset across parallel durable executions, isolate and retry the branches that fail without reprocessing the ones that succeeded, and offload checkpoints to S3 so a job too big for a single invocation survives restarts. We'll tune concurrency to protect a downstream database from overload, then compare the durable-functions approach with other design patterns on both developer velocity and cost. Leave with patterns you can apply to your own data workloads immediately.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Coding the tool layer for AI agents on Serverless
speaker: Jacob Cravinho, Matt Boland
abstract: Agents don't need new infrastructure - they need access to what you've already built. In this code talk, you'll retrofit a Serverless API into a production-ready agent tool, live in code. Implement an MCP server with versioned tools, wire it to AgentCore Gateway for discovery and invocation, then expose an entire Step Functions workflow, human-in-the-loop gates and all, as a single callable tool. Add scoped agent identity, watch an unauthorized call get blocked, then an authorized one go through. Walk away with a repeatable playbook for turning existing APIs into agent-ready tools.

title: Compete to build an AI agent with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
speaker: Xavier Loup, Laurent Guizard
abstract: Organizations are ready to move beyond rule-based workflows to agents that reason, adapt, and act. In this gamified workshop, you'll use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to assemble a realistic conversational banking agent end-to-end: orchestration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness; secure tool integration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway; and guardrails with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy. Prebuilt modules accelerate development so you can focus on agent logic. Compete in real time as your agent's accuracy and efficiency are scored on a live leaderboard. Leave with a working agent pattern you can adapt to your own use cases and bragging rights on the leaderboard.

title: Composable Agentic AI: Build Your Partner Offerings for Enterprises
speaker: Sindhura Palakodety, Sujatha Kuppuraju
abstract: Enterprises deploying agents in production are converging on a common pattern: distributed systems with stable layer contracts, bounded autonomy, and security and observability built in from day one. That raises a concrete question for AWS partners - does your product plug into the architecture your customers are already standardizing on? In this hands-on workshop for ISVs and consulting partners, you'll learn the composable Enterprise Agentic AI Reference Architecture, see exactly where your product fits at each layer, and build alongside AWS GenAI services, that compose into a single coherent production system. You'll leave with working reference code for an enterprise-ready agentic architecture and a playbook for co-building on the AWS agentic stack.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano I

title: Composing the right orchestration for serverless workflows
speaker: Dan Ronald
abstract: Both AWS Lambda durable functions and AWS Step Functions handle retries, long-running execution, and failure recovery - so how do you choose? In this session, we cut through the confusion with a clear decision framework across three scenarios: human-in-the-loop approvals, long-running AI agent workflows, and multi-service sagas. We'll also show a hybrid pattern where Durable Functions handle inner business logic while Step Functions orchestrate at the macro level - code-level flexibility inside, visual observability outside. Leave with a practical framework and a real production example to guide your next serverless workflow decision.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Compute innovation with the AWS Nitro System
speaker: Sudeep Sharma, Filippo Sironi
abstract: The AWS Nitro System has fundamentally changed how we build and deliver EC2 instances, accelerating our pace of compute innovation while improving security and performance for customers. This session explores the Nitro architecture and the latest innovations it enables: multi-host for smaller metal sizes, reduced blast radius, higher performance, how Nitro has helped us in accelerating the pace of innovation, and delivering Flex instances. We'll dive deep into how the Nitro System continues to push the boundaries of what's possible in cloud compute.

title: Computing‑Power‑Cooling Synergy: Building the Future of Global Data Infrastructure (sponsored by Kehua Tech)
speaker: Lane Peng
abstract: The rapid growth of AI workloads is driving new demands for large-scale data center infrastructure, with challenges in power supply, high-density cooling, and system integration. In this session, we will share real-world deployment practices and introduce end-to-end infrastructure solutions, including highly reliable UPS power systems, liquid cooling technologies, and turnkey integrated solutions. We will explore how computing, power, and cooling synergy can optimize data center efficiency, improve deployment agility, and accelerate the development of AI-ready infrastructure. This presentation is brought to you by Kehua Tech, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Configure Security & Governance Controls for AWS Quick
speaker: Leo Mentis Raj Selvaraj, Marshall Bunch
abstract: Implement comprehensive security and administrative controls for AWS Quick. Practice configuring identity integration, access policies, and data governance frameworks. Learn to establish monitoring, auditing, and compliance controls that meet enterprise requirements. Work through scenarios covering user management, content governance, and security best practices for Quick Suite environments in production.

title: Connect agents across frameworks live using the A2A open protocol
speaker: Saurav Mohanty, Madhukiran J
abstract: Agents built on different frameworks need to talk to each other. In this session we will build two agents on Strands and LangGraph, then wire them together using the A2A protocol hosted at the Linux Foundation. You will see the full handshake: AgentCard publication for discovery, task negotiation, streaming artifact exchange, and multi-turn collaboration between agents that share nothing except the protocol. We will deploy both sides on AgentCore Runtime and demonstrate cross-framework interoperability working live. You will leave with the patterns to make any framework's agents collaborate over a standard wire.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Connect and secure service-to-service networking on Amazon ECS
speaker: Radhika Nayar, Irene Garcia Lopez, Danilo Silva, Pedro Henrique Oliveira, Henrique Santana
abstract: When your containerized services grow beyond a single cluster, networking becomes the bottleneck. Security groups block health checks, cross-VPC traffic needs custom solutions, and encrypting traffic feels like a full-time job. In this builder's session, configure secure service-to-service communication on Amazon ECS using Service Connect for discovery and encryption, VPC Lattice for cross-account connectivity, and load balancer patterns for external traffic. Implement end-to-end TLS, test failover between services, and observe traffic flows in real time. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Connect Decisions Fireside Chat: Samsung and TE Connectivity on agentic supply chains
speaker: Jeet Dattani, Gautam Kamdar, Ozgur Dogan
abstract: Only 25% of organizations feel ready to prevent disruptions, and 85% take two weeks or more to resolve urgent ones. In this fireside chat, supply chain leaders from Samsung and TE Connectivity join AWS to discuss the challenges enterprises face across industries such as automotive and consumer electronics manufacturing. Samsung plans demand across hundreds of thousands of product and market combinations every week. Hear how Connect Decisions AI agents take on the planning work itself, reasoning across sales history, market signals and product relationships to make and explain decisions at that scale. TE Connectivity will share how Connect Decisions AI agents works across 200,000 SKUs to surface stockouts and cash tied up in inventory that its ERP does not see. Get a firsthand view of what it takes, hurdles included, and walk away with a practical path forward.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Connect everything, everywhere: AWS global connectivity
speaker: Shridhar Kulkarni, Sidhartha Chauhan
abstract: Point solutions don't scale globally. Stitching together and managing dozens of them creates gaps. In this session, discover what's new in AWS Cloud WAN and AWS Direct Connect: simplified hybrid connectivity, smarter segmentation, and real-time visibility across global traffic. See how AWS Cloud WAN's policy engine and AWS Direct Connect's latest capabilities combine to deliver seamless connectivity from anywhere to anywhere. Discover patterns to build a borderless, resilient global network.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Connectivity strategies across AWS Partitions
speaker: Kunal Kumar Sharma, Rohit Aswani
abstract: Organizations increasingly operate across AWS commercial, GovCloud, Sovereign Cloud, and China Regions to satisfy regulatory, data residency, and national security requirements. But connecting them introduces networking challenges that go well beyond standard multi-Region design. In this session, learn cross-partition connectivity patterns using AWS Site-to-Site VPN, AWS Direct Connect, and application-layer proxies alongside DNS resolution strategies, compliance boundary enforcement, and operational trade-offs. We walk through architectural blueprints for securely linking partitions while preserving the isolation guarantees they exist to enforce, and share lessons learned from customers navigating ITAR, GDPR, and national sovereignty mandates at scale.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Connect NetApp FSx for ONTAP File Data to AI Apps with S3
speaker: Beerinder Mann, Sean Phuphanich, Nava Ajay Kanth Kota, Virgil Ennes, Jay Horne
abstract: Your AI workloads need enterprise data including documents, datasets, and unstructured content already sitting in ONTAP. The usual answer is to copy it to S3, build a sync pipeline, and hope nothing drifts. There's a better option. This session shows how to use FSx for ONTAP file shares directly via the S3 API so Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker can read them in place with no migration, no pipeline. Your existing access controls and data management policies stay intact. We'll cover the architecture, configuration steps, and how to pair ONTAP's data management capabilities with S3-based AI/ML services.

title: Connect your Amazon ECS services without the complexity
speaker: Simone Tallevi-Diotallevi, Henrique Santana
abstract: Service-to-service communication in containerized environments introduces routing, discovery, and encryption challenges. This chalk talk explores when to use Service Connect, VPC Lattice, load balancers, or direct service discovery on Amazon ECS and how to combine them as your architecture grows. Understand the trade-offs across latency, cost, and operational overhead so you can match the right pattern to each workload. Bring your architecture questions for an open technical discussion.

speaker: Joe Wagner, Jesse Lepich

In this code talk, join AWS Network Security experts as they walk through practical techniques, and new capabilities, to simplify rule-writing experience with AWS Network Firewall. Through live examples, learn to structure rule groups to meet common use cases and deploy according to best practices. This session will dive deep to keep policy writing easy to manage as your environment grows. Walk away with hands-on patterns you can apply immediately to tame rule complexity and ship changes with confidence.

title: Constrain AI agents with permissions boundaries and Cedar in AgentCore
speaker: Ravid Glam, David Sokolik
abstract: Your AI agents need permissions to be useful, and unconstrained permissions lead to unintended consequences. In this workshop, you build defense-in-depth governance for agentic workloads. You create scoped IAM execution roles with permissions boundaries, enforce mandatory Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through IAM policy, validate agent policies with IAM Access Analyzer, and add deterministic Cedar enforcement in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The result constrains what agents can do while still letting legitimate actions through.
