abstract: METR and Horizon3 debate containment versus defense as the right approach to securing AI agents in production. This session covers the tradeoffs between containing agent behavior through strict boundaries versus building defenses that let agents operate with more autonomy, and what security teams should weigh when deciding how to secure agents running in production environments.

title: Context engineering for agents: memory, SQL, knowledge graphs & skills
speaker: David H Gardner, Don Simpson
abstract: An agent's context window is a finite attention budget, and database-backed agents must keep that context current, selective, and traceable. In this session, architect solutions to trace a task as it builds context using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, Amazon Neptune, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Examine how agents cache hot state, retrieve operational rows, apply SQL filters, maintain vector and full-text indexes, refresh stale records, traverse knowledge-graph relationships, load skills, and discover MCP tools. Explore freshness policies, invalidation, provenance ledgers, access boundaries, and compaction patterns for production-grade agentic applications.

title: Context engineering for production agents on AgentCore
speaker: Phelipe Fabres, Noor Randhawa
abstract: An agent is only as good as what fills its context window. System prompts, skills, tool definitions, conversation history, retrieved documents, long-term memory, they all compete for limited space. Get the mix wrong and you waste tokens, degrade reasoning, or lose critical instructions mid-conversation. This chalk talk breaks down every layer of context that shapes agent behavior on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover how to structure system prompts, define skills effectively, manage tool context through gateway, retain the right conversation history, and use Memory strategies to persist what matters across sessions. Bring your agents, we optimize them live.

title: Context Over Code: Making AI-Native Development Work at Scale
speaker: Matt Houghton
abstract: AI coding assistants generate code quickly, but that's not the problem most teams need solved. After rolling out an AI coding companion to 150+ engineers, we learned the real unlock was rethinking how we work, not how fast we type. This session covers our path from AI code companion to AI-Driven Development Lifecycle: building a Context Store with Bedrock Knowledge Bases and MCP to surface decades of institutional knowledge, implementing steering and verification patterns, and managing the organizational change that makes AI-native development stick. You'll leave with a framework for scaling AI beyond individual productivity.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Continuous Attack Chains Across Every Surface (sponsored by Terra)
speaker: Ofek Haviv
abstract: Most security tools score vulnerabilities in isolation, but attackers do not think in isolation. This session shows how Terra continuously chains signals into real attack paths across web applications, APIs, AI systems, and network infrastructure using agentic AI, the same way a human adversary would pivot from one weak point to the next. Every proposed chain is validated by an expert human pentester before it becomes a finding, turning a pile of low severity noise into a small number of confirmed, exploitable risks. Learn how continuous, cross surface attack chaining changes what a security team should actually prioritize first. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) on AWS
speaker: Emil Lerch, Leo Zhadanovsky
abstract: Whether you're shipping a monolith or hundreds of microservices, every change needs to reach production safely and quickly. In this session, learn how to build a CI/CD pipeline with AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild using infrastructure as code. The pipeline will utilize AI agents running on Amazon Bedrock to review every change—pull requests and direct commits alike—for security flaws, code quality, architecture, and accessibility. The agents report what they find, while you write rules to determine whether ship...or stop. AWS CodeDeploy will orchestrate canary deployments that roll back automatically when an issue is detected by an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Controlling the AI Software Factory (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
abstract: AI isn't just making software faster; it's changing how software is produced. Engineering teams now run agents that write code, review PRs, validate releases, and deploy around the clock. The promise is real, but so is a new problem: how do you stay in control of systems that never stop evolving? Edith Harbaugh, CEO of LaunchDarkly, argues the defining challenge of the AI era isn't generating code, it's controlling autonomous systems in production, where agents drift and the old detect-fix-redeploy playbook breaks down. She and a panel of industry leaders will share what they’ve learned building their own AI software factories, and how engineers stay in charge.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Control what goes out: egress security for AI workloads
speaker: Bashuman Deb, Sofia Aluma, Akshay Choudhry
abstract: Most AWS workloads send traffic out in two ways, DNS queries and network connections, and attackers can abuse both to exfiltrate data. This session shows how to lock down both paths. We cover DNS Firewall enhancements for the DNS path, Network Firewall improvements for outbound connection control, and how running DNS Firewall and Network Firewall together gives you one view of DNS security. We also cover URL and domain categories, managed threat intelligence, and extending egress protection to containerized and AI workloads.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Conversational AI at Scale: S&P Global Energy's 30+ Genie Agents (sponsored by Databricks)
abstract: Evaluating complex financial data shouldn't start with schema research and SQL. In this session, Databricks will introduce Genie Agents, which let business and technical users ask questions in plain language and get back trusted answers, tables and visualizations. S&P Global Market Intelligence will then demonstrate how it built Genie into S&P Capital IQ Workbench on Databricks and AWS, and how it is scaling Genie Agents towards coverage of about 90 core datasets. Learn how automated AI bundles (dataset documentation, SQL examples, business definitions, joins and synonyms) and entity resolution keep answers accurate, and how notebooks let technical teams check and extend the results. All governed end to end by Unity Catalog. Hear how this cut data evaluation time and shortened sales cycles. Leave with a blueprint for turning data products into conversational experiences customers trust.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Conversational AI to accelerate Apache Spark operations on Amazon EMR
speaker: Melody Yang, Narendra Gupta
abstract: Customers manage dozens of Apache Spark applications on Amazon EMR — and every major upgrade, unexpected failure, or performance regression pulls engineers away into reactive firefighting. In this workshop, experience a fundamentally different approach with AI-powered agents that handle the undifferentiated heavy lifting of Spark modernization and incident resolution. You'll work hands-on with conversational agents such as the Apache Spark Upgrade Agent and the Apache Spark Troubleshooting Agent across real-world scenarios on EMR Serverless and EMR on EC2 to simplify the operational burden through natural language, automated code transformation, workload analysis and data quality validation.

title: Core banking agent-ready: From composable to agentic financial services on AWS
speaker: Neha Daudani, Michelle Mei-Li Pfister
abstract: The shift from composable to agentic banking is a re-architecture. Discover the reference architecture for turning a core banking platform into an intelligent core with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for orchestration, Amazon ECS for the control plane, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases for domain context, and Amazon EventBridge for event-driven ingestion. We explore two consumption patterns ISVs can offer bank customers: exposing core banking APIs to customer-owned agents, and shipping a managed agentic layer for conversational AI and autonomous lending, deposit, and payment operations, eliminating up to 70% of repetitive manual work. Learn the hard-won lessons on infrastructure, governance, and product differentiation.

title: Correlate database query latency to user impact
speaker: Phani Kumar Lingamallu, Alex Livingstone
abstract: Diagnosing performance degradation across distributed applications requires more than isolated database or application metrics. It demands correlated, end-to-end telemetry. This code talk demonstrates a scenario that unifies database performance signals with application-layer telemetry using OpenTelemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Learn how to implement trace-to-query correlation, design log aggregation patterns for accelerated root cause analysis, and build metric relationships that surface bottlenecks across the full stack. You'll be able to connect a slow database query to its downstream user impact.

title: Cost-effective serverless data integrations and workflows for AI-ready data
speaker: Sakti Mishra, Shrey Malpani
abstract: AI is only as good as the data beneath it and building high-quality, well-integrated data products shouldn't break your budget. In this session, learn how to build cost-effective AI-ready datasets using AWS Glue, Amazon MWAA and Apache Iceberg. We'll show how Glue Data Quality and Glue serverless ETL, now with generative AI-assisted development, lets you ingest, transform, and prepare high-quality data at scale. We’ll demonstrate how Amazon MWAA serverless empowers a single DAG to coordinate workloads across AWS Glue, and other engines - all of this while paying only for what you use. Pairing this setup with Apache Iceberg further enhances your AI workloads with query-ready production data pipelines that move the needle without breaking the bank.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Cost optimization for Amazon DynamoDB
speaker: John Terhune, Lee Hannigan
abstract: Developers love building on powerful, serverless Amazon DynamoDB, and as their production tables grow in size and traffic, they want to discover what mechanisms and optimizations can be applied to reduce costs. Cost optimization can be done both in the design phase and during operations. In this session, learn how to model and measure costs, explore Database Savings Plans to reduce spend on predictable workloads, and discover cost optimization tools that can help you along the way.

title: Craft, Don’t Vibe, Your MVP
speaker: Matt Lewis
abstract: Many people today use LLMs only for code generation. The best teams embrace AI across all stages of the SDLC. The decisions made before building the first version of your product directly affect its viability and success. Rather than relying on vibe coding to make these decisions implicitly, agents can be used to evaluate architectural options, compare trade-offs and challenge assumptions before a single line of code is created. This session explores how high-performing teams are investing time capturing standards, patterns and expertise, making them available for agents to apply consistently. Learn from practical real world examples how AI is being used to accelerate the delivery of production-ready systems, rather than those that carry technical debt from day one.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Creating resilient multi-channel customer experiences with Amazon Connect
abstract: modernized its digital customer service capability by migrating priority banker groups from legacy messaging platforms to Amazon Connect Chat. The transformation delivered a scalable, integrated, and future-ready messaging environment while improving banker productivity, operational control, and reporting capabilities, and enabling a pathway to enhanced self-service and assisted-service experiences. Deloitte led the end-to-end migration through a structured release approach, encompassing experience design, backlog and epic management, governance, business readiness, training, cutover planning, and operational risk management using AWS services. This session explores the strategy, execution, and lessons learned from delivering a successful enterprise messaging transformation. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Crossing the Kill Chain: Detection and Response When Attackers Pivot Between Clouds
speaker: Ameya Paldhikar, Geoff Sweet
abstract: When an attacker gains a foothold in one cloud and pivots into another, the kill chain crosses boundaries that no single-cloud tool follows on its own. Detecting it starts before the incident, with the preparation that makes the cross-cloud seam visible: centralizing and normalizing telemetry across your estate. In this chalk talk, we work through how to prepare for, detect, and respond to cross-cloud lateral movement together. Using real attack sequences, we showcase how to build the detection and response using AWS Security Hub, Amazon CloudWatch, and multicloud telemetry sources. You'll leave with an alerting framework and correlation patterns you can run against your own environment.

title: Cross-modal search with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings
speaker: Gowtham Shankar, Wale Akinfaderin, Sapeksha Vemulapati
abstract: Build search and RAG that understand more than text. In this hands-on workshop, you'll use Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings that embeds text, documents, images, video, and audio into one semantic space for cross-modal retrieval. You'll generate embeddings across modalities, load them into a vector store, and build a working app that searches with text, an image, or an audio clip and retrieves relevant results from any modality. We'll cover indexing strategies, query routing, and accuracy tuning for production agentic RAG. Bring your laptop.

title: Crypto escape room: race to migrate to quantum resistance
speaker: Jay Viera, Arun Krishnaswamy, Shankar Rajagopalan, Margo Cronin, Phoebe Sorkin
abstract: The migration to post-quantum cryptography is underway and here's a chance to hone your skills. In this gamified builders' session, each team races a countdown clock through different cryptographic migration challenges: TLS endpoint migration, ML-DSA key for code signing, quantum ready PKI, and an audit of your PQ posture. Teams complete quests using the AWS Key Management Service (KMS), AWS Private Certificate Authority, and AWS Secrets Manager services. A live leaderboard tracks progress across teams. Leave with new skills and the confidence to build quantum-resistant cryptographic infrastructure.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Cryptographic computing on AWS: homomorphic encryption in practice
speaker: Jonathan Herzog, Ruben Merz
abstract: What if you need to process sensitive data without exposing it to the system performing the computation? In this hands-on workshop, use fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) to evaluate selected ML models while inputs remain encrypted and only the data owner decrypts the results. Work through encrypted inference for medical images, spam messages, and financial transactions in Amazon SageMaker Studio, then deploy a validated FHE model bundle to an AWS Lambda serving path. Examine the architecture, trust boundaries, performance constraints, and operational trade-offs that determine where FHE is practical today. Leave with concrete AWS patterns for privacy-sensitive and regulated workloads.

abstract: Ctrl+Alt+Ship is a choose-your-own-adventure experience with self-paced labs spanning Kiro, Amazon Quick, and Amazon Connect Customer. Start with the Kiro IDE for AI-native development, or level up to multi-agent workflows. Solve an escape-room-style corporate crisis using Quick, your AI work assistant, choosing between a guided investigation or an advanced multi-step operation to plan, execute, and automate your way to cracking the case. With Connect Customer, see how AI resolves customer issues, gives agents context, and helps supervisors improve service—or go hands-on with the agentic CX designer, a no-code visual canvas, to build conversational AI. AWS facilitators from each product team will be available to answer questions. Labs are 30-60 min. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed.

title: Customer Care Reimagined: How Barclays UK Embeds AI in CX Journey
speaker: Aly Galal
abstract: Discover how Barclays UK is reimagining Customer Care by connecting AI across the end-to-end journey. Instead of isolated pilots, Barclays UK has built joined-up capabilities on Amazon Connect Customer and Amazon Bedrock, delivered as incremental releases. Hear how four AI capabilities, from real-time colleague assistance to automated coaching across 100% of interactions, are already live and making a measurable difference for colleagues and customers. Barclays UK and AWS share the lessons learned, reusable architecture and how this portfolio is evolving to customer-facing journeys.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

speaker: Echeyde Cubillo, Haritez Narrisetty, Sharlina Keshava, Deepak Rupakula, Heng Zhang, Nicole Marie Meyers
abstract: Domain-specific AI delivers accuracy that is difficult for general models to match. In this session, see how real customers use Amazon Nova Forge to accelerate the path from idea to production..

title: Customize and serve models at scale on Amazon EKS
speaker: Sajjan Gundapuneedi, Christina Andonov, Salva Jung
abstract: Serving and customizing models in production often involves running expensive GPUs at high utilization, maintaining low latency as traffic spikes, and scaling to demand without over-provisioning. Increasingly teams are doing it on Amazon EKS. This session covers how to efficiently run GPU workloads, select the right accelerator for each workload, and apply optimization techniques that increase utilization and lower costs. Explore model customization through fine-tuning and RAG, and serving and autoscaling patterns that keep inference fast and efficient. See how hybrid workloads span cloud and on-premises GPUs with EKS Hybrid Nodes and where AWS is investing next.

title: Customize open-weight models for accuracy, cost, and latency on SageMaker AI
speaker: Michael Oguike, Ganesh Hegde, Oded Vainas
abstract: Off-the-shelf frontier models often fall short on accuracy, cost, or latency your specialized tasks demand. That's why organizations from retail to financial services are customizing open-weight models to power domain-specific workflows and agents. In this session, learn why and how to customize open-weight models with Amazon SageMaker AI, including using serverless model customization and techniques such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Then hear how Intuit customizes models on its proprietary financial data to deliver personalized customer experiences, achieving up to 5% higher accuracy and 50% lower latency than general-purpose LLMs, while cutting costs on key accounting workloads.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Customize workspaces and build guided workflows using AI in Connect Customer
speaker: Taylan Unal, Freddy Jimenez, Jen Featherling, Douglas Park, Michael Prappas
abstract: In this builder session, you'll use no-code tools to design human agent experiences in Amazon Connect Customer. Create persona-specific workspaces - customizing layouts, apps, and views so frontline agents, back-office workers, and supervisors see only what they need. Build guided workflows in natural language: describe the view you want, and AI generates it. Set up AI agents to fill out forms in real time, freeing human agents to focus on the customer. Then test end-to-end to see how custom layouts, AI-generated views, and AI agents work together to speed resolution. Walk away with workspaces built in minutes, not days.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Customize workspaces and build guided workflows using AI in Connect Customer
speaker: Taylan Unal, Freddy Jimenez, Jen Featherling, Douglas Park, Michael Prappas
abstract: In this workshop, you build the complete agent and business user experience in Amazon Connect Customer. First, you create persona-specific workspaces using the no-code UI builder, customizing page layouts, applications, and views so frontline agents, back-office workers, and supervisors each see only the information, tools, and guidance they need. Then, you create AI-powered guided workflows using natural language: describe the experience you want, and AI generates the step-by-step workflow automatically. You test and validate end-to-end in the Agent Workspace, seeing how custom layouts and AI-built guides work together to accelerate resolution. Walk away with persona-tailored workspaces and working guided workflows built in minutes instead of days.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Custom SRE agents: From prompt to proactive ops with DevOps agent
speaker: osamamu Munir, Bhavani Kanneganti, Rohit Sharma, Harish Goud Mandhadi, Garrett Pollard
abstract: In this builder session, learn how to create custom SRE agents that turn a simple prompt into automated, environment-specific operational workflows. Using pre-configured tools and integrations, you'll define agents tailored to your priorities, whether that's anomaly detection, performance optimization, cost analysis, or resiliency recommendations. See how agents combine real-time observability data with structured reasoning to surface actionable improvements without manual investigation. Walk away with hands-on experience designing an agent that monitors your operational patterns and proactively recommends next steps, so your team spends less time diagnosing and more time shipping.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Cut cost migrating agentic AI workloads to Graviton5 on EKS AutoMode
speaker: Borja Pérez Guasch, Jon Loinaz Anton
abstract: Learn how to cut agentic AI infrastructure costs by migrating to AWS Graviton5 on Amazon EKS Auto Mode — with no compromise on latency or reliability. This hands-on workshop covers the full playbook: building multi-architecture container images, designing ARM64 NodePools, configuring IAM Roles for Service Accounts for secure agent-to-AWS communication, and tuning Graviton-optimized inference runtimes for predictable tail latency. Run live cost benchmarks against x86 equivalents to see exactly where Graviton5 pays back, and instrument with CloudWatch Container Insights to confirm performance parity. Walk away with a reusable pattern, a reproducible benchmark methodology, and a clear migration path you can apply to your own workloads the same week.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano IV

title: Cut through Kubernetes signal overload with unified observability
speaker: Saurabh Garg, Ankita Saxena, Yagr Xu, Debojit Roy, Francis Valbuena
abstract: Kubernetes at scale buries teams in high-cardinality signals that traditional pipelines truncate or split across separate backends, so the answer you need is never in one place. In this hands-on builders session, you send OpenTelemetry metrics and logs from an EKS cluster into Amazon CloudWatch, deploy Container Insights, and decide which signals actually matter. You use automatic resource enrichment to build your own dashboards and alerts, deciding what to alert on and why rather than running pre-made scripts. You leave knowing how to cut through high-cardinality noise and set up alerts that drive action.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Cut through the noise: risk-based prioritization for your security findings
speaker: Michael Davis, Nicholas Hans Jaeger
abstract: Security Hub prioritizes critical security risks and helps you respond at scale. By correlating threats, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations across AWS and multicloud environments, it surfaces attack paths and prioritizes what needs attention first. In this chalk talk, we deep dive into how exposures work, how risk prioritization scores are calculated, and how to operationalize the findings in your environment.

title: Cut through the options: Choosing the right AWS connectivity solution
speaker: Daniel Neri, Jordan Rojas Garcia
abstract: AWS offers a growing range of connectivity services, including AWS Direct Connect, AWS Interconnect (multicloud and last mile), AWS Transit Gateway, and AWS Cloud WAN. But when should you use one over another? In this chalk talk, evaluate your connectivity options and avoid over-engineering your network design. Walk through real-world scenarios and a structured decision framework to understand which service aligns with your requirements. Attendees gain clear guidance and discover practical decision tools for selecting the right service for your scenario. Come prepared with your questions.

title: Cut token costs by 50%: Building context efficient agents with Strands
speaker: Liz Radway, Thomas Oosterhuis
abstract: AI agents degrade as conversations exceed context windows. You need retrieval strategies, compression policies, and adaptive storage backends. This code talk covers the three-tier context cache hierarchy of AWS's open source Strands Agents SDK. We'll discuss context management as composable primitives with extension points for custom backends, compression, and retrieval. We'll explore trade-offs between framework and agent-controlled context, how plugins compose without coupling, and where abstractions break under extreme workloads. For developers building or extending agent frameworks.

title: Cut your data lake and lakehouse bills: Cost and performance tuning best practices
speaker: Behram Irani, Rohit Vashishtha
abstract: Open data lakehouses and data lakes, built on open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, can quietly accumulate cost through uncompacted small files, over-partitioned tables, and inefficient scan patterns. In this session, learn advanced Iceberg cost savings and tuning techniques on AWS that cut storage and compute costs while improving performance. We cover partitioning strategies, predicate pushdown optimizations, compaction tradeoffs, Graviton efficiencies, Intelligent-Tiering storage and how to eliminate common anti-patterns that inflate your bill. Learn from practical examples on Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, Amazon EMR and leave with a comprehensive playbook to lower your analytics costs
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Cyber defense at the frontier: What we learned building Vega on Amazon S3
speaker: Eli Rozen
abstract: Vega runs AI threat detection directly on data sitting in Amazon S3. This session covers what the Vega team learned building AI-driven threat detection directly against data in S3, the architecture behind that approach, and what it means for the frontier of cyber defense as AI threat detection moves closer to where the data lives.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Danske Bank's AI City: Scaling AI agents across an enterprise
speaker: John Bustamante Madsen, Kasper Tjørntved Davidsen, Anantharaman Seshadri
abstract: Getting AI agents into production across a regulated enterprise means solving governance and security first. Danske Bank started with a handful of generative AI experiments and now runs more than 40 use cases in production. In this session, learn how Danske Bank built "AI City"—a governed, reusable platform that cut time-to-production from months to days. See how they structured the platform so new teams can ship agents without rebuilding authorization, logging, or model access controls from scratch, with production examples from personal banking, compliance, and capital markets, and explore the Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore architecture underneath it all.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Dark Factory or Human in Every Loop: Building the Agentic SDLC in Between (sponsored by Port IO)
abstract: Your developers ship faster than ever. Your organization doesn't. The bottleneck moved from writing the code to everything that happens after it. Agents can help, but only with a trustworthy picture of your org and real permission to act in it. That's an agentic SDLC. Nobody ships you one, because yours is shaped like your organization. So we'll build one live for a company that doesn't exist: a t-shirt printer whose three factories disagree on what a medium is. Then we take the humans out and see how dark the factory gets. An agent built it in two hours. This presentation is brought to you by Port IO, an AWS Partner.

title: Data & AI Keynote
speaker: Brittany Doncaster, Andy Warfield, Marianne Johnson, Swami Sivasubramanian, Hannes Mühleisen
abstract: The future is already here...it's just not evenly distributed in production. Most teams have agents that shine in a demo and stall before they do real work. The ones who get to production changed three things: how agents reach their data, how they measure what agents are worth, and the limits they set. Join Swami Sivasubramanian and Andy Warfield to learn how to make these same shifts in your organization.

title: Data & AI Security, Resilience and Recovery in AWS (sponsored by Veeam)
speaker: Roy Adiel, Johan Huttenga
abstract: As AI adoption accelerates on AWS, cloud and platform teams need to know exactly what Veeam can do to keep their data secure and their environments resilient. This session takes you on a tour of Veeam's capabilities built for the AWS developer and cloud practitioner: discovering sensitive data, monitoring AI agent activity, and closing visibility gaps before they become incidents. You'll see how security posture and backup protection work together in practice, giving teams confidence in what's protected. And when something does go wrong, precise, granular recovery means restoring exactly what changed, nothing more. This presentation is brought to you by Veeam, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Roman I

title: Datacenter to Cloud: Safety, Security, & Trust for AI Agents & Models (sponsored by Red Hat)
speaker: Mikhail Shapirov, Josh West
abstract: Deploying enterprise AI requires a unified framework across four governance pillars: Safety, Security, Risk, and Trust. Demystify multi-layer vulnerabilities spanning base models, agentic harnesses, and tool usage, addressing threats like Mythos model risks. Learn defense-in-depth strategies for agents—including sandboxing, privilege control, reasoning tracing, and dynamic red-teaming—to mitigate prompt injection, data leakage, and excessive agency. We’ll map these practices to global frameworks like NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act to ensure continuous production readiness. This presentation is brought to you by Red Hat, an AWS Partner.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Data Environments for Agents
speaker: Eugene Wu
abstract: AI agents increasingly query databases, modify files, and operate applications. Their effectiveness depends on the environments in which they act: what information they can discover, which alternatives they can explore, and what happens when they make mistakes. This session examines how data environments can help agents accomplish more while bounding the consequences of failure. Drawing on research from Columbia’s Data, Agents, and Processes Lab, we explore branching and recovery across databases and live execution state, data flow controls that enforce policies and guide agent behavior, and evaluations that reveal bottlenecks in finding and using information. Participants will leave with a framework for reasoning about the responsibilities of models, execution systems, and human interfaces when building agentic applications.

title: Data governance for trustworthy AI: from raw data to trusted products
speaker: Jose Romero, Kalyan Kumar Neelampudi
abstract: In this hands-on workshop, transform fictional retailer RetailMax's raw, ungoverned data into trusted, governed data products using Amazon SageMaker platform . Learn to build a business glossary and metadata forms, create an analysis-ready dataset with an ETL job, and trace end-to-end data lineage. Gain hands-on experience enforcing data quality rules, enriching and publishing a governed data product, and sharing it through a publish-and-subscribe model with approval workflows and least-privilege access. Discover how to deliver trustworthy, explainable answers with the Gen-AI data agent. Leave equipped to build the governance and metadata foundation that makes data — and the AI that runs on it — trustworthy across your organization. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Data mesh at scale: The automation layer, proven at Experian
speaker: Romi Patel, Mohammed Ali Syed, Rohit Kumar Singh
abstract: Federated data ownership is easy to draw and hard to enforce. Is governance enforced in process, or in the platform? Enforce it in the platform, and the hard part becomes the seam between central policy and self-serve provisioning most teams never build. On Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio we architect that seam: one project per data-domain for blast-radius isolation, contracts that block non-compliant publication, policy that cascades but only tightens, and a reconciler turning Git-committed JSON into infrastructure. Experian runs it across dozens of data domains in regulated financial services, cutting domain onboarding from months to self-serve.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Data mesh on AWS: governance, identity, and end‑user attribution
speaker: Mert Hocanin, Zach Mitchell
abstract: Data mesh promises domain‑owned data as a product — but the hard part is governance: who can access what, and how you prove it after the fact. In this interactive chalk talk, we whiteboard two patterns for building a data mesh on AWS and debate when each one fits. The first is a centrally governed mesh using attribute‑based, fine‑grained access controls across separate producer, consumer, and governance accounts. The second is a peer‑to‑peer mesh where the producer directly approves each consumer's subscription. We'll follow a single data product through the AWS Glue Data Catalog from publication to subscription, wire enterprise identity (federated from your existing identity provider, such as Okta or Entra) all the way through to the query, and show how trusted identity propagation and end‑user attribution give you per‑user accountability you can audit end to end.

title: Data mesh to agentic AI: Building an AI-ready enterprise on AWS
speaker: Prasanna Ramaswamy, Rishi Gera
abstract: How do you build an AI-ready data foundation in a global investment organization without compromising trust, governance, or speed? CPP Investments—manager of one of the world’s largest pension funds—is evolving from fragmented data toward a governed enterprise data platform on AWS, using data mesh principles, federated ownership, and platform engineering to scale with guardrails. Join their CTO for a look inside the architecture, operating model, and critical trade-offs shaping this evolution, and how it brings trusted data closer to investment decisions while laying the foundation for conversational data experiences and agentic AI.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Data Prep to Deployment: How Tencent Games Scaled to 1,000 GPUs on SageMaker HyperPod
speaker: Shreyas Adiyodi, Haoming Li, Xulong Gao
abstract: In a live match, speech AI must answer before the action ends. Hear how Tencent Games brought it to one of the world's most popular games, from first cluster to production in weeks. See the architecture behind it: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod for data processing, training, and inference near players worldwide. Then learn what HyperPod does underneath: cluster resilience that finds and replaces unhealthy nodes and recovers training automatically, rapid scale-out, task governance that pools training and inference by priority, and built-in observability.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Data protection and resilience with AWS storage
speaker: Danny Christian Johnston, Stuart Lupton
abstract: Risks to data availability are intensifying, and the cost of getting recovery wrong is rising. Recovering well means recovering deliberately, not reactively, with a strategy built for the unpredictability of what can go wrong. In this session, you'll learn how the 3-2-1-1-0 defense-in-depth framework provides that structure, guiding you from failure scenario analysis through recovery objective planning to layered protection across local, cross-region, and immutable isolated copies. The result is a playbook for how AWS storage services bring each layer to life, from native replication and disaster recovery to centralized backup with immutable isolated vaults for cyber recovery.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Data protection and the post-quantum shift
abstract: Encryption, key and secrets management, and data sovereignty all face new pressure as post-quantum timelines compress. Bring your plans for post-quantum migration, secrets rotation at scale, and protecting sensitive data in regulated and sovereign environments. Compare timelines and approaches with others who are planning the same moves.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Dealing with Terraform/IaC/Compliance in AI-era
abstract: Meetup to discuss how our Terraform-related activities has changed in modern AI-era and what kind of new (or well-forgotten old) challenges we have to deal with as we combine Terraform and AI for daily DevOps/SRE tasks. Lets discuss what works well, what doesn't, what is getting harder to implement, and what kind of experiences we have gained. Lets bring the pain points - they often lead to great discussions and solutions!
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Death of the Request-Response: Architecting Serverless for Multi-Agent Loops on AWS
abstract: Traditional REST APIs and synchronous request-response patterns are poorly equipped for the era of Agentic AI. When autonomous multi-agent loops operate over minutes or hours—evaluating context, invoking tools, and collaborating — holding open an HTTP connection is an anti-pattern. Join this community meetup to explore how serverless architectures must evolve for an agentic world. We will tear down synchronous legacy models and map out purely asynchronous, event-driven topologies. Discover how to leverage AWS Lambda Durable Functions, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to orchestrate long-running agent workflows. We’ll also discuss handling open standards like the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in a serverless ecosystem.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Decision Frameworks, Evaluation, and Cost Management with AWS Quick
speaker: Sandhya Khanderia, Sagar Rao
abstract: Moving from one agent to enterprise-wide automation means choosing the right path — Flows, Automate, Custom Agents, persistent agents — and the right trigger model. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a decision framework that bakes in evaluation and cost management from the start, not as afterthoughts. We'll connect orchestration across 25+ connectors, skills, and workstreams to measurable outcomes and dollars. Bring your automation backlog — you'll leave with a decision matrix, eval harness, and ROI story.

title: Decision Mgmt at Scale: Common Patterns for Modernizing Real-Time Decisioning on AWS (sponsored by Redis)
speaker: Siva Palanisamy
abstract: Every card transaction has a split second to be evaluated before it is approved, and the systems behind that decision are under pressure to be faster, smarter, and easier to govern. Join Siva Palanisamy, Executive Vice President of Data Platforms at Mastercard, for a look at common industry patterns for modernizing real-time decisioning on AWS. Learn how rules and machine learning models work together, why tail latency matters more than averages, and how in-memory data stores can serve as a real-time feature layer. Siva will share lessons learned and take your questions. The session closes with a look at how AI agents are taking shape in financial services, where memory, context, and auditability are essential. This presentation is brought to you by Redis, an AWS Partner.

title: Decision patterns for AI Agents with Amazon Connect Customer
speaker: Mansoor Ali Khan, Ganesh Prabhu Jayachandran
abstract: Contact center AI agents require critical architecture decisions around tool integration, voice prompt engineering, and quality evaluation at regulatory scale. In this chalk talk, we walk through the decision framework for choosing first-party tools versus AWS Lambda versus MCP integrations based on latency, complexity, and compliance requirements. Explore deterministic state-machine patterns for voice prompt engineering with Amazon Connect Customer AI Agents. We discuss automated evaluation pipelines using Amazon Connect Customer Conversational Analytics and generative AI to score 100% of interactions. Debate trade-offs and leave with a decision model you can apply to your own contact center environment.

title: Decoder with Nilay Patel, live at AWS re:Invent
abstract: The Decoder podcast comes to AWS re:Invent for a live conversation about big ideas shaping business and technology. Hosted by The Verge Editor-in-Chief Nilay Patel, Decoder features conversations with a diverse cast of innovators and policymakers at the frontiers of business and technology, exploring how they’re navigating an ever-changing landscape, what keeps them up at night, and what it all means for our shared future.

title: Decompose a monolith database into microservices with agentic AI
speaker: Angus Tong, Saurabh Sharma
abstract: Enterprise architects face a critical challenge: breaking monolithic database-centric applications into microservices while managing risk and cost. Where do you draw domain boundaries? How do you extract 20 years of business logic from stored procedures into the application layer? This chalk talk reveals the two-layer decomposition strategy—combining database structure and runtime execution patterns—to identify service boundaries. Leveraging AWS Transform and Kiro, collapse months of manual analysis, design and development into hours of executable code. Through live whiteboarding, learn the data-driven framework enabling business logic extraction, independent deployment, licensing cost reduction, and faster modernization.

title: Decouple and scale Amazon ECS workloads with event-driven patterns
speaker: Masatoshi Hayashi, Matthew Meckes
abstract: Not every container workload needs to run all the time. Some should wake up when an event arrives, process it, and stop. Amazon ECS makes this straightforward, but choosing the right trigger pattern matters. In this chalk talk, discuss how to connect events to containers using Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SQS, and AWS Step Functions. Walk through four common patterns: single-event task launch, queue-based consumer scaling, fan-out processing, and multi-step workflow orchestration. Explore how to handle failures gracefully with dead-letter queues and retry policies, and how Amazon ECS provides serverless compute for event-triggered deployments.

title: Deep dive into Amazon Aurora and its innovations
speaker: Grant McAlister
abstract: With an innovative architecture that decouples compute from storage and advanced features like Aurora Global Database and low-latency read replicas, Aurora reimagines what it means to be a relational database. Aurora is a built-for-the-cloud, serverless relational database that delivers unparalleled performance and availability at global scale for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and DSQL. In this session, dive deep into the newest Aurora features. Explore how Aurora supports agentic AI through vector search and MCP servers for agent access. Also, learn about Aurora DSQL, the fastest serverless distributed SQL database.

speaker: Seung Yeol Hyun, Marc Bowes
abstract: Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database that uses decades of Amazon innovation and operational excellence. In this session, dive into the design and key innovative technologies that make Aurora DSQL the ideal choice for new applications and applications that require the highest level of resilience. Learn how active-active architecture in Aurora DSQL delivers single- and multi-Region resiliency and virtually unlimited scale

Learn how the implementation of these features in your organization can improve resilience, performance, and the effectiveness of your applications.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

abstract: Architect high-performance, resilient network infrastructure using Network Load Balancer and Gateway Load Balancer. This deep dive covers advanced load balancing, multi-protocol support, and security appliance integration at scale. In this session, we explore NLB source IP preservation, and GWLB transparent inspection architecture. Topics include performance and resilience capabilities including Zonal Shift and Zonal Autoshift. Whether you're running financial trading platforms, gaming backends, or large-scale SaaS, walk away with practical blueprints for designing architectures that deliver high availability and predictable performance while maintaining inline security inspection and compliance.

We’ll cover different IPAM and routing strategies for hybrid pod networks, including Cilium BGP control-plane integration with your on-premises infrastructures. We’ll also explore various load balancing and Kubernetes services networking options for your hybrid nodes. Additionally, we’ll deep dive into the new Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway, demonstrating how it simplifies pod-to-pod communication, webhook connectivity, and AWS service integration across cloud and on-premises environments - without requiring changes to your existing network infrastructure.

title: Deep dive on S3 Files with use case architectures and best practices
speaker: Smitha Sriram, Jimmy Zuber, Amir Levy
abstract: What if every application, AI agent, and team in your organization could access S3 data as a shared file system? With S3 Files, connect thousands of compute resources to your data in S3 through a high-performance file interface that scales to multiple terabytes per second. Stop duplicating data between object and file storage. Stop building staging workflows just to read a file. In this session, you'll see how S3 Files turns S3 into the shared file system your workloads already expect, and how customers are replacing copy-heavy pipelines with direct file access today.

title: Deepfakes, Deception, and the New Rules of Reality (sponsored by KnowBe4)
speaker: Perry Carpenter
abstract: Deepfakes are transforming the rules of trust. As AI-generated voice, video, and imagery become easier to create, attackers use synthetic media to make deception feel familiar, urgent, and credible. In this session, KnowBe4 shows how deepfakes fit into broader social engineering campaigns built around narrative, timing, and cross-channel reinforcement. The fake clip is rarely the whole attack; it is one piece of a larger story designed to short-circuit judgment when it matters most. Attendees will learn what separates an interesting tech demo from a nation-state-level attack. They will see how these attacks work and why convincing stories and cognitive biases override technical skepticism even in well-trained people. Perry Carpenter will also cover how organizations can prepare for high-stakes moments when trust is under pressure—before the call comes in, not after This presentation is brought to you by KnowBe4, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Defeat Player Evasion: AI Moderation at Scale on Amazon Bedrock.
speaker: Anand Iyer, Christina Defoor
abstract: Players evade moderation with leetspeak, homoglyphs, emoji sequences, and fast-evolving slang. Brute-force AI classification catches evasion but is cost-prohibitive at scale. In this workshop, build a tiered moderation pipeline on Amazon Bedrock that routes 80–90% of traffic through deterministic normalization and pre-filters before invoking a model. Ambiguous content gets classified by Amazon Nova at sub-500ms latency. Only the hardest cases escalate to multi-agent analysis on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for context-dependent decisions. Configure per-category thresholds, instrument cost-per-decision tracking, and stress-test against real gaming evasion patterns. Walk away with a deployable, cost-optimized pipeline. Laptop required

title: Defense in depth for Strands AI agents with Cedar, AgentCore, and Rex
speaker: Trevor Schiavone, Abdu Mahmoudi, Nadhya Polanco, Emre Alptekin, Matt Eglin
abstract: AI agents that generate and execute code on remote systems need more than a single permission check - they need policy enforcement at every trust boundary. In this builders' session, you’ll configure Cedar policies at two distinct enforcement points for a Strands pre-built operations agent : AgentCore Policy on AgentCore Gateway and Trusted Remote Execution (REX) on the target remote host. You’ll see why both are necessary, how they compose, and how the agent gracefully adapts when it hits either boundary.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

abstract: Proving business impact at the C-suite level is what separates a deployment partner from a strategic advisor. That's where the Value Realization Plan (VRP) comes in, the structured approach at the heart of the AWS Business Value Realization motion. We'll cover building a compelling case for change, defining KPIs that resonate with executives, and driving adoption through change management. Learn the pitfalls that stall outcome conversations, how to accelerate buy-in, and how to frame impact in terms executives act on. Leave with a repeatable approach for your next engagement and a foundation for a customer success practice that scales.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

We share early results and outline how organizations can begin preparing today for the fault-tolerant era.

title: Democratizing precision time on EC2: make clocks work for you
speaker: Josh Levinson, Shamik Chakraborty
abstract: Distributed systems builders have avoided relying on wall clock time for anything critical. Times are changing. Amazon Time Sync now delivers microsecond accuracy on EC2, making clock precision a feature, not a bug, in your system design. We whiteboard how customers in databases, AI, financial services, and media approach design in new ways, and share our open source ClockBound work on the clock error bound as a standard interface for your applications.

abstract: Join this session to learn about Amazon Aurora DSQL's optimistic concurrency control (OCC). Explore building an application to understand the impact of OCC on your relational workloads, how it differs from traditional databases, and how to achieve the desired semantics in DSQL's OCC model.

title: Demystifying AWS KMS authorization: building key policies that scale
speaker: Kevin Kevin, Patrick Palmer
abstract: Authorization to your key involves a mix of key policies, IAM policies, grants, SCPs, and VPC endpoint policies — each playing a distinct role in access decisions. This talk demystifies how these policies are evaluated in the context of AWS KMS, then applies that understanding to create a scalable policy design. You'll learn about ABAC, using grants for dynamic delegation, and AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) which offers a simpler yet scalable way to share keys in your organization. You'll leave with the mental model to predict outcomes and reusable patterns that grow with your organization.

title: Demystifying the shared security model on Amazon ECS
speaker: Jooyoung Kim, Sai Charan Teja Gopaluni
abstract: Running containers in production demands security controls at every layer. This chalk talk covers the Amazon ECS shared responsibility model, including IAM policies for task isolation, VPC networking with awsvpc mode, and runtime protections. Explore how Amazon ECS Managed Instances and AWS Fargate automates security patching and enforces instance refresh cycles while maintaining workload availability. Discuss practical patterns for secrets injection, image scanning, and network segmentation. Bring questions about securing your specific container architectures for an open technical discussion.

title: Deploy AI agent sandboxes on EC2
speaker: Jeff Underhill, Kinnar Sen
abstract: AI agents write, execute, and iterate on code autonomously. Every session needs an isolated sandbox to run untrusted code safely. This session explores how customers deploy agent sandboxes on EC2 across distinct patterns, each offering different trade-offs between isolation, latency, and performance across our instance families. We cover isolation trade-offs, cost per sandbox-second, and capacity planning at scale. Attendees leave with a decision model for selecting the right pattern based on their scale, security posture, and operational maturity.

title: Deploy AI agents on containers with Amazon S3 Files and S3 Vectors
speaker: Samyak Kathane, Kiran Chukkala
abstract: Build a multi-agent architecture on Amazon EKS using S3 Files as the shared workspace and S3 Vectors as persistent semantic memory. Mount an S3 file system across agent containers using standard POSIX file I/O. Agents read, write, and hand off artifacts without custom SDKs or message brokers. A background process generates embeddings stored in S3 Vectors, giving agents long-term memory they query semantically. Deploy a self-managed orchestrator that spawns agents, routes tasks via file system events, and retrieves vector history. Walk away with a production-ready, self-managed multi-agent system.

Watch AI teammates plug into the workflows your planners already follow, connect to the systems you already run, and improve as they learn your business. You will see a live product walkthrough, learn where AI takes work off your team's plate, and leave with a clear picture of how to add planning capacity without retraining people or rebuilding your stack.

title: Deploy and manage blockchain nodes on AWS
speaker: Yinal Ozkan, Everton Fraga
abstract: Self-managing blockchain nodes at scale requires expertise in infrastructure sizing, storage optimization, chain synchronization, snapshot management, and patching, amid rapidly evolving protocols. In this session, explore a reference architecture for deploying self-managed nodes on AWS using Amazon EC2 and AWS Blockchain Node Runners, an open source initiative. The session includes a whiteboard walkthrough of a sample solution, diving deep into each component, addressing key challenges, and exploring AI-driven node deployment with Kiro and how to leverage AWS DevOps Agent for management.

title: Deploy and optimize world models with agentic AI workflows
speaker: Steven Warren, Michaelangelo Battaglia, Megan McKenzie, Bashir Mohammed, PhD, Gyanesh Kumar
abstract: World models generate real-time video by learning environment dynamics, which powers interactive simulation for gaming, robotics, and autonomous driving, but deploying these latency-sensitive pipelines is complex. See the agent identify bottlenecks, then select optimized kernels from Hugging Face or write custom kernels from scratch. You will apply these agentic tools yourself to reach optimized, real-time inference on silicon built specifically for AI.

title: Deploying a Fitness App from Specs with Kiro and AgentCore
speaker: dima Farer, Sri Kola
abstract: In a simulated scenario, Fitness trainers waste 30 minutes daily on manual data entry and cannot spot trends across clients. In this SimuLearn session, you build FitTrack AI using Kiro's spec-driven workflows and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You design flexible schemas, create agent tools for client management and natural language analytics, deploy the agent on ECS Fargate, configure Bedrock Guardrails for health safety, and implement anomaly detection using database change streams.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom V

title: Deploying AI Agents that handle PHI with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
speaker: Adam Birnbaum, Shreya Singh
abstract: Your clinical team wants an AI agent that summarizes patient notes—but one leaked SSN means a $1.5M HIPAA penalty. In this session, we build a working Amazon Bedrock Agent with HIPPA controls baked in. Guardrails automatically redact low-risk identifiers and block critical PHI, routing flagged content through Amazon EventBridge to an SQS review queue. AWS CloudTrail captures the full audit trail, and IAM restricts the agent to BAA-covered services only. You leave with a deployable CDK stack ready for production.

title: Deploying Frontier Voice Agents Privately on AWS (sponsored by ElevenLabs)
speaker: Nicolas Bernier
abstract: Frontier voice agents are already handling live customer calls inside health systems, banks and insurers, without audio ever leaving the customer's AWS account. This session covers the architecture that makes that possible, from in-VPC deployment and zero data retention to integration with their existing stack. Working from a production deployment taking real calls, we walk through the latency budget that keeps conversational voice feeling human, the trade-offs private deployment brings, and how to size it for your own environment. Leave with an understanding of where ElevenAgents fits in your current environment, a reference architecture and a deployment checklist. This presentation is brought to you by ElevenLabs, an AWS Partner.

title: Deploying Governed AI Agents in Clinical AI
speaker: Mark Logan, Ekta Walia Bhullar, Bret Borota
abstract: Millions of patients wait too long for imaging each year as demand outpaces capacity, and the shortage is projected to worsen significantly by 2030. Radiology Partners is tackling this with MosaicOS, a full imaging lifecycle system powered by agentic AI that spans order placement through billing. In this lightning talk, learn how MosaicOS uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to orchestrate multiple AI models across the radiology workflow while maintaining governance and observability required in regulated clinical environments. See how agentic orchestration moves radiology from tool-level automation to coordinated, clinician-directed intelligence at scale.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Deploying mission-critical applications with Amazon EBS
speaker: Vicky Dewani, Saurabh Bindoo
abstract: Millions of customers run their performance-intensive enterprise applications and databases on AWS. In this workshop, explore deploying a high-performance application on Amazon EC2 and Amazon EBS for optimized availability, resiliency, and cost performance. Discover and choose the ideal Amazon EC2 instance types and Amazon EBS volume types for various workloads. Learn about on-demand storage flexibility and performance using Elastic Volumes. Monitor and optimize Amazon EBS using Amazon CloudWatch metrics, and observe how AWS DevOps Agent autonomously investigates and helps remediate storage performance issues. Build resilience and fault tolerance using AWS Fault Injection Service. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Deployment strategies for highly available edge applications
speaker: George Oakes, Afaq Khan
abstract: Organizations need to be able to deploy critical applications that are highly available and fault-tolerant at the edge. These workloads are often some of the most demanding in terms of durability and availability requirements. Deploying workloads on AWS hybrid cloud and edge computing services like AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts requires planning for networking, compute, storage, and other failure modes. In this chalk talk, dig into each of these services, review use cases, and examine reference architectures. Learn design considerations and deployment patterns for high availability and disaster recovery.

title: Deploy, tune, and scale AI workloads on AWS with self-managed agents
speaker: Aniruddha Deodhar, Alex Iankoulski
abstract: Setting up AI infrastructure, deploying AI workloads, evaluating and tuning performance, and scaling up are tasks that require deep domain knowledge and substantial time investment. In this chalk talk, learn how to simplify these tasks by using self-managed agents on AWS. Explore an agentic architecture capable of autonomous operation, knowledge management, and self-improvement. Review a reference implementation and watch a demo of agent-driven AI workload deployment and performance benchmarking. Then discuss how to build and run your own self-managed agentic harness on AWS.

title: Deploy without drama: Safe, automated releases on AWS
speaker: Michael Michael, Mark Rambow, Anastasia Giannoulas
abstract: Releasing software shouldn't mean holding your breath. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild, and AppConfig help you automate safe, hands-off deployments to Amazon EC2, ECS, and Lambda across accounts and Regions. Learn to apply canary and linear traffic-shifting strategies, wire CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollback, and use stage-level conditions to gate promotions on integration tests. Whether you're deploying a single service or orchestrating hundreds, leave with patterns for zero-downtime releases you can trust.

title: Deploy your applications with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK)
speaker: Jorge Diaz Alvarado, Pahud Hsieh
abstract: In this workshop, build and deploy applications using infrastructure as code with the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). Create resources using familiar programming languages, apply CDK Mixins to compose reusable behaviors across constructs, and safely reorganize stacks with CDK Refactor. Learn maintenance and operations tips including cross-account output references and programmatic deployments with the CDK Toolkit Library. Get an introduction to building your own constructs. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Design an open, cost-effective and high-performant lakehouse with Apache Iceberg on
speaker: Radhika Jakkula, Saman Irfan
abstract: What does it take to build a lakehouse that's open, fast, and cost-effective? In this chalk talk, we unpack real architectural decisions behind Apache Iceberg on AWS—from Amazon S3 Tables (delivering up to 3x faster queries and 10x higher TPS) to unified metadata management with the AWS Glue Data Catalog across Athena, EMR, and Glue ETL. Bring your questions as we whiteboard trade-offs around schema evolution, ACID transactions, time-travel queries, and avoiding vendor lock-in. Leave with actionable patterns tailored to your workload.

title: Designing for Operability: Catching Performance Gaps Before Scale
speaker: Jofia Jose Prakash
abstract: A training workload had plenty of GPU capacity, yet utilization remained low and training time kept increasing. The GPUs were healthy. The real bottleneck was upstream: the data pipeline could not feed them fast enough, leaving expensive accelerators waiting for work. This talk walks through how we traced that utilization gap, found where throughput was being lost, and identified the signals that could have exposed the problem earlier. Through this production experience, we’ll look at what it means to design for operability before scale, when performance, utilization, and cost problems are still easier to fix.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Designing performant and cost-effective data lakes on Amazon S3 Tables
speaker: Ankit Kalyani
abstract: Apache Iceberg data lakes that aren't thoughtfully planned can accumulate small files, excessive metadata, and redundant snapshots, ultimately degrading query performance and inflating costs. In this session, we dive into the design and maintenance choices that determine whether your Iceberg lake stays fast and cost-efficient or slowly deteriorates, including compaction strategies, snapshot expiration, and partition design. For each, we'll walk through the trade-offs, what happens when you get it wrong vs. right, and how Amazon S3 Tables can automate the heavy lifting for you. Leave with actionable strategies to balance performance and cost at scale.

title: Designing Portable Multicloud Architectures with Open Standards
speaker: Ellie Tamari, Shankar Ramachandran, Clark Richey
abstract: Enterprises pursuing multicloud strategies often equate portability with containerization, but true architectural portability requires deliberate decisions across the full stack. In this session, we start from the foundational layers of compute, storage, and networking and build outward through data, security, observability, AI, etc. At each layer, we explore how open specifications enable portability, in what parts of your architecture does portability matter most and how to make deliberate portability decisions across your stack.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Designing real-time voice AI experiences
speaker: Juan Diego Medina, Jose Antonio Gomez Mora
abstract: Voice is becoming a primary interface for AI products, but building voice experiences that feel natural is hard: latency, interruption handling, and turn-taking all have to work together. In this session, we walk through the design and architecture decisions behind real-time voice AI experiences on AWS, covering latency budgets, interruption handling, and how to keep conversations feeling natural. You'll leave with a practical framework for designing and building your own voice AI product.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Designing security governance for your AWS multi-account foundation
speaker: Ishai Shvartz, Avik Mukherjee
abstract: AWS gives you flexibility to design your multi-account environment, but customer needs guidance choosing the right security services to deploy, where, and how to validate the deployment against AWS best practices. This session shows how the AWS Security Reference Architecture provides a prescriptive security blueprint you layer on top of your account governance foundation. Using whiteboarding, you cover OU design, service prioritization, centralized vs. distributed placement, design considerations, validation with SRA Verify, and deployment acceleration. You leave with a tailored governance model ready for implementation.

title: Designing the AWS Secure Research Environment: Architecture deep dive
speaker: Chris Riddle, Devin Hicks
abstract: Discover how the AWS Secure Research Environment (SRE) helps research institutions stand up NIST 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 infrastructure. Explore the architecture: Landing Zone Accelerator (LZA) customization, multi-account strategy with Control Tower Account Factory, preventive SCPs versus detective controls, Network Firewall egress, and automated evidence collection feeding Security Hub. No setup is required. Using a simulated pipeline, you work through and gain a deep understanding of the LZA configuration customizations an SRE needs, customize them for your organization, and leave with your own SRE config files. We provide next-step instructions for deploying those configs in a real, customer-owned AWS environment later.

title: Designing your AWS network for scale: From one VPC to many
speaker: Christian Elsen, Mokshith Kumar
abstract: You started with a single Amazon VPC, and it worked. But as your organization grows, so does your network complexity. In this chalk talk, we'll work through the decision points of scaling from one VPC to many. When should you split workloads? How do you connect VPCs - peering, hub-and-spoke, or mesh? How do you segment traffic, centralize inspection and egress, plan IP addressing at scale, and integrate hybrid connectivity? Bring your architecture challenges, and we'll draw through solutions together on the whiteboard.

title: Design your AWS Transform pipeline for parallel modernization at scale
speaker: Deepak Dixit, Anitha Deenadayalan
abstract: How do you modernize thousands of applications concurrently to meet aggressive migration timelines? In this chalk talk, we'll work through architectural patterns for scaling AWS Transform with CI/CD integration: parallel processing with serverless compute, programmatic orchestration via APIs, container strategies, observability at scale, and campaign coordination across teams. Bring your use case and whiteboard it with us. Whether you need pipeline integration, secure private repo processing, or a self-service modernization platform, we'll design your architecture together.

title: Design your cedar authorization model with AI coding agents
speaker: Julian Lovelock, Kevin Hakanson
abstract: Your identity provider handles authentication, but how do you design the authorization model that follows? In this chalk talk, learn how to use OIDC token claims from providers, including Amazon Cognito, with a Cedar-based authorization model. We'll walk through implementing RBAC, ReBAC, and ABAC patterns locally or in Amazon Verified Permissions, and show how to use AI coding agents (Kiro, Claude) to generate your schema and policies. Bring your use case for this interactive session. You'll leave with a repeatable approach to designing fine-grained authorization from scratch.

title: Detection in the Agent Era, and the Metrics That Matter (sponsored by Datadog)
speaker: Andrew Krug
abstract: Detection teams can't hire fast enough, so agents are arriving in every SOC. But how do you know they work? We ran Datadog's threat hunting agent on our own environment first. This session covers hunting, analyst, and detection engineering agents, four golden signals of rule efficacy, and one metric that matters: human hours saved. You'll see the real results, what went wrong, and a framework to evaluate agents against your own AWS telemetry before you trust them with your SOC.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Deterministic control for probabilistic agents: proving safety holds
speaker: John Tristan
abstract: AI agents are probabilistic: vulnerable to prompt injection, hallucination, and unexpected tool composition. The controls around them must be deterministic. This session explores how to define provable safety envelopes for autonomous agents, drawing from the authorization and formal verification research behind AgentCore policy. We examine how automated reasoning guarantees policy correctness, how neuro-symbolic approaches combine LLM flexibility with mathematical verification for policy authoring, and how agents' action spaces can be reduced before execution. Attendees will also get a first look at new research extending these guarantees to emerging agentic authorization challenges.

title: Deterministic meets probabilistic: Patterns for reliable AI integration
speaker: Xin Chen, Bin Liu
abstract: Production systems demand determinism. AI outputs are probabilistic. The boundary between these two worlds is where this must be resolved. This chalk talk will whiteboard the contracts and integration patterns that hold that boundary: typed interfaces treating model output as untrusted input, propose/commit separation so AI never performs its own side effects, asymmetric verification, bounded generate-verify-repair loops, and compensating actions in place of rollback. We'll work through typical anti-patterns that quietly reach production, where to place the contract in your architecture to avoid these, and the reliability arithmetic that these patterns enable.

title: Developer Keynote
speaker: Clare Liguori, Marc Brooker, Eric Johnson, Neha Rungta
abstract: Building software has never moved faster, and it has never asked more of developers. In this keynote, AWS Engineers and Heroes from the community tackle what's still hard: going from idea to a live app in minutes, building agents that actually work, and trusting code you didn't write yourself. Expect live demos, hard-won lessons from the AWS team that built a new service with an AI software factory, and an honest look at how the developer's job is changing. Come see how AWS is making it easier to build anything you can imagine, then go build it.

title: Developing Apps from Specs with Kiro
speaker: Sam Shalil SHALIL, Bruno Marcondes
abstract: Kiro, the Agentic IDE, transforms a single natural language prompt into structured requirements, a technical design, and an executable implementation plan. In this SimuLearn session, you build a city event management application by guiding Kiro through its spec-driven workflow: generating EARS-format user stories, reviewing architecture decisions, and executing a sequenced task list that produces a working MVP. You also configure a Kiro Hook that automatically validates data files on save.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom V

title: Develop with natural language and agentic AI in Amazon SageMaker
speaker: Juan Luis Polo Garzon, Shreya Jain
abstract: Dive into how data analytics and data engineering workflows are changing with natural language and agentic AI in Amazon SageMaker. Using the SageMaker Data Agent, we'll show how a single conversation can take you from a business question to a governed, scheduled data pipeline, and how to keep that data trustworthy with data quality checks defined in natural language.

title: DevEx 2026: The AI Era (sponsored by Atlassian)
speaker: Andrew Boyagi
abstract: The hype machine says AI makes developers faster. This was true in 2025, when 68% of devs said they were saving 10 hours per week, but we’re not in 2025. Our 2026 data shows only 26% of devs are still saving 10 hours per week, but are facing more bottlenecks with increasing levels of cognitive load. The role of a developer has shifted, with organisations moving from AI adoption to looking for impact. This is presenting developers with new opportunities and challenges. What are the organisations and developers who are moving faster, and delivering at a higher quality point doing differently to those still looking for impact? In this session, we’ll explore the results from the latest State of DevEx report, diving into how developer roles have changed, and how you can unlock the transformational power of AI. This presentation is brought to you by Atlassian, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: DevOps and Modernization Jam
speaker: Nir Pilo, Sushma Nagaraj
abstract: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Tackle hands-on DevOps environments to improve applications and modernize architectures using multiple AWS services. What are the limitations of the current solution? How can you do it better? Whether you're new to AWS or a seasoned Cloud Ninja, this is your chance to demonstrate and grow your skills. Guided exercises, helpful clues, and AWS expert support throughout. All you need: a laptop, a desire to learn, and a competitive spirit.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Palace Ballroom I

Whether you're new to AWS or a seasoned Cloud Ninja, guided exercises and AWS experts support all levels. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

title: Digital sovereignty: Verifiable controls, greater choice, & innovation
speaker: Stephane Israel, Mustafa Isik
abstract: Evolving regulations and geopolitical shifts are forcing organizations to rethink how they protect data, limit access, and maintain control in the cloud, without slowing AI adoption. In this session, learn how AWS helps customers meet digital sovereignty requirements through verifiable, auditable, and enforceable controls, including the AWS European Sovereign Cloud. Learn what AI sovereignty means in practice, get answers to the most common questions, and hear how AWS and partners are helping organizations stay compliant without compromising on capability.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Disaggregated inference at scale: when to split prefill from decode
speaker: Henan Wang, Bailey (Sohyeon) (Sohyeon) Cho, Toshinobu Akazawa, Alex Iankoulski, Keita Watanabe
abstract: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto independent GPU pools, eliminating the interference that lets one long prompt stall active generations and letting each phase scale independently. There is a trade-off: the KV cache must cross the network, and a well-cached unified deployment can still perform better depending on traffic. In this hands-on builders session, run both architectures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, move the KV cache between pools over Elastic Fabric Adapter, and benchmark them against realistic agentic traffic. Learn a decision framework based on input length, prefix reuse, and latency targets, with runnable configurations.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Distributed transactions with Step Functions and durable functions
speaker: Leticia Dornelas, Ricardo Marques, Roberto Perillo, Victor Kazuyuki Shinya, Rogelio Ramirez Rubio
abstract: Distributed transactions across microservices break in ways monoliths never did: partial failures, inconsistent state, rollbacks that don't roll back. In this builders' session, build a payment processing using saga pattern that orchestrates multiple serverless microservices using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions. You'll implement compensation mechanisms that handle partial failures, compare orchestration approaches for short-lived versus long-running transactions, and monitor transaction flows across distributed services. Walk away with working saga patterns and the observability setup to troubleshoot them in production. Bring your laptop.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1
