title: Dive deep into Amazon DynamoDB
speaker: Amrith Kumar
abstract: This session provides a deep dive into Amazon DynamoDB and shares insights into how DynamoDB is architected and how it’s able to deliver the scalability and response times that customers have come to expect. DynamoDB is used by over one million AWS customers, and powers hundreds of applications that exceed half a million requests per second. In this talk we explore the architecture of DynamoDB, and of several specific features. You will understand how we architected DynamoDB to deliver predictable low latency at any scale, and how best to develop your own applications to delight your customers.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Dive deep into Amazon DynamoDB using design puzzles
speaker: Robert McCauley, Jason Hunter
abstract: In this session, dive deep into how Amazon DynamoDB works at scale by collaboratively solving a few design puzzles that may seem simple but are actually complex. Learn how to look beyond the obvious solution to find a more effective and scalable one with an understanding of how DynamoDB operates.

title: Don't ban it, broker it: Govern AI coding agents with Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Karthik Mokashi, Jayanth Ranjan
abstract: AI coding agents are becoming embedded in development workflows. In regulated environments (e.g.,financial services), that raises concerns around data residency, code exfiltration, auditability, and runaway costs. But banning the tools creates shadow AI. In this session, we'll whiteboard a better path by pointing AI coding agents at Amazon Bedrock through a gateway in your VPC. One control point for identity, data residency, prompt inspection, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, cost controls, and immutable audit. We'll walk through the request lifecycle, debate trade-offs around latency, budgets, and MCP tool calls, and show how the same broker pattern governs any agent touching sensitive data.

speaker: Adam Azzam
abstract: The hard part of background agents is the background, not the agent. We'll talk about the common design that software factories have converged to and why building environments for agents is still hard. This presentation is brought to you by Modal, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Don't rewrite your APIs: Make them agent-ready for agentic AI
speaker: Piyali Kamra, Amit Maindola
abstract: Organizations want agentic AI, but valuable capabilities sit behind legacy APIs, AWS Lambda functions, and internal services. In this chalk talk, we explore practical, low-lift patterns for making existing endpoints agent-ready without replacing systems of record. Using a financial services scenario, we walk through how OpenAPI specs, AWS Lambda facades, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway expose existing endpoints as composable agent tools. We show how existing RBAC and OAuth scopes map into Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Cedar policies so you reuse your governance posture. Walk away with a 5-level maturity model you can apply to your own API estate.

title: Drive multi-server migrations from discovery to cutover with AWS Transform
speaker: Patrick Kremer, Harpreet Virk
abstract: Migrating VMware or other on-premises environments to AWS involves dozens of coordinated steps, and most teams spend more time planning handoffs than actually moving workloads. In this workshop, you'll experience how AWS Transform's agentic AI orchestrates the full migration lifecycle: intelligent discovery, AI-driven wave planning, automated network translation, and server rehost execution. Specialized AI agents coordinate across each stage, making autonomous decisions while keeping you in control. You'll leave with hands-on experience using agentic AI to execute a real end-to-end multi-server migration. Laptop required.

title: Drug discovery and materials use cases with Amazon Braket and Q-CTRL
speaker: Nick White, Alex Shih
abstract: Classically hard problems such as simulating strongly correlated electrons and 1D NMR spectra, critical to material and drug discovery, can be sped up on quantum computers but until now had not been demonstrated. Q-CTRL shows how Fire Opal on Amazon Braket enables simulating 1D NMR spectra for spin systems up to 34 qubits and achieved a 3,000x speedup on the Fermi-Hubbard model at 120 qubits, demonstrating practical quantum advantage. title: DynamoDB: the database designed for trillion-scale vector search
speaker: Rashmi Krishnaiah Setty, Abhinav Duggal
abstract: As vector search becomes a standard component of AI applications, scaling to billions or even trillions of vectors while maintaining single-digit millisecond latency and high recall remains a significant challenge. In this session, deep dive into the decisions made when building vector indexes for DynamoDB, including how vector indexes shard alongside table data, the scatter-gather query mechanism that keeps latencies tight, and the filtering that avoids recall degradation at scale. Learn how the partition key in DynamoDB maps naturally to multi-tenant workloads, enabling per-tenant index isolation without operational overhead. Discover the trade-offs between recall, latency, and cost in production for real-time vector search.

title: EC2 at 20: Rebuilding the control plane while it is running
speaker: Don McGarry
abstract: Amazon EC2 launched in 2006 as four services backed by a single MySQL database. Twenty years later, it is one of the largest distributed systems ever built — and most of that original architecture had to be replaced while serving production traffic, with no maintenance window and no change to the API contract customers depend on. In this session, EC2 engineers dive deep on two of the hardest migrations: making the control plane Availability Zone independent so a single-AZ event cannot escalate into a regional one, and moving EC2 metadata off MySQL. We walk through the failure modes that forced each decision, how correctness was verified before every cutover, how we proved a single-AZ failure stays in a single AZ, and the things we got wrong along the way. You will leave with migration and isolation patterns you can apply to your own systems at any scale.

abstract: Automated theorem provers can reason symbolically about a system's behavior and prove properties like "no user can ever escalate their own privileges" across all possible inputs. In this session, learn how to encode your problem in first-order logic: starting with a logic puzzle to build intuition, then a toy authorization language, and finally what it takes for a full production system like Cedar, a fine-grained authorization language built with high assurance. We discuss challenges including ensuring correctness and completeness of the encoding.

abstract: You don't need another post-mortem to know why enterprise AI projects fail. Organizations that have moved AI from pilot to production know it runs on context. A knowledge layer shows AI how facts relate, what's changed, and what's already been decided. Trained on siloed data, a model sees disconnected records, not relationships, and can't reason well without that context. The knowledge layer connects GenAI and agentic systems to data that's organized and accessible. In this session, we'll cover why the knowledge layer is the missing piece your enterprise AI needs, and what your organization gains from implementing one: Trust every AI answer, back to your source data. Prove every AI decision with a complete audit trail. Synthesize intelligence across disparate systems and teams. Use your existing data investments instead of replacing them. title: Enterprise buying trends and the startup playbook for AWS Marketplace
speaker: Aaron Edell, Lewis Howarth
abstract: Selling into enterprise can be a big hurdle for startup founders. In this interactive session, learn how enterprises actually buy and walk through getting your startup discoverable on AWS Marketplace and co-sell ready. It demystifies the buying process and shows startups exactly what they need to grow. See the steps, ask questions, and leave knowing exactly how to reach enterprise customers.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Enterprise-Grade Outcomes. Within Reach for Growing Businesses. (sponsored by Accenture)
speaker: Dusshyant Roy, Chris Wegmann
abstract: Discover how Accenture Edge for AWS helps growing organizations (under $3B in annual revenue) achieve the same transformative outcomes as larger enterprises through pre-built, outcome-driven solutions designed for speed, simplicity, and value. We are taking enterprise-grade talent and tools and making them accessible and approachable. Translation: Big outcomes at lower costs thanks to pre-configured solutions. Hear real examples of customers that accelerated cloud adoption, reduced costs, strengthened security, and modernized faster with Accenture and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Enterprise-Ready: How NetEase Governs AI at Scale
speaker: Dan He, Xiangxin Lin, Zhuobin Huang
abstract: Learn how NetEase, one of the world's largest gaming companies, is building enterprise AI governance as AI adoption scales across the organization. Discover how Amazon Bedrock enables multi-model routing, cost controls, and team-level budget management to optimize AI usage. See how NetEase enforces governance with company-wide AI policies, Bedrock Guardrails for content safety, and Bedrock AgentCore for orchestrating agentic AI workflows with centralized governance and observability. Learn why a platform-first approach to cost, access, and safety is critical for enabling AI innovation at enterprise scale.

title: Escaping IIoT Pilot Purgatory: Why Your Database Breaks at Scale (sponsored by Tiger Data)
speaker: Matty Stratton
abstract: Seventy-four percent of industrial IoT projects stall somewhere between pilot and production. The hard part is that the pilot worked. That is exactly what makes the failure so difficult to diagnose. Pilots succeed because a few hundred sensors over a few weeks fits comfortably in almost any database. Production does not. Storage costs compound faster than the budget that approved them, ingest hits a cliff with no warning, and the real-time dashboard that sold the project turns into a loading screen. See where industrial systems and typical AWS pipelines reach their limits and how to scale beyond them. We’ll explore a proven architecture using AWS IoT Core, Amazon Kinesis, AWS Lambda, and a single Postgres database to support more than one million connected devices reporting every second. This presentation is brought to you by Tiger Data, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Essentials for migrating from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
speaker: Mike Revitt, Pini Dibask
abstract: Migrating from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition can be a transformative journey, offering significant cost savings and performance benefits. However, this transition requires careful planning and execution. In this session, discover the essential things you need to know to ensure a smooth and successful migration from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL and the optimal architectures to enable such a migration. Learn best practices and pitfalls to avoid from seasoned experts who have helped many customers walk this path.

title: EU operational autonomy in action: AWS European Sovereign Cloud
speaker: Zoltan Albrecht
abstract: The AWS European Sovereign Cloud is built on fully isolated infrastructure within the EU, operated exclusively by EU-resident staff, with no access from outside Europe. In this lightning talk, learn from the AWS European Sovereign Cloud Managed Operations team what independent operations means in practice and how it works day to day.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Eval-Driven LLM Routing: Cut Costs Without Losing Accuracy
speaker: Luca Bianchi, Olivier Leplus
abstract: This session shows how to build an eval-driven LLM routing system: harvest a production eval dataset, define accuracy KPIs using LLM-as-judge, set a non-negotiable accuracy floor as the practitioner's decision, benchmark candidate models, and generate a routing policy optimized for cost within that floor. Result: approximately 80% cost reduction at maintained accuracy. A reference architecture you can start implementing immediately.

title: Evaluate, Disclose, Safeguard: A Production-Readiness Framework for AI Agents
speaker: Gulcin Batmaz, Nawaz Varda
abstract: Every organization is building AI agents, but few have made it to production. You can't prove it works, you can't prove it's responsible, and compliance won't sign off. In this chalk talk, we walk through a production-readiness framework for AI agents on Amazon Connect. First, evaluation: measuring resolution with the Connect Simulation API to score AI agents on the same bar as human agents. Second, responsible AI: disclosure patterns that build trust, escalation triggers for sensitive journeys, and harm avoidance for regulated industries. Third, safeguards: defense-in-depth governance for agents that process refunds and access sensitive data, including asymmetric PII, MCP tool authorization for human confirmation, and automated escalation when confidence drops. Leave with a checklist: what to measure, what to disclose, what to block, and when to ship.

title: Evaluate Enterprise AI Agents with an Eval-First Approach
speaker: Jonathan Dion, Rashmi Sahasrabudhe
abstract: A successful agent demo does not guarantee production readiness because agents can behave inconsistently across question types and multi-turn sessions. In this spotlight lab, you build two custom evaluators for an agent: THELMA, which scores single-turn RAG quality across seven dimensions including hallucination detection via groundedness scoring, and Mind the Goal, which computes Goal Success Rate across entire conversations and attributes failures to root causes. You register both as native AgentCore evaluators, run batch evaluations, and use diagnostic outputs to pinpoint exactly what to optimize first.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Palace Ballroom II

title: Evaluating AI agents for production in financial services
speaker: Jorge Castans Garcia, Jannis Kambach
abstract: Financial institutions building AI agents face a core challenge: how do you prove an agent is reliable enough for production when regulators demand explainability and consistency? How do you reliably detect when a production agent's behavior drifts? In this chalk talk, we explore patterns for rigorous agent evaluation in regulated environments. We discuss defining ground truth, measuring agent quality with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, and automating re-evaluation as prompts, tools, and parameters evolve. Leave with practical blueprints for constructing datasets, choosing metrics, and building continuous agent evaluation workflows for production.

title: Evaluating AI Agents for your Nonprofit: From Vibes to Metrics on AWS
speaker: Krutika Khinvasara, Omar Tabbakha
abstract: You shipped an agent. How do you know it works? For organizations where AI decisions affect people's lives, rigorous evaluation isn't optional — it's ethical. This chalk talk introduces a structured evaluation framework combining Amazon Bedrock model evaluation, AgentCore observability, and CloudWatch metrics. We cover building eval datasets, measuring tool-use accuracy, detecting hallucination in agentic chains, benchmarking latency and cost, and setting up automated regression testing. Leave with a repeatable eval pipeline you can plug into CI/CD — turning agent quality from subjective to measurable.

title: Evaluating AI Agents with Langfuse (sponsored by ClickHouse)
speaker: Doneyli De Jesus, Lotte Verheyden, Marc Klingen
abstract: Production agents need more than infrastructure. They need an open source foundation for understanding behavior, evaluating quality, and improving continuously without sacrificing control of their data. In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Langfuse combine secure agent infrastructure with open source observability and evaluation, powered by ClickHouse. See how teams capture OpenTelemetry traces, debug trajectories and tool calls, evaluate production quality, turn failures into datasets, and prevent regressions before deployment. We will share a practical architecture for unifying policy and telemetry across AgentCore, EKS, and other runtimes so teams can ship trustworthy agents faster. This presentation is brought to you by ClickHouse, an AWS Partner.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Event-driven agents at scale: building agentic AI on Amazon MSK
speaker: Luca Perrozzi, Masudur Rahaman Sayem
abstract: Production agents need to dispatch long-running actions, wait on external systems, fan results out to analytics, and re-enter the conversation when work finishes — not sit in a synchronous loop. In this session, we present reusable patterns for building multi-tenant, event-driven agentic systems on Amazon MSK: dispatch-and-resume for long-running tool calls, topic and partition design keyed to tenant and conversation, decoupling the agent loop from channels and analytics, and durability and replay so in-flight work survives deploys and retries. Learn a practical approach for designing agentic SaaS that stays reliable as load, tools, and channels grow.

title: Event-driven AI agents for security triage with AWS Continuum
speaker: Lavanya Bandari, Ashish Kumar
abstract: Security teams need to detect, correlate, and respond to threats faster than manual processes allow. AWS Continuum validates exploitable findings and AI coding agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore close the loop. Agents remediate critical and high-severity findings, re-scan them, and open a pull request that AWS DevOps Agent reviews. For regulated industries, agents never merge their own fixes. Unresolved or new issues escalate to humans, and every fix has an audit trail. We walk through a real-world example in which a fix inadvertently introduced a new vulnerability and show how the automated loop caught it before it reached production. Leave with patterns to cut time-to-remediate and keep every change explainable.

title: Event storming: Find your service boundaries before production does
speaker: Jim Fernandes, Ramesh Chidirala, John Dougherty, Vaibhav Sabharwal, Yongzhe Ren
abstract: Split a system in the wrong place and you get a distributed monolith: coupled services with network hops instead of function calls. This session tackles the problem most teams get wrong, where to draw the boundary, using Event Storming. Together we map a real domain, trace information flow between actors, and identify natural division points, deciding ownership, data locality, transaction scope, and deployment independence at each boundary. Every decision is evidence based, grounded in observed event flow rather than intuition. Then you go hands on, taking one boundary and deploying it as an independent service on AWS. Leave with a repeatable method for boundary definition plus working code you built yourself. Bring your laptop.

title: Everyone is a Coder. Govern what they build. (sponsored by Coder)
speaker: John Zink, Abhipal Singh, Nicky Pike
abstract: Suddenly, everyone is a coder. People who never wrote code now build apps, dashboards, and prototypes with AI, faster than most teams can govern them. The result is shadow AI, ungoverned data, and IP risk. See how a leading global private investment firm gave citizen developers a governed place to build on its existing AWS infrastructure, replacing scattered, unmanaged tools. Learn how approved models, scoped templates, centralized container management, and a complete audit trail let hundreds of builders move fast inside guardrails. Attendees leave with a practical model for governing AI adoption on their own AWS environment. This presentation is brought to you by Coder, an AWS Partner.

title: Everyone Says They Have an Ontology. Almost Nobody Does (sponsored by TextQL)
speaker: Ethan Ding
abstract: Ontology has become one of the defining ideas in enterprise AI. Every cloud and data platform now claims to have one. They rarely converge on the same structure, conventions, or architecture. Those differences determine whether an ontology can support agentic AI. That test comes down to three things: how it's structured, how it's generated from the systems and context already in place, and how it stays current as the business changes. This talk lays out the practical requirements for an ontology built for agentic AI, drawing on the architecture TextQL runs across the messiest data estates at Fortune 50 companies. This presentation is brought to you by TextQL, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Everything you've wanted to know about performance on EC2 instances
speaker: Arthur Petitpierre, Seth Fox
abstract: Getting the best compute performance is an art, and knowing low-level details helps a lot. This talk covers everything you've wanted to know: memory topology, accessing hardware counters, hyperthreading side-effects, and how to properly run performance tests and optimize your latency for production.

title: Evolve Amazon DynamoDB data models with no application impact
speaker: Craig Howard, Greg Krumm
abstract: Master advanced techniques for evolving Amazon DynamoDB data models without application interruption. Learn versioning strategies, backward compatibility patterns, and migration approaches for production applications. In this session, architect a solution that covers attribute addition and removal, data type changes, and index modifications while maintaining 24/7 availability. Explore real-world migration scenarios, rollback strategies, and handling distributed application dependencies. The best practices covered in this session are essential for teams managing large-scale DynamoDB applications requiring continuous evolution while serving millions of requests.

title: Evolve your observability for the agentic era
speaker: Nikhil Dewan, Matheus Arrais
abstract: Your agent passed every test last week. Today the same prompt returns a different, pricier answer, and nobody can say why. Agents drift as models and prompts change beneath them, and a green dashboard won't catch it. This session covers what evaluations ("evals") are: automated checks that score an agent's output for quality, accuracy, and cost. You'll learn how an eval-driven loop catches that drift on live traffic, traces it to the change that caused it, compares models and prompts, and attributes spend down to the agent and user, so regressions get blocked before they reach production. Then see how Amazon CloudWatch Omni does this across AWS and other clouds, covering your agents and applications in one place.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Expand your GPU playbook: Amazon EC2 G7e/G7 for inference and training
speaker: Theo Wu, Leah Tucker
abstract: Not every ML workload needs the same GPU. Amazon EC2 G7e and G7 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with GDDR7 and native FP4 support, deliver strong price-performance for inference and select training use cases. This session breaks down where G7e and G7 fit: inference prefill (competitive FLOPS per dollar) and decode (FP4 and higher concurrency help close the HBM gap), and training via pipeline parallelism. The session covers the toolchain (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TransformerEngine, CUTLASS FP4 kernels), a TCO comparison, and a decision framework for choosing G7e and G7 versus P-series instances.

title: Expedite model loading times on Kubernetes using kro and ACK - from storage to GPU
speaker: Ramesh Mathikumar, Kumudhan Cherarajan
abstract: LLM inference on Kubernetes is bottlenecked by loading multi-gigabyte model weights through the storage → network → CPU → PCIe → GPU path. In this chalk talk we benchmark four approaches to accelerating model delivery to GPU memory: SOCI for lazy-loading container image layers, s5cmd parallel downloads, Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI streaming, and Run.ai Model Streamer for direct S3-to-GPU pipelining. We walk through when each technique shines, how they compose together, and the tradeoffs platform teams face when optimizing inference cold starts on Amazon EKS. Learn how kro and ACK enable declarative provisioning of optimized storage pipelines, allowing platform teams to compose reusable stacks.

title: Experience catalog federation on AWS: build a multi-cloud open data lakehouse
speaker: Shubham Purwar, Nidhi Nayak
abstract: Enterprise data teams have distributed data catalogs across multiple cloud providers, each with partial visibility and no shared query surface. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how catalog federation unifies cross-cloud data silos into an open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Using Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation with Apache Iceberg as the open, engine-neutral table format for seamless interoperability and zero data duplication across AWS, Snowflake, and Databricks, you'll federate remote catalogs to build a unified lakehouse on AWS to run AI-assisted business analytics.

title: Expert Defense Within Reach: Agentic SecOps with Splunk and AWS (sponsored by Splunk by Cisco)
speaker: Todd Beebe, colin gibbens, Peter Prizio
abstract: Security teams operating on AWS need a faster path from signals to action without adding more operational complexity. In this session, Splunk and AWS will explore a new approach to cloud and AI-native security operations designed for faster onboarding, earlier detection, and more efficient investigation and response. You’ll leave with practical insights into AI-first SecOps and how AWS-centered security teams can improve outcomes, regardless of the size or maturity of their security operations. This presentation is brought to you by Splunk by Cisco, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Exploit a software vulnerability, then stop it: From code to containment
speaker: Vishal Lakhotia, Paul Kelsey
abstract: Step into the role of a DevSecOps engineer tasked with hardening your organization's web applications after a security audit. In this hands-on workshop, a simulated lab walks you through real threat scenarios, and you respond using layered AWS security services. Start with AWS Security Agent to catch vulnerabilities pre-deployment, then use Kiro's agentic capabilities to auto-remediate issues without leaving your IDE. Scan EC2 instances and SBOMs for supply-chain risk, apply virtual patches via AWS WAF, and fully remediate with AWS Systems Manager. Finally, contain an active GuardDuty-detected incident by blocking C2 communication with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall and AWS Network Firewall, proving that layered defenses hold even against unpatched vulnerabilities.

title: Explore agentic data engineering in Amazon SageMaker
speaker: Vishnu Vettrivel, Saurabh Bhutyani, Varsha Velagapudi
abstract: Data engineering teams lose time to siloed data, manual ETL, and tribal knowledge. This session shows how agents change that in Amazon SageMaker. Use SageMaker Data Agent to trace errors, refactor code, and deploy pipelines in natural language, then bring your own agents through MCP servers to work with third-party clients and models directly on your data. See how the same agentic approach extends across SageMaker, so teams can consolidate fragmented pipelines, standardize environments, and put agents to work on more of the data engineering lifecycle.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Extend Amazon EKS clusters for on-premises and edge use cases
speaker: Eric Vasquez, Jared Thompson
abstract: This chalk talk covers strategies for modernizing distributed applications with Amazon EKS across AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, and AWS Outposts. It demonstrates how EKS delivers a consistent experience across these deployment options, minimizing latency and enabling data residency. The session explores deploying a real-world application to an EKS cluster across distributed environments while maintaining a unified control plane. It covers use cases and design patterns for architecting resilient and scalable applications, following AWS Well-Architected Framework principles for consistency and security.

title: Extend AWS WAF to the APIs your AI agents call (sponsored by Wallarm)
speaker: Tim Erlin
abstract: Network and edge controls stop the traffic patterns they were built to recognize. AI agents introduce a different pattern: authenticated requests, at machine speed, against business logic rather than known vulnerabilities. Teams running AWS WAF often find these requests pass inspection because nothing about them is malformed. In this session, examine how agent-driven traffic reaches APIs, which risks fall outside signature and rate-based inspection, and what an additive API security layer contributes. Learn how teams instrument existing AWS WAF deployments for API-level visibility, apply real-time redaction to sensitive data in responses, and enforce without adding latency. This presentation is brought to you by Wallarm, an AWS Partner.

title: Extending your cloud network with Amazon Leo satellite connectivity
speaker: Camden Forgia, May Riggle
abstract: Your cloud network doesn't have to end where fiber does. In this interactive whiteboard session, you'll design hybrid network architectures that combine Amazon Leo's low-earth orbit satellite connectivity with AWS networking services including VPN, Transit Gateway, and Cloud WAN. We'll start with Leo's real-world performance characteristics: latency, throughput, and availability. Then, we'll work through three architecture patterns: first-day connectivity for new sites, primary connectivity for remote locations, and satellite-based redundancy for existing terrestrial links. You'll leave with reference architectures you can adapt to your environment and a clear understanding of how the constellation fits in your network design.

title: Fanatics path to AWS: 5 data centers, 1,800 servers, 48% savings
speaker: Parth Soni, Andrew Krug, Parker Bradshaw, Tim Strayer, Ron Artinger
abstract: If your migration is stuck because no one can agree on what moves first while licensing costs compound and dependencies stay undocumented, the problem isn’t willingness. It’s sequencing. Fanatics Commerce had 1800 servers across five data centers and projected 48% infrastructure savings on AWS. Their team shares the structured path: OLA for licensing clarity, DAP for dependency mapping, EBA for organizational alignment, MAP for execution. Walk away with: (1) a concrete OLA-to-MAP sequence, (2) an AI-assisted dependency mapping approach that surfaced connections no one had documented (3) a phased AWS Transform modernization strategy that earns engineering trust before scaling.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Fast and easy bulk operations with Amazon DynamoDB
speaker: Colin Leek, Ruskin Dantra, Jason Hunter
abstract: In this session, learn patterns for executing fast, safe, cost-aware bulk operations in Amazon DynamoDB using AWS Glue, Spark SQL, and open source tooling that hides the complexity. Discover how to find, filter, diff, load, and update billions of items in parallel. Explore how lightweight AI can make bulk work more powerful and user-friendly. Learn proven patterns, real-world workload insights, and tools that simplify DynamoDB bulk processing.

title: Faster root cause analysis for IAM access denied errors
speaker: Matt Luttrell, Matthew Heck
abstract: When an IAM request is denied, teams can spend valuable time finding the root cause. Now, access denied error messages go beyond surfacing the policy type or ARN that blocked a request—they tell you the exact reason access was denied. In this session, we'll walk through how the feature works, how to put it to use, and considerations for larger AWS environments where different policy types are owned by different teams.

title: Fault-tolerant AI agents: Choosing the right recovery pattern
speaker: Jeetendra Vaidya, Sonal Panda
abstract: When an AI agent crashes at step 20 of 30, you can't just start over. Once state accumulates, an unexamined retry becomes dangerous. Most teams default to the wrong recovery strategy because they apply stateless retry thinking to stateful workflows. In this session, we compare three approaches: replay-based recovery with idempotent tool execution, checkpoint-and-resume with human-in-the-loop pause/resume, and event-driven compensation across trust boundaries. We'll whiteboard each pattern, map it to real failure scenarios, and build a decision framework based on your agent's state model and fault domain.

title: FDE for startups: What it is, why you need it, and how to run it
speaker: Mo Ahmed, Shane Rai
abstract: The enterprise contract is signed. The next ninety days decide whether it renews, grows, or becomes a pilot nobody mentions again. Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) is how a growing number of AI startups make those ninety days count: engineers who sit inside the customer, own production code, and answer for a business result rather than a ticket queue. This session starts with what FDE is and how it differs from solutions engineering, customer success and professional services. We follow one AI startup through a single enterprise deployment and into its second year. You’ll leave with a practical guide to scoping a deployment around a business outcome, getting through enterprise security and production, turning each deployment into reusable product, and knowing when to hire your first FDE.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Financial data modeling with Amazon DynamoDB
speaker: John Terhune, Robert McCauley, Arjan Schaaf, Greg Krumm
abstract: Designing business applications for low latency, high throughput, high consistency, and high availability presents unique challenges at scale. In this session, learn how to model business entities including accounts, journals, and ledgers using Amazon DynamoDB to support workflows that process millions of requests per second. Explore distributed computing patterns that leverage multi-Region replication features in DynamoDB. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

speaker: John Terhune, Robert McCauley, Arjan Schaaf, Greg Krumm
abstract: Designing business applications for low latency, high throughput, high consistency, and high availability presents unique challenges at scale. title: Find and Fix Exploitable Code at Machine Speed with AWS Continuum
speaker: Shweta Shrestha Thapa, Kafayat Adeyemi, Lily Ashidam, Meriem SMACHE, Poornima Venkatesan
abstract: In this hands-on builders' session, you integrate AWS Continuum into your development workflow, where a frontier agent scans and remediates code before it leaves your IDE. Write code with intentional vulnerabilities, run context-aware code reviews that go beyond pattern matching, review prioritized findings with structured evidence, and use Kiro to fix issues in real time. Leave with three controls you can reuse: a pre-commit scan, a pull request gate, and a context-aware pentest you can revalidate.

title: Find and fix storage bottlenecks for self-managed OLTP on EC2 with EBS
speaker: Anthony Thunyin, Shiju Purushothaman
abstract: ​​When you run a self-managed OLTP database on Amazon EC2, the storage bottleneck is rarely where you assume. This hands-on session teaches a repeatable method for finding and fixing it. Use Flexible IO tester and a PostgreSQL/pgbench workload to connect storage metrics to database symptoms. Measure latency, IOPS, throughput, and queue depth; determine whether the limit is the volume, instance bandwidth, or I/O pattern; then tune the right EBS volume configuration. Validate every change with EBS detailed performance statistics and CloudWatch. Leave with a proven sizing-and-tuning method for database workloads on EC2.

title: Find failure modes faster: AI-powered resilience assessments
speaker: Matthew Lanza, Ricardo Piqueras Bonet
abstract: Manual resilience reviews are slow, inconsistent, and routinely miss failure modes that don't surface until an incident occurs. In this workshop, you'll use the generative AI-driven assessment engine in AWS Resilience Hub to automatically discover dependencies across AWS services, internal endpoints, and third-party systems. You'll evaluate workloads against the Well-Architected Framework and your own defined resilience policies including availability SLOs, RTO, and RPO targets, then receive prioritized, actionable recommendations tied to business impact. Working with a reference architecture, you'll build a complete end-to-end assessment and leave with a repeatable framework you can run against any workload as your architecture evolves. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Fine-Tune Agents That Reason: Multi-Turn RL on SageMaker AI
speaker: Ruchi Bhatia, Sandeep Raveesh
abstract: Agents that do real work, such as financial advising, coding, or customer operations, have to reason across many turns, call tools, and recover when a step fails partway through a conversation. Better prompts and bigger models don't solve this, because leading LLMs drop in performance when instructions arrive over several turns. We'll whiteboard how managed multi-turn reinforcement learning (MTRL) in Amazon SageMaker AI trains a model on your agent's full trajectory. You connect your agent in under 10 lines of code. SageMaker AI handles rollouts and checkpointing, and it catalogs each trained model automatically. We'll cover reward design and rollouts in managed gym environments. We'll also show how decoupled training compute keeps GPUs from sitting idle, and where smaller specialized models beat larger ones at a lower inference cost. Bring your agent use case, and we'll map out how to train it.

title: Fine-tune and evaluate NVIDIA Open models on Amazon SageMaker (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speaker: Curt Lockhart, Sandeep Raveesh
abstract: Learn how to customize NVIDIA Open models using Amazon SageMaker without managing training infrastructure. This session walks through preparing a dataset, fine-tuning the model, and evaluating the customized model against the base model to measure improvements in quality. Attendees will leave with a practical workflow for adapting NVIDIA's open models to domain-specific use cases on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: FinOps for AI: Cost allocation strategies for Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Brenno Passanha, Judith Lehner, Ariel Fu, Yuriy Prykhodko, Eric Scott Christensen
abstract: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how spend maps to business outcomes. In this builders' session, you'll get hands on with the latest cost management capabilities for Amazon Bedrock. You'll tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control Gen AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. You'll then query new product metadata in CUR2 and visualize cost-per-million-token trends in CUDOS. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

title: FinOps for AI: Cost allocation strategies for Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Brenno Passanha, Judith Lehner, Ariel Fu, Yuriy Prykhodko, Eric Scott Christensen

title: FinOps for AI: Scale Investments That Work. Stop Ones That Don't. (sponsored by Kion)
speaker: Tatum Tummins
abstract: Most organizations can tell you what they spend on AI. Fewer can tell you what they're getting for it. FinOps for AI closes that gap, but it takes three things: visibility into spend by use case; controls that act on what the data tells you instead of just surfacing it; and value tracking that connects spend to outcomes your stakeholders can evaluate. This session includes real examples of token attribution, guardrail patterns that respond to data, and a model for turning ROI signals into corrective action. This presentation is brought to you by Kion, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Firefighting to decision making: Agentic AI for supply chain
speaker: Colby Ward, Ali Zagros
abstract: You have a forecast. You have a replenishment plan. What could possibly go wrong? Plenty — 85% of supply chain organizations take two weeks or more to resolve urgent issues, and planners spend that time firefighting: thousands of exceptions, hours of triage, and the signal buried in the noise. In this chalk talk, explore how Amazon Connect Decisions uses agentic AI to turn firefighting into decision making. See how planners describe monitoring rules in plain language, how agents measure the noise before a rule ever goes live, investigate root causes autonomously, and recommend actions such as purchase orders, transfers, or expedites — leaving a handful of grouped, prioritized decisions, with the reasoning shown.

title: Firewall policy management for mixed regulated and legacy workloads
speaker: Dario Goldfarb, Ian Olson
abstract: Your firewall policy now has to cover new workloads on modern tech stacks alongside legacy systems still running Windows. Some of them fall under financial regulations, and others under privacy controls. In this code talk, we show how new firewall management features help you write policy elements your team can understand and maintain, avoid policy sprawl, and spend less time preparing for audits.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Fix a Security Hub finding once with four layers of controls
speaker: Todd Kudlicki, Maitreya Ranganath
abstract: You remediate a finding today and see the same class of finding next week. This chalk talk shows how to break that cycle. You take a real AWS Security Hub finding category and work through four control layers. An SCP stops the misconfiguration, an AWS CloudFormation Guard rule catches it before deployment, an AWS Config rule detects existing violations, and AI-generated auto-remediation corrects drift. Each finding you remediate this way becomes a rule that keeps it from coming back.

title: Fleet-wide AIOps for Amazon EKS with the AWS DevOps Agent
speaker: Sai Vennam, Lucas Soriano Alves Duarte
abstract: Operating one EKS cluster is manageable. Operating a fleet of them is where the hard problems live: failures that surface far from their cause, VPC CNI IP exhaustion, Karpenter churn, and upgrades that stall across clusters. This chalk talk shows how AIOps and the AWS DevOps Agent bring order to operations at fleet scale. See how the DevOps Agent correlates signals across clusters to find root cause instead of chasing symptoms. Learn how it turns noisy telemetry into a diagnosis and a recommended fix. Discover the guardrails that let agents act on your fleet safely, with the blast radius bounded.

title: For startups: Bringing vibe-coded apps to AWS
speaker: Shrey Kapoor, Les Lamprecht
abstract: You vibe-coded an app over the weekend. Now you want to move it to production on AWS with auth, a database, and an architecture that scales. In this hands-on session, walk your prototype from code to live app on AWS. You'll generate a migration plan, provision infrastructure with the Agent Toolkit, and deploy with AWS Blocks. Bring your own startup scenarios, and we'll work through them together with the people who built the tools.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Foundational Model Ops with Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Mona Mona, Vinay Arora
abstract: Build a fine-tuning pipeline that proves its own results. In this workshop, run the full loop, baseline eval, fine-tune, RL, re-eval, against the same bar every time. Start with a benchmark baseline on a Hugging Face model. Then fine-tune with QLoRA on Amazon SageMaker AI Training Jobs, with full control over your training script and compute. Add an RL pass with RLAIF or RLVR to optimize against a reward signal the benchmark alone can't score, and re-evaluate against that same baseline to see whether the gain is real or just a lower loss number. Put the whole sequence into a SageMaker Pipeline so it reruns on new data without manual rework. Bedrock Guardrails sit at the deployment gate.

title: Founder's therapy
speaker: Dave Abrameto, Aaron Edell, Abhishek Dubey, Karlo Delos Reyes
abstract: Founders get real about building a company—the wins, the mistakes, the 3 a.m. moments when everything feels impossible. In this intimate session, you'll hear candid stories about what actually works and what doesn't, and have space to share your own struggles and ask the questions you're afraid to ask on a conference floor. Expect honest conversation with peers who've been where you are. No slides, no polish, just founders talking to founders.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Four agents, one answer: multi-agent synthesis on AWS
speaker: Aneel Murari, Sindhu Pillai
abstract: Turning messy, unstructured sources into summaries you can trust takes more than one model. We walk through a working multi-agent system where four specialized agents (a searcher, an analyst, a verifier, and a synthesizer) collaborate to produce cited, evidence-backed results, each running on the Bedrock model best suited to its job. We dissect the hard parts of multi-agent design (message routing, shared state, bounded retries, and cost control). Leave with patterns you can replicate for evidence-backed synthesis in your own domain.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Four labs to shrink your Windows and SQL Server licensing bill
speaker: Thiago Mantovani, Vitor Euphrasio da Silva, Thiago Sousa Goncalves, Luciano Bernardes, Nits Jeganathan
abstract: Lift-and-shift gets you to the cloud, but it doesn't solve the licensing costs that follow. In this builders' session, you'll work through four labs to reduce your Windows and SQL Server spend on Amazon EC2: (1) enable Compute Optimizer for continuous fleet right-sizing; (2) use Optimize CPU to align cores with compute requirements; (3) classify SQL Server HA clusters to remove passive-node licensing fees; and (4) downgrade SQL Server Enterprise to Standard edition. Leave with a production-ready cost optimization blueprint.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Builders' Session

title: Free your .NET app from Windows licensing with AI-powered portability
speaker: Khurram Khawaja, Mangesh Budkule
abstract: This workshop walks you through modernizing a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to cross-platform .NET 10. You will learn how to transform a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor using AWS Transform Interactive Mode. Throughout the session, you will interact with the AI agent in real-time asking questions, reviewing assessment and transformation plans, and examining transformation results, including code diffs and build verification. Finally, use Kiro to identify and fix post-transformation runtime issues, such as layout problems, and containerize and deploy the transformed application to Amazon ECS Fargate using the Kiro IDE.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano IV

title: Fresh Threats, Stale Defenses: The Race for Real‑Time Security (sponsored by Booz Allen)
speaker: Joseph Gillespie
abstract: Cyber conflict has entered a new phase, accelerated by AI that increases the volume, velocity, and sophistication of attacks. The shift is not that attackers are unstoppable — it is that they operate on a faster clock than the systems meant to contain them. Their advantage is freshness: exploiting what changed before defenders reconcile it, exploiting uncertainty before it becomes understanding, and exploiting stale proof before records drift from reality. AI compresses discovery and action, scaling tasks that once required teams. In this session, learn how defense can be rebuilt around real‑time truth, continuous visibility, and inspectable, defensible action. This presentation is brought to you by Booz Allen, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: From $0 to $100M ARR: Scaling real-time voice AI on AWS
speaker: Zexia Zhang
abstract: Retell AI went from $0 to $100M ARR building real-time voice AI agents on AWS. This session covers the architecture and scaling decisions behind that growth, the infrastructure choices that let Retell AI handle real-time voice at scale, and what founders building voice AI products can learn from their path to $100M ARR.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: From 1,500 to 1M+ databases a week: how Supabase provisions at scale
abstract: With Supabase, developers can use AI agents to build application backends in minutes instead of weeks. Adoption grew from 1,500 databases launched daily in early 2024 to more than one million in a single week in Q3 2026. Running entirely on AWS, Supabase uses Amazon S3 and Amazon EC2 instances with AWS Graviton processors alongside Amazon EKS and Amazon CloudWatch to support that growth. This session shows how startups can use Supabase to launch AI applications quickly and examines the infrastructure behind its database provisioning at scale. Builders of developer tools and AI applications will explore how simpler backend setup reduces the time needed to test ideas.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: From 1 to 20,000: Scale reliably on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS
speaker: Chelsie Zhang
abstract: As AI workloads scale, infrastructure failures become inevitable, causing stalled jobs, degraded throughput, and wasted accelerator capacity. In this chalk talk, we'll show how to build resilient AI workloads on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS. We'll whiteboard the full resiliency stack: Neuron DRA Driver for topology-aware scheduling; UltraServer Operator for provisioning UltraServer workloads; Neuron Observer for sub-second fault detection; and Device Taint for automated recovery. These patterns support fault-tolerant distributed training and inference from a single accelerator to 20,000. You will leave able to assemble this resiliency stack yourself and keep training and inference running through hardware failures.

title: From AI-Assisted Engineering to Autonomous Operations (sponsored by Dynatrace)
speaker: Margarita Rubio, Jon Griffiths
abstract: As enterprise AI matures, the opportunity extends far beyond software development. Join United Airlines, AWS, and Dynatrace to discover how insights powered by AI, full stack cloud observability, and runtime intelligence are helping engineering and operations teams improve reliability, accelerate delivery, and reduce operational complexity. Learn how leading organizations are using real-time data to automate investigations, predict issues before customer impact, and move toward autonomous operations. The session will cover real-world adoption lessons, AI governance considerations, and practical steps to balance automation with accountability while unlocking greater value from AI across the software lifecycle at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Dynatrace, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: From AI Pilots to Enterprise Impact: NJIT's Blueprint for AI Governance and Adoption (sponsored by Kyndryl)
speaker: Blake Haggerty, Jessica Saperstein
abstract: Many organizations are racing to implement AI use cases but struggle to scale beyond isolated experiments. New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT) faced a similar challenge, with AI activity emerging across the institution without a unified strategy, governance model or operating framework. In partnership with Kyndryl, NJIT established an AI governance strategy, operating model and leadership alignment process that transformed fragmented experimentation into a coordinated, institution-wide programme. Join NJIT, Kyndryl and AWS to learn how governance, stakeholder alignment and dedicated operating models can accelerate AI innovation with confidence. Discover why successful AI transformation begins with strategy before technology, and how organisations can move from experimentation to scalable impact. This presentation is brought to you by Kyndryl, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: From AI proof of concepts to enterprise-grade production systems on Ubuntu (sponsored by Canonical)
speaker: Aaron Whitehouse
abstract: AI stacks are complex, interdependent, and high-stakes. Spinning an AI prototype is easy while making it enterprise-ready is much more challenging. Most organizations can’t keep track of their dependencies within their AI projects, leading to solutions that fail security checks and break easily. How do you move to a robust, secure AI solution that is built to last? Learn how to architect, secure, and maintain a resilient enterprise-grade AI infrastructure on Ubuntu, without sacrificing speed. This presentation is brought to you by Canonical, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: From AI Tasks to Autonomous Multi-Agent Workflows with AWS Quick
speaker: Ramon Lopez, Mike Hogan
abstract: The workflows that matter most in financial services span multiple systems, require multiple types of expertise, and today rely on people as the coordination layer. One person pulls data, another reviews it for compliance, a third routes it for approval. That coordination tax is where your team's time disappears. AWS Quick changes that equation. Instead of one AI assistant doing one task, specialized agents each handle their piece and hand off to the next automatically. The human stays in the loop for judgment calls, not for data gathering and routing. Hear from a customer who moved from standalone AI use cases to compound, multi-agent workflows with AWS Quick. Learn how they identified which workflows to orchestrate first, how they designed agent handoffs that satisfy compliance, and what it means now that the coordination layer runs autonomously.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: From AI that responds to AI that delivers measurable outcomes with Zendesk and AWS (sponsored by Zendesk)
speaker: Hannah Deveney, Bailey Backal
abstract: AI can answer a customer’s question while leaving the work unresolved. In this session, discover how Zendesk and AWS connect secure AI, customer context, and service workflows to help teams move customer service requests toward meaningful outcomes. Learn how AI can take action across systems, carry context through a handoff, and bring in human judgment when needed. See how Zendesk Contact Center brings these capabilities to life on voice, connecting AI and human agents to move customer interactions toward better outcomes.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: From AI to Action: Powering Agentic Enterprises with AWS and Infosys (sponsored by Infosys)
abstract: As AI evolves from generating insights to driving action, leading organizations are adopting intelligent agents to transform how work gets done. Hear from enterprise leaders as they share their journeys to building agentic businesses with AWS and Infosys, accelerating decision making, improving productivity, and unlocking measurable business value at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Infosys, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: From AI to enterprise impact: Deploy decision agents on AWS in one day
speaker: Jaime Zornoza
abstract: What if your enterprise could go from AI ambition to AI-powered decisions in just one day? This session examines how Aily Labs orchestrates agents across business functions and supports deployment in regulated enterprises.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: From carbon data to action: Optimize AI workloads on AWS
speaker: Benoit de Chateauvieux, Fabio Grimaldi
abstract: Not all workloads are equal in carbon impact, but how do you know which choices matter most? In this chalk talk, we pull back the curtain on how AWS measures and allocates cloud emissions, balancing scientific rigor with practical usability. Through real-world examples, you'll see how this data reveals meaningful differences across diverse AI workloads. You'll leave with an understanding of the methodology behind your carbon data and how to apply those insights to build AI workloads with a lower environmental footprint, and, often, lower cost.

title: From chatbot to proactive agent: Connect AI to your nonprofit systems
speaker: Madhu Bussa, Mike George
abstract: Agents stall at the demo stage because core enterprise systems — ERPs, legacy databases, and internal APIs — were never built for AI. In this session, we whiteboard two patterns to bridge the gap: request-driven integration via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with access-control interceptors, and event-driven routing via Amazon EventBridge with confidence-based human-in-the-loop fallback. We trace both approaches using a legacy system with no modern API surface — wrapping its interfaces as MCP tools without modifying the original code. The patterns apply whether your blocker is a SOAP endpoint, a stored-procedure layer, or a REST API with no auth story for agents. Leave with a maturity rubric and two practical reference architectures.

title: From Confirmed Exploit to AWS WAF Rule in Minutes (sponsored by Terra)
speaker: Spencer Chin
abstract: A confirmed exploit still needs a code fix, and that fix often takes days or weeks. The exploit path stays open the whole time. This session shows how Terra Security turns a validated pentest finding into a scoped virtual patch inside the application's existing AWS WAF: matched to the specific attack, not a site-wide block, activated by a human on your team, and checked against both the exploit and normal traffic before you trust it. You will leave with a clear picture of how the integration works and a model for closing the gap between proof and fix without breaking the app you are protecting. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: From containers to containment: trust the boundary, not the agent (sponsored by Docker)
abstract: For a decade, teams have trusted containers to run the same way everywhere. Coding agents raise the stakes: the thing inside now installs packages, accesses credentials, and acts on its own. In this session, see how the idea that made containers the standard becomes containment for agents: a Docker sandbox that limits what an agent can reach, hardened images beneath what it builds, and a record of what it was allowed to do and what was stopped, under policies set once for every developer. The agent gets room to work; the boundary gets the trust. That is what running on trust means. This presentation is brought to you by Docker, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: From CSV to Iceberg: Understanding open data formats on Amazon S3
speaker: Ran Pergamin, Danny Jones
abstract: Building a data lake on Amazon S3 and need to decide between Parquet, Hive, and Iceberg – or understand how your team already did? In this session we develop the mental model for storing structured data on Amazon S3 and trace how it evolved. Understand formats from CSV to Parquet that accelerate analytic queries, walk through the evolution of table and partition schemas that organize data at scale, and learn how open table formats like Apache Iceberg bring database-like capabilities to your data lake. Leave with a clear picture of each and how Amazon S3 Tables bring it all together as a fully managed experience.

title: From Databases to Agentic AI: Powering Innovation with AMD EPYC on AWS (sponsored by AMD)
speaker: Ray Prado, Jeremy Girven
abstract: Today's organizations need infrastructure that can efficiently support everything from mission-critical databases to next-generation AI applications. Join AMD and AWS to explore how customers are leveraging Amazon EC2 instances powered by AMD EPYC processors across Amazon RDS, analytics, Agentic AI, HPC, and cloud-native applications. Learn how AMD-powered AWS infrastructure delivers compelling price-performance, scalability, and operational efficiency while helping organizations accelerate innovation, optimize costs, and meet growing compute demands. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: From Data Overload to Action: A Voice-Enabled Digital Assistant for O&G Field Ops (sponsored by PwC)
speaker: Russell King, Brian Morris, Dhruv Shah, Liz Morris
abstract: Field operators in oil and gas often have to piece together production data, equipment alarms, safety notifications, and maintenance priorities from multiple systems to decide how to spend their day. Join Continental Resources and PwC to discover how they collaborated to develop a voice-enabled, mobile-first AI capabilities built on AWS that brings prioritized route-based worklists, well-health visibility, shift handover insights, and voice work note capture into one place. The session covers the journey from frontline challenges to scaling across multiple basins, including the phased delivery approach and lessons learned from field operators, and shows how to move beyond AI experimentation to capabilities embedded in everyday workflows.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: From Demo to Production: The Craft Behind AI Agents at Scale
speaker: Gerardo Arroyo Arce, Diana Castro Cordero
abstract: Your agent reasons, calls tools, and demos beautifully. Then production happens. This session is about the craft that lives after the demo: the unglamorous engineering that separates agents that ship from agents that stay in notebooks. Using real AWS accounts and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, I'll walk through deterministic guardrails that make destructive actions impossible (not just discouraged), spend limits an agent can't prompt-inject its way past, evaluation you can trust, and the IAM that silently breaks first. You'll leave with a production-readiness framework for agentic systems—and honest stories about everything that failed on the way there.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: From discoverable to buyable: Commerce stacks for agent-driven shoppers (sponsored by Stripe)
speaker: Danny Smith
abstract: Join Stripe on how AI is changing how shoppers find and buy products—and what it means for your commerce stack. With 20% of holiday ecommerce traffic projected from AI agents, this session is designed for retail leaders moving from "exploring" to "ready." Converting this traffic requires a different approach to catalog readiness, checkout, fraud, and fulfillment. Attendees will leave with clear priorities to act on today and carry into 2027. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: From documents to decisions: Agentic AI for federal operations
speaker: Raghavarao Sodabathina, Harsha Tadiparthi
abstract: Accelerate mission-critical federal operations with agentic AI—from public-information analysis to sensitive document workflows. This expert chalk talk explores patterns for document review, supply chain optimization and classified medical health records backed by real-world implementations. Whiteboard multi-agent orchestration with Amazon Bedrock, including least-privilege tool access, human approval, auditability, and failure recovery. Compare Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for eligible workloads such as regulatory review, grants, and benefits processing with FEDRAMP (Class C and D). Further explore container-based agent architectures for IL4/IL5 environments using authorized AWS services and models.

title: From First Workload to the Autonomous Enterprise: Transform and Scale with SAP on AWS (sponsored by SAP)
speaker: Steve Van Wyk
abstract: Agentic AI is making ERP modernization more urgent than ever. To coordinate decisions across the organization enterprise, AI must be grounded in a modern cloud ERP foundation—one that connects data, processes, business rules, and controls. ERP is no longer just where work is recorded. It has become the operational foundation that enables enterprise agentic AI and ultimately the Autonomous Enterprise.​ SAP and AWS are partnering to help clients accelerate their AI vision Autonomous Enterprise where people set direction, AI executes operational tasks, and organizations respond faster to change leveraging a single intelligent system with full business context. Join us to explore how SAP on AWS helps moves organizations of all sizes to move beyond isolated AI pilots to enterprise-wide outcomes delivered with reliability and confidence.​ This presentation is brought to you by SAP, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: From Fragmented Infra to Golden Path: An Internal Developer Platform on EKS
speaker: Johannes Koch
abstract: Every team wanted to ship faster, but each was reinventing the same wheels: clusters, pipelines, infrastructure, access. So we built an internal developer platform on Amazon EKS — one golden path that lets product teams go from idea to running service without becoming Kubernetes experts. This is the honest story of that journey. We'll show how we used EKS as the foundation, Crossplane to provision cloud infrastructure through Kubernetes APIs, and Argo CD to drive everything through GitOps. We'll walk through the challenges that nearly derailed us and share what actually moved the needle. You'll leave with a realistic map of the terrain: what worked, what hurt, and what we'd do differently.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: From Gen AI to Agentic AI: Transforming Finance Operations on AWS with Barclays (sponsored by Capgemini)
speaker: Avin Handa, Corey Cederquist
abstract: Barclays is transforming finance operations through an AWS-powered AI platform that combines Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector knowledge bases, and Agentic AI. The platform unifies structured and unstructured finance data to automate SOX controls, enhance management reporting, enable finance data enrichment, and support intelligent decision-making across strategic finance initiatives. Built with enterprise-grade governance, explainability, and auditability, the solution helps strengthen control effectiveness, improve regulatory compliance, and accelerate reporting outcomes. Learn how AI-powered agents, explainable workflows, and governed human-in-the-loop processes are driving operational efficiency, enhancing regulatory confidence, improving audit readiness, and laying the foundation for autonomous finance operations. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: From hardware to application: new EC2 monitoring capabilities
speaker: Ben van der Merwe, Caroline Frost
abstract: This chalk talk covers EC2 health monitoring across hardware, instance, and application layers, including new functionality like EC2 Application Status Checks. Application Status Checks enable you to detect application health impairments by monitoring your applications via configurable paths and ports for HTTP/S. You will learn how to use EC2 health signals to build operational automation for your workloads and integrate these signals with Auto Scaling Groups and Kubernetes.

title: From Hours to Minutes: Fast Android Builds and Virtual Testing on AWS
speaker: Hendrik Schoeneberg, Raphael Hofer
abstract: Automotive software teams lose hours to a slow development cycle: Android builds run for hours, and testing means waiting on scarce physical target hardware. This chalk talk shows how to compress that cycle on AWS. SourceFS cuts Android build times from ~3 hours to under 5 minutes, and the Virtual Engineering Workbench (VEW) lets engineers test against virtual targets in the cloud instead of queuing for physical boards. We'll build up the reference architecture live, show where each piece fits, and walk through the adoption path customers are on today.
