title: From human search to agent retrieval on OpenSearch Service
speaker: Tia White, Sohaib Katariwala, Achal Kumar
abstract: Agents don't search like humans. They fire hundreds of sub-queries per task, need to carry knowledge across sessions, and act on whatever they retrieve. In production, teams hit the same walls: wrong retrieval cascades into wrong actions; when knowledge disappears between sessions, agents repeat work and mistakes; and teams need to see what an agent retrieved, why it acted, and what happened downstream. In this session, learn how Amazon OpenSearch Service helps agents find, remember, and observe on one open foundation, see it in a live demo, and hear how Intuit uses OpenSearch Service across its platform and products.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: From Infrastructure to Intelligence: Building the Full AI Stack in Saudi Arabia (sponsored by HUMAIN)
speaker: Tareq Amin, Rahul Randery
abstract: From Infrastructure to Intelligence: Building the Full AI Stack in Saudi Arabia Building AI at scale means bringing together far more than compute. This conversation will bring together HUMAIN, AWS and technology partners to explore how infrastructure, cloud, data, models and enterprise applications are being connected in Saudi Arabia, and what it takes to make those layers work as one system. The panel will look at partnerships at play across the stack, including the HUMAIN–AWS AI Zone, HUMAIN Fabric on AWS Marketplace and ALLAM on Amazon Bedrock, and discuss what this emerging ecosystem could enable for customers in MENA and around the world. Suggested Panelists: - Tareq Amin, HUMAIN - ⁠Tanuja Randery, AWS - ⁠Enterprise AI Customer (TBC) - Model Provider (TBC: Adobe/Cohere) This presentation is brought to you by HUMAIN, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: From Intent to Interconnection: Building Multicloud Networks in Minutes (sponsored by Equinix)
speaker: Ben Thomas
abstract: Modern enterprises span clouds, AI providers, private infrastructure, partners, and sovereign environments, yet networking is still built one connection at a time. Equinix Fabric One introduces a new approach: declare the business outcome you need and let the platform automatically compose the secure, resilient, any-to-any network required to deliver it. In this live demo, see how Fabric One transforms multicloud networking into an intent-driven experience. Watch a simple declaration trigger automated routing, cloud peering, encryption, resiliency, and failover across multiple providers and destinations. See how Equinix enables organizations to move from “choose, design, configure, operate” to “declare, compose, deliver.” This presentation is brought to you by Equinix, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: From Legacy to Agentic: Modernization Beyond the Code (sponsored by SoftServe)
speaker: Ruslan Kusov
abstract: What if modernization started beyond the code? SoftServe is reimagining application modernization by working backwards from business needs and desired outcomes to determine what should change and why. In this session, see how SoftServe Agentic Application Modernization combines this outcome-driven approach with CAST Software, AWS Transform, Kiro, AI-DLC and specialized AI agents to accelerate discovery, assessment, transformation, and validation. Learn how SoftServe provides the AI foundation to orchestrate and govern these agents, turning modernization into an intelligent, repeatable journey that enables AI for organizations, connects business intent with technology decisions and execution on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by SoftServe, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: From Manual to Autonomous: Agentic AWS Partner Growth via Quick & MCP
speaker: Abhisheikh Lahoti, Musa Musayev, Jing Ning
abstract: Expertise locked in SMEs doesn't scale, and manual partner operations are expensive. The answer is architectural. Amazon Quick, Partner Central MCP Server, and Marketplace AI experiences cut three costs. Cost of sales: AI Listing Experiences, prospecting and co-sell PC agents, demand generation, Funding Agents, and Express Private Offers. Cost of customer operations: Tools to manage customers at scale, auto-renewals, adoption-nudging and reporting agents. Cost of partnerships: automated AWS Specializations, onboarding and journey agents, and Partner revenue telemetry. We cover real-time SME guidance, MCP integration, and orchestration across Partner Central and Marketplace. Leave ready to build your own workflows at scale.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: From MCP poisoning to defense: securing the agent tool supply chain
speaker: Trevor Schiavone, Markus Rollwagen, Abdu Mahmoudi, Joe Rudd, Desiree Brunner
abstract: MCP is becoming the standard for connecting AI agents to tools, but MCP servers are packages that present supply chain risk. In this builders session, you will observe a live MCP tool poisoning attack, then build three defense layers hands-on: gateway validation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Policy to restrict tool actions, a pre-deployment integrity scanner that detects silent tool definition changes, and runtime monitoring that flags anomalous tool behavior. Leave with a working understanding of how MCP supply chain attacks work and how to defend against them.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: From migration to continuous modernization: reduce tech debt at scale
speaker: Neha Goswami, Vidheer Gadikota, Everett Dolgner
abstract: Learn how agentic AI is transforming enterprise modernization from one-off projects into an always-on practice. In this session, we explore how organizations are accelerating cloud migration, modernizing mainframe, Windows, and custom applications, and continuously reducing tech debt across their entire portfolio, evolving their pipelines from CI/CD to CI/CD/CM (continuous modernization). See how teams are compressing modernization timelines from years to months while keeping codebases current and AI-ready. Hear from product leader Neha Goswami on the latest innovations and what's ahead.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Roman I

title: From Millions of Gamers to AI at Scale: Roblox's Hybrid AWS Architecture Unleashed
speaker: Vandana Tewani, Ivan Marcin, Ravi Kiran Chirravuri
abstract: "Auto-scaling was only the beginning. At Roblox, scaling means continuously adapting to changing capacity, hardware availability, GPU constraints, and unpredictable global demand. Join Roblox to learn how they combine AWS with on-premises infrastructure to dynamically place workloads across regions, architectures, and AI providers. Using EC2 Capacity Health Visualizer, hybrid scheduling, multi-region load balancing, self-hosted AI inference alongside Amazon Bedrock, and heterogeneous compute (x86, Graviton, Inferentia, Trainium, GPUs), you will learn how Roblox keeps gaming and AI services responsive under record-breaking load."
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: From MIT Lab to Market: Building Efficient AI for Every Enterprise
speaker: Tiffany Bloomquist
abstract: Manya Ghobadi, founder and CEO of Systalyze and MIT associate professor, spent nearly a decade at MIT studying how to make AI faster, more efficient, and more sustainable. Then she set out to bring that research into the hands of every enterprise. In this fireside chat with Tiffany Bloomquist, Director of APJ Startups at AWS, Ghobadi shares the story behind her company: the moment she realized an academic insight could solve a real business problem, what it took to move from the lab to the market, and why she believes high-performance AI shouldn't demand unlimited resources. Join us for an honest conversation about the inspiration, the journey, and the lessons behind building a deep-tech startup on AWS.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: From Observer to Builder: AI Observability at HubSpot (sponsored by Cribl)
speaker: Bill Emmett, Joshua Andre
abstract: Go from observer to builder with Cribl and AWS. Keep tabs on your AI usage, spend, and sensitive-data risk all in one place. Hear how HubSpot is building apps to automate their team’s workflows and work smarter with AI. This presentation is brought to you by Cribl, an AWS Partner.

title: From our Agents to yours: Build, Optimize and Certify
speaker: Ivan Kopas
abstract: AWS builds its certification exams, from foundational cloud to agentic AI, using production AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. In this session, we show how we built our reasoning agents with AWS Well-Architected practices to solve real operational challenges: climbing latency, spiraling token costs, and non-deterministic failures. You’ll leave with concrete patterns to apply on AWS, plus a clear path to validate those skills through AWS Certification
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: From Pilot to Enterprise Scale with AWS Quick
speaker: Gayatri Ohri, Rekha Seshadrinathan
abstract: EchoStar evaluated 11 AI assistants before selecting AWS Quick, which was then deployed to 8,000 employees with training and pre-populated skills. Next in EchoStar’s plans are integrating Quick with a third party gateways for observability and governance. Come and hear how this was done, uptake and innovations improving the efficiency of employees and teams. Discover some of the challenges integrating into existing enterprise systems, the continued activities needed to keep advancing high value usage and what are the appropriate metrics to track. Walk away with a repeatable framework for taking AWS Quick from pilot to production and enterprise efficiency.

title: From pod to multi-region: Resilient workloads on Amazon EKS
speaker: Ioannis Lioupras, Jean-Francois Landreau
abstract: Building resilient workloads on Amazon EKS requires thinking in layers, from pod-level reliability to multi-region failover. In this chalk talk, explore each layer: Pod Disruption Budgets and Topology Spread Constraints, Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode for fast node recovery, EFS vs EBS for stateful workloads, AWS Backup for cross-region protection, and Route 53 with ARC for region switching. Debate active-active vs active-passive tradeoffs and validate RTO/RPO targets with Resilience Hub.

room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: From prompts to loops: inference best practices for agents
speaker: Nathan Jones, Aris Tsakpinis
abstract: Every layer of an agent, from context and harness to planning loops, places additional demand on the inference engine. Each model turn created by planning, tool use, retrieval, reflection, or retry shapes cost, latency, and reliability. This chalk talk traces that evolution on Amazon Bedrock and shows the inference impact of each layer, with best practices to get them right: versioning prompts, grounding context, engineering a reliable harness, setting verifiable goal conditions, and designing loops that know when to stop. Leave knowing how each layer shapes cost, latency, and reliability.

speaker: Kamen Sharlandjiev, Matt Sampson
abstract: Data engineers spend weeks building pipelines describable in a single sentence. AI agents change this by autonomously discovering data, building transformations, and orchestrating workflows via natural language. Explore how AWS SageMaker Data Agent gives engineers access to analytical tools and data allowing them to quickly create ETL Pipelines . See a live demo of an agent composing a pipeline from a single prompt. Leave with patterns and tools to start building.

title: From proofs to production: Neurosymbolic AI and provable security
speaker: Byron Cook
abstract: AWS has spent a decade proving the correctness of critical infrastructure, from IAM policy evaluation to cryptographic implementations and network isolation. This session traces the evolution from early automated reasoning tools to today's neurosymbolic AI, where formal verification and large language models converge. We examine how mathematical proof engines like Lean, combined with reinforcement learning and agentic workflows, enable provable security guarantees at scale. Attendees will learn how specification-driven development, whole-service data flow analysis, and Bedrock Guardrails' automated reasoning checks are moving the industry beyond "test and hope" toward mathematically verified trust.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: From prototype to production agents across clouds
speaker: Mitul Patel, Guillermo Tantachuco, Ganapathi Krishnamoorthi
abstract: Most agent prototypes share the same shape. One loop, a long lived key on every tool, memory in a side table, the rules in the prompt, and a trace that ends at the model call. It works in a demo. Production readiness and portability across clouds come down to the same four decisions, identity, tool access, state, and governance. In this chalk talk we draw that prototype and rebuild it live into a production agent, one decision at a time, with the room voting at every fork, including how to split the agent, where rules live, how identity federates across providers, where memory has its home, and how one governance layer sees every hop. Then we add a new cloud provider to the drawing and show how little changes.

title: From raw data to custom model: Dataset prep with Amazon SageMaker AI
speaker: Amin Dashti, gzappia Zappia
abstract: Great models start with great data. In this hands-on workshop, use SageMaker AI Agent skills to profile, curate, and validate datasets for the full model customization lifecycle — no infrastructure to manage. Assess data completeness and distribution, apply auto-labeling at scale, run human-in-the-loop review for edge cases, and fix quality issues like deduplication and toxicity filtering. Generate synthetic data to fill coverage gaps, then prepare datasets for Supervised Fine-Tuning, Direct Preference Optimization, Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, and RLAIF. Launch training, evaluate with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploy. Walk away ready to go from raw data to custom model in hours.

title: From reactive operations to autonomous resilience: How Agentic AI is redefining SRE (sponsored by HCLTech)
speaker: Ramesh Ramakrishnan
abstract: Traditional SRE was built to restore systems quickly, but today’s complex, distributed environments demand more than reactive operations. This lightning session explores how agentic AI is redefining SRE by enabling autonomous detection, decision-making, remediation, and continuous learning. It examines how observability can extend beyond infrastructure metrics to connect system health with customer experience and business outcomes. Attendees will learn how HCLTech and AWS are helping enterprises to create resilient, self-optimizing environments by converging AI, observability and operations. The speakers will highlight why autonomous resilience is becoming a competitive advantage and the practical steps organizations can take to progress toward Level 5 autonomous operations while retaining appropriate human oversight and governance.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: From Reactive to Proactive: Omnichannel AI Outreach with Connect Customer
speaker: Jeremy Puent, Bernie Valderrama
abstract: Every organization is building AI agents for inbound, but who's automating outreach? In this workshop, you become a carrier responding to a device safety recall. Instead of posting a notice and waiting for calls, you build a system that identifies affected customers, prioritizes them by risk and value, and uses an AI agent to reach them before they ever pick up the phone. Walk away with a working proactive outreach engine and the architecture to deploy anticipatory engagement at scale.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Pompeian IV

title: From Risk Signal to Recovery: Building Agentic Resilience with MCP (sponsored by Commvault)
speaker: Akshay Joshi, Lawrence Chang, Hiren Chandiramani, Oron Noah
abstract: AI agents are changing cloud operations from human-led workflows to machine-speed decisions and actions. But when agents can access, modify, and move critical data, resilience must become part of the operating model, not a recovery step. Join experts from Commvault, Wiz, and AWS to explore an architecture where MCP connects security context, data intelligence, and recovery capabilities. We'll demonstrate how security signals can guide protection and recovery decisions across Amazon S3 and other cloud services, turning risk insights into governed actions. Learn the guardrails, controls, and architectural patterns behind the workflow, and leave with practical insights for bringing these capabilities into your own cloud-native environments. This presentation is brought to you by Commvault, an AWS Partner.

title: From rules to reasoning: Build an intelligent tagging compliance agent with AgentCore
speaker: Ibrahim Cesar, Francesco Provino, Gautam Bhaghavatula, Avi Harari, Nour Shlian
abstract: AWS Config rules detect missing tags, but what about resources where the correct tag value isn't obvious? In this builder session, you'll create an AI agent using AgentCore that goes beyond detection to intelligent remediation. Your agent analyzes resource context, account ownership, VPC placement, creator identity, naming patterns to infer correct tag values, and handles ambiguous cases by requesting human input. Start where Config rules end: not just "is it tagged?" but "what should the tag be?"

title: From SAP to Agentic AI: Building a unified data strategy on AWS
speaker: Abhijeet Jangam, Diego Lombardini
abstract: This chalk talk presents a unified architecture spanning SAP Business Data Cloud, Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS-native services. Learn how AWS enables progressive modernization from zero-copy federation via BDC Connect, to Iceberg-based lakehouse architectures, to AI-powered analytics with Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, and QuickSight. We introduce the AWS for SAP MCP Server, accessing OData services as AI-ready tools via Model Context Protocol. Live demos showcase AI agents resolving supply chain exceptions, generating Customer 360 insights, and accelerating BW modernization.

title: From self-managed to AWS managed: agentic AI for Kafka and MQ migrations
speaker: Mazrim Mehrtens, Vignesh Selvam
abstract: Migrating self-managed Apache Kafka and RabbitMQ to Amazon MSK and Amazon MQ is hard. Topic mapping, offset translation, ACL migration, and the notoriously long cutover phase slow teams down for weeks. In this chalk talk, we walk through these challenges and show how agentic AI paired with AWS replication tooling compresses the longest migration phase from days to minutes. Watch a complete live migration executed end-to-end in under 60 minutes and leave with a repeatable playbook for your own migration.

title: From shopping agents to shoppers: Amazon CloudFront patterns for peak retail
speaker: Sagar Desarda, Andrew Templeton
abstract: Peak retail traffic is no longer just more shoppers. AI shopping agents, scrapers, and personalized experiences now collide on the same edge. In this session, learn advanced Amazon CloudFront patterns to handle all three. See how to classify and verify agentic traffic using CloudFront Functions, Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore, and AWS WAF Bot Control, then serve tiered responses without touching origin. Hear how you can serve AI-powered personalization on every page in about a millisecond by encoding decision-tree models in KeyValueStore, fed by an Amazon Bedrock pipeline. Discover battle-tested patterns for your next cyber week.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: From Signals to Action for SDG&E and SoCalGas: AI-Powered Cybersecurity on AWS (sponsored by Accenture)
speaker: Brent Shaffer, JONATHAN HOLT, Ben Gordon
abstract: AI is reshaping cybersecurity, but security teams must act faster without adding complexity. San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E) and Southern California Gas Company (SoCalGas), AWS, and Accenture deployed Accenture Cyber.AI on AWS to create a unified view of cyber risk and identify the highest-priority actions across the enterprise. Learn how the team integrated existing security investments, addressed governance and architecture requirements, and operationalized AI-driven risk management. Speakers will share key design decisions, implementation lessons, and practical guidance for using AI to improve cyber resilience, strengthen security operations, and maintain control of data and infrastructure in cloud environments. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: From static to dynamic - modernizing bidirectional federation
speaker: Mohamed Keshk, Ram Maharajapuram
abstract: Static credentials remain the most common source of identity-related security incidents, yet many workloads still rely on them across trust boundaries. AWS now eliminates them in both directions. Humans and workloads outside AWS can use OIDC, SAML, or X.509 certificates to federate in and obtain temporary AWS credentials. Conversely, IAM outbound identity federation lets AWS workloads exchange IAM identities for short-lived JWTs when calling external clouds like Azure and Google Cloud, AI providers like OpenAI or Anthropic, SaaS platforms like Databricks and Snowflake, and your own applications. This session covers how to configure trust, scope credentials, and enforce authorization controls.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: From static to self-improving agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
speaker: Sid Singh, Philip Klose
abstract: AI agents that learn from every production cycle deliver better outcomes without retraining or manual prompt tuning. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations scores live agent behavior across multiple quality dimensions and how the optimization capability discovers better system prompts and tool configurations from production traces. Learn how the agent improves continuously from production results, expert corrections, and revised context your team contributes. We'll demonstrate the full observe-evaluate-improve cycle with an underwriting agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents Framework, then discuss how the pattern applies to claims, fraud, and customer service agents.

title: From system thinking to outcome thinking: The AI-native architect
speaker: Tarik Makota, Andrew Baird, Ryan Law
abstract: The architect role is changing faster than at any point since the cloud itself emerged. AI is reshaping not just what architects build, but how they think, where they spend their time, and what organizations expect. We share observations from leading a global transformation of thousands of AWS Solutions Architects into AI-native practitioners: what shifted in daily practice, what surprised us, and what broke. We explore how outcome-oriented thinking replaces system-oriented thinking, and why the line between building and advising is dissolving. You leave with a practical mental model for how the architecture role delivers value in an AI-native world.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering At Scale
speaker: Doug Clauson, Pooja Giri, Ricardo Britto
abstract: Most developers use AI coding assistants as interactive tools and see modest gains. A small cohort works differently: they treat agents as autonomous workers they direct and validate, and the results are a step function in productivity improvements, not an increment. In this session, we break down what these power users do differently, share success stories, where experts still find friction, and the bottlenecks coming next. We'll share demos so you leave with concrete, repeatable practices for getting orders-of-magnitude more out of Kiro agents.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: From Vibe Coding to Cloud-Native: Agentic Patterns for Production
abstract: Vibe coding made it easy to build software. Getting a prototype to production is the hard part. Using Rethrow as a case study, this session shows how AI agents assess an app, plan and run a migration, change code, and iterate through build-and-verify loops with little human input. We compare headless agent workflows with interactive sessions over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), and cover what keeps agents safe in multi-tenant environments, like scoped credentials, retry budgets, failure escalation, and property-based verification.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: From vulnerability to exploit to fix: closing the loop with AWS Security Services
speaker: Jason Schamp, Aliaksei Ivanou, Chad Short, Travis Rocco, Kiran Dongara
abstract: You start with a deployed e-commerce web application containing OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities like SQL injection and SSRF, hardcoded credentials, and a dependency CVE. Using Amazon Inspector and AWS Continuum (formerly AWS Security Agent), you discover and validate existing flaws, reproduce the exploit chain, and push Continuum-generated fixes through CI/CD. When Amazon GuardDuty detects the active exploitation, including credential theft and prompt injection against an AI assistant, you isolate the compromised instance and harden it. Walk away with a repeatable closed-loop workflow: Inspector finds it, GuardDuty catches it, Continuum fixes it.

title: From Workloads to Agents: Rethinking Cloud Resilience (sponsored by Cohesity)
speaker: Monsef Elalamy, Theresa Miller
abstract: Under the shared responsibility model, you own the security and recoverability of your entire cloud estate - and that estate now includes AI agents. In this session, HUB International will share their experiences.​ Agents are becoming core infrastructure, executing actions across interconnected systems at machine speed. Yet most organizations can't recover agent memory, credentials, or configurations any better than they could recover a corrupted server a decade ago. Join us to see how Cohesity's resilience platform extends AWS-native protections to agents and infrastructure alike, so risk doesn't outrun your ability to recover. This presentation is brought to you by Cohesity, an AWS Partner.

title: From your first Amazon EKS cluster to a self-serve developer platform
speaker: Jesse Butler, Nirmal Mehta
abstract: The best Kubernetes platforms are invisible to the people who use them. Developers provision, deploy, and scale through self-service interfaces without needing Kubernetes expertise, while platform teams reclaim the cycles once spent on cluster operations and lifecycle management. That is the standard now that Amazon EKS is engineered to deliver. Come hear how EKS sees developer experience evolving: Auto Mode removing undifferentiated operational load through managed compute, scaling, and add-ons; EKS Capabilities exposing AWS services as governed, self-serve building blocks; and AI agents taking on operational workflows (upgrades, diagnostics, remediation) that platform teams have owned for years.

title: From Zero to 20,000 Desktops: Getting Started with AWS Quick
speaker: Jose Kunnackal John
abstract: Your team is drowning in context-switching: toggling between email, documents, data tools, and chat just to complete a single task. Productivity tools promise to help, but most add complexity instead of removing it. In this fireside chat, hear from customers who faced that exact challenge and deployed an AI work companion across 20,000+ users in under 90 days. Learn what convinced their leadership to invest, how they integrated AI into daily workflows without disrupting existing tools, and what the first 90 days of adoption actually looked like. Walk away with a practical roadmap for bringing AWS Quick AI assistant to your workforce at scale.

title: Frontier Engineering Applied: Rethinking Infrastructure for the Agent Era
abstract: Frontier engineering means rethinking how we solve hard infrastructure problems. When agents run autonomously, assessing codebases, planning migrations, and executing changes with minimal human input, the constraints shift. Rethrow is a cloud migration platform built to prove this works at scale. This session covers how we keep agents honest: ensuring they follow cloud architecture best practices, validate against approved services, use escalation mechanisms for edge cases, and maintain predictability and consistency across runs. What we solved, what still breaks, and what's next.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

speaker: Rajeev Srinivasan
abstract: To unlock transformative business outcomes, AI agents require a foundation of trusted data with rich enterprise context. Delivering success means bridging the knowledge, trust, and action gaps across a highly complex data landscape. In this session, learn how Informatica Intelligent Data Management Cloud (IDMC) provides the comprehensive AI-ready data needed to power reliable agentic workflows. Explore how headless IDMC architecture via integrations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Agent Registry and Amazon Quick fuels agents with trusted enterprise context and end-to-end governance, driving impactful results and long-term project success. This presentation is brought to you by Informatica, an AWS Partner.

title: Full-stack data agents using Box MCP and AWS
speaker: Gopal Surapaneni, Janardhan Molumuri, Chidambaram Muthappan, Padmaraj Anand, Oscar Carrasquero
abstract: Organizations struggle to assess contract compliance as terms live in unstructured documents while structured financial and risk data sit in operational databases across the enterprise. In this session, build an AI agent that performs real-time contract compliance analysis, bridging unstructured content stored in Box with operational structured data on AWS. Using Box MCP in AWS Marketplace, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon Aurora, you implement a multi-MCP architecture, routing to Box for contract extraction and to AWS databases for operational data, producing auditable compliance determinations citing both unstructured content and structured data. You must bring your laptop to participate.

abstract: Building modern web and mobile front ends means juggling a lot of moving parts, and everyone's stack looks a little different. We'll talk through how AWS Amplify helps you define backends in code and ship full-stack apps fast, how AWS AppSync powers real-time and offline data with managed GraphQL and WebSocket APIs, and how AWS Device Farm lets you test across real browsers and mobile devices before your users do. Whether you're starting a greenfield app or scaling an existing one, come ready to steer the conversation.

title: Fundamentals to scale Kubernetes across your organization
speaker: Math Bruneau, Raj Athavale

You can learn how to optimize scaling with Karpenter, automate day-to-day operations with EKS Auto Mode, troubleshoot real-world issues, and extend clusters on-premises with EKS Hybrid Nodes. Get hands-on building resilient, production-grade clusters on Amazon EKS following industry best practices and explore the latest Amazon EKS features, choosing only the modules that matter most to you.

title: Future-proof your keys: HSMs to AWS KMS in the post-quantum era
speaker: Kevin Kevin, Derek Tumulak
abstract: Cryptography is changing fast. The dedicated HSM you rely on today, whether AWS CloudHSM or an on-premises appliance, carries operational overhead that will only grow as the industry moves toward post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and stricter digital sovereignty requirements. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now covers most workloads that once required dedicated HSMs, with the same FIPS 140-3 Level 3 security, lower cost, and zero infrastructure management, while giving you a clear on-ramp to PQC and the sovereignty controls to keep your keys and data under your control. In this chalk talk, bring your architecture and we'll work through it together: we'll assess your workload, map signature and encryption migration paths, and show how moving to KMS puts you on the fastest path to post-quantum readiness. Meet the AWS Cryptography team and leave with a plan and concrete next steps.

title: Gaining insights with S3 Metadata and annotations
speaker: Sumaja Kapa, Bimal Gajjar, Lee Kear, Lokesh AP, Fabio Lattanzi
abstract: Learn how S3 annotations let you attach rich, structured context (JSON, XML, YAML, or plain text) directly to your objects without re-uploading them. In this session, you will configure annotations on a live dataset, build an enrichment pipeline that attaches AI-generated summaries on ingest, query annotation payloads at scale through S3 Metadata's Apache Iceberg table in Athena, and wire an AI agent that discovers and retrieves objects using annotation-based search. You leave with patterns for zero-read agentic discovery and metadata architectures that scale to billions of objects.

title: Gatekeepers & guardrails: Secure AI agents across your nonprofit stack
speaker: Jason Rodriguez, Ramanathan Muralidhar
abstract: AI agents that reach across your tools via MCP are a force multiplier — but letting an agent call OAuth-protected APIs means handling credentials, identity, and blast radius. Get it wrong and you expose sensitive data. In this code talk, deploy an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and walk through three-legged OAuth live: secure token storage via AgentCore Identity, identity propagation across agent chains, confused-deputy prevention, and guardrails on tool results. Whether you're a 5-person nonprofit team or a 5,000-person enterprise, leave with deployable IaC for your own environment.

title: Gemini gets closer to traders with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
speaker: Ina Rademacher, Joshua Smith, Chirag Jain
abstract: Gemini, a NASDAQ-listed crypto exchange, serves traders with diverse latency needs. For the most latency-sensitive workloads, AWS Outposts at Gemini's NY5 facility runs adjacent to the matching engine with sub-millisecond connectivity via cross-connects. For cloud-native traders, AWS Local Zones in NYC deliver sub-2ms latency to the matching engine through Amazon VPC peering: bringing compute into New York Local Zone cuts round-trip latency by roughly 80%, with provisioning in minutes rather than months. For customers prioritizing simplicity, the AWS Region offers a fully managed API that also serves agentic trading systems via Model Context Protocol (MCP). Hear how Gemini's tiered model turns compute placement into a competitive lever for your location-sensitive workloads.

title: GenAI chip selection: From training to inference
speaker: Kumar Shubham, Barak Nissim
abstract: Every GenAI workload hits the same question: GPU, Trainium, Graviton, or Inferentia—and when do you use each? In this chalk talk, we walk through a practical decision tree covering model training, real-time inference, and agentic AI workloads. We then go deep on inference cost optimization: right-sizing GPU instances, offloading pre/post-processing to Graviton, using Spot for batch inference, prompt caching, and moving production inference to Inferentia2. Expect opinionated guidance, real customer math from teams that cut inference costs without sacrificing latency, and a whiteboard framework you can take back to your team on Monday.

title: Get Mythos-ready: Continuous Offensive Security (sponsored by Terra)
speaker: Shahar Peled, Supreet Kaur
abstract: AI ships code faster, and frontier models like Claude Mythos find exploits at machine speed. Open-weight models that anyone can run now find many of the same veulnrabilities. Traditional security testing cannot keep pace with AI adversaries. This session shows what Mythos readiness looks like: continuous validation of what changed, not a full retest of everything. Learn how to separate true risk from theoretical vulnerabilities, and see how a trained agentic swarm turns raw exposure signals into verified, exploitable findings your team can act on.

speaker: Robert Belson, Madhu Samhitha Vangara
abstract: You can build an agent in an afternoon. Getting it to production takes months. title: Getting the capacity you need: EC2 Launch APIs and Intelligent Auto Scaling deep dive
speaker: Justin Kwong, Samruddhi Kochkar
abstract: Getting the right compute at the right time is a two-part challenge: launching instances effectively and scaling them intelligently. This deep dive covers both. First, we explore RunInstances—EC2's oldest and most important API—sharing launch best practices, how flexibility helps you get the capacity you need, and how EC2 Fleet incorporates advanced strategies into your calls. Then we go under the hood of EC2 Auto Scaling, and the intelligence that also scales DynamoDB, WorkSpaces, EMR, SageMaker AI, and Aurora. Learn how to use target tracking, predictive scaling, and auto-tuning to automatically and intelligently scale your workloads.

title: Ghost agents: Governing ephemeral AI & machine access in real-time (sponsored by SailPoint)
speaker: Stephen Cortese
abstract: Ephemeral AI agents and cloud workloads spin up, access resources, and vanish in minutes, never landing in traditional identity registries. How do you govern what you can’t track? The answer lies in securing the non-human identities (NHIs) they leave behind. Join SailPoint for a live demo on governing ephemeral agent behavior. We’ll show you how to untangle NHI ownership, expose over-privileged access, and establish real-time governance over transient machine identities before they expose your cloud. Walk away with a blueprint to manage non-human access risk at cloud scale. This is clarity you can act on. This presentation is brought to you by SailPoint, an AWS Partner.

speaker: Kunal Ghosh, Joel Farvault, Prasad Nadig, Luis Campos, Aritra Ghosh, KiKi Nwangwu
abstract: An AI agent pointed at a data catalog that has schema but no meaning will guess — and in a regulated environment, guessing is a compliance liability. Enrich the catalog with business context — Skill Assets, golden queries, business glossary terms, ownership, and access restrictions — then connect an MCP-compatible AI agent and watch its answers shift from hallucination to governed, data-literate reasoning. Use semantic search to discover data by business meaning, add queryable metadata forms at scale, and leave with architecture patterns to roll this out across your existing catalog. You must bring your laptop to participate.

This session shows how NeuBird AI has helped teams recover 200 plus engineering hours a month and cut incident costs 60 percent or more, not by hiring more people or buying more dashboards, but by giving one agent the job of running production so your senior engineers can go back to building it. speaker: Jesse Lepich, Bryan Van Hook
abstract: How do you secure that which has no network? AWS services such as S3, SQS, and DynamoDB help teams build and scale faster but come with a different set of security implications than services that live in your VPC. In this session, you'll learn about best practices and architectural patterns for building secure networks on AWS using network features like DNS firewall, and Network firewall and layering them with AWS IAM policies like VPC endpoint policy, and Resource Control Policy to help ensure that your resources that live outside of your network behave like they are in your network.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Gotta detect 'em all: finding rogue devices with Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Jenifer Wang, Reshad Habibzai, Anthony Castaneda, Insoo Jang, Collin Chew
abstract: Participants build and command autonomous drone fleets to identify rogue devices using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, AWS IoT Greengrass, and Strands Agents. This gamified scenario showcases a Human-Machine Teaming architecture in which AI operates autonomously within defined trust boundaries, with human-in-the-loop escalation at configurable confidence thresholds.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Governance foundations for AI workloads that grow into autonomous agents
speaker: Rodolfo Brenes, Nivas Durairaj
abstract: Agentic workloads are reaching production, and governance has to keep up without slowing teams down. This session shows how to build a governance foundation for AI with AWS Control Tower, AWS Config, AWS Organizations, and automatic evidence collection, then extend it to autonomous agents. You apply preventive and detective controls to Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker, automate compliance evidence, and map controls to frameworks such as ISO 42001. The same controls hold whether the workload is a single model call or a fleet of agents acting on their own.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Govern and optimize AI agents for desktop work on WorkSpaces
speaker: Ed Mahlum, Andrew Morgan
abstract: Your most valuable business processes often run inside desktop applications and mainframes that expose no APIs for AI agents to call. In this session, learn how to use Amazon WorkSpaces to give agents a governed desktop where they operate these applications directly, just as an employee would. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into scoping what agents are permitted to do, auditing agent actions, and configuring agent identity. We'll walk through strategies for agent optimization: how to choose the right agent tools, select the right model for your workflow, and build reusable agent skills. Applied together, these techniques cut task time, lower cost, and increase the accuracy of your agent workflows.

title: Govern, Bill, and Attribute: The Unit Economics of Production Agents
speaker: Daniele Stroppa, Obaid Kazi
abstract: Your agent demo costs $0.02 a call; in production it's $4. Can you still price it profitably, and can you capture the full AWS consumption it drives downstream? This chalk talk walks the complete unit economics of a production agent: right-sizing cost with prompt caching, model routing, and tool-call minimization; pricing through consumption versus outcome-based billing; and attributing the full impact through AWS Marketplace metering and PRM, so it converts into AWS investment back to you. Real examples like bid optimization, content moderation, and shopping advisors ground each step.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Govern data and AI agents with lineage and context in AWS Glue Data Catalog
speaker: Navneet Srivastava, Abbas Makhdum, Jorge A Lopez
abstract: AI agents generate SQL, surface insights, and take action on your data. Without governance guardrails, they hallucinate column meanings, query stale tables, and return wrong answers with high confidence. In this session, learn how to ground your AI agents in trusted metadata using AWS Glue Data Catalog. See how to flow business context like glossary terms, descriptions, and quality scores into agent workflows so they generate accurate, schema-aware queries instead of guessing. Walk away with practical patterns for governing AI-assisted analytics the same way you govern human analysts
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Governed ModelOps: From customization to deployment with SageMaker AI
speaker: Siamak Nariman, Bobby Lindsey, Sunita Koppar, Naresh Nagpal
abstract: Join us in working through the ModelOps lifecycle, starting with experiment, train, register, approve, to deploy, anchored by the Amazon SageMaker catalog system of record. Using SageMaker managed MLflow and the catalog within SageMaker AI Studio, you'll build governance in as you go with no end-of-cycle compliance scramble. Training runs auto-catalog with model cards, lineage, and audit trails; you'll discover assets with semantic search, trace lineage with OpenLineage, configure access control, gate promotion on quality and compliance, and publish models across accounts. You'll leave able to trace any endpoint to its dataset, experiment, and approval in seconds.

title: Governing AI assets at scale with MCP Gateway and Registry
speaker: Amit Arora, Sabeena Shafaq
abstract: As enterprises onboard AI assets (MCP servers, Agents, Skills) they face a governance problem: no unified way to discover, authenticate, or observe them. MCP Gateway and Registry is an open source control plane with centralized registration, OAuth2 auth, semantic tool discovery, and end-to-end telemetry. Walk through the project's architecture, pluggable auth and storage backends, and deployment patterns on Amazon EKS. An AI/ML platform VP shares their production rollout, governance patterns that scaled across business units, and lessons learned contributing back upstream.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Governing autonomous AI agents across cloud boundaries
speaker: Arko Dutta, Prema iyer
abstract: When autonomous agents coordinate across cloud boundaries, who enforces the rules — and how do you revoke access instantly when one goes rogue? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard governed multi-agent coordination: Cedar as a portable policy engine across AWS, Azure, and GCP, A2A protocol for cross-cloud agent communication, and a kill switch for instant revocation. The audience picks the scenario — flight delays, trade failures, or healthcare cancellations — and we draw how policy, identity, and coordination work at each boundary crossing.

title: Governing Hundreds of Accounts in Minutes: Agentic AI Meets Landing Zone Operations
speaker: Randy Domingo, Bo Lechangeur
abstract: When you manage hundreds of AWS accounts, governance can fall behind. Drift accumulates, controls take days to propagate, and problems go undetected until something breaks. We demonstrate Landing Zone Accelerator 2.0 with built-in AI that lets operators use natural language to apply organizational changes in minutes, if not seconds. We deploy org-wide security controls, provision accounts, and enforce encryption through a Bedrock-powered interface supporting CloudFormation and Terraform. An AI agent generates each change plan, and before anything is applied, an org-wide preview catches conflicts and policy violations. Issues are surfaced up front instead of discovered after a break. Attendees learn how we built LZA 2.0 with Kiro spec-driven development and Rust, and how to design pre-deployment previews that keep multi-account operations safe.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Govern your context layer for AI agents with AWS Context
speaker: Leonardo Gomez Virahonda, Emily Zhu
abstract: Learn how to carry your existing data permissions into a governed context layer your AI agents need to work accurately across structured and unstructured data. AWS Context assembles semantic data from your catalogs, glossaries, query logs, and access patterns into one governed context layer, honoring the governance contract placed on your data assets. Each user's identity flows through the agent so every answer is scoped to what they are authorized to see. We will whiteboard and interact on how identity propagates, how retrieval is filtered, and where permissions break.

title: GPU cluster failure patterns on AWS: observe, diagnose, recover
speaker: Daisuke Miyamoto, Harish Rao, Natarajan Chennimalai Kumar, Keita Watanabe, SooJung Lee
abstract: At scale, GPU clusters fail in ways that single-node debugging does not reveal: NCCL timeouts that are actually storage problems, DataLoader forks that silently hang collectives, and GPUs that pass health checks yet corrupt results. In this hands-on builders session, diagnose these failures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter. Read NCCL debug logs, interpret all-reduce bus bandwidth against per-instance baselines, and run open-source health checks that catch faults early. The session provides a failure-signature runbook and a triage method drawn from operating large GPU fleets on AWS.

title: GPU orchestration using NVIDIA Run:ai across the edge
speaker: Alex Iankoulski, Siva Devabakthini, Robert Belson
abstract: AWS and NVIDIA have collaborated for over a decade to deliver GPU-accelerated solutions across the cloud and edge, yet Kubernetes still treats GPUs as opaque, unshareable integers. In this Level 400 code talk, learn how to deploy NVIDIA Run:ai on Amazon EKS and execute a complete model lifecycle on shared GPU infrastructure. Using Terraform, provision EKS clusters on Amazon EC2 instances with NVIDIA L4 GPUs, install the Run:ai control plane and cluster agents, and configure project-scoped GPU quotas with priority-based sharing. Then see how Run:ai orchestrates a QLoRA fine-tuning job on Qwen3-14B and serves the resulting adapter with vLLM so you can compare base model responses against your fine-tuned model in real time.

title: Graviton5: Migrate your workloads, cut costs, get better performance
speaker: Sudhir Raman, Ali Saidi
abstract: AWS Graviton5 delivers up to 25% better compute performance than the previous generation, features caches up to five times larger, and offers some of the fastest memory performance available in the cloud. But what do those improvements actually mean for your workloads? In this session, we go beyond the spec sheet into real-world benchmarks across databases, web applications, and ML inference. Hear from a customer who migrated production workloads across multiple Graviton generations and the compounding performance and cost gains they achieved. Walk away with concrete performance data and a practical framework to evaluate Graviton5 for your own migration.

title: Graviton. Serverless. Apache Iceberg. Your guide to a modern data warehouse strategy
speaker: Raza Hafeez, Divya Ananthanarayanan, Manikandan Paramasivan
abstract: You need your data warehouse to be fast, open, and accessible to everyone on your team. This session shows you how to get there with Amazon Redshift. Take advantage of Graviton-powered RG instances for faster analytics at lower cost. Eliminate the complexity of managing infrastructure with Redshift Serverless. Query open data formats directly in your data lake with native Apache Iceberg support. And put insights in the hands of every team with natural language access. You'll also learn how multi-warehouse architectures let teams scale independently without duplicating data. Leave with a clear architecture strategy you can apply to your environment.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Grievances, Gripes, and Genuine Developer Feedback
abstract: This is your open mic. Something in AWS drives you up the wall? A workflow that takes nine steps when it should take two? A console that hides the one button you need? An error message that reads like a ransom note? We want to hear all of it. This isn't a sales pitch or a roadmap tease — it's a room where developers vent honestly and we listen, write it down, and actually bring it back to the service teams who can fix it. We can't promise every pet peeve becomes a launch, but we can promise it won't disappear into a void. Bring your frustrations; leave feeling heard.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Grounding LLMs in Truth: Build a Live Fact-Checking Pipeline
speaker: Vince Palazzo, Guillaume Marchand, Florian Clanet, Alen Zograbyan, Iryna Oliinykova
abstract: Walk through the reference architecture of a real-time fact-checking pipeline built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See how a live audio stream is turned into fact-by-fact verdicts (true, misleading, or false), with source citing at broadcast-compatible latency. Learn how to build it yourself using a chain of specialized agents on AgentCore, hybrid search on Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and custom tool-use hooks. Leave with a mapped path to create a reference architecture, plus answers to the concrete design questions blocking you such as: agent sharding, tabular corpus indexing, guardrails, and streaming reasoning to the UI.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Ground your agents with AWS Context and Amazon SageMaker
speaker: Hari Thatavarthy, sandeep Adwankar
abstract: Agents are only as good as the context they're given. In this session, see how AWS Context makes the agentic experience in Amazon SageMaker more accurate and useful by grounding agents in business metadata. We'll show how context-aware agents like SageMaker Data Agent break complex requests into structured, multi-step plans, generate validated SQL, Python, and PySpark against your real data, and keep humans in the loop with built-in checkpoints. You'll learn practical techniques to feed the right context to your agents, connect additional sources, and turn a capable assistant into one that truly understands your environment.

title: Growing role of CPUs in AI: Inference and agents AI on EC2
speaker: Anton Valter, Anuj Purohit
abstract: CPUs play a critical and growing role in production AI systems. This session explores two CPU-intensive AI patterns on EC2. First, AI inference: serving language model predictions at scale using Graviton and x86 instances, with real-world cost and latency tradeoffs. Second, agentic AI: running sandboxed environments where autonomous agents compile code, execute tools, and interact with external systems, requiring fast, isolated, ephemeral compute. We share production architectures, performance benchmarks across instance families, and practical guidance on matching your AI workload to the right EC2 CPU. Walk away with a decision framework for running AI beyond GPUs.

title: Guardrails for AI-generated Serverless infrastructure
speaker: Tomas Mihalyi, Stan Fan
abstract: Coding agents generate full serverless architectures in seconds, but without guardrails they produce over-permissioned IAM policies, skip encryption at rest, and deploy resources that violate your organization's tagging and cost policies. In this chalk talk, discuss operational controls for AI-generated infrastructure: automated security reviews that catch policy violations before deployment, cost estimation gates that flag unexpected spend, compliance checks against organizational standards, and MCP server configurations that enforce service boundaries and naming conventions. We whiteboard which guardrails to automate versus which require human review, and where teams are getting the balance wrong.

title: Guide to deploying landing zones & modernized networks in hours
speaker: Evgeny Karasik, Efrat Manor Portnoy
abstract: Reimagine what migration looks like when landing zone setup and network translation go from weeks to hours. In this chalk talk, we show how AWS Transform's agentic AI compresses that timeline, from migration inventory to fully deployed, validated landing zones and modernized networks. See how production-ready account structures deploy through Control Tower with guardrails in place, and how firewall configurations become optimized VPCs, subnets, and security groups. Bring your questions and hear from the experts building these capabilities.

title: HA and DR design patterns for Amazon RDS for SQL Server and Oracle
speaker: Javeed Mohammed, Eric Felice
abstract: Explore high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) design patterns for SQL Server and Oracle databases on Amazon RDS. In this session, learn about the features offered by Amazon RDS for business continuity, including Multi-AZ deployments, read replicas, and cross-region replication. Discover the customizations that Amazon RDS enables for HA and DR while also allowing you to bring your own license (BYOL) for SQL Server. Also learn how globally resilient solutions architected with Amazon RDS minimize downtime and meet stringent business continuity requirements for mission-critical workloads.

title: Hadoop to EMR & Airflow: Lessons from Migrating 90+ Data Pipelines
abstract: Migrating one data pipeline to the cloud is a project; migrating dozens is a program. In this meetup, compare notes with peers who have moved Hadoop and Oozie-era workloads to Amazon EMR and Apache Airflow. Discuss how to sequence pipelines by dependency, prove old and new outputs match, right-size EMR clusters for Spark and ML jobs, and cut over without breaking downstream consumers. Bring your migration stories. Leave with a peer-built checklist and a network of practitioners to call when your next migration stalls.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Hands-on distributed training with AWS Trainium and PyTorch
speaker: Samir Araujo, Hanno Bever
abstract: Get hands-on with AWS Trainium and PyTorch's TorchTitan to train models using a fully native PyTorch workflow. This workshop walks you through distributed training on Trainium, covering cluster setup, parallelism strategies, and performance optimization, all through familiar PyTorch APIs. Whether you're training LLMs or fine-tuning domain models, you'll learn how Trainium and TorchTitan simplify scaling without sacrificing native PyTorch flexibility. You will leave able to scale model training on Trainium without changing your PyTorch workflow.

title: Hands-on: Harden your AI agents with Nitro Confidential Computing
speaker: Arvind Raghu, Sudhir Reddy Maddulapally
abstract: Agentic AI systems autonomously orchestrate tools, integrate third-party components, and make decisions, introducing risks from compromised dependencies and agents deviating from intended behavior. Protecting prompts, agent memory, retrieval context, and model weights requires strong isolation and verifiable trust. In this workshop, you will build agentic AI apps, identify threats from untrusted supply chains and uncontrolled autonomy, and mitigate them using AWS Confidential Computing on EC2 with cryptographic attestation, isolated execution, open weight models, and Amazon Bedrock.

title: Hands-on Network Defense with AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 DNS Firewall
speaker: Lawton Pittenger, Brian Westmoreland
abstract: In this workshop, you'll build a comprehensive network security architecture using AWS Network Firewall and Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall. You'll configure egress and VPC-to-VPC traffic inspection, IDS/IPS filtering, and container-aware rules for dynamic workload protection. Explore DNS-layer defenses, including DNS tunneling detection, and gain visibility into AI service traffic through domain category filtering. Through real-world scenarios, you'll cover the most common use cases and leave knowing how these services work together to defend your network. This workshop is for security and network engineers who are comfortable with Amazon VPC networking and AWS Transit Gateway.

title: Hands-on training world models and deploying agents for Physical AI
speaker: Jianying Lang, Pierre Lienhart, Tong Zhang
abstract: Physical AI is transforming robotics and autonomous systems with world models that enable agents to understand and interact with their environments. Training and deploying these large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) models requires complex distributed infrastructure. AWS Trainium and AWS Neuron simplify this with PyTorch integration: apply standard distributed training techniques using familiar APIs while the software stack handles multi-device coordination, compilation, and optimization. In this hands-on session, fine-tune a transformer-based world model, implement parameter-efficient training strategies, and deploy trained agents for real-time inference. You will build the skills to adapt Physical AI models and deploy robotic agents across large clusters.

title: Hands-on with AWS DevOps agent
speaker: Shyam Sunder Kulkarni, Dan Malloy
abstract: AWS DevOps Agent is your always-available operations teammate that investigates, resolves, and proactively prevents incidents. In this hands-on workshop, take the on-call seat: inject real faults into a live microservices store on Amazon EKS, partner with the agent to root-cause them in minutes, and judge its mitigation plans. Then extend it — encode your team's expertise as skills, connect custom MCP tools, automate investigations from alarms, and approve agent-executed fixes. Leave with production-ready patterns that keep your infrastructure running.

title: Hands-on with the AWS Network Firewall proxy for secure egress
speaker: Preetkumar Shah, Rahi Patel, Geoff Sweet, Hunter Chilcote, Anvesh Koganti
abstract: AWS Network Firewall now gives you the flexibility to act as an explicit forward proxy for outbound traffic on the firewall you already run. Clients connect to it directly by its proxy FQDN, so no route-table changes are required. The proxy attaches to a NAT gateway and terminates each client connection, letting one firewall consolidate egress for multiple VPCs regardless of overlapping CIDRs. In this builders session you'll get hands-on deploying the proxy and building layered egress controls, up to and including outbound TLS inspection. You'll leave knowing when and how to use the firewall proxy to centralize and enforce egress controls for private workloads.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Happy Hour in Expo
abstract: Turn ideas into innovation at the Expo Happy Hour. Meet AWS experts, see partner demos, and enjoy complimentary drinks. Sponsored by ResolveAI.

title: Healthcare & Life Sciences AI Agents: From Spec to Demo in 120 Min
speaker: Ariella Sasson, Necibe Ahat, Nadeem Bulsara
abstract: Healthcare and life sciences teams face pressure to apply generative AI, but they struggle to move from proof-of-concept to prototype. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use Kiro IDE and spec-driven development to build a functional AI agent, progressing through requirements, design, implementation, and live demo. Choose from four use cases: extract data from handwritten GMP batch records, orchestrate single-cell RNA-seq pipelines on AWS HealthOmics, identify clinical trial candidates using biomarker analysis, or build a patient access agent on Amazon Connect Health. You'll create a deployable agent, reusable specs, and a repeatable methodology for rapid AI development in regulated environments.

title: Hidden trade-offs in distributed architectures
speaker: Anahit Pogosova
abstract: Asynchronous event-driven architectures enable loosely coupled, scalable, and resilient systems. But the devil is in the details, and hidden complexity emerges when components interact under real-world pressure. Consistency, latency, failure handling, and cost aren't determined by architecture diagrams but by the trade-offs behind the integration patterns and services you choose. Through a real-world case study using AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB, DynamoDB Streams, and AWS Step Functions, you'll investigate unexpected system behavior and uncover the trade-offs behind it. You'll leave with a sharper intuition to see beyond cloud abstractions and make more intentional architectural decisions for resilient systems.

title: High latency! Is it the code, the container, or the host?
speaker: Oliver Smyth, Rodrigue Koffi
abstract: Your app is slow, but is it the code, the container, or the underlying host? When your stack spans clouds, hybrid, and on-prem, correlating application performance to infrastructure health means jumping between tools and guessing at root cause. Join this session as we walk through how to map application signals such as traces, errors, and latency directly to the infrastructure, regardless of where it runs. You'll see how to pinpoint whether the problem is your app or the compute it sits on, without stitching dashboards together manually.

title: How 2 Billion Records Became One Data Product at Verisk (sponsored by Senzing)
speaker: Gurpinder Dhillon, Gurshish Dang
abstract: Every insurance data product, underwriting or claims, hinges on one question: is this the same person or organization across systems? Verisk answers it once, at scale, treating the answer as a data product. This session unpacks how Verisk used AI-powered entity resolution on AWS to turn fragmented, siloed, acquisition-inherited data into one reusable identity asset, a proprietary entity ID appended across policies, claims, and enrichment data, not another MDM project. A five-person team built this across 2 billion records and 400 million identities with sub-second response. That data commands premium value, and identity became infrastructure, not a cleanup project. This presentation is brought to you by Senzing, an AWS Partner.

At CMT, we are applying new AI architectures to better understand mobility data, particularly road and driver risk. You'll learn how they're now using GitLab Duo Agent Platform and Amazon Bedrock to accelerate development toward their next lunar lander. title: How Amazon Ads Built a Service Mesh Without a Control Plane Service
speaker: Yiwen Luo, Soham Kale, Garry Galinsky
abstract: Most service meshes require dedicated infrastructure just to manage the mesh itself. In this session, we walk through the architecture end to end: Envoy sidecars on Amazon ECS for service-to-service communication, an edge proxy for external ingress, and the serverless control plane that ties it together.

For an ISV, shipping agents to many customers means solving multi-tenancy, per-customer isolation, identity delegation, and cost attribution before writing any agent logic. This session shows how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore handles that undifferentiated work. Twilio and Typeform join on stage to share how they built agent products on AgentCore and serve large numbers of end users without building custom infrastructure. Both stayed framework-neutral and spent their engineering effort on the agent experience rather than the plumbing beneath it. Expect specific isolation, identity, and cost-attribution patterns that move an ISV's agent product from prototype into production.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: How Itaú built cell-based resilience for critical workloads across clouds
speaker: Bruno Emer, Jorge Rua, Guilherme Greco
abstract: Mission-critical workloads require extreme resilience without the latency penalty of multi-region architectures, especially when strong consistency and real-time external integrations are required. In this session, discover how cell-based and shard-based architectures reduce blast radius and contain failures across cloud providers while keeping latency within strict thresholds. Explore traffic management patterns between cloud providers, data replication strategies including synchronous and asynchronous approaches, and consistency models. Learn how architectural adapters enable workload portability and provider independence. Gain practical patterns for cross-cell replication and automated failover, with examples from Itaú Unibanco's production environment.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: How IT leaders actually pulled off their cloud migrations
speaker: Rama Kolli, Ravi Kishore, Boatner Blankenstein
abstract: How did other organizations get their on-premises environments to AWS? In this panel, migration leaders from global organizations share exactly how they did it, including those moving off VMware and other aging infrastructure. You'll hear the real planning decisions, execution strategies, and lessons learned that made their transitions successful. They'll also share where they're headed next with modernization and innovation. Whether you're just getting started or pushing past roadblocks, you'll leave with proven strategies and practical insights to accelerate your own cloud migration.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

speaker: Deborah Matteliano Simeoni
abstract: Franchise operators run restaurants, not BI tools. In this session, learn how Jack in the Box delivered store-specific performance reports and actionable insights straight to every operator's inbox across 2,100+ locations. We'll cover throttle-aware parallel orchestration, failure isolation patterns, and how this approach turns business intelligence into a scalable, zero-friction communication channel that drives operator engagement and revenue. Walk away with a reusable blueprint for high-volume, per-location reporting in any multi-unit retail or restaurant business
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: How Kiro learns: an AI coding agent that improves with every session
speaker: David Killmon, Trevor Mack, Navyata Bawa
abstract: Learn how Kiro turns working sessions into durable knowledge and how to design, debug, and evaluate an agent’s memory lifecycle. See how Kiro extracts learnings from explicit instructions and task outcomes, such as successful build commands or rejected pull requests. Explore how it consolidates new knowledge with existing memories, resolves contradictions and expiring facts, and retrieves only relevant context for tasks. You’ll also learn how provenance keeps memories auditable and correctable, how memory stays consistent across IDE, CLI, and web, how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory scopes knowledge globally or by repository, and how retrieval quality is measured by task outcomes.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: How KOHO governs banking AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
speaker: Tyler Caldwell
abstract: KOHO, a Canadian fintech, governs its banking AI agents using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. This session covers the governance model KOHO built to keep AI agents compliant and auditable in a regulated banking environment, and what other Fintechs can learn from applying AgentCore to agent governance in regulated industries.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: How leading AI builders push the frontier with AWS Trainium
speaker: Young Mo Kang, Kamran Khan, Arjun Desai
abstract: Hear from four AI leaders building experiences that didn't exist a year ago: real-time video generation, world models, physical AI, and LLMs for drug discovery. These breakthroughs demand both high performance and low cost to work at all. AWS Trainium helped turn that future into production reality. Each panelist walks through their use case: the specific technical barrier they hit, how they used Trainium to get past it, and what shipping it to customers unlocked.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: How LG U+ cut migration time 50% with AI-powered app refactoring
speaker: Yoojong Lee, Bhavna Sarathy
abstract: Moving servers to the cloud without modernizing the applications on them just moves your technical debt to a new address. LG U+ needed to modernize applications before they could migrate them, and doing both sequentially would have taken too long. In this session, LG U+ shares how they ran AI-powered modernization and migration in parallel across 87 systems spanning 1,579 virtual servers and 107 physical servers. The result: roughly 20% migration velocity improvement and a 50% reduction in Java migration time through AI-assisted refactoring. You'll learn how to modernize at scale without slowing down the move.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: How LSEG Built a Multicloud Internal Developer Platform with Kubernetes and AI
speaker: Richard Chester, Dean Bryen
abstract: At London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), deploying enterprise workloads traditionally took weeks or months of onboarding, governance, networking, and operational setup. In this session, we’ll share how a small AI-augmented engineering team built RouteOne: LSEG’s fully managed multicloud application platform, enabling developers to deploy compliant workloads across multiple cloud providers in minutes by committing their code and a single YAML definition. We’ll explore the Kubernetes-based control plane, enterprise guardrails, and AI-native developer experience powered by APIs, MCP and agent skills. We’ll also share lessons learned from using AI-assisted engineering practices to rapidly deliver a lean, enterprise-grade platform in a regulated environment.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: How Marriott built AI-powered travel search with agents on AWS and model on GCP
speaker: Kenny Hammerlund, Bharat Lakhiyani
abstract: Marriott's guest-facing AI travel search, Ask Bonvoy, runs across two clouds by design: Gemini Flash on GCP handles conversational reasoning, while AWS powers the agentic backbone — EKS for orchestration, Aurora PostgreSQL with pgVector for RAG retrieval, and Bedrock Guardrails for real-time safety. This split lets Marriott pick the best model for the job without re-platforming, and scale across 9,000+ properties. In this lightning talk, learn how Marriott's engineering team wired a multi-cloud agentic architecture with model portability built in — and walk away with cloud-agnostic patterns for inference routing, agentic orchestration, and safety guardrails across clouds.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: How Max Mara built multicloud FinOps with open source
speaker: Alessandro Bellini, Yuriy Prykhodko
abstract: Max Mara runs hundreds of applications across AWS, GCP, Alicloud, and on-prem serving 20+ million monthly visits, but had no unified view of cost or correlation to business outcomes. In this session, hear how they implemented open-source Cloud Intelligence Dashboards with FOCUS (FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification) to consolidate all sources into a single framework. Learn how unit economics — "Cost per Order" across 11 brands — drove 21% monthly cost optimization with minimal engineering effort. Walk away with an open-source based playbook for multicloud FinOps that delivers measurable results at enterprise scale.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: How Moeve turned natural language into enforced governance controls
speaker: Rayco Martínez Hernández, Luis Rodriguez Montilla, Nicole Klatt
abstract: Translating compliance requirements such as GDPR or NIS2 into enforceable controls usually means writing policy by hand. Moeve built a Governance Control AI Assistant on Amazon Bedrock to change that. You see how engineers ask questions in natural language and the system turns their intent into SCPs, hooks, and AWS Config rules assigned at OU and account scope, validated through CI/CD and GitOps. Moeve shares the architecture and what it learned running the assistant in production.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: How Netflix auto-selects the right storage for every ML training workload
speaker: Shweta Keshavanarayana, Jake Luszcz
abstract: ML training workloads demand fast data access, but choosing the right storage for a given workload is complex. At Netflix, we solved this by building an intent-driven storage layer that takes workload characteristics and automatically selects, provisions, and mounts the optimal storage for that workload. Our users write code once; the backend adapts transparently. In this session, we share the architecture behind our selection framework, how we built a high-throughput S3 disk cache, and how you can apply the same pattern using generally available AWS storage services to reduce cost and eliminate storage guesswork.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: How neurosymbolic AI formalizes natural language into verifiable logic
speaker: Dimitra Giannakopoulou, Aman Goel
abstract: Organizations want to automate enforcement of critical rulesâ€”financial, legal, regulatoryâ€”yet those rules live in ambiguous natural-language documents. Bridging this gap is error-prone and expensive. In this session, we show how neurosymbolic AI enables subject-matter experts to formalize natural-language rules into mathematical logicâ€”capturing the original intent in an unambiguous, executable, and verifiable form. We cover the mathematical foundations and demonstrate through practical examples how formalized rules can serve as agent guardrails, compliance checks, and trusted knowledge sources. Attendees will leave with a deep understanding of how neurosymbolic techniques can help them formalize and operationalize their own domain rules.

Novartis decided not to optimize the old model but to replace it, building an AI-native ecosystem spanning information, decision, and physical AI across the drug development lifecycle. In this session, hear how AI now writes over 80% of their RWE protocols in production, then go deep on intelligent decision systems that optimize clinical trial planning, and formulation optimisations that improve the medicines Novartis creates. A Paytm-built foundation model learns from 100B+ activity sequences, while specialized SLMs and voice models enable sub-second interactions across 10+ languages. Beyond the customer lifecycle, Pi Agents powers sales, marketing, support, and operations. This session explores how Paytm combines these models with agents to understand, decide, and act.

abstract: Philips, a global health technology company, identified an opportunity to accelerate customer quoting for complex solutions combining equipment, software and services. Working with EPAM, Philips built the solution on AWS using an AI-native approach. A team of fewer than 20 used Amazon Kiro across the software development lifecycle, with Amazon Bedrock and the Strands Agents SDK powering an agentic architecture. The result is Sensei, an AI-powered sales experience. This session shares practical lessons for applying agentic AI, accelerating development and business operations, embedding governance, and moving from prototype to enterprise production at scale. title: How Prime Video Built an AI-assisted Creative Suite on AWS
speaker: Kartik Garg, Rachel Kelley

Prime Video AI Studios built the AI-Assisted Creative Suite on AWS to compress production to under 12 months, with plans to extend support to live-action shorts, second-unit VFX, and feature films. The suite is powered by AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK that select models, build creative workflows, construct prompts, and evaluate outputs. Learn how Prime Video trains and serves their first-party diffusion model fleet on Amazon SageMaker and EKS, running on Amazon EC2 P6 GPU clusters for production-grade throughput and latency.
