speaker: Ranil Piyaratna, Kate Totaro, Vikram Modgil
abstract: What if companies could meet growing hiring demands without increasing recruiting costs? PulsedIn faced a critical challenge: growing demand for nurses, limited recruiting capacity, and candidates who often worked outside traditional business hours. Using Amazon Connect Talent, PulsedIn is bringing AI-led interviews to healthcare recruiting, giving candidates the flexibility to interview on their own schedules while helping recruiters manage growing hiring demand. This approach aims to remove hiring bottlenecks, increase recruiting capacity, and support business growth without adding recruiters at the same rate. Hear directly from PulsedIn’s leadership about why they chose Amazon Connect Talent, how it's transforming their recruiting process, and what they've learned along the way.

abstract: Many organizations successfully pilot generative AI but struggle to scale adoption. Rail operators worldwide are now exploring how agentic AI can transform mission-critical operations and improve service reliability. Deutsche Bahn (DB) and Norfolk Southern are among the organizations leading this journey. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, they are transforming rail operations through AI agents embedded into the systems that support daily operations across their transportation networks. The solution combines AI agents and human oversight to automate incident resolution, support operations teams, and improve service reliability. This session explores the journey from proof of concept to production, the governance and safety guardrails required for adoption, and how lighthouse programs are becoming blueprints for enterprise-wide agentic process transformation. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: How Ramp tracks and governs AI spend down to the team, model, and API key
speaker: Alexander Chau, Jigna Gandhi, Richard Wang, Siddhi Surana
abstract: When AI token spend spans multiple providers and dozens of teams, knowing who spent what, on which model, and whether it's COGS or OpEx requires its own pipeline. We'll cover ingesting usage data from third-party AI APIs, processing with Temporal workers, persisting on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, running on Amazon ECS Fargate, and surfacing anomalies before they hit your invoice. See how Ramp attributes spend by provider, model, team, and API key, and attributes cost down to the request-level when teams connect their router, gateway, or internal data. Learn how Ramp separates COGS from OpEx for accurate unit economics, then closes the loop with governance.

Over seven years, RBC built a multicloud Kubernetes platform spanning AWS, Azure, and on-premises, purpose-built for financial services under multi-jurisdictional oversight. RBC shares how they eliminated vendor lock-in by migrating to open-source databases and messaging, established a "golden path" that lets teams deploy to any cloud without rearchitecting, and extended that foundation into agentic AI operations for automated root-cause analysis and remediation. Walk away with a practical playbook for building a compliant, portable multicloud platform that strengthens your security posture at every layer.

The solution ingests documents and surveys, applies consistent scoring, and translates results into prioritized actions spanning skills, resources, processes, and tools. Learn how Securian moved from periodic, manual assessments to an on-demand decision engine that helps technology leaders' direct investment where it matters most. title: How to Deploy Purpose-Built Clinical AI Agents to Production with Speed and Scale
speaker: Ankit Maheshwari, Deepti Chugh
abstract: Providers lose hours daily to documentation, manual coding, and admin work. Leading health IT builders are solving this with purpose-built AI on AWS. In this chalk talk, Innovaccer joins AWS to share how they trained task-specific clinical small language models that deliver consistent outputs where general-purpose LLMs produce unacceptable variance. We use their architecture as a jumping-off point to discuss the full spectrum of paths to production: custom model training on accelerated compute, multi-step agentic workflow orchestration, and embedding fully managed clinical AI capabilities into existing applications.

title: How to Govern an agent fleet: auto-approve the routine, escalate the ambiguous
speaker: Ganesh sedhai, Matej Macek
abstract: Your teams are building agents faster than anyone can review them by hand, and that creates operational and security risk along with the visibility problem. In this workshop, you build a layered controls stack for an agent fleet. You enforce content and business-logic boundaries with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, apply an evaluator pattern for policy validation, and track compliance posture with AWS Config conformance packs. Then you connect these into an operating model that approves routine actions automatically and sends only the ambiguous ones to a person, so you can deploy more agents than your team could review individually.

title: How to improve your security and governance maturity and prove it to your auditor
speaker: Dario Goldfarb
abstract: With so many security best practices available, knowing what to do first is a challenge. In this session, you learn how to use the AWS Security Maturity Model to systematically identify and prioritize security improvements for your AWS workloads through a phased approach. You discover how to extend your governance capabilities to manage security consistently across multi-cloud environments. Finally, you see how automatic evidence collection helps you continuously demonstrate compliance to auditors, turning security posture into provable assurance.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: How to leverage an internal buy-back process to accelerate new service adoption?
abstract: Internal buy-back processes can slow new service adoption, but designed well they can be the fastest path to it. In this Meetup, we'll show how to align finance, procurement, and engineering on a buy-back model that funds early experiments without waiting for annual budget cycles. You'll learn how to define clear entry criteria, use pilot funding to prove value, and convert successful workloads into committed spend. Attendees will hear real examples from AWS and customers who used this approach to shorten approval cycles and accelerate adoption.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: How to run parallel coding agents without sitting in the loop (sponsored by SpaceXSI)
abstract: Running multiple coding agents in parallel can increase throughput, but only if technical leads and engineers avoid being pulled into every agent’s execution loop. Join this session to learn how Grok Bot is an orchestration layer for technical knowledge work, coordinating workflows while saving time and mitigating costs. Through live demos, see Grok Bot operate from its own VM and browser, maintain authenticated tool access, monitor usage, and provision cloud agents on demand. We’ll be joined by a customer in production as well as SpaceXAI engineers as they share the workflows they run today. This presentation is brought to you by SpaceXSI, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: How to solve for multicloud identity lifecycle management
speaker: Joshua Stultz, Phillip Spies, Rodney Underkoffler
abstract: Organizations operating in multiple clouds face a compounding multi-cloud identity lifecycle governance challenge. How do you provision, manage, audit, and decommission identities when each cloud provider enforces different authorization models, attribute schemas, and lifecycle hooks? In this session, the National Institutes of Health (NIH), a federal research organization, describes how it uses a centralized identity governance platform to provision identities and entitlements across AWS and Microsoft Azure. You will learn how to avoid governance divergence and design identity lifecycles where access reviews, birthright provisioning, and decommissioning work consistently, regardless of which cloud the identity lands in.

title: How to think about NUMA: Optimizing AI inference on EC2
speaker: Tyler Jones, Kinnar Sen
abstract: Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) topology shapes how every byte of model weight reaches a compute core, and misalignment silently costs throughput. This session explains why NUMA matters for memory locality when running models on EC2, and what changes across Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. CPU inference requires deliberate alignment of threads to data, especially as SIMD and AMX instructions amplify memory bandwidth demands per core. Even on GPU instances, host-side NUMA affects preprocessing and KV cache offload. Understand your hardware topology and leverage it to get the most from your inference workloads.

title: How to Use AI Agents to Run Genomics Pipelines Faster and Cheaper
speaker: Mark Schreiber
abstract: Sequencing costs less than ever, but turning that data into answers is still slow and expensive. Bioinformatics teams spend weeks building and debugging pipelines, managing infrastructure, and paying for idle compute while scientists wait on results. This lightning talk shows how AI agents can write, validate, launch, monitor, and troubleshoot genomics workflows from plain-language requests, so researchers can get to analysis without becoming infrastructure experts. Workflows run on AWS HealthOmics, a managed service for running bioinformatics workflows at scale without managing servers. We’ll share performance and cost results from popular open-source pipelines, and you’ll leave with practical patterns you can apply to your own work.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: How to use AI to develop and deploy controls from your internal policies
speaker: Pujah Goviel
abstract: You maintain internal security policies but turning them into implemented, risk-prioritized controls could be manual and slow. This lightning talk demonstrates how to use Kiro to develop and deploy controls at scale across three layers. Preventive controls that block non-compliant actions, detective controls that identify violations and trigger remediation, and proactive controls that validate configurations before deployment. You leave with a practical approach to using AI to accelerate the entire control lifecycle from policy to enforcement.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: How Trainium powers the next AI frontier, from silicon to application
speaker: Alberto Taiuti, Gregory Chanan, Colin Brace
abstract: Every AI breakthrough demands innovation across the full stack: chips, servers, software, and the models built on top, each layer making the next one faster and cheaper to run. In this session, discover how AWS and frontier AI builders drive full-stack innovation on AWS Trainium to scale post-training and reinforcement learning, serve at high throughput, and bend the cost-per-token curve. Examine real architectural decisions from silicon to application, then look ahead to what's next in Trainium and AWS infrastructure. You will see how each layer of innovation compounds and learn where to place your bets on AI infrastructure.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: How Vanguard Scales AI Oversight Without Scaling Human Review (sponsored by Capgemini)
speaker: Piyush Saxena, Ayush Sharma, Jithin Pradeep
abstract: Human review can't scale linearly with generative-AI volume. Vanguard's AI Center of Excellence built a closed-loop oversight system where every AI response is scored by an LLM-as-judge, confirmed or overturned by a subject-matter expert, and routed through a confusion matrix: confirmed catches sharpen the agent, disagreements calibrate the judge. Each SME label grows a benchmark that resets how much oversight the next cycle needs, proving mathematically that coverage can fall while risk holds flat. Built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda-hosted detector SLMs, SQS, DynamoDB, and SageMaker, the loop moves toward real-time interruption of harmful responses before customers see them. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: How Vanguard uses SageMaker HyperPod from training to inference for custom LLMs
speaker: Kareem Syed-Mohammed, Swapnil Palod, Vinay Arora, Ritesh Shah, Jithin Pradeep
abstract: Enterprises that own their AI lifecycle across training and inference can adapt their models as fast as their users' need change. Vanguard outgrew off the shelf models and built infrastructure that runs custom large language models (LLMs) and specialized small language models (SLMs) side by side. Go inside the implementation to see how Amazon SageMaker HyperPod powers resilient multi node training and high throughput inference. Hear lessons from engineering alongside AWS product teams.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: How WBD Became the First Media Company to Go Agentic Across AdTech
speaker: Dr. Nage Sethu, Ashish Kapur, Ken Sam Kanagaraj
abstract: Buying and selling media has historically been manual, constrained by legacy systems and fragmented tools. Warner Bros. Discovery is changing that. As the first media company to integrate agentic AI workflows into every system across the media lifecycle, WBD is leapfrogging the competition by embedding autonomous agents at every step: planning, forecasting, optimization, and measurement. This converged platform makes linear TV as addressable and measurable as digital. Learn how WBD and AWS are replacing decades of manual process with self-improving agents that drive precision, yield, and entirely new monetization models at scale.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: How Wisconsin DOR cut suspended tax returns with AWS Quick
speaker: Sohaib Tahir, Bradley R Thome
abstract: Every suspended tax return pull staff into manual review and delays refunds. The Wisconsin Department of Revenue, a 2026 FTA Award winner, tackled this by building a serverless analytics solution with Amazon S3, Amazon Athena, and AWS Quick across more than 3 million returns a year. Using generative AI, the team translated processing rules into plain language and generated queries, cutting suspended returns by 80% on targeted rules and saving thousands of staff hours. Walk away with a repeatable architecture, best practices, natural-language analytics patterns, and an approach for protecting sensitive and regulated tax data.

title: How Woodside handed SOC monitoring to AWS SIR to focus on threat hunting
speaker: Philip Winstanley
abstract: Routine monitoring and alert triage leave security teams stretched thin. In this session, hear how a global energy company worked with AWS Security Incident Response to change what its SOC spends time on. The company handed eyes-on-glass monitoring and incident response operations to AWS, which freed its security staff for proactive threat hunting. You see how integration with existing ITSM workflows made adoption straightforward, and how the combined team sped up detection, containment, and resolution during a real supply chain attack.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: How Workday built multicloud data interoperability foundation for Agentic AI
speaker: Mehreen Ali, Avijit Goswami
abstract: As enterprises scale agentic AI, the hardest problem is often giving agents secure, governed access to data spread across multiple clouds. Physically copying the data between clouds introduces cost, latency, and governance risk. In this session, you will learn how Workday leverages Apache Iceberg catalog federation to build bidirectional, zero-copy integration that enables cross-cloud data access without duplicating or moving data. You will see how this open standard based approach lets AI agents reason over trusted enterprise data in place, with governance and business context preserved.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: How YipitData Builds AI-Native Analytics with AWS, Databricks, and OpenAI (sponsored by Databricks)
speaker: Sully Clark, Ankith Ede, Anup Segu
abstract: YipitData gives customers a self-service way to answer analytical questions using agents grounded in its data, completing custom requests in 30 minutes compared with the two weeks previously needed. This session walks through the production architecture behind that experience, combining Databricks for data governance and observability, OpenAI for reasoning and intelligence, and AWS for application resiliency and hosting. Learn how a custom agent harness connects OpenAI frontier models to Databricks SQL Warehouses, with Amazon ECS and ElastiCache supporting the application and asynchronous agent execution. We cover Unity Catalog access boundaries, dedicated agent identities, durable session state in Lakebase, and evaluations that check SQL, tool use, and answer consistency. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Hugging Face on AWS: AI Model Deployment at Scale
speaker: Saurav Mohanty, Prajwal Nag Ramesh
abstract: AWS and Hugging Face collaborate on open source Deep Learning Containers, optimized inference frameworks, and Neuron integrations that make deploying community models production-ready. This session covers the open source stack - from Transformers library optimizations for Graviton and Trainium to TGI container contributions - that enables customers to serve Hugging Face models at 50% lower cost. Learn deployment patterns used by enterprises running open weight LLMs at millions of requests per day.

title: Human+AI Collaboration: How Amazon Deploys Autonomous Operations on AWS
speaker: Joseph Rosing, Elad Dwek, Chris Keane, Romi Patel
abstract: Amazon deploys humanoids, autonomous mobile robots, and humans as a unified workforce operating side-by-side on the fulfillment floor. Learn how Amazon evolved an AI-powered verification pipeline, built with Amazon Nova on Bedrock to validate 200K+ items, into a fleet orchestration platform dispatching foundation-model inference across humanoids, quadrupeds, AMRs, and drones. We deep-dive into the architectural patterns enabling humans to work alongside robots at scale: a serverless Lambda backend that abstracts the robot form factor, multi-vendor humanoid integration, and edge deployment strategies. You'll leave with a framework for physical AI orchestration of heterogeneous fleets while optimizing throughput and cost.

title: Hybrid Kubernetes made simple: EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway for on-prem and edge AI
speaker: Gaurav Priyolkar, Bruno Lopes, Karan Thanvi, Karine Ferrari, Jarod Oliver
abstract: Enterprises are migrating from legacy hypervisors to Kubernetes-native stacks but need hybrid connectivity without complex network changes. In this builder session, attendees set up the newly launched Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes gateway to seamlessly connect on-premises worker nodes to a cloud EKS control plane without modifying existing network infrastructure. They deploy an AI inference workload spanning cloud and edge, configure pod-to-pod communication across environments, implement data residency controls, and validate failover scenarios.

title: Identity for humans, workloads, and AI agents
abstract: Machine identities now outnumber people, and AI agents act on their own across your systems. This meetup works through least-privilege for non-human identities, short-lived credentials, workforce access at scale, and modernizing federation. Bring how you are adapting IAM for agents and the people who manage them, and compare approaches with peers facing the same shift.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: I didn't know AWS WAF did this
speaker: Kartik Bheemisetty, David MacDonald
abstract: Think AWS WAF is just for blocking SQL injection and XSS? Think again. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll dive into creative, real-world use cases, from deploying honeypots and shedding traffic, to stopping account fraud and mitigating DDoS at scale. We'll explore advanced configurations, walk through customer-tested patterns, and whiteboard strategies that make WAF a powerful tool in your security arsenal. Bring your questions and experiences, we're here to discover the "AWS WAF does that?" moments together.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan I

title: I didn't know my AI agent was doing that!
speaker: PJ Ng, Shane Carragher, Shanna Chang, YoungMin Joung, Yash Doshi
abstract: AI agents are non-deterministic - they can burn tokens, stall, or drift into wrong behaviour with no warning, and teams often have no visibility until something breaks. In this hands-on builders session, you will use Amazon CloudWatch to observe live agents from both the console and your IDE: trace what an agent actually did, spot failures, and surface anomalous behaviour. Working with real agents - a production agent and a custom chatbot - you build the detection and alerting yourself and leave able to apply it to the agents you run in production.

title: Implement AI agent safety controls with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
speaker: Milan Bavadiya, Prasanth Ponnoth
abstract: Scaling AI agents into production without safety controls creates compliance, cost, and operational risk for financial services organizations. In this workshop, build an agent safety control system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Starting with a deployed agent, configure three signal pipelines: observability via Amazon AgentCore Observability and Amazon CloudWatch; cost monitoring with AWS Budgets; and Amazon AgentCore Runtime Evaluation for behavioral deviation detection. Then build an admin control panel that aggregates alerts and enables human-in-the-loop interventions including session termination and fine-grained authorization via Cedar policies. Leave with a proven approach you can replicate to deliver responsible, governed AI agents at scale.

speaker: Fernando Galves, Kyle Palasti
abstract: Learn how to extend Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to hybrid and edge services to build distributed agentic apps using Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-to-agent (A2A) communication with on-premises data. Get hands-on with hybrid agentic AI using Amazon Bedrock and Strands Agents while exploring AWS hybrid and edge solutions for data residency compliance.

title: Implementing an eval strategy while building AgentCore agents without a QA team
speaker: Dhiraj Mahapatro
abstract: Startups shipping AI can move fast for the same reason a car can. You trust the brakes. For agents, evals are those brakes. In this session, you build an agent locally with AgentCore and evaluate it as you go with Amazon CloudWatch Omni, without a QA team. Every change you make in your IDE is scored on sessions, responses, and tool calls, so you see right away whether your agent got better. When the scores hold, deploy the same agent to AWS and keep the same evals running on production traffic. Leave with an eval workflow a lean team runs solo, so you can keep your foot on the gas.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Implement semantic caching for AI agents using ElastiCache for Valkey
speaker: Yaron Sananes, Madelyn Olson, Kevin McGehee, Elad Bernstein, Eran Balan
abstract: Semantic caching uses vector similarity search to retrieve cached LLM responses for semantically equivalent queries, reducing inference latency and cost in agentic AI architectures. In this session, dive deep into implementing semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, covering embedding generation, similarity scoring, and relevance threshold tuning. Explore advanced production patterns including per-user cache namespacing for personalized responses, tenant isolation strategies to prevent cross-tenant data leakage, and techniques for validating that cached responses remain contextually appropriate for incoming queries at scale. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Improving operations with agentic AI
speaker: Elliot Markowitz, Greg Eppel, Igor Sedukhin
abstract: Your operational telemetry is growing faster than your team. Learn how agentic AI can work across your observability stack, correlating metrics, logs, and traces to detect issues, identify root cause, and initiate remediation without waiting for a human to connect the dots. Explore patterns for agents that triage alerts, reduce noise, surface actionable insights, and execute operational runbooks. See how to integrate agents into your monitoring and incident response workflows, from signal detection through resolution. Leave with practical approaches to reduce mean time to recovery, eliminate repetitive toil, and give your team time to focus on reliability improvements that matter.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Improving your database agility with Amazon FSx
speaker: James Kuhlke, Andrew Peng
abstract: Customers self-manage databases on AWS to maintain full control over architecture, functionality, availability, and performance. Amazon FSx provides the high-performance, highly available storage they need to do this at scale. This workshop will whiteboard production architectures for self-managed databases on Linux and Windows using Amazon FSx for OpenZFS, NetApp ONTAP, and Windows File Server. Learn how to architect for high performance and high availability, implement zero-copy snapshots and clones for rapid database refresh, and accelerate backup and recovery. Whether you run Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, or PostgreSQL, bring your architecture questions.

title: Incident response tabletop: supply chain

title: In-Country HPC: How TGS Processes Seismic Data on AWS Brazil
speaker: Kun Jiao, Faisal Asif
abstract: TGS -- one of the world's largest multi-client geoscience data providers -- faced a significant cost challenge running its business-critical Rackmon EFWI GPU workload at scale. By strategically deploying this workload on AWS infrastructure in Brazil, TGS leveraged Brazil's ReData Special Tax Regime to dramatically reduce the tax burden on GPU-intensive seismic processing. The result: material cost savings on one of the most computationally demanding workloads in the energy industry -- and a reusable in-country processing architecture that can serve future customers with data residency requirements in other geographies.

title: Innovate faster, stay compliant: Innovation Sandbox for financial services
speaker: Gonzalo Escarra, Peter DeVries
abstract: Financial services organizations need to experiment fast while meeting regulatory and governance requirements. In this chalk talk, explore how organizations deploy Innovation Sandbox on AWS to give teams safe, ephemeral environments without compromising security posture. We’ll discuss real-world patterns for network isolation, automated guardrails via SCPs, and time-bound account lifecycles that satisfy risk committees and regulators. We’ll walk through how organizations balance developer autonomy with controls mapped to frameworks like SR 26-2 and OCC heightened standards, and you’ll leave with practical approaches for rolling out Innovation Sandbox on AWS while keeping compliance teams confident.

title: Innovating with agentic AI inside Amazon, powered by AgentCore
speaker: Yash Parikh, Mihir Patel, Amanda Lester
abstract: Amazon runs thousands of AI agents internally, built on the same AgentCore platform available to every AWS customer. Teams across the company have replaced manual workflows with agents that act autonomously, cutting process times from weeks to hours and eliminating thousands of lines of custom orchestration code. This session brings together the Amazon builders behind these transformations to share the AgentCore capabilities that made it possible, the failure modes they hit at scale, and the design patterns that separate agents that demo well from agents that survive production. Every pattern discussed is one you can adopt today.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Innovation in identity security: how we protect the cloud & help you do it too
speaker: Kristen Haught, Ilya Epshteyn, Alan Garver
abstract: Learn how AWS approaches identity as the foundation of cloud security - both protecting AWS infrastructure and enabling customers to operate securely at scale. Explore how AWS innovates in access management and develops prescriptive, service-specific guidance helping organizations adopt services confidently, drives secure-by-default authorization across 300+ services, and ensures IAM policies work predictably. Millennium Partners will share how they use AWS guidance and threat modeling to evaluate new services, strengthen their security posture, and give developers freedom to innovate faster.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Inside Amazon EKS: the resilient foundation for critical workloads
speaker: Sri Saran Balaji Vellore Rajakumar, Shane Corbett, George John
abstract: Real-time financial systems, large-scale AI, and mission-critical platforms run on Kubernetes, and they demand a robust engineering foundation. This session goes under the hood of what makes Amazon EKS the backbone for the most demanding workloads. See how cellular isolation contains blast radius and EKS Provisioned Control Planes eliminate downtime during peak operational periods, backed by an industry-leading SLA as clusters scale into large fleets. Learn how EKS Auto Mode integrates with Application Recovery Controller zonal shift to protect the control plane and running pods during an impaired Availability Zone, keeping critical applications available with no extra configuration.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Inside Amazon S3: How a one-page design reached planetary scale
speaker: James Bornholt, George Porter
abstract: When Amazon S3 launched in 2006, its design requirements fit one page: scalable, reliable, fast, inexpensive, simple, with no single points of failure. The system was built to treat component failure as normal and use scale as an advantage. Today those founding principles describe an architecture serving hundreds of millions of requests per second across tens of millions of drives, maintaining eleven nines of durability while shipping features without downtime. Hear S3 principal engineers trace the decisions from single host to strong consistency at global scale, how formal methods verify correctness, and how the team balances innovation with operational safety.

title: Inside Amazon S3 Vectors: architecture and cost optimization for vector search
speaker: Dmtiri Pavlichin, Bryan Wilkinson
abstract: Vector embeddings power everything from semantic search to RAG, but running them at scale often means high infrastructure costs and operational overhead. In this session, go inside the architecture of Amazon S3 Vectors to see how it delivers vector search at up to 90% lower cost than specialized alternatives, with support for up to 2 billion vectors per index. We'll whiteboard the indexing approach that makes this possible, then explore recent enhancements, including a 100x increase in the per-query search result limit and reduced query pricing, and what they mean for your application's performance and cost.

title: Inside Amazon S3 Vectors: architecture and cost optimization for vector search
speaker: Bryan Wilkinson, Dmtiri Pavlichin

title: Inside DuckDB and how AWS Analytics puts it to work
speaker: Eric Jones
abstract: DuckDB has become one of the most talked-about innovations in analytics, and now the team behind it, DuckLabs, is part of AWS. In this session, dive deep into the architecture of DuckDB, the in-process analytical database that brings fast OLAP performance to laptops, serverless functions, and data pipelines. Learn how its vectorized execution engine, columnar storage, and zero-dependency design make it well suited for embedded analytics, local development, and edge processing. Explore real-world use cases, performance characteristics, and how DuckDB complements AWS analytics services, including Amazon S3, AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, and Amazon Redshift. Whether you're a data engineer, data scientist, or architect, gain the technical depth to put DuckDB to work.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Inside NKI: Evolution of the Trainium kernel language
speaker: Liran Alon
abstract: NKI is a Python DSL for programming Trainium directly, beyond PyTorch/JAX. This talk goes deep on how NKI evolved, what worked, what didn’t, and what we learned. We cover how the graph-compiler lowers PyTorch/JAX to Trainium and its limits, and how NKI bypasses them for peak performance, from tile programming to direct control over instructions, scheduling, and allocation. We discuss design tradeoffs, and how the compiler evolved from parsing to tracing and diverged from the graph-compiler for predictable lowering, while providing abstractions, tools, and meta-programming for productivity, debugging, profiling, and agentic development. We also demonstrate new capabilities and advanced optimizations.

title: Inside OpenAI’s Cyber Defense Factory (sponsored by OpenAI)
speaker: Matt Boyle, Shikhar Kwatra
abstract: Drawing on lessons from OpenAI's internal Defense Factory, see how you can put agents to work discovering vulnerabilities and driving fixes autonomously. Learn how to implement continuous defense with OpenAI tooling, Daybreak cyber models, and AWS infrastructure including Amazon Bedrock, drawing on lessons from OpenAI's internal Defense Factory. Explore routing findings to the right owners, reducing duplicate findings, and using development environments to validate vulnerabilities and test fixes. As broadly available cyber models help threat actors find decade-old vulnerabilities, this session focuses on how defenders can put continuous defense into practice.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Inside Real AI Software Factories: Lessons From the Teams Building Them (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
speaker: Jonathan Nolen, Shardul Vaidya, Jaz White, Dylan Garcia
abstract: Everyone's talking about AI software factories. Far fewer have actually built one. In this panel, engineering leaders who are automating their full SDLC go past the hype to the real work: where agents accelerate delivery, where they break, and what it takes to keep humans in control as autonomy scales. Expect specifics, not theory—what worked, what didn't, and what they'd do differently. Whether you're experimenting with coding agents or scaling toward autonomous delivery, you'll leave with practical patterns for building a factory that's genuinely fast and safe. Join leaders from LaunchDarkly, Ramp, AWS and more for an honest conversation about engineering at agent speed.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Inside the engine that powers Bedrock inference at scale
speaker: Anthony Liguori
abstract: Serving large language models at scale means running two phases: processing the prompt (prefill) and generating tokens (decode). Prefill is compute-bound, while decode is limited by memory bandwidth, so running both on the same hardware can leave capacity idle. This session goes inside the engine that powers Amazon Bedrock inference. We examine how disaggregated inference runs each phase on its own pool of accelerators, and the challenges that follow: moving the KV cache between pools, keeping both pools busy as traffic shifts, and choosing parallelism strategies for unpredictable long-context workloads. Leave with a deeper understanding of the tradeoffs involved in optimizing inference latency, throughput, and cost at scale.

title: Inside the frontier: What builders are creating at OpenAI (sponsored by OpenAI)
speaker: Dominik Kundel, Evan Weiss
abstract: How are builders at OpenAI turning big bets into systems and new products used across the company? Through demos and firsthand stories, go behind the scenes of ambitious projects with the people who built them. Discover the problems they’re tackling, the frontier capabilities that made their ideas possible, and what they’ve learned putting them into practice. Leave with practical lessons for bringing your own ideas to life with OpenAI.

title: Inside the Governed Agentic Software Factory at Enterprise Scale (sponsored by CloudBees)
abstract: Code is now abundant. AI agents now write, test and deploy code autonomously; the bottleneck has shifted from generating code to governing what reaches production. Loreli Cadapan, VP of Product at CloudBees, takes you inside the governed agentic software factories that the world’s most regulated engineering organizations are building, where every change, human or agent, is visible, auditable and accountable. The work starts after the code changes: encode existing rules as enforceable policy across your toolchain, keep humans in the loop where it matters, and ship software you can stand behind. Because you write code for a reason, and we make sure that reason becomes true. This presentation is brought to you by CloudBees, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Inside the up to $50B SI and HPC investment in AWS Government Regions
abstract: Government agencies and the industrial base need compliant, mission-ready infrastructure for Super Intelligence (SI) and HPC. Learn how AWS is investing up to $50 billion to deliver nearly 1.3 gigawatts of purpose-built capacity and new capabilities across the AWS GovCloud (US), Secret, and Top Secret clouds. See how Amazon Bedrock supports agentic SI, with model choice from Amazon, Anthropic, OpenAI, and NVIDIA and built-in responsible SI safeguards. Then get the latest Government Regions updates that help accelerate mission delivery. Ideal for mission owners, architects, and technical leaders.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Inside T-Mobile's Kinetic Edge: Real-Time Physical AI at Scale
speaker: Matthew Feider, Waqar Afzal
abstract: In a Physical AI world, tokens traveling across a telecom network must trigger real-world actions with sub-millisecond latency. Learn how T-Mobile built its Kinetic Edge Platform using AWS Outposts, Amazon SageMaker, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, delivering deterministic performance, ultra-low latency, and precise synchronization on a network serving 130M+ customers. We'll cover how to assess Physical AI network requirements and map them to AWS infrastructure options. You'll leave knowing how to build AI into the network edge and where it creates the most value.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Inside UK AISI: stress-testing frontier AI safety on Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Kyle McMaster
abstract: The UK AI Security Institute leads global research into harmful AI capabilities, assessing frontier models for risks like offensive cybersecurity, bioweapon design, and psychological manipulation. In this talk, UK AISI representatives walk through how they built their evaluation infrastructure on Amazon Bedrock, from model access and prompt orchestration to result analysis. Hear highlights from recent research projects and the engineering decisions that make safety evaluation repeatable at scale. Together, these examples show how rigorous AI safety research runs in production on AWS.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Inside Zeta Global's open lakehouse architecture on AWS
speaker: SOUMIL SHAH, Shivam Patel
abstract: Are you building a data lakehouse and wondering how others have approached the same challenges? Go behind the scenes of a real AWS customer data architecture. Zeta Global's AI Marketing Platform serves thousands of clients using 245 million consumer profiles, but multi-hour data lag times and rising per-tenant costs were limiting growth. Learn how Zeta built an open streaming lakehouse with Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon EMR, and Amazon MSK that processes 10 TB daily across 10,000+ Apache Iceberg tables, cutting time-to-insight from hours to minutes while maximizing multi-tenant infrastructure efficiency at scale.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Instant Fan Gratification: AI-Powered Media Ops for Austin City Limits Music Festival
speaker: Anubhav Mehrotra, Mateo Thompson, Robert Raver
abstract: Austin City Limits Music Festival is innovating the fan experience for live music. When an artist creates a viral moment, festival teams have an opportunity to share it with fans while the excitement is still building. In this session, learn how Austin City Limits Music Festival built a platform that brings media assets together so teams can search, create, and publish in near-real time. Built using the guidance for a Media Lake on AWS, along with Amazon Bedrock, the platform uses AI-driven moment detection to surface key content automatically. We cover architecture, lessons from festival-scale deployment, and impact on fan experience.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: Instant Play Demos on Twitch – Increasing Player Engagement
speaker: Todd Sharp, Henry Goffin, Frank Zhu
abstract: From game builds to live campaigns, take a deep dive into the best practices and constraints around launching Instant Play Demos on Twitch, powered by Amazon GameLift Streams. This innovative approach to game marketing enables developers to reach potential players and let them try your game before they buy it. No downloads or installs required, just a WebRTC enabled browser and an internet connection. Learn what kind of content makes for a great demo, engine-specific best practices, and the benefits of launching a campaign and how they perform compared to traditional marketing channels.

title: Instrument a service with OpenTelemetry
speaker: Phani Kumar Lingamallu
abstract: In this live demo, we take an uninstrumented service from zero observability to correlated metrics, logs, and traces in minutes using Open Telemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Walk through the shortest path to production-grade instrumentation: SDK configuration, collector setup, signal routing, and surfacing the first actionable insight.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Integrate Agents with MCP Servers and Tools using AgentCore Gateway
speaker: Marco Tamassia
abstract: Your agent may handle basic conversations well, but to take real-world actions it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this hands-on lab, use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to expose Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tools with JWT authorization. Register tool targets, connect to a pre-deployed nutrition coach agent, and validate how it dynamically discovers and invokes new capabilities at runtime without redeployment.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Palace Ballroom II

title: Integrating AI agents with event-driven architectures
speaker: Tolga Orhon, Marco Jahn
abstract: Most multi-agent systems start with direct API calls between agents—then debugging becomes impossible, one slow agent blocks the chain, and replaying a failed workflow means re-running everything. In this chalk talk, discuss why event-driven patterns solve these coordination problems and how to design multi-agent systems using EventBridge for routing, human-in-the-loop controls that pause and resume agent actions via events, and compute selection—such as Lambda, Fargate, or AgentCore—based on your agent's execution profile. Bring architecture questions; we'll whiteboard patterns for decoupling agents across domains without sacrificing observability.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Intelligent Co-Sell in Action
speaker: Raj Kandaswamy, Tom Thayer
abstract: A new generation of agentic capabilities now works alongside AWS Partners at every stage of the deal—anticipating the next move, cutting the busywork, and surfacing opportunity right where sellers already work. This high-energy demo session follows a deal from first opportunity to proven outcome.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Intelligent document processing with generative AI on AWS
speaker: Roop Bains, Niklas Breuer
abstract: Description: In this workshop, you build an intelligent document processing pipeline on AWS that turns unstructured documents into structured, verifiable data. First, extract text, tables, and layout in the format and granularity your downstream application expects. Then configure a pipeline that splits a multi-document package, matches each document to the right schema, and extracts the fields you need. Each value comes with a confidence score and its source location, so you can decide what to automate and what to send for human review. You leave with a working pipeline you can adapt to your own documents. Bring your laptop.

title: Intent-Based Access Control for AI Agents that Actually Do Things (sponsored by WorkOS)
speaker: Abhishek Hingnikar
abstract: Agent permissions offer two bad options: approve every action manually, or skip permissions and trust the prompt. Auto-approve protects your laptop; it won't stop an agent from deleting a thousand CRM records. Roles and scopes suit static users, not agents whose next action depends on the last prompt. This session introduces Intent-Based Access Control (IBAC), where the agent's intent, not a pre-assigned role, is the unit of permission. WorkOS built Airlock on it: mission-bound tokens, every call evaluated against intent, decisions resolving to allow, deny, or escalate. Live demo across Gmail and Linear, including a blocked exfiltration and real-time human approval. This presentation is brought to you by WorkOS, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Introducing AWS Context: Build governed intelligence for agents at scale
speaker: Steve Ash, Aditya Krishnan
abstract: AI agents need to understand what your data means, how it connects, and which definitions and rules apply to each use case. AWS Context automatically builds a governed knowledge graph by unifying structured and unstructured data, managed knowledge bases, and technical and business metadata from AWS and third-party sources. This shared foundation grounds agents in your organization’s data, business rules, relationships, and domain knowledge. In this session, dive into the reference architecture and learn best practices for integrating agents with AWS Context, including considerations for identity management, workload sizing, and production deployments.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Inverting the medallion: Serving reads without hitting Gold
speaker: Laks Sundararajan, Chaitanya Vejendla
abstract: Most teams default to Gold as the serving layer. For regulated systems-of-record like health data stores, ledgers, compliance archives, that's rarely the right choice. They're built for durability and interoperability, not production read traffic. The inverted pattern writes promote up the medallion, reads come from purpose-built Silver projections and Gold holds contractual semantics and never serves directly. In this chalk talk, work through change-data-capture synthesis without source support, write/read path splitting, and a routing gateway developers can't bypass. Bring your most painful regulated read path. Leave knowing when to invert, how to scope projections, and what your gateway must enforce.

title: Investigating Threats to AI: Incident Response to Compromised AI Workloads
speaker: Kyle Shields, Steve de Vera
abstract: As organizations adopt generative AI on AWS, security teams need to extend their investigation capabilities into the AI layer. In this hands-on workshop, participants work through a realistic multi-phase incident — tracing a compromised credential from initial exposure through privilege escalation into Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases and AI agents. Using GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, and Athena, you'll reconstruct the full attack chain and walk away with the skills to detect, investigate, and respond when threat actors pivot from traditional cloud resources into generative AI workloads.

title: Is Your Code Ready for AI Agents? Modernizing Legacy Apps for AI
abstract: Everyone wants AI agents in production. But most enterprise apps were built long before agents existed. Their APIs are hard to discover, auth wasn't designed for machine callers, and few systems recover safely when an agent retries a call. Join peers working through this right now for an open conversation. We'll swap real experiences on finding readiness gaps in your code with tools like AWS Transform, deciding what to modernize first, and choosing where agents make sense versus simple automation. Bring your challenges, wins, and lessons learned. No slides, just honest discussion with people solving the same problem.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: It's live. Now what? Operating AI on Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Alan Yao, Rashim Gupta, Jayadev Vadakkanmarveettil
abstract: Your AI workload is live. You own three questions: what broke, whose spend is it, and are you still running the right model. Answer the first two with Amazon Bedrock metrics: why latency alone cannot tell you what broke, how output tokens per second separates a slower model from a longer answer, why throttling starts before you reach your quota, and how to attribute spend by caller identity and request metadata. Answer the third with evals: see how Airbnb sets a model and reasoning effort per workload across 3,000 engineers.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Japan Wrap-up Session
speaker: Issei Kawasaki, Taro Hirose, 泰宏 Kose, Kempei Igarashi
abstract: This session will be delivered in Japanese and provides a comprehensive recap of the major announcements and strategic updates from the keynote sessions throughout the event. Experienced speakers will summarize the most impactful innovations and key messages from AWS leadership. Designed for a broad audience, from developers and engineers to business decision-makers, this session will help you identify and prioritize the announcements most relevant to your organization. It will also help you prepare to share what you learned at re:Invent with your teams when you return to the office

title: Java to Graviton: three migration tools, one decision tree
speaker: Jake Wolf, Hahnara Hyun
abstract: Three tools belong in your toolbelt for moving Java from x86 to AWS Graviton. AWS Transform custom runs across hundreds of repos and integrates with CI/CD. The open-source Java skill runs locally in your coding agent, no AWS credentials needed, with final validation on Graviton hardware. The APerf MCP server measures x86 vs. Graviton performance before and after you migrate so you can rightsize. Each fits a different team size, repo count, and timeline. Watch all three run live on one codebase, see where each succeeds and hands off, and leave with a decision framework for when to use each.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Journey to post-quantum (PQ) authentication in AWS
speaker: Avni Rambhia, Oren Nachman
abstract: You use certificates for identity, keys for token signing, and long-lived roots of trust. Now you need to migrate to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) for authentication. In this session, learn how AWS helps you start and stay PQ-ready while preserving backwards compatibility, performance, and AI-friendly security by default. We will demystify the present state and future trajectory of PQ authentication. We discuss the updated CNSA 2.0 dates when RSA and EC will no longer satisfy authentication requirements and the uncertainty around PQ public certificate formats and Merkle Trees in non-browser scenarios.

title: Keeping Your Lakehouse Fast: Optimization Methods for Performance & Cost (sponsored by Cloudera)
speaker: Dipankar Mazumdar
abstract: A common challenge with large-scale Apache Iceberg tables is keeping performance and costs under control as use and volumes grow. Optimizing tables is the solution, but it’s a tough problem to solve. As data volumes grow, querying effectively requires deliberate tuning and optimization strategies. Streaming ingestion, small files, delete files, aging metadata can gradually increase query latency and costs. In this session, you’ll learn the core optimization techniques that every Iceberg developer should understand, including partitioning, compaction, clustering, cleaning, and data skipping. You'll also learn how these techniques improve query planning and when to apply them. At the end of the session, you’ll see how these best practices can be automated using Cloudera Lakehouse Optimizer to improve performance and reduce costs. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Keep sleeping at 3am: Elastic watches your Prometheus metrics so you don't have to (sponsored by Elastic)
speaker: Jessee Miller
abstract: When your kubernetes cluster fires at 3am, who's investigating? In this session we'll show Elastic Nightshift — our autonomous AI SRE — detecting a real Kubernetes incident and working it end to end: from alert to root cause to remediation, with its reasoning made transparent at every step. Nightshift draws on native Prometheus and PromQL metrics in Elastic. Kubernetes logs, out-of-the-box EKS dashboards and workflows, and ES|QL subqueries that correlate metrics with logs and traces in a single investigation. We'll also show how the 30x faster columnar metrics engine and full telemetry retention give Nightshift the complete context it needs to work like your best engineer This presentation is brought to you by Elastic, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Keep your open source observability, move to managed scale
speaker: Nilo Bustani, Santiago Benavidez, Lucas Vieira, Camila Soares Camara, Ingrid Alitzel Sánchez Elguea
abstract: Teams standardized on Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch should not have to abandon their tools to get scale and lower operational overhead. In this hands-on builders session, you will learn about instrumentation and collection powered by OpenTelemetry, and explore that telemetry into managed open source services: ship metrics to PromQL in Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces in Amazon OpenSearch Service, and correlate all signals in Amazon Managed Grafana. Own your telemetry pipelines end-to-end with open standards and AWS managed services.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Kiro as your founding engineer
speaker: Phelipe Fabres, Jean Malha
abstract: The habits you establish in your first 90 days can shape your codebase for years. This session examines how to work with Kiro as your founding engineer, starting with the project context it needs to produce useful code. We cover how to structure development work so output stays consistent as your product grows, and which early mistakes make a codebase harder to maintain. Founders will learn how to give Kiro clear context and maintain consistent code quality as delivery accelerates. The focus is on decisions you can make early to keep the codebase maintainable as the pace of delivery increases.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Kiro Crew: Architecture of an open source AI coding agent built on Kiro
speaker: Joe Guo, Bolin Chen
abstract: Kiro Crew is an open source AI coding workspace built on Kiro CLI that grew from a side project to 39,000 users and nearly 500 contributors inside Amazon. Unlike single-session assistants, Kiro Crew combines multi-step task orchestration, tool-use planning, and a shared context layer for real engineering workflows. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through how Kiro Crew decomposes complex tasks, selects and chains tools, manages execution state, and integrates with existing developer environments. We'll discuss the design trade-offs that enabled rapid adoption and our journey to open source.

title: Kiro Writes the PR. Nobody Validates the App. (sponsored by TestMu)
speaker: Shantanu WALI
abstract: Kiro can now build a whole feature on its own: write the spec, implement it, and open the PR without anyone sitting in the loop. That’s real progress. But nothing in that pipeline actually runs the app and checks it against what the spec promised. The checks that gate the PR look at the code, not the behavior. So the PR arrives looking done, and “done” is still just a guess someone has to trust. The good news is Kiro already produces the one thing a testing agent needs to close that gap: a clear, structured spec of what the feature is supposed to do. We’ll show Kane-CLI plugged in as a Kiro Power, reading that spec, actually running the app the way a user would, and reporting back proof, not just a checkmark, before the PR merges. This presentation is brought to you by TestMu, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: KNFSD File Cache: Extending Your NFS Storage into the Cloud
speaker: Andy Hayes, DJ Rahming
abstract: Need to cache and serve NFS data from on-premises filers, across Availability Zones and Regions, or from other cloud providers with full read and write-back support? In this chalk talk, dive into KNFSD File Cache, an open-source, kernel-based NFS caching proxy on Amazon EC2 that transparently extends existing NFS storage into AWS. A single Terraform module stands up a production-ready, autoscaling cluster with high throughput and at low cost. Discuss hybrid and burst-compute patterns across M&E, HPC, Financial Services, and Life Sciences industries—eliminating latency without migration, client changes, or vendor lock-in.

title: Knowledge Representations for Autonomous Software Lifecycle Management
speaker: alexis Henry, Ankur Shanbhag
abstract: What formal properties must a software representation satisfy for agents to manage entire application lifecycles autonomously â€” reasoning at the specification level, not the code level? This session examines the open scientific questions behind agentic code understanding: encoding both structural topology and business semantics into a unified knowledge graph, extracting and grounding business rules when institutional context has been lost, enabling agent reasoning over large heterogeneous graphs without coherence degradation, and establishing deterministic validation signals that replace human judgment with formal guarantees. Drawing from graph theory, knowledge representation, specification mining, and formal verification research, we explore what makes these problems hard, where current approaches break at scale, and what architectural principles make full-lifecycle autonomy tractable. Attendees will leave with a rigorous understanding of the representation and reasoning foundations required for agents that donâ€™t just generate code but understand, validate, evolve, and replace software as knowledge.

title: Know your data: discovery, context, and AI agents in Amazon S3
speaker: Monica Vyavahare, Harsha Battapady
abstract: Organizations store billions of objects in Amazon S3 but struggle to answer basic questions: What do I have? Where did it come from? Is it still relevant? Learn how S3 Metadata and annotations turn your storage into a searchable, context-rich data estate. See how to attach business meaning directly to objects, query metadata at petabyte scale through managed Apache Iceberg tables, and drive governance workflows from metadata signals. Then discover how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit give AI agents governed access to your data, and how AWS Context lets them reason over relationships across your S3 data.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Koa: NVIDIA Nemotron-Powered CRM Reasoning Inside Salesforce’s AWS Trust Boundary (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speaker: Petro Junior Milan, Shubham Mehrotra
abstract: Salesforce Koa is a family of CRM reasoning models post-trained from NVIDIA Nemotron open models. Koa is in production on AWS, inside Salesforce's trust boundary. This session covers technical insights on how Koa was built and how Salesforce serves the model on AWS. Additionally, attendees will learn how Salesforce enforces trust and safety controls in the serving layer outside the model. This session is relevant to any team building and deploying custom open models for the enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Kubernetes-native agentic AI on Amazon EKS with open source primitives
speaker: Vikram Mehto, Anuj Dewangan
abstract: Production agentic AI needs a scalable runtime, governed LLM access, persistent memory, observability, tool discovery, and secure code isolation. In this workshop you'll build all six on Amazon EKS using native Kubernetes primitives and open source projects. Tackle all six end-to-end or take individual modules home. Deploy LiteLLM as a multi-model gateway, Mem0 for user-scoped memory, Langfuse for observability into reasoning and tool calls, an MCP registry for tool discovery, and sandboxes for hardware-level code isolation. Leave with a scalable, GitOps-ready, portable reference architecture.

title: KYC in 90 Seconds: Real-Time Onboarding with AgentCore
speaker: Avinash Dalvi, S Logesh
abstract: Opening a bank account should take seconds, not days. This session shows how AI agents can speed up KYC while keeping the final decision under control, specialized agents that run on Agentcore Harness investigate identity, documents, fraud signals, and screening results, with checks running in parallel. AgentCore Gateway routes tool requests through Cedar policies before tools run, while deterministic rules decide whether a case moves forward or needs human review. The session follows a clean case, an ambiguous case, and a new risk event after onboarding. Attendees leave with a pattern for regulated agentic systems.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Lab Maker: From Prompt to Personalized Lab in Minutes
speaker: ADAM B
abstract: Lab Maker on AWS Skill Builder generates personalized hands-on labs from natural language prompts, allowing you to learn and experiment in the Console without incurring costs or risking production environments. During this session, we will generate a custom lab in real time before saving and sharing it with a team, demonstrating the full creation-to-collaboration workflow. We will then push Lab Maker further by generating a lab for a recently launched AWS service and uploading real organizational constraints to show how the tool adapts to your specific environment. You will leave this session with the knowledge and confidence to create your own labs.

title: Lambda for every scale and workload shape
speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
abstract: Honeycomb spends millions of dollars a year on Lambda. Every cold query runs through a map-reduce backend that used to mean one tier, Lambda Functions, regardless of shape. We outgrew Lambda Functions, not Lambda: Managed Instances now absorbs steady-state baseline traffic at roughly 7.5x lower cost than Functions, MicroVMs takes spikes of load tolerating 1.5 seconds of added latency, and Functions still catches bursty spillover. We'll walk through the observability and benchmarks that drove each cutover, and the routing logic deciding which tier a query lands on before it executes. You'll learn how to scale your serverless workloads multiple orders of magnitude without linear cost.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Lambda Managed Instances: Always-on Serverless Compute
speaker: Nihar Sheth, Pushparaju Thangavel
abstract: Some Lambda workloads run constantly. For steady-state, high-throughput functions, per-invocation pricing becomes more expensive than running the same code on EC2, but you don't want to manage instances. Lambda Managed Instances give you EC2 economics with multi-concurrency while Lambda handles instance lifecycle, patching, and scaling. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the decision: when Managed Instances beat standard Lambda pricing, what workloads migrate cleanly versus what needs adaptation, and how to model your break-even point. Bring your Lambda bill. We'll help you find where Managed Instances save money and where they don't.

title: Lambda MicroVMs: Secure stateful sandboxes for code execution
speaker: Alexander Vladimirov, Anton Aleksandrov
abstract: AI agents generate code, customers upload plugins, and third-party extensions need execution environments. All of it requires strong isolation. In this chalk talk, we discuss Lambda MicroVMs: VM-level, isolated sandboxes with filesystem state that persists across invocations. We cover the security model (how isolation boundaries prevent lateral movement), stateful session management for multi-turn agent interactions, lifecycle controls that limit resource consumption, and integration patterns with Step Functions and EventBridge for orchestrating sandboxed workloads. Bring your multi-tenant architecture questions. We'll whiteboard where MicroVMs fit versus standard Lambda.

title: Lambda MicroVMs: The Missing Serverless Primitive for Multi-Tenant Agents
speaker: Darshit Pandya
abstract: Lambda Functions are stateless and time out after 15 minutes. Fargate tasks are expensive to keep warm. When building multi-tenant agent platforms, I needed per-tenant isolation without per-tenant cost. Lambda MicroVMs solve this: Firecracker VM-level isolation, 8-hour stateful execution, auto-suspend when idle, instant resume on next request. This session walks through the architecture I built, replacing always-on containers with MicroVMs as per-tenant agent sandboxes. I'll share the tradeoffs, what surprised me, and a deployable pattern you can take home and ship.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Lambda performance tuning and cost optimization
speaker: Joe Losinski, Matt Diamond
abstract: Most Lambda functions run at default memory settings, which means you're paying more for slower execution. Right-sizing memory often reduces cost and latency at the same time. In this chalk talk, we go beyond memory tuning: cold start elimination with SnapStart and provisioned concurrency, architecture-level savings like batching and right-sizing event source mappings, and when Lambda Managed Instances deliver better economics than per-invocation pricing. We whiteboard the decision points using real cost data and discuss which CloudWatch and Cost Explorer metrics actually drive optimization decisions.

title: Land migrated workloads with controls already in place
speaker: Jakob Altevolmer, David Piet
abstract: Most migrations add governance controls after workloads land on AWS, and that creates rework. This chalk talk shows how to build guardrails into your AWS Transform migration workflow with AWS Organizations, IAM Identity Center, AWS Config, and AWS Security Hub so workloads arrive with controls in place. Bring your migration challenges, and we design a secure-by-default landing together that carries governance through each phase of the migration.

title: Large-scale VMware exit: engineering a 10,000+ server migration wave engine
speaker: Siavash Irani, Shiva Vaidyanathan
abstract: Organizations facing VMware licensing pressure need more than a migration plan. They need a structured exit strategy spanning assessment, mobilization, migration, and modernization. In this session, we discuss how AWS Transform drives business outcomes at each phase: portfolio assessment that quantifies TCO reduction, wave planning that protects application uptime, automated cutover orchestration that eliminates risk, and post-migration modernization that captures cloud-native savings. Drawing from real-world examples, we explore how teams compressed 18-month timelines into ten or lower using AWS Transform and agentic capabilities for migrating compute, database and storage resources, then open the discussion to address your specific use cases.

title: Latest trends: Network/EBS intensive workloads on Amazon EC2 instances
speaker: Anti Gyori, Aaron Chen
abstract: EC2 network 'n' and EBS-optimized 'b' instances deliver the highest, most consistent network and EBS performance in the cloud. Join us for a tour of the latest Graviton and Intel instance types in these families, plus the networking and EBS technologies that unlock peak performance for your workloads. Learn how customers leverage these instances for new workloads associated with AI/ML training and inference, and traditional network-intensive workloads such as security & network virtual appliances, and EBS-intensive workloads such as SQL, NoSQL, and in-memory databases.

speaker: Luana Fares, David Ugarte, Alessandro Micco, Sid Ahmed boudboub, Pasha Digori

In this builders session, deploy a web application with built-in load balancing, autoscaling, TLS, and canary deployments configured automatically. Explore the full service lifecycle from creation through updates to deletion and see how shared ALBs keep costs low across multiple services. Ideal for developers new to Amazon ECS or looking to simplify their deployment workflow. Bring a laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Layered security for Amazon EKS: Patterns that scale
speaker: Liz Duke, Rodrigo Bersa
abstract: Kubernetes gives you powerful primitives for running workloads at scale, but its default configuration prioritizes flexibility over security. In this chalk talk, we work through a layered defense strategy for Amazon EKS: hardening the control plane, implementing least-privilege RBAC and pod security standards, securing the software supply chain, enforcing network segmentation, and building runtime threat detection. We'll discuss real-world patterns customers use to move from reactive security posture to proactive guardrails — covering both EKS Auto Mode and self-managed configurations. You'll leave with actionable strategies you can apply immediately.

title: Learn faster: Experimentation in an AI world
speaker: Ben Shumpert, Steve Rice
abstract: AI makes it possible to generate and test far more product variations than a team could create by hand. But running more experiments only helps if you can release each variation safely, measure the right signals, and separate meaningful results from noise. In this code-focused session, you’ll learn how to use AI and feature flags to control experiment variants, target audiences, adjust exposure, and shut down underperforming tests without redeploying. We’ll also examine how Amazon has recently used AI in experiments on Amazon.com to create variations and extract better signals from the results.

title: Learn how to build a Genomics PCS pipeline on AWS
speaker: Shubhendu Dubey, Kumar Shubham
abstract: Build and run a real genomics variant-calling Slurm pipeline on AWS PCS using a mixed Graviton + GPU fleet. This session will cover PCS queue design, Slurm partition strategy, FSx for Lustre, and result aggregation to Amazon S3. By the end, you’ll create a reproducible, production-grade HPC workflow for life-sciences workloads.

abstract: In this talk, we'll describe some of the resilience testing we've been doing in AWS. We'll talk a bit about the Game Day Region, why it exists, and how we use it. We'll talk about the types of test we run, the philosophy behind them, and some takeaways that you, our customers, can also apply.
