title: Leaving VMware Without Breaking Your Microsoft Estate
abstract: Most VMware estates are full of Windows Server and SQL Server, so a VMware exit forces Microsoft licensing, support, and modernization calls at the same time, usually against a renewal clock. This is an open, off-the-record conversation for people in it right now. Topics on the table: BYOL and license mobility math, SQL re-platform versus lift-and-shift, dual-vendor cost traps, and how much to modernize before you move. No slides, no pitch. Bring a question or an example of how you've tackled this.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Lessons in Scale and Innovation Through the Deployment of AI Agents
speaker: Bruno Arnal, Mark Wu, Jeffrey Eckhaus, Junjie Tang
abstract: AI agents on AWS are transforming how Amazon teams build, ship, and operate at velocity and scale. Discover how Amazon Finance Operations, supporting 6,000+ analysts across nine global service centers, deploys AI agents to resolve millions of contacts and hundreds of thousands of cases annually, automating low-value tasks and running autonomous workflows in a high-stakes finance environment. Then explore how Amazon Operation’s Workforce Intelligence & Scheduling Engine (WISE) enables them to orchestrate the operating, management, and adjustment of labor and flow across more than 1,200 facilities. When a gap in a tool, process, or service appears, it spins up autonomous coding agents on Bedrock AgentCore to build, test, and deploy solutions or mechanisms to close the gaps. Leaders will share the innovations that enabled them to stop managing systems and start orchestrating them.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Let your agent break a fake AWS: emulators and agent benchmarks
abstract: Agents learn AWS by calling it, and every mistake in a real account costs money, time, or a cleanup ticket. Local emulators such as LocalStack and Moto let an agent create, break, and reset cloud resources in seconds, which also makes them a place to benchmark agents on real AWS tasks. Bring the emulator you use, or why you stopped. At the whiteboard we'll map where emulators match real AWS and where they drift, how to score an agent by the resources it leaves behind, and what a shared practice cloud for agents needs.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Let Your Database Speak: AI Agents for RDS and Redshift
abstract: Can AI agents help us make better database capacity and cost decisions, or do they just create more alerts? We’ll start with two concrete AWS examples: an RDS for PostgreSQL workload where spending more may protect reliability, and a Redshift workload where daily contention raises the question of shared versus isolated capacity. Then we’ll compare how teams use telemetry, runbooks, agent recommendations, and human approval to make these decisions. Bring a database challenge or an agent experiment of your own. This is a peer discussion about what works in practice, not a product demo.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Level up your bot defense for mobile apps and web with AWS WAF SDK
speaker: Tzoori Tamam, Harith Gaddamanugu, Madhusudhan Rao
abstract: In this session, we'll dive into AWS WAF offerings for advanced bot mitigation. Learn how to go beyond basic rule-based blocking and build dynamic, data-driven defenses that adapt as threats evolve, including AI agents acting on behalf of users and attackers hiding behind residential proxies. We'll explore AWS WAF managed rules, use labels for granular request inspection and integrate SDK workflows to automate threat response across mobile app, JavaScript and API traffic. Through real-world scenarios, you'll see how to tell legitimate users and good agents apart from sophisticated bots, catch proxy-driven abuse that IP reputation alone misses, reduce false positives and keep your application fast on every surface. Bring your questions and learn how to build scalable, intelligent bot protection at the edge.

title: Leverage the power of MCP servers for resource inventory and compliance
speaker: Pal Patel, Francisco (Chico) Ferreira
abstract: AI agents can now interact with AWS services through the Model Context Protocol. In this code talk, we live-build a governance agent that uses MCP to query AWS Config for resource configurations. You'll see how to construct compliance checks, detect configuration drift, and trigger automated remediation using natural language all powered by Config's recording and advanced query capabilities. We explain the architecture decisions and trade-offs so you can adapt this pattern to your own governance workflows.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Lifecycle of a pod: trust boundaries in VM-isolated containers
speaker: Fletcher Woodruff, Todd Neal
abstract: Trace a pod from kubelet's RunPodSandbox call to process execution inside a VM isolated sandbox, then dissect the hard problems at each boundary crossing: how do you enforce policy on what runtime actions are allowed? How do you transport container images into an isolated environment the parent cannot read? Where does attestation fit, and how can you truly trust what is running inside? We examine how the trust model shifts between untrusted host and untrusted guest, explore the tradeoffs between CRI compatibility and security invariants, and discuss how EKS is approaching VM-level workload isolation

title: Lights, Camera, Fargate—A Reality-TV Startup Hardened for Scale on AWS
speaker: Erik Hanchett, Brian Hough
abstract: In six weeks on reality TV coding show The Full Stack, we built DataSwarm — a data-observability solution shipped as an open-source CLI with cloud-hosted data analysis and remediation. Great demo, wrong architecture. When real users arrived, the demo cracked. So we pivoted. Long-running agents moved off Lambda onto ephemeral ECS Fargate tasks. API keys swapped for firewalled Amazon Bedrock, feature-branched CI/CD with dev-to-prod promotion, and Next.js behind CloudFront, S3, and Lambda@Edge. We break down each tradeoff from first idea to first customer. Leave knowing how to tell demo-grade architectures from customer-grade ones — and when to make the jump.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Live AI and the Infrastructure Behind It (sponsored by Decart)
abstract: AI is entering a new era: from static generation to live experiences. From shopping to entertainment, digital experiences are becoming live, visual, and personalized. In this session, Decart will explore the infrastructure powering this shift, what it takes to deliver AI-generated video in real time, and how to bring these experiences to scale. Join us for a look at the technology behind Live AI, and where it’s going next. This presentation is brought to you by Decart, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Live-code inference patterns for agentic workloads on Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Bruno Pistone, Daniel Wirjo
abstract: Agentic workloads are multi-step, tool-calling, and retrieval-augmented, which means they stress the inference layer differently than a single prompt. In this code talk, we build three patterns live: function calling, multi-step reasoning chains, and retrieval-augmented generation with Knowledge Bases. For each, you see how it behaves at the inference level, including token consumption, latency, and retry logic, and how to tune it for cost and speed. The completed code covers all three patterns and can be adapted to your own agents.

title: Lives on the Line: Modernizing National Weather Forecasting on AWS
speaker: Kari Sheets, David Santore, Rayette Toles-Abdullah
abstract: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's National Weather Service (NWS) is modernizing the platform forecasters rely on across 170+ locations. Join AWS and NOAA to whiteboard the NWS Enterprise Cloud (NEC), the foundation providing secure, scalable landing zones where HIVE applications and CIRRUS data services operate. We'll explore decomposing a legacy desktop into micro-frontends and domain microservices on Amazon EKS, decoupling applications from data through an API abstraction layer, scaling independently during severe weather, and maintaining continuous Authority to Operate (ATO). We'll also discuss how Amazon SageMaker brings machine learning assistance to forecasters. Bring your modernization questions.

title: Live Streaming: Real-time Captions & Translation with AWS
abstract: How can live-streaming platforms deliver accurate multilingual captions with minimal delay? This technical meetup uses a working AWS architecture to explore real-time captioning and translation with Amazon IVS, Amazon Transcribe, Amazon Bedrock (for context-aware translation), API Gateway WebSockets, and WebVTT. Participants will examine the end-to-end media and caption flow, latency bottlenecks, synchronization, translation quality, connection management, and scaling patterns. The demonstration will serve as a starting point for attendees to compare implementation approaches and share production lessons from building accessible multilingual streaming experiences for media, education, events, and enterprise communications.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Living Off the Agent: Detecting and Preventing Lateral Movement in Agentic AI
speaker: Emmanuel Isimah, Victor Okonyia
abstract: "Living off the land" (LOTL) attacks use native OS tools to evade detection. In 2026, techniques evolved to "Living off the Agent" (LOTA), compromising enterprise AI agents through subtle prompt injections to exfiltrate data, escalate privileges, and move laterally. Red team studies identified vulnerabilities in production AI agents with distinct LOTA patterns. This chalk talk explores the LOTA taxonomy, detection strategies, and architectural containment patterns. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we'll whiteboard defenses together.

title: Load-bearing coupling: Finding the coupling you can't cut
speaker: Matt Coles, Paul Moran
abstract: Teams break up monoliths to move faster, then find the pieces still fail together. Some coupling is doing real structural work: invariants spanning writes, ordering guarantees, timing assumptions baked into callers. Cut it and you get a distributed monolith, the same dependency with new failure modes. In this session, we whiteboard real systems, insert seams, and price what each dependency costs to cross a boundary: consistency, backpressure, retry semantics. Apply a simple test: if a circuit breaker can't open here without breaking correctness, that coupling is load-bearing. Bring your hardest dependency; leave knowing which coupling to cut, which to keep, and why.

title: Logging strategy for agentic investigations
speaker: Siddharth Bhate, Brad Gilomen
abstract: Most logging strategies get built one team at a time. Each team picks its own destination and format, so an AI agent investigating an incident has to search across accounts and reason over a dozen schemas. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard a CloudWatch logging design that centralizes logs and enriches them on ingest with service context, so your agents start every investigation with what they need. We'll debate what to transform at ingest versus keep raw, and which logs earn hot storage. Bring the log setup you run today and we'll redraw it with you.

title: LSEG: Scaling multi-agent AI with assurance on Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Zan Kavtaskin, Richard Chester, Christopher Hughes
abstract: London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) manages one of the world's largest risk intelligence datasets, processing millions of records that demand continuous curation and validation. In this session, learn how LSEG built a durable agentic AI framework on Amazon Bedrock—orchestrating multi-agent workflows that combines deterministic rules, AI enrichment, and human review to reduce false positives in financial crime screening. LSEG will share their approach to continuous AI assurance with golden dataset evaluations and staged rollout gates with real-time observability and automated rollback to safely scale automation while maintaining the accuracy global financial institutions require.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Machines on-call for humans: how enterprises are transforming reliability with AI SRE (sponsored by ResolveAI)
speaker: Manveer Sahota, Claire Yin
abstract: Trusting an AI SRE to own reliability outcomes is a different decision from trusting an agent in a chat window. On the critical path, it works on every alert and ticket, not only the few that reach a person, and getting to root cause is no longer enough. It has to know what production looks like right now, reach the right answer fast enough to act on, work inside the controls you already have, and run at a cost that holds up at that volume. It also has to get better each time, because every agent shares one memory of what the last investigation found. That is what turns on-call into something wider: changes checked after they ship, drift caught before it pages anyone, and the backlog nobody has time for finally worked. Engineering leaders from SAP and Cisco describe what that took across their business units, and how a pilot became an AI-led reliability transformation.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Magic the Gathering: Experienced Play
abstract: Join us for an exclusive Magic: The Gathering sealed event tailored for experienced players! Dive into competitive play and test your skills in this special collaboration with Wizards of the Coast. It's an gathering you won’t want to miss.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom I

title: Magic the Gathering: Learn to Play
abstract: New to the game? Join us for an exclusive collaboration with Wizards of the Coast! Jump into a dedicated "Learn to Play" session complete with provided decks and expert guided instruction.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom III

title: Make every GPU count: Maximizing GPU efficiency for inference at scale
speaker: Meng Dong, Erik Anderson, Archana Balakrishnan
abstract: When an inference fleet spans thousands of interconnected NVIDIA GPUs in NVL72 racks, scheduling decisions cascade. Place a job wrong, and it fragments a capacity block, starves NVLink bandwidth, or strands GPUs behind a topology boundary. In this session, AWS and OpenAI will share scheduling and bin-packing strategies developed for production inference on Amazon EC2 UltraServers. Explore rack-aware placement that respects 72-GPU NVLink domains, approaches for mixed workload profiles (prefill vs. decode vs. batch), capacity block utilization maximization, and Kubernetes scheduling primitives that enforce topology constraints. Leave with actionable blueprints to efficiently schedule GPU inference at scale.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Make the agent code while you sleep
speaker: Keerthi Sreenivas Konjety, Govindhi Venkatachalapathy
abstract: Anyone can prompt an agent. The hard part is getting it to work the way you want—for hours, unattended, without going off the rails. This advanced workshop digs into orchestration. You'll build a custom agent, then set a goal so strong the agent can't redefine it or declare victory early. You'll decompose work across subagents, use directives like /goal to keep execution on track, and design guardrails that let an agent run long and autonomously while landing where you intended. We'll use Kiro, but these patterns transfer to any agentic system. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Make your vector search faster, more relevant, and cost-efficient
speaker: Hajer Bouafif, prasadnu Mohan Prasad
abstract: You have a vector workload running and questions piling up: How do I raise relevance? How do I control cost as I scale? Which ranking technique fits my data? We give you a quick tour of vector capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service, then spend the rest of the session working through your problems. Topics on the table include hybrid search combining lexical and vector results, ranking with reciprocal rank fusion, maximal marginal relevance, and filtering strategies, when to reach for Automatic Semantic Enrichment or neural sparse vectors instead of building your own embedding pipeline, and cost optimization techniques including quantization, tiered storage, GPU-accelerated indexing, and auto-optimization. Come with a workload in mind and leave with tuning direction for your specific situation.

title: Making Enterprise Data AI-Ready Without the Data Engineering Overhead (sponsored by Eon)
speaker: Yaniv Ehrlich, Gonen Stein
abstract: Enterprise data is spread across databases, object stores, and compute, but making it usable by AI often requires months of data engineering and a growing web of pipelines to build and maintain. In this session, we’ll show how Eon continuously discovers, connects to, classifies, and transforms data across Amazon RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EC2, S3, and more into a unified, AI-ready data layer. We’ll walk through the architecture and semantic layer on AWS, then share how agents can use Amazon Bedrock to query that governed context in natural language through MCP, with Claude, Amazon Quick, and other AI clients. This presentation is brought to you by Eon, an AWS Partner.

title: Making foundation models performant on AWS Trainium3
speaker: Matthew McClean, Fabian Güra
abstract: Many of today's largest foundation models are mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, and modern MoE models place several performance demands on AI chips and their HPC systems. This session walks through those demands and how AWS Trainium3 and the Trn3 UltraServer respond. See how to train and serve with PyTorch, TorchTitan, and vLLM, then profile with Neuron Explorer and choose between a config change, an NKI Library kernel, or a custom NKI kernel. Two customers share their experience running on Trainium3.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Making Kiro Crew work for your team
speaker: Kyle Seaman, Hillel Antonov, Aaron Longwell
abstract: Kiro Crew is the persistent, open source development workspace that remembers your context, learns how you work, and coordinates across your unique tools and workflows, so you come back to progress instead of another workflow to restart. In this session, you'll learn how to make Kiro Crew work for your team: wire in the tools your team already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape shared memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold and maintain team standards and best practices.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: Making sense of messy enterprise data with AI on AWS
speaker: Ryan Bradley, Thomas Coombs
abstract: Organizations struggle to make sense of their data when it's scattered across inconsistent formats, ad-hoc naming conventions, and incomplete records. In this workshop, you will build a scalable pipeline that uses generative AI to transform product descriptions into structured data ready for downstream analysis. Inspired by how AWS tackles life cycle assessment across its data center fleet in the AWS Sustainability Console, you will use Amazon Bedrock and other AWS services to ingest, classify, and contextualize data to deliver sustainability intelligence. You'll then deploy AI agents to orchestrate queries and execute analysis tasks, providing you patterns for any domain.

title: Making your Amazon Aurora cluster more resilient
speaker: Tim Stoakes, Pini Dibask
abstract: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale. Hundreds of thousands of organizations trust Aurora for their workloads today. In this session, learn about features such as Aurora Global Database and Amazon RDS Proxy, and discover best practices to achieve high availability for Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL database clusters. The session includes a whiteboarding discussion on high availability and disaster recovery solutions to help maximize application resilience.

title: Malware Protection: hands-on detection and response for malicious files
speaker: Omner Barajas, Anthony Harvey, Fabian Serrano Morales, Shay Grinberg, Pedro Gadelha
abstract: In this one-hour builder session, get hands-on with the core capabilities of Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection. Configure on-demand S3 scanning using the SendObjectMalwareScan API, set up automated EBS volume scanning for EC2 instances, and build event-driven response pipelines that quarantine infected objects before they spread. Walk through real malware samples triggering findings, interpret scan results, and integrate with Security Hub for centralized visibility. Leave with a working malware detection and response workflow deployed in your own account.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Manage cloud costs and AI spend with AWS Cost Management
speaker: Bowen Wang, Matt Berk, Jordi Espasa Clofent
abstract: Join this breakout to learn how AI is helping teams manage cloud costs more effectively, and why managing the cost of AI itself is becoming just as important. We cover AWS FinOps enhancements across both dimensions. On the "AI for FinOps" side, learn how your team can operate more efficiently through automation and agentic workflows. On the "FinOps for AI" side, see how you can access and manage your AI spend with granular cost data and governance. Walk away with a repeatable governance model as you scale AI with confidence.

title: Managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at scale: customer lessons
speaker: Robin Douglass Rodriguez, Dave Gadling, Pratik Mankad
abstract: AWS shares customer best practices for managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at hyperscale. Network teams discusses how they operate one of the world's largest Direct Connect footprints, spanning multiple regions and supporting AI training workloads that serve billions of users. We deep-dive into new monitoring capabilities: Amazon CloudWatch metrics for BGP session health and prefix counts, VIF rate limiters that prevent bandwidth contention across shared connections, and Network Synthetic Monitor for proactive path-level health diagnostics. Attendees will learn strategies for alerting, capacity planning, and building unified dashboards for cross-Region network visibility.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Managing APIs on AWS
speaker: Giedrius Praspaliauskas, Eric Johnson
abstract: Your next API consumer might not be a person. AI agents, MCP servers, and coding assistants are calling APIs programmatically, and they need machine-readable schemas, predictable error contracts, and discoverable endpoints. Customers also face challenges in API discovery, management, and adoption while delivering unprecedented scale with robust security controls. In this session, we cover Amazon API Gateway and API management, discuss how to design APIs that serve both human developers and autonomous agents without maintaining separate interfaces.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: Managing Bots, Mentoring Brains: The Future of Hybrid Leadership
speaker: Tamrah Barber, Leila Langlois, Purva Upasak
abstract: The traditional playbook for executive leadership is undergoing fundamental change as hybrid ecosystems of human employees and autonomous AI agents become commonplace, with agents acting as co-workers, specialists, and decision-makers. This shift requires executives to expand their skill set, dividing organizational goals between human creative strategy and agentic operational execution. Moving past the AI hype, this session examines how human roles must evolve from executors to context engineers and decision architects, and how career progression must be rewritten when entry-level and repetitive work is owned by digital labor. Explore how women in leadership will adapt and build tomorrow's leaders.

title: Managing software vulnerabilities in the agentic world
speaker: Anthony Verleysen, Nirali Desai
abstract: Vulnerability management is evolving beyond detection. As AI agents generate and deploy code at machine speed, security teams need a fundamentally different approach to identifying, prioritizing, and resolving software vulnerabilities. In this session, explore how AWS thinks about the future of vulnerability management — from contributing to open source vulnerability databases and detecting malicious packages before they reach your pipeline, to enforcing remediation at scale without slowing development velocity. Learn how to shift from reactive CVE chasing to a proactive posture that accounts for AI-generated code, autonomous deployments, and the expanding software supply chain.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Manifold Bio scales drug discovery workloads 4x across AWS regions
speaker: Erik Swanson
abstract: Manifold Bio scaled its drug discovery compute workloads 4x by distributing them across multiple AWS regions. This session covers the architecture behind that scale-out, the challenges of running scientific compute workloads across regions, and what other biotech and drug discovery startups can learn from Manifold Bio's approach to scaling compute-intensive research on AWS.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Map once and prove everywhere across multiple compliance frameworks
speaker: Brian Stucker, Kevin Donohue
abstract: Regulatory frameworks like SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and the EU AI Act each demand separate assessments, yet a significant portion of their requirements overlap. You spend time collecting duplicate evidence for controls you already have. This chalk talk introduces the control inheritance approach and shows how a single AWS Config rule or organizational policy can satisfy requirements across multiple frameworks. You walk through real examples of framework overlap, automation patterns that eliminate duplicate evidence collection, and a governance approach you can implement immediately.

title: Mapping and Securing the Enterprise AI Attack Surface (sponsored by Zscaler)
speaker: Mark Ryan
abstract: AI is racing across the enterprise—showing up in endpoints, apps, workflows, agents, and data paths faster than most security teams can track. But securing AI takes more than knowing where it exists; it requires understanding how data flows, where it comes from, where it goes, and which users, devices, apps, and AI endpoints interact with it along the way. In this session, we’ll explore how to map the AI attack surface and its data lineage while securing the AI endpoints where innovation actually happens. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

title: Mastercard: Training a large transaction model on billions of transactions
speaker: Steve Flinter, Gurinder Singh, Josh Allbright
abstract: Large language models transformed text. Large transaction models (LTMs) aim to do the same for payment and commerce data. Instead of brittle, hand-crafted feature pipelines feeding hundreds of specialized models, LTMs are transformer-based foundation models pre-trained directly on billions of anonymized transactions, learning rich representations of transactions, merchant behavior, consumer activity, and financial risk. This session introduces Mastercard's LTM program, the architectural choices behind it, and the unique challenges of tokenizing and training on tabular and sequential financial data at massive scale. We show how foundation models power diverse production use cases, from fraud detection to personalization to reaching underserved cardholders.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Mastering agentic development: skills, custom agents, and steering
speaker: Derek Chiles, Pavitra Krishnan
abstract: The best results from agentic AI don't come from clever one-off prompts, but from shaping how agents work. In this session, go beyond prompting to learn techniques that apply to any agentic coding tool. Craft reusable skills that encode your team's know-how, build custom agents tuned to specific jobs, and use steering files to carry your conventions and architecture across sessions. We'll cover how to set goals the agent will actually follow, when to let it run autonomously, and how to tell a skill that's useful versus noise. We'll demo live in Kiro, but the principles transfer wherever you work.

title: Mastering LLM tokenomics: From token costs to business outcomes
speaker: Anurag Singh, John Cherian
abstract: Financial institutions are scaling generative AI and agentic workloads to production and need strategies to keep costs aligned with business value. With enterprise workloads requiring retrieval, orchestration, validation, and governance layers, understanding token economics becomes critical to sustainable growth. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through design patterns for controlling token consumption while maintaining quality, including prompt compression, semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache, tiered model routing with Amazon Bedrock, and cost attribution using Amazon CloudWatch. We'll whiteboard the hidden cost drivers in agentic AI systems and share design patterns that financial institutions use to control token consumption while maintaining quality.

title: Master the Cloud: Strategic Upskilling for Organizations
abstract: Ready to accelerate your organization's cloud journey? Discover how leading companies are closing the cloud skills gap through innovative upskilling strategies that deliver real results. Learn practical approaches for building cloud capabilities across your organization, from creating internal champions to measuring success. Connect with peers, share experiences, and leave with actionable strategies.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Maximize EKS efficiency: Auto Mode, Graviton, and Spot best practices
speaker: Ramesh Mathikumar, Olawale Olaleye
abstract: Achieving optimal compute efficiency on Amazon EKS demands more than choosing the right instance. It requires an intelligent infrastructure layer that continuously optimizes on your behalf. In this chalk talk, learn how teams use EKS Auto Mode to eliminate infrastructure toil with up to 40% faster node boot times, over 40% faster scale-out, and up to 70% faster consolidation. Discover how pairing Auto Mode with AWS Graviton5 (M9g, C9g) and EC2 Spot can reduce total cluster spend by up to 40%. You'll leave with actionable strategies for multi-architecture scheduling, right-sizing, and Spot diversification.

title: Maximize GPU utilization across training and inference on HyperPod
speaker: Rama Thamman, Giuseppe Angelo Porcelli
abstract: Join this chalk talk to explore how SageMaker HyperPod serves as a unified GPU pool for data processing, training, post-training, and inference — no re-platforming required. Through live whiteboarding and demos, we cover how customers like HUMAIN maximize GPU utilization across workloads and multiple teams on shared clusters using advanced scheduling techniques. We also show how SageMaker Studio gives AI practitioners a single place to iterate on generative AI development, with team isolation. You will leave with practical patterns for running the full model lifecycle on resilient, shared infrastructure

title: Maximizing block storage performance for high-intensity workloads
speaker: Marc Olson, Jody Gibney
abstract: Amazon EBS handles over 222 trillion I/O operations daily. Performance matters, a lot, but it’s not just about average performance, it’s about stable low latency that minimizes outliers or tail latency. io2 Block Express volumes are designed for that purpose with consistent sub-millisecond latency and 99.999% durability for critical applications such as SAP HANA, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and more. Learn about how its performance characteristics optimize compute utilization, leading to cost efficiency and the success of many performance-demanding use cases.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Maximizing EC2 NVMe local storage
speaker: Qi Wu, Sanjeev Malladi
abstract: Discover how to leverage the latest high-performance Nitro SSDs in EC2 storage-optimized instances for data-intensive workloads. This technical session explores new capabilities for monitoring and managing NVMe instance storage, including enhanced performance metrics like latency, IOPS, and throughput to optimize and troubleshoot your workloads. We will also dive into the new AWS Local Instance Storage (LIS) CSI driver for simplified NVMe volume management in Amazon EKS. Learn best practices for storage performance monitoring and integrating the LIS CSI driver in containerized applications.

title: MCP and A2A for SaaS: making your product agent-ready
speaker: Luca Guida, Rohith Vijayasankar, Gaurav Acharya, Alexander Pogorielov, Frederic Schoenberger
abstract: Agentic AI is reshaping how SaaS products reach end customers. Alongside browser and API interactions, exposing capabilities through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and distributing agents via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol is fast becoming the norm. In this session, build the two pieces every multi-tenant, agent-ready SaaS needs: an MCP server exposing your tools and resources, and an A2A endpoint with agent cards for inter-agent calls. Discover reference architectures for MCP in front of existing APIs, A2A agent cards, and authentication and authorization on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Leave with a blueprint for being a citizen in the agentic ecosystem.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: MCP is Just An MVP. Context Layers Are The Sequel. (sponsored by Atolio)
speaker: Pete Griffiths
abstract: MCP lets agents connect to systems. It's a minimum viable product, not a complete way to run that connection at scale. Raw database access hit the same wall decades ago, before warehouses and data lakes brought structure and governance at scale. Point-to-point agent connections hit it again: costs climb with every added tool call, latency stacks with every cross-system hop, and permissions rarely travel with retrieved data, making synthesized knowledge a sharper security risk than raw SQL ever posed. This session traces that history, breaks down each failure mode, and maps what a sovereign context layer built for agents solves. This presentation is brought to you by Atolio, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Measuring emergent risks in frontier models
speaker: Rahul Gupta
abstract: As frontier models scale in capability, so does their potential for deceptive and manipulative behavior—risks that static, single-turn evaluations fail to capture. We present our multi-layered approach to measuring emergent deception under Amazon's Frontier Model Safety Framework (FMSF), combining automated benchmarks, expert red-teaming, and uplift studies. We will dive deep into two innovations: D-REX, a benchmark detecting discrepancies between benign outputs and malicious internal chain-of-thought reasoning; and LH-Deception, a multi-agent simulation revealing emergent "chains of deception" across extended task sequences. Together, these tools address critical gaps in frontier safety evaluation and inform deployment governance.

title: Migrate and modernize infrastructure from your IDE with agentic AI
speaker: Meir Raviv, Efrat Caspi
abstract: Migration and modernization involve dozens of manual steps across landing zones, networking, and containerization. What if you could drive the entire workflow from your IDE? In this code talk, you'll see how Kiro and AWS Transform work together as an agentic toolkit. First, generate a multi-account landing zone as infrastructure as code. Next, feed a VMware configuration export to the network agent and get Terraform modules or CDK constructs for VPCs, security groups, and production-ready network topology. Then point the containerization agent at a repo to produce ECR images and deploy to Amazon EKS.

title: Migrate and modernize workloads with AWS Outposts
speaker: Brianna Rosentrater, Vaibhav Phadnis
abstract: Organizations running on-premises workloads on legacy virtualization platforms are looking to migrate applications to AWS and modernize them to be more resilient and operationally consistent with their cloud workloads. AWS Outposts supports customers on this journey and is now available in second-generation single- and multi-rack offerings that deliver new instance types and Amazon EBS storage, up to 40% better price-performance, and enhanced networking features for monitoring and security. This session covers migration and modernization strategies for organizations looking to move to a cloud operating model on-premises, as well as strategies for first-generation Outposts customers to upgrade to the latest generation.

title: Migrate on-premises storage to AWS with agentic AI
speaker: Kiran Chukkala, Martyn Storey
abstract: Migrating on-premises storage to AWS typically means weeks of manual assessment, business case building, and wave planning before a single byte moves. AWS Transform's agentic AI capabilities handle the full lifecycle, from automated assessment and business case generation to wave planning and execution, reducing that timeline to hours. In this lightning talk, see how to migrate storage from VMware estates, enterprise databases, and associated data with AI handling the complexity. Leave knowing how to start your first Transform project and accelerate time to results.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Migrate, Optimize and Operate SAP Workloads at Scale
abstract: Join AWS experts and SAP specialists to accelerate your cloud journey with Unified Operations (UOps) for SAP Native and RISE. In this session learn how to accelerate your end-to-end cloud journey with UOps for SAP with best practices for migration, performance optimization, complex business integrations, and resilient cost optimized operations. Learn about how to migrate at speed to AWS for SAP Native and RISE with specialized Go-Live teams, HA and DR practices, and cost optimization with expert-led proactive guidance for SAP workloads.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Migrate SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL with AI-powered conversion
speaker: Vikas Babu Gali, Koushik Rajagopal
abstract: Migrating SQL Server databases with stored procedures, triggers, and complex T-SQL constructs to Aurora PostgreSQL typically takes weeks of manual schema conversion and dependency resolution. In this workshop, you'll walk through the end-to-end workflow using AWS Transform's agentic AI: assess your SQL Server database, automate schema conversion, resolve dependencies, then hand off to your local IDE where you review, refine, and deploy converted database objects directly. You'll leave knowing how to reduce weeks of manual effort to hours while improving conversion accuracy and confidence.

title: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB with AI-powered schema design
speaker: Kevin Willis, Keren Tseytlin
abstract: Amazon DynamoDB schema design is the number one barrier to adoption, requiring upfront knowledge of access patterns and partition strategies, which most teams learn through trial and error. New AI-powered schema design tools for DynamoDB change that. In this live coding session, follow along as a banking payment-processing application is migrated from a relational database to DynamoDB. The session covers workload analysis, optimized table design generation, cost and throughput tradeoff comparisons, and iterative refinement toward production-quality schemas, including reviewing AI-generated code, refining the implementation, migrating data, and demonstrating the complete end-to-end solution.

title: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB with AI-powered schema design
speaker: Kevin Willis, Keren Tseytlin
abstract: Amazon DynamoDB schema design is the number one barrier to adoption, requiring upfront knowledge of access patterns and partition strategies, which most teams learn through trial and error. New AI-powered schema design tools for DynamoDB change that. In this live coding session, follow along as a banking payment-processing application is migrated from a relational database to DynamoDB. The session covers workload analysis, optimized table design generation, cost and throughput tradeoff comparisons, and iterative refinement toward production-quality schemas, including reviewing AI-generated code, refining the implementation, migrating data, and demonstrating the complete end-to-end solution.

title: Migrate workloads to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
speaker: Jim Mlodgenski, Douglas Bonser
abstract: Running self-managed document databases at scale introduces significant operational burden, version lock-in, and rising infrastructure costs. Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) addresses these challenges with a fully managed, highly available service. In this session, examine compatibility features that simplify migration from existing document database environments, and work through architecture decisions affecting performance, cost, and reliability. Discover how enhancements in version 8.0 deliver up to 5x compression and 7x query performance improvement. Discuss common migration blockers, schema transformation approaches, and newest compatibility additions that reduce friction during cutover. Learn a framework for planning and executing document database migrations on AWS.

title: Migrate your NAS to the cloud: Building AI-ready file storage
speaker: Luke Miller, Andrew Crudge
abstract: Enterprises store vast amounts of business-critical data on NAS systems, but aging hardware and rising costs are only part of the story. Legacy file storage also locks data away from modern AI workloads. Learn proven strategies for migrating NAS environments to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, then connecting that data to AWS analytics and AI services, including options like S3 Access Points, Amazon Bedrock, and SageMaker. We cover assessing your NAS estate, executing migrations with minimal disruption, and choosing the right path to unlock your data for modern workloads. You leave with a practical framework for modernizing file storage.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Migrating a Managed Assistant API to Strands Agents SDK
speaker: Dharamendra Kumar, Ryan Coleman, Kyle Ahn
abstract: As organizations scale AI agent deployments, the gap between managed APIs and production-grade frameworks becomes a migration challenge. This talk describes a large-scale migration from a managed assistant API serving hundreds of agent projects to Strands Agents, selected for its deterministic orchestration, multi-provider portability, and open-source extensibility. The migration replaced three subsystems (orchestration, conversation persistence, and observability) while preserving all existing tool implementations. This session details the architectural decisions, backward-compatible tool migration, security constraints for production deployment, and evaluation methodology that validated quality parity. These patterns generalize to any organization migrating from managed AI APIs to open-source agent frameworks.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Migrating petabytes of data: Real-world strategies with AWS DataSync
speaker: Ameen Khan S, Wali Akbari
abstract: Learn how to plan, build, and implement the migration of 10 petabytes of on-premises data with AWS DataSync. Through interactive discussion and whiteboarding, explore effective approaches for data categorization and creating transfer job manifests that map directly to cost-optimized S3 storage classes. Discover how this data migration architecture accelerates the migration of client data to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP. This chalk talk provides practical insights and best practices for executing large-scale data migrations to AWS.

title: Mitigating prompt injection with structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan, Mac Stevens
abstract: Prompt injection works because LLM outputs are unconstrained. Structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock compiles a JSON Schema into a grammar and enforces it during decoding so every token the model emits is a valid position in the schema. In this code talk, we live-code defense schemas for sentiment analysis, intent classification, and SQL validation, then attack them with real injection payloads. We cover provider differences between Claude and open-weight models, strict tool use for agentic workflows, and how to combine grammar enforcement with input validation for defense in depth.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: ML, automotive, and robotics simulations at scale on AWS Batch
speaker: Jason Rupard, Peter Dachnowicz, Nikita Buldakov, Aylmer Britto Rex Harison
abstract: Simulation and ML workloads share a hard problem: they must burst to enormous scale, run to completion reliably, and do it without a standing fleet draining budget between runs. This session shows how AWS Batch orchestrates large-scale simulation and training pipelines end to end. See how AWS Batch schedules and scales compute on demand, so jobs run when needed and nothing sits idle otherwise. Learn how simulation outputs flow through a shared data lake into GPU-accelerated training, closing the loop between data and models. Discover the orchestration and scheduling patterns that keep a real customer's high-throughput pipeline efficient.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Model customization in production: When does fine-tuning pay off
abstract: Fine-tuning can cut cost and latency, or add weeks without a clear win. Whether you're weighing your first custom model or running one in production, join fellow builders and AWS model customization specialists for a peer-led discussion with no slides. Trade experiences with fine-tuning, distillation, and reinforcement learning on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI. Together, we'll dig into what decides the outcome: data readiness, the baseline to beat, proving the custom model is better, and whether the cost math holds at scale. Connect with peers and compare notes on what worked.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Modeling Human Preference: Pairwise Battles to Agentic Systems
speaker: Pradeep Natarajan, Swastik Roy
abstract: Every time we rank an LLM, we're building a model of human preference — yet for most queries there's no ground truth, only a person's sense of which answer is better, shifting with expertise, culture, and expectations. This session examines how we model preference across two regimes: pairwise battles, arena-style voting ranked through Bradley-Terry, and agentic systems, where preference spans long-horizon, multi-step, tool-using tasks. Reward models and LLM-as-judge are themselves learned preference models; from our experience at Amazon, we examine when to trust them and how to separate progress from preference-overfitting. Attendees will learn what modeling preference at scale demands.

title: Modernize a Legacy Telecom Billing App with AWS Transform Custom
speaker: Efrat Nir-Berger, Anil Maheshwari, Rabindra Shakya, Guy Ben-Baruch, Albeda Siddique
abstract: Got an old telecom application buried under decades of technical debt? In this hands-on session, you'll take a legacy BSS billing system and modernize it using AWS Transform Custom. Start by analyzing the codebase to understand business logic, dependencies, and technical debt. Then apply a built-in catalog transformation to upgrade the language and framework instantly. Next, define your own custom transformation in natural language to convert legacy interfaces to modern APIs. Validate, test for functional equivalence, and deploy to AWS. Walk away with a running modernized app and reusable transformation recipes, plus hands-on experience modernizing real-world telecom applications.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Modernize and containerize legacy apps to Amazon ECS with AWS Transform
speaker: Diego Dalmolin, Asiel Bencomo Corona, Avinash Desireddy, Jayaprakash Alawala, Abhishek Nanda, Ian Choi
abstract: Your application runs on an old Java runtime with outdated dependencies. You know it belongs in containers but the upgrade path feels daunting. In this builders session, take a legacy monolithic application and use AWS Transform to identify blockers, upgrade dependencies, generate multi-stage Dockerfiles, build and scan container images for vulnerabilities, and deploy to Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. See how the agent handles multi-repo applications and validates containers before production. Walk through the full lifecycle without writing a single Dockerfile by hand. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Modernize confidently with production intelligence
speaker: Venugopalan Vasudevan, Harvinder Nagpal
abstract: Static code analysis tells you what to modernize. It doesn't tell you what breaks when you do. Runtime dependencies, real traffic patterns, and operational risk stay invisible until cutover, when surprises are most expensive. AWS DevOps Agent adds the missing ingredient: production intelligence fed directly into your AWS Transform modernization plan. The result is assessments grounded in reality and migrations that stay safe through execution. In this chalk talk, we discuss how to incorporate production intelligence from DevOps Agent into an automated migration pipeline by Transform Custom. Bring your modernization challenges to discuss.

title: Modernize legacy applications into cloud native event-driven systems
speaker: Nirmal Mehta, Chris McPeek
abstract: Join us to learn how to plan and automate your application modernization using agentic tools. We show how to reverse-engineer your applications and dependencies from existing code, then generate a event-driven cloud native target architecture. See how teams move from monoliths to event-driven microservices, deployed as containers or serverless applications, in weeks, and make your applications agent-ready in the process.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Modernize legacy batch into event-driven with AWS Transform & Kiro
speaker: Subramanian (Subu) Karuppiah, Rene Simoes, Ramachadra Desaraj, Pablo Alonso Prieto, Sourav Sarkar
abstract: Batch processing has powered critical enterprise workloads for decades, from mainframes running COBOL and PL/I to distributed systems on legacy Java. The trade-off? Overnight batch cycles that business processes can no longer afford. In this session, reimagine batch as event-driven microservices using Domain-Driven Design. AWS Transform reverse-engineers business rules from legacy code across platforms with full traceability, and Kiro translates that understanding into microservices specifications, generates production code, and creates Infrastructure as Code for AWS deployment. Leave with a repeatable pattern for reimagining batch workloads as real-time, event-driven microservices built on business rules that took decades to refine. Laptop required.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Builders' Session

title: Modernize .NET Applications with AWS Transform and Kiro
speaker: Clayton Markos
abstract: Legacy .NET Framework applications tied to Windows limit your deployment options and increase operational costs. In this lab, you use AWS Transform for .NET in Interactive Mode to automatically port a .NET Framework 4.8 Web Forms application to .NET 10 Blazor application. You review the AWS Transform generated assessment report and migration plan, accept the automated transformation, then use Kiro to identify and fix the residual runtime issue that remains after the port.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Palace Ballroom II

title: Modernize SAP business processes with agentic AI on AWS
speaker: Shirli Cohen, Stephan Kremer
abstract: Enterprise processes span SAP for ERP, Salesforce for CRM, and ServiceNow for ITSM, connected by aging, brittle integrations that are slow to change. Agentic AI offers a better path: replacing point-to-point integrations with agents that reason across applications. In this workshop, you modernize an SAP-centric business process by orchestrating Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents over Model Context Protocol, including the AWS for SAP MCP Server. You implement cross-application use cases spanning finance, supply chain, and operations then leave with a deployable reference architecture for moving from custom integrations to agent-orchestrated workflows.

title: Modernize the data layer, then scale the AI: A Cisco Case Study (sponsored by MongoDB)
speaker: Mohammed Hamzeh, Abhijit Chakraborty, Rajiv Papneja
abstract: Enterprise AI agents depend on applications running on data layers built for a different era. So, how do enterprises modernize applications at scale? Cisco migrated a workflow automation platform running tens of millions of workflows a month—and the AI support assistant built on it—to MongoDB on Amazon EKS without disrupting live operations. The assistant has since resolved 1M+ support cases on its own and is on track to handle most of Cisco’s support volume. Discover: • Modernization patterns MongoDB sees across enterprises on AWS, from tool-assisted migration to targeted rewrites, and how to choose between them • How Cisco’s distinguished engineer sequenced the migration and what had to change in the data model • What the AI assistant can do now that it couldn’t before Leave with a practical checklist for planning a modernization that supports AI and agentic workloads. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Modernize Windows to Linux and SQL to PostgreSQL with agentic AI
speaker: Aidan Keane, Gianpaolo (GP) Albanese
abstract: Moving workloads from Windows to Linux and SQL Server to PostgreSQL has always been a complex, multi-step project. Agentic AI changes the game by orchestrating the entire journey for you. In this expert-level workshop, you'll start with on-premises Windows Server workloads in a simulated data center and migrate to Amazon EC2 covering agent installation, continuous replication, and cutover. Then you'll modernize by upgrading SQL Server to PostgreSQL and migrating PHP to Amazon EKS, applying replatforming patterns in practice. You'll leave with end-to-end experience executing OS and database modernization, accelerated by agentic AI. Laptop required.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano IV

title: Modernize with Purpose: Bringing Sustainability and GenAI into Your Migration Journey
abstract: Migration and modernization programs are usually justified by cost and agility. They are also a good moment to lower carbon emissions and prepare for generative AI. Sustainability and GenAI are often planned separately from the migration itself, and that can mean duplicated work later. This session looks at how organizations can bring all three goals into one modernization plan on AWS. We will cover how to set a carbon baseline with the AWS Sustainability Console and which modernization choices tend to lower emissions, such as AWS Graviton, managed and serverless services, storage lifecycle policies, and Region selection. We will also look at how GenAI can speed up migration work like code analysis and transformation, and how a modern data and application foundation makes GenAI adoption easier afterward. Attendees will compare approaches, share what has worked in their own organizations, and leave with practical ideas for making sustainability and GenAI part of their modernization roadmap.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Modernize your CI/CD pipeline with AWS
speaker: Phil Seokpil Kang, Pablo Silva
abstract: In this workshop, build modern CI/CD pipelines using AWS CodePipeline through the AWS Management Console. Learn how to work with monorepos and branching strategies. Explore safe-deployment features including canary and linear traffic shifting, CloudWatch alarm gates for automatic rollback, stage-level conditions that run integration tests before promotion, and concurrent execution modes to improve pipeline performance. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Modernize your full .NET and SQL Server stack with AWS Transform
speaker: Jose Guay, Tekena Orugbani
abstract: Modernizing Microsoft workloads means tackling .NET and SQL Server together, not as separate projects. In this workshop, you'll use AWS Transform to compress this effort into a single sprint and reduce operating costs by up to 70% by moving off costly licenses. Working from a legacy app, you'll port .NET Framework code to modern, cross-platform .NET, migrate SQL Server to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, then containerize and deploy to Amazon ECS or EKS. You'll leave with a proven approach to transform your full stack into a scalable, cloud-native architecture. Come ready with your personal GitHub account. Laptop required.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Pompeian IV

title: Modernizing Care for Medicaid and Medicare Patients: Montefiore's Cloud Journey
speaker: Deepesh Chandra, Matt Dinger
abstract: Montefiore Einstein is one of New York's leading academic health systems, serving 1.3 million Bronx residents across 11 hospitals and 300+ ambulatory locations. To best care for patients, most of whom rely on Medicare or Medicaid, Montefiore needed to modernize its enterprise technology. Montefiore selected AWS as its strategic cloud provider to build a secure, scalable, and resilient foundation that strengthens security and optimizes costs. This session explores how the transformation—including an Epic migration—enables AI-powered clinical decision support, improves the reliability of critical medical records, and expands patient access through Amazon One Medical. Learn the strategies, lessons, and cloud-first approach driving better outcomes for the patients and communities Montefiore serves.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Modernizing file transfer with AWS Transfer Family
speaker: Ulili Nhaga, Madhukumar Adavi, Randy Boutin
abstract: Legacy file transfer platforms are costly to maintain and fragile under pressure. When outages and bottlenecks start compounding, patching isn't enough. In this session, learn how AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed foundation for secure file exchange that scales with demand. We'll cover core capabilities including managed SFTP servers, connectors, browser-based web apps, and event-driven automation. A customer joins to share how they replaced a failure-prone platform with a modern, AWS-native architecture on Transfer Family and S3.

title: Modernizing HPC on AWS: Migration at scale with PCS
speaker: Ekjot Basra, Andrea Rodolico, Ala Abunijem
abstract: AWS Parallel Computing Service (PCS) is helping teams modernize their HPC infrastructure by making it easier to migrate off legacy schedulers without disrupting engineering velocity. In this session, hear how organizations have moved to PCS at scale, including how Amazon Leo migrated 400 engineers and achieved 20% cost savings and 50% faster jobs. Walk away with practical migration patterns, performance tuning strategies, and architecture decisions that apply whether you're running simulations, modeling, or other compute-intensive workloads.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Modernizing Legacy Telecommunications OSS/BSS Systems
speaker: Visu Sontam, Antonello Arpino
abstract: Legacy modernization is one of the most complex challenges facing Telecommunications companies today. In this Chalk Talk, we will explore strategies to accelerate VMware and mainframe migrations using Agentic AI. Using a real-world scenario, we will walk through how AWS Transform and Amazon Bedrock are used to meet the technical and business requirements of these projects and explore trade-offs in migration design and infrastructure choices. Come ready to discuss your own migration challenges!

title: Modernizing .NET to Serverless: Native AOT and SnapStart, live
speaker: Doug Perkes, Lasse Christiansen
abstract: .NET workloads on Lambda have historically meant slower cold starts and JIT warmup time that doesn't match Serverless execution patterns. Native AOT and SnapStart on .NET 10 close that gap, bringing cold starts under 200ms, but modernization isn't flip-a-switch. In this code talk, modernize a .NET function to AOT live, watch it fail, then fix it on stage: serialization with source generators, reflection-based DI replaced, trimming warnings resolved. See real measurements across AOT, SnapStart, and the managed runtime. Walk away with a library compatibility matrix and modernization patterns for your own .NET Serverless journey.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Modernizing Real-Time Market Data with Amazon Kinesis and Apache Flink
abstract: Real-time data feeds are among the hardest streaming workloads: quiet one moment, and a flood of messages the next, consumers expect reliable, low-latency delivery. In this meetup, explore a reference architecture for a high-throughput streaming pipeline using Amazon ECS, Amazon Kinesis, and Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink. See how a containerized Docker stack lets you build and test locally, then discuss decoupled ingestion, stream replay, and migration strategies with fallback mechanisms. Bring your streaming war stories and leave with a working repository and reusable architectural patterns.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Modernizing VMware workloads with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
speaker: Satya Vandrangi, John Jamail
abstract: Migrating VMware workloads to AWS often means rethinking storage, but it doesn't have to. In this chalk talk, we explore how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides a storage foundation built for VMware migrations. Learn how FSx for ONTAP delivers multi-protocol support, enterprise data management, and ONTAP compatibility that VMware administrators already know. We'll discuss real world migration patterns, cost optimization through deduplication and compression, and high availability with Multi-AZ and zero RPO. Bring your questions and join us to design a migration strategy that minimizes disruption and maximizes your existing ONTAP investments.

title: Modernizing your compute stack with Lambda's new execution models
speaker: Eric Johnson, Chris McPeek
abstract: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. Lambda's new execution models change that: durable functions add checkpointed orchestration, Managed Instances provide always-on compute at EC2 economics, and MicroVMs offer hardware-level sandboxes with persistent state. In this breakout, we discuss the operational decision tree: which execution model to standardize on for each workload class, how to manage mixed-model deployments, monitoring differences across models, and when to migrate workloads between them. Bring your workload portfolio. We'll help you build an operational playbook for multi-model Lambda.

title: Monetize AI Bot Traffic: Agent-Ready Media with AWS WAF & AI Analysis
speaker: Arturo Velasco, Carlos Salazar
abstract: More than half of web traffic now comes from AI bots that consume content built for humans while returning little value to publishers. This hands-on workshop tackles both the content and the monetization side. First, you'll build a pipeline that converts images, video, and audio into concise, agent-friendly markdown summaries including interpreting what's shown, said, and meant, while preserving the originals for human readers. Then you'll monetize bot traffic with AWS WAF AI traffic monetization, setting per-request pricing by bot verification tier and collecting payment via the x402 protocol. You'll build a working dual-audience pipeline and WAF pricing configuration you can deploy against your own media.

title: Monitor Agent Performance and Telemetry using AgentCore Observability
speaker: Eyal Tamir
abstract: A personal finance assistant agent deployed on AgentCore Runtime starts showing intermittent failures and slow responses. In this lab, you will use AgentCore Observability with CloudWatch GenAI dashboards and Transaction Search to diagnose production issues. Trace errors through spans, correlate telemetry with application logs, and identify root causes including a tool timeout and conversation history bloat. Apply fixes, redeploy to AgentCore Runtime, and set up CloudWatch Alarms to catch issues before users do.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Palace Ballroom II

title: Monitor and optimize costs for Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Adam Richter
abstract: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how that spend maps to business outcomes. In this lightning talk, see how to tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Monitoring and optimizing Amazon S3 with observability tools
speaker: Mario Kiessling, Roshan Thekkekunnel
abstract: As your S3 data estate grows across buckets, tables, and directory storage, operational visibility becomes critical for cost control, performance tuning, and security investigations. In this chalk talk, learn how to build a comprehensive observability strategy for Amazon S3. We will introduce S3 Storage Lens for organization-wide metrics and recommendations, server access logs for request-level diagnostics, CloudWatch metrics for real-time alerting, and S3 Metadata for storage analytics. We will walk through use cases for each tool, including when to reach for one over another, and deep dive into Storage Lens for optimizing at scale. Bring your monitoring questions as we work through real scenarios for identifying cost anomalies, diagnosing latency issues, and auditing access patterns across multi-account environments.

title: More than a heartbeat: Designing health checks that matter
speaker: Andrew Gray, Satish Katpally
abstract: Great health checks tell you exactly how your application is really performing, not just that a port is open. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard meaningful health check patterns across ELB, Amazon Global Accelerator, and Amazon Route 53 that covers how to validate database readiness, confirm replica currency, and verify end-to-end request success. We'll explore thresholds, timing configurations, and graceful failover strategies. Bring your architectures, including diagrams, napkin sketches, or draw live on the whiteboard, and we'll design your health strategy together. Leave with actionable patterns that reflect true application liveness.

title: Move Agent Rules Out of the Prompt
abstract: Agents need context to be useful, and running them in production demands control and determinism. Most enterprises try to get both by packing rules into the system prompt, but a prompt is a request, not a control. In this session we move the constraints into the architecture. Policy as code (Cedar, and Dogwood for rules that depend on what the agent already did, such as order, approvals and volume) governs which tools an agent may call. Underneath, the purpose-built databases that supply its context (vector, graph, relational, key-value) enforce their own permissions, as long as the user’s identity actually reaches them. We’ll map where each rule belongs, show which ones can be formally proven and which can’t, and demo a Bedrock agent stopped by its architecture rather than by its prompt.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Move AI agents from prototype to production with 1Password (sponsored by 1Password)
speaker: Matt Porter
abstract: Giving an AI agent real work means connecting it to real systems without exposing their credentials. For developers, platform engineers, and security teams, this lightning talk demonstrates how 1Password, AWS Strands Box with AWS Credentials Daemon can give sandboxed agents access to the services they need while keeping secrets outside the agent. We’ll show how developers connect credentials managed in 1Password, how Box injects them into permitted requests, and how local policies restrict what the agent can do. We’ll also explore the path to centrally managed authorization, approvals, and time-limited access across local and cloud deployments. This presentation is brought to you by 1Password, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Move code modernization at scale from one-time to continuous
speaker: Varun Kulkarni, Moshe Barlev
abstract: Technical debt doesn't stop accumulating when a modernization project ends. Across thousands of repos, outdated dependencies, framework drift, and security gaps compound daily. So why treat code modernization at scale as a one-time campaign? In this chalk talk, we'll explore how AWS Transform is evolving into always-on, autonomous remediation at portfolio scale. We'll dig into what continuous mode looks like in practice, what early enterprise customers are seeing, and how this changes the way your teams think about maintaining code health over time. Bring your questions.

title: Move to AI: Modernizing for GenAI Readiness
abstract: Every organization will deploy AI agents against existing systems — the question is whether those systems are ready when it happens. Answering it used to mean 4–8 weeks of interviews and fragmented tooling; AWS Transform now answers it in minutes, from your actual code. This meetup goes under the hood of two managed analyses — Agentic Readiness Analysis (is a service safe for an agent to call?) and Modernization Analysis (where are the cloud-native gaps and the fastest path to close them?) — covering archetype classification, context-sensitive severity, readiness classifications, and how to scale from a single repo to a full portfolio.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Move your app to AWS Elastic Beanstalk and forget the ops
speaker: Aritra Nag
abstract: Running a production application should not mean owning the infrastructure under it. This lightning talk shows how AWS Elastic Beanstalk assumes ongoing operational responsibility for your applications — deployment, scaling, patching, monitoring, and upgrades — whether you bring source code, a container image, or an existing workload. In a few minutes, you will see how to identify which workloads are ready to move and what the path looks like, so your teams ship applications while AWS runs the operations underneath. You own the application. AWS owns the operational responsibility.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Move your multi-tenant agents to serverless AgentCore
speaker: Hoseong Seo, BK Chaurasiya
abstract: Running multi-tenant agents on Kubernetes gives you flexibility, but it introduces certain operational overhead like cluster management, scaling decisions, and identity plumbing. In this workshop, you'll migrate agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's serverless infrastructure without giving up isolation or control. Starting from a working agentic SaaS application on Amazon EKS, you'll progressively refactor each component onto AgentCore: implement tenant isolation, configure shared MCP tools with per-tenant scoping, and instrument tenant-aware memory and observability. You'll validate tenant separation at every step and leave with hands-on experience moving multi-tenant agent infrastructure to a managed architecture. Laptop required.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano IV

title: Moving from reactive to proactive operations with AI Agents
abstract: AI agents are changing how engineering and operations teams manage production environments. As applications become more complex and distributed across AWS, multicloud, and on-premises environments, teams have an opportunity to move beyond reactive incident response toward more proactive operations. Join AWS experts and fellow practitioners for an interactive discussion on how AI agents are transforming operations, from preventing incidents and accelerating troubleshooting to automating operational tasks and continuously improving reliability. We’ll explore emerging approaches, real-world challenges, and lessons learned, including how AWS DevOps Agent is helping teams make this shift.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Multi-agent AI: Orchestration and choreography, compared
speaker: Archana Ambavane, Dimple Dhar
abstract: Every multi-agent AI system needs a coordination layer. The hard question is who decides what happens next: a central orchestrator or the agents themselves. In this session, you deploy the same five-agent travel booking pipeline through both orchestration (Step Functions) and choreography (EventBridge). Run identical load tests, inject the same failures, and add a sixth agent to each. Measure blast radius, extensibility cost, and debugging speed to see where the two approaches diverge. Leave knowing when to orchestrate, when to choreograph, and how to combine both in one architecture. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Multi-Agent Operations for Broadcast & Streaming
speaker: Osmar Bento Junior, Bryan Samis
abstract: When live or streaming video breaks, every second costs revenue and audience trust. This session shows how to build coordinated AI agents using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands SDK that ingest observability data from AWS Media Services and partners, reason across signal domains, and accelerate root cause identification. Walk away with an architecture for agentic operations that turns reactive troubleshooting into proactive resolution.
