title: Penetration testing every deployment with AWS Continuum
speaker: Shuo Yang, Jeremy Schiefer
abstract: Your applications ship far more often than they get a penetration test. AWS Continuum for Penetration Testing (formerly AWS Security Agent) uses AI agents to test running web apps and APIs, and it validates every finding before a developer sees it. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how a test plans, runs, and proves its findings. Then we wire it into your pipeline as a gate that tests only the commits since the last cleared run and blocks promotion on validated findings. Bring your pipeline and your questions.

title: Performance tuning for streaming ingestion with Apache Iceberg
speaker: Angel Conde Manjon, Sergio Garces Vitale, Shana Schipers, Diego Garcia, Francisco Morillo
abstract: Unlock real-time streaming into Apache Iceberg with advanced performance tuning. Learn how to optimize ingestion pipelines using Apache Kafka and Apache Flink for fraud detection, IoT monitoring, and real-time analytics. This session covers throughput optimization through partitioning, parallelism, write distribution, batching, and checkpoint tuning. Discover techniques to reduce small file issues with compaction, minimize write amplification with deduplication, and maintain low-latency ingestion at scale, turning raw streaming data into actionable insights with efficiency and reliability.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Persistent memory, shared context, instant discovery. Solving storage for AI agents
speaker: Claire Edgcumbe, Jordan Dolman
abstract: Production AI agents need to remember what happened yesterday, share work with other agents today, and find the right data in milliseconds. Most storage wasn't built for this. This session introduces the S3 stack purpose-built for agentic workloads. S3 Files provides a shared file system for multi-agent artifact handoff. S3 Vectors stores embeddings as long-term semantic memory that persists across sessions and restarts. S3 Metadata makes every object discoverable by tag, time, or custom attribute without scanning. Learn reference architectures for coordination, checkpointing, least-privilege access patterns, and framework integration.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Personal AI agents that learn: building with Hermes Agent on AWS
abstract: What would you build with an AI agent that learns new skills on its own? Hermes Agent is an open-source AI agent that improves itself as you use it. Hervé Bizira, Chief Business Officer at Nous Research, joins Joseph Dolivo, Principal Technologist at AWS Startups, for a fireside chat about how Hermes learns the way your team works and saves it as skills the next person can reuse. They'll also cover how to choose models on Amazon Bedrock based on what a successful task costs. To close, you'll set up your own personal agent with Hermes Agent and Amazon Bedrock and leave with an agent that has already learned something from you. Make sure to bring a laptop!
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Physical AI for MedTech: From Intelligent Devices to Business Impact
speaker: Juli Hysenbelli, Shaun Qualheim
abstract: Physical AI — AI that senses, reasons, and acts in the physical world — is reshaping medical devices. From surgical robots to connected infusion pumps, imaging to wearables, every next-gen device needs training, simulation, edge deployment, and fleet management at scale. In this chalk talk, we’ll architect the full Physical AI stack on AWS for medical devices — SageMaker for model training, IoT Greengrass for edge inference, regulated OTA at fleet scale, and NVIDIA solutions integrated into the AWS backbone. We’ll whiteboard the hard tradeoffs — edge vs. cloud, regulatory constraints, and scaling from prototype to 100K devices. Leave with a reference architecture and a clear path to pilot

title: Physical AI in Telecom: A Framework for Workload Placement
speaker: Young Jung, Angelo Sampietro, Umer Chaudhary
abstract: Some physical AI workloads need sub-millisecond performance at edge cell sites, others are better suited to a full AWS Region, and many fall in between on AWS Local Zones or AWS Outposts. In this chalk talk, we provide a framework for matching each workload to the right option. We trace the physical AI development lifecycle, examining how data sovereignty, latency, data gravity, and token economics interact to shape placement decisions at each phase. Based on real-world use cases, we discuss the options so you leave with a placement framework you can apply immediately.

title: Physical AI on the Move: How Torc Robotics Trains and Scales Autonomous Trucks on AWS
abstract: Torc Robotics, an independent Daimler Truck subsidiary, is transforming freight with self-driving trucks, powered by physical AI. Discover how Torc is bringing Level 4 driverless trucks to the highway on AWS, using Amazon S3 to store petabytes of driving data and Amazon EC2 to scale GPU-based reinforcement learning and validation. Learn how AWS enables Torc to build more reliable systems faster – providing the infrastructure for Torc to turn multimodal sensor data into training-ready datasets, curate critical scenarios in minutes with AI agents, and validate driving policies against millions of simulated miles. Leave with key insights on how to bring autonomous vehicles to the road at scale.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Pinpoint latency in microservices with distributed tracing
speaker: Kevin Lewin, Carlos Henriquez Quintana
abstract: Diagnosing latency across a high-scale Amazon EKS environment is complex when pods scale dynamically and trace context fails to propagate across service boundaries. In this code talk, we instrument containerized microservices with OpenTelemetry, propagate context across service hops, and correlate spans, metrics, and logs in Amazon CloudWatch. Live coding shows how a single slow request reveals the exact container and code path responsible for degradation, using targeted span attributes and exemplars to make Kubernetes-scale traces navigable. You'll also see the trade-offs behind sampling strategies and collector deployment topologies that affect overhead, fidelity, and cost at production scale.

title: Pit Crew AI: Building Multi-Agent Cloud Operations on AWS
speaker: Pablo Inchausti, David Petrocelli
abstract: AI can generate code at racing speed, but production workloads still require continuous attention to security, reliability, cost, and operational risks. In this Code Talk, we build a multi-agent architecture on AWS inspired by a Formula 1 pit crew. Using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, MCP, GitHub, Jira, and Infrastructure as Code, we evolve from a single agent to a team of specialized agents for security, cost optimization, reliability, and observability. Through a live demonstration, you’ll see how agents turn cloud findings into engineering tasks. Attendees will leave with reusable architectures, orchestration patterns, and examples for cloud operations on AWS.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Pitfalls of SaaS: Return of the agent
speaker: Anubhav Sharma, Bill Tarr
abstract: Every SaaS architect has hit the classics: noisy neighbors saturating infrastructure, compounding costs eating margins, deployment models chosen too early. Agents amplify all of them — and add surprises. One agent generates more API calls in a minute than a human makes in a week. Shared memory leaks context across tenants in ways no IAM policy catches. Autonomous tool calls cascade across services with no human in the loop. Revisit classic SaaS pitfalls through an agentic lens: familiar problems in new costumes, genuinely new failure modes, and what to change before you find out the hard way.

title: Planning for migrations, and operating databases on AWS with Redgate (sponsored by RedGate)
speaker: John Martin, Kellyn Gorman
abstract: Moving a database from on-premises to the cloud is easy to get wrong: undersized instances, surprise costs, unplanned downtime. Join Kellyn and John as we look at Redgate Monitor's new database migration planning feature, designed to help you size, plan, and cost a move with real data instead of guesswork. We will also explore how Redgate Monitor is evolving to support the next generation of database operations, supporting teams who are using AI assistants and Agents who need access to observability data quickly, giving operational staff faster answers and smarter recommendations when managing complex database systems. This presentation is brought to you by Red Gate, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Policy to Proof: govern deployments at machine speed
speaker: Welly Siauw, Jerry Peter, Jean Velez Torres, Vinicius Elias, Pujah Goviel
abstract: When agents and automated pipelines deploy at machine speed, manual sign-off can't keep up, so the proof has to be built into the pipeline itself. Developers want to ship fast, governance teams want controls enforced, and compliance teams want evidence. In this builder session, you'll build a CI/CD pipeline that satisfies all three: cfn-guard validation against policy rules, CloudFormation deployment, Config evaluation after deployment, and a compliance report generated as a pipeline artifact. The full policy-to-proof loop in one pipeline. You leave with a working pipeline where every deployment validates governance rules and produces audit evidence on its own.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Post-quantum cryptography tabletop experience
abstract: Quantum computing is advancingâ€”is your cryptographic infrastructure ready? In this immersive tabletop, executives will confront the urgent reality that current public-key cryptographic standards face obsolescence. Make high-stakes decisions on migration timelines, technology selection, and stakeholder coordination as quantum threats loom over customer data, transaction systems, and competitive intelligence. Balance budget constraints against discovery, risk prioritization, and implementation speed while navigating regulatory requirements and operational continuity. Compete to build quantum-resistant infrastructure before adversaries exploit today's vulnerabilities. Leave with actionable strategies for leading a post-quantum cryptography migration that protects trust and secures competitive advantage.

title: Post-quantum readiness at scale with AWS and DXC Technology
speaker: Rushir Patel, Douglas Skirving
abstract: Post-quantum migrations succeed when organizations can discover cryptographic assets, assign ownership, and continuously manage risk. Organisations are facing a rapid increase in machine identities, service identities, APIs, containers, AI workloads, and other cryptographic assets. At the same time, certificate lifetimes continue to shrink, making manual lifecycle management increasingly unsustainable. AWS and DXC Technology show how enterprise governance connects with crypto agility. See how DXC built a cryptographic asset intelligence and orchestration platform on AWS to discover and correlate assets across AWS and enterprise PKI, automate certificate lifecycles, and assess post-quantum readiness. A live proof of concept demonstrates inventory, prioritization, and continuous reassessment. Leave with an operating model aligned with NIST and CNSA 2.0 timelines.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Post-Quantum Readiness on AWS: Where Do You Start?
abstract: Data encrypted today could be decrypted later by a future quantum computer, and the move to post-quantum cryptography is already underway across AWS. This practical meetup brings together security and platform engineers to compare how they are preparing. We'll discuss building a cryptographic inventory, where AWS already supports hybrid post-quantum TLS on service endpoints such as AWS KMS, AWS Certificate Manager, and AWS Secrets Manager, and what that means for your clients and SDKs. We'll also cover designing for crypto agility so algorithms can change without rewrites, and deciding which data and systems to address first. Come at any stage, share what you've tried, and leave with a practical starting plan.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Powering Agentic AI with Real - Time Market Data Transformation for LSEG (sponsored by AMD)
speaker: Mike Thompson, Stuart Bunyan, Madhusudhan Rangarajan
abstract: Traditional 1:4 CPU-to-GPU architectures are evolving as agentic AI increases demand for orchestration, analytics, retrieval, and database processing. Join AWS, AMD, and LSEG to learn how organizations are building AI-ready infrastructure with Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts powered by 5th Gen AMD EPYC™ processors. Hear how LSEG modernized a 7,500-system estate supporting 120 million financial instruments, achieved sub-4ms latency targets, and accelerated its cloud-native transformation. Discover how customers are improving price-performance, lowering infrastructure costs by more than 30%, and creating a scalable foundation for AI, analytics, and mission-critical workloads. This presentation is brought to you by AMD, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Powering your agentic AI experience with AWS streaming and messaging
speaker: Sarang Bapat, John Morkel, Subham Rakshit
abstract: Organizations are accelerating innovation with generative and agentic AI and getting there depends on a handful of real-time data primitives: durable, high-throughput ingestion; stream processing and enrichment; low-latency, event-driven delivery; and a scalable place to land and serve data. In this session, learn how these primitives come together to power the real-time patterns behind agentic AI and where each one fits: streaming into a real-time semantic layer for fresh retrieval context, event-driven agent invocation so agents act the instant something happens, and continuously sourcing agentic data stores with live data. Following a single transaction end to end, we'll show where each primitive breaks when the consumer is an agent, the design decisions you still own, and a reference architecture you can apply right away.

title: Powering Your Forward Deployed Engineers with Kiro and AIDLC
speaker: Mansi Suratwala, Fabio Braga de Oliveira
abstract: Learn how to power your Forward Deployed Engineers with AI-driven delivery in this hands-on workshop. Work through a full agentic-driven development lifecycle using Kiro: elaborate requirements, generate domain models and code, produce tests and IaC, and deploy, all while staying in control of architecture decisions. Along the way, see how partners scaled persona-based agents across the SDLC, with gains of 2-10X velocity, 3-5X productivity, and 50-70% reduction in design cycle time. Leave with a repeatable approach your teams can apply on the next engagement, and the next, sharpening your AI-driven delivery.

title: Power streaming analytics on AWS with AI-driven insights
speaker: Swapna Bandla, Austin Groeneveld
abstract: Learn how to build a modern, streaming analytics solution for real-time data processing and power it with agentic AI capabilities to analyze events and extract patterns for actionable responses. This session will provide a hands-on experience on building a streaming solution using Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka for real-time data ingestion, using Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink for complex event processing, and Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock Agent Core to take immediate action. Further evolve this solution to demonstrate the integration with Amazon S3 Tables for deeper analysis.

title: Powertools for agent DevOps: Debug reasoning, not just exceptions
speaker: Philipp Page, Andrea Amorosi, Henrique Graca, Leandro Cavalcante Damascena, Stefano Vozza
abstract: Your agent returned the wrong answer — no exception, no alarm, it just reasoned poorly. Traditional monitoring catches crashes, not bad decisions. In this builder session, you'll use Powertools for AWS Lambda to build agent observability: Logger with log buffering to capture decision context only on failure, Tracer with annotations for confidence scores and tool selections, and Metrics tracking token cost and reasoning steps. Wire OTEL with Strands SDK for end-to-end traces across the agent loop. You leave with dashboards that answer "why did the agent decide this?" - not "did it crash?"

speaker: Nick McCord, Karthic Chinnannasamy
abstract: Edge compute is a practical way to build faster, smarter applications. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll dive into how Amazon CloudFront empowers developers to run custom logic at the edge using CloudFront Functions, Lambda@Edge, and the Key Value Store. We'll explore real-world use cases, architectural patterns, and recent feature launches that unlock powerful personalization, performance optimization, and cost efficiency. Come ready to whiteboard, ask questions, and discover how to push intelligence closer to your users.

title: Practical PKI for On-Prem Devices with IAM Roles Anywhere
speaker: Ben Bridts
abstract: Secure authentication of your humans and machines is a challenge every organization faces, especially if your proof of identity is not already in AWS. In this session, we'll talk you through multiple ways to set up or use PKI - such as Belgium's eID or a hardware key - to securely access AWS with phishing resistant authentication built using IAM Roles Anywhere. This will include live demos and code samples. By the end of the session we will stop worrying about plain text credential storage because we can use trusted hardware instead.

title: Preventing unintended access: a practical guide to data perimeter controls
speaker: Abhi Yadav, Nitin Kulkarni, Sowjanya Rajavaram, Manas Chhabra, Vaibhav Chowla
abstract: Are you looking to prevent unintended access to your data and mitigate data exposure risks? This hands-on session demonstrates how data perimeter controls implemented through service control policies (SCPs), resource control policies (RCPs), and VPC endpoint policies help keep corporate data within organizational boundaries. You'll build data perimeter policies for real-life security scenarios and validate their effectiveness using an assessment tool. By the end, you'll have practical knowledge on how to help ensure only trusted identities access trusted resources from expected networks.

title: Prime Video Financial Systems on the Road to 10x Velocity with Kiro
speaker: Tulip Gupta, Kannan Ekanath, Robert Cicero
abstract: This chalk talk will deep-dive into Prime Video Financial Systems' journey toward 10x engineering velocity with Kiro. Starting at 3x through AI-assisted sprints, the team evolved to autonomous agent-driven delivery, where agents pick up tasks, implement code, raise code requests, address feedback, and merge 24/7 without human intervention. Each step compounds, enabling parallel execution, zero idle time, and freeing engineers to focus on design and review. This is an honest, in-progress story that demonstrates the concrete methodology, structured specs, persistent Kiro sessions, and architectural decisions required to move from acceleration toward order-of-magnitude transformation.

title: Private AI agent egress: VPC Lattice meets AgentCore Gateway
speaker: Shubham Singh
abstract: Your AI agents need to call private MCP servers, internal REST APIs, and OAuth providers, but those backends must never touch the public internet. In this lightning talk, we demo how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway uses managed Amazon VPC Lattice endpoints to route agent traffic privately into your VPC. We'll configure a private MCP server target, show traffic staying on the AWS backbone, and cover key patterns including intermediate domain routing, private certificate workarounds with ALB, and cross-account connectivity. Walk away with a repeatable pattern for secure, zero-public-internet agentic workloads.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Processing PII without exposing it with AWS Nitro Enclaves for confidential computing
speaker: Sathish Kumar Prabakaran, Abhishek Jawali
abstract: How do you process PII data at scale without giving your data pipeline access to the plaintext? In this workshop, you combine AWS Nitro Enclaves for confidential computing with Amazon EMR on EKS to build a high-assurance screening system. AWS Nitro Enclaves provides isolated compute environments within EC2 instances to protect highly sensitive data. Encrypted records are sent to an enclave, where data is decrypted only after AWS KMS verifies the enclave's cryptographic attestation. Screening rules are applied and only the decision is returned. Plaintext never leaves the enclave boundary. The pattern generalizes to any workload processing highly sensitive data at scale.

title: Production Agentic Trading: Build the pipeline Moeve runs on AgentCore
speaker: Aristides Fernandez, Loreto Albinana
abstract: This session details the implementation of an agentic workforce managing the trade lifecycle in production energy trading operations. In this workshop, you'll build the pipeline Moeve runs in production: a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that extracts deal data from unstructured emails, resolves ambiguity deterministically against master data, and carries evidence per field. You'll harden it with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails on input and output, then score it for accuracy and run-to-run consistency, including the fields that measured badly, and why. You'll leave with a reusable pattern for production deployment of mission-critical trading workflows with strict latency and reliability requirements.

title: Productionize, secure, and scale agentic applications on Amazon ECS
speaker: Suguna Devarla, Raj Bagwe, Ashok Srirama, Shamanth Devagari, Sathya Balakrishnan
abstract: AI agents are easy to prototype but hard to run in production. They have unique compute requirements, isolation between tenants, networking that connects to tools and APIs, and infrastructure that scales with unpredictable workloads. In this builders session, deploy an agentic AI application on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate and take advantage of what containers give you, including task isolation, unlimited runtime for long-running agent conversations, VPC networking for secure tool access, and Service Connect for multi-agent communication. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Production-ready Lambda: Security and performance patterns
speaker: Sahil Bhimjiani, Parnab Basak, Ezzel Mohammed, Abhishek Agawane, John Lee
abstract: A Lambda function that handles traffic well in prototype isn't necessarily production-ready—there's a gap between "works" and "hardened." In this builders' session, take a working Lambda function and add the security and performance layers that production demands. You'll implement least-privilege IAM policies, add request validation and secrets management, reduce cold start duration with SnapStart and right-sized memory, and configure reserved concurrency for predictable performance under load. Each change includes the trade-off: what you gain, what it costs, and when to skip it. Bring your laptop.

title: Program the Physical World: AI Apps on Ring (sponsored by Ring LLC)
speaker: Harish Komaragiri
abstract: Ring cameras and sensors watch over millions of homes, storefronts, and jobsites, and now anyone can build on them. The Ring Developer APIs give your apps real-time events, video, and device data with customer-granted permissions, so they can see what happens in a physical space and act on it. In this lightning talk, the Ring Developer team shows real apps built three ways: AI apps sold through the Ring Appstore, automations for your own sites, and multi-site operations for enterprise teams. See the opportunity behind them, and how your AI coding agent can build one with the Ring MCP server and Amazon Bedrock.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Protect EKS and ECS workloads without chasing pod IPs
speaker: Bongkyoon Choi, Amish Shah
abstract: Pod IPs in Kubernetes change constantly as containers scale and restart, making IP-based firewall rules brittle and hard to maintain. In this lightning talk, learn how container attribute-based rules in AWS Network Firewall let you write policy using native attributes like namespaces, cluster names, and labels instead of ephemeral IPs. We'll show how a container association auto-discovers matching pods, refreshes IP mappings in near real-time, and enriches alert logs with container context for faster troubleshooting and audit. Bring the same Layer 7 inspection, FQDN filtering, and managed IDS/IPS protections you already trust to your Amazon EKS and ECS workloads.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Protect MCP endpoints on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with AWS WAF
speaker: Piotrek Witkowski, Alex Moening
abstract: As enterprises move generative AI agents from prototype to production, securing the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes a first-class requirement - not an afterthought. In this hands-on workshop, you'll attach AWS WAF natively to a Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with no ALB, no VPC Interface Endpoint, and no Lambda proxy required, enabling managed rule groups, rate-based rules, and IP-based access controls that protect every tool behind the Gateway with a single configuration. We will launch simulated attacks and watch AWS WAF block them in real time. Finally, you'll leverage an agent that pulls signals from AWS WAF, helps you remediate threats, and generates a plain-English incident summary.

speaker: Piotrek Witkowski, Alex Moening
abstract: As enterprises move generative AI agents from prototype to production, securing the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway becomes a first-class requirement - not an afterthought. In this hands-on workshop, you'll attach AWS WAF natively to a Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with no ALB, no VPC Interface Endpoint, and no Lambda proxy required, enabling managed rule groups, rate-based rules, and IP-based access controls that protect every tool behind the Gateway with a single configuration. We will launch simulated attacks and watch AWS WAF block them in real time. Finally, you'll leverage an agent that pulls signals from AWS WAF, helps you remediate threats, and generates a plain-English incident summary.

title: Protect, recover, validate: Data resiliency for AWS storage
speaker: Rucha Kiwlekar, Allyn Henderson
abstract: Data protection strategies today must span workloads and prove recovery works before an incident demands it. In this workshop, you'll implement recovery and data protection strategies for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, and Amazon EBS with AWS Backup. Using a financial services application architecture, you'll configure protection mechanisms for ransomware and insider threats and execute step-by-step recovery procedures against simulated cyber threats. Recover across multiple services, validate restored data integrity, and walk away with patterns to strengthen your own recovery capabilities. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

title: Proving your defenses work: validating GuardDuty runtime detection
speaker: Muhammad Wasiq (AWS), Bryan Van Hook
abstract: Your board wants to know your detections work and auditors want evidence. The only way you find out today is when something real hits. In this code talk, you;ll see us build a detection validation program that answers the question before it gets asked. We'll live-code realistic attack scenarios mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, generate the correlated signals that trigger GuardDuty runtime findings, scope detection rules to specific accounts, and interpret findings as they fire. You'll walk out with a repeatable framework your team can run after every GuardDuty update to prove coverage, not assume it.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Pushing AI Boundaries: Transform Marketing with Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker and AWS (sponsored by Adobe)
speaker: Siddhartha Srivastava
abstract: As generative AI matures into autonomous ecosystems, enterprise marketing demands a new era of collaboration. In this session, discover how Adobe and Amazon co-innovate to deliver next-generation AI capabilities for marketers, business practitioners, and developers. At the center of this revolution is Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker, an advanced AI teammate powered by Adobe Harness. We will showcase how Coworker and its flexible, headless capabilities seamlessly unite Adobe’s deep customer experience expertise with the power of AWS. Attendees will discover how this combined innovation enables teams to transition from manual execution to goal-based, automated workflows with built-in governance. Join us to learn how this partnership helps enterprise organizations take a massive leap forward in operational effectiveness and unlock entirely new business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Adobe, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Put your coding agent in a torture chamber
abstract: Coding agents write code faster than any team can read it. Verification-driven development (VDD) moves trust from reading diffs to checks the agent can't talk its way past: acceptance gates frozen before work starts, bugs planted on purpose that the tests must catch, and a receipt a person signs off on. One open-source project runs this with more than 1,100 planted faults. Bring your pipeline and the ways agents have gamed it. At the whiteboard we'll map where your process still depends on someone reading code, and which checks tell a passing build from a correct one.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Put your data to work: build a knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Siamak Ziraknejad, Dani Mitchell, Aakash Upadhyay, Nabil Ezzarhouni, Sunita Koppar
abstract: Your data lives in documents, images, databases, warehouses, and relationships between entities. In this builders session, build a knowledge assistant that works across all of it on Amazon Bedrock. Use Managed Knowledge Bases with multimodal ingestion to handle PDFs and images, add natural-language querying over structured data, and wire in GraphRAG for questions that span connected entities. Then make it enterprise-ready: secure tenant isolation, concurrency-aware ingestion, and the Agentic Retrieval API for multi-hop, cited answers. Leave with a deployed stack and retrieval patterns you can reuse across your organization.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: PyTorch optimizations: Faster AI and lower costs with AWS Graviton
speaker: Juan Mestre, Hellen Avila Rosa
abstract: Small language models are a great fit for CPUs: cheap to run, simple to deploy, and good enough for many real workloads. In this session we explore the latest PyTorch optimizations for Arm-based hardware and how to get the most out of them on AWS Graviton, from the kernel performance that decides inference speed to lower cost per token and more users per instance. We cover real benchmark results on live instances and what it looks like to run small models on Arm today. Whether you are tuning a model, sizing instances for production, or just curious about what the community has been shipping, come get a grounded view of where things stand.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Quantum Error Correction - Progress, Hardware, and What's Next
speaker: Tyler Takeshita, Mao Lin
abstract: Quantum computers have the potential to solve some of today's most challenging computational problems — but they suffer from significantly higher error rates than their classical counterparts. In this talk, we introduce quantum error correction (QEC) and compare the hardware requirements of leading QEC methods against the commercial roadmaps of quantum hardware companies. To ground the discussion, we begin with a brief revisit of classical error correction before walking through recent breakthroughs in quantum error correction. Attendees will leave with an informed perspective on where QEC stands today and the challenges that will define the field's progress in the coming years.

title: Quantum-proof your IoT fleet: migrate devices to Post-quantum cryptography OTA
speaker: Pravin Nair, Samuel Waymouth
abstract: NIST has announced post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards and CNSA 2.0 requires quantum-resistant algorithms by 2027. IoT devices deployed today operate for 10–20 years, so they need to be quantum-resistant from day one. In this workshop, migrate a real ESP32-S3 SoC from classical TLS to post-quantum cryptography over the air with zero physical access required. Connect to AWS IoT Core, trigger an OTA delivering ML-KEM and ML-DSA with quantum-safe certificates from AWS Private CA, and watch your device reboot into PQC-secured MQTT. No embedded experience needed. You leave with the ESP32-S3 and open-source code to quantum-proof your fleet at scale.

title: Queue-based decoupling trade-offs for event-driven workloads
speaker: John Lee, Bailey (Sohyeon) (Sohyeon) Cho, NS Sabah, Michael Orman, Justin McGinnity
abstract: Every decoupling pattern makes trade-offs, and the right one depends on your workload's constraints. In this session, you work through scenarios with competing demands: exactly-once processing, tenant isolation, back pressure, and ordering. Using SQS and Lambda, you configure queue types and concurrency controls, tune batching behavior, and observe how your consumer scales under each configuration. Each scenario forces a trade-off between throughput, ordering, isolation, and cost. You leave knowing which trade-offs to accept for your workload and why. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Race to migrate and modernize with agentic AI at the EBA cloud party
speaker: Rajesh Kumar, Maria Armstrong
abstract: Imagine compressing months of cloud migration and modernization into days, tackling legacy code, tight timelines, and cross-team coordination head-on. That's exactly what the Experience-Based Acceleration (EBA) method delivers. In this hands-on, gamified EBA workshop, cross-functional squads split into workstreams and race to migrate and modernize a legacy app and its databases, apply cloud best practices, and deploy the transformed architecture, all in the cloud. Experience firsthand how EBA shatters silos and compresses migration and modernization from months into days with AWS Transform and Kiro. You'll get repeatable playbook your team can run on Monday. Ready to play?
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Pompeian IV

title: Ransomware resilience with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
speaker: Jay Horne, Luba Vaisberg
abstract: Ransomware does not wait for a scheduled backup window, and neither should your defenses. In this chalk talk, learn how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP's built in Autonomous Ransomware Protection uses machine learning to catch abnormal file activity and automatically create protective snapshots before damage spreads. We cover configuring detection policies, integrating alerts with AWS security services, locking down recovery points with SnapLock, and building automated response workflows. Bring your questions as we design a defense in depth strategy together, one that gets your file data back fast when an attack happens, not just one that flags it.

title: Ready before the surge - smart ELB capacity reservations
speaker: Ikenna Izugbokwe, Hema Halagatti
abstract: Your Load Balancer scales automatically for most traffic, and now you can prepare it for predictable spikes before they arrive. Product launches, flash sales, live events, and Monday-morning market opens deserve a load balancer that's ready instantly. Load Balancer Capacity Unit (LCU) Reservation pre-provisions a capacity floor so your infrastructure is never caught cold. In this session, we introduce new capacity management capabilities across ALB, NLB, and GLB that turn reservation planning into a data-driven workflow. Learn how to analyze historical patterns, set the right capacity floor, and release reservations with confidence.

title: Real-time agentic architecture on AWS: from batch to real-time AI
speaker: Chinmayi Narasimhadevara, Ankita Mishra
abstract: Batch jobs and cron schedules fail silently and delay agentic AI outcomes: a missed run, a stuck lock, or a partial write goes unnoticed, adding lag between the moment an event occurs and the moment an agent responds. This advanced deep dive rethinks the architecture—loosely coupled services that deploy and fail independently, wired through events. We show how shifting transactional and analytical workloads to real-time, event-driven patterns fuels responsive agentic AI on AWS.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan I

title: Real-time AI video enrichment with AWS Elemental Inference
speaker: Vipul Patel, Phil Harrison, Kiran Patel
abstract: Retrofitting videos to add subtitles, vertical formats, social cuts, and searchable metadata often means new encoders, manual editors, and multiple integrations. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Elemental Inference can help extend reach, enhance engagement, and improve monetization by layering subtitling, vertical framing, key-moment clipping, and contextual metadata onto live and on-demand video without rebuilding your stack. Learn about the benefits of a single managed service that will improve latency, quality, and lower costs for video workflows.

title: Real-Time Pattern Detection with Flink CEP and Agentic Workflows
abstract: When fraud, outages, or anomalies show up as patterns across millions of events, batch processing is too late. Join builders running stream processing on AWS to compare how they detect complex patterns in real time with Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink and Amazon MSK. The host opens with a short look at a production CEP pipeline where rules change without job restarts and matches hand off to agentic workflows for enrichment and action. Then the room takes over: How do you version and test detection rules? How do you manage state and checkpoints at scale? When should an agent act on a match automatically, and when does it need a human? Bring your streaming war stories and leave with patterns from peers. Some Flink familiarity helps but is not required.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Real-world migrations: Lessons learned migrating to AWS Outposts
speaker: Frankie Negro, Marcelo Andrade, Scott Rose
abstract: Organizations with data residency and digital sovereignty requirements face a critical question: how do you move workloads from on-premises infrastructure to AWS Outposts without disrupting compliance posture or operations? This Level 300 session distills lessons from migrating customers to Outposts across industries, organization sizes, and migration strategies, featuring SERPRO, Brazil's federal data processing company, and AT&T, migrating telecom workloads at scale. The session walks through the processes that delivered results, the quantifiable outcomes measured, and the critical mistakes to avoid. Learn how to select the right migration approach and navigate common blockers. The session also covers transitioning from first-generation to second-generation Outposts hardware.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Architecting AI Governance & Security at Scale
speaker: Hasan Mehdi Rizvi, Omkar Deshmane, Dodd Pfeffer
abstract: Everyone wants AI. Nobody wants to be the team that shipped it without security and governance. In this Rodeo, you'll join a team and face three demanding stakeholders: a security hawk, a data visibility champion, and a platform lead, racing to get Agentic AI live. Your team's mission: build a governance architecture that keeps all three happy. Together, you'll whiteboard, debate, and build against the clock, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns. Best architecture rides away with the win.

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Building an AI-Ready Data Foundation
speaker: Arnab Ghosh, Jigna Gandhi, Anurag Singh
abstract: Your data estate wasn't designed for AI agents. Nobody's was. But somewhere between your RDBMS, NoSQL clusters, and that untouchable data lake, an agentic-ready architecture waits to be built. In this Rodeo session, your team draws a challenge: a legacy warehouse needing a semantic layer, a sprawling lake needing an ontology, or a metadata mess that lets agents in without letting governance out. Your job: build a data layer that makes agents productive, keeps compliance calm, and gives analysts self-service. You'll whiteboard ontologies, debate metadata, and wire up multi-agent access against the clock. Best architecture rides away with the win.

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Designing Agentic AI Applications
speaker: Avichal Chum, Viraj Padte, Piyali Kamra, Mastan Shaik
abstract: Ever stared at multiple disconnected systems held together by manual handoffs and thought, "there has to be a better way"? Agentic AI is that better way. In this hands-on Rodeo session, you team up to design an end-to-end agentic solution for a real-world scenario: multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop decision points, and MCP integration. Swap ideas with other teams, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns for turning manual chaos into autonomous workflows. Bring your A-game, the best design rides off with the win.

title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Transforming Customer Experience with AI
speaker: Troy Dieter, Jacob Scheatzle, Disha Jayswal
abstract: "Your call is important to us." Nobody believes that anymore, and neither do your customers. Contact centers are being rebuilt around AI, and getting the architecture right is what separates the experiences people love from the ones they dread. In this Rodeo session, you'll join a team and design the transformation yourself: voice AI that understands people, routing that knows why they're calling, and handoffs to humans that don't start with "can you repeat your issue?" You'll whiteboard, swap ideas with teammates, and build against the clock, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns. Saddle up! The design that finally makes "your call is important to us" true rides off with the win.

title: Rebuild a legacy ETL pipeline as serverless with AWS Transform
speaker: Oren Waldman, Vineedh George, Francisco Fagas, Vimala Pydi, Aditya Chaphekar
abstract: Enterprise data teams maintain ETL pipelines built on legacy tools like stored procedures, custom bash scripts, IBM DataStage and others, that resist migration due to undocumented dependencies. In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to discover and map an existing ETL pipeline, generate a modernization blueprint, and rebuild it as a serverless workflow using AWS Glue and Step Functions. Each attendee picks one legacy source module (stored procedures, bash/SQL scripts, or DataStage jobs etc) and works hands-on through discovery, transformation logic analysis, and deploying a modernized pipeline.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Rebuild CI for AI coding agents with content based caching (sponsored by RWX)
speaker: Dan Manges, Tommy Graves
abstract: Continuous integration was designed around human pace. A developer pushes a branch, a webhook fires, and a ten minute wait feels acceptable. AI coding agents break that assumption, and validation becomes the longest part of the cycle. Explore how RWX rebuilt the layer underneath continuous integration for agent driven work, including content based caching that skips work already proven unchanged, graph based task execution, a container runtime built for reuse, and a command line interface agents call directly rather than waiting on Git. Learn which parts of a pipeline are structurally slow and which are simply misconfigured. This presentation is brought to you by RWX, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Rebuilding a Platform's Foundation on DynamoDB Streams and Lambda
speaker: Awedis Keofteian
abstract: Our platform had single points of failure baked into its original design. In this session, I walk through how we closed those gaps across all five AWS Well-Architected pillars: moving event-driven workloads onto DynamoDB Streams and Lambda, cutting costs through smarter data tiering, and building the observability needed to trust the new design under real operational pressure.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Recover and prove your full stack without disrupting production
speaker: Pritam Bhalerao
abstract: Meeting your recovery time and point objectives is non-negotiable. For your critical workloads, that means orchestrated, tier-aware recovery within minutes, with a plan you've actually tested. Most teams haven't, because testing often means disrupting production. So, the plan stays on the shelf and RTOs stay theoretical. In this session, see AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicate servers into low-cost staging and recover the full stack in the right order, in minutes, then rehearse the same failover without production noticing. Learn how to run non-disruptive recovery drills against your own environment and prove your RTOs before an incident does it for you.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Recursive Self-Improvement on the Job
speaker: Yu Su
abstract: This talk will discuss RSI (recursive self-improvement) agents that proactively and continuously learn on the job. Agents onboard a new knowledge job just like human employees. Through RSI, we show that agents can outperform human testers on the same job across accuracy, efficiency, and cost. The talk will end with a discussion on the future of human-AI collaboration.

title: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure
speaker: Sanket Nasre, Aoife Egan
abstract: AI can write your infrastructure in seconds — but did it build what you asked for? In this workshop, you'll apply test-driven development to AI-generated infrastructure. Describe your architecture in plain English, then use Kiro's spec-driven development to decompose it into discrete, testable behaviors. Kiro iterates through each one: writing a failing CDK assertion that encodes it (red), generating minimal infrastructure to pass it (green), then advancing to the next. Once green, refactor toward production readiness using cdk-nag rule packs to enforce Well-Architected practices. Leave with meaningful test coverage and a repeatable pattern for raising your organization's infrastructure coding standards. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Red team CTF: when auth and guardrails aren't enough
speaker: JaQuan Thompson, Mac Stevens
abstract: The best way to secure an AI agent is to think like the attacker. In this CTF-style session, you start with a production-realistic agent - AgentCore runtime, Bedrock Guardrails, Cognito authentication, and three MCP tools - and you systematically exploit it. Across 6 challenges, you poison trusted data sources, bypass prompt-level access control, jailbreak an authenticated session, compromise a third-party MCP server, exfiltrate data through authorized channels, and burn the inference budget. After each breach, you enable the real fix and verify the attack fails. You will compete on a live leaderboard and leave with a fully hardened agent and a defense-in-depth playbook.

title: Red teaming Aurora and gen AI: offense, defense, response
speaker: Alexander Rubin, Will Sovran
abstract: Databases and generative AI workloads are high-value targets that demand continuous adversarial testing. In this session, learn how AWS red team engineers use AI to discover innovative ways to strengthen Amazon Aurora and other cloud-native database services against modern threats. Explore how red team findings shape architectural decisions that contain blast radius by design, and how AI-augmented detection and response mechanisms close the loop at machine speed. Learn a practical framework for red teaming cloud environments and AI systems, designing for assumed breach, and building response capabilities that match the velocity of modern threats.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Reduce EKS cluster compute costs with EC2 Flex instances
speaker: Christian Melendez, Santosh Kumar, Esra Kayabali, Saurabh Modh, Nati Cohen
abstract: Container orchestration promises to improve resource utilization, but often we find ourselves with nodes that over-provision CPU, and therefore overspend. This might happen when our workloads have a high memory footprint, or when the number of replicas is driven by resilience targets and not actual load. In this session, we'll learn how easy it is to save cost in these situations without losing performance by taking advantage of EC2 Flex instances (e.g., C8i-flex, M8i-flex, R8i-flex). You'll migrate existing EKS cluster nodes, monitor relevant metrics, and measure the actual cost improvement.

title: Reduce incident response time on Amazon ECS with AI observability
speaker: Bhupendra Washishtha, Sushanth Mangalore
abstract: You get paged. Your ECS service is returning errors. You open six tabs, task logs, ALB metrics, deployment history, CloudWatch alarms, container health and start piecing together a timeline by hand. In this chalk talk, explore how AI-powered observability changes that workflow. See how CloudWatch Investigations ingests your existing telemetry, correlates signals across services and infrastructure, and produces root cause analysis in minutes instead of hours. Discuss how to structure logs and metrics so automated investigation actually works, and how Managed Daemons keep your collectors consistent without redeploying applications. Bring your incident response questions for an open discussion.

title: Reduce LLM inference costs up to 80% through caching with Valkey
speaker: Jeff Duffy, Kevin McGehee
abstract: LLM inference depends on limited GPU memory, and a KV cache lets agentic AI applications reuse computed intermediate states across prompts to reduce latency and costs. In this talk, we explain how KV caching works and walk through a production architecture using Valkey as a high-performance datastore, LMCache for KV reuse at inference, and llm-d for cache-aware routing. You will leave with practical implementation guidance and a framework for evaluating when a KV caching tier is the right choice to reduce costs for your AI applications.

title: Reduce LLM inference cost with Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey
speaker: Meet Bhagdev, Madelyn Olson
abstract: Agents resend long, repeated prompts every turn. GPUs keep recomputing the same context. In this session, learn how to use Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey as a shared KV cache to cut cost per token and time to first token. See how inference engines such as vLLM store and reuse KV state across GPU servers with ElastiCache. Any server can skip repeated prefill, even after a restart. The session covers the architecture and patterns that optimize cost or latency, including representative benchmarks and guidance on when caching pays off.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Reduce spend and data movement with Amazon Redshift Data Sharing and Graviton
speaker: Poulomi Dasgupta, Erika Nagamine
abstract: Organizations sharing data across business units often rely on slow, error-prone ETL jobs that create costly duplication. Amazon Redshift Data Sharing enables secure, live access across provisioned and serverless warehouses — within or across accounts and regions — eliminating data movement entirely. Additionally, Graviton-powered Redshift RG instances accelerate workloads on Apache Iceberg tables through optimized columnar processing and parallel I/O. In this session, learn how to break down data silos with cross-warehouse data sharing and boost open data lakehouse performance with Redshift on Graviton.

title: Reducing Lambda cost with Graviton and managed instances
speaker: Sahil Bhimjiani, ISHITA CHAKRABORTY, Jay Colodner, Anup Rajpara, Jay Formosa
abstract: Lambda's default x86 pricing works fine until your steady-state workloads make the per-invocation model expensive at scale. In this builders' session, start with a baseline workload and apply two cost levers: migrate to ARM64 (Graviton) for better price-performance, then deploy on Lambda Managed Instances for EC2 economics with multi-concurrency on steady-state traffic. You'll measure before-and-after cost and performance data at each step, evaluate when each approach makes sense versus default Lambda pricing, and leave with a repeatable migration playbook. Bring your laptop.

title: Re-Engineer Enterprise Processes for Agentic AI on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (sponsored by Camunda)
speaker: Daniel Meyer
abstract: Enterprise AI is moving from experimentation to production, but legacy workflows designed without AI in mind keep agents disconnected from the processes, systems, and controls that determine successful business outcomes. Understand why reengineering now matters: organizations that preserve legacy workflows risk slowing AI adoption while others redesign operations for an AI first world. Discover how Camunda ProcessOS works with Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to discover, re-engineer, and improve end-to-end processes. See how Camunda’s agentic orchestration combines deterministic controls with dynamic AI agents, human approval, observability, and auditability. Learn why you need to re-engineer now, and stop adding agents to yesterday’s workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Camunda, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Refactor your monolith for multi-tenancy and agentic AI in one pass
speaker: Sunil Ramachandra, Aswin Vasudevan
abstract: Most ISV monoliths get modernized in three sequential passes: refactor, then multi-tenant, then agentic. Three trips through the same code, each longer than the last. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into the unified refactor pattern that makes tenancy and agentic bets in the same window. We'll explore how data partitioning decisions shift when agents are also a target, when Amazon EKS becomes the substrate for both migrations, and which patterns create more debt than they solve when combined wrong. Leave with a framework for the one refactor window you can afford. Bring your questions.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Regional Community Builders: The Global AWS Community Exchange
abstract: What can AWS communities learn from one another across regions? This interactive exchange brings together Community Builders, User Group leaders, organizers, and practitioners to share what their communities are building, what is working, and what they want to create next. Through short community showcases, structured peer discussions, and a Global Community Exchange Wall, participants will exchange practical ideas, share proven approaches, and identify opportunities for cross-region collaboration. Attendees will leave with ideas they can adapt in their own communities, new connections, and potential collaborations that can continue beyond re:Invent.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Regulation to Innovation: A Global Enterprise Guide to Digital Sovereignty (sponsored by Accenture)
speaker: Emanuele Baldassarre
abstract: Digital sovereignty is a growing priority for global enterprises operating across Europe as they navigate regulatory requirements, geopolitical uncertainty, and increasing demand for cloud and AI innovation. Organizations must balance data residency, compliance, resilience, and business agility without slowing transformation. Learn how leading enterprises are using AWS European Sovereign Cloud as part of a broader cloud strategy to meet sovereignty requirements while continuing to adopt modern cloud services and AI. Accenture will share practical approaches to assessing sovereignty needs, designing compliant architectures, and integrating sovereign cloud capabilities into enterprise environments. Attendees will leave with actionable guidance for balancing trust, resilience, compliance, and innovation at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Reimagine legacy apps to be agentic AI ready with AWS Transform & Kiro
speaker: Alyson Keenan, Vipin Gupta
abstract: Enterprise core applications were built for stability, not agentic AI. Tightly coupled dependencies across mainframe and interconnected systems make it nearly impossible to add intelligent capabilities without rearchitecting. In this workshop, take a legacy application through the full modernization journey: scope it, reverse-engineer existing behavior with AWS Transform, classify logic into deterministic microservices and AI agents, design target layers with Kiro, build the agentic layer on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, then deploy and validate. Leave with hands-on experience rebuilding a legacy application into an architecture ready for agentic AI. Laptop required.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano I

title: Reimagining Patient Engagement with AI and Cloud (sponsored by Incedo Inc.)
speaker: Jackie Dioguardi, Nitin Seth
abstract: Life sciences organizations are exploring how AI and cloud can transform engagement across the patient journey. This executive discussion will examine how connected data, generative AI and intelligent automation can enable more personalized, timely and responsive patient experiences. The conversation will explore opportunities to reduce friction, improve engagement, drive adherence, and deliver more connected omnichannel experiences aligned with business priorities. It will also address the challenges of data fragmentation, governance, trust and adoption. Attendees will gain practical executive perspectives on moving beyond AI experimentation to scalable, responsible solutions that deliver meaningful value for patients and life sciences organizations. This presentation is brought to you by Incedo Inc., an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Reimagining the Operating Room: Gen AI's Impact on Surgery (sponsored by Deloitte)
speaker: Sara Siegel, Nadine Hachach-Haram
abstract: Explore how Generative AI, powered by Proximie and AWS, is fundamentally reshaping the operating room. This session will detail how computer vision and LLMs are creating the OR of the future, supported by Deloitte, to improve productivity and treat more patients in UK NHS Trusts. Attendees will gain insights into the practical application of this powerful alliance and why this innovative approach is vital for the future of healthcare. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Reinvent cloud security with runtime and AI (sponsored by Upwind)
abstract: This session explores the evolution of cloud security and why traditional approaches fall short in the era of ephemeral compute and agentic AI. While legacy CloudSec relied on static scanning for visibility, today’s environments are dynamic, real-time, and increasingly autonomous, resulting in blind spots, excessive noise, and incomplete protection. We’ll examine how AI-driven and hybrid cloud architectures introduce new challenges across visibility, protection, and validation, from cross-provider gaps to real-time attack vectors and model vulnerabilities. To address this, Cloud and AI security must move beyond static analysis to a unified, runtime-driven approach. By continuously monitoring activity across the environment and embedding security throughout the SDLC, including production, organizations gain real-time context, better prioritization, and proactive threat mitigation. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

title: Reliable data processing with AWS serverless services
speaker: Ash Naik, Elizabeth Davis
abstract: In this chalk talk, learn how to optimize your serverless data processing workflows at scale. We cover AWS Step Functions Distributed Map for massive parallel batch processing and AWS Lambda durable functions for durable execution workflows. See how to combine these with Lambda event source mappings for stream and queue processing. We discuss cost optimization strategies and when to choose each approach for your data workload.

title: Renaissance Dad: building an agentic learning app for my 9-year-old with Kiro
speaker: Sylvain Bruas
abstract: Werner Vogels told us to become Renaissance Developers — curious polymaths who blend disciplines and own what they build. I took it literally: as a dad, I used Kiro and agentic AI to build a learning app that helps my 9-year-old practice math and school lessons. In this session, I'll share the full architecture: an OCR agent that imports exercises from photos of school notebooks, an adaptive agent that personalizes difficulty, and a coaching agent that guides instead of correcting. We'll deep-dive into multi-agent orchestration patterns, vision model integration, spec-driven development with Kiro, and the guardrails required when your end user is a child. Attendees will leave with reusable agentic patterns applicable far beyond education.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Replacing eligibility rules engines with Neurosymbolic AI in HHS
speaker: Nafi Colette Diallo, Max Clements
abstract: State HHS agencies spend hundreds of millions maintaining eligibility rules engines built on Drools or proprietary tooling. These systems are brittle, expensive, and impossible to audit. We built a different path: Ingesting policy, using Large Language Models, and building a formal logic representation, followed by using neurosymbolic techniques to produce a verified rule set, enabling deterministic eligibility decisions with full audit trails. No hallucinations. Provable correctness. We walk through the architecture, show a working prototype processing SNAP and Medicaid policy, discuss pricing at scale, and share early results from state engagements.

title: Reshape AI-driven software development for your startup with harness engineering
speaker: Simran Singh, Rutwik Bangali
abstract: Startups build software with AI coding agents, but new models ship every few weeks, and open-weight models rival frontier ones at a fraction of the cost. An agent is a combination of the model along with a harness: the context, tools, deterministic checks, and human decision points. In this session, we will walk you through how a lean team can build a thin configurable harness incrementally, enabling them to swap models underneath as needed and build context from continual learning loops. You'll leave knowing what to set up first, when to let agents run autonomously, and what decisions stay human.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Resilience patterns for the disconnected edge with Amazon Leo
speaker: Nick Matthews, Adam Palmer
abstract: Every resilient system eventually has to answer one question: what happens when the network you depend on isn’t there? In this session we discuss Amazon Leo, a low earth orbit satellite connectivity service, as a forcing function to explore patterns for architecting across unreliable, high-latency, and intermittently connected links. We’ll walk through the trade-offs behind routing, data-in-transit security, and where to place compute when bandwidth is scarce and connectivity is a variable. We’ll ground the discussion in hybrid resiliency and edge data collection for AI/ML, but the takeaway is portable to any architecture spanning boundaries you don’t fully control.

title: Resilience starts where your assumptions end, feat. Autodesk
speaker: Zaiba Jamadar, John Formento, Jason Niemczyk
abstract: The challenge most companies face is knowing where they stand with resilience, being willing to validate their assumptions safely, and disciplined enough to continuously improve without slowing delivery. In this session, we walk through Autodesk's journey with resilience testing and automated recovery failover as proof that investing in validation pays off, and you leave with a repeatable lifecycle for turning your own assumptions into proven capabilities. Discover how the next-generation AWS Resilience Hub handles the tedious work like mapping dependencies, assessing posture, and preconfiguring resilience tests, leaving your teams to focus on closing the gap between the system you think you operate and the one you actually do.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Resilience strategies and insights
abstract: Whether you're just getting started on your resilience journey or looking to take it to the next level, pull up a chair and talk shop with AWS resilience experts. This is an open opportunity to ask questions and explore new strategies for elevating your organization's resilience. Dive into disaster recovery strategies, discuss how to leverage AI to assess and test the resilience of your end-to-end services — everything is on the table. Bring your questions, talk to our experts, and leave with practical ideas you can put to work right away.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Resilient by design: Last Mile and Multicloud Interconnect
speaker: Steve Bruggeman, Donald Quindardo
abstract: Connecting a data center, a branch office, or another cloud to AWS has meant weeks of partner coordination, cross-connects, BGP configuration, and redundancy you design. AWS Interconnect - last mile and AWS Interconnect - multicloud move that work into the AWS Console and API, with resilient design built in. We start with the AWS Direct Connect building blocks and whiteboard what changes. You stop ordering cross-connects, configuring BGP, and designing redundancy. You still choose where it connects: a virtual private gateway, AWS Transit Gateway, or AWS Cloud WAN. Bring your hybrid and multicloud challenges.

title: Resilient Cloud Ops: From IaC to Fault Injection
speaker: Joel Medois
abstract: Production infrastructure needs two guarantees: repeatable deployment and proven resilience. In this bootcamp, use AWS CDK and CloudFormation to define and provision cloud resources as code, eliminating manual configuration drift. Then validate your architecture under stress. Troubleshoot VPC connectivity using flow logs, inject controlled faults with AWS Fault Injection Service, and confirm your infrastructure recovers gracefully. Deploy it right, then prove it holds.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom III

title: Resilient VLM Training at Scale on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
speaker: Roy Allela, Aravind Neelakantan
abstract: Training vision-language models at scale fails in predictable ways — node crashes mid-epoch, checkpoints corrupt, and GPU clusters sit idle during recovery. In this hands-on workshop, build resilient VLM training pipelines on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that survive real-world failures. Configure automatic health monitoring and node replacement, implement fault-tolerant checkpointing strategies, and design distributed training topologies that resume without losing progress. Using open-source frameworks on multi-node GPU clusters, you'll train a VLM end-to-end while simulating and recovering from infrastructure failures. Leave with battle-tested patterns for keeping large-scale training runs alive.

title: Resolve Amazon ECS incidents faster with AWS DevOps Agent
speaker: Olawale Olaleye, Premdass Ravidass, Yaki Ratz, Bharath Gajendran, Rajalakshmi Ramasubramanian
abstract: Incident investigation on Amazon ECS means correlating signals across task logs, service events, deployment history, and CloudWatch metrics - scattered data that takes hours to piece together. In this builders session, deploy AWS DevOps Agent against an ECS workload and experience autonomous incident response. The agent discovers your service topology, receives CloudWatch alarms, investigates autonomously by testing hypotheses against telemetry data, and delivers root cause analysis with specific remediation steps. Practice the full workflow from alarm to resolution without manually searching a single dashboard. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Builders' Session

title: Resolve it all: Build hybrid DNS architectures on AWS
speaker: Kunj Thacker, Mevlit Mustafa
abstract: Your enterprise runs workloads across multiple Amazon VPCs while maintaining connectivity to on-premises data centers, and DNS is the glue holding it all together. In this workshop, build a realistic hybrid DNS architecture using the latest Amazon Route 53 capabilities. Participants will learn how to centralize DNS configurations with Route 53 Profiles, replace conditional forwarding rules with native delegation using Resolver Delegation Endpoints, and detect and block DNS-based threats with DNS Firewall. Bring your laptop and resolve hybrid DNS once and for all.

title: Resolving and Preventing Production Incidents with AWS DevOps Agent
speaker: Ryan Gallaway, Vicente Aguilar
abstract: AWS DevOps Agent investigates production incidents end-to-end: tracing failures to the responsible change, guiding the fix, and verifying recovery. Once the service is stable, the agent converts root cause findings into automated prevention rules that enforce mandatory review gates on the same class of risk in future deployments. In this SimuLearn session, experience the full investigate, resolve, and prevent lifecycle as one continuous workflow in a single session.

title: Responsible AI Enablement: Balancing Innovation, Governance and Control (sponsored by Island)
abstract: Most organizations are currently stuck between two worlds: the urgent need to adopt AI to remain competitive, & the critical mandate to protect corporate data & reputation. AI is evolving faster than any tool in IT history, and faster than any organization can keep up with. The temptation to simply block access to AI is strong, but just saying "No" means ceding the advantage to those able to say "Yes!". The 3 Pillars of a "Secure Yes": Visibility: Knowing what AI is being used across the org. Accountability: Defining who owns the data & the output. Resilience: Building frameworks that adapt as regulations change. In this session, we will outline the framework for secure AI adoption. We will move past the hype to discuss how leaders can build visibility, maintain accountability, and foster a culture of responsible innovation. This presentation is brought to you by Island, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Rethinking Agentic Security: How Cyera Scaled AI Securely in Days (sponsored by Cyera)
speaker: Joe Tustin
abstract: As AI shifts from assistive systems to autonomous agents, data becomes the control surface. Agents need a goldilocks balance of data, identity, and process access: enough to be effective, too much and you end up on Twitter. Cyera solved this internally, reaching 88% weekly AI usage across engineering and non-engineering teams in 17 days. Adoption was not the hard part. The wiring was. How do you govern access and give builders a permit path so they ship instead of wait? Join us for what we learned, and what it means on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Rethinking the AWS SDK for Python: Async, streaming, and more
speaker: Alessandra Romero, Jonathan Gaytan
abstract: If you've ever wrapped boto3 in asyncio, juggled thread pools for concurrent AWS calls, or wished for proper streaming support, this session is for you. With the new AWS SDK for Python, async is native, concurrent calls no longer require thread-pool workarounds, and bidirectional streaming enables use cases like live transcription and speech-to-speech that go beyond what's available in boto3 today. Follow along as we put those capabilities to work with clean concurrent calls, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Transcribe streaming, and a practical path to migrating your own code to the new SDK.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Rethinking the boundary between messaging and streaming
speaker: Stephan Schiller, Marco Jahn
abstract: Modern event-driven architectures still separate cleanly into "queues" and "streams," but real workloads no longer do. Requirements like replay, ordering, high throughput and more, increasingly appear across both patterns, making the wrong service choice costly to unwind. This session explores the architectural spectrum across messaging and streaming systems, drawing on services such as Amazon SQS, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon MSK. Throughout the talk we will build a real world architecture and will provide guidance when to choose messaging, streaming or a hybrid approach, and which trade-offs matter most.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Rethink release management for the agentic coding era
speaker: Arun KM, Carl Caum
abstract: GitOps was designed for human-speed change. Agentic coding tools now generate pull requests faster than any team can review and safely release. Your release process is the new bottleneck. In this code talk, we'll live-code a GitOps release workflow where AWS DevOps Agent acts as an intelligent release manager, validating the results through a release pipeline at every promotion gate. Instead of manual approvals, DevOps Agent uses production intelligence (runtime dependencies, service health, deployment risk) to make real-time go/no-go decisions. Learn how to wire DevOps Agent into your GitOps reconciliation loop so releases match the velocity of agentic code generation without sacrificing safety.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Right Compute, right time, right price: A decision framework for HPC and AI at scale
speaker: Sudhi Bhat, Avi Kulkarni
abstract: Large-scale HPC and AI workloads share the same hard problem: getting the right compute, at the right time, at the right price. In this chalk talk, we cover the architecture and provisioning decisions that matter when you move beyond a single instance. Architecture side: cluster design for distributed AI training and tightly coupled HPC simulation, networking trade-offs and where CPUs (x86, Graviton) fit alongside GPUs in production pipelines. Provisioning side: Capacity Blocks for predictable GPU bursts, On-Demand Capacity Reservations for sustained workloads, Spot for fault-tolerant jobs, and Savings Plans for steady-state fleets. We share real customer examples leveraging Amazon EC2 across HPC and AI/ML. Bring your hardest capacity and cost questions.

title: Right-size and scale Amazon ECS with effective autoscaling patterns
speaker: Debojit Bhadra, Shalabh Srivastava
abstract: Autoscaling containerized workloads means scaling both tasks and the infrastructure underneath them. This chalk talk explores Amazon ECS autoscaling patterns including target tracking, step scaling, and scheduled scaling across AWS Fargate and Amazon ECS Managed Instances. Understand how these patterns interact with capacity providers so you can balance performance against cost. Discuss right-sizing tasks, handling traffic spikes, and avoiding over-provisioning. Bring your scaling challenges for an interactive technical discussion.

This chalk talk explores Amazon ECS autoscaling patterns including target tracking, step scaling, and scheduled scaling across AWS Fargate and Amazon ECS Managed Instances. Understand how these patterns interact with capacity providers so you can balance performance against cost. Discuss right-sizing tasks, handling traffic spikes, and avoiding over-provisioning. Bring your scaling challenges for an interactive technical discussion.

title: Right-size your observability: maximize signal, minimize spend
speaker: Kevin Fallis, Raj Ramasubbu
abstract: Your telemetry is scattered across tools. Your storage costs keep climbing. Your AI agents are a black box. In this chalk talk, we'll tackle your problems head-on with Amazon OpenSearch Service. Bring your toughest scenarios. Ask how our purpose-built log analytics engine reduces cost while boosting query performance. Ask how to unify logs, traces, and metrics into a single OpenTelemetry-native pane of glass with cost efficiency. If you're building AI agents, ask how to trace LLM calls, track per-invocation cost, and debug multi-agent workflows. And for any workload, ask how to stack cost levers like right-sizing, tiered storage, and writeable warm to maximize savings.
