title: Right tool, right layer: Combining ML models and autonomous agents
speaker: Kinnera Vajjala, Chetan Sharma
abstract: Financial institutions deploy dozens of models and manual workflows that struggle to work together at scale. Machine learning excels at fast, explainable decisions while agentic AI orchestrates multi-step workflows with reasoning and adaptability. Real value is knowing when to use each and combining them into one system. In this chalk talk, we present a decision framework and demonstrate an architecture where machine learning models score and detect while agents reason, act, and close the loop while delivering the auditability regulators require. We walk through a Know Your Customer (KYC) example, then open the floor. Bring your use case.

title: Rise of Autonomous Clinical Data Management: AI Agents Accelerating Drug Development (sponsored by Cognizant)
speaker: Nareen Katta, Gaurav Sharma
abstract: Explore how autonomous AI agents are transforming clinical data management from a collection of manual processes into an intelligent, continuously learning system that improves quality, accelerates study execution, and shortens the path from protocol to patient impact. Clinical trials generate unprecedented volumes of complex data, yet many Clinical Data Management (CDM) processes remain highly manual, resource-intensive, and constrained by siloed workflows. Critical activities such as protocol interpretation, clinical trial data systems build and configuration, edit check generation, data review, data quality management, reconciliation, and database lock often reside on the critical path to study completion. This presentation is brought to you by Cognizant, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Rivian's journey to Multi-Availability Zone factory resilience on AWS Outposts
speaker: Peter Dachnowicz, Adam Shake
abstract: Discover why Rivian chose AWS Outposts to support mission-critical manufacturing applications that produce vehicles at its Normal, Illinois, plant. Explore how Rivian architected highly redundant infrastructure across multiple Outposts racks, using fast Amazon EC2 provisioning and scaling to meet production line demands. This session covers Multi-Availability Zone deployment for high availability, Amazon RDS read replicas across racks for database resilience, and AWS Unified Operations for proactive observability across its hybrid environment. Learn how Rivian plans to scale this model into its 9-million-square-foot mega factory in Georgia.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Road to re:Invent
abstract: Watch Road to re:Invent | The official re:Invent Hackathon in-person and on livestream, starting at 12 PM. Get up front as teams compete in an in-person hackathon where the pressure is on. Be sure to catch the Special Guests, VIP Cameos, and the thrilling finale where these talented developers showcase their innovative solutions and one team will be crowned 2026 champion walking away with $100K. Don't miss the excitement as we celebrate the creativity of building and technical excellence of the AWS community.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: Robinhood: Scaling in-app agentic trading to every investor on AWS
speaker: Viraj Padte, Sreeram Ramji, Chirantan Mahipal
abstract: How does Amazon combine people, AI and robots to get new sites ready? Hear how Amazon Robotics runs thousands of autonomous mobile robots on one shared map, and recovers lost robots with agents on Amazon Bedrock. Then follow a pilot that takes last year's computer-vision readiness checks, built with Amazon Nova on Bedrock, from a tablet to a humanoid robot that walks a site and scans each station, so people can focus on the decisions. We go deep on the AWS architecture, from edge navigation to a serverless backend, and share what broke, what we learned and patterns you can reuse.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Route, cache, and batch: a multi-model decision framework on Bedrock
speaker: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan, Chris Greenwood
abstract: Treating every request the same is what makes inference expensive at scale, and most of that cost is repeat work you already paid for. This chalk talk whiteboards how prompt caching on Amazon Bedrock eliminates redundant computation across system prompts, shared context, and multi-turn conversations, then shows where Intelligent Prompt Routing and batch inference extend the savings further. We walk through cache-hit economics, how to structure prompts for maximum reuse, and when routing or batching is the better lever. Bring your traffic patterns and questions, and leave with a caching-first cost strategy tuned to your workloads.

title: Route or escalate: Confidence boundaries in multi-domain AI agents
speaker: Roland Barcia, Kandha Sankarapandian
abstract: Building a GenAI system that answers questions across technology domains is straightforward — until the model doesn't know the answer and doesn't say so. For builders designing multi-agent or RAG-based systems, this session presents the confidence-gated routing architecture: classifying every query into high-confidence retrieval, low-confidence escalation to a human specialist, or cross-domain composition. We cover why flat vector retrieval fails multi-domain queries, the trade-offs of graph-based knowledge ontology, and the evaluations framework measuring confidence calibration. Walk away with a routing pattern you can apply any time your AI system must self-report uncertainty rather than hallucinate with authority.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Routing events at scale with Amazon EventBridge
speaker: Patrick Meiler, David Roberts
abstract: Amazon EventBridge simplifies event routing for distributed applications. In this chalk talk, we show how to centralize multi-account event routing without custom infrastructure, using the enhanced custom event bus. We will discuss routing policies, event discovery with schema registry, and access controls that let platform teams govern while app teams move independently. We also explore rate limiting and backpressure so your applications gracefully handle traffic spikes and protect downstream systems without losing events. Along the way, we highlight new multi-account patterns the enhanced custom event bus enables.

title: Run AI on GPUs and accelerators with Amazon ECS Managed Instances
speaker: Raphael Beamonte, Abhishek Nautiyal, Olly Pomeroy
abstract: Running AI and ML workloads in containers means choosing the right accelerator, keeping it busy, and scaling without paying for idle capacity or keeping users waiting. Amazon ECS Managed Instances manages the infrastructure lifecycle, so you can add GPUs and other accelerators to new or existing ECS clusters. In this session, examine architecture patterns and best practices for batch, event-driven and real-time AI workloads. Learn how to right-size accelerator capacity, run smaller models on fractional GPUs, reduce cold starts, scale to zero when there is no work, and recover from hardware failures. Hear how a customer built and scaled their production AI infrastructure on Amazon ECS Managed Instances, and leave with patterns you can apply to your own clusters.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Run hybrid multi-cloud networks with one operational model (sponsored by Selector AI)
speaker: Michael Bonnett Jr
abstract: Most enterprises run workloads across AWS, other clouds, and on-premises data centers, and each environment brings its own tools, data model, and telemetry. When an application becomes unreachable, operators rebuild the network path by hand across consoles during the incident. Follow a financial services network team that set out to run AWS, Google Cloud, and its data centers as one network. Explore the architecture behind that model: unified collection, a common resource identity, resource groupings, a single alarm lifecycle, and deterministic path tracing. See it applied to one incident, and leave with design patterns for any cloud operations stack.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Running AI agents you can trust on Amazon EKS
speaker: Carlos Santana, Matthew Meckes
abstract: AI agents are rapidly moving from prototype to production, and running them at scale presents new challenges. Untrusted, AI-generated code executes in your environment. Many agents share the same infrastructure. Workloads spin up, act, and tear down constantly. Join this session to learn how to run agents securely on Amazon EKS with VM-level isolation, wire up the primitives agents need for tools, memory, and orchestration, and manage fleets of short-lived, bursty workloads. You'll also see how the same EKS platform you run your critical workloads on extends into the agentic era and where we're headed next.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Running compute-efficient workloads on Amazon EKS Auto Mode
speaker: Erez Zarum, Dmitry Nutels
abstract: Amazon EKS Auto Mode, powered by open source Karpenter, simplifies infrastructure management while optimizing compute resources. Karpenter provisions Amazon EC2 Instances based on the requirements of your workload. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll gain practical experience in advanced workload scheduling, continually compute optimization with Karpenter consolidation, explore AWS Graviton and AWS spare capacity through Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Whether you’re new to EKS Auto Mode, or an experienced operator you’ll learn best practices for running efficient workloads on Amazon EKS while simplifying Kubernetes cluster management.

title: Running untrusted code in sandboxes with AWS Lambda MicroVMs
speaker: Thiago Pádua, Daniel Abib, Raphael Lima, Sathya Shanmugha, Ayush Kulkarni
abstract: AI coding assistants generate code. Customers upload plugins. Third parties submit extensions. All of it needs to run somewhere and that somewhere can't be your production environment. In this builders' session, use AWS Lambda MicroVMs to build secure sandboxes that execute untrusted code at scale with hardware-level tenant isolation. You'll configure sandbox lifecycle management, implement resource limits and permissions boundaries, and test failure modes when code misbehaves. Walk away with a working isolation architecture you can adapt for your own multi-tenant workloads. Bring your laptop.

title: Running Vercel in Your Own AWS Account (sponsored by Vercel)
speaker: Brandon Tuttle, Glenn Phillips
abstract: This session explores how Vercel Enterprise customers can run workloads in their own AWS account while continuing to use the Vercel developer experience. You’ll learn about the separation between the Vercel control plane and customer runtime, and why this model can help organizations meet data privacy, security, and compliance requirements. You’ll see how the setup works through a live walkthrough and demo, and how this architecture can support broader access to tools like v0, Amazon Q, and other coding agents. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Run With the Best AMD in the Cloud — What's New and What's Next
abstract: 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors now power six EC2 instance families on AWS: general purpose (M8a), compute-optimized (C8a), memory-optimized (R8a), high-frequency (M8azn), large-memory EDA (X8aedz), and HPC (Hpc8a). All deliver up to 30% better performance and 19% better price-performance than previous generations — with M8azn and X8aedz offering the highest CPU frequency in the cloud at 5 GHz. In this meetup, we'll walk through the full 8th-gen AMD portfolio, share real-world performance data including CPU-based inference workloads, and we'll discuss a bit of the future.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Run your largest SAP HANA on AWS: EC2 High Memory deep dive
speaker: Vikas Ratna, Linda Wang
abstract: Running SAP HANA at scale requires infrastructure that matches the size and criticality of your enterprise resource planning (ERP) workloads. Amazon EC2 High Memory instances deliver up to 32 TB of memory in a single instance today, backed by the AWS Nitro architecture for consistent performance and hardware-level isolation. In this session, we dive deep into why customers choose High Memory instances for SAP HANA and the benefits they have gained from modernizing their ERP on AWS. Hear how enterprises are scaling production ERP to 32 TB to gain performance and improve operational efficiency, and walk away with architectural guidance and real-world deployment patterns for running your largest SAP HANA workloads in a scale-up configuration.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: S3 Cost Clinic: Architecting for Scale Without Overspending
abstract: S3 makes storing data easy, but controlling costs at scale requires architectural decisions. This interactive meetup uses real-world scenarios to explore storage classes, lifecycle policies, access patterns, retention, retrieval, replication, and monitoring. Attendees will diagnose an unexpected S3 cost increase, compare architecture options, and discuss the trade-offs between cost, performance, and availability. Rather than a presentation, the session is a collaborative “S3 Cost Clinic” where builders can challenge assumptions, share approaches, and learn from different perspectives. Each scenario provides practical patterns attendees can take back to their own AWS environments.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: SaaS Agents Anywhere
speaker: Erik Anderson, Anthony McClure
abstract: Customers make deliberate choices about where their workloads run. For SaaS vendors delivering agentic products, that means the runtime has to meet the workload where it is, not the other way around. This chalk talk teaches the everywhere agent pattern for SaaS: keep the control plane on AWS, run the agent runtime and data-plane execution wherever the customer's data lives. Learn three decisions: which destinations to support and when (multi-cloud, on-prem, or both), how to run agent runtimes outside AWS without rewriting your control plane (packaging, model backend selection, dependency portability), and how to manage identity, observability, and lifecycle across environments you don't own. Leave with the decision framework for shipping SaaS agents anywhere the customer's data lives.

title: SaaS Agents Anywhere: building distributed agentic deployments
speaker: Markus Doepke, Hasan Tariq
abstract: SaaS vendors deploy agents across a spectrum: fully provider-hosted, fully tenant-controlled, and hybrid models in between. Once customers have data residency or cost-visibility requirements, deployment topology determines the operational pattern. In this workshop, build a distributed agentic deployment on AWS spanning your accounts and a tenant's, then exercise the three concerns that surface everywhere on the spectrum: lifecycle management of agents you can't directly see, observability across account boundaries, and reliability when the agent runs somewhere you don't operate. Leave with a working reference deployment you can adapt to your own tenancy model.

title: Safer, simpler, faster upgrades with managed blue/green deployments
speaker: Paola Lorusso, Ryan Shevchik
abstract: Blue/green deployments for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS simplify the process of upgrading and performing maintenance on your databases. In this chalk talk, you will architect a blue/green database upgrade solution to support major or minor engine version upgrades and perform schema changes with minimal and predictable downtime. Active participation is encouraged as you architect a solution to meet your requirements. In open discussion, learn the trade-offs involved in database management when using blue/green deployments and how to design the most effective upgrade solution to meet your needs.

title: Same code, any compute: Portable architecture on AWS
speaker: Daniel Abib, Rafael Barbosa, Nicolas Tarzia, Swarna Kunnath, Michael Costa
abstract: Your business logic shouldn't be coupled to a compute service. In this session, apply Hexagonal Architecture and 12-factor patterns to design workloads where compute is a deployment decision, not an architectural one. Through live code, see the same logic packaged as a Lambda function, a Fargate task, and an EKS pod using AWS Lambda Web Adapter and runtime-neutral handler patterns. You'll learn where portability pays off, where it adds unnecessary abstraction, and how to evaluate the trade-offs between pay-per-request, always-on containers, and orchestrated clusters for your workloads.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Same Query, Different Results: AI Agents for Migration Validation
abstract: Matching row counts does not guarantee a successful database migration. What happens when reports disagree because of rounding, NULL handling, timestamps, or duplicate records? Join data engineers, database specialists, and architects to discuss agent-assisted migration validation using Amazon Bedrock and Strands Agents. Explore how agents could select comparison tools, investigate discrepancies, and assemble evidence for human review. Through realistic SQL migration scenarios and small-group discussion, attendees will compare validation strategies, read-only access boundaries, and ways to evaluate an agent’s explanations. Bring a migration challenge and exchange ideas for making validation more systematic.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Sandboxing AI Agents on EKS: Isolation That Scales
speaker: Adit Modi, Ishan Modi
abstract: AI agents execute untrusted code — one prompt injection away from data exfiltration. This session covers building graduated isolation for autonomous agents on EKS using the agent-sandbox controller. You'll learn why runtime tiers (runc → gVisor → Firecracker) map to different threat models, how SandboxClaim resources manage ephemeral agent lifecycle, and Cilium FQDN egress filtering that prevents exfiltration without blocking legitimate tool use. We'll whiteboard Karpenter NodePool design for gVisor-capable nodes, discuss cost tradeoffs between isolation levels, and share what breaks when you over-isolate. Leave with a production-ready isolation framework.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: SAST Is Dead: Program Analysis for AI Agents (sponsored by Semgrep)
speaker: Daghan Altas
abstract: LLMs didn't kill security testing, they exposed tools that guess at context they don't have. This talk explains what we learned by reinventing program analysis for new end users: builders and agents. We had to develop benchmarks and add determinism with program slicing to better control costs and deliver the optimal price per true vulnerability detected. This presentation is brought to you by Semgrep, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Scalable LLM inference, easy on the ops: CrowdStrike on SageMaker AI
speaker: Felipe Lopez, Vivek Singh, Ruxandra-Maria Caba
abstract: When adversaries move in seconds, security has to move faster. CrowdStrike shares how they built scalable, real time LLM inference on Amazon SageMaker to power threat detection at massive scale, where sub second latency is a hard requirement. Learn how dedicated, configurable endpoints gave them full control over performance, while SageMaker AI's managed infrastructure removed the operational overhead.​
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Scale agentic development with automated orchestration
speaker: Rodrigo Azevedo, mac Merritt, Romain Dura
abstract: As you delegate more complex development work to AI agents, manual coordination can limit how much you can take on. Learn how to automate multi-agent orchestration to reduce supervision while maintaining your quality standards. This session explores patterns for dividing work among focused agents and building reusable processes that include verification. Through examples from the Kiro team and HERE Technologies, see how these principles apply in Kiro workflows and learn the trade-offs in context management, execution time, and cost.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Scale AI-powered software development securely with Bedrock
speaker: Sriharsha M S, Pedro Javier Paez, Jose Navarro
abstract: Your dev teams are adopting AI coding agents fast: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and more. Without a shared control plane, every team rolls its own auth, cost tracking, and rules. In this builders session, build one control plane using Amazon Bedrock and LiteLLM that manages all of them. Route every agent's model calls through Bedrock and enforce your security policies in one place. Apply consistent identity, observability, and cost controls across every agent, then put it to work on a real coding task.

title: Scale data for RAG and AI agents cost-effectively with Amazon S3 Vectors
speaker: Venkata Sistla, Dhanika Sujan
abstract: Discover how S3 Vectors transforms retrieval workloads for AI agents and RAG pipelines with native vector storage and query capabilities. This session explores recent enhancements that deliver deeper, more comprehensive search results per query while dramatically reducing costs at scale, reducing the need for multiple round trips while running large-scale RAG, semantic search, and AI workloads. Learn architecture best practices, performance optimization techniques, and diverse vector use cases, from semantic search to large-scale RAG implementations.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Scale financial Risk and Quant Research with AWS Batch and Amazon ECS
speaker: Boris Litvin, Matthieu Bonville
abstract: Financial institutions run millions of simulations overnight to price options, stress-test portfolios, and satisfy regulators. Scaling those workloads means balancing queue depth against compute cost. AWS Batch on Amazon ECS eliminates that tradeoff — containers scale elastically, Spot instances cut compute cost, and job orchestration handles retries and memory tuning without custom scripts. In this chalk talk, walk through a production architecture where a quantitative hedge fund runs its entire research compute on AWS Batch. Then open the whiteboard and discuss how to apply these patterns to your own pricing engines, VaR calculations, or scenario analysis workloads.

title: Scale, optimize and deploy inference with Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode
speaker: Erez Zarum, Sheetal Joshi
abstract: Accelerated workloads make node provisioning challenging. Picking the wrong instance, scheduling constraint, or disruption policy impacts GPU utilization and drives up costs. This deep dive covers how Amazon EKS provisions and scales accelerated compute for real inference workloads, whether you run managed Auto Mode or self-managed Karpenter. See how both select across GPU and accelerator families and honor topology-aware scheduling. Learn the NodePool and disruption settings that keep utilization high without hurting latency-sensitive serving. Discover how Dynamic Resource Allocation and GPU sharing squeeze more inference out of every device, plus accelerator-aware node repair that keeps long-running jobs healthy.

title: Scale production agents reliably with AgentCore
speaker: Shishir Bharathi, Satveer Khurpa
abstract: What changes when you go from ten agent sessions to ten thousand? In this chalk talk, whiteboard the architectural and operational patterns that determine whether your agents perform reliably at scale. Discuss microVM isolation for secure multi-tenancy, elastic scaling that handles traffic spikes without capacity planning, and long-running task handling with human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Cover resiliency patterns: what happens when a tool call fails, how to handle model timeouts, and designing for graceful degradation. Walk through the infrastructure decisions you make once and benefit from forever. Bring your scaling scenarios and we architect solutions together.

title: Scale Through Partners: The Partner-Led SMB Growth Engine
speaker: Ethel Garcia Simon Matachana
abstract: SMB is a $1T opportunity—98% of global businesses are small/mid-size, 81% are increasing AI spend, yet fewer than 300 AWS partners hold the SMB Competency. This session unpacks AWS's Indirect Selling engine: new incentives aligned to growth, AI-powered lead generation, SMB solution selling, and a Partnership Maturity Framework turning opportunistic engagement into repeatable business practice. You'll leave with unit economics proving indirect selling reaches SMBs globally, a clear activation timeline from Opportunity through full Business Practice, and specific first moves to build a scalable, profitable SMB practice on AWS—your 20-minute roadmap to outsized growth.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Scale your coding agents beyond the laptop with AgentCore
speaker: Aravind Subramanian, Sanghwa Na
abstract: Developers want Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro with laptop-like feel but without laptop limits: no parallelism, no persistence, no isolation. In this hands-on workshop, you will deploy a coding agent to AgentCore's runtime in three commands, then build real workflows: a code review agent, PR automation, and a repo consolidation job. You will run agents in parallel across isolated microVMs, persist and share state with BYO S3 and EFS, connect models through Bedrock, and wire an agent to wake on GitHub events and work in the background. Leave with working code you can drop straight into your own repos.

title: Scaling agent memory with Amazon S3 Vectors and S3 Files
speaker: Samyak Kathane, Venkata Sistla
abstract: Persistent, scalable memory is foundational to production AI agents. In this session, learn how the combination of S3 Vectors and S3 Files provides a unified memory layer for agents by using S3 Vectors for embedding-based semantic recall and S3 Files for low-latency, mutable working memory and shared state across agent sessions. We’ll cover architecture patterns for short-term and long-term memory, multi-agent memory sharing, and managing memory lifecycle and cost as usage grows, including how recent S3 Vectors enhancements improve retrieval economics at scale. Leave with patterns for memory architectures that scale to millions of agent interactions.

title: Scaling AI agents: How Forlex turned failures into mechanisms
speaker: Danilo Muniz
abstract: Forlex uses production failures to set boundaries for 150+ AI agents operating in regulated workflows. Silent regressions, runaway tail latency, and privilege creep emerged as Forlex scaled its agent fleet. This session covers how Forlex turned each failure into a durable mechanism, covering the guardrails, monitoring, and operational practices that let them scale agents safely in production.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Scaling AI Defenses with AWS and CrowdStrike (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
speaker: Rob Solomon, Drew Curd
abstract: AI is accelerating innovation — and accelerating attackers. From prompt injection and data exfiltration to cloud privilege escalation, adversaries are increasingly exploiting AI-powered architectures to move faster than traditional defenses. In this session, AWS and CrowdStrike experts will demonstrate how organizations can securely build and defend modern AI workloads running on AWS. Attendees will explore real-world architectures using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore and see how attackers move across identity, cloud, and AI services to exploit security gaps. Through live demonstrations and architectural guidance, the session will show how AWS and CrowdStrike help organizations surface shadow AI; visualize attack paths across code and AI services; stop AI-specific attacks; automate protection workflows; and deliver real-time cloud detection and response (CDR) across modern AI environments. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Scaling and securing MCP Servers with AWS Load Balancing and WAF
speaker: Eitav Arditti, Max Hausner
abstract: MCP servers are becoming essential infrastructure in enterprise AI environments, and running them in production demands both scalability and security. Join this chalk talk to explore patterns for scaling and securing your MCP servers using AWS native services. We'll cover how to configure Application Load Balancer for MCP traffic characteristics, implement health checks and routing policies, and scale horizontally across availability zones. We'll also cover how to enforce security controls with AWS WAF, including request filtering, rate limiting, and tool-level access policies. Whether you're running a handful of MCP servers or deploying at enterprise scale, you'll leave with actionable architectures for production-ready deployments.

abstract: MCP servers are becoming essential infrastructure in enterprise AI environments, and running them in production demands both scalability and security. Join this chalk talk to explore patterns for scaling and securing your MCP servers using AWS native services. We'll cover how to configure Application Load Balancer for MCP traffic characteristics, implement health checks and routing policies, and scale horizontally across availability zones. We'll also cover how to enforce security controls with AWS WAF, including request filtering, rate limiting, and tool-level access policies. Whether you're running a handful of MCP servers or deploying at enterprise scale, you'll leave with actionable architectures for production-ready deployments.

title: Scaling data and AI products in the enterprise
abstract: Organizations are moving quickly to adopt data mesh and data and AI product architectures across large, federated enterprises. Yet many are running into familiar challenges with governance, organizational silos, and broader data dysfunction. In this meetup, we’ll share real-world stories and discuss what’s working, what’s not, and how organizations are combining technology and process to establish effective governance and drive meaningful business outcomes.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Scaling EC2 Spot with a focus on capacity, GPUs, and allocation
speaker: Sirena Akopyan, Chad Schmutzer
abstract: Today, organizations run ML training, inference, and large-scale simulations on Spot across CPU and GPU instance families. But scaling Spot successfully requires understanding how capacity actually behaves. In this session, the EC2 Spot product leader shares what the data reveals: which diversification strategies consistently deliver high fill rates, how allocation strategies differ for CPU vs. GPU workloads, and when tools like Spot Placement Score and EC2 Capacity Manager make the difference. You'll leave with a modern playbook covering instance diversification, multi-Region/AZ deployment, checkpointing for long-running jobs, and capacity rebalancing patterns the largest Spot customers use today.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Scaling ElastiCache globally: 500+ clusters & 1.3 trillion ops/day
speaker: Artem Zheltak, Vadym Voitiuk
abstract: Managing ride-hailing demand across 1,100+ cities and 8+ million daily transactions in real time requires scalable, resilient, sub-millisecond in-memory data operations. In this session, learn how inDrive evolved from a monolithic on-premises Redis OSS cluster to over 500 distributed Amazon ElastiCache clusters spanning 8 AWS Regions, executing 1.3 trillion operations daily. Discover how inDrive eliminated bottlenecks in single-CPU utilization, network saturation, and hotspot shards, and how a zero-downtime migration to the Valkey engine on ElastiCache improved performance and reduced costs. Learn a production-tested blueprint for scaling data-intensive systems across multiple AWS Regions.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Scaling Frontier AI model inference on AWS Trainium
speaker: Pinak Panigrahi, Achintya Pinninti, Andre Gomes
abstract: Every team moving AI to production hits the same wall: scaling frontier model inference against growing token demand, tighter latency budgets, and spiraling compute costs. This workshop tackles that problem head-on. See how purpose-built chips change the inference economics equation as you deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium, apply optimization techniques, and connect the Neuron software stack to familiar open-source frameworks without rewrites to achieve superior tokenomics. You will leave able to run performant, cost-effective frontier model inference in production on AWS Trainium yourself.

title: Scaling inference compute across clusters (sponsored by Baseten)
speaker: Colin McGrath
abstract: Your traffic outgrows a single cluster long before you expect it to. Colin McGrath explains how Baseten runs inference across more than 80 GPU clusters and roughly 15 cloud providers as one system: how capacity gets found and claimed, how requests get routed to the right region under real load, how large models get delivered to new clusters quickly, and how autoscaling behaves when traffic is bursty and cold starts are expensive. He covers what happens when a whole region goes down, and the patterns that matter most for teams scaling past one cluster. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Scaling interactive generative AI at Netflix with AWS Local Zones
speaker: Justin Rosen, Daniel Heckenberg, Mathew George
abstract: Generative AI VFX and Animation teams at Netflix require the latest GPU hardware for creative workflows, including real-time rendering, VFX editorial, and color correction. These workloads demand low-latency access to high-performance compute close to creative teams. AWS Local Zones make this possible by placing Amazon EC2 G7e instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs in the Los Angeles metro. Netflix's Studio GenAI Infrastructure, including GenAI Sessions and Universal Compute Service, uses Local Zones to serve just-in-time combinations of software and hardware in secure, isolated sandbox environments. Tools like ComfyUI and AI Toolkit with complex dependencies run on task-oriented, elastic GPU assignments, so Netflix scales creative AI workloads efficiently without managing physical infrastructure.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Scaling ISV Revenue: Accelerating Co-Sell with AWS Marketplace
speaker: Erin Smith
abstract: AWS Marketplace has become the fastest path for ISVs to scale co-sell, but unlocking its full potential means going beyond procurement and using it as the backbone of how you sell. This session unpacks how high-performing ISVs combine ISV Accelerate with AWS Marketplace to accelerate co-sell. Three points separate top performers: (1) structuring AWS seller alignment to generate Marketplace-routed pipeline, (2) using private offers and channel-partner workflows to compress enterprise deal cycles by 30-40%, and (3) mining Marketplace buyer signals to drive expansion and proactive renewal. Walk away with a focused playbook for turning Marketplace into a scalable revenue motion.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Scaling Multi-Account IAM at Netflix: Access, Visibility and Credentials
speaker: Jay Dhulia, Prateek Sharma
abstract: Managing IAM across a large, fast-growing AWS footprint quickly outgrows manual review — every permission change creates friction for engineers and queue time for operators. We'll cover a control-plane approach that ties together high-level IAM abstractions, automated workflows, and business context to drive the majority of AWS access needs. Developers describe intent against concrete resources instead of hand-writing JSON; Access Analyzer–backed probes auto-approve routine changes; administrators get a single pane of glass over SCPs, identity and resource policies, CloudTrail/S3 errors, and AWS Config history. Credential delivery flows through the same plane, enabling context-aware scoping for human and agentic callers alike.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: Scaling Multi-Cluster EKS Without Burning Your Infrastructure Budget
speaker: Sagar Utekar
abstract: Managing hundreds of Amazon EKS clusters breaks standard multi-tenant architectures under the weight of shared control planes, noisy neighbors, and runaway cross-AZ data transfer costs. This interactive chalk talk skips the slides to whiteboard the painful realities of multi-cluster fleet topology at scale. We will dissect the architectural trade-offs between monolithic clusters and localized micro-clusters, mapping out exact blast-radius constraints. Bring your worst infrastructure bottlenecks; we will openly debate cluster life-cycle automation, shared VPC patterns, and cost-allocation frameworks, leaving you with a battle-tested blueprint to optimize fleet operations on Monday morning.

title: Scaling operations with MCP, ACP, and A2A
speaker: Babu Samayapuram Suthanthira Raju, Jyothi Madanlal
abstract: Operational complexity doesn't scale linearly but your approach to managing it can. In this chalk talk, we'll use AWS DevOps Agent to explore three protocols shaping how operations teams work at scale: MCP (connecting to operational data and actions), ACP (delegating tasks to purpose-built agents), and A2A (coordinating across autonomous agents). We'll discuss how protocol choice affects decision-making, when to extend capabilities vs. delegate, and how to design architectures that grow with your operational footprint. Leave with a clear mental model for when to reach for each protocol and how they fit together.

room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan I

title: Scaling Pharma Transformation Through Data-Driven Agentic AI (sponsored by Tech Mahindra)
speaker: Deepak Gupta
abstract: Hear from a leading U.S. pharmaceutical company on its journey to transforming enterprise AI from isolated experiments into a scalable business capability. Discover how Tech Mahindra helped establish trusted data foundations, harness Agentic AI to enrich product and customer master data, unlock semantic intelligence, and create governed data products that power enterprise-wide insights, including drug demand forecasting. This session will explore the architectural principles, governance strategies, and leadership decisions required to scale compliant, trusted, and value-driven AI. Join Tech Mahindra and a pharma industry leader to learn how data-driven Agentic AI is reshaping the future of the intelligent pharma enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by Tech Mahindra, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Scaling website delivery with Amazon CloudFront: one configuration, many sites
speaker: Derek Ziehl, Evan Lecklider, Harith Gaddamanugu, David MacDonald, Kartik Bheemisetty
abstract: Most enterprises don’t run just one website, they run many: a corporate site, regional or sub-brand sites, plus internal portals for each. Managing TLS certificates, WAF rules, and cache behavior separately for every one creates configuration drift, inconsistent security posture, and operational overhead that scales with your site count. In this workshop, you’ll use Amazon CloudFront to define a single reusable baseline configuration and apply it consistently across many websites - whether they represent different brands, business units, or access levels - while still allowing targeted overrides where a site genuinely needs to differ (stricter WAF on internal portals, a custom origin for a sub-brand). You’ll leave with a working reference architecture and a decision framework for what belongs in the baseline vs. the override.

title: Secrets rotation patterns for agentic pipelines at scale
speaker: Enrico Bonaccorsi, Francesc Sala
abstract: Autonomous agents provision, consume, and rotate credentials without a human in the loop. In this chalk-talk, work through how to build a secrets lifecycle for multi-step agentic workflows: issue dynamic secrets using AWS temporary credentials and leverage AWS Secrets Manager for secrets rotation, Scope each agent with resource policies and VPC endpoint conditions to enforce a data perimeter, and apply AWS KMS envelope encryption so ephemeral secrets never persist in plaintext. Leave with deployable templates for zero-standing-privilege secret delivery across chained agent invocations.

title: Secure agents at scale on Amazon ECS with VM-level isolation
speaker: Ashok Srirama, Nick Peters
abstract: If you run agents, multi-tenant services, or regulated workloads on shared infrastructure, the isolation boundary is an important security consideration. This session shows how to design that boundary using VM-level isolation on Amazon ECS. You will leave knowing how to isolate tenants and untrusted agent workloads from one another, apply least-privilege execution toward compliance obligations, and run it all efficiently at scale. Whether you build agentic AI platforms or sensitive multi-tenant applications, you will walk away with a practical blueprint for strong isolation on ECS.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Secure AI Agent Access with AgentCore Identity
speaker: Amit Sukhwal
abstract: Not every caller should have access to your AI agents, and you should verify who is calling them before responding. In this hands-on lab, you deploy an IT help desk agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and configure AgentCore Identity to enforce inbound authentication. You set up an Amazon Cognito user pool as the identity provider, obtain and decode a JSON Web Token (JWT), and test that the agent rejects unauthenticated callers while allowing verified employees through.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Palace Ballroom II

title: Secure AI the same way you secure everything else on AWS
speaker: J.D. Bean
abstract: You already run security and governance on AWS with IAM, CloudTrail, KMS, and VPC boundaries, and AI workloads on Amazon Bedrock inherit all of it. This chalk talk shows how: IAM scoping for model access, data perimeter policies, full prompt and response logging in CloudTrail, and KMS encryption at rest and in transit. There is no separate governance stack to learn and no new tools to onboard. Apply the security patterns your organization already trusts to AI workloads on Bedrock.

title: Secure and modernize code simultaneously with agentic AI
speaker: Anand Bilgaiyan, Sreekumar Nair
abstract: Most modernization teams bolt security on as an afterthought, creating costly late-stage vulnerabilities. In this code talk, you'll follow along as we build a custom agent using Strands Agents SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that takes a security-first approach. We wire up AWS Transform agents for tech debt analysis via MCP integrations, connect AWS Continuum for deep code-level vulnerability scanning, and orchestrate everything through Kiro. The result: an agent that synthesizes a security-hardened modernization plan and autonomously executes it. See AI agents collaborate in real time to transform and secure code simultaneously, eliminating handoffs between teams.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Secure and Scalable Multi-Tenant Deployment Patterns for AWS Quick
speaker: Vineet Kachhawaha, Chin Rane
abstract: As organizations scale their adoption of AWS Quick across business units, subsidiaries, and partner ecosystems, deploying a secure multi-tenant architecture becomes critical. This chalk talk explores proven deployment patterns that balance tenant isolation, governance, and operational efficiency when rolling out AWS Quick at enterprise scale. We will walk through two primary isolation strategies: multi-account separation using AWS Organizations for environment-level boundaries (dev/staging/prod), and namespace-based logical isolation within a single account for user-cohort segmentation.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Secure by design: the AWS foundation for your AI applications
speaker: Maitreya Ranganath, Josh Du Lac
abstract: As organizations put AI and agents into production, leaders need confidence that their cloud provider is secure by design. This session explains how AWS foundational security extends into AI services and which AI security capabilities build on that foundation. You see the controls customers use to protect their most critical AI workloads.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Secure Coding Agents for Regulated Environments with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (sponsored by Act Security)
speaker: Offir Levy
abstract: Learn how HUB International, a top-five global insurance broker, partnered with AWS and Act Security to securely bring autonomous coding agents into a regulated enterprise environment, without giving the agents standing credentials or expanding the attack surface. The team transformed the local Claude Code experience into a secure, per-user cloud sandbox on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, preserving the familiar IDE and terminal workflow while moving execution to the cloud. See how OIDC authentication through the corporate IdP, per-call token minting through AgentCore Identity, and Cedar-based authorization for tools exposed through AgentCore Gateway enforce per-user, per-action access. Finally, discover how Act Security sustains least privilege over time and enforces narrower policies - whether you are deploying AgentCore for the first time or hardening an existing environment. This presentation is brought to you by Act Security, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Secure development in the age of AI coding agents
abstract: Code is increasingly written and reviewed by agents, which shifts where application security has to live. Talk through securing AI coding agents, threat modeling the agentic software development lifecycle, and keeping protection continuous rather than a gate at the end. Bring your pipeline and the places security still slows it down.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Secure petabyte-scale data transfers with AWS DataSync
speaker: Sachin Gupta, Manchun Yao, Christie Lee
abstract: Organizations moving data across AWS regions or into AWS need transfers that are fast, secure, and manageable at petabyte scale. In this session, learn how AWS DataSync helps you accelerate large-scale migrations and automate ongoing data movement. We'll show how capabilities like DataSync Enhanced mode help you move data faster with less operational overhead, then hear from Snap about how they moved billions objects and petabytes of data across AWS Regions in weeks. We'll close with best practices for maximizing performance and cost efficiency in your own DataSync deployments.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Secure your CI to operate at machine speed (sponsored by Chainguard)
speaker: Reid Tatoris
abstract: AI agents are changing how software is built, introducing new security challenges across the software supply chain. CI environments are particularly vulnerable, with access to sensitive credentials and elevated permissions. We’ll explore how Chainguard's trusted artifacts, isolated build environments, and integrations with AWS can reduce risk from development through deployment and what securing software delivery looks like when AI agents are doing more of the work. This presentation is brought to you by Chainguard, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Securing AI agents: Governance patterns for regulated workloads
speaker: Manjit Chakraborty, Neeraj Roy
abstract: Financial institutions building agentic AI platforms face a fundamental problem: security and governance controls were designed for humans and applications, not autonomous agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard the architecture decisions that matter most—covering identity, authorization, secrets, tenancy, and governance—and classify each as a one-way or two-way door. We'll walk through concrete patterns including agent authentication, agent-to-tool authorization, application-layer data segregation, and a multi-source governance model using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon CloudWatch, and AWS CloudTrail. Leave with decisions you can apply to your own agentic platform.

title: Securing AI Agents on AgentCore
speaker: Joe Huang, Prabhu G
abstract: A customer runs a support agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that reaches destinations nobody reviewed and takes requests from any caller. In this SimuLearn session, you work the case as their security expert. Behind Amazon API Gateway, AWS WAF Bot Control labels each script and AI crawler, and you write the rule that refuses them with a 403 that names the reason. On the way out, AWS Network Firewall tags every destination by content category. You watch in alert mode, then reject AI and search categories while permitted sites still load. You leave knowing how to classify, then control, what enters and leaves an agent.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom V

title: Securing AI and Autonomous Agents: Protecting the Lifecycle Across Any Platform (sponsored by Fortinet)
speaker: Chad Larter, Jason Mordeno, Ali Bidabadi
abstract: AI agents are actively running code, accessing databases, and making critical business decisions across every industry. But as these systems gain independence, they also introduce complex security risks throughout their lifecycle. Are you ready to protect a system that learns and acts on its own as your organization embarks on the AI journey? Join our panel of top AI and cybersecurity experts as they break down the end-to-end security of AI systems and agentic applications. We will explore real-world customer challenges and share practical strategies to safeguard autonomous agents across cloud and on-premises environments. This presentation is brought to you by Fortinet, an AWS Partner.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Securing AI coding agents: defense in depth across the development lifecycle
speaker: Mac Stevens, Alex Waddell
abstract: AI coding agents optimise for task completion, not security, generating code and PRs faster than humans can review. This chalk talk presents a defense-in-depth framework spanning five pillars - pre-generation, authoring, PR, pipeline, and deployment - with three lines of defense at each: deterministic controls, AI screening, and human judgment. We cover author-time techniques (steering, specs, scoped MCP, hooks) and build-time gates (SAST, SCA, IaC scanning, AI-assisted review, approval) using Kiro, AWS Security Agent, CodePipeline and more. Leave with a layered model you can apply on Monday.

title: Securing and observing Amazon EKS clusters
speaker: Jens Walther, Megan Velez Rivera, Edgar Costa Filho, Hans Nesbitt, Shamanth Devagari
abstract: In this hands-on session, explore how to automate the identification, analysis, and mitigation of risks in Amazon EKS clusters. Learn how to implement robust security controls—including role-based access control (RBAC), EKS Pod Identity, and service accounts—to apply least-privilege access and secure workload isolation. Discover how to use AWS CloudTrail and Amazon CloudWatch to gain deep visibility into EKS cluster activities, enabling real-time monitoring and automated risk detection. You will learn the skills to automate risk management processes, helping your Kubernetes workloads remain resilient against evolving threats.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Builders' Session

title: Securing and optimizing your software supply chain with Amazon ECR
speaker: Purvi Goyal, Mridul Chopra
abstract: Your software supply chain gets harder to manage as you grow. In this interactive chalk talk, we whiteboard the decisions teams face at each stage of that lifecycle: securing the supply chain against real threats, launching large images fast, operating at scale across accounts and Regions, and managing the lifecycle to cut cost and attack surface. We go deep on security with Amazon ECR, Amazon Inspector, and Amazon GuardDuty, including hardened base images, scanning, SBOMs, signing, admission control, and runtime threat detection on Amazon EKS and Amazon ECS. You leave with patterns you can apply across your container estate. Bring your questions and your own architecture.

title: Securing and optimizing your software supply chain with Amazon ECR
speaker: Mridul Chopra, Purvi Goyal

room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Securing applications at machine speed in the frontier model era
speaker: Evan McHenry, Matt Meck
abstract: Frontier AI models discover code vulnerabilities in minutes. Security teams still take days or weeks to validate, prioritize, and fix them. AWS Continuum closes that gap with one continuous workflow: discover risks in your code, prioritize by real exploitability, validate in a sandbox with reproduction steps, and remediate at machine speed within guardrails you define. In this session, we walk through how Continuum operates end-to-end: building a security context graph from your infrastructure, identity, and code to determine what is reachable, confirming exploitability through sandboxed proof-of-concept, and generating validated fixes. You see graduated trust in action, starting with human approval and promoting to autonomous remediation as confidence builds. You leave understanding how to move from manual triage to continuous discovery, validation, and remediation.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems
speaker: Kunle Adeleke, Daniel Wells
abstract: Multi-agent systems create a larger attack surface than single-agent deployments: prompt injections that propagate across agent boundaries, identity spoofing, tool-chain escalation, and data exfiltration through natural-language covert channels. In this chalk talk, we threat-model this risk using the OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, then whiteboard defense-in-depth patterns for validating inter-agent messages, enforcing least-privilege orchestration, and detecting anomalous behavior before it cascades. Leave with a set of recommendations and architectures that demonstrate how to layer security controls in a multi-agent system.

title: Securing OpenClaw deployments on AWS
speaker: Maxim Raya, Itay Meller
abstract: In this session, we introduce the OpenClaw architecture, compare the major variants and their security posture differences, and then map the threat landscape for AWS-hosted deployments. Drawing on years of experience helping customers deploy, we cover the infrastructure and runtime threat landscape. You will leave with a reference architecture that applies defense-in-depth principles to such OpenClaw deployments on AWS, minimizing risk without sacrificing capability.

title: Securing software and AI supply chains with Network Firewall at Coupang
speaker: Amish Shah, Andrew (Kyungshik) Shin, Sang Won Kim
abstract: Coupang, South Korea's largest e-commerce platform, runs millions of daily transactions on AWS. At that volume, each open source library, container base image, and AI model weight pulled from the internet is a supply chain risk. This session goes deep on the AWS Network Firewall architecture and its newer capabilities, including centralized management and container-aware egress inspection. Coupang shows how it built egress control that scales automatically across a container-first fleet, automates allowlist management, and limits exposure to rogue AI dependencies and dynamic payloads without slowing developers down.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Securing the agentic enterprise
abstract: Autonomous agents reason, decide, and chain tool calls, which creates identity, governance, and threat surfaces that traditional models never had to handle. This meetup goes deep on threat modeling agents, prompt injection, securing the tool and MCP supply chain, and isolating multi-agent systems. Share where your agent security program is working and where it is still open.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Securing the agent loop with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
speaker: Felipe Lopez, Shivani Singh, Sreedhar Gade
abstract: You screen the prompt on the way in and the answer on the way out. In between, tool results carry external content straight into the model's context and tool arguments carry the model's decisions out to your systems, without inspection. The middle of the loop is where indirect prompt injection lands. Where you place a guardrail inside the loop is a design decision. In this chalk talk, we place Bedrock Guardrails checks inside the agent loop. We examine ApplyGuardrail and InvokeGuardrailChecks, work through where each one belongs, and look at what risk remains when the checks are in place.

title: Securing the AI-Native Cloud (sponsored by Upwind)
abstract: In this session, we will demonstrate how AI is redefining cloud security by moving beyond static posture management to real-time, context-aware protection. The session will showcase how organizations can gain continuous visibility across their environments and respond to threats as they emerge. Attendees will see how AI-driven analysis of runtime behavior enables faster detection of anomalies, prioritization of real risks, and automated response across dynamic, multi-cloud infrastructures. The session will highlight how security teams can reduce noise, strengthen security processes, and proactively respond to threats before they escalate. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

title: Securing the Bedrock: A Strong API Foundation for AI Innovation (sponsored by Kong)
speaker: Amit Shah, Bryce Macher, Jonathan Kindberg
abstract: AI moves fastest when it moves along a governed path. Lanes, on-ramps, and speed limits are what let a highway run at full speed. Your agents are no different. Their path is the data path: every API call, model request, and event stream they touch. Kong shows how an AI control tower across API, AI, and event traffic governs all of it, and how it fits with your AWS infrastructure. Bryce Macher and Jonathan Kindberg from FanDuel will share their experiences, learnings, and advice on connectivity and scaling across the enterprise.

title: Securing the Enterprise in the Age of AI Agents: From Zero Trust to Agentic Security (sponsored by Zscaler)
speaker: Dhawal Sharma
abstract: AI isn’t just another workload—it’s introducing agents that act, connect, and make decisions at machine speed. This session reframes Zero Trust for an agent-driven world: how to govern agent-to-agent communication, constrain access to sensitive data, and reduce risk without slowing the business. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Securing your AI-accelerated software supply chain with AWS Well-Architected
speaker: Anshu Bathla, Rohit Verma
abstract: Modern software depends on open-source packages from npm, PyPI, and Maven. AI assistants pull them into your codebase faster than ever, sometimes suggesting packages that don’t exist or shouldn’t be trusted. Attackers exploit this through “slopsquatting.” Supply chain incidents show registries targeted via credential compromise, typosquatting, and token farming at scale. This workshop builds a layered defense aligned to the AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar. You replace long-lived credentials with OIDC, sign artifacts with AWS Signer, and govern dependencies with CodeArtifact package groups. You scan AI-generated and human-written code with Amazon Inspector, then detect threats with GuardDuty and Security Hub. You leave with a defense-in-depth blueprint that scales with AI-accelerated development across your environment.

title: Security compliance and hardening with EC2 Image Builder
speaker: Anuj Butail, Manny Sidhu
abstract: Discover how to leverage EC2 Image Builder to create secure, compliant, and hardened AMIs. Learn to automate security baseline implementation, including CIS benchmarks. We'll demonstrate building compliance checks into Image Builder pipelines, integrating vulnerability scanning, and implementing automated testing for regulatory standards.

abstract: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. Work through simulated incident response scenarios - including a sponsored challenge from Fortinet to test your skills securing cloud workloads with Fortinet's network and cloud security platform. Can you find the breach and prevent the next one? AWS experts and guided exercises support all levels. All you need: a laptop, curiosity, and a competitive spirit.

speaker: Nir Pilo, Felipe Baron
abstract: Come with your team of 2 or join one on the spot. Compete head-to-head, race the leaderboard, and win prizes. title: Security leverage at AI velocity: the operating model shift
speaker: Ram Ramani
abstract: The speed AI gives your developers is also available to attackers, so AI investment is now a security decision as much as an engineering one. This session covers three changes to how security teams work when engineers pair with frontier agents. Agents carry application context across design, code, and pen testing, so security coverage keeps pace with development. When an agent builds a working proof of exploit for a finding, or shows that an existing control already blocks it, the security team no longer has to argue over whether the finding is real, and the false-positive queue shrinks. Agentic development environments also let you put preventive controls on what agents generate. We cover how to adopt these practices and which signals show they're working.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Security → Zero-Trust Identity & Data Protection in AWS Quick
speaker: Munish Gopal, Priya Kakarla
abstract: Security reviews stall AI rollouts more than any capability gap, and agentic AI raises the bar. This chalk talk goes past "is it secure?" to the architecture that gets a CISO to yes for AWS Quick. We'll whiteboard the full identity path in Quick: SSO through providers like Okta and Ping, with end-user identity propagated to the data so authorization is enforced per user, in real time, across 1P AWS and 3P sources. Then we extend that trust to Quick agents: agent identity, deterministic policy checks on every tool call, and data protection, including Purview DLP, default guardrails, deny-by-default, and full SIEM auditability.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan I

title: See the routes change: Live BGP with AWS Direct Connect
speaker: Harold Lotz, Josh Dean
abstract: AWS Direct Connect can feel like a mystery beneath the surface, and many customers never get hands-on access. In this show and tell, we change that. Starting from a live connection and on-premises router, watch a Direct Connect maintenance unfold in real-time from both sides of the BGP session. See how AWS signals maintenance ahead of time through AS path prepending, graceful shutdown, and how traffic shifts to the backup path before any route is withdrawn. Whether you run 1G or hundreds of 100G ports, leave with the policy and checklist to get through your next maintenance without a page.

title: See where every AI dollar goes on Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Yiwen Zhang, Fahad Ahmed
abstract: AI spend scales fast, and you can't optimize what you can't attribute. In this code talk, build Bedrock cost visibility live: combine CloudWatch metrics and supported invocation logs for timely usage signals with Cost Explorer and CUR 2.0 for billing reporting. Add attribution by IAM principal and cost-allocation tags, then assemble a dashboard that maps spend to teams, workloads, and models while accounting for each source's freshness and granularity. Turn that visibility into action: match steady workloads to Reserved Tier, choose models for price-performance, and set budgets and alerts. Use these signals to reconcile engineering usage with finance reports.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Select and launch the right EC2 instance for your workload and budget
speaker: Tirtho Deb, Ian Bablewski
abstract: With hundreds of EC2 instance types spanning compute, memory, storage, and accelerator families, choosing the right one can be overwhelming. In this session, learn a practical framework for matching your workload characteristics—CPU, memory, network, and storage requirements—to the optimal instance type and size. We cover cost-performance tradeoffs across On-Demand, Spot, and Savings Plans, share real-world selection patterns for common workloads, and demo tools that simplify decision-making. Leave with a repeatable process to right-size from day one.

title: Self-Healing Enterprise-Wipro & AWS Moving from System of Record to System of Action (sponsored by Wipro)
speaker: Saurabh Vadhera
abstract: For decades, enterprises have invested in technologies that digitize, automate and optimize work. Yet when disruptions occur, decisions still depend on emails, escalations, meetings and manual coordination across teams. The next phase of enterprise transformation is about creating enterprises that can sense change, assess impact, coordinate responses and drive outcomes at speed. Wipro and AWS demonstrate how intelligent agents, enterprise systems and human expertise come together to create a Self-Healing Enterprise, one that can proactively identify issues, orchestrate actions across functions and continuously adapt while keeping humans accountable for critical business decisions. Through a realistic business disruption scenario, see how organizations can evolve beyond visibility and automation towards systems of action that improve resilience, responsiveness and operational efficiency. This presentation is brought to you by Wipro, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Self-Improving AI: The Race to Autonomous Systems
speaker: Glenn Rachlin, Jerry Tworek
abstract: Frontier labs are racing to build AI systems that improve themselves, and they're tackling it from different angles. This panel brings together Jerry Tworek, co-founder and CEO of Core Automation, and Richard Socher, co-founder and CEO of Recursive, to discuss their work on open-ended learning algorithms, reward alignment, and hardware co-design. Led by Deap Ubhi, Director of Technology at AWS Startups, they'll explore how they're thinking about speed, safety, and scale, and where reward hacking and hardware limits get in the way. You'll leave understanding the different technical strategies emerging in frontier AI and what each one prioritizes.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge
speaker: Fernando Galves, Chris McEvilly
abstract: As organizations use agentic AI to automate complex infrastructure operations, many have data residency, low latency, and security requirements that depend on running AI closer to their data. This workshop explores how customers deploy self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge to meet these requirements while enabling autonomous operations. Learn how to architect, provision, configure, and optimize AI agents that run locally, and how to extend the same architecture to AWS hybrid and edge infrastructure such as AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts.

title: Self-Tuning Demand Forecasts: How Agentic AI Puts Business Users in the Driver's Seat
speaker: Colby Ward, Ali Zagros
abstract: Amazon Connect Decisions is redefining how organizations approach demand forecast tuning. Traditionally, improving forecast accuracy meant navigating complex data engineering pipelines and hyperparameter optimization — work that was time-intensive, technically demanding, and largely inaccessible to business users. In this chalk talk, we unpack how Amazon Connect Decisions takes an agentic approach to solve this: intelligent agents continuously self-tune demand forecast models by incorporating business user feedback directly into the refinement loop, removing the undifferentiated heavy lifting. Walk through a live demonstration of self-tuning in action, learn how this business-first approach shifts forecast ownership to the people who understand the demand signals best, and discuss how Amazon Connect Decisions is shaping the future of agentic supply chain solutions.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Self-verifiable watermarks: defending AI provenance against forgery
speaker: Weitong Ruan, Fan Yang
abstract: As organizations deploy generative AI at scale, watermarking has become the critical trust layer for establishing content provenance, meeting emerging regulatory requirements, and protecting brand integrity. But what if an adversary could stamp a fake watermark onto any image and frame your service? We show a diffusion-based forgery attack bypasses current defenses with just 1,000 samples. To close this gap, we introduce a self-verifiable message mechanism—SeedBind and ContentBind—that transforms verification into a structural consistency check, reducing forged bit accuracy to near-random without modifying the underlying watermarking pipeline. Discover how to harden AI provenance at scale.

title: Sell to the AI Buyer, Scale Revenue, and Build Long-Term Value
speaker: Boone Quesnel, Jeff Falcon, Christopher Spandikow
abstract: The buying journey is shifting to AI agents and assistants that evaluate and procure software autonomously. If your solution isn't readable and transactable by a machine, you're invisible to a growing share of the market. This session shows AWS Partners how to show up for the AI buyer, from listing optimization to working alongside other agents, and how a growth toolkit (trials, bundling, demand generation) turns visibility into compounding revenue. Walk away with an implementation path that covers day-one discoverability through long-term governance.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

speaker: Yoni Leibowitz
abstract: Sequoia and Edelbyte share what VCs are really looking for when evaluating AI-first startups. This session covers how investment criteria have shifted for AI-native companies, what separates fundable AI startups from the rest, and what founders should understand about how VCs are thinking about AI-first business models today.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Serverless application testing in the age of agents
speaker: Brian Krygsman, Rajdeep Banerjee
abstract: Serverless and agentic tools let you ship fast. A strong testing foundation is what makes that speed sustainable - for you and your agents. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the testing patterns that matter most for serverless and event-driven applications: structuring code for testability, validating service interactions in the cloud, and building harnesses for asynchronous workflows. Join to explore local versus cloud testing tradeoffs and what new test dimensions agents enable for serverless developers. Walk away knowing how to give your agents the feedback loops they need to move quickly, iterate autonomously, and stay on the rails.

title: Serverless at 1M RPS: Lambda, DynamoDB & SQS Scaling Lessons
speaker: Jay Colodner, Nishtha Yadav
abstract: We push Lambda, DynamoDB, and SQS to one million requests per second and share what breaks. Learn partition-aware DynamoDB design for extreme write throughput, Lambda concurrency shaping to prevent downstream crush, SQS as a backpressure buffer with adaptive batching, and retry amplification math that turns a blip into a cascade. We present real numbers: cold start budgets at scale, the exact crossover point where serverless cost exceeds containers, and the operational trade-offs at each threshold.

title: Serverless compute built for the web
speaker: Julian Wood, Samrat Karak
abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. Learn how AWS Lambda Web Functions host the web server and frameworks you already run, including server-side rendering and streaming, with no adapter layer. Web Functions reduce cold starts because each execution environment serves many requests at once. Active CPU billing reduces costs when functions wait on a database or model. Deploy easily and safely, get an HTTPS endpoint, and serve users in multiple AWS Regions from one global URL. Whether you're migrating an existing app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical guidance for production-ready serverless web development.

title: Serverless developers in the agentic era: What changes, what doesn't
speaker: Julian Wood
abstract: Serverless architectures that worked well for API backends and event processing now have a new type of consumer: AI agents that call your functions as tools, generate events, and write code that deploys alongside yours. In this session we cover where existing serverless patterns hold up without modification, what actually changes, and how to start with what you have and add only what you need. See how the calls you already run can become tools that describe themselves to the agent that uses them. Learn how coding agents and skills make best practices part of every build, and where doing less with AI pays off.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Serverless Hosting for Agents: Lambda vs. Bedrock AgentCore Runtime
abstract: The era of static microservices is giving way to the world of autonomous AI agents. But where and how should these agents be hosted on AWS? In this 60-minute meetup, we deconstruct the paradigm of "Serverless for Agents" and compare the two primary hosting options: the battle-tested, highly flexible AWS Lambda and the specialized, managed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime. Beyond comparing individual features of both options, we will analyze the architectural trade-offs regarding state management, latency, runtime security, identity, observability, and governance features like built-in policy controls.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Serverless Java in 2026
speaker: Christian Mueller, Lefteris Karageorgiou
abstract: Java on Lambda used to mean cold start anxiety and compromised JIT performance. Not anymore. SnapStart and GraalVM Native AOT deliver sub-second startup, while Lambda Managed Instances bring steady-state JVM workloads full JIT optimization at EC2 economics. Lambda MicroVMs support long-running workloads and AI agents, while Lambda Durable Functions enable complex, stateful application orchestration. This chalk talk explores how Lambda supports a broader range of Java workloads, discusses refactoring patterns for moving Java monoliths to Serverless, framework choices on Lambda, and how AI-assisted tools identify decomposition boundaries and generate Lambda handlers from existing service classes. Bring your Java architecture!

title: Serverless Java in 2026
speaker: Lefteris Karageorgiou, Christian Mueller
abstract: Java on Lambda used to mean cold start anxiety and compromised JIT performance. Not anymore. In this chalk talk, we go beyond cold starts: discuss refactoring patterns for moving Java monoliths to serverless, framework choices that work well on Lambda (and ones that don't), and how AI-assisted tools identify decomposition boundaries and generate Lambda handlers from existing service classes. Bring your Java architecture.

title: Serverless observability: OpenTelemetry and vended logs
speaker: Maxime David, Franklin Aguinaldo
abstract: Debugging distributed serverless applications used to mean stitching together X-Ray traces, CloudWatch logs, and custom metrics from multiple extensions. In this chalk talk, we cover setup and configuration, end-to-end tracing with API Gateway vended logs, and distributed tracing across Step Functions, EventBridge, and SQS. We also discuss observability for agentic workloads: tracking token consumption, tool call success rates, and workflow checkpoint state. Bring your observability questions, especially around cost at scale: sampling, filtering, and cardinality management.

title: Serverlesspresso: Build an event-driven app from the ground up
speaker: Serda Kasaci Yildirim, Diana Cheng
abstract: Build a fully event-driven, serverless coffee-ordering web application using AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and Lambda durable functions. Design scalable, fault-tolerant architectures as you simulate customers placing orders and baristas managing them in real time. Discover how durable functions simplify complex workflow orchestration by checkpointing progress, automatically recovering from failures, and pausing execution while waiting on long-running tasks—all without managing additional infrastructure or writing custom state management code. You must bring your laptop to participate.
