title: Serverless streaming data processing with AWS Lambda and Apache Kafka
speaker: Diego Casas, Nikita Tibrewal, Franklin Aguinaldo, Kensuke Shimokawa, Matt Kahn
abstract: Build a serverless streaming data pipeline in 60 minutes. In this builders' session, you design and deploy a real-time location tracking app that ingests events from Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK), processes them with AWS Lambda, and pushes live updates to a dashboard through AWS AppSync—no consumer fleet to manage, no scaling logic to write. Experiment with Lambda event source mapping for Kafka, applying recent improvements in filtering, batching, and error handling. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: ServiceNow: The Super Intelligence Control Tower for Business Reinvention (sponsored by ServiceNow)
speaker: Gian Mario Deluigi, Martin Ristov, Alex Mastrodonato
abstract: AI without workflows is just expensive advice. The next generation of AI leaders are moving beyond disconnected copilots and isolated use cases to reinvent how work gets done. Join ServiceNow to learn how the Super Intelligence Control Tower for Business Reinvention helps organizations govern AI, connect enterprise data, and orchestrate work across every agent, model, and workflow. Discover how AI that thinks and workflows that act enable enterprises to deploy AI quickly while maintaining trust, security, and control. This presentation is brought to you by ServiceNow, an AWS Partner.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Serving world models on AWS Trainium with native PyTorch
speaker: Lingfan Yu
abstract: The next major leap in AI is predicting and interacting with the physical world. World models bridge digital reasoning with real-world execution, introducing new infrastructure demands for video generation, robotics, and gaming workloads. We'll explore the emerging architecture of world models and why AWS Trainium, purpose-built for better price-performance, is well suited to serve them. Learn how native PyTorch support with torch.compile fuses operations into optimized device graphs, and how NKI custom kernels accelerate critical operators like attention. You'll leave able to move world model inference from eager prototyping to compiled deployment using familiar PyTorch workflows.

title: Set the Bar, Then Beat It: Architecting Tailored AI with Forge
speaker: Omid Razavi, Anjali Narayan-Chen
abstract: When we set out to build Forge, Amazon's foundation model customization platform, we learned that the fastest path to the tailored AI solution is a disciplined loop with one measurable bar that governs every decision. The team behind Forge will whiteboard it end to end: (1) set the bar by defining and measuring "good" as explicit accuracy, latency, and cost thresholds, then build a candidate leaderboard against it; (2) improve toward that same bar by optimizing prompts, context, and inference serving; and (3) when optimization still falls short of the bar, choose a customization approach that modifies model weights at the pre- or post-training stage. Leave with lessons to design the optimal AI solution tailored to your use case.

title: Setting up the Right AI Architecture: Bringing Together Agents, Teams, and Context (sponsored by Notion)
speaker: Ian McClanan
abstract: Every organization is building their AI architecture in real-time: deciding which agents to use, which data sources to connect them to, and figuring how to get teams to collaborate across it all. These different layers have been arranged over many years of procuring tools, but can sometimes feel like a jumbled mess in the AI era. This session offers a practical way to reexamine your tech architecture. We'll cover four patterns that recur across organizations as they try to structure their business for the AI era, plus pitfalls to avoid to ensure your tech stack is optimized for AI. This presentation is brought to you by Notion, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Shaping the Future of Guest Support at lululemon with an AI-powered experience
speaker: Hannah Bloking, Shadi El Baba
abstract: What if you could design Guest Support for the future, not just improve the operation you have today? At lululemon, that question shifted the conversation. Rather than patching together fragmented tools and manual planning processes, the team envisioned the experience they wanted to create for guests and their people, then worked backward to build it. The result was a unified, AI-powered experience launched globally, giving employees more time to build meaningful connections with guests. This session explores how lululemon built a fundamentally different future for Guest Support and the principles leaders can use to do the same at their organization.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Shared file storage for containers, serverless, and Lambda
speaker: Eric Heinrichs, Jacob Strauss, Samyak Kathane
abstract: Containers spin up and disappear. Your application state needs to outlive them. Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, and Amazon S3 Files give your containerized and serverless workloads durable, shared file storage. We'll break down when to choose each service based on access patterns, performance, and cost. You'll see how real teams run stateful microservices using EFS on ECS/EKS, leverage FSx for high-performance file system workloads, and unlock POSIX capabilities to S3 object data for analytics and AI workloads with S3 Files.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Shared judgment: security culture for the agentic era
speaker: Samantha Wylatowska, Jonathan Jenkyn
abstract: Your agents are reviewing PRs, shipping code, and answering messages. They communicate on your behalf, surfacing every weak relationship in your org. Soft skills have never mattered more. Shift Left and Shift Down brought security in as automation to build trust in systems. Agents have moved the question to trust between humans. Security teams have historically operated at a remove: by org chart, tooling, and reputation. That distance becomes a liability when agents reduce the time between decision and consequence. This session is about building a security function whose core output is shared judgment with the engineers it serves.

title: Shared Responsibility for Resilience: Build, Test, and Prove Recovery with GenAI
abstract: Resilience is a shared responsibility between AWS and customers, and clear ownership keeps recovery on track. This session walks through the AWS resilience toolkit. We cover Next Generation AWS Resilience Hub, which uses GenAI-powered failure mode assessments to evaluate workload posture, Application Recovery Controller, and AWS Fault Injection Service for controlled, repeatable failure testing. We also cover the programs that help customers adopt them such as Resilience Program Accelerator and the Resiliency Core Program. Through real examples from AWS and customers, attendees leave with a model for ownership, a prioritized test plan, and a roadmap to improve their resilience posture.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Ship agents, not chaos: a 90-day pattern for production on AWS. (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
speaker: Asim Iqbal
abstract: AI agents are moving from pilots into production faster than most organizations can govern them, and independent teams building in parallel are creating what practitioners now call agent sprawl. This session presents a repeatable 90-day pattern that converts sprawl into governed agents ready for production, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Guardrails, and Kiro alongside NIST AI RMF and the Well-Architected Generative AI Lens. Architects, platform owners, and public-sector leaders see how a governed runtime, evidence-based mission KPIs, and cost discipline turn compliance into an accelerator. Audit-ready patterns from CDW customer engagements across regulated commercial and public-sector missions are included This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Ship Agents You Can Trust: An Agent Evaluation Framework for Partners
speaker: Vishal Srivastava, Neha Wadhwani, Gizem Gur
abstract: Partners shipping production agents at scale need to answer: is this good enough for customers? Agentic transformation doesn't end at build; quality evaluation is the missing layer. In this chalk talk, we walk through an open-source evaluation framework: define test criteria for your agent, run it in a sandbox on Bedrock, calibrate an automated judge against human labels, and track failure rates in CI. For multi-agent systems, attribute failures to the agent that caused them, not where the harm showed up.

In this session, we build the pipeline stages: validate policies at pull request time with Access Analyzer, simulate critical access paths before deployment, preview Service Control Policies (SCP) impact against real CloudTrail data, and automatically triage Access Denied errors in production using IAM's new debugging API and autofix recommendations. title: Shipping AI at Full Velocity: Securing the Agentic Pipeline from IDE to Runtime (sponsored by Wiz)
speaker: Jiong Liu, Luke Beeson
abstract: Autonomous AI agents are no longer just writing code; they are calling APIs, spinning up cloud resources, and executing commands across build pipelines. But with this level of autonomy, zero-day vulnerabilities can propagate across your stack faster than ever. Staying resilient requires shifting security directly into the agent’s execution loop. Through live demos and an interview with Capita CISO, Luke Beeson, on their rapid AWS adoption, discover how to embed guardrails directly into agentic IDEs. Learn to catch vulnerabilities and overscoped tool permissions as code is written, and walk away with a battle-tested framework to ship agentic AI at full velocity on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Wiz, an AWS Partner.

speaker: Jason Ostroski, Angel Marchena
abstract: See how Western Governors University uses Bluebox by Dynatrace and AWS Kiro to deliver AI-generated code with greater confidence. By combining live production intelligence with AI-assisted development, teams can provide agents with real runtime context, detect issues quickly, and create evidence-backed GitHub Issues for rapid remediation. Learn how Bluebox supports the software lifecycle before, during, and after deployment, helping teams validate fixes, reduce risk, and accelerate software delivery. This presentation is brought to you by Dynatrace, an AWS Partner.

title: Shipping to AWS with coding agents: where does yours get stuck?
abstract: Coding agents write the infrastructure code, run the CLI, and open the pull request. Then they hit permission errors, service quotas, console-only steps, and docs written for people. Bring the last thing your agent tried to deploy on AWS, shipped or stalled. On the whiteboard we'll trace the path from first prompt to running workload, mark where agents stall, and swap what gets them through: MCP servers, agent skills, infrastructure as code, sandboxes, and what you still do by hand. The hosts benchmark agents on real AWS tasks and will take what you share back to service teams.

speaker: Jean Malha
abstract: Startups burn precious time building infrastructure plumbing instead of shipping their actual idea. AgentCore handles the plumbing, agent identity, memory, gateway, and runtime, so you can focus on the product. In this session, we walk through standing up an agent on AgentCore end to end, covering what it handles for you and what you still own. You'll leave with a clear picture of how to go from idea to a running agent without building infrastructure from scratch.

title: Ship Reliable AI Agents with Strands Evaluation and AgentCore Evaluations
speaker: Guillermo Ojeda
abstract: Your AI agent works in demos, but can you trust it enough for production? How do you test behavior that can vary on every run, and catch regressions when prompts, models, tools, or workflows change? In this 300-level Code Talk, we'll turn real-world agent failure modes into representative test cases, evaluate both answers and actions, and add risk-based quality gates into CI/CD. Using Strands Evaluation and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations, you'll leave this session able to design and implement an evaluation pipeline tailored to your own agents, backed by a public reference implementation you can adapt.

speaker: Johnny Hand, Satya Mishra, Ramzi Souri
abstract: AI has changed who finds zero-days and how fast. Submissions to the TrendAI™ Zero Day Initiative™ (ZDI), a vendor-agnostic bug bounty program, are up 4x. For Pega, which runs thousands of AI-powered enterprise applications on AWS, any unknown flaw in its software stack becomes exposure for its customers. In this session, Pega and TrendAI™ share how they shrink that exposure window together. Learn how an agentic engine built on 20 years of ZDI research finds and validates zero-days, and how virtual patching protects AWS environments before a fix ships. Leave with practical steps to reduce zero-day exposure in your environment. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.

title: Simile: Making interview-trained AI that predicts consumer decisions
abstract: Simile built AI models trained on interviews that predict consumer decisions, essentially a “what-if” machine for consumer behavior. title: Simple Governance: How Kiro Makes Enterprise Policies Human-Friendly
speaker: Vipin Mohan, Nima Kaviani
abstract: Kiro agents execute code, invoke models, and interact with external services on behalf of developers. Enterprise administrators desire to constrain what agents can do without slowing developers down. We built a centralized governance system backed by Dogwood/Cedar that compiles admin-authored policies into governance documents enforced across every client (IDE, CLI, Web,Mobile) and server-side services. The system separates governance from configuration, uses deny-wins semantics with fail-closed enforcement, and scopes rules by hierarchies. Learn how we use Kiro itself to author and analyze governance policies to make enterprise controls human-friendly and manageable.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Simplify Data Analytics operations with AI-powered Apache Spark agents on AWS
speaker: David Zhang, Mohit Saxena
abstract: Running analytics workloads at scale carries a hidden operational tax: teams commonly lose significant engineering time to debugging failures, leave performance and cost improvements on the table, and spend months on each version upgrade. In this talk, we walk through a family of AI-powered agents for AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, and Amazon Athena. The Spark Troubleshooting Agent finds the root cause of a failure and recommends the code or config fix - cutting debugging time from hours to minutes. The Spark Upgrade Agent plans an upgrade, transforms the code, and validates both runtime and data quality - turning months into hours. We share what worked in production for both agents - the design choices, failure modes, and validation strategies that made them reliable - and distill lessons that generalize to any team applying LLMs to complex infrastructure.

speaker: Aarthi Srinivasan, Amir Bar-Or
abstract: As organizations unify data across Amazon S3 data lakes, S3 Tables, and Amazon Redshift using the open data lakehouse architecture, securing access at scale becomes critical. In this chalk talk, we dive deep into simplifying trusted identity propagation so end-user identities — not shared service roles — reach the data plane, designing multi-dimensional tag-based access control taxonomies that scale automatically through inheritance, enforcing column-level and cell-level security across federated catalogs, and auditing every access event to individual users.

abstract: As your compute spreads across multiple clouds and on-premises, every environment ends up with its own agents, tooling, and consoles. Patching, access, and monitoring happen a different way in each one, and no single view shows what is running or how it behaves. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to bring every instance under one operational model with AWS Systems Manager, no matter where it runs, and then get metrics and logs from all of them into Amazon CloudWatch. We work through the tradeoffs and patterns that hold at scale. Leave able to run and observe your whole fleet as one.

title: Simplify secure file sharing with Transfer Family no-code web apps
speaker: Emma Harrison, Madhukumar Adavi
abstract: Traditional file transfer solutions often require complex client software, custom scripts, or technical expertise, creating barriers for business users who need to share data. Learn how AWS Transfer Family web apps enable secure, browser-based file transfers that automatically trigger data processing workflows. We'll show you how to build automated pipelines that process files upon upload while maintaining enterprise-grade security through AWS IAM Identity Center for your workforce or Amazon Cognito for external users. Discover how to streamline file ingestion, kick off validations, and orchestrate downstream processing, starting with a simple drag-and-drop interface for your end users.

speaker: Sam Grace, Annie Cimack

In this chalk talk, we walk one application through six failure modes — PII exposure, phantom citations, out-of-scope advice, unreviewed judgments, hidden bias, and unaccountable decisions — and whiteboard a defense-in-depth architecture using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, AgentCore, Automated Reasoning, and human-in-the-loop patterns. Leave with a responsible AI stack applicable to any form factor — chatbot, agent, RAG pipeline, or model call — whether you serve donors, patients, customers, or citizens.

abstract: Enterprises are waking up to a hard truth: the AI their business now depends on runs on infrastructure, models, and pricing they don't control. In this session, Boomi's engineering and AI leadership show a different path — AI agents that run anywhere you choose (your Amazon VPC, your data center, behind your firewall) powered by small language models fine-tuned to each agent's job and served entirely on infrastructure you govern. You'll see the full architecture on AWS — Amazon EKS, EC2 GPU instances, Amazon S3, Aurora, MSK, and Amazon Bedrock as a governed escalation path — plus the fine-tuning pipeline (LoRA SFT + DPO), the evaluation gate that decides when a small model is ready, and a live demo of an agent reasoning locally at a fraction of the latency and cost of a frontier LLM. abstract: Every day, employees install browser extensions, IDE plugins, and open-source packages with powerful access to corporate devices, code, credentials, and data. We've normalized a practice that may someday seem as unthinkable as smoking on airplanes. In this session, we'll expose hidden risks in plugin and package ecosystems, show why traditional application controls miss this rapidly changing software layer, and explore what security teams must rethink as AI makes software adoption faster and increasingly autonomous. title: Stop fixing, start preventing with Well-Architected Agent
speaker: Saurabh Saxena, Ramesh Seshadri
abstract: Reactive incident response grows more expensive as environments scale. AWS Well-Architected Agent shifts resilience and security from periodic review to continuous, automated assessment. Its agentic reasoning identifies single points of failure, recovery gaps, and vulnerabilities across 100+ services, ranking findings by workload criticality and business goals. Crucially, each recommendation includes cross-pillar trade-off analysis - showing cost and performance implications — so you improve resilience and security without unintended consequences elsewhere. Walk away able to catch risks before they become incidents.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Stop Moving AWS Data. Turn It into Action with Splunk​ (sponsored by Splunk by Cisco)
speaker: Adrian Acuna, Heath Johnson
abstract: Machine data across AWS environments is growing faster than teams can move, normalize, and analyze it. What if you could stop moving all that data and start putting it to work? In this session, learn how Cisco Data Fabric, powered by Splunk, federates data across AWS and enterprise sources, correlates it at scale, and prepares it for AI and agentic workflows. Through practical architecture patterns and a live demonstration, you’ll see how to reduce data movement and operational cost while turning distributed telemetry into trusted context, faster decisions, and action.​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk by Cisco, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Stop Rolling Back AI Agents: Production Patterns That Work
speaker: Gunnar Grosch, Nadia Reyhani, Kristine Armiyants
abstract: The demo shipped. The agent went live. Then someone pulled it back. 74% of organizations that have deployed an AI agent have rolled it back or shut it down, and the rate rises to 81% among those reporting fully mature guardrails. Getting agents into production got easier. Keeping them there without hurting customers did not. We'll walk through the failure patterns behind rollbacks: agents that fail silently, prompts treated as safety boundaries, and monitoring that overlooks non-deterministic failures. You'll leave with the patterns that prevent them: infrastructure-level guardrails, blast radius containment, and observability built for probabilistic systems.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Roman I

title: Stop the bleed: control and optimize agent costs on AgentCore
speaker: Mona Mona, Willie Lee
abstract: Your agent cost $0.02 per session in testing. In production it's $0.14 and climbing. Token consumption grows unpredictably as agents retry, loop, and fan out across tools, and most teams have no visibility into where the money goes. This chalk talk breaks down where agent costs actually hide and how to control them on AgentCore: per-session budgets that kill runaway loops, model routing that drops to cheaper models for simple subtasks, cost attribution at the team and workload level, prompt caching strategies, and how to measure the tradeoff between cost and quality with evaluations.

title: Stop threats at DNS: what's new in Route 53 DNS Firewall
speaker: Adhish Bhobe, Jesse Lepich
abstract: DNS is where threats are first visible and Amazon Route 53 DNS Firewall is turning that visibility into defense. This session explores how Route 53 DNS Firewall's evolving security capabilities help you resolve, inspect, and protect egress DNS query traffic to the internet across global, multi-account environments. See how deeper integration with other AWS security services, expanded DNS threat detection, wider visibility, and a growing partner ecosystem come together to strengthen your first line of defense. Whether you run a single VPC or a global network across AWS and hybrid networks, you'll leave with a clear picture of how DNS security for egress traffic is advancing and how to put it to work.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Stop troubleshooting your AWS network from memory and stale diagrams
speaker: Neil Yajnik, Kartik Ganesh
abstract: Your network grew faster than your documentation. Routes were added in a sprint, VPC attachments stacked during migrations, and somewhere along the way, your team lost the full picture. When something breaks, you're troubleshooting from memory and stale diagrams. In this session, learn how to turn that around in hours instead of months. See how to point AI-assisted tooling at your live environment to map every resource, trace every traffic path, and surface misconfigurations before they become incidents. Then take it further: modernize what you find with current AWS network security capabilities. Walk out with a repeatable workflow you can run against your own network this week.

title: Storage decisions when you're building a multi-tenant business
speaker: Dave Roberts, David DeLuca
abstract: When your business delivers cloud services to your customers, how you map tenants to storage is one of the earliest architectural choices, and it shapes everything that follows: onboarding automation, billing boundaries, isolation guarantees, and how accounts, users, and data relate to each tenant. Your workload mix adds another dimension, because data types using object, file, or block storage drive the handling of tenancy differently. In this chalk talk, we walk through silo, bridge, and pool deployment models, examining how workload profile, tenant count, and business requirements drive the choice. Bring your architecture and we'll work through it.

title: Storage performance in EC2 instances: What matters to your workload
speaker: Tanmoy Sen, Kshitij Tambe
abstract: Peak SSD IOPS and throughput dominate benchmarks, but production workloads tell a different story. In this chalk talk, we explore why latency-consistent mixed read/write performance drives real application outcomes across database, analytics, and distributed file system workloads. We'll walk through how workload profiles map to different performance dimensions (throughput vs. IOPS vs. latency consistency), how real-world write mixes reveal true storage performance, and how emerging AI workloads are creating demand for an entirely new storage performance profile.

title: Strategies for agentic-ready architectures on Amazon EKS
speaker: ENG HWA TAN, Omri Shiv
abstract: As AI agents become first-class workloads, the platforms that host them must evolve. This session explores how Amazon EKS enables agentic-ready architectures — combining multi-tenancy isolation, dynamic scaling, and fine-grained security boundaries to safely run autonomous agent workflows at scale. We'll examine how platform engineering patterns born from SaaS modernization (control plane/application plane separation, tenant-aware networking, and cost allocation) translate directly to orchestrating multi-agent systems. Attendees will learn practical patterns to provision, isolate, and observe agentic workloads on Kubernetes while maintaining operational control and cost efficiency.

title: Strategies for optimizing your migration: Lessons from ExxonMobil
speaker: Parker Caputo, Christine Megit, Valerie Rosenfield
abstract: Migrating to the cloud and running efficiently once you're there are two different disciplines. In this session, hear ExxonMobil's firsthand journey from a large-scale lift-and-shift migration to a disciplined, data-driven optimization practice, and the role the AWS Optimization and Licensing Assessment (OLA) played both before the move and after, for ongoing optimization. Parker Caputo (ExxonMobil) shares how his team used real utilization data to right-size 1300+ EC2 instances and realize over $2M in annualized savings without sacrificing performance. We'll then explore the tools and programs that make optimization an informed decision at any stage, and close on the layer most native tools can't see on their own: Microsoft licensing. Learn why licensing can represent 30–50% of Windows and SQL Server workload TCO, and how to optimize it as part of your cloud cost strategy.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Streamlining Claims Processing with Amazon Quick
speaker: Ryan Forger, Ryan Leavitt
abstract: Claims adjusters spend hours retrieving policy data, applying business rules, and drafting decision letters manually. In this SimuLearn session, you use Amazon Quick Automate to orchestrate the entire claims process. You configure REST API and MCP connectors, build a multi-step workflow with Custom Agent steps, and chain together policy retrieval, rules validation, and AI-powered letter generation. The workflow handles missing data gracefully and stores audit-ready decision letters in S3.
room: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Augustus Ballroom V

title: Strengthen identity verification with Amazon Rekognition
speaker: Divyesha Malhotra, Vicky Katara, Palak Mehta
abstract: Learn how to use Amazon Rekognition Face Liveness to help confirm a real person is present during digital onboarding. This session explores how to integrate liveness checks into your application, detect spoofing attempts, and support identity verification workflows.

title: Surviving the drop: Build a flash-sale control plane with CloudFront
speaker: Sanchith Kandaka, Fenil Patel, David MacDonald, Harith Gaddamanugu, Kartik Bheemisetty
abstract: Product drops, ticket on-sales, and viral promotions can spike traffic 50x in seconds - and origin infrastructure is the wrong place to absorb it. In this workshop, build a complete launch-day control plane using Amazon CloudFront Functions and CloudFront KeyValueStore. Implement a launch gate with VIP early access, a percentage-based throttle that dials traffic to your purchase origin in real time, sticky A/B testing for product pages, and a global kill switch - all controlled by KeyValueStore updates that propagate worldwide in seconds, with zero deployments and zero origin changes. Along the way, use edge location metadata for geo-staggered launches and trace every gate decision with CloudFront Functions access logging. Leave with patterns you can apply to any high-demand launch event. Attendees must bring a laptop.

title: Switch models in production without disrupting customers on Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Shash Sapre, Claudio Mazzoni
abstract: Your application is working in production, and then a newer model arrives with better benchmarks or lower cost. You need to decide whether moving is worth the risk. A switch can change outputs, break prompts, raise costs, and create weeks of retesting. This session shows how to reduce that disruption on Amazon Bedrock. Test candidate models against your own use cases, compare quality, latency, and cost, and update prompts without rewriting them by hand. See how Advanced Prompt Optimization scores your current model against candidates on your own data, giving each candidate a fair prompt, so you can measure the impact before rollout. Leave with a practical plan for switching models without disrupting customers.

title: Tackling a $30M fraud crisis with ML: California Community Colleges
speaker: Mitul Ganger, Julia Arreguy
abstract: The California Community Colleges, the largest higher education system in the U.S. serving 1 in 4 community college students nationally. Since 2024, it has faced a fraud crisis targeting over $30M, as stolen-identity breaches and generative AI made ghost-student attempts cheaper and harder to catch. Machine learning (ML) on Amazon SageMaker now screens applicants centrally, driving a 64% decrease in attempted fraud year over year. Campus-level detection tools add a second layer, catching 2x more fraudulent applications than human review alone. This session covers the ML architecture, how it integrates across 116 campuses, and how reclaimed seats and aid dollars directly improved access for legitimate students.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Tag once, find anything: scale resource tracking across accounts
speaker: Mohamed Othman, Nisha Notani
abstract: Inconsistent tags make it hard to see what runs where. In this code talk, we build automation that keeps tagging clean at scale: a tagging schema that defines the keys and values that matter, an AWS Config rule that flags non-compliant resources, and an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that remediates them automatically or with approval. We also query untagged resources across thousands of resources and multi accounts. Leave with working code you can adapt for cost allocation, access scoping, and AI-assisted root-cause analysis.

title: Taking Every Interaction from Mundane to Magic: Agentic CX with Connect Customer
speaker: Srinivas Akella, Cecilia Bolich, Pasquale DeMaio
abstract: Every brand is racing to put AI in front of its customers, the biggest opportunity in a generation, but also a risk. In 2026, deflection is dead. Even the customers you help are quietly leaving, because being processed isn't the same as being known. In this session, the VP, Amazon Connect Customer, and SVP, Client Operations Technology, U.S. Bank, show what's possible when serving customers is AI-first by design: your brand shows up before they ask, and every customer feels like your only customer. If you own the customer relationship, this is the one session you can't afford to miss.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Roman I

title: Talk to your market data: Agentic AI meets exchange feeds
speaker: Sribalaji Thirunavukkarasu, Ravindra Kori, Santhosh Sampath, Alket Memushaj, Samrat Lamichhane
abstract: In this builders’ session, connect an Amazon Bedrock agent layer to a high-performance data pipeline that turns 560M IEX exchange messages into an interactive playground. Analysts describe trading ideas in natural language (no SQL or Python required) while the agent queries Parquet data, generates strategy logic, runs backtests, and returns results. Dig into the C++ parsing, serverless orchestration with AWS Batch and AWS Fargate, Amazon S3, and guardrail patterns that make it production ready. Leave with architecture patterns, a cost model, and a blueprint for adding an agentic layer that takes anyone from market intuition to tested strategy in minutes.

title: Tapestry, Grupo Boticario & Nestle Purina on agentic commerce
speaker: Isabel Miranda, Todd Carter, Mandeep Bhatia, Ann Scharenberg
abstract: AI agents are changing how consumers discover and buy, splitting into two investments: retailers building conversational shopping on their own properties, and consumer goods companies optimizing how their products surface when agents shop on a consumer's behalf. In this session, hear how Tapestry built the Kate Spade AI Gift Concierge that turns luxury gifting into a guided conversation; Grupo Boticario launched an agentic Virtual Assistant orchestrating product discovery and checkout for millions of users; and Nestle Purina implemented an Answer Engine Optimization strategy, using their native chatbot Allie to pressure-test how external AI engines surface proprietary brand data before releasing it into circulation.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Target to Molecule: Bayer & Capgemini accelerate Crop Protection R&D with BioNeMo (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speaker: Lukas Kuckelkorn, Dr. Janosch Achenbach, Javier Moreno
abstract: Bayer's CropKey strategy relies on target-based and profile-driven discovery to develop the next generation of crop protection solutions. A key challenge is enabling broad access to advanced AI models for protein structure prediction, target exploration, molecular docking, and molecular design, which are often complex and costly to operate. This session highlights how Bayer and Capgemini built a scalable, cloud-native platform on AWS that provides researchers with easy access to state-of-the-art biomolecular AI capabilities by leveraging NVIDIA BioNeMo NIMs. By operationalizing foundation models in a secure and cost-efficient environment, the platform helps close critical knowledge gaps in early discovery and accelerates the application of AI across the crop protection R&D pipeline. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Teaching agents to pay with Stripe (sponsored by Stripe)
speaker: Ben Smith
abstract: AI agents can already search, reason, and call tools. What changes when they can spend money, too? This talk explores the shift from human checkout to machine-native commerce, where payments become part of an agent's reasoning loop. We will look at how agents can discover and purchase products today, then explore Stripe’s Machine Payments Protocol and a future where agents autonomously pay for APIs, compute, data, and other capabilities needed to complete a task. When software becomes the buyer, developers may need to rethink not only checkout, but also how software itself is discovered, priced, and consumed. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Teaching Quick to Remember and Connect with Memory and Knowledge Graphs
speaker: Adi Kalyanpur, Thomas Delteil
abstract: Every conversation with an AI assistant starts from scratch. Your agent doesn't remember what worked yesterday, can't tell you who owns a project without searching again, and repeats the same mistakes because failures are never captured. In this chalk talk, we show how AWS Quick breaks out of statelessness with two primitives: a continuous-learning memory layer where a background agent extracts reusable knowledge after each session and scores it with a probabilistic confidence model, and a personal knowledge graph that connects people, projects, decisions, and evidence across your tools so the agent has a map of your world before it reads a single document. We'll whiteboard the architecture and the tradeoffs that shaped it, then open it up — bring your hardest questions about memory staleness, confidence calibration, graph noise, or making agents that actually get better over time.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Teaching Telemetry to Think: From Raw Signals to Root Cause
speaker: Shiva Kasiviswanathan, Krishna Balasubramanian
abstract: An AI agent investigating an incident starts cold: no sense of normal, no topology, no causal history. It rebuilds context from raw documents every time. What if the telemetry understood itself first? We'll examine an intelligence layer for agentic observability, where streaming detectors and a live service graph distill billions of signals into incident observations, then fine-tuned reasoning models, built on open-weight LLMs, correlate them into ranked root causes. Whiteboard with us on the hard parts: what to teach a model versus retrieve at inference, how domain fine-tuning beats frontier scale, and where reasoning models still fail.

title: Tech debt anonymous: bring your worst code to this chalk talk
speaker: Venugopalan Vasudevan, Avi Nidumbur
abstract: We all have it: the monolith nobody wants to touch, and the pile of small apps and Lambda functions racking up end-of-life notices. This chalk talk is your support group. Bring your real modernization headaches and we'll discuss how AWS Transform tackles the whole spectrum. On one side, Transform custom handles the big, complex jobs: decomposing Java and .NET monoliths, translating languages, upgrading frameworks at scale. On the other, continuous modernization autonomously scans thousands of repositories, prioritizes what's drifting, and opens remediation pull requests on a schedule. Bring questions about your own portfolio and leave with a plan of attack.

title: Technical Innovations Keynote
speaker: Oliver Cameron, Colm MacCarthaigh, Ron Diamant, Matt Wood, Amy Herzog
abstract: Agents don't follow a script. They change plans mid-task, reach for tools they didn't know they'd need, and create demand you can't predict. For two decades, the hardest workloads builders brought to AWS have pushed us to rethink everything from Graviton and Trainium to the shape of the data center network, to the way storage scales, and how we prove systems behave as intended. Join AWS's top engineers and scientists for an under-the-hood look at the technology that came out of that pressure, the kind of story you won't hear anywhere else. See how AWS infrastructure adapts as your work changes, freeing you to stop engineering around constraints and build anything you can imagine.

title: Techniques for Cost-Optimized Video Understanding on AWS
speaker: Maheshwaran G, Aravind Rajendran, Sanjay Singh, Devendra Sharma, Wei Teh
abstract: Video understanding unlocks powerful insights from media assets, but cost concerns often slow adoption. In this hands-on session, we walk through practical techniques for building cost-optimized video understanding pipelines on AWS. You'll learn how to reduce inference costs, right-size your architecture, and accelerate time to value without sacrificing accuracy. Whether you're processing thousands of hours of content for metadata enrichment, content moderation, or search, these patterns help you scale AI-driven video analysis while keeping your bill predictable.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Tekion: Reinventing automotive retail with agentic AI on AWS
speaker: Vibhu Pareek, Santosh Golecha
abstract: Automotive retail runs on complex, menu-driven workflows — scheduling service, ordering parts, structuring deals, closing books. Tekion, whose cloud-native platform powers thousands of dealerships, reimagined it as conversational AI, the industry's first AI-native automotive DMS. Built on Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, Tekion's production agents — spanning sales, service, parts, F&I, and accounting — execute actions rather than suggesting them, serving every role from service advisor to dealer principal. Learn how Tekion architected a reusable agent platform, applied guardrails for safe autonomy, and turned industry operations AI-native.

title: Telecom Contact Centers: Design Patterns for integrated AI Agents
speaker: Shalima Bhalla, Robin Harwani
abstract: IVR frustrates telecom customers, and the context from the automated interaction is gone when a human finally receives the call. Come to this chalk talk ready to work on what replaces it. After a short framing of the design space, the group takes on three questions. How should a customer-facing AI agent on Amazon Connect be built, and where do its boundaries sit? How does full conversation context survive the handoff? Should OSS and BSS integration use MCP, prebuilt Amazon Connect integrations, or both? Bring your toughest scenarios. In this working session, we will reason through the trade-offs live.

title: Telecom NOC operations: Automating incident response with AI agents
speaker: Daniel Lupescu, Cheng Liu
abstract: Modern telecom networks span thousands of distributed components, forcing network operations teams to interpret high volumes of alarms, separate root causes from downstream symptoms, and coordinate remediation across systems under time pressure. In this workshop, you will build AI agents that read, reason about, and execute Standard Operating Procedures for network deployment and remediation. First, deploy a 5G standalone core on Amazon EKS using an agent built with the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock. Next, operate a closed-loop remediation agent, inject real failures, and observe how it detects, correlates, and resolves problems.

title: Tenant-isolated agent memory: one IAM policy for AgentCore Memory
speaker: Nihilson Gnanadason, Daniel Wirjo
abstract: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. We cover the actorId and namespace conventions, the Token Vending Machine that mints per-tenant credentials, and the anti-patterns that break isolation as you scale. Leave with the reference architecture and the IAM policy template you can use on Monday.

title: Tenant isolation at scale: Network patterns for ISVs on AWS
speaker: Tom Adamski, Rizwan Mushtaq
abstract: As ISVs scale their SaaS platforms, network architecture becomes a critical decision: balancing tenant isolation, compliance, and operational efficiency. In this chalk talk, examine proven connectivity patterns using AWS PrivateLink, AWS Transit Gateway, and Amazon VPC Lattice for multi-tenant environments. Explore how to enforce strong tenant boundaries at the network layer, handle cross-account connectivity at scale, and reduce operational complexity as your business grows. Whether building a new multi-tenant platform or evolving an existing one, leave with architecture blueprints ready for production.

title: The 7 Rs in the Real World: Honest Migration War Stories
abstract: Every migration looks clean on the whiteboard. Then reality shows up. This peer-to-peer round table is for anyone moving workloads to AWS: mid-migration, cleaning up after one, about to start, or here to learn. We'll trade stories about the 7 Rs, like the rehost that became a refactor and the "retain" that's still retained three years later. Expect quick interactive rounds: "Which R is it?" votes, hot takes, myth vs. reality, and ask the room. We'll build a shared dos and don'ts list, and ask whether, in the AI era, a workload is even worth migrating. No slides.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: The AgentCore Governance Loop: Policy, Guardrails, Observability
speaker: Harpreet Singh Siddhu
abstract: Building an agent takes an afternoon. Operating it safely across a team takes architecture. In this session learn how to build a multi-agent reference platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and walk the full governance loop including cataloging agents for discovery, enforcing what they can do with Cedar policy at the gateway, filtering what they can say with Guardrails, and tracing behavior through observability. You will learn where the pieces integrate cleanly and where the seams break. You leave with a governance reference architecture you can adapt to any agentic workload, plus the lessons the documentation leaves out.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: The Agent Harness: Unifying Fragmented Tools for Mission AI Advisors
speaker: Mrudhula Balasubramanyan, Praveen Nerellapalli
abstract: Advisors across mission-driven organizations—financial advisors, benefits navigators, program coordinators—juggle fragmented tools, manual research, and delayed plan delivery while clients go underserved. AI agents change this equation. See how to collapse this fragmentation into configuration using the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness. Learn to securely plug domain-specific skills and disparate Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers directly into the harness to generate tailored action plans in real time. Then, deploy the agent to isolated microVM sessions utilizing native memory strategies and Bedrock Guardrails. Leave with sample configurations, deployment patterns, and blueprints for building production advisors that scale.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: The Agent Harness You Own on AWS for Regulated Industries
speaker: Jacky Chan
abstract: In regulated industries the model is easy; the governable, auditable, defensible agent is hard. AgentCore ships primitives, but the governance harness you own on top is the real work. We build the rails it does not give you: a fail-closed, blocklist-first permission gate where deny beats a broad allow; a hash-chained audit verifiable off-cloud; and a RACI gate binding every action to a named human. Each maps onto a managed AWS primitive — Identity, Guardrails, Evaluations, Lambda MicroVMs for isolation — naming where the primitive ends and your code begins. You leave with the rails.

title: The Agentic MSP: AI Agents & Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in Action
speaker: Ayush Kanyal, Bappaditya Dutta
abstract: MSPs managing hundreds of customer environments can no longer rely on manual, reactive workflows. In this hands-on workshop, MSP teams will deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — using natural language to monitor, diagnose, and remediate issues across accounts in real time. Participants will trigger live incidents, orchestrate autonomous fixes with DevOps, FinOps, and Security agents, and explore how Kiro and AWS Transform accelerate development and modernization. The session covers agent-to-agent coordination, cross-account operations, and MCP-based tool access. MSPs will leave with a production-ready blueprint to transform operations from reactive to agentic. Laptops required — everyone builds live.

title: The Agentic MSP: How AI Compounds Customer Outcomes at Every Layer
speaker: Ben Reed
abstract: The most profitable Managed Services Providers aren't just using AI internally. They're creating a compounding cycle: automate your own operations with Agentic AI, deliver measurably better outcomes to customers, then help those customers adopt AI themselves so the results multiply. This session shows how the AWS Managed Services Provider Program rewards that progression, from foundational automation through outcome-based delivery powered by AI agents. Leave with your own assessment and a concrete plan to reach the next level.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: The agentic restaurant: AI agents that run your kitchen
speaker: David Bounds, Pranjit Biswas
abstract: The restaurant industry is transforming as AI agents move from pilots to production. Leading QSR and casual dining brands are deploying a "virtual general manager," multiple specialized agents orchestrated together to optimize drive-thru ordering, kitchen workflows, labor scheduling, and guest experience in real time. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard a multi-agent architecture using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, with Amazon Nova Sonic powering voice ordering at sub-2-second latency. We design a supervisor agent coordinating specialists across drive-thru, kitchen prep, inventory, and labor scheduling. Explore how agents share context, resolve conflicts, validate decisions against synthetic personas before deployment, and maintain human-in-the-loop oversight. Bring your architecture challenges.

title: The Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Postman)
abstract: Autonomous agents are no longer assisting the software development lifecycle. They are rewriting it. When agents write, review, test, and ship code at machine speed, the SDLC stops being a sequence of human handoffs and becomes a control problem. This session covers the failure modes that only appear at scale: review queues that no human can absorb, test suites that validate the wrong invariants, provenance gaps that make incidents unexplainable, and CI/CD pipelines built for tens of commits a day now absorbing thousands. It closes with the specific architectural decisions engineering leaders should be making now, drawn from our own experience running agents in production. This presentation is brought to you by Postman, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: The agent orchestration spectrum: Agents, Step Functions, or Lambda?
speaker: Håkon Eriksen Drange
abstract: "Orchestration mode matters more for end user experience than just model choice. In this live-coding session, I build the same GenAI workload three ways: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, AWS Step Functions, and AWS Lambda durable functions - and show what each costs in latency, dollars, and debuggability on a production content platform. Leave with a reusable decision framework to match orchestration to your workload."
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: The Amplification Effect: How AI Sharpens the Builder
speaker: Umesh Sampat, ADAM B
abstract: Replacement anxiety dominates the AI conversation, but builders who use AI as a daily collaborator are discovering the opposite: AI amplifies human capability. This breakout session presents a practical framework for using AI tooling as a skills accelerator. We'll show how builders who integrate AI into daily workflows develop stronger critical thinking, faster adaptability, and deeper domain reasoning. Drawing from real-world examples, you'll learn how the act of collaborating with AI and refining its direction builds the exact human capabilities organizations need most. Walk away with a progression model from proficiency to mastery and techniques to start sharpening your skills immediately.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: The annual forecast for where sports AI is heading
abstract: Once a year, the sharpest voices in communications go on the record about what comes next, then answer for it when the year arrives. This session brings that ritual to sports. A broadcast analyst convenes league partners, former players, and media voices from the NFL, NBA, PGA TOUR, F1, and Bundesliga, and each one makes a specific, dated prediction about how AI reshapes their sport within three years, then defends it to a skeptical room. The real question underneath, which AI to adopt now, faces everyone in the seats.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: The Art of the Impossible: How Amazon Builds on AWS
speaker: Tulip Gupta, Sujatha Guthikonda, Naresh Narayanan
abstract: Discover how two Amazon teams tackled seemingly impossible problems with agentic AI running on AWS. Prime Video enabled content discovery at a scale where personalized curation was never feasible, building an AI discovery assistant powered by agentic search on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, vector-powered retrieval, and frontier and custom LLMs on SageMaker. Launched to millions of customers, it replaced endless scrolling with conversation starters like "hidden gems from the '80s" and natural voice exploration. Amazon Pharmacy now autonomously resolves most of its hundreds of thousands of monthly customer contacts while staying HIPAA compliant. Specialized agents on Amazon Bedrock Agents and Amazon Connect handle billing, fulfillment, and pharmacist workflows, hand off to humans, increasing satisfaction. Learn to apply their approaches to your own seemingly impossible problems.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: The AWS CLI in an Agentic World: Less Tokens, More Done
speaker: Alex Shovlin, Liam Greenamyre
abstract: AI coding agents are increasingly orchestrating cloud infrastructure, but they can be expensive and slow when every action requires chaining low-level API calls. The AWS CLI offers a different path: composable, structured commands that collapse multi-step workflows into single invocations. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Agent Toolkit gives AI agents first-class access to AWS through the CLI, why purpose-built commands are inherently cheaper for agents to execute, and what "developer experience for machines" means for CLI design going forward.

speaker: Olga Madejska, James Gray
abstract: From model testing to capacity planning, compute can be complex and costly to get wrong. As development moves into an agentic era, see how AWS Console innovations provide a trusted tool to support your workflow, verify instances, save costs, govern with confidence. Move faster. Stay in control.

title: The AWS network I would build today: Identity over topology (sponsored by Tailscale)
speaker: Lee Briggs
abstract: Modern AWS environments can grow from a handful of VPCs into complex regional and global routing topologies. This session explores a different model: keeping VPC networking local and predictable while using identity-aware connectivity between users, workloads, and networks. See how Tailscale connects AWS environments and resources, including those that cannot run an agent, and explore an experimental integration with AWS Gateway Load Balancer and GENEVE. Attendees will learn the tradeoffs, where native AWS networking remains the right choice, and how identity-aware networking can reduce connectivity complexity without sacrificing control. This presentation is brought to you by Tailscale, an AWS Partner.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: The Best Engineer in the Room Doesn’t Write Code (sponsored by Anaconda)
speaker: Emilie Schario
abstract: AI generates code faster than teams can review and ship it. The bottleneck has moved, and so has the work of the highest leverage engineers. Engineers build coding factories: repeatable systems that combine user intent, persistent context, agent execution, automated checks, and human judgment. Drawing on AWS’s AI-Driven Development Life Cycle, we’ll see how Kilo by Anaconda meets developers where they work and how Amazon Bedrock brings model choice into the factory, tracing one build failure through verification and escalation. Attendees leave with a framework for agent workflows that deliver, and a clearer view of where engineering judgment matters. This presentation is brought to you by Anaconda, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: The Best Intel in the Cloud — What's New and What's Next
abstract: Custom Intel Xeon 6 processors — available only on AWS — now power a full portfolio of 8th-generation EC2 instances: compute-optimized (C8i), general purpose (M8i), memory-optimized (R8i, X8i), local storage (C8id, M8id, R8id), network-optimized, EBS-optimized, and dataplane packet processing families. All deliver up to 20% better performance and 15% better price-performance than previous generations. In this meetup, we'll walk through the portfolio, share real-world performance data including CPU-based inference workloads, and we'll discuss a bit of the future. Whether you run databases, HPC, or web serving, come learn where Intel instances fit in your architecture.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: The Capability Overhang: Ask More of the Frontier (sponsored by Anthropic)
speaker: Matt Bleifer
abstract: Frontier models can do more than anyone asks of them. At Anthropic, the hardest part of testing a new model is finding work hard enough to make it fail. Outside, most teams hand Claude the tasks they gave last year's model. This session closes that gap: what the newest Claude models do on AWS when you delegate the job, not the task. Multi-day autonomous work, large migrations end to end, agents that verify their results and keep going. Evals, live demos, and how our researchers keep raising the bar. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: The cloud holodeck: Stream NVIDIA Omniverse, scale headless sim on AWS
speaker: Kurt Scheuringer, Dan Cotting
abstract: Interactive simulation needs RTX-class GPUs engineers lack; rendering millions of frames needs a fleet nobody wants to babysit. Amazon DCV streams a full NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim workstation from EC2 G instances to any browser, while AWS Batch runs the same scenes headless across GPU fleets for scale. The AWS Visual Asset Management System is the control plane: launching jobs, tracking runs, and versioning outputs. Walk through the architecture behind a cloud viewport and a thousand-run batch job.

title: The co-build playbook: Turn AWS partner programs into deployable industrial solutions (sponsored by Belden)
speaker: Fred Holahan, David Ricks
abstract: Manufacturers know their machines generate valuable data — yet most digital initiatives stall before they scale, trapped between legacy OT protocols and cloud analytics that were never designed for the plant floor. This session shows how a connected partner ecosystem closes that gap. Learn how Belden acquires, conditions, and secures data at the physical layer, and how Edge2Web Factory Insights turns that data into high-powered analytics and AI-enriched insights based on AWS IoT SiteWise. Discover the reference architecture behind a joint deployment, from edge protocol connectivity to AI-driven insight. See how co-development with AWS compressed the path from whiteboard to production. And explore how to apply this pattern to your own operations. This presentation is brought to you by Belden, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: The Cogs of a Well-oiled Software Factory
speaker: Graham Neubig
abstract: The "Software Factory" is a new buzzword for a fully autonomous agent driven software development process. Many organizations are trying to set up such a factory, but this is easier said than done. In this talk, from my experience setting up such factories for ourselves and other businesses, I will explain some of the elements of a software factory (issue triage, spec generation, implementation, review, and testing), and some of the pain points that we have experienced at each step. I will also cover how to evaluate the effectiveness of each of these steps and how to build a self-improvement pipeline so the factory gets better and better with feedback from its human supervisors.

title: The Control Plane for Your Agent Workforce: Governance, Cost and ROI at Scale (sponsored by Cognition)
abstract: Cognition has rolled out Devin, the autonomous software engineer, at the world's largest Fortune 500 companies. Along the way, we learned that scaling an agent workforce hinges on three questions every enterprise asks: How do we onboard agents? How do we know they're delivering value? How do we ensure they only do what they're supposed to? Drawing from real deployments, this session introduces the practical patterns we developed to answer them — governance, cost controls, ROI measurement, and federated configurations. You'll leave with a playbook for turning agents from a promising pilot into a trusted, scaled workforce. This presentation is brought to you by Cognition, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: The coordination decision: when to orchestrate and when to let go
speaker: John Dougherty, Aishwarya Subramaniam
abstract: Distributed workflows need coordination, and most teams pick one approach everywhere: a central orchestrator, or independent services reacting to events. Both fail at scale: orchestration bottlenecks every team's releases, and choreography lets flows stall silently because no component owns the outcome. This session teaches a per-flow method: does any component need to own the flow end-to-end, including completion, failure compensation, and ordering? Using a logistics platform running both patterns on AWS Step Functions and Amazon EventBridge, see the real costs of each, and where orchestration and events hand off.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: The cost of compute
abstract: AI demand is growing faster than the grid, the water supply, and the communities that host data centers can easily absorb. Voices from energy, policy, and global systems design lay out the real tradeoffs of scaling compute responsibly. Moving beyond isolated infrastructure metrics, they'll use complex systems thinking to evaluate the true footprint of AI. They'll explore where the power will come from, which efficiency gains are realistic, and how macro technology decisions directly impact equity, social justice, and local communities. You'll leave with the systems-level frameworks and language to bring true equity and global sustainability into your own infrastructure planning.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: The cost of over-engineering: When your architecture fights you
speaker: AMAN Raj, Nitin Kumar
abstract: Not every workload needs microservices, event-driven patterns, or serverless. Over-decomposed architectures create distributed monoliths, event spaghetti, and operational nightmares that cost more and move slower than the monolith they replaced. In this chalk talk, examine real-world anti-patterns: services split too small, queues added without purpose, and abstractions that add latency without value. We’ll whiteboard decision frameworks for right-sizing architecture, including the signals that tell you when decomposition earns its complexity and when it doesn’t. Bring your diagrams and discuss where simplification improves speed, reduces cost, and strengthens reliability. Leave able to right-size your own architecture with confidence.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: The Economics of an AWS Partner: Revenue, Incentives & AWS Marketplace
speaker: Jahnai Bilovsky, Snigdha Sahi
abstract: A forward-looking session reframing Partner economics for the year ahead. Revenue measurement is no longer just tracking, it's the backbone connecting all AWS Partner Programs. Walk away with a clear action plan to position for next year’s benefits.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: The economics of inference: Where startups are finding efficiency
speaker: Banghua Zhu, Brooke Mullen
abstract: AI companies are finding it harder to earn margins even as inference prices have dropped twentyfold. This session covers where startups are finding efficiency and margin in an environment of falling inference prices, and what RadixArk has learned about the economics of running AI workloads profitably as the underlying cost curve keeps shifting.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: The Evaluator Is the Algorithm: Evolving SOTA for $15
speaker: Rohit Malshe
abstract: We discovered a phase transition in LLM-guided code evolution: when the evaluation function provides smooth gradient signal, SOTA emerges automatically regardless of model choice; when it doesn't, no compute compensates. This "evaluator-dominance principle" emerged from stress-testing evolutionary search across 403 problems in 27 domains on Amazon Bedrock — 20× the scale of Google's original AlphaEvolve — achieving 96% SOTA-matching at $15/problem median cost. We'll present the Bedrock-native architecture (MAP-Elites, staged evaluation cascade, Opus/Haiku phase routing), a production vehicle routing deployment saving 1.28% on 100,000-customer routes at $530 total spend, and the evaluator design methodology that determines success or failure.

title: The FinOps Control Room
abstract: Your next AWS bill might not be driven by servers. It might be driven by tokens. AI is changing the economics of the cloud. Every model call, token, inference request, and autonomous agent introduces a new cost decision, and traditional cloud optimization alone isn’t enough. The FinOps Control Room brings practitioners together to investigate the economics behind modern AWS workloads, from infrastructure and architecture choices to AI inference, tokenomics, agent costs, and runaway usage. Expect real-world stories, practical strategies, and candid conversations on making AI and cloud spend visible, measurable, and accountable. Bring your toughest cost mystery. Let’s open the dashboard, follow the money, and figure out what’s really driving the bill.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: The Frontier Doesn't Hold Still: Running Claude Agents at Scale on AWS (sponsored by Anthropic)
speaker: Lauren Polansky, Daniel Xu
abstract: Enterprises are moving faster with AI than ever. And they're falling further behind. Once the first agents land and the numbers look good, most teams turn to cost control while the frontier keeps moving. This session covers how to do both with Claude on AWS: the security and compliance controls enterprises require, execution inside your own boundary, observability and cost governance, and the safeguards that let you trust agents with more. Then how to keep expanding what agents do as new models arrive, so efficiency doesn't become the ceiling. This presentation is brought to you by Anthropic, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: The future of Agents with Sierra and AWS
speaker: Deap Ubhi
abstract: Enterprise AI agents are reshaping customer experience, and success requires infrastructure and architecture built for enterprise scale. Join Pol Sanchez, founder of Sierra, in this fireside chat to explore the infrastructure demands that separate agents that work at scale from those that only work in demos: reliability, low latency, burst capacity, and the security and compliance posture that regulated industries demand. Discover why the winning architecture isn't locked to a single model. Instead, choose and swap models based on the task, with Amazon Bedrock enabling that diversity at scale. Learn how the future of agents extends beyond smarter individual agents to specialized agents collaborating directly in real conversations, sharing context, and resolving more customer issues in fewer interactions while keeping customers in control.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: The future of Kubernetes on AWS
speaker: Ray Qureshi, Vara Bonthu, Mike Stefaniak, Raghav Tripathi
abstract: Kubernetes has become a standard for organizations looking to modernize their application portfolios. AWS developed Amazon EKS to make Kubernetes more accessible to organizations of all sizes, helping them focus on what matters most for their businesses. In this session, join Amazon EKS product leadership to learn about the latest innovations and strategies for building Kubernetes platforms and applications faster, including building and orchestrating agents. Discover how various organizations use Amazon EKS to run their most demanding applications in the cloud, on premises, and at the edge.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: The Future of Security
speaker: Chet Kapoor
abstract: AI has changed security forever. For decades, security was built for humans: dashboards, queries, alerts. That model can no longer keep up when the system and threats are both moving at machine speed. The future of security runs on context, reasoning, and action. AI agents are now identifying security issues before they are exploited, validating and addressing them with increasing levels of autonomy. Join Chet Kapoor, AWS VP of Security, Search, and Observability, to see how AWS is building security for this new era. Hear how customers secure their agent workloads and how they use AWS services to build trust and enable autonomous systems to handle a growing range of security work.

title: The golden path for agentic workloads: safe by default on Amazon EKS
speaker: Dima Breydo, Tsahi Duek
abstract: Every team is shipping agentic apps, and they are landing on your platform faster than you can review them. As the platform team, you own the blast radius: untrusted code, over-broad permissions, and unbounded egress you never signed off on. This code talk walks through the controls that let you say yes safely. See how to enforce VM-level isolation for workloads running untrusted or AI-generated code. Learn how to scope identity and network egress so an agent reaches only what it should. Discover how to codify these as policy so every new agent inherits the guardrails by default.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: The Governance Gap Keeping AI Agents Out of Production (sponsored by WSO2)
speaker: Rania Khalaf
abstract: Every leader is under pressure to show AI value now. Some move fast, and agents sprawl across teams with no shared controls. Others lock everything down, and pilots never reach production. Both point to the same gap: governance maturity hasn't kept pace with agent speed. This talk covers how governance becomes an accelerator, not a blocker, to production AI. You’ll learn how to design identity, policy, and guardrails from day one, so agents ship with the same controls whether they run on AWS Bedrock, hybrid, or otherwise. Get the principles right early, and agents move from pilot to production without every team reinventing governance on their own. Takeaways: Why AI programs sprawl or stall, and what governance maturity looks like in between. How trusted AI governance turns into speed instead of slowing teams down. What governance principles to design in from day one, on AWS & beyond. This presentation is brought to you by WSO2, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: The judgment gap: when Terraform scans clean but fails the audit
speaker: Anton Babenko
abstract: Checkov, trivy, and Prowler check rules someone already wrote. SOC 2 CC6.1 is a sentence open to interpretation. Between them sits the judgment gap, where AI-generated Terraform for S3, CloudFront, API Gateway, and Lambda often lands. We map the gap on the whiteboard together: take real controls from SOC 2 and PCI DSS, set them against what scanner rules verify, and mark what is left over. Then we discuss what closes the remainder: better authoring-side skills, human review, multi-model review, or accepting the risk. Bring a control your team owns; we trace where its enforcement lives, or does not.

title: The Last Mile of Agentic AI: Get Agents Adopted with Bedrock & Quick
speaker: Morris Singer, Abhishek Maligehalli Shivalingaiah, Stanley Chukwuemeke, Abhinav Sarin, Martin Ristov
abstract: Your customers increasingly live inside an AI work surface, and your product needs to be there too. In this hands-on session, you'll take a SaaS product—its API and a simple agentic capability—and bring it into Amazon Quick using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll adapt it for AgentCore, wire up secure identity, then build Chat Agents, Research, Flows, and Apps that put your product's intelligence in front of users. Customers get your whole product in Quick, as-is. Walk out with a working reference pattern and the ability to spin up POCs for product leadership.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: The Mathematics of Backlogs: Why Your Queue Will Never Drain
speaker: Tejas Ghadge, Rajesh Kumar Pandey
abstract: Your consumers are healthy, your pods are green - yet your backlog isn't shrinking. Why? Because systems provisioned for steady-state have zero recovery capacity. In this chalk talk, we'll derive the formulas that govern backlog formation and drain, explore the non-linear utilization cliff where small traffic spikes become catastrophic, and work through the real-world complications: retry amplification, stale-message degradation, and multi-stage cascades. Bring your architectures - we'll whiteboard whether they can actually recover from failure, or just survive it.

title: The multi-account AWS Backup playbook: centralized data protection
speaker: Stuart Lupton, Mark Choi
abstract: Deploying AWS Backup across hundreds of accounts brings challenges that a single-account setup never surfaces: centralized policy enforcement, cross-account and cross-Region copy, delegated administration, and consistent compliance evidence across the organization. This chalk talk walks through the patterns that hold up in large AWS Organizations - backup policies at the OU level, delegated administrator setup, cross-account vaults, and monitoring that scales. Bring your toughest multi-account backup questions; we'll whiteboard the architecture and trade-offs together.
