speaker: Stuart Lupton, Mark Choi
abstract: Deploying AWS Backup across hundreds of accounts brings challenges that a single-account setup never surfaces: centralized policy enforcement, cross-account and cross-Region copy, delegated administration, and consistent compliance evidence across the organization. This chalk talk walks through the patterns that hold up in large AWS Organizations - backup policies at the OU level, delegated administrator setup, cross-account vaults, and monitoring that scales. Bring your toughest multi-account backup questions; we'll whiteboard the architecture and trade-offs together.

title: The Neuron Stack: Enabling open source ML solutions on AWS Trainium
speaker: Maen Suleiman, Gregory Chanan, Alex Nails, Jeff Boudier
abstract: The Neuron software stack has evolved into an open source-first architecture. Developers can read, modify, and contribute to the components that compile, optimize, and execute ML workloads on Trainium. This session covers how Neuron enables open source ML solutions on Trainium. We show what's open source, how it integrates with upstream projects like PyTorch and distributed training frameworks, and how developers use these tools without modifications. Attendees leave understanding the Neuron stack, which parts are open source, and how to use and contribute to them.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: The next chapter at eero. (sponsored by Amazon Eero)
speaker: Jackie Lipman, Megan Mullins
abstract: eero started in 2015 with the goal of bringing fast, reliable, mesh wifi into homes around the world. Since then, eero has continued to push the boundaries of what wifi can do. With the same effortless setup, cloud managed intelligence, and best in class reliability that they're known for, eero is now building networking solutions designed to perform at scale in the most demanding environments. In corporate headquarters, fulfillment centers, and multi-site locations, eero is proving that great networking can be quick to deploy, easy to manage, and much more cost effective than legacy solutions. It's the way networking should be.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: The Next Phase of AI for SRE: Distributed Reasoning for Enterprise Operations (sponsored by Ciroos)
speaker: Ananda Rajagopal
abstract: AI for SRE isn’t just a speed or accuracy problem; it’s a problem of deeper understanding. This session explores how team members across different domains in an enterprise can use a shared AI reasoning layer to operate production systems and collaborate effectively to increase reliability. We’ll show how this AI reasoning layer handles the extremes of alert storms and alert silence, catching deployment-triggered anomalies before they cause production impact. Learn how teams are moving beyond reactive dashboards, using state-of-the-art techniques to instantly correlate cross-domain telemetry, execute complex investigations, and achieve proactive reliability in dynamic cloud and hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by Ciroos, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: The Old Security Playbook Is Dead
speaker: Amy Herzog
abstract: The window between a vulnerability existing and being exploited has collapsed from years to minutes. As a result, standard security practices, such as patching SLAs, shift-left reviews, and traditional AppSec, are dead. Join AWS Chief Information Security Officer Amy Herzog as she shares how AWS reimagined security to stop AI-enabled threat actors. You will see the fundamentals AWS has enforced for decades, now running at machine speed, and learn what AWS does on both sides of the shared responsibility model. You will leave knowing what to change in your own operations to raise your security bar.

title: The Physical AI Toolchain: A Full-Stack Solution with AWS and NVIDIA (sponsored by NVIDIA)
speaker: Ali Shahrokni, Abhishek Srivastav
abstract: Get hands-on building a complete Physical AI pipeline using the AWS and NVIDIA toolchain. This workshop walks you through each stage—synthetic data generation with Isaac Sim, foundation model training with GR00T and Cosmos, digital twin simulation in Omniverse, edge deployment via IoT Greengrass, multi-robot orchestration with AgentCore, and continuous learning with SageMaker using NVIDIA OSMO. Walk away with a working blueprint you can apply to manufacturing, logistics, or autonomous systems. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

title: The rules for AI are being written right now and nobody’s watching
speaker: Sarah Eichten, Caroline McKee, Christina Mitine, Soumya Srinagesh Tulloss
abstract: The question isn’t if AI will change our future. It will. The question is who gets to shape it. The rules that will govern AI for the next decade are being written right now, and the people in those rooms will shape how trustworthy and fair these systems become. Yet the people shaping these rules don't reflect the full range of perspectives that AI will impact. This session brings together leaders who built their way into those rooms, turning that knowledge into real influence. Come find out what it takes to stop watching the rules get written and start writing them.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: The security you inherit: how the AWS platform protects your workloads by default
speaker: Matt Meck, Marshall Jones
abstract: Every organization has finite security resources. The more the platform handles, the more your team can focus on securing what is unique to your application — your data, your logic, your users. In this session, we explore the security capabilities built into the AWS platform that work before you write a single IAM policy. From threat intelligence that blocks malicious actors at the network edge, to Nitro's zero operator access architecture that eliminates an entire class of insider risk, to automated reasoning that mathematically proves your policies behave as intended — these are protections you inherit just by running on AWS. We also cover PrivateLink for eliminating public internet exposure, default encryption, and S3 Block Public Access. Understand what the platform already handles so you can direct your security investment where it matters most: the application layer.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: The state of commercial open source in the age of AI
speaker: Kamal Gupta, Kristy Cook, Thomas Dohmke, Jean-Francois Drweski
abstract: How do open source companies turn adoption into revenue? In this panel, four founders and operators dig into the hard parts of building a business on open source. They'll talk about what customers are willing to pay for when the code is free, where companies find it hard to make money, and why closing enterprise deals can be so challenging. And they'll explore what AI changes for open source companies, and what it doesn't. Expect a candid, practical conversation for founders building in the open. Join Matthieu Lavergne (Serena), Thomas Dohmke (CEO, Entire and ex-GitHub), Kamal Gupta (CEO, Omnistrate), and Kristy Cook (Union.ai, the team behind Flyte).
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: The Trade Desk's Cloud Journey: AI-Assisted Optimization to AI Agents
speaker: Shreyas Shah, Sharik Pahwa
abstract: The Trade Desk operates a real-time advertising platform on AWS, where infrastructure must handle massive scale while making bidding decisions in milliseconds. At that volume, cloud cost optimization is a continuous discipline, not a one-time audit. In this breakout, The Trade Desk shares how it moved from manual cost audits to an AI-assisted approach: an internal MCP server that lets AI agents investigate cost and usage data, surface savings across services like S3, NAT Gateway, EBS, and Graviton, and apply a repeatable method for optimizing workloads over time. You'll see how the team structured the agents, what they found, and where the approach is headed.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: The Web Wasn't Built for AI Agents. Now What? (sponsored by Oxylabs)
speaker: Patricija Zemaityte
abstract: What does it actually take to give AI agents reliable access to the live web? Explore how web scraping infrastructure is evolving to power the next generation of AI agents. In this presentation we'll discuss how to access fresh web data, turn messy webpages into agent-ready data, and enable agents to interact with websites — spend less time managing web access infrastructure and more time building agents that get things done. Because the future of AI isn't just about how smart our models are. It's about what we enable them to do. This presentation is brought to you by Oxylabs, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Think Beyond DevOps: SRE, SOC, and Compliance in One AWS DevOps Agent
speaker: Shaoyi Li, Richard Fan
abstract: As AI speeds up releases, continuous security control assurance and detecting threats in millions of telemetry signals get harder. We transformed AWS DevOps Agent into one agent for SRE, SOC and compliance, effectively addressing AI-era cloud security challenges in production. With AWS Config Conformance Packs for compliance-as-code and security MCP for finding triage, it produces point-in-time compliance and well-architected assessments, and drives alarm-triggered agentic SOC investigations within a controlled agent space, automating responses and keeping human-in-the-loop on high-risk mitigations only. You'll learn the methodology to design an agentic compliance and SOC solution that ports seamlessly into your own environment.

title: Think Beyond DevOps: SRE, SOC, and Compliance in One AWS DevOps Agent
speaker: Shaoyi Li, Richard Fan
abstract: As AI speeds up releases, continuous security control assurance and detecting threats in millions of telemetry signals get harder. We transformed AWS DevOps Agent into one agent for SRE, SOC and compliance, effectively addressing AI-era cloud security challenges in production. You'll learn the methodology to design an agentic compliance and SOC solution that ports seamlessly into your own environment.

title: Thinking agentic: What developers using Serverless need to know
speaker: Dhiraj Mahapatro, Heeki Park
abstract: You've been building event-driven, async systems for years. Agents are a new type of consumer in your existing architecture. In this chalk talk, we discuss what actually changes: reframing functions as tools with schema-first interfaces, managing agent state with storage and checkpoints, and handling non-deterministic failures from LLM calls. We walk through a practical path from "I have a serverless app" to "my app has agent capabilities," adding capabilities incrementally without rewriting what already works. Bring your architecture. We'll whiteboard where agents fit in what you've already built.

title: Thinking agentic: What developers using Serverless need to know
speaker: Dhiraj Mahapatro, Heeki Park
abstract: You've been building event-driven, async systems for years. Agents are a new type of consumer in your existing architecture. In this chalk talk, we discuss what actually changes: reframing functions as tools with schema-first interfaces, managing agent state with storage and checkpoints, and handling non-deterministic failures from LLM calls. room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan I

title: Thousands of Databases, $250 a Month: Operating an Agentic Database Estate on AWS (sponsored by CockroachDB)
speaker: David Joy
abstract: What if ~1,000 production-grade databases cost $250/month? Most teams pay more to keep a few clusters idle, each sized for peak load, running at 85–95% unused capacity and provisioned ticket by ticket. That model is breaking. AI agents create databases faster than platform teams can provision, secure or retire them. One engineering group grew from 13 databases to 392 in four months. At 1,000, managing one cluster at a time stops working. This session shifts focus to the estate with 3 architectural changes on AWS: - Separate storage from compute, eliminating upfront capacity. - Run isolated virtual clusters on shared hosts without creating sprawl. - Use agentic operations to observe the estate and recommend actions your team approves. See live demos, a reference architecture and cost model behind the numbers. Bring your hardest questions about running stateful workloads at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by CockroachDB, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Threat detection and IR in AgentCore workloads
speaker: Nima Fotouhi, Mike Saintcross
abstract: Step into an AWS environment where command-and-control callbacks from agent tools, exfiltrated credentials, and disabled safety guardrails occurred across AgentCore workloads. Your mission: detect, investigate, and respond. Using Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub alongside CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability, you'll triage findings, correlate security events with application traces, map entity relationships, isolate compromised resources, and build automated remediations. You'll leave with practical skills to secure AgentCore systems you can trust.

title: Threat Detection and Response on AWS: Reducing Noise, Acting Faster
abstract: AWS provides strong detection services, but many teams still struggle with too many alerts and slow response. This meetup brings together security engineers to share how they detect and respond to threats on AWS. We will discuss tuning GuardDuty and Security Hub findings, centralising logs with Security Lake, investigating with CloudTrail and Detective, automating response with EventBridge and Lambda, and running incident response exercises. We will also talk about what teams changed after real incidents and how they measure detection quality. Attendees are welcome to share their setups, questions and lessons learned.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Threat modeling the agentic SDLC: from user story to deployment
speaker: Brad Dispensa, ionut ionescu
abstract: "Threat modeling the agentic SDLC with ThreatForest Agentic development is speeding up, and traditional threat modeling assumes a person makes the decisions. In this code talk, you follow one process end to end. You threat model a user story with the autonomous threat modeling built into AWS Continuum, carry it through the developer workflow, and take it to deployment. You see how ThreatForest, an agentic tool built on the Strands framework, generates attack trees and MITRE ATT&CK mappings on its own, and how to build a mitigations catalog your organization can reuse. We also show where traditional threat modeling can be used for agentic systems."

title: Threat research: how attackers use AI to persist and how to evict them (sponsored by TrendAI™)
speaker: Tom Kellermann, Ashish Rajan
abstract: Patching a vulnerability doesn't remove an attacker who is already inside your environment, and AI workloads introduce new persistence surfaces: agents with standing permissions, compromised MCP servers, and poisoned vector stores that survive redeployment. In this session, a CISO and a threat research leader show how attackers establish persistence in modern environments and what to do about it. From long-lived IAM access keys to over-permissioned Amazon Bedrock agents, learn which persistence techniques to hunt first and how to evict attackers for good. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Threat technique catalog for AWS: practical controls for real TTPs
speaker: Shannon Brazil, Cydney Stude
abstract: Threat actors are evolving faster than ever, leveraging AI-generated exploits and automated attack tooling to move at machine speed. AWS CIRT sees these techniques firsthand across customer incidents of all sizes. The Threat Technique Catalog for AWS (TTC), extending the MITRE ATT&CK framework, documents these recurring TTPs with detection and mitigation guidance specific to AWS. This session covers how to turn observed attacker patterns into an advantage: build actionable detections and mitigations into your security operations before the next incident hits.

title: Token Counts to Business Impact: Measurable AI Architectures at Scale
speaker: John Masci, Pranav Sharma, Alex Iankoulski
abstract: As AI workloads scale, the question shifts from "what does this cost?" to "is this delivering real value?" The answer depends on your workload, architecture, and adoption maturity. We present progressive architecture patterns using agentic software development — from vibe-coding to cloud agents to self-hosted inference to custom models — with a live demo across the AWS AI Stack, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker HyperPod, and Trainium, showing how the right metrics evolve with your architecture. You'll leave with cost-per-outcome comparisons, spend controls that work at scale, and an ROI measurement framework with architecture patterns to implement across any AI workload.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Token-efficient retrieval for production AI agents (sponsored by Exa)
speaker: Louis Walsh
abstract: Most agent bills aren't driven by the model, they're driven by the context it's given. Raw web pages, HTML boilerplate, and 10 blue links padded with irrelevant text quietly multiply token spend and degrade answer quality. This lightning talk walks through how Exa engineered retrieval to hand LLMs exactly the text they need: neural search that returns precise passages instead of whole pages, highlight extraction tuned to the query, and context-budgeting techniques that cut input tokens dramatically without hurting accuracy. Using real production traces, we'll show how token-efficient retrieval changes the economics of agents at scale on AWS, and give you a practical checklist you can apply to any RAG or agent pipeline this week. This presentation is brought to you by Exa, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Tokenomics for AI on AWS: Local inference plus Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Spectro Cloud)
abstract: Power users in AI teams building on AWS face the challenge of frontier models delivering the best answers and token costs scaling with adoption. Not every prompt requires frontier models. The ones that do, belong on the best endpoint. This talk covers a working pattern for enterprise inference on AWS: PaletteAI Inference Launchpad running local open-weight models for routine requests, Amazon Bedrock as the burst target to extend capacity, and frontier models as needed for complex work. We will show how routing, quotas, and per-team attribution keep tokenomics predictable, so platform teams can enable AI adoption without inheriting the bill. This presentation is brought to you by Spectro Cloud, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Tokenomics: Model Routing and Real ROI from Every Token
abstract: Token use is growing fast as teams move generative AI and agents into production. Cutting usage is not the goal. Getting more value from every token is. Join peers to swap what is working. How do you match the right model to each task? When do routing, caching, or smaller models pay off? How do you stop agents from burning tokens in loops? And how do you show leaders the return, not just the bill? Bring your wins, your lessons, and your open questions. Leave with practical ideas you can try next week.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Tokenomics of attacks: how AWS defends you from AI-powered threats
speaker: Paul Bodmer, Alexandra Lee
abstract: AI isn't just transforming how we build, it's transforming how attackers exploit. In this session, AWS threat researchers share the intelligence they observe in real time: the prompts adversaries feed into AI systems, the tokenomics that make AI-powered attacks devastatingly scalable, and the shrinking window between vulnerability disclosure and weaponized exploitation. We'll share first-hand threat intel from MadPot, AWS's globally distributed honeypot network, and show how AWS protects AI-based workloads. You'll learn how AWS Active Threat Defense capabilities proactively block malicious infrastructure before it reaches your workloads, so you can innovate with AI confidently while staying ahead of emerging threats.

title: Tokenomics: Understanding What Your AI Actually Costs (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
speaker: ryan ries
abstract: Your AI pilot ran smoothly and stayed on budget. Then you launched, and the invoice was much higher than the estimate. This session breaks down why that happens and what to do about it. We'll walk through where AI spend actually goes once a system leaves the demo stage, why agentic AI costs differently than a simple chatbot, and how choosing the right model for each task, not just the flagship model for everything, can cut spend dramatically without hurting quality. You'll leave with a practical framework for tracking cost, avoiding common budgeting traps, and having a more confident conversation with finance the next time AI spend comes up. This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Too many tools: Building software in the age of agents
speaker: David Yanacek, Priyatam Mudivarti
abstract: AI now touches every stage of software delivery: coding assistants, autonomous agents, modernization tools, security scanners, operations, and the list grows every week. Which do you actually use, and when? This open discussion helps you make sense of the SDLC tooling landscape. Bring your scenario and we'll talk through it together: when to hand work to an autonomous agent versus a deterministic tool, how to chain AI across design, code, review, and operations without creating new bottlenecks, and how to avoid adopting every shiny agent at once. Leave with a plan for building software with AI, not just a tool list.

title: Too many tools: Building software in the age of agents
speaker: David Yanacek, Priyatam Mudivarti

room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: TP ICAP: Driving revenue through faster decisions with agentic AI
speaker: Shahen Bokhari, Animesh Kundu, Scott Harding
abstract: Trading opportunities slip away when teams can't synthesize fragmented data fast enough to act. In this session, global broker TP ICAP will share how it built First Mate on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, an AI sales-trading tool that uses generative AI to identify and act on opportunities in global markets more effectively. Discover how First Mate ingests real-time data, applies domain reasoning, and delivers actionable recommendations to brokers in seconds. We’ll discuss the architectural decisions and outcomes behind the journey from prototype to production. You’ll learn how to bring agentic AI to time-sensitive operations where speed-to-insight can drive revenue.

title: Trace Lineage From AI Endpoints and Models to Data
speaker: Nishchai JM, Karthik Devaraj
abstract: Every number in a dashboard and every answer from an AI agent rests on a chain of data you may not be able to see. Can you prove where it came from? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard one lineage graph connecting endpoints, models, jobs, and tables across your pipelines on Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon Athena, anchored on the AWS Glue Data Catalog. We trace a production number back to the tables that fed it, work out what breaks before a schema change ships, and have an AI agent show the provenance of its own answer.

title: Track cross-domain attack vectors with AWS Security Hub extended
speaker: Aliaksei Ivanou, Frank Schwarzenau
abstract: In this 20-minute lightning talk, see how AWS Security Hub Extended correlates signals across endpoint, identity, email, data, browser, and AI domains into a single attack narrative. We show how cross-domain correlation surfaces attack vectors invisible to any single tool, and how customers deploy preconfigured detection patterns for immediate value.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Train and deploy large-scale models with governance at every step
speaker: Paulo Pontes Vieira de Aragao, Amin Dashti
abstract: Training a large-scale model is the easy part. Getting it into production with the right data flowing in, governance enforced, and multiple deployment paths ready is where most teams stall. This chalk talk works through how to build one training pipeline on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, bring in enterprise data that amplifies model value while respecting data protection policies, and deploy the same model into Amazon Bedrock for inference or Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for agent orchestration. Governance follows the model at every step. No bolted-on compliance. You leave with an architecture you can build against immediately.

title: Training Agility’s Digit robot for manufacturing with Amazon SageMaker
speaker: rian Bogle
abstract: Agility Robotics' humanoid robot Digit is being trained for manufacturing work using Amazon SageMaker. This session walks through the training pipeline that gets Digit from simulation to real-world manufacturing tasks, covering the data, simulation, and SageMaker-based training workflow that makes it possible. You'll leave with a view into what it actually takes to get a humanoid robot production-ready for manufacturing environments.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Training and simulation turn robot capabilities into useful products
speaker: Natsuki Kataoka, Deap Ubhi, Arne Nordmann, Sam Sinha
abstract: Making humanoid and autonomous robots useful takes more than a capable chassis. In this panel moderated by Deap Ubhi, who leads startup Solutions Architects globally at AWS, leaders from NEURA Robotics, 1X, and Highlanders dig into the intelligence behind their robots: how they train and simulate behaviors, which AI models they rely on, and how data pipelines support development. They also explore the application layer that turns raw capability into products. Founders and robotics builders will hear how these teams connect training and simulation with real-world deployment.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Transform Episodic Content into High-Converting Microdramas
speaker: Saurav Bhattacharya, Chris Swan
abstract: Turn your episodic content into binge-worthy microdramas. In this session, you'll learn how to build both single- and multi-episode formats, multiply one source into a library of platform-ready content assets, and monetize a story in multiple ways including advertising, subscription, and social distribution. We'll walk through scroll-stopping production techniques optimized for vertical, mobile-first viewing, and the pacing and cliffhanger patterns that drive completion and re-watch rates. Leave with a repeatable workflow for producing microdrama series at scale and a clear playbook for turning your existing catalog into high-converting, platform-ready short-form videos.

title: Transforming business and SAP with Amazon Innovations
speaker: Soulat Khan, Paul Chen, Shankar Lakshmanan
abstract: The SAP landscape is changing, with customers not just asking “How can you help us migrate and run our SAP applications in the cloud?”, but instead: “How can you help us transform our business, simplify our business processes, and leverage AI to serve our customers and employees?”. Join this session to learn how our marquee customers are combining SAP modernization with Amazon's extensive portfolio to revolutionize customer experiences. You'll hear how customers are redefining customer experience and transforming business processes including finance procurement, manufacturing, operation etc by leveraging Pan-Amazon services, and AWS AI services alongside SAP.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Transforming Customer Experiences Through Tapestry’s Order Management (sponsored by Digitate)
speaker: Sonal Sharan, Asif Iqbal
abstract: Customers expect fast, personalized, and seamless experiences across every interaction with a brand. For Tapestry, connecting consumer feedback, sentiment, and operational signals is key to identifying issues that can impact customer experience and brand reputation. In this session, Sonal Sharan will share how Tapestry is leveraging ignio's AI Agents to continuously analyze these signals, surface emerging concerns, and provide real-time visibility into business-impacting issues. Intelligent workflows help prioritize and route issues for faster resolution, while actionable insights support more proactive customer engagement, resulting in a more connected, responsive, and customer-centric organization delivering exceptional experiences across Tapestry’s leading brands. This presentation is brought to you by Digitate, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Transforming legacy core to agentic AI with Nissan & Bread Financial
speaker: Kalyan Chunduri, Ilene Eng, Tim Gray
abstract: Legacy mainframe applications were built for stability, scale, and batch-oriented processing, but they were never designed to power real-time, intelligent, agentic experiences. Modernization changes that. Discover how Nissan reimagined core operations into a cloud-native platform designed for responsiveness, adaptability, and AI-ready workflows. Hear how Bread Financial is evolving beyond credit-processing architectures to accelerate innovation by decomposing monolithic capabilities into bounded context services, creating a modern foundation for autonomous workflows. See how both used AWS Transform to extract business rules from decades-old applications and Kiro to forward-engineer production-ready code. Learn how modernized applications unlock the architecture that makes agentic AI possible.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Transform your SaaS for the agentic AI era on Amazon ECS
speaker: Dhammika Sriyananda, Karthik Annamalaisamy
abstract: Your multi-tenant SaaS application runs on Amazon ECS. Now your customers expect AI-powered features but adding agents to an existing platform introduces new challenges, including tenant isolation for model access, per-tenant memory and conversation state, cost attribution across shared infrastructure, and agent orchestration at scale. In this workshop, you start with a working SaaS application on Amazon ECS and progressively add agentic capabilities. Implement tenant-aware agent routing, deploy agent tools with ECS task-level security boundaries, add persistent memory per tenant, scale agents, and govern tenant's token spend with rate limits, quotas, cost attribution. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Transform your SaaS for the agentic AI era on Amazon ECS
speaker: Karthik Annamalaisamy, Dhammika Sriyananda

title: Triomics speeds cancer trial matching with Amazon Bedrock
abstract: Triomics speeds up cancer clinical trial matching using Amazon Bedrock. This session covers how Triomics built its trial-matching pipeline on Bedrock, the challenges of applying AI to clinical trial workflows, and what it takes to speed up matching patients to trials in a high-stakes healthcare setting.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Trivia Night with Jeff Barr
abstract: Join AWS Chief Evangelist Jeff Barr for an unforgettable trivia night where teams will test their AWS expertise.
room: TAP Sports Bar (located in MGM Grand)

title: Troubleshooting and recovering failed Amazon ECS deployments
speaker: Mikhail Shapirov, Vikram Venkataraman
abstract: Your Amazon ECS deployment just failed: new tasks will not launch, traffic is not shifting, and your team needs to ship an update now. In this code talk, we live-troubleshoot real failures step by step, showing how to diagnose the root cause, recover the service, and build guardrails that prevent repeat failures. We then go further, using the AWS DevOps Agent and ECS remote MCP tools to diagnose issues faster by correlating signals and surfacing likely causes. You will leave with a repeatable troubleshooting playbook for ECS deployments, both manual and AI-assisted.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

We then go further, using the AWS DevOps Agent and ECS remote MCP tools to diagnose issues faster by correlating signals and surfacing likely causes. You will leave with a repeatable troubleshooting playbook for ECS deployments, both manual and AI-assisted.

title: Trust at Scale: Unlocking Enterprise Agentic AI (sponsored by Qlik)
speaker: James Welsh
abstract: Agentic AI dies at scale. It is easy to get one agent working on one dataset for one team. The challenge is trusting its answers across hundreds of thousands of users, regions, languages, regulators, and constantly changing data. AWS provides global infrastructure, security, data residency, and compliance controls to scale AI. Qlik provides trusted governed data, business context, and intelligence that agents can rely on. See how Amazon Bedrock and the Qlik MCP Server bring trusted Qlik intelligence to production agents and any LLM including Amazon Quick. Learn how enterprises can scale agentic AI without sacrificing trust governance or choice. This presentation is brought to you by Qlik, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Trust but verify: Building the audit loop for AI agents in production
speaker: Farzin Bagheri, Justin Ossai, Bhavini Bhatia, Vinodkumar Mandalapu, Simone Pomata
abstract: An AI agent can answer every request successfully and still make the wrong decision. In this builders’ session, you will build an end-to-end audit loop on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using Amazon CloudWatch for traces, AgentCore Evaluations to apply an LLM-as-a-judge against business rules, and AWS DevOps Agent to investigate alarms. Then watch a customer service agent refund a customer without required human approval, while traces show zero errors. Reconstruct the decision, and see the loop automatically surface what error monitoring misses.

title: Trusted intent: How Kiro proves your specs before writing any code
speaker: Nadia Labai, Brian Beach
abstract: Your AI agent writes code fast, but is it building what you actually meant? Kiro's requirements analysis goes far beyond asking an LLM to generate a spec. It combines auto-formalization, SMT solvers, and neuro-symbolic techniques to mathematically detect ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. In this session, learn how we turned decades of formal methods into a developer experience that feels like answering simple yes/no questions while catching the bugs that cost the most to fix.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Trust in Depth: Giving agents more freedom without losing control
speaker: Erin Kraemer, Cami Novelli-Killeen, Brooke Jamieson
abstract: You're accountable for what your AI agents do, but they act faster than anyone can review. So capable agents wait while the work piles up. There's a way out of that bind. Join this panel for a candid discussion of how you build trust across the agent lifecycle: scope the agent to its job, know which agents are acting, bound what it does and says, and see what it did after. Then learn how provable bounds let you set how far an agent goes, and prove it stays there. Come ready to question your own systems. Leave able to answer.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Roman I

title: Trusting agents in production: end-to-end security with AgentCore
speaker: Fei Yuan, Guilherme Greco
abstract: AI agents call APIs, access databases, and act on behalf of users, making security non-negotiable before you go to production. But they introduce new attack surfaces: persistent sessions, autonomous tool execution, and permissions that compound across steps. This session shows how to secure agents end to end with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: microVM isolation so sessions can't leak into each other, identity propagation so every action traces back to a user, Gateway policies that control which tools agents can reach, and Cedar authorization for least-privilege at every call. Leave with a blueprint for production.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Trusting an Autonomous Agent With Your Production Environment (sponsored by NeuBird)
speaker: Andrew Lee
abstract: The biggest barrier to autonomous operations isn't capability, it's trust.Handing an incident to an autonomous agent raises a fair question. How do you know it is not guessing from raw log lines. This session shows how NeuBird AI reasons over your live environment and shows the causal chain behind every root cause, not a coincidence in the metrics. We’ll examine the guardrails that make production deployment safe: VPC-native execution, zero external data retention, complete auditable reasoning paths, and human-gated action approvals. Learn how to safely transition from human-driven triage to trusted, autonomous production operations on your own terms. This presentation is brought to you by NeuBird, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Trust Issues: A Healthy Relationship With Your AI Agents (sponsored by MontyCloud)
speaker: Eric Morrissey
abstract: Your Cloud Center of Excellence needs a new operating model in the age of AI. Everyone is racing to build agents, but no one is governing them. MontyCloud is an AI-native, autonomous CloudOps platform built on one conviction. As agents become easy to create, value moves to trusted execution. Walk away with a blueprint for turning insights into governed workflows, and governed workflows into trusted outcomes. See a live demo where any agent, model, or tool acts only with the right context, identity, policy, approvals, and cost controls. Learn why the unit of value is the governed workflow. This presentation is brought to you by MontyCloud, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Trust the Agent, Keep the Keys: The Journey to Autonomous Operations (sponsored by PagerDuty)
speaker: Nick Whiley, Kevin Murray, Art Rogers, Alice McElroy
abstract: AI is shipping more code to production than ever before, but incidents are taking longer to resolve. Hear from peers at different stages of operational maturity, all testing out ways to put AI and automation to work so their teams get more time back for innovation. Panelists will share how they decide what's safe to automate outright, where to keep a human in or on the loop, and where full human judgment still matters. You'll hear what convinced them to hand over more control, what happened when it didn't go as planned, and how they cut toil without losing their grip on the systems they're accountable for. This presentation is brought to you by PagerDuty, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Turbocharge your Agentic Consulting Practice with Agentic Consultants
speaker: Raja N, Aaron Sempf, Lalit Khatter, kiran kumar ballari, Ansley Verzosa
abstract: Partners are building agentic consulting practices with human consultants, but what if they could deliver 10x more engagements by augmenting their teams with consulting agents? In this hands-on builders' session, work alongside a team of consulting agents that guide a human consultant through structured discovery — asking the right questions and validating assumptions — then build out business requirements, generate agent designs and AWS architectures, calculate ROI-backed financial models, and export ready-to-use Statement of Work — all in a single, AI-accelerated workflow you can take straight back to your practice.

title: Turn a Bee wearable into your re:Invent notetaking companion
speaker: Kourtney Meiss, Emerson Sklar
abstract: re:Invent keynotes don't slow down for note-taking. Last year's CEO keynote announced roughly 28 launches in two hours. Careful notes still leave you with names, not links. So build an agent that does the finding. Participants in this workshop will get a Bee Pioneer wearable: it transcribes while you listen, and a double-press bookmarks anything worth a deep dive. Your agent (Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock) reads the transcript and researches each announcement through the AWS MCP Server, producing one markdown file linking every launch to its docs. Then make it yours: benchmark cheaper models, post to Slack, or run it in the cloud.

speaker: Vijay Shekhar Rao, Michael Tschannen
abstract: Your AI agents pass the demo but struggle in production because of limited accountability and controls. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard a governance framework that closes the loop. You get governed agent accounts with AWS Control Tower, hard API boundaries with AWS Organizations policies, and runtime tool-access controls and behavior scoring in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. AWS Config detects drift from policy and triggers automated rollback. You leave with a repeatable, observe-score-remediate pattern for keeping AI agents operating within your policies."

title: Turn AWS Marketplace listings into self-service buyer journeys
speaker: Nora Zhang, Salvador Lopez Beneyto, Justin Cook
abstract: Make it easier for customers to find, subscribe and deploy your software in by providing a self-service path from evaluation to purchase. In this session, explore how to transform your AWS Marketplace listing using demos, free trials, AI-guided evaluation and usage-based pricing. Learn the repeatable patterns for reducing procurement delays, measuring buyer progression, activating listings, and directing qualified buyers.

title: Turning AI deserts into markets — 0 to 30+ countries in 18 months
speaker: Moritz Amann
abstract: There is a major gap between what AI can achieve and where enterprises are extracting value from it today. Closing that gap requires strong execution, deep partnerships and a new approach to implementation. Drawing on Wonderful’s experience across 100+ deployments in 35+ markets, Moritz Amann, GTM Switzerland, will explain what it takes to put AI into production across entire enterprises and workflows, particularly in fast-moving, complex markets. The session will explore how enterprises can use the AWS ecosystem to move beyond isolated AI initiatives and deploy AI at scale without compromising security, compliance or governance. Attendees will leave with a practical view of the infrastructure, integrations and implementation discipline required to turn AI’s potential into measurable enterprise value.

speaker: Dominic Smith, Jonny Skerratt
abstract: Abstract: PwC-built Generative AI data processing solution for Pacific Life Re, hosted on AWS. The solution automates the ingestion, transformation, validation, schema mapping, and PII redaction of client actuarial datasets that arrive in different formats, languages, and quality levels. In short, it helps PLRe move from manual, time-consuming data preparation to a secure, auditable, AI-enabled workflow that can reduce processing times from weeks to days, improve data quality, and provide clean, validated outputs for actuarial, pricing, and R&D teams. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Turn PQC readiness into the trust story your board needs
speaker: Angela Morrison, Jonathan Jenkyn
abstract: Organizations planning post-quantum cryptography (PQC) migrations face the same three questions: where do I start my migration plan, which workloads do I prioritize, and how do I get buy-in from leadership? With NIST PQC standards finalized, the algorithm question is settled, the open question is how to plan and fund the transition. In this chalk talk we whiteboard the PQC Readiness Maturity Model: five levels from discovery to quantum-ready, each with measurable milestones. You leave with a practical framework to scope your inventory, prioritize transitions, modernize how you protect data, and build the board narrative that funds your migration program.

title: Turn security logs into actionable intelligence
speaker: Dan Girard, Erik Weber, Yohan Ponniah, Rafael Pereyra, Thomas Sceifers
abstract: Security teams drown in logs but struggle to investigate fast. In this hands-on session, turn raw security telemetry from CloudTrail, S3 access logs, and VPC flow logs into actionable intelligence with Amazon CloudWatch. We'll centralize logs in the CloudWatch Unified Data Store, then query across sources to investigate real scenarios: after-hours data access, credential misuse, and exfiltration patterns. You'll build a security dashboard that surfaces who did what, from where, and when. Walk away with reusable queries and dashboards you can deploy in your own accounts, moving from reactive log search to proactive security visibility.

speaker: Rochak Karki, Shivam Patel
abstract: Forward-looking organizations aren't just migrating to AWS — they're using migration to transform their entire security posture. You'll use Amazon GuardDuty to detect runtime-level threats and malware, Amazon Inspector to prioritize software vulnerabilities, and AWS Security Hub to correlate findings into actionable exposures. You'll finish by building an automated remediation pipeline that isolates compromised resources without human intervention. Leave with a repeatable Day 1 security playbook for any migrated workload. title: Turn your coding agent into an always-on dev team with AgentCore
speaker: Mark Benyovszky, Prajit Pabbati
abstract: Claude Code, Kiro, and Codex are impressive individually, but in an enterprise they run stateless, isolated from team context, and invisible to governance. AgentCore turns any coding agent into a production system: shared memory so the agent understands your architecture across sessions, microVM isolation so jobs run in parallel without interference, identity propagation so agents access only what they should, and full trace observability so you know what every agent did and why. This session shows what changes when you pair popular coding agents with a production platform, and how our customer deployed this across hundreds of developers.

title: Twenty years of cloud architecture
speaker: Colm MacCarthaigh
abstract: Instant, vast scale and elasticity. Infrastructure as Code. Eventual consistency. Immutable infrastructure. Serverless. Event-driven computing. Internet of Things. Chaos engineering. Zero trust. Pervasive observability. Twenty years of cloud have produced an extraordinary density of patterns — each arriving with conviction and shaping what came next. Some became invisible foundations we build on without thinking. Others evolved in ways nobody predicted. And the evolution continues — now with agentic architectures. What has stood the test of time? What's still evolving? And what can we learn to be ready for the next twenty years?

title: Unattended Coding Agents: Memory, Guardrails, and Cost Control - Kiro Crew
abstract: Your coding agents behave for ten minutes. Overnight, they lose context, repeat mistakes you already corrected, burn credits nobody budgeted, and leave work you can't verify. This meetup is for people past the demo, running agents on schedules, in CI, or across repos. Bring one thing that broke. We'll compare how teams keep memory across sessions, scope write permissions when nobody is approving, track what each agent costs, and prove agent output before merge, builders who run Kiro agent fleets unattended daily. A working session, not a product demo.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

abstract: Your CX data already knows where automation will pay off. See Agentic Analytics pinpoint the opportunity, then watch that recommendation become a working AI agent — built, tested, and scaled live. ​ This presentation is brought to you by NiCE, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Understand your network: practical network observability on AWS
speaker: Leonardo Solano, Claudia Izquierdo
abstract: You're collecting Amazon VPC Flow Logs and Amazon CloudWatch metrics, but still can't answer "why can't this instance reach the internet?" In this chalk talk, explore practical approaches to network observability on AWS, no deep expertise required. Cover the key logs and metrics that actually matter, how to read them, and how to set up simple dashboards and alerts that tell you something is wrong before your users do. Bring your monitoring questions, and we'll discuss real scenarios to help you build observability that works for your team.

title: Under the hood of Kiro Crew: orchestration, memory, and safe autonomy
speaker: kirankumar chandrashekar, Ryan Yanchuleff, Chris Abbey
abstract: Handing real work to a crew of agents raises real questions: How does it coordinate parallel subagents without losing the thread? How does memory save across sessions so agents don't start cold? How do you give agents access to your code and CI while staying safe? In this chalk talk, we'll dig into how Kiro Crew works: observable multi-agent orchestration over Agent Client Protocol, self-evolving memory and skills you can inspect and edit, scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs, and defense-in-depth security with sandboxing, denied-by-default commands, and signed audit logs. Bring your architecture and security questions and we'll whiteboard through them.

title: Under the hood with Amazon EBS: Achieving sub-millisecond latency
speaker: Kirill Davydychev, Swapnil Dinkar
abstract: Amazon EBS powers mission-critical applications with consistent sub-millisecond latency across millions of volumes. This session offers a behind-the-scenes look at the architectural innovations and engineering practices that make this possible. Learn how EBS leverages the AWS Nitro System, purpose-built hardware, and advanced I/O path optimizations to deliver reliable low-latency performance at hyperscale. Gain insights into how these capabilities translate into performance benefits for databases, analytics platforms, and latency-sensitive workloads.

title: Unexpected resilience: Lessons from a thousand incidents
speaker: Giorgio Bonfiglio, Steve Bruggeman
abstract: After years of investigating incidents - both within AWS and across customer industries - some resilience lessons stand out. Not the obvious ones, but surprises no runbook could anticipate. We share the strangest, most counterintuitive findings from years of troubleshooting under pressure: failure modes nobody planned for, fixes that made things worse, and patterns that only emerge after enough failures. This isn't a best-practices talk - it's a field guide to building resilience from the unexpected. You'll leave with a sharper eye for hidden risks in your infrastructure - and fresh leads on things you didn't know were there.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Unified commerce intelligence for Amazon Vendors on AWS Quick
speaker: Duncan Watson, Manikanta Gona Grafsgaard
abstract: Vendors selling on Amazon generate rich signals across commerce and advertising—order trends, catalog performance, competitive pricing, campaign metrics, and customer engagement. The opportunity lies in connecting these signals into a unified view that drives faster, smarter decisions. In this chalk talk, we design an architecture composing two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers—the SP-API MCP Server for Selling Partner operations and the Amazon Ads MCP Server for campaigns—behind AWS Quick as a conversational layer. We whiteboard cross-domain queries like correlating ad spend with order velocity or surfacing catalog insights that inform campaign strategy.

title: Unified observability with Amazon OpenSearch Service
speaker: Alex Tarasov, Aruna Govindaraju, Cedric Pelvet, Jay Agnihotri
abstract: Most teams run observability across fragmented tools: one for metrics, another for logs and traces, each with its own cost model and blind spots. In this session, you work hands-on to consolidate your observability stack on Amazon OpenSearch Service. You integrate Amazon Managed Prometheus for metrics, configure native OpenTelemetry ingestion for traces and logs, and see how a single pane of glass eliminates the context-switching that slows down investigations. Then you optimize for cost and scale: warm tiering, direct query for infrequently accessed data, and O-series instances for log-heavy workloads. Finally, you use AI-powered investigation to perform natural-language root-cause analysis across your unified telemetry and monitor your agents' behavior in production. You leave with a working observability setup that scales, costs less, and investigates faster.

title: Unifying fragmented data: A lakehouse for the agentic AI era
speaker: Prasad Shetty, Himanshu Sahni
abstract: Financial services organizations face growing data volumes, strict regulations, and architectures where siloed warehouses and separate data lakes fragment data, drive up costs, and slow insights. In this chalk talk, we walk through a modern Lakehouse architecture on AWS that combines the cost benefits of data lakes with the governance and performance of data warehouses. We explain how Amazon S3 Tables with managed Apache Iceberg and AWS Glue Catalog semantic search deliver a single governed data foundation supporting agentic AI, traditional AI/ML, and analytics workloads. Learn practical patterns for a scalable Lakehouse you can apply immediately.

title: Unlock cost efficiency with Graviton savings tools
speaker: Rosa Corley, Rajani Guptan
abstract: While AWS Graviton delivers up to 40% better price-performance, uncovering those savings across your fleet shouldn't take weeks of manual analysis. Building a concrete migration plan for a specific environment is where teams get stuck. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an Amazon Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities over time. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill that any AI coding agent can run against your accounts to produce a prioritized migration roadmap on demand. This lightning talk demonstrates both tools against a real-world scenario, showing how to analyze compute usage, visualize potential savings, and turn efficiency insights into actionable migration plans you can use to accelerate your Graviton adoption.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Unlocking inference: How OpenRouter scaled to 10M+ users with AWS
speaker: Glenn Rachlin
abstract: As AI moves from experimentation to production, developers want access to every leading model through one simple interface. OpenRouter and Amazon Bedrock unlock this access for millions of customers. In this lightning talk, OpenRouter's Head of GTM, Glenn Rachlin shares how the two companies partnered to support that hypergrowth. Learn what it takes to scale an AI platform globally, how startups and AWS can grow together, and what OpenRouter's journey shows about where AI adoption is heading.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

abstract: Critical business data remains locked inside SAP ERP and BW systems, limiting real-time insights and AI-driven automation. In this hands-on workshop, learn how to break down data silos using a modern, cost-effective architecture without expensive ETL pipelines. Explore a unified analytics strategy spanning Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS-native services that enables end-to-end SAP data modernization. Then, build with the AWS for SAP MCP Server, enabling agentic AI to orchestrate across SAP, Salesforce, and AWS without writing code.

title: Unlock intelligent AI with MCP-powered agentic Neptune graph reasoning
speaker: Melissa Kwok, Kelvin Lawrence
abstract: Graph-based agentic reasoning empowers AI systems to dynamically interact with the rich context and relationships in an Amazon Neptune graph, enabling intelligent, flexible, and scalable AI solutions that extract valuable insights from complex, interconnected data. In this session, build a generative AI application for investment analysis spanning the full lifecycle, from raw unstructured data to autonomous AI agents, by combining Neptune, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Construct autonomous AI workflows that extract entities and relationships from raw EDGAR data, build a domain knowledge graph, surface actionable insights from graph relationships, and build an agent to find investment analysis trends. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Unlock Secure Vibe Coding on AWS Today (sponsored by Superblocks)
abstract: Your business teams already build apps with AI, often on real company data. Most of those apps never make it to production. The rest run without guardrails, and IT can't see who built what or what data it touches. Blocking the tools doesn't stop the building. This session lays out a third option: a reference blueprint for governed vibe coding in your own AWS account. Learn how to set guardrails once for every AI-built app, catch vulnerable code before it ships, keep a full audit trail, and make sure every app still has an owner when its builder leaves. This presentation is brought to you by Superblocks, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Unlock Workday data with AWS: Building Trustworthy Agents (sponsored by Workday)
speaker: Mark McCauley
abstract: Generative AI agents and analytics in AWS are only as effective as the enterprise context behind them. While tools like Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Quick deliver powerful reasoning capabilities, grounding those models in authoritative, real-time HR and financial data traditionally requires complex ETL pipelines, custom integrations, and data duplication. In this session, we’ll demonstrate how Workday natively bridges this gap on AWS. Through live cross-system AI agent demos, you’ll see how to deliver unified, real-time enterprise insights without writing ETL code or moving data. This presentation is brought to you by Workday, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Unlock your AWS Graviton potential using Graviton Savings Dashboard and AI skills
speaker: Rosa Corley, Rajani Guptan, Bhavik Gandhi, Julio Chaves, Jake Wolf
abstract: How much can you save by migrating to Graviton? In this builder session, explore two complementary ways to answer it, hands-on. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an AWS Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill any AI coding agent runs against your cost and usage data to produce a prioritized migration plan. Use both tools against a sample fleet, identify migration candidates, and see how quickly cost data becomes a migration strategy. Walk away with actionable insights and a deployment kit for your own accounts.

title: Unlock your S3 data for AI agents
speaker: Majisha Namath Parambath, Harsha Battapady
abstract: You’ve built a rich data lake in Amazon S3. Now how do your AI agents actually find and use that data? In this chalk talk, explore patterns for connecting AI agents to S3 resources, including S3 Tables, S3 Metadata, and annotations, with real-time, governed access. Learn how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit for AWS help agents discover and operate on your data, how the AWS Context knowledge graph surfaces relationships agents can reason over, and how curated skills handle common data lake and analytics workflows. Bring your questions as we discuss permission boundaries and practical integration patterns.

title: Use AWS Continuum to move from annual pentesting to continuous security
speaker: Jeremy Schiefer, Cameron Smith
abstract: AI coding tools can make developers 10–20x more productive and yet many organizations may only be able to pentest critical apps once a year. The rest need to go untested entirely. In this builders' session, use AWS Security Agent (now part of Continuum) to run an on-demand penetration test against a live application. You'll triage findings by exploitability, validate real-world impact, and apply automated code remediations. Leave with prescriptive next steps to scan your own applications using a frontier AI agent that secures workloads from design through deployment. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Using AI for Impact: Achieving Sustainability and ROI on AWS
speaker: Steffen Grunwald, Francesca Stobbione, Alexis Bateman
abstract: AI is accelerating sustainability at unprecedented speed, but only if the infrastructure behind it keeps pace. In this session, we will explore how AWS makes AI infrastructure more sustainable through hardware design decisions that minimize embodied carbon, custom silicon optimized for energy efficiency, and ML-driven data center optimization. Amazon Operations will show how AI and ML turn facility maintenance into prescriptive, autonomous operations: optimizing HVAC, water, and utilities for greater equipment reliability, and sustainability. Leave with a clear understanding of the AWS services powering these solutions, how AWS is building a more sustainable infrastructure, and how to get started with tracking and reducing your environmental impact.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Using AI to scale legacy app modernization with Experian & Itaú
speaker: Gaurav Arora, Douglas Suryan, Paulo Vitor Pereira
abstract: A successful modernization approach only matters if it scales beyond the first pilot. Experian and Itaú share how they grew their approach with AWS Transform and Kiro from a single engagement into an enterprise-wide operating model. Experian compresses mainframe analysis from months to days, then standardizes modernization across 550+ workloads and multiple regions with a fully agentic reverse-engineering pipeline. Itaú expanded to 43 business domains, processing nearly 140 million lines of code in a single month. Leave with the operating models that scale modernization from one application to the entire portfolio, unlocking AI-driven capabilities along the way.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Red Theater

speaker: Tom Lawlor
abstract: In this session, you will be given time to attempt a microcredential exam of your choice on AWS Skill Builder. These timed, hands-on exams test your skills in a live, provisioned AWS environment and test on popular topics. The product and developer team will be onsite to walk you through the UI and introduce the exam. title: Vector search, agents, and image matching with Amazon DynamoDB
speaker: Deepthi Mohan, Mo Kamioner, Arjan Schaaf, Greg Krumm, Lee Hannigan
abstract: Amazon DynamoDB supports native vector search, enabling semantic queries, agentic recommendations, and image-based matching without additional infrastructure. In this session, explore how to design a single-table data model for a recipe database, bulk-load thousands of items with embeddings, and build three vector-powered features: semantic search, a smart recommendation agent, and image-based meal matching. Learn how to configure vector indexes, composite keys, and global secondary indexes on a fully serverless stack, and leave with reusable patterns to add vector search to your own DynamoDB workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Verifying Post-Quantum Cryptography at Speed
speaker: Hanno Becker
abstract: Traditionally, cryptographic engineering involves a performance/assurance trade-off: clean code is easy to audit and maintain, yet slow; handwritten assembly is fast, yet hard to validate. Discover how automated reasoning helps to overcome this tension, following the example of mlkem-native and mldsa-native, two open-source post-quantum cryptography libraries co-maintained by AWS and deployed in AWS-LC, Amazon's cryptography library. In these libraries, constraint solving enables automated superoptimization at the assembly level, while formal verification vets the result. Contrary to the popular belief that assurance costs speed, it is automated reasoning that enables deep optimization, verification and rapid deployment of cryptographic code at cloud scale.

title: Vertiv’s Amazon Quick Journey: Scaling Agentic AI Globally with Deloitte & AWS (sponsored by Deloitte)
speaker: Mohamad Said, Bhavik Rao
abstract: Vertiv, a global digital infrastructure company, faced fragmented AI experimentation, limited accessibility, and complex enterprise integrational barriers preventing consistent scaling. Vertiv's AI journey began with VeGA, a GenAI platform turned agentic with their recent release of VeGA 3.0. Powered by Amazon Quick, it enables employees to generate content, automate workflows, and create custom applications. In one year, nearly one-third of the workforce was registered in VeGA, spanning functions across all functions and regions. Attendees will learn the architectural blueprint for evolving from basic AI assistants to intelligent agentic systems, including connectors used, data streamlining strategies, and practical implementation steps. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Virtualization Architecture Behind AgentCore's Runtime Security Model
speaker: Marc Brooker
abstract: Journey into the sophisticated virtualization architecture that powers AgentCore's runtime security model. This session examines the intricate mechanics of session isolation at the virtualization layer, exploring advanced techniques in compute and memory virtualization, virtual machine snapshot optimization, and virtual memory deduplication. Drawing from operating systems research and systems security principles, we'll demonstrate how these components work together to create robust security boundaries for agent workloads. Attendees will gain deep technical insights into the mathematical and systems-level concepts that position AWS at the forefront of secure agent runtime architectures, showcasing our industry-leading approach to securing code execution in agent environments.

title: Visa: Building autonomous defense for payments security in the agentic AI era
speaker: Luke Wilson, Vaijayanti Korde, Gaurav Priyolkar
abstract: Visa secures one of the world's largest payment ecosystems, processing over $14 trillion across 300+ billion transactions annually. As AI-powered threats evolve, Visa is reimagining cybersecurity through hybrid-cloud architecture with 70+ controls framework, AI-driven operations, and an agentic control plane designed for autonomous defense. Built on an Agentic harness with Zero-Trust principles and AWS capabilities, such as Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Nitro Enclaves, and cloud-agnostic security controls, Visa continuously detects and mitigates risk across its cloud environment. Discover how Visa is building a security foundation for the agentic AI era, protecting today's payments ecosystem while enabling AI-powered applications and autonomous workloads.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Visualize and interpret domain knowledge graphs using AI
speaker: Colin Marden, Ana Suja Lucia, Jun Zhang, Marco Masciola, Kenta Sato
abstract: Complex systems like supply chains, energy grids, and decarbonization efforts are difficult to model because relationships between actors are hidden across siloed data. A knowledge graph can surface these connections, helping organizations simulate what-if scenarios and act on high impact opportunities. In this builder session, use Amazon Neptune to construct an ontology-typed knowledge graph that maps stakeholder dependencies and sustainability regulatory impacts. Then simulate competing interventions and use an Amazon Bedrock agent to interpret which action drives the broadest impact. Leave with a reusable pattern for modeling complex systems and identifying high-leverage intervention points.

title: Visualizing agent identity privileges to monitor multi-agent behavior
speaker: Alex Waddell, Meg Peddada
abstract: If one of your AI agents quietly gained admin-level access right now, would you know? In multi-agent systems, each handoff between agents can widen permissions, and traditional monitoring won't catch it. In this code talk, we build a real-time graph answering three questions: who are my agents, what can each one do, and what can they reach through each other? We connect IAM roles, Cedar policies, and CloudWatch data into one visual map, then add alerts that fire the instant any permission chain exceeds what you defined. You leave with the tool that catches it first.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Visualizing multi-tenant isolation: Catch your noisy neighbors
speaker: Amit Lulla, Sam Sanders
abstract: Managing multi-tenant platforms forces trade-offs between cost, complexity, and performance. This session tackles two common challenges: tenant data isolation and the noisy-neighbor problem. Starting from a single-tenant architecture, you consolidate into a shared Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster, building isolation through Cognito-issued JWTs, Lambda-based dynamic policy generation, IAM authentication, and RDS Proxy connection pooling. Then you implement queuing tiers with Amazon SQS to manage load. Visualize real-time request flows, data isolation, and noisy-neighbor effects on your own dynamic architecture simulation and a central 16,000-LED display. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Visual reasoning will be bigger than language reasoning
speaker: Ranjay Krishna
abstract: Today’s vision-language models can describe images fluently, yet still struggle with the spatial and perceptual reasoning required for robotics. This talk argues that visual reasoning—reasoning through points, sketches, trajectories, depth maps, and other grounded representations—will become more important than language reasoning for physical agents. It traces progress from benchmarks exposing fundamental perception failures to methods that teach models to reason directly in visual space. These ideas culminate in robotics foundation models that convert visual plans into robot actions. The resulting systems are interpretable, steerable, deployable zero-shot on affordable hardware, and competitive with proprietary models trained on substantially more data. We showcase how these ideas are advancing the goal of accessible, general-purpose robotics to the broader research community.

title: VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts with AWS Transform
speaker: Aditya Lolla, Gokul Chandra Purnachandra Reddy
abstract: Many organizations struggle to migrate VMware workloads due to complex dependencies, network translation challenges, and the need to support both cloud and on-premises targets. In this workshop, you use AWS Transform MGN, an agentic AI service, to execute an end-to-end VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts. You work through AI-driven discovery, dependency mapping, intelligent wave planning, automated network conversion, and orchestrated execution. See how Trianz's Concierto platform also integrates with AWS Transform to streamline migration to AWS Outposts with automated orchestration and operational governance.

title: Voice AI on AWS silicon: Cartesia’s AWS Trainium stack
speaker: Arjun Desai
abstract: Cartesia built a voice AI platform that runs end-to-end latency on AWS Trainium silicon. This session covers how Cartesia architected their stack to hit that latency bar, the tradeoffs of building on custom silicon, and what it takes to make voice AI feel truly real-time in production.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Warehouse Alchemy: How Eni's AI agents cut days of sourcing to minutes
speaker: Andrea Corneo, Paolo Romagnoli
abstract: Eni operates one of the world's most complex upstream supply chains, managing exploration and production materials across warehouses on multiple continents. Tubular items alone represent €1.5 billion out of a €2.5 billion inventory — scattered across dozens of facilities with fragmented visibility. Engineers searching for available spare parts faced a manual, days-long process of cross-referencing spreadsheets, navigating import restrictions, certifications, third-party stock, and delivery schedules — often resulting in unnecessary new purchases while surplus materials sat idle in distant warehouses. With Eni's expansion into fast-track development, biofuel production, and CCUS, the traditional material management approach couldn't keep pace with the speed and complexity of global operations.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Watch AWS Transform convert SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL live
speaker: Prasad Rao, Alexander Dragunov
abstract: Modernizing SQL Server and its dependent .NET applications to Aurora PostgreSQL typically requires months of manual effort across schema conversion, stored procedure rewriting, and application code changes. In this code talk, see how AWS Transform uses agentic AI to automate this journey end-to-end. Through a live walkthrough, we'll showcase complex schema transformations, T-SQL to PL/pgSQL stored procedure conversions, Entity Framework provider updates, and wave-based orchestration of multi-database estates with human-in-the-loop validation checkpoints. Ask questions throughout. Leave with patterns for modernizing SQL Server at scale.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Well-Architected in your AI coding agent: Find gaps before you commit
speaker: Ibrahim Cesar, Kevin Hakanson, Murithi Gitonga, Swapnil Singh, Aaron Castellanos
abstract: Architecture reviews happen at milestones: a design review here, an operational readiness check there. But AI coding agents make architectural decisions dozens of times a day, and governance that runs at milestone pace can't keep up. In this session, you will configure open-source Well-Architected skills in your coding agent, run a full Well-Architected review and catch resilience, security, and operational gaps in minutes. Then author a custom skill that encodes your team's standards and trade-offs. You leave with a review loop that runs every commit. Bring your laptop to participate.
