title: What AI can't automate
speaker: Kelsey Hightower
abstract: You're being asked to automate more of your own work every quarter. Kelsey Hightower, one of the most trusted voices in cloud-native, talks through what intelligent automation actually means for platform engineering: which parts of building and running software it will absorb and which parts of your judgment become more valuable. Expect candid opinions on platform teams, developer experience, and the habits that still separate good systems from fragile ones, leaving you with a sharper sense of where to spend your time as the manual work disappears.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: What Building an SRE Agent Taught Us About Agents at Scale
speaker: Dipin Thomas, Arshad Zackeriya, Geethika Guruge
abstract: Anyone can wire up an agent, but operating one safely and cheaply across thousands of sessions is where developer craft begins. Grounded in a production SRE agent we built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK, this session dissects engineering around agentic models: session isolation, context management, and least privilege identity. What broke, and how we fixed it: an agent with too much access, context bloat that wrecked cost, a crash during a tool call that forced durable recovery. You will see where architectures leak, how to evaluate on production traces, and tradeoffs behind resilient agent infrastructure.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: What Can Neurosymbolic AI Prove About Agent Behavior?
speaker: Nadia Labai
abstract: AI agents that write and execute code autonomously create a fundamental trust problem: how do you guarantee behavioral boundaries without constraining the flexibility that makes agents useful? This chalk talk examines how neurosymbolic AI is making provable guarantees practical at scale: autoformalization translating natural-language constraints into temporal logic, satisfiability solvers whose exponential improvement keeps pace with exponentially harder verification problems, and LLMs guiding proof search in theorem provers like Lean, creating a virtuous cycle where better proofs yield stronger provers. We'll stratify what can be proved today, what requires LLM-discovered inductive invariants, and where undecidability still draws a hard line.

title: What FanDuel learned running containers on dozens of AWS Outposts
speaker: Santosh Vallurupalli, Ramsey McGrath, Josh Coen
abstract: Running containerized workloads across dozens of AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts demands operational patterns that hold up at fleet scale. In this session, learn how FanDuel operates Amazon EKS across a huge hybrid edge fleet with a focus on high availability, patching, observability, service disruption handling, and autoscaling. The session digs into how workloads respond gracefully to service link and hardware disruptions, and how autoscaling behaves when compute is fixed and on-rack. Discover the operational model that keeps a large edge fleet healthy without growing the platform team at the same rate.

title: What happens in Bedrock stays in Bedrock
speaker: Steve Kendrex, Chase Kernan
abstract: You want to ship AI, but your compliance team won't sign off until the solution meets their regulatory requirements. This session shows how Bedrock protects data from the hardware up, with zero operator access enforced at the chip so no one, not even AWS operators, can access your prompts and completions. See how data residency controls and strict workload separation extend that protection, and how those guarantees map to the compliance frameworks your teams already use. Use what you learn to make the security case for approving your AI workload.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: What makes a model trustworthy?
speaker: Aysen Ilkbahar, Eric Burns
abstract: Every team shipping AI has to pick a model that fits the use case and own the trade-offs that come with it. Kay Firth-Butterfield leads Anthropic, NVIDIA, and Reflection through how they think about that choice: what weights mean for customization and control, when building smaller models on an open base pays off, and how to balance trust and safety against what the use case needs. No two use cases are alike, so expect trade-offs and judgment calls instead of a checklist.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: What's new and what's next for Amazon ECS
speaker: Rayman Aeron, Alexandr Moroz
abstract: Amazon ECS keeps getting simpler to run and more capable at scale, and this session provides a product and engineering leadership view of where it is headed next. See how recent investments make ECS faster to deploy applications on, more cost-efficient, and ready for a new class of AI and agentic workloads. We'll discuss the range of compute options, from Fargate to Amazon ECS Managed Instances and how they provide customers choice and flexibility. You will leave this session knowing how to apply the newest ECS capabilities to your workloads today, and what to plan for as the roadmap unfolds.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: What's new in Amazon Bedrock
speaker: Sharadha Kandasubramanian, Shalendra Chhabra
abstract: AI moves fast: new models, new economics, and new governance capabilities. Attend this breakout to learn about the latest innovations across Amazon Bedrock. We cover recent model additions from OpenAI, Anthropic, and more, along with advances in inference and updates across security, governance, and cost management. Whether you are new to Bedrock or tracking the latest releases, see what is available today and where to focus next.

title: What's new in Amazon Redshift
speaker: Naresh Chainani, Matthew Jung, Milind Oke
abstract: Cut costs, query faster, and unify your warehouse and data lake without trade-offs. In this session, learn how new Graviton-powered RG instances deliver better price-performance, a built-in data lake engine lets you read and write Apache Iceberg tables in place, multi-warehouse architecture gives teams independent scale with shared data, and Redshift Serverless improvements let you get insights on your data without managing infrastructure. Whether you're consolidating on open table formats or building the analytics backbone for AI agents, walk away knowing exactly how to put these capabilities to work.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: What's new in Amazon Route 53: DNS innovations for 2026
speaker: Bhargav Talluri, Hardik Rathod
abstract: Explore the latest innovations in Amazon Route 53, AWS's fully managed DNS service. This session covers 2026 launches including Route 53 Global Resolver for secure anycast DNS resolution from anywhere without VPNs, DNS Views sharing across accounts, and expanded DNS Firewall threat protection through partnerships. In this session, we also cover Profiles enhancements for simplified multi-VPC DNS management with granular IAM controls, and expanded domain registration support. Learn how these capabilities help you secure DNS resolution, simplify hybrid and multi-account architectures, and strengthen your DNS security posture at scale.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: What's new in Amazon SageMaker platform
speaker: Brian Ross, Shikha Verma, Derek Chau
abstract: Amazon SageMaker platform is where data engineering, analytics, and AI come together. In this session, see what's new across the platform including innovations in lakehouse architecture that eliminates silos between data teams and AI teams, catalog capabilities for data discovery and governance, and streamlined development experiences that get you from raw data to production models faster. Whether you are building pipelines, running SQL analytics, or training models, learn how SageMaker platform delivers enterprise-grade governance with the flexibility to work the way your team needs.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: What's new in Application Security: Securing applications at machine speed
speaker: Daniel Santana, Christopher Rae, Joao Melo
abstract: AI is accelerating your release cadence. AWS application security capabilities help engineering teams ship secure applications faster, including AI-powered workloads. In this session, learn how AI-driven services enforce organizational guardrails before code is written, perform threat modeling, review code for vulnerabilities, generate fixes automatically, and enable on-demand penetration testing. See how to codify these into paved pathways that give developers room to build with AI while maintaining consistent security standards. Leave with a clear plan for embedding AWS application security into your platform, from design through continuous validation.

title: What's new in AWS Data Processing
speaker: Kinshuk Pahare, Anurag Singh, Bryan Liles
abstract: Explore the latest advancements in AWS Analytics designed to transform your data processing landscape. This session unveils powerful new capabilities across key services, including Amazon EMR for scalable big data processing, AWS Glue for seamless data integration, Amazon Athena for optimized querying, and Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) for complex workflow orchestration. Discover how these innovations can supercharge performance, optimize costs, and streamline your entire data ecosystem. Whether you're looking to enhance scalability, improve data integration, accelerate queries, or refine workflow management, join us to gain actionable insights that will position your organization at the forefront of data processing innovation.

title: What's new in AWS Serverless
speaker: Giedrius Praspaliauskas, Gifty Edwin
abstract: The serverless landscape moves fast, and the months leading up to re:Invent bring a wave of new capabilities for building event-driven applications. This hands-on workshop is your chance to explore the latest releases the moment they land. Build with the newest serverless features, work through the technical trade-offs that matter in real systems, and leave with production-ready patterns you can apply the moment you're back at your desk. You must bring your laptop to participate.

speaker: Nikhil Dabhade, Praneeta Prakash
abstract: Web developers are under pressure to deliver differentiating experiences to more users, faster than ever. Building secure, reliable, scalable applications at 10x speed takes solutions that let developers start easily, ship quickly, and iterate without friction. In this breakout, we'll share how AWS is evolving to meet the needs of modern full-stack developers from defining backends in code and connecting real-time data, to deploying and scaling globally with minimal overhead. Join us to see what's new and where full-stack development on AWS is headed.

title: What's new with Amazon S3... and now files!
speaker: Shakhi Hali, Ben Grubin
abstract: Twenty years of redefining storage, and Amazon S3 continues to evolve beyond objects to serve you wherever you are and however you work with data. This session highlights that evolution, led by the convergence of object and file storage with the launch of S3 Files, delivering full file system access to your S3 data without sacrificing scalability or economics you expect from S3. We also explore S3 Vectors for AI workloads, S3 Metadata for richer data discovery, and S3 Tables for managed Apache Iceberg data lakes. Come see what’s launched, what’s next, and how to put it all to work.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

title: What's new with OpenSearch: AI-native search, agents & observability
speaker: Dotan Horovits, Andrew Ross
abstract: The OpenSearch project has shipped its most transformative year ever. From agentic search with persistent memory, to GPU-accelerated vector search with 58% throughput gains, to a reimagined observability stack with Prometheus and Apache Iceberg support, the 3.x release train delivers capabilities builders can use today. OpenSearch Ambassador Dotan Horovits and TSC Chair Andrew Ross walk you through what's new, what it means for your architecture, and how to put it to work, whether you're building RAG pipelines, deploying monitoring, or creating AI agents.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: What's new with the AWS Sustainability service
speaker: Marta Fraga
abstract: If you've ever wanted to know more about the environmental impact of your cloud usage, this session is for you. In this lightning talk, learn about the latest features of the AWS Sustainability service, including expanded impact areas beyond carbon, increased data granularity, and programmatic access via APIs. We walk through how to use the service to track progress against your sustainability goals and integrate environmental data into your existing workflows and reporting processes. Whether you're just getting started or already reporting on cloud emissions, this session has you covered.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: What SOA taught us about building agents in production
speaker: Andrew Baird
abstract: You’ve taken AI agents from prototype to production, and now you own the hard parts: orchestration sprawl, brittle integrations, and behavior hard to test or observe. The patterns that hold up in production look a lot like ones SOA builders already know. This session explores what emerged: multi-agent orchestration mirroring service meshes, tool-use protocols (MCP) formalizing what APIs did for services, evaluation frameworks echoing contract testing, and hard-won lessons about agent observability and trust boundaries. You leave with concrete patterns from the SOA playbook, updated for the agentic era.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: What to do next after your cloud migration
speaker: Caio Ribeiro Cesar, Baruch Waknine, Yogi Barot
abstract: Rehosting gets workloads to AWS, but that's just the beginning. This session covers the first 90 days after cutover: stabilizing the environment, building observability so decisions are based on real utilization data instead of pre-migration assumptions, applying auto-scaling and right-sizing adjustments that accelerate ROI, and knowing when a workload is ready to modernize versus when to leave it alone. AWS specialists share the decisions and strategy to turn your freshly migrated environment into one worth the investment.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: When agents disagree: Resolving competing goals in cloud operations
speaker: Storm Alexander Manterola Guijt, Asal Shams
abstract: When two agents manage the same workload, each optimizing a different objective, conflicting actions are the default, not the exception. A consensus layer changes the pattern: pillar-aligned agents carry workload goals and live signals as context, reason toward agreement, and produce a single decision playbook before any action executes. In this session, you build one pillar agent from scratch, configure its context layer, connect it to the consensus flow, and watch shared context resolve a live disagreement without rules or priority overrides. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: When Agents Go Rogue: Runtime AIDR and MCP Response Workflows on AWS (sponsored by Wiz)
speaker: Hen Perez, Shashank Golla
abstract: The agent is off to work as soon as execution rights are granted. A coding agent in YOLO mode begins searching a developer workstation for secrets to expand its cloud permissions. In this session, discover how to detect and stop rogue or compromised agents at runtime by connecting behavioral detections directly to automated cloud remediation. We’ll break down AI agent threat challenges: intent drift, an expanded blast radius driven by broad runtime permissions, and the shrinking window to respond when a critical zero-day vulnerability emerges. You’ll also see how the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can connect to your security toolchain to build automated response workflow to answer: Are we affected? Are we protected? Through tangible AWS examples, explore key architectural patterns and leave with an actionable checklist for securely building and governing agents in AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Wiz, an AWS Partner.

title: When agents run code: sandboxes for reliable DevOps
speaker: Simon Moore, Chetan Suri
abstract: LLMs hallucinate. Code doesn't. When your AI agent investigates a production incident, some answers demand computation, not just reasoning. In this code talk, we crack open the sandbox in AWS DevOps Agent: an ephemeral, investigation-scoped Linux environment where the agent writes and runs code inside a Lambda MicroVM with read-only AWS access and zero lateral blast radius. We'll discuss how networking allowlists, pre-installed packages, and executable skills give you deterministic, auditable results for log parsing, metric correlation, and multi-source analysis. Bring your problems and we'll whiteboard the isolation boundaries live.

title: When agents write the code, what does a PM do?
abstract: Coding agents can turn an idea into a working prototype in an afternoon. When building gets cheap, the hard part of product work moves to deciding what is worth building, and why. Join product managers, founders and builders for an open conversation on how product work is changing: discovery, prioritization, measurement and working with engineering when agents do much of the building. Share what has worked for you, what broke, and what you are still figuring out. No slides and no pitch, just peers, a whiteboard and real experiences.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: When AI agents make high-stakes decisions: Build governance on AWS
speaker: Sabrina Petruzzo, Sophie Bacon
abstract: When AI agents approve aid applications, triage patients, or allocate resources, failure isn't a bug — it's a harm. In this workshop, build a production governance layer for high-stakes agentic workflows using AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock, and AgentCore. Implement human approval gates that don't kill velocity, audit trails that satisfy regulators, cost budgets with automatic circuit-breakers, and guardrails for consistent enforcement of policies. Test your governance stack against adversarial scenarios. Leave with a deployable framework applicable anywhere AI decisions affect people — social services, healthcare, finance, or government.

title: When Guardrails Break: Defense in Depth for Non-Deterministic AI (sponsored by Darktrace)
speaker: Margaret Cunningham
abstract: Organizations are deploying copilots, agents, and LLM-driven workflows into production faster than governance and security can adapt. This is no longer just “model risk.” Non-deterministic AI opens a new attack surface across prompts, agents, data pipelines, and runtime behavior, while AI itself acts as both defender and adversary. Guardrails and policy controls remain necessary but cannot reliably detect novel behavior, unsafe tool use, or risk that only emerges when AI interacts with identities and systems in context. This session presents a defense-in-depth model for securing AI, including a practical blueprint for where foundational controls end. It explains why AI must be treated as both an attack surface and an operational system requiring continuous monitoring and containment, and why behavioral oversight is becoming the decisive layer for securing AI at scale.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: When one tenant spikes 100x, your architecture decides who pays
speaker: Shubhankar Sumar, Damian Niezgoda
abstract: One tenant spikes 100x. The architecture either isolates the blast radius or turns it into every tenant's outage. Multi-tenant platforms face four decisions at this boundary. Where to place isolation so one workload cannot starve another. How fan-out creates backpressure that propagates upstream. When fair queuing replaces custom throttling code. What qualifies as real-time versus safely queueable. In this chalk talk you decide where your isolation boundaries belong and what trade-offs each placement creates. Bring your own scaling problem. We draw the architecture together.

title: When security, speed, and trust all matter: Lessons from Project Glasswing
speaker: Clarke Rodgers, Hart Rossman
abstract: In 2026, a frontier AI model demonstrated it could discover and chain software exploits at machine speed. This new reality forced the industry to confront an entirely new class of offensive capability. In this session, learn how AWS Security's Office of the CISO engaged executive customers and partners to build playbooks to help assess AI-era vulnerability management and remediation. We share the lessons implemented with customers, the internal changes AWS made to operate as a more secure AI-first organization, and practical steps every security team can take now.

title: When tags run out: cost allocation for AI and multi-tenant workloads (sponsored by DoiT)
speaker: Amit Kinha
abstract: Tag-based allocation works until the resource stops belonging to anyone. A multi-tenant EKS cluster, a shared inference endpoint, a queue five services write to: each lands on the bill once, charged to whoever provisioned it. No amount of tagging discipline fixes that, because there is nothing to tag. This session covers where tag coverage structurally breaks down, and the alternative: measuring the running system to attribute shared spend to the team, feature, and customer that caused it, then reconciling back to the bill so the allocation still foots. Includes what this looks like in production on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by DoiT, an AWS Partner.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: When Telemetry Steers the Robot: Observability for Physical AI (sponsored by groundcover)
speaker: Matthew Randle, Noam Levy
abstract: Path Robotics is pushing physical AI beyond the lab into tough industrial environments. Its Obsidian AI model autonomously welds production parts, while Rove brings that intelligence into shipyards on a Boston Dynamics quadruped. When AI moves into the physical world, observability becomes mission-critical. Built on AWS, Path needs visibility into AI applications, robot motion, and welding arcs, where traditional observability tools fall short. In this session, Path Robotics and groundcover share how they replaced legacy SaaS observability with a BYOC architecture spanning commercial and sovereign environments. groundcover’s eBPF sensor delivers instant visibility into agentic applications and field robotics, providing critical production context. This presentation is brought to you by groundcover, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: When the Lights Flicker: Engineer Minimum Viable Enterprises for Sovereign Resilience (sponsored by Tata Consultancy Services)
speaker: Manav Sadana
abstract: Geopolitical shocks. Compromised suppliers. Hijacked identities. AI-accelerated attacks. Disruption is now the operating environment. Sovereignty is no longer about where data lives, but what keeps running when the lights flicker. This session introduces Active Sovereignty, which treats sovereignty as continuous, engineered control rather than a compliance checkbox. At its heart is the Minimum Viable Enterprise (MVE): the critical core a business cannot afford to lose across cloud, security, data, AI and the digital workplace. It gives provable control over data, operations and technology, exactly where it matters. Attendees will discover the three moves required for Active sovereignty: (1) designing the MVE, (2) building resilience, and (3) owning the residual risk. You'll leve this session understanding that sovereignty isn't declared, it's engineered.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Where do agents fit? A capability-first approach to agentic AI
speaker: Mukund Rao, Sushanth Mangalore
abstract: Not every workflow needs an agent, and forcing agentic AI where it doesn't fit adds nondeterminism, cost, and failure modes a deterministic design would have avoided. This chalk talk introduces a capability-first methodology for architects and engineering leaders evaluating agentic paths in their workflows, manual or software-driven. At its core is the scoring framework that scores the inherent nature of the work across key dimensions to reveal where agents genuinely fit. You'll walk away with a repeatable rubric your teams can adopt immediately to decide whether agency is required in your workflows.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan I

title: Where embeddings live: Designing production retrieval on AWS
speaker: Amee Shah, Harshil A Shah
abstract: Where should vector embeddings live? In your operational database, a dedicated vector store, or across several? In this session you evaluate the trade-offs across latency, data freshness, cost, and retrieval quality. You implement the same retrieval pattern across three engines: Amazon OpenSearch Service for combined lexical and vector search, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector for SQL-native filtered retrieval, and Amazon S3 Vectors for cost-optimized scale. You learn the workload patterns these engines handle best, so you can tell where a single store is enough and where a hybrid architecture pays off. You leave able to answer where your embeddings should live, backed by patterns you built yourself. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Where's the slowdown? Build observability from frontend to databases
speaker: Samir Behara, Sasi Kiran Malladi
abstract: When an application slows down, the cause can hide anywhere from the frontend to the database, and siloed tools make teams guess. In this workshop, you will build full-stack observability across application, infrastructure, and database layers, bringing RDS and Aurora signals and database logs into one store and correlating them with audit activity. You decide what to trace and build the dashboards that connect a symptom to its root cause. Leave with skills to trace any slowdown across layers in a single pane.

title: Which customization compute? A decision approach for model fine-tuning
speaker: Shashi Kiran, Kanwaljit Khurmi
abstract: Off-the-shelf models work for prototyping, but production forces a choice: which technique and which compute to use. In this chalk talk, we work through the decision framework live, covering when to start fine-tuning after you've pushed the limits of in-context learning and which fine-tuning technique to use. Learn how to choose among Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization, training sessions, training jobs, and Amazon SageMaker HyperPod based on your traffic, budget, and control needs. We'll demo supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on SageMaker AI and use it to help you choose the right compute. Bring your questions.

title: Who Checks the Agents? Quality and Governance for the Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Qodo)
abstract: Agents now plan work, write code, generate tests and open PRs—sometimes without human review before production. Yet most teams rely on a trust model built for a slower SDLC: one reviewer, one merge gate and one chance to catch what went wrong. That model fails when agents operate at every stage and final review can’t reveal what happened upstream. This session treats trust as a property of the pipeline, not a final checkpoint. We’ll explore why the system generating code shouldn’t also verify it, how to turn tribal standards into enforceable, auditable controls, and where independent review belongs between spec and deploy. Key takeaways: Why end-stage review fails in an agent-driven SDLC. How to enforce and trace standards across teams, repos and AI tools. How to decide what can merge automatically, what needs human review and how to document that decision for auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Qodo, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Roman I

title: Who gets to decide the future?
abstract: All week you'll hear what technology will do. This conversation argues that you're the ones deciding. One of tech's most compelling storytellers, joins an expert in tech societal impacts, and an acclaimed novelist who imagines how societies hold together after disruption. Together they separate hype from real capability and ask how today's build choices shape whose future gets built.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: Who's missing from your model?
speaker: Michael Running Wolf
abstract: Every dataset reflects choices about who is included. Researchers working on fairness in machine learning and Indigenous language technology examine who's absent from the data, teams, and user bases behind today's AI. They'll show how those gaps turn into product failures and what builders are doing about it, including community-governed data and better ways to measure fairness. You'll leave knowing what your own gaps may be costing you.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: Who’s Pulling the Strings? Securing GitHub from Rogue AI Agents (sponsored by Zscaler)
speaker: Mrigank Singh
abstract: With the rise of autonomous AI agents like Devin, Cursor, and Amazon Q, the security boundary has shifted from the network perimeter directly to the developer's workspace. These AI tools and automated integration pipelines establish dynamic, encrypted connections straight to GitHub, third-party repositories, and cloud workloads—creating blind spots that legacy firewalls cannot see. Join us as we map out this highly interconnected AI developer ecosystem and showcase why traditional security fails. We will share a unified, proxy-based Zero Trust architecture that inspects encrypted developer traffic, secures access to critical repositories, and isolates untrusted AI actions. You’ll leave with an actionable blueprint to protect your code, APIs, and AI integrations while maintaining peak developer velocity. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Who's Your Security MVP? Here's How AI Ranks Them (sponsored by Trellix)
speaker: Martin Holste
abstract: Yeah, yeah, AI SOC, we get it. But what really goes into getting wins out of AI in security vs saving a couple of clicks? This talk will show the importance of small (dumb) LLM's and how they create opportunities for secops by allowing you to use more tokens, anywhere you want. It will demo how you can go beyond enriching a few alerts to stack rank your most valuable security tools in an ROI thunderdome. You'll learn the AI confidence guardrail framework you need so you to actually start taking actions on your behalf without accidentally deleting all your VM's when you asked it to "eliminate all vulnerabilities." Seeing is believing, so there will be real-world demos of where AI works, where it doesn't, and why--bring your 3D glasses. This presentation is brought to you by Trellix, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Why do we want robots to be like us?
speaker: Catie Cuan, Sri Elaprolu
abstract: Robots don't need faces, personalities, or a sense of humor, yet we keep building them in our own image. AWS's Director of Frontier AI Science and Engineering Sri Elaprolu digs into that instinct with Catie Cuan, a choreographer who dances with robots, and Simone Giertz, the maker famous for building gloriously bad ones. Both have built careers watching people react to machines that move, joke, and spectacularly fail. Together they explore what makes a machine feel trustworthy and when human likeness gets in the way. It's a playful, practical session for anyone designing agents, interfaces, or products people need to trust.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Summit 216 | Showcase Theater

title: Why Enterprise RAG Fails: Document AI and Ontology Patterns on AWS
speaker: Bhuvaneswari Subramani, Ayyanar Jeyakrishnan, Vivek Raja P S
abstract: Most teams blame embeddings, vector databases, or foundation models when RAG systems underperform. In practice, failures often originate earlier in the pipeline where business meaning is lost during document ingestion. This session explores production Document AI patterns on AWS, including layout-aware extraction, ontology-driven classification, semantic chunking, metadata enrichment, and retrieval optimization. Using financial services examples, we demonstrate how domain ontologies improve extraction accuracy, retrieval relevance, and explainability. Attendees will learn practical architecture patterns, implementation tradeoffs, and a framework for building scalable, trustworthy RAG systems for enterprise workloads.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Why Multi-Agent Systems Fail in Production (And How to Fix It) (sponsored by MongoDB)
speaker: Luiz Alves, Anuj Panchal
abstract: Most AI agents don't fall apart in production because the model isn't smart enough. They fail because state is fragmented: one agent can't see what another already learned, and nobody can reconstruct what was retrieved, decided, or handed off. In a multi-tenant setting, that's a governance problem, not just a debugging one. This session shows an architecture that fixes it by giving every layer a clear job: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore manages session context and end-to-end tracing, MongoDB Atlas handles durable memory, tenant-aware vector search, and audit history, and the MongoDB MCP Server connects the two so access stays governed. You'll watch agents share state, retrieve tenant-scoped data, and leave a replayable decision trail. Leave with a reference architecture for multi-agent state sharing and a model for what audit-ready really looks like. A MongoDB & AWS technical session. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Winning enterprise customers with AWS Global Startup Program
speaker: Josh Epstein, Matt Nagle, Meiran Galis, Itamar Friedman
abstract: The AWS Global Startup Program helps startups win and expand enterprise accounts. This session covers how the program drives growth for startups moving into enterprise customers, the resources and support it provides, and how founders can tap into it to accelerate their own path to winning and expanding enterprise business.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Winning the DDoS Game: defend your app under real-time attack
speaker: Julian Garcia, Jonathan Woods
abstract: Compete in a team-based environment where you face real-time threats aimed at your web application. Use the latest capabilities in AWS WAF and AWS Shield to mitigate HTTP floods, web exploits, and malicious bots that disrupt your customers. This risk-free event puts teamwork to the test as you work under pressure. Watch a real-time scoreboard as your team works through each level. Whether it's volumetric attacks or the new wave of AI-driven traffic hitting your APIs, you'll leave prepared to defend against what's coming next. The most effective team earns a prize!

title: Winning the War on Fraud with Network-Powered Intelligence (sponsored by Vonage, Part of Ericsson)
speaker: Oscar Rodriguez, Ramesh Krishnan
abstract: Fraud is winning. SIM swaps have surged over 1,000%; synthetic identity cases are up 60% year-over-year, legacy OTP defenses are structurally broken — and fraudsters know it. Every industry feels it. Banks, healthcare providers, retailers, rideshare and delivery platforms, all fighting the same battle, all demanding the same answer: security that doesn't sacrifice the customer experience. As the first and only communications and Network API provider to achieve the AWS Financial Services Industry Competency, Vonage is changing the equation. Discover how enterprises are moving to a model where identity is verified silently at the network layer, before fraud happens. Built on AWS, powered by direct carrier intelligence. This presentation is brought to you by Vonage, Part of Ericsson, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Women in AI/ML: hard questions on AI systems, careers and leadership
abstract: Running an agentic system in production and trusting it are different problems; this is the gap is where most AI programs stall. Leaders deciding where AI capability gets built see that signal well before the market does. Senior AWS leaders in AI/ML and Support will answer open questions on how they forecast failure before customers encounter it and prepare their teams for it, how to judge which AI investments are returning value, and how to build a career that survives a technology resetting every few months. This session is hosted by the Women in AI/ML community, open to everyone.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Women in Tech: AI Trends, Bets, and Skills for 2027
abstract: AI is reshaping how we build, invest, and lead, and women in tech have an opportunity to shape what comes next. Join AWS women leaders and allies for an open conversation on three questions: Which AI trends matter most for 2027? Where should you and your organization invest your time and budget? Which skills will set you apart as agents take on more of the work? We will build a shared map on the whiteboard, swap career stories, and connect with peers. Everyone is welcome. Leave with new connections and a concrete next step for your AI journey.

abstract: Join AWS for an afternoon celebrating women in tech and allies. Connect with leaders across industries in a welcoming, energetic atmosphere with curated food, beverage, and surprise moments throughout. abstract: Experience the expo floor alongside a powerful community of leaders. Join The Female Quotient and AWS Women of the Cloud at Casa Playa for opening remarks from Female Quotient CEO Shelley Zalis, then walk together to the Global Impact Zone. title: Women Who Build, Lead & Scale
abstract: What does it take to build, lead, and grow in an ecosystem that never stops evolving? From navigating complex technical challenges and making architectural decisions to leading teams, building products, winning customers, and scaling businesses, women across the AWS ecosystem bring perspectives and experiences the community needs to hear. This meetup creates space for women to share what they are building, the challenges they are solving, the lessons they have learned, and the questions they are still figuring out. Whether you work in engineering, sales, marketing, product, leadership, or entrepreneurship, come ready to exchange ideas, learn from real experiences, and leave with fresh perspectives and connections that last beyond re:Invent.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Workload Identity Federation in multicloud environments
speaker: Simran Singh, Preetam Rebello
abstract: Eliminating long-lived credentials across clouds is essential for secure multicloud operations. This session presents three proven identity federation patterns: leveraging native OIDC providers from Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure to assume AWS IAM roles with short-lived tokens, federating Kubernetes service accounts across cloud boundaries, and using SPIFFE/SPIRE for cryptographic workload identity across Kubernetes clusters. We walk through architecture decisions, trust policy design, and security best practices for each approach - covering GCP Workload Identity, Microsoft Entra ID federation, and cross-cluster OIDC. Attendees leave with actionable blueprints for credential-free multicloud access.

title: Workload Identity Federation in multicloud environments
speaker: Simran Singh, Preetam Rebello
abstract: Eliminating long-lived credentials across clouds is essential for secure multicloud operations. title: World models for indoor robots: what breaks and why
speaker: Parmida Atighehchian, Sarik Ghazarian, Andrea Thomaz
abstract: World models promise to give robots predictive understanding of their environment, yet applying them to indoor robotics exposes fundamental gaps in how transformers reason about geometry. In this session, we present findings from building a trajectory-conditioned lidar world model for Diligent Robotics' hospital fleet on AWS. We examine why standard loss metrics fail for generative spatial predictions, why rotation breaks factored attention even with explicit conditioning, and the minimal set of inductive biases needed to restore geometric coherence. Attendees leave with a diagnostic framework for spatial reasoning failures in transformer-based world models.

title: World Models & Physical AI: The next frontier in intelligent systems
speaker: Jessica Inman, Andy Chen, Sam Sinha, Eric Saleh, Murtaza Chowdhury
abstract: World models—AI systems that simulate and predict complex environments—are emerging with new modalities including Video, Vision, Language, Action to power physical AI, autonomous systems, and real-time video generation. From humanoid robotics to immersive entertainment, these models are transforming how machines perceive, think, and interact with the physical world. In this panel, hear from researchers and customers on how they're building and deploying world models in production, the business opportunities they unlock, and the unique technical challenges they present. Learn how AWS AI infrastructure powers these use cases at scale with speed, efficiency, and automatic fault recovery.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: World Models: The New Frontier for Interactive Media
speaker: Gorkem Yurtseven, Alberto Taiuti, Pronoy Chopra
abstract: 2026 is the year of world models: AI that generates entire environments you can move through in real time, where the scene stays consistent and responds to you frame by frame. But plenty of things get labeled "world models" now, and it's hard to tell what's real. Join Pronoy Chopra from the AWS Startups Frontier AI team in conversation with two companies building at the front of this space: Reactor, whose platform serves real-time worlds at interactive speed, and fal, the inference platform running 1,400+ models for teams like Adobe, Canva and Shopify. We'll cover what world models actually are, where they're being used in studios, games and sports today, and the hard part nobody warns you about: what it takes to serve them at low latency and sane cost. If you're building interactive media, this is the grounding you need before you bet on one.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Theater

title: Wrong, Not Broken, & Why your Observability should know the difference, feat. 3M
speaker: Imaya Kumar Jagannathan, Kimberlee Otto, Nikhil Kapoor
abstract: When an agent fails, it rarely throws an error. It gives the wrong answer, and diagnosis takes hours. The cause may be the model, the prompt, or bad downstream data, with evidence scattered across tools. Learn techniques to identify issues across agents and services and correlate them into one incident. We look ahead to AI agents investigating incidents alongside engineers, using open-standard telemetry accessible to engineers and agents with purpose-built tools and system context. See how 3M is using CloudWatch Omni addresses each, and leave with agent development techniques, reference architectures for agentic observability, and ways to optimize observability with OpenTelemetry.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: You cannot write the eval for a failure you have not seen yet (sponsored by Arize AI)
speaker: Aparna Dhinakaran
abstract: LLM-as-a-judge works beautifully when you already know what you're looking for. You write the rubric, validate it against human labels, and it catches the failure you designed it to catch. But agents in production don't fail the way you anticipated. They fail as they meet new tools, new users, and environments that shifted underneath them, and every new failure arrives after the rubric was written. This talk argues the evaluation layer itself must become agentic. Instead of specifying a metric, you describe the behavior you want, and a judge with tool access inspects the trace, finds the spans that matter, classifies what went wrong, and generates labels you can monitor against. We'll cover why this became viable only recently, where it fails, and how to keep an agentic judge honest against human labels, so you know when to reach for one and how to validate it. This presentation is brought to you by Arize AI, an AWS Partner.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Your Agent Has an Upstream Dependency You Can't See (sponsored by Brave)
abstract: Verify, don't trust: a reproducible needle test that surfaces undeclared upstream calls in any stack. This presentation is brought to you by Brave, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Your Agent Is in Production. Can You Explain What It Did? (sponsored by Datadog)
speaker: Andrew Krug
abstract: Your team shipped an agent to production last quarter. It works, mostly. When it doesn't, nobody can explain why. This session covers what changes when non-deterministic systems enter your stack: which signals actually matter for agentic workloads, how to trace a multi-step agent across tools and models, and where AI agents can safely take action in your own operations. Live examples from Datadog LLM Observability, the Agent Console, AI Guard, and Bits AI. You'll leave with an instrumentation checklist. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Your agent wants a bigger job: The next era of agents at work (sponsored by OpenAI)
speaker: Teri Yu, Madhav Thattai, Chris Dickens
abstract: What would you make AI responsible for if it could work across days, teams, and business systems? Drawing on lessons from inside OpenAI, explore how agents can expand the work your organization takes on. Learn how OpenAI’s frontier models, agent runtimes, and connectors bring intelligence and organizational context together, enabling agents to act as coworkers and collaborate across teams and functions. See how dots and Bedrock Managed Agents for OpenAI can take on bigger jobs.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Your AI agent gets a budget when Agentic AIOps meets FinOps (sponsored by ManageEngine)
speaker: Ananthkumar KS
abstract: AI agents can now detect, diagnose, and act in seconds. Observability tells them what is happening. The harder question is how they decide. What is an action worth, and what should an agent optimize for? The intersection of Agentic AIOps and FinOps answers both. The result is a blueprint for business-aware autonomous operations, and three practical steps to apply it in your own environment. This presentation is brought to you by ManageEngine, an AWS Partner.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Your Business Is Multiplayer. Your AI Should Be Too. (sponsored by PromptQL)
speaker: Suku Krishnaraj
abstract: Your company runs on a network of teams, partners and stakeholders. Yet most AI works with one person at a time and forgets everything between sessions, so the work and the context stay trapped in private chats. This session introduces a different model: multiplayer AI built on shared context. When teams and their AI draw on one governed, continuously updated source of organizational knowledge, work moves across people without starting over, answers stay consistent, and each person's permissions are respected. Come see what it takes to make your AI as multiplayer as your business already is.
room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

title: Your data is your AI advantage: From foundation to business value
speaker: Ram Vittal, Anastasia Tzeveleka
abstract: Your AI is only as good as the data underneath it. Most teams treat data preparation and model serving as separate problems, then wonder why costs spike and quality drops at scale. This chalk talk connects the two. We whiteboard how to design governed data products that feed customization, inference on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and agent workloads on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Then apply cost levers like prompt caching, distillation, and batch inference that compound when built on clean, governed data. You leave with the design decisions that let you scale AI with confidence and control.

title: Your data, optimized models, lower costs: Turn business knowledge into AI you control
speaker: Karan Bhandarkar, Rosa Català, Pooja Karadgi, Akash Bhatia
abstract: With dozens of models now available and new ones launching every week, customers face three questions: which models to start from, when does model customization unlock added performance or savings, and when to replace a model, either because their own needs changed or because a better model emerged. In this session, learn how to build custom evaluations for your specific use case with your own data, then reuse it choose the model for your use case based on quality and cost, track how customization improves performance, and confidently decide when a model is ready to deploy to production. When requirements change or new models become available, you can update and rerun the evaluation, enabling ongoing improvement of performance and cost against your specific business needs.
room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Your data, your engine: How open source and open standards power analytics on AWS
speaker: Ram Nottath, Arun Shanmugam
abstract: Open table formats and open-source engines like DuckDB give organizations the freedom to choose the right tool for each workload, from interactive dashboards and exploratory analytics to large-scale data processing, with no lock-in. In this session, learn how to capitalize these open tools to build on AWS and turn it into a competitive advantage for your business. We deep dive into the application of each engine, how they complement one another across the analytics lifecycle, and how data governance capabilities like catalog access, fine-grained governance, and consistent table management on AWS further simplify multi-engine architectures in production.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: "You're Absolutely Right!" — And Other Things Your Agent Says Before Breaking Prod
abstract: Your coding agent is great until it confidently invents an API that doesn't exist, writes an IAM policy that grants nothing or everything, or debugs a CloudFormation stack by guessing. The difference between an agent that wastes your afternoon and one that genuinely ships is mostly in how you set it up. Come trade tactics for getting Kiro, Claude Code, Cursor, and friends to excel at AWS work — writing code that deploys, debugging live in your account, triaging issues, and knowing when to trust the output versus when to read every line. Bring your best prompts, your context-setup tricks, and your favorite "I can't believe it actually did that" stories — good and bad.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Your IPs, your rules: Dynamic edge routing without NAT for AWS BYOIP
speaker: Ammar Latif, Srinivas Kurla
abstract: Some workloads need the public IP the world sees to live directly on the Amazon EC2 instances, with no translation in the path. Email gateways rotating sender IPs, VPN concentrators assigning a dedicated address per client, or security appliances terminating traffic on the exact advertised address need the instance to own those public IPs. In this live-coding talk, we build that model end-to-end on AWS: writing CloudFormation for BYOIP pools and Bring Your Own ASN, coding NAT-free ingress routing so traffic arrives untranslated, and configuring BGP peering with Amazon VPC Route Server for high availability.

title: Your network, your rules: Global routing policies with AWS Cloud WAN
speaker: Mandar Sridhar Alankar, Shubham Singh
abstract: As global networks scale, they demand deterministic traffic paths, not best-effort routing. In this workshop, gain granular control over traffic flows between Regions, VPCs, and on-premises locations using AWS Cloud WAN routing policies across a multi-Region network. Through hands-on labs, configure route filtering to control reachability, summarize prefixes to reduce routing table complexity, and influence preferred paths with BGP attributes. Leave with practical skills to design scalable, policy-driven connectivity architectures. Bring your laptop.

title: Your new playbook: Operationalizing security in a world of AI
speaker: Eric Brandwine
abstract: The timeline for responding to a security issue has compressed. Change is now constant and can be bewildering, and as security professionals we still need to deliver on our promises to customers. In this session, Eric Brandwine, AWS VP and Distinguished Engineer, will show you what you can do, today, to help your security team move faster and more effectively, and to adapt to the new world of change. Eric will draw on decades of experience building security at AWS to share the architectural patterns, operational best practices, and mental models that help teams move from announcement to adoption. Whether you're a security leader setting strategy or a practitioner building the systems, you'll leave with a clear understanding of how to take advantage of the new opportunities in front of you and to raise your security bar.

title: Your next Quantum developer might be an AI agent
speaker: Erik Garcell, Ishaan Pakrasi, Nick White
abstract: AI is changing who can build quantum applications. See how AI assistants including Kiro, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Jupyter AI, and Classiq help developers move from natural-language prompts to optimized quantum workloads on Amazon Braket. Learn how AI generates code, synthesizes hardware-aware circuits, benchmarks on simulators and QPUs, and integrates with HPC resources. Through real examples, you'll see how AI-native workflows reduce complexity, accelerate experimentation, and make quantum development accessible to more builders.

title: Your playbook for modernizing 988K lines of .NET in 2 days
speaker: Mustaali Dehnuwala, Anitha Deenadayalan
abstract: Transaction Network Services (TNS) needed to modernize their internal payment related platform that included 274 projects, 988K lines of code, and 20 years of legacy .NET Framework to .NET 10. Their estimate: six months. The result: two days, 26 modules migrated, and 34 security vulnerabilities resolved. In this session, you'll learn what made it possible - from upgrading shared libraries first, running deterministic tools before AI, using human-verified tests, to keeping engineers on the keyboard after the tools stop running. Walk away with a practical, repeatable playbook for accelerating large-scale .NET modernization
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Your playbook: turn your scattered databases into AI-ready infrastructure
speaker: Aarthi Raju, Sudhir Balasubramanian
abstract: Business-critical data scattered across Oracle, SQL Server, and VMware or Nutanix-hosted databases is the number one blocker to deploying agentic AI at scale. In this lightning talk, you'll get a practical playbook for database migration to AWS: real licensing challenges, cost optimization strategies, and modernization pathways that accelerate the path to cloud-native databases using AWS Transform and agentic AI. You'll leave with a clear migration framework that turns fragmented data estates into AI-ready infrastructure, no matter where your databases live today.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Your regulator set your RTO. Not your architecture.
speaker: Hossam Ebrahim, Paul Armstrong
abstract: Organizations with pre-approved failover regions recover in hours. Those without recover in weeks. Same impairment. Same services. One governance decision separates them, and it’s made years before the event. This session presents architectural patterns for multi-Region recovery under sovereignty constraints, drawn from real operational experience with regulated workloads under regional pressure. Three categories: decisions that set your resilience ceiling before any event, dependencies that create circular failure during recovery, and assets nobody backs up until they become the critical path. You leave with the decisions to evaluate before your next DR test.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Light Blue Theater

title: Your runtime Is being deprecated. Your weekend isn't.
speaker: Renuka Krishnan, Alpna Sharma Daniels
abstract: Your inbox fills with runtime deprecation notices—hundreds of Lambda functions on Node.js 20, Python 3.10, and whatever's next. Handling them one by one drains capacity you'd rather spend on features. This hands-on workshop flips the script: instead of chasing individual apps, you'll modernize a fleet. Using AWS Transform custom, you'll run AWS-provided transformations to upgrade Lambda runtimes at scale, then stand up continuous modernization to scan repositories against a baseline, prioritize what's drifting, and open pull requests automatically. Turn a wall of end-of-support alerts into a queue of ready-to-merge PRs. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Your system made a decision. you cannot explain it.
speaker: Haresh Nandwani, Richard Ainley
abstract: Your system makes a decision. A human makes a decision. Both write to the same log in the same format. Three months later you need to know which was which. You cannot tell. This is not a logging problem. It is a runtime architecture problem. If decision origin is not captured at the boundary when the decision happens, no system can recover it after. Whether you need this for compliance, debugging, or customer trust, the architectural fix is identical. In this chalk talk you will decide: what to capture at the decision boundary, how much context to store, and when reproducibility justifies the cost.

title: Your Users Aren't Waiting to Build AI Agents. Are You Ready?
speaker: Rian Brooks-Kane, Ian Mckay
abstract: The spreadsheet wizards and automation tinkerers in your organization are already reaching for low-code and visual builder tools to assemble AI agents on their own. Call it citizen agent building: either governance sprawl, or your fastest path to scale. This interactive chalk talk gives platform, security, and data leaders a reference pattern that puts low-code builders on top and Amazon Bedrock beneath, so the security, data residency, and governance enterprises need come from the foundation rather than from each agent. Amazon Bedrock makes governance possible; your architecture makes it the default.

title: Your WAN, reimagined: SD-WAN on the AWS global backbone
speaker: Anandprasanna Gaitonde, Mehdi Dahane
abstract: Your enterprise WAN was built for a world where applications lived in data centers. That world is gone, but you're still paying for MPLS circuits and waiting weeks for new sites. What if you could replace that backbone entirely? AWS offers the largest global infrastructure footprint of any provider: resilient, agile, low-latency, and encrypted. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how to connect your SD-WAN to AWS Cloud WAN, maintain segmentation from branch to VPC, and pay only for what you use—no long-term contracts. Bring your WAN architecture and we'll show you what it looks like without the middlemen.

title: Zero-Downtime Deployments on AWS: What Actually Works
abstract: Everyone wants zero-downtime releases, and few teams get there without scars. This peer discussion brings together developers, architects, and platform engineers to compare what works in production on AWS. We'll work through four prompts: choosing between blue/green, canary, and rolling deployments with AWS CodeDeploy, Amazon ECS, Lambda aliases, and weighted routing; changing database schemas without breaking running code; handling long-lived connections, caches, and DNS during cutover; and deciding when to roll back automatically. Bring a deployment that went wrong, or one you're proud of, and leave with a shared checklist of patterns and pitfalls from the room.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | AWS Meetups

title: Zero-Shot demand forecasting with Chronos 2, SMUS & AWS Quick
speaker: saadari Adari, Prakash Srinivasan
abstract: Stockouts and overstocks quietly erode margin through lost sales, markdowns, and misallocated working capital. Traditional forecasting models take months to train and fail on new products and locations. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to architect zero-shot demand forecasting pipelines using Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio with Chronos 2—the time-series foundation model built and proven on Amazon's own retail demand at scale—requiring no historical training. We cover SMUS notebooks for experimentation, Chronos 2 for multivariate prediction, and AWS Quick for conversational forecast analytics.

title: Zero to multimodal in 60 mins: Building Live Sync on Connect Customer
speaker: Andrei Papancea, Joe Sullivan
abstract: What does it take to synchronize a live voice conversation with a real-time visual interface — and make it feel like magic? In this chalk talk, we'll answer that question by building one from scratch. Starting from first principles, we'll construct a fully functional voice AI agent that leverages the patented Live Sync on Amazon Connect Customer: the signaling that keeps voice and visual in lock-step, the state machine that drives bi-directional interaction, and the rendering layer that turns conversational intent into on-screen UI in real time. No slides, no hand-waving — just building, live, from zero to a working multimodal agent in 60 minutes. At the end, we'll deploy what we built and every phone in the room becomes a live demo.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Zero to one: Crafting a GTM playbook for frontier AI startups
abstract: You built a model the world hasn't seen before. Now you need your first ten enterprise customers and the playbook that got the last generation of SaaS startups to market won't work for frontier AI. Pricing is different, buyer psychology is different, and the competitive window is measured in months, not years. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard what a go-to-market strategy actually looks like for frontier AI startups navigating the zero-to-one phase while still searching for product-market fit. We'll cover how to identify your beachhead customers, position against incumbents and leverage AWS distribution channels to accelerate enterprise traction.
room: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum Event Plaza | Startup Plaza Studio

title: Zero-Trust by Design: How Bee Protects Personal Data Even from Itself on AWS
speaker: Gopinath Jagadesan
abstract: Personal agentic AI represents a new frontier; devices that understand you deeply enough to act on your behalf. Bee is Amazon's AI wearable that helps users capture and act on insights from their daily lives. But deep personalization demands deep trust and privacy. In this session, learn how the Bee team architected a zero-trust pipeline using AWS Nitro Enclaves and confidential computing to keep sensitive data cryptographically isolated at every stage. We'll share the attestation models, data minimization tradeoffs, and design principles you can apply to build AI-powered experiences your users trust from day one.
room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Zero trust for non-human identities: IAM for autonomous agents
speaker: Yaniv Cadosh, Shimi Rokah, Arvind Ayyaswamy, Brendan Paul
abstract: Agents access tools, call APIs, and delegate to other agents. They need layered identity controls at every stage. In this builders' session, apply zero trust principles to a multi-agent environment using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll configure agent identities with OAuth providers, enforce least privilege via OBO token exchange, differentiate agents from humans with IAM MCP condition keys, and set Gateway rules blocking unauthorized access. Then, you stress test your setup using cross-chain access, privilege escalation, identity spoofing to see each blocked by a different layer you built.
room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

title: Zero-Trust Identity & Data Protection in AWS Quick
speaker: Art Chan, Shane Thompson
abstract: Anyone can generate apps from a sentence - the hard part is governing them and getting them in front of the right users. This chalk talk whiteboards the full lifecycle of AWS Quick Apps: building them from natural language with no separate hosting, wiring in data and actions through MCP, and the three sharing paths - private, public URLs, and enterprise sharing gated behind admin approval workflows.
